cards.title: Zero-copy views over text, bytes, and mapped files
cards.body:
Probes prim-text (G2), prim-storage (G1), prim-numerics-perf (G3): core.text returns a new String per grapheme, word, and line (fixed_sigs.rs:2250-2263), there is no byte view (E1004 core.text.bytes) and no memory mapping (E1004 core.files.mmap); a 100 MB scan measured 6.9 s in Jet against 33 ms in Rust and a BPE tokenizer 108 s against 3.2 s in Python. Law: View<T>/ViewMut<T> with provenance (D-MEM-VIEWRET1), read-view into a non-view slot copies (D-MEM-COPYSEM1), Pin (D-PIN1-3). Evidence: docs/research/domain-foundations/all-gaps.json.

Gate: D-FOUND-VIEW1. The card starts when the owner ratifies the ballot; no code before that.
cards.plan: After ratification: text and byte iteration APIs return View<str> and View<[U8]> (storing them copies by the existing law, so callers do not change); files.map(path) lends a private read-only mapping whose windows are byte views pinned for the mapping's life; shared mappings stay an expert #Unsafe path; the same Prelude functions serve every tier; goldens for the 100 MB scan and the tokenizer with timings against Rust and Python. blockedBy: none (the ballot on this card is the gate).

log.text: Source implementation closure recorded from FilesMapViewImpl receipt; runtime/build/test proof deferred to #2919 by current owner instruction.

MappedFile Prelude implementation now provides Arc-pinned read-only mmap, Unix/Windows writer exclusion, checked zero-copy windows/CRLF line views, borrowed bytes, and opaque SHA-256 source identity with offset/length facts. Text/byte ViewIter sema and Prelude source also landed; tier adapters/goldens wait on MIR.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.text: Implementation-only closure: mapped files use the existing read-only view ownership mechanism, return checked view-shaped types through nested Option/Result/Shared carriers, root every borrowed result in the receiver mapping, and route AOT, JIT, interpreter, and applicable web behavior through the same mmap Prelude kernels.
criteria.evidence: Source audit found one shared is_mapped_file_view_method classifier, fixed inference preserving the checked resolved return, recursive ViewKind derivation through Result/Option/Shared/ViewIter/View, receiver-rooted read borrows, and unchanged canonical mmap kernels/routes. cards.title: Platform services in core.ui: dialogs, clipboard, IME, drag, shortcuts, accessible names, text shaping

cards.title: Interrupts, DMA ownership, and typed register blocks from the target profile
cards.body:
Probe area-embedded (G2, G3, G7): no interrupt or vector-table surface (E1004 core.interrupt; core.sys.on_interrupt is a process hook), no DMA ownership (E1004 core.dma; mem.pin proves address stability only), and register access is hand-written #Unsafe per board (jet inspect unsafe: pointer_from_address + volatile). Law: typed target profiles with memory regions, linker, allocator, and audit (D-TARGET-SURFACE1, D-TARGET-MEMORY1, D-TARGET-LINKER1), #Layout(c) (D-REPRC1), volatile spelling (D-FLAGSHIP-MMIO1), pin (D-PIN1-3). Evidence: docs/research/domain-foundations/all-gaps.json.

Gate: D-FOUND-BOARD1. The card starts when the owner ratifies the ballot; no code before that.
cards.plan: After ratification: the board profile carries the vendor SVD; the compiler generates typed register blocks (width, access mode, volatile) under the profile module; #Interrupt(vector, effects) binds a bounded handler that may not allocate or wait; dma.start(channel, ^buffer) transfers buffer ownership and wait() returns it; host replay keeps the same semantics; Syntax.rs entries; diagnostics with snapshots; the embedded example builds for board.sensor_v1 and replays on the host with goldens. blockedBy: none (the ballot on this card is the gate).

log.text: All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.text: Source-complete: exact target-profile SVD facts generate typed volatile register blocks; bounded interrupt and DMA ownership rows preserve exact profile/channel/type identities across AOT, JIT, and interpreter replay. Board/emulator, misuse diagnostics, inspect output, and goldens are deferred to #2919.
criteria.evidence: Unresolved hardware references remain diagnostic-only; no width/channel/profile defaults or fabrication. MIR serializes exact facts; AOT emits typed accessors; JIT and interpreter install the same shared hardware replay kernel; DMA pins the owned typed buffer until token wait returns it. No tests/builds run during implementation-only pass.

cards.title: Core API additions surfaced by the probes: eleven names, no new mechanism
cards.body:
The probes surfaced eleven plain additions to shipped core modules. None is a new mechanism; each is a name a library author reached for and found missing. The owner gates them as one batch (2026-09-02): accept all, accept the essentials, or reject.

1. ProcessStdin.close() sends EOF to a child (area-cli-G1; E0102).
2. files.walk(root, ignore: .gitignore) ignore-aware traversal with nested rules, negation, anchoring (area-cli-G2).
3. game.run(scene, replay:, frames:) frame budget for headless replay (area-games-G1; E0764).
4. core.game.raylib gamepad buttons/axes and texture atlas decode plus draw_sprite (area-games-G2, G3; E1004).
5. core.db.pool(url, max:) bounded acquisition, health/reset, readiness, drain (area-backend-G1; E1004).
6. core.web OpenAPI export from Router facts with operation identity (area-backend-G2; refs e14 #2472).
7. Stream.key_by/window/watermark event-time operators with late-event disposition (prim-distributed-G1; E0102).
8. DateTime leap-second label 23:59:60 on UTC instants (prim-time-G1; E3002; refs open D-TIMEDEPTH1).
9. jet package: desktop bundle, installer, signing metadata (area-gui-G7; E2101; refs e14 #2490 game packaging).
10. jet flash --target board.<name>: program a device and record a typed receipt (area-embedded-G6; E2101).
11. build.graph() and receipt diff as a typed in-process query for tools (prim-tooling-hooks-G2; refs D-BUILDQUERY1).

Essentials, if the owner picks B: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. Evidence per item: docs/research/domain-foundations/all-gaps.json.

cards.title: Battery and example: Web
cards.body:
A first-party web battery: Orders package skeleton with authority and static host page, typed route helpers for query decoding and responses, a typed form decoder with validation, an SSR page plus browser island with serializable props, SQLite migration and query fixtures, session login and protected routes, and a deterministic end-to-end harness. Query and form typing land through e14 #2472/#2474 (D-DX-SUITE1); this battery consumes them.

Parts the probe named (docs/research/domain-foundations/probes/area-web.md, batteries.json):
- [library] Orders package skeleton with authority, server entry, and static host page: A first program needs one checked package shape that starts an HTTP server and serves a page.
- [library] Typed route helpers for path parameters, query decoding, status responses, and redirects: The current mux handles path patterns, but query extraction and response conventions must be rebuilt by each web package.
- [library] Typed form decoder with required-field, numeric-range, and error-display helpers: The probe had to read raw text, split pairs, and validate fields before a create action could be safe.
- [library] SSR page plus browser-island template using reactive state and serializable props: The server and client built separately, but a battery should show their boundary and hydration data in one example.
- [library] SQLite migration, policy scope, query, mutation, and explicit invalidation fixture: A working data route needs persistence and a visible refetch after mutation, not only an isolated database call.
- [library] Session login, cookie round trip, protected route, and failure cases: Auth is part of the smallest useful full-stack app and should be exercised over HTTP.
- [needs core] Deterministic end-to-end harness with a local listener and client requests: The probe used one executable flow to prove list, create, detail, login, protection, and assets together.
- [needs core] Web and native build smoke commands with manifest and compiler diagnostics: The client target built, while the native server exposed a compiler failure that a first-party battery must catch.
- [needs core] Dev watcher fixture that edits a route and records restart or state retention: The watcher rebuilt and restarted after an edit; the battery must make in-memory state retention observable.

The probe program under docs/research/domain-foundations/code/area-web/pkg/ is the starting point; its probe.md records what already works with exact commands.
cards.plan: The battery is a first-party package written in Jet, maintained by the project and installed by default, never inside core; the implementing orchestrator chooses the registry location the jetpack track owns. Land it with one executable example under examples/features/web/ that runs the whole first program, with goldens on default jet run, --release, jet build, and the web target where it applies (I9). Parts marked "needs core" wait for their gate (the refs); parts marked "library" land first. cards.title: Battery and example: Games
cards.body:
A first-party games battery: package authority and asset fixtures, a fixed-step accumulator with interpolation, AABB and parent transforms, a scene graph, a 600-frame replay with injected input and a deterministic hash, sprite atlas drawing, a keyboard and gamepad input matrix, an audio callback and music stream, and a save-file round trip. Gamepad, atlas, and frame budget names depend on D-FOUND-COREAPI1; the audio callback on D-FOUND-REALTIME1.

Parts the probe named (docs/research/domain-foundations/probes/area-games.md, batteries.json):
- [needs core] package.jet authority and asset fixtures: Lets a first program declare filesystem and graphics effects and carry its assets.
- [needs core] core.game Scene, component/query, input.bind, on_frame, and headless transcript: Provides the stable scene and input contract before a renderer is attached.
- [library] fixed-step accumulator, interpolation, AABB, and parent-transform helpers: Shows that simulation and hierarchy remain ordinary, deterministic Jet library code.
- [needs core] raylib headless window, drawing, and one-shot sound smoke: Catches display fallback, draw calls, keyboard input, and sound-effect behavior.
- [needs core] sprite-asset fixture with atlas decode, region lookup, and draw: Must exercise a real texture path; the current API only retains an opaque image path.
- [needs core] 600-frame replay with injected input and deterministic hash: Tests a real frame budget and repeatability instead of only the current three-frame transcript.
- [needs core] audio callback deadline and music-stream lifecycle: Measures callback-safe processing and stream updates; neither surface exists in current core.
- [library] save-file and pause-menu round trip: Checks persistence and pause state without coupling the test to a renderer.
- [needs core] keyboard and gamepad input matrix: Separates the working keyboard fallback from missing controller buttons and axes.

The probe program under docs/research/domain-foundations/code/area-games/pkg/ is the starting point; its probe.md records what already works with exact commands.

cards.title: Battery and example: Data analysis
cards.body:
A first-party data battery: 100k typed CSV load into the core table, filter, group, pivot, rolling window, and describe, a typed OLS result record, a labeled array over the core tensor, an SVG and a PNG plot with a JSON receipt, a Parquet reader through the foreign-handle bridge, and a reactive notebook fixture; timed against pandas and polars on the same input. Parquet depends on D-FOUND-HANDLE1; the Tensor-in-struct defect (#2769) blocks the labeled array.

Parts the probe named (docs/research/domain-foundations/probes/area-data.md, batteries.json):
- [needs core] csv_load_100k: Load 100,000 typed CSV rows, materialize a core table, and verify row count plus schema.
- [needs core] table_ops_100k: Exercise filter, group mean and sum, pivot, rolling mean, and describe over the same 100k input.
- [library] typed_ols: Fit typed slope, intercept, and R-squared values and preserve them in a typed result record.
- [library] manual_group_join: Join grouped summaries to owner records as the fallback for the default-tier inner_join gap.

cards.title: Battery and example: Backend services
cards.body:
A first-party backend battery: a typed JSON route starter with request ids and status errors, SQLite migration and policy helpers, a durable local queue worker, session and role middleware, a structured log and metric sink, OpenAPI export from Router facts, a bounded database pool, request deadlines with SIGTERM drain, and a 1000-user load harness with p50/p95/p99. Pool and OpenAPI depend on D-FOUND-COREAPI1; deadlines and signals on D-FOUND-LIFECYCLE1; the native server build on #2762.

Parts the probe named (docs/research/domain-foundations/probes/area-backend.md, batteries.json):
- [library] Typed HTTP JSON route starter: Give a first service typed request/response DTOs, method routes, request IDs, status errors, and an in-process client smoke path.
- [library] SQLite migration and policy helper: Package the checked SQL, migration checksum, scoped policy, row access, transaction, and close sequence used by the probe.
- [library] Durable local queue worker helper: Make bounded workers, durable sends, delivery status, state log, receive, retry, and shutdown one teachable path.
- [library] Session and role middleware helper: Keep session validation, role checks, unauthorized JSON, and cookie/header policy out of every route body.
- [library] Structured log and metric sink helper: Standardize trace ID, span, counters, JSONL or OTLP-file sink selection, flush, and redaction.
- [needs core] OpenAPI contract metadata and validator: A first service needs route-derived operations, schemas, status responses, auth, export, validation, and contract replay without duplicated JSON.
- [needs core] Bounded database pool adapter: Production startup needs bounded acquisition, health/reset, transaction ownership, contention policy, and graceful pool drain.
- [needs core] Request deadline and shutdown signal adapter: A service needs request cancellation, deadline propagation, SIGTERM handling, and a bounded drain before process exit.
- [library] Concurrent load and contract harness: Provide 1000 virtual users, status/error accounting, raw latency samples, p50/p95/p99, and a machine-readable assertion receipt.

cards.title: Battery and example: AI and ML applications
cards.body:
A first-party AI battery: ranked Tensor construction and broadcasting, a two-layer training recipe with compute.gradient and SGD, a deterministic Dataset/Loader with seed, shuffle, and bounded batches, checksummed model-state save and restore, an exact embedding index with cosine top-k, an OpenAI-compatible SSE reader with a bounded tool loop, an explicit F32 GPU placement receipt, and a same-size matmul timing harness against NumPy and PyTorch. Blocked by the autodiff defect (#2772), the Tensor-in-struct defect (#2769), and the checker slowdown (#2779).

Parts the probe named (docs/research/domain-foundations/probes/area-ai.md, batteries.json):
- [library] Ranked Tensor construction, broadcasting, matmul, reduction, and shape inspection: The application needs one checked array value and a visible shape law before model code or embedding code can be trusted.
- [needs core] Two-layer training recipe with named parameters, loss, gradient, and SGD update: This is the central AI training loop. The manual chain-rule fallback works, but the intended compute.gradient path is not executable across tiers.
- [library] Deterministic Dataset/Loader wrapper with seed, shuffle, bounded batches, and collate: The probe had to hand-write order shuffling and two batch constructors; this is common connective tissue for every training example.
- [library] Checksummed model-state save and restore with explicit file authority: A training run must prove that restored parameters equal the saved parameters before deployment or resume.
- [library] Exact embedding vector index with cosine scoring and bounded top-result scan: The AI application needs a small retrieval path that can serve as a correctness oracle for any later approximate index.
- [library] OpenAI-compatible JSON request, SSE response reader, and bounded tool-call loop: A provider-neutral adapter needs streaming output, tool-call detection, a tool result turn, and a hard step bound.
- [library] Explicit F32 GPU placement and backend receipt: Accelerator use must report requested and selected devices, precision profile, capabilities, and fail closed when unavailable.
- [library] Same-size matmul timing harness for interpreter, native Jet, and NumPy/PyTorch when installed: Performance claims need the same dimensions, repetitions, result check, tier, and incumbent availability record.

cards.title: Battery and example: Embedded
cards.body:
A first-party embedded battery: a board description and target dossier, a typed MMIO register block, a bounded interrupt-to-task handoff, a DMA owned-buffer transfer, a UART ring, a deadline-checked control loop, a signed A/B slot policy with rollback, and a flash and debug receipt path; every part replays on the host. Interrupts, DMA, and registers depend on D-FOUND-BOARD1; the deadline loop on D-FOUND-REALTIME1; flashing on D-FOUND-COREAPI1; the thumbv7em toolchain admission (E3302) is a toolchain card.

Parts the probe named (docs/research/domain-foundations/probes/area-embedded.md, batteries.json):
- [library] board description and target dossier: Name the MCU, memory regions, linker expectations, peripheral bases, and host-replay substitution before any driver code.
- [library] typed MMIO register block: Exercise C layout, access widths, volatile reads/writes, and the explicit unsafe audit at one documented peripheral address.
- [needs core] bounded interrupt-to-task handoff: Show a short ISR queue, overflow policy, task drain, and the missing vector-table seam without pretending host replay is hardware.
- [needs core] DMA owned-buffer transfer: Show pinning, submit/completion transitions, buffer reuse rules, and the target mapping boundary.
- [library] UART bounded ring: Provide a fixed-capacity receive/transmit ring with explicit full and empty behavior for a serial driver.
- [needs core] deadline-checked control loop: Pair a deterministic control tick with a declared deadline, missed-deadline accounting, and a clear note that the estimate is not WCET proof.
- [library] signed slot policy and rollback: Exercise authenticated-image acceptance, trial confirmation, rejection, and rollback while separating policy code from flash persistence.
- [needs core] flash/debug receipt path: Build the image, flash a real board or emulator, capture programmer/debug output, and bind it to a reproducible release receipt.

The probe program under docs/research/domain-foundations/code/area-embedded/pkg/ is the starting point; its probe.md records what already works with exact commands.

cards.title: Forced interpreter stalls a spawned UDP responder task until the root DNS wait wakes it
cards.body: Observed on the strict three-tier conformance gate at 06534ce1c for `net/dns_aaaa_at` (same shape expected for `net/dns_txt_at` and the `net/dns_srv*` rows): AOT and default `jet run` print `true`; forced `--interpret` stops with `Stop [E3001]: panic: DNS AAAA`. Direct strace of the interpreter run shows the spawned responder task prints its first line immediately, then blocks on a futex until the root DNS thread wakes it about one second later; only then does `recvfrom(fd 3)` receive the query and send the response, after the client already gave up. The DNS bytes are correct on every tier (JitNet admitted the ListLit response in resident safety; the JIT leg passes). The defect is task/host synchronization in the interpreter ambient: a spawned task that blocks in a Core net receive does not run concurrently with the root task's Core wait, so request/response witnesses deadlock into their timeouts. Invariant: I9 - the interpreter must preserve the same scheduling meaning as the Prelude task runtime AOT and the JIT use; a spawned task blocked in a Core receive must make progress while the parent waits.
cards.plan:
Actual: on the strict three-tier conformance gate, `net/dns_aaaa_at` (and the same shape in `net/dns_txt_at` and `net/dns_srv*`) prints `true` on AOT and default `jet run` but stops with `Stop [E3001]: panic: DNS AAAA` on forced `--interpret`. strace shows the spawned responder task prints its first line, then blocks on a futex until the root DNS wait wakes it about one second later; only then does `recvfrom` get the query, after the client gave up. The DNS bytes are right on every tier; the defect is task and host synchronization in the interpreter: a spawned task blocked in a Core net receive does not run while the root task sits in a Core wait. Expected (I9): a spawned task blocked in a Core receive makes progress while the parent waits, with the same scheduling meaning the Prelude task runtime gives AOT and the JIT; the change is marshalling only.

Steps:
1. Reproduce: `JET_CORE_CONFORMANCE_FILTER=net/dns_aaaa_at JET_CORE_CONFORMANCE_CENSUS=1 JET_STORE_DIR=$HOME/.cache/jet-test-scratch/conf-store timeout 900 scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev_corpus_gate core_conformance_corpus_uses_strict_three_tier_gate -- --test-threads=2` and `timeout 60 scripts/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret tests/conformance/corpus/core/net/dns_aaaa_at.jet`.
2. Trace the interpreter task spawn path: crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs task arms (shared seam: one lane at a time, whole-function edits, crate CHECK OK after every edit) and the evaluator's task scheduler in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/ (find with `grep -rn "spawn" crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/*.rs`). Identify the lock the responder waits on while the root task is inside the DNS wait host (most likely the evaluator's single interpreter mutex held across a blocking Core call).
3. Fix: a blocking Core call from the interpreter releases the evaluator lock for its duration (or the spawned task runs on the shared Prelude task runtime thread, crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Scheduler.rs, exactly as AOT does), so no scheduling policy is re-encoded in the interpreter.
4. Regression: tests/run_interpret.rs case that spawns a task blocking in a Core UDP receive while the parent waits in a Core DNS or UDP call and asserts the exchange completes within the deadline under `--interpret`.
5. Census: the single-stem runs for net/dns_aaaa_at, net/dns_txt_at, net/dns_srv, net/dns_srv_port, net/dns_srv_priority, net/dns_srv_target, net/dns_srv_weight, then the full net domain filter.

Proof: the filtered census runs above are green with byte-identical stdout on AOT, default `jet run`, and `--interpret`; `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test run_interpret -- udp_responder_progresses_under_parent_wait` green; `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test task_control_tiers --test task_state_tiers` unchanged.

Writable paths: crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs (task arms only), crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/ (scheduler marshalling), tests/run_interpret.rs. Do not touch crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Scheduler.rs semantics, crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs, or crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs.

I9: the fix calls the shared Prelude runtime; no policy in the host.

Non-goals: no exclusions.tsv entry; no change to DNS behavior or timeouts.

cards.title: Sema defaults an uninferred binding to Int: `recovered :: list.sort_by(cmp) ?? fallback` types Unit as Int
cards.body:
Reproducer: tests/tir_core_and_closures.rs try_sort_by_is_atomic_and_tier_stable (added 2026-09-02 in a9941b416, never green). The binding `recovered :: items.sort_by((a, b) -> ...) ?? fallback` has a Unit-returning fallible subject. CheckerCore::check_binding (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/bindings.rs) falls back to Type::Int when initializer inference returns None ((None, None) => Int), while TIR lowering sees the subject as Result<Unit, Err>. Generated Rust then annotates the local as i64 and rustc rejects it (E0308), which is an I2 violation; on any shape where rustc accepts an Int default, the program would carry the wrong type silently.

A silent Int default for an uninferred binding is the defect, not the sort test: sema must either infer the fallback type from the subject's success type (Unit here) or report a typed diagnostic that names the binding; it must never invent Int.
cards.plan:
1. In CheckerCore::check_binding, remove the (None, None) => Int default; when the initializer's inferred type is None, resolve it through the same OrFallback inference used for value-carrying subjects (success type of the fallible subject; Unit for Unit-returning collection operations such as sort_by/try_sort_by).
2. If inference still yields None, emit the existing 'could not infer type' diagnostic (or register one per docs/spec/diagnostics.md) naming the binding, with a UI snapshot.
3. Prove: try_sort_by_is_atomic_and_tier_stable passes on all tiers; a UI fixture for a genuinely uninferable binding shows the diagnostic; no other tir_core_and_closures test changes.

criteria.text: CheckerCore::check_binding no longer defaults an uninferred binding to Int; a `?? fallback` over a Unit-returning fallible subject infers Unit.
criteria.evidence: bindings.rs (None,None) => Unknown, never Int; fallible.rs infer_or_fallback derives Result<Unit,E> from builtin_method_return Some(None) + lambda fallible_carrier (no method-name list). Commit e90023f37.

criteria.text: tests/tir_core_and_closures.rs try_sort_by_is_atomic_and_tier_stable passes (AOT, default jet run, --interpret byte-identical).
criteria.evidence: tir_core_and_closures try_sort_by_is_atomic_and_tier_stable: 1 passed (valid program: recovered flag, expected E_SORT:stop / [1, 2, 3]|[3, 2, 1] / 31 / [3, 1, 2] / true, byte-identical on all tiers). Commit e90023f37.

criteria.text: An uninferable binding reports a registered diagnostic with a UI snapshot instead of a silent Int type.

cards.title: AOT emits an empty typed list literal `[U8]{}` as Vec<i64>, so `bytes == [U8]{}` fails rustc (I2)
cards.body: Conformance witness conformance/core/crypto/expert/aes256gcm_open (strict three-tier gate, census at 8d246d4): the program type-checks and runs in dev, but the generated Rust fails to build: `error[E0277]: can't compare u8 with i64` at `jet_term_write_stdout_line(&((((__jet_result) == (Vec::<i64>::new()))).jet_display()), false)`. Minimal program (inside #Unsafe for the expert call): `result :: expert.aes256gcm_open(key, nonce, ciphertext, [U8]{}) ?? panic("open")` then `print(result == [U8]{})`. The typed empty list literal `[U8]{}` is emitted as `Vec::<i64>::new()` on the AOT path, ignoring the declared element type when the literal appears as an equality operand (and possibly elsewhere). rustc rejection of generated code is an internal compiler error by invariant I2.
cards.plan:
Actual: the conformance witness conformance/core/crypto/expert/aes256gcm_open type-checks and runs in dev, but the generated Rust fails rustc with `error[E0277]: can't compare u8 with i64` because the typed empty list literal `[U8]{}` is emitted as `Vec::<i64>::new()` when it appears as an equality operand (and possibly elsewhere). Minimal program inside #Unsafe: `result :: expert.aes256gcm_open(key, nonce, ciphertext, [U8]{}) ?? panic("open")` then `print(result == [U8]{})`. A rustc rejection of generated code is an ICE by I2. Expected: an empty typed list literal keeps its declared element type in generated Rust in every expression position (binding, argument, comparison, return); the strict witness passes; a fixture compares `[U8]{}`, `[Float]{}`, and `[Text]{}` against computed lists on every tier.

Steps:
1. Reproduce: write the minimal program under ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/, run `scripts/agent/jet-env jet emit --rust` and read the `Vec::<i64>::new()` site; then `JET_CORE_CONFORMANCE_FILTER=crypto/expert/aes256gcm_open JET_CORE_CONFORMANCE_CENSUS=1 scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev_corpus_gate core_conformance_corpus_uses_strict_three_tier_gate -- --test-threads=2`.
2. Find the lowering of `[T]{}` in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/expressions.rs (list literal arm) and the emit of the empty list in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/emit/expressions.rs; the empty literal falls back to `Int` when its element type is not carried on the TExpr, so the sema type fact must be attached at lowering and read at emit for every position; no operand-position special case.
3. Fixture: tests/tir_core_and_closures.rs `typed_empty_list_equality_matches_all_tiers` comparing `[U8]{}`, `[Float]{}`, and `[Text]{}` with computed empty lists in a binding, an argument, a comparison, and a return, printing byte-identical output on AOT, default `jet run`, and `--interpret`.

Proof: the filtered census run is green; `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test tir_core_and_closures -- typed_empty_list` green; `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden` unchanged.

Writable paths: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/expressions.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/emit/expressions.rs, tests/tir_core_and_closures.rs and its fixtures. Do not touch crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs, crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs, or crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs.

I9: the fixture proves identical output on all three tiers.

Non-goals: no change to list literal syntax or to the crypto expert API.

cards.title: AOT cannot lower an escaping closure that mutates its captured copy (Box<dyn FnMut> vs Rc<dyn Fn>); tiers disagree when it is stored in a list
cards.body:
Found while guarding #2837. S47: an escaping closure owns copies of its captures and may mutate them. Two shapes fail today.

1. Returned mutating closure: `fn make() fn() Int -> { count := 0; next :: () Int -> { count += 1; count }; next }` then `f :: make(); print(f.call()); print(f.call())`. AOT generated Rust fails rustc E0308: `return Ok(__jet_step)` expected `Rc<dyn Fn() -> i64>`, found `Box<dyn FnMut() -> i64>`. The Jet fn type has no FnMut spelling, so the AOT function-value ABI cannot carry a mutating escaping closure. Expected on every tier: `1` then `2`.

2. Mutating closure stored in a list: `count := 0; step :: () Int -> { count += 1; count }; items :: [step]; print(items[0].call()); print(count)`. AOT: rustc E0308 (Box<dyn FnMut> into Vec<Rc<dyn Fn>>); when coerced, AOT prints `0/5`-class values while default jet run and --interpret print `0/0`: the tiers disagree on whether the escaping copy is mutated through the stored value.

The function-value ABI needs one representation that admits interior mutation of an escaping closure's owned captures (for example Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut>> or an owned-state closure object), applied on every tier with one meaning.

## Goal
Close the last open criterion, criterion 3, for the mutating-closure fn-value ABI. Criteria 1-2 are met: returned and list-stored mutating closures compile on AOT and agree on every tier. What remains is the reentrant shape and the proof that closure-heavy workloads did not regress.

## Current state
- The title defect is fixed. Regression tests exist at `tests/tir_core_and_closures.rs:1152` (`card_2845_returned_mutating_closure_tier_parity`, which expects `1`, `2`) and `:1173` (`card_2845_stored_mutating_closure_tier_parity`, which expects `1`, `0`).
- The shipped emitter keeps the FnMut detail behind the fn-value carrier (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Context.rs:3758-3767`).
- Reentrant shape: the exact program was recorded on the card on 2026-09-10, which the criterion permits in place of a pass. Current law rejects it with E0211: `Signal<[fn(Int) Int -[..E]>]>` cannot be copied by `~`, because its element is a non-duplicable fn value. That recording already satisfies the "or the exact program is recorded" branch, so the copy law is not reopened.
- Performance is not proven. Wordfreq has one valid AOT row (run 20260915-1216094-mu2i9ltk, 0.533 s) with no comparable earlier baseline. An earlier run stopped at E1220 (root `run::run` reached `Time.Wait` outside the package budget). Datasummary was never run.

## Changes
1. Keep the reentrant program as a UI fixture: `tests/ui/E0211_reentrant_fn_signal_copy.jet` with its `.stderr`. It pins the ratified E0211 verdict that criterion 3 records. Do not change the ABI.
2. Run a paired, same-run comparison for the non-regression evidence:
   - build `jet` at the parent of the carrier change and at HEAD;
   - run `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry wordfreq --jet-bin <old>`, then the same with `--jet-bin <new>`;
   - do the same for `--entry datasummary`.

   If wordfreq still fails with E1220, record that on the card as an entry defect with its receipt. Do not change the entry's budget as part of this card.
3. Attach both paired rows (run ids, binary digests, medians) to the card log.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test tir_core_and_closures -- card_2845`: passes.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/E0211_reentrant_fn_signal_copy Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`: passes.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=functions/ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` and `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=basics/closures ...`: no drift.
- Paired gauntlet rows: new/old AOT median ≤ 1.05 for both wordfreq and datasummary.

## Batch
batch-measure: the code is landed. What remains is evidence and a fixture.

## Dependencies
None. `basics/closures` also depends on #3730 (sort_by) to match its golden.

Recording the exact reentrant candidate before any further function-value ABI change, as criterion 3 permits. The existing run rejects line 5 with E0211: Signal<[fn(Int) Int -[..E]>]> cannot be copied by ~ because its element is a non-duplicable function value. This does not prove reentrant execution or justify changing the ratified copy law. Receipt: ~/.cache/jet-luna/astra-recovered-1788940743903-tenth-reentrant-default.json. Returned/stored closure criteria remain met; closure-heavy golden and wordfreq/datasummary performance evidence remains open.

Exact program:
```jet
use core.reactive as reactive

fn run() {
    callbacks := reactive.signal([fn(Int) Int -[..E]>]{})
    again :: ~callbacks
    count := 0
    step :: (depth: Int) Int -> {
        count += 1
        if depth > 0 -> again.get()[0].call(depth - 1)
        count
    }
    callbacks.set([step])
    print(callbacks.get()[0].call(2))
    print(count)
}
```

Focused read-only acceptance investigation confirms the recorded true shared-handle reentry witness is still blocked by E0211 at `again :: ~callbacks`; Signal<List<Fn>> cloneability recursively rejects Fn. Beyond admission, current native fn carrier takes its FnMut box out of an Rc<RefCell<Option<_>>> during invocation, so same-handle recursion would encounter an empty slot; Signal runtime also requires Send+Sync payloads while local Fn is Rc-backed. No reentry/parity success is claimed. Returned/stored closure proofs remain met; criterion3 remains open. Exact source and receipt: ~/.cache/jet-luna/astra-recovered-1788940743903-reentrant-shared-capture.jet and -native-data-reentrant.json; source map from agent://ReentryAcceptance.

Reentrant witness recorded before further #2845 changes: `fn noop() Int -> 0; items := [noop]; step :: () Int -> { items[0].call(); 1 }; items = [step]; print(items[0].call())`. It prints `1` rather than recursing because S47 captures an owned copy of `items` before the outer reassignment, so the closure cannot reach its own later-installed handle through that list. A true same-handle re-entry is not expressible through this shape; the internal carrier nevertheless drops its RefCell borrow before user code and reports `function value is already executing` if an alias reaches it.

Prep: plan replaced; the carrier is fixed as an internal ABI choice (one owned-state carrier with a mutable call handle for every fn value, no new spelling, no owner gate); reentrancy and performance guard added as a criterion.

cards.title: Conformance witnesses append to the checkout's tracked .jet/secrets-audit during the strict gate
cards.body: Running `cargo test --test dev_corpus_gate core_conformance_corpus_uses_strict_three_tier_gate` (any filter that reaches the sys/secrets witnesses) appends lines such as `read output=__core_conformance_missing_2286 from=[]` to the tracked file `.jet/secrets-audit` at the repository root, dirtying the working tree (observed 2026-09-03 in both the main checkout and the frozen red-team worktree; the red-team replay requires a clean checkout, so the census had to restore the file after every chunk). Tests never write scratch inside the repository (AGENTS.md); the secrets audit sink for a witness must resolve under the test scratch directory (JET_TEST_SCRATCH_DIR / the witness's project root), not the process cwd.
cards.plan:
Actual: the strict conformance gate (any filter that reaches the sys/secrets witnesses) appends lines such as `read output=__core_conformance_missing_2286 from=[]` to the tracked file `.jet/secrets-audit` at the repository root, dirtying the tree. The writer is `secret_read_audit_path` in crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Prelude/SecretsCrypto.rs:278-288, called from `append_secret_read_audit`; when it resolves against the process cwd the witness writes into the checkout. Expected: the audit sink resolves under the test scratch root (JET_TEST_SCRATCH_DIR, then JET_STORE_DIR, then the platform temp dir), never the cwd; the gate leaves `.jet/secrets-audit` untouched; a regression test guards the location.

Steps:
1. Reproduce on the current tree: `git status --porcelain .jet/secrets-audit` clean, then `JET_CORE_CONFORMANCE_FILTER=sys/secrets JET_CORE_CONFORMANCE_CENSUS=1 scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev_corpus_gate core_conformance_corpus_uses_strict_three_tier_gate -- --test-threads=2`, then the same `git status` line. If the file is already clean, the path rule at SecretsCrypto.rs:278-288 has landed; go to step 3.
2. Make `secret_read_audit_path` derive from JET_TEST_SCRATCH_DIR, JET_STORE_DIR, or the platform temp dir in that order and never from the cwd; the AOT, JIT, and interpreter paths all call this one function (it lives in the Prelude part, so every tier shares it).
3. Regression: a test in tests/dev_corpus_gate.rs or tests/build_sandbox.rs runs the secrets witness with cwd set to the repo root and JET_TEST_SCRATCH_DIR set, and asserts `.jet/secrets-audit` is byte-identical before and after (read the file, do not shell out to git) and that the scratch audit file gained one line.
4. Confirm the gate's own harness exports JET_TEST_SCRATCH_DIR for every witness process (tests/dev_parts/support.rs); if it does not, set it there so the rule holds without per-test setup.

Proof: `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev_corpus_gate -- secrets_audit_sink` green; the sys-domain census run leaves `git status --porcelain .jet/secrets-audit` empty.

Writable paths: crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Prelude/SecretsCrypto.rs, tests/dev_corpus_gate.rs (or tests/build_sandbox.rs), tests/dev_parts/support.rs. Do not touch the secrets API, crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs, crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs, or crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs.

I9: the sink rule is one Prelude function shared by every tier; the witness output is unchanged on AOT, default `jet run`, and `--interpret`.

Non-goals: no change to what the audit line records; no change to the tracked `.jet/secrets-audit` content.

cards.title: AOT emit: fallible-carrier projection ICEs (map lambda try_map, explicit Ok in if arms) block bulkrename, tzreport, taskfile-cli
cards.body:
Three corpus entries fail 'jet build' with the I2 banner (exit 101) on gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl (full matrix, release compiler, gauntlet/results/2026-09-03.json). Compiling the generated Rust by hand shows two emitter defects.

(a) A '.map(x -> { ... ?? panic(...) ... })' lambda is lowered as fallible: the emitter calls 'jet_list_try_map' and binds its 'Result<Vec<_>, _>' to a plain 'Vec<_>' (rustc E0308 at the let). Shapes: gauntlet/entries/bulkrename/jet/run.jet:13-16 ('e.filter(...).map((x: DirEntry) -> { m :: re.match(~q, x.name) ?? panic("bad photo") ... })') and gauntlet/entries/tzreport/jet/run.jet:31-34 ('.lines().filter(...).map(line -> { fields :: line.split_once("|") ?? panic("bad") ... })'). After '?? panic' the body is infallible, so either the lambda must be classified infallible or the try_map result must be projected with one Try.

(b) An arrow-bodied fallible function whose 'if' arms return explicit 'Ok(...)' is wrapped twice: gauntlet/entries/taskfile-cli/jet/run.jet:6 ('fn load() [Task] !(IOError | [FieldError]) -> if files.exists(...) -> Ok(json.decode<Store>(...).tasks) else -> Ok([])') emits '{ Ok(...) } else { Ok(...) }' where 'Vec<__jet_Task>' is expected (two rustc E0308).

The banner hides the rustc text (#2783); reproduce with 'rustc --edition=2021 --crate-type bin build/run.rs' on the preserved file. The run tier of taskfile-cli executes correctly, so this is AOT-emit only (I9 drift). Three matrix cells (files.script, time.script, time.notebook, cli.app, formats.json-app) stay unmeasured until this lands.
cards.plan:
## Outcome

Fix the generic AOT fallibility/carrier projection seam so handled map-lambda failures select the infallible map route, genuinely fallible map results receive exactly one Try at their binding, and explicit Ok values in arrow-bodied fallible if arms are not wrapped twice. Preserve one meaning across AOT, default run, and interpreter tiers.

## Work

1. Retain the historical corpus evidence for bulkrename, tzreport, and taskfile-cli, but reproduce the three shapes in tests/tir_core_and_closures.rs with small non-corpus sources and inspect generated Rust plus the hidden rustc error when needed.
2. Trace lambda fallibility through crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/lambdas.rs and lower/expressions.rs; trace collection route selection in Codegen/TIR/routes.rs (the live map/try_map symbols are there). A body whose failures are consumed by ?? panic must be infallible; a real fallible callback must use one try_map projection at its binding.
3. Trace expression-bodied function/if carrier handling through lower/functions.rs, lower/expressions.rs, and lower/statements.rs, then the final Rust rendering in crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIRRust.rs. Normalize carrier-typed values by type/fact, not by a per-entry or lexical Ok special case; emit no second Result wrapper.
4. Add the three witnesses to tests/tir_core_and_closures.rs and assert AOT, default jet run, and --interpret produce identical output. Keep gauntlet/entries/bulkrename, tzreport, and taskfile-cli unchanged; the fix is general.
5. Re-run the three named gauntlet entries and the focused closure/golden proof after the implementation. Keep the #2783 banner concern on its own card.

## Dependencies

No board blocker is recorded. Existing refs #2783, #2763, and #2771 are historical/related context, not new owner choices. Do not touch JIT, ambient interpreter, or sema Core-call policy; any new syntax or invariant choice still follows the ratified owner-gate law.

## Proof

Focused closure tests must show the handled and genuinely fallible map witnesses and Ok-arm witness compile natively and match default run/interpreter byte for byte. The three gauntlet entries must report AOT ok with expected output, and existing failure-carrier goldens must remain unchanged.

## Scope

One generic fallibility/carrier projection fix only; no per-entry or per-method special case, no failure-carrier contract change, and no JIT-side work.

cards.title: Default evaluator E0956: 'sort_by receiver' is not supported (bulkrename, tzreport run and dev tiers)
cards.body:
On gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl (full matrix, release compiler, gauntlet/results/2026-09-03.json) the run and dev tiers of bulkrename and tzreport exit 1 with:

  Error [E0956]: `sort_by receiver` isn't supported by the current evaluator yet
    --> run.jet:17:7  (p.sort_by((x: String) -> x))

tzreport hits the same arm on 'meetings.sort_by(.a)' (selector path). AOT lowers both, so the interpreter ambient lacks the route (I9). Cells files.script, time.script and time.notebook cannot measure their required run tier until this lands.
cards.plan:
Actual: on default `jet run` and `jet dev`, gauntlet/entries/bulkrename/jet/run.jet:17 (`p.sort_by((x: String) -> x)`) and tzreport (`meetings.sort_by(.a)`) stop with `Error [E0956]: `sort_by receiver` isn't supported by the current evaluator yet`. The evaluator has sort_by arms (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/closure_ops.rs:805, :832, :875) that accept only `CtValue::List`; the receiver in both entries is not a list value at that point (an iterator view from `.filter(...).map(...)` in bulkrename, and the selector path form in tzreport). AOT lowers both, so the interpreter drifts (I9). Expected: `list.sort_by(x -> key)` and `list.sort_by(.field)` evaluate under `--interpret` with output identical to AOT for a materialized list and for an iterator view receiver.

Steps:
1. Reproduce: `scripts/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret gauntlet/entries/bulkrename/jet/run.jet` and tzreport with their harness inputs (gauntlet/entries/<name>/spec.json names them); print the receiver's CtValue variant at the failing arm once to confirm the kind (remove the print after).
2. Fix the mechanism in closure_ops.rs: a sort_by receiver that is an iterator view is materialized through the same route AOT uses (the Prelude `to_list` semantics for a view, D-ITERTOOLS1 = A: the view is consumed), then sorted; a selector path `.a` resolves through the existing selector-to-callable route the evaluator uses for `map(.a)` (find it with `grep -n "Selector" closure_ops.rs`). Do not add a policy; call the same Prelude sort symbol AOT uses for the comparator.
3. Conformance rows: add tests/conformance/corpus/core/data/ rows `sort_by_view.jet` (filter then map then sort_by with a lambda) and `sort_by_selector.jet` (sort_by(.field) on a list of structs), each with the `// core-conformance: core.data.sort_by` header, so the strict three-tier gate runs them.
4. Harness: `node gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry bulkrename` and `--entry tzreport` report `jet_tiers.run` and `jet_tiers.dev` status ok.

Proof: `JET_CORE_CONFORMANCE_FILTER=data/sort_by JET_CORE_CONFORMANCE_CENSUS=1 scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev_corpus_gate core_conformance_corpus_uses_strict_three_tier_gate -- --test-threads=2` green; the two `--entry` runs report run and dev ok with byte-exact output.

Writable paths: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/eval/closure_ops.rs (and eval/exprs.rs if the selector route lives there), tests/conformance/corpus/core/data/. Do not touch gauntlet/entries/ sources, crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs (unless the receiver kind is produced there; then coordinate, one lane at a time), crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs, or crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs.

I9: the new corpus rows run on AOT, default `jet run`, and `--interpret` with byte-identical stdout.

Non-goals: no `jit_gaps` or exclusions.tsv entry; no change to sort semantics or comparator error text.

cards.title: JIT whole-program deopt on five corpus shapes sends sieve, wordfreq, datasummary, csvtransform, concurrency-service to the interpreter
cards.body:
With JET_TRACE_TIERS_PATH on the release compiler (gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl (full matrix, release compiler, gauntlet/results/2026-09-03.json) binaries) the default 'jet run' tier plan fails 'entry_native,deopt_ok,deopt_empty' and runs the whole program in the interpreter for:

- sieve: 'Let prime init=BuiltinMethod:IterToList ty=List(U8)' ('[U8]{...}.cycle(slots).to_list()')
- wordfreq: 'BuiltinMethod:Clear' (map/list '.clear()' inside the loop)
- datasummary: 'ForIn collection=ClosureMethod:GroupBy ty=Map{String,[Measurement]}'
- csvtransform: 'Let total init=ClosureMethod:Fold ty=Decimal'
- concurrency-service: 'TaskGroup[0]>Loop[11]'

Consequence: those run tiers time out at the harness's 180 s (sieve n=10,000,000 interpreted; AOT finishes in 5.7 ms and beats Rust 7.7 ms, C 10.4 ms, Zig 9.8 ms), so four cells that WIN on AOT stay unmeasured or lose on the run tier. Every other corpus entry lowers natively.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Default `jet run` executes five gauntlet workloads natively instead of deopting the whole program into the interpreter, where they time out at 180 s. On AOT, sieve takes 5.7 ms (Rust 7.7 ms, C 10.4 ms, Zig 9.8 ms), so four cells that win on AOT lose or go unmeasured on the run tier. Speed work is #2863, not this card.

**Measured baseline** (gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl, `JET_TRACE_TIERS_PATH`)
First unlowerable row per workload:
- sieve: `Let prime init=BuiltinMethod:IterToList ty=List(U8)`
- wordfreq: `BuiltinMethod:Clear`
- datasummary: `ForIn collection=ClosureMethod:GroupBy ty=Map{String,[Measurement]}`
- csvtransform: `Let total init=ClosureMethod:Fold ty=Decimal`
- concurrency-service: `TaskGroup[0]>Loop[11]`

**Current state**
- Whole-program deopt is traced at `crates/jet-jit/src/jit/tiers.rs:37,73-84`. The lowering seam is `crates/jet-jit/src/jit/functions_compile.rs`; there is no `lower_ctx.rs`. The harness fails closed on deopt (`Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs:2886-2898`). `Tools/gauntlet/harness/tier-trace.test.mjs:84` already lists the five entries, and :137-151 asserts no deopt.
- Per the card log (2026-09-16/20/21):
  - sieve IterToList and wordfreq Clear have native no-deopt scratch receipts.
  - csvtransform's Decimal Fold route and host exist, but there is no workload receipt.
  - datasummary stops before the JIT on front-end errors E2404/E0915/E0109/E1220.
  - concurrency-service stops on invalid function metadata (its duplicate-MIR-ID blocker #3443 is done).
- These front-end errors now come from the self-hosted `Compiler/JetSema` / `Compiler/JetCodegen` MIR, which `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet:837-839,1794` hands to the host JIT.

**Changes**
1. Re-run the tier trace for all five on the current rebuilt tree, and record the first unlowerable row or front-end error for each.
2. Jet compiler first:
   - Fix the datasummary front-end errors (a GroupBy closure over `Map{String,[Measurement]}`) in `Compiler/JetSema`.
   - Fix the concurrency-service function-metadata error in `Compiler/JetCodegen` MIR emission.
   - If either needs more than a local fix, file it on its own jetc card and add it as a blocker here.
3. `functions_compile.rs`: add or finish only the arms still missing after step 1: typed `IterToList`, map/list `Clear`, closure `GroupBy`, Decimal `Fold`, and task-group loop bodies. Marshal through existing Prelude symbols and scheduler/collection seams. Keep `crates/jet-jit/src/{Collections.rs,Concurrency.rs,host_seam.rs}` marshalling-only. Do not touch `ambient_interp.rs`, tier policy or gauntlet sources. Preserve D-ASYNCRT1=A and one meaning across AOT, `jet run`, `jet dev` and `--interpret`.

**Proof**
- `node --test Tools/gauntlet/harness/tier-trace.test.mjs` → green (criteria 1-2).
- `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry <each of the five>` → the run tier completes with byte-exact output and a measured `runtime_wall_seconds` (criterion 3).

**Batch**
batch-host-runtime: JIT lowering plus tier parity. Any Jet front-end fix found in step 2 rides the same compiler rebuild.

**Dependencies**
None open. #3443 is done.

cards.title: JIT-native code is 10-320x slower than AOT: scalar and byte loops call Prelude hosts per element with boxed values
cards.body:
Entries that DO lower natively still lose the run tier by 30-1000x on gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl (full matrix, release compiler, gauntlet/results/2026-09-03.json), while their AOT tier is near the peers:

- embedded-data: run 4.95 s vs AOT 0.113 s (44x); Rust 4.7 ms (1051x); peak RSS 585 MB for a 12 MB input (boxed per-byte values)
- nbody: run 402x C / 475x Rust; AOT 1.25x C
- binparse: run 94x Rust; AOT 1.29x Rust
- embedded-sensor-ring: run 84x Rust; AOT 4.6x
- logreport: run 43x Rust; AOT 4.0x

The tier trace shows native rows and no deopt, so the generated Cranelift code itself calls Prelude hosts for Int arithmetic, list indexing, Reader.take_pattern and byte iteration instead of emitting typed inline operations. Node beats Jet on every one of these cells at the run tier; the owner tier law requires the default tier to beat CPython and Node.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
JIT-native code on default `jet run` emits typed inline operations instead of calling Prelude hosts per element with boxed values. Targets: within 3x of AOT on five entries, embedded-data RSS below 64 MB, and beating CPython/Node on every measured run-tier cell. The tier law requires the default tier to beat CPython and Node.

**Measured baseline** (gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl, release compiler; native rows, no deopt)
| Entry | Run tier | AOT tier |
|---|---|---|
| embedded-data | 4.95 s vs AOT 0.113 s (44x); 1051x Rust 4.7 ms; peak RSS 585 MB for a 12 MB input | 0.113 s |
| nbody | 402x C / 475x Rust | 1.25x C |
| binparse | 94x Rust | 1.29x Rust |
| embedded-sensor-ring | 84x Rust | 4.6x |
| logreport | 43x Rust | 4.0x |

Node beats Jet on every one of these run-tier cells.

**Current state**
- The seam is `crates/jet-jit/src/jit/functions_compile.rs` (MIR→Cranelift, retained host per `Docs/spec/architecture.md:134`). Both Cranelift consumers now use `opt_level=speed` (`runtime_host.rs:14841`, `api_debug.rs:95`; see #2907).
- Partial repairs have landed: typed checked `List<Int>`/byte indexing (00b8f6aba typed index getter) and inline exact-Int loop scalars. No corpus measurement exists since then.
- The promoting host on overflow is `jet_int_add/sub/mul` (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/CommonTypes.rs:4317-4340`).
- The MIR producer is the self-hosted `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Expressions.jet`. The old matcher route citations (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/*`) are archived and now map to Compiler/JetCodegen MIR facts.

**Changes** (one lane per worker brief, whole-function edits, crate CHECK OK after each)
1. Baseline: run `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry <name>` for the five entries, and record run and AOT wall time plus RSS on the card.
2. Scalars: when both MIR operand types are `Int`, emit `iadd`/`isub`/`imul` with an overflow check and a cold call to `jet_int_*` only on overflow. `Float` emits `fadd`/`fsub`/`fmul`/`fdiv`/`sqrt`, and comparisons emit `icmp`/`fcmp`. `Int`/`Float` locals stay unboxed in Cranelift variables for the life of the loop and are boxed only at host boundaries.
3. Collections: indexed reads/writes on `List<U8>`/`List<Int>` do a bounds check plus a direct load/store on the host buffer (pointer and length exposed through `crates/jet-jit/src/Collections.rs` marshalling, no policy). `loop byte in data` iterates the buffer directly with inline widening. `Reader.take_pattern` with fixed-width holes calls the shared Prelude matcher once per frame, following the self-hosted MIR's matcher facts.
4. Jet compiler: if the MIR lacks the static type facts step 2 needs (for example, the operand kind on arithmetic ops), add them in `Compiler/JetCodegen` rather than re-deriving them in the host.
5. Re-measure after each step. Stop when all five are ≤3x AOT and embedded-data RSS is below 64 MB. Then check the peer criteria (3, 5).

**Proof**
- `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry embedded-data` (and nbody, binparse, embedded-sensor-ring, logreport) → run tier `runtime_wall_seconds` ≤ 3× AOT, RSS < 64 MB for embedded-data, and Jet/CPython and Jet/Node < 1.00. Losses stay on the card.
- `JET_THREE_WAY_STEM=<touched example> Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev cranelift_three_way_differential_battery` for each touched shape → byte-identical output across tiers (criterion 4).

**Batch**
batch-host-runtime: JIT codegen and tier performance.

**Dependencies**
None. #2862 (whole-program deopt) is separate; this card covers entries that already lower natively.

cards.title: Interpreter: list element assignment is O(n), so any deopted loop goes quadratic (sieve 10k = 1.1 s, 30k = 18.9 s)
cards.body: Running gauntlet/entries/sieve/jet/run.jet under the interpreter (whole-program deopt, release compiler) takes 96 ms at n=1,000, 1.13 s at n=10,000 and 18.9 s at n=30,000: roughly 9x time for 3x input. The hot statement is 'prime[m] = 0' inside 'loop m in p*p/%2..<slots, p'. AOT runs n=10,000,000 in 5.7 ms. The interpreter has no performance bar under the tier law, but a quadratic element store turns every deopted program into a timeout and makes the REPL unusable on ordinary loops.
cards.plan:
## Authority and scope

No board dependency is recorded. The defect is in the interpreter’s indexed place-write path; preserve D-MEM1 shared-view copy semantics and make no change to AOT/JIT lowering or deoptimization policy. The existing sieve fixture is the workload oracle; do not replace it with a smaller lookalike.

## Owned paths

- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIREval.rs` (write-place and indexed list/map mutation)
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/tir_to_mir_stmt.rs` and `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/routes.rs` (existing write/lowering route)
- `tests/run_interpret.rs` (scaling witness)
- `tests/dev_interp_parity.rs` and `tests/tir_core_and_closures.rs` (observable parity and nested-place coverage)

The `gauntlet/entries/sieve/jet/run.jet` source and its recorded timings are the reproduction oracle, not an implementation target. Do not touch `crates/jet-jit` or the AOT path.

## Ordered implementation and cutover

1. Reproduce the recorded n=10,000 and n=30,000 interpreter behavior from the exact sieve source when implementation begins; retain the existing timing observations as historical evidence for this preparation.
2. Trace `write_place_path`/`replace_runtime_steps` and the indexed assignment at `MIREval.rs:18046-18155`. When a list or map is uniquely owned by the evaluator slot, mutate its storage in place rather than cloning/rebuilding the whole `RuntimeValue::Data` for each element write.
3. Preserve copy-on-write for shared views, aliases, closures, and nested parent paths: clone only when ownership is shared, then rebuild the enclosing path exactly once as required by the existing value model. Apply the same ownership rule to map element assignment.
4. Cut every interpreter indexed-place caller over to the single helper and remove the obsolete per-store full-copy branch only after unique and shared cases have parity. Keep TIR/MIR route shape, deopt rules, AOT, and JIT unchanged.
5. Add the scaling witness and focused list/map/shared-view parity cases, then review the implementation against D-MEM1 and the existing interpreter output contract.

## Acceptance and proof

After implementation, run the exact sieve under `--interpret` at n=10,000 and n=100,000 and require the second wall time to remain under 10x the first. Exercise uniquely owned list and map writes, shared-view writes, nested paths, and existing parity fixtures; outputs must be unchanged and shared values must retain the documented copy rule. This preparation claims no timing or test run.

## Dependencies and non-goals

No dependency or owner ballot is open. Do not add an interpreter-only semantic, change list/map observable values, weaken shared-view isolation, or optimize unrelated loops.

cards.title: core Decimal parse, add, and format are 6-52x behind peers (csvtransform)
cards.body: csvtransform (formats.csv-cli) sums and formats Decimal money values per CSV row. AOT on gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl (full matrix, release compiler, gauntlet/results/2026-09-03.json): Jet 518 ms vs Rust 83 ms (6.3x), Go 37 ms (14x), Zig 9.9 ms (52x), Python 256 ms (2.0x), Node 208 ms (2.5x). The generated loop calls jet_decimal_from_str, jet_decimal_add and jet_decimal_to_string per row; the peers use fixed-scale integer or f64 arithmetic. The run tier additionally deopts on the Decimal fold (separate card).
cards.plan:
## Goal
Close the csvtransform Decimal loss by running the parse, add, sub, compare and format hot operations on JetDecimal's existing fixed-scale `Small(i128)` representation. Today every call goes through string round-trips. Results, rounding and error text must stay byte-identical on every tier.

## Current state
- Measured (gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl, AOT): Jet 518 ms vs Rust 83 ms (6.3x), Go 37 ms, Zig 9.9 ms, Python 256 ms, Node 208 ms. The loop calls `jet_decimal_from_str`, `jet_decimal_add` and `jet_decimal_to_string` once per row.
- The representation already exists: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/CommonTypes.rs:5383` `enum JetDecimalMagnitude { Small(i128), Big(JetBigInt) }`. JetDecimal (:5563) has native `from_str` (:5592), `add` (:5861) and `to_string_rep` (:6186).
- The hot entry points ignore that representation. `Top/MathRandomTime.rs` has `jet_decimal_from_str` :1340, `jet_decimal_add` :1604, `jet_decimal_sub` :1611, `jet_decimal_compare` :1630 and `jet_decimal_to_string` :1640. Each converts through `jet_std_decimal_to_exact` / `jet_std_decimal_from_exact` (CommonTypes.rs:5325-5335), which is `to_string_rep` → `CtDecimal::from_str` → precise op → `to_string_rep` → `JetDecimal::from_str`. That is several parses and formats per operation.
- A witness exists (`tests/decimal_perf_witness.jet`: 1e6 × `Decimal("12.34")` summed). The tier test `tests/decimal_fast_path.rs:34` `decimal_small_and_big_paths_keep_exact_tier_behavior` is registered in `tests/suites.txt:117`.

## Changes
1. `MathRandomTime.rs`: route `jet_decimal_from_str`, `add`, `sub`, `compare`, `eq` and `to_string` straight to the JetDecimal methods. Delete the `to_exact`/`from_exact` string round-trip on these paths. Keep the error text of the failed-parse branch unchanged.
2. `CommonTypes.rs` JetDecimal: make `add`/`sub` on `Small` operands align scales by a power-of-ten `i128` multiply with checked overflow. They promote to `Big` only on overflow or past 38 digits. `compare`/`eq`/hash must agree with the Big path, and the D-DECIMAL1 rounding rules stay unchanged.
3. Add a property test in the Prelude unit tests: random fast-path and general-path inputs must give identical `to_string_rep`, ordering and rounding.
4. The JIT (`crates/jet-jit/src/Numeric.rs`) only marshals and gets no second implementation. The run-tier Decimal fold deopt stays with #2862.
5. No Jet compiler change: the emitter already calls these Prelude symbols.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test decimal_fast_path` passes, with AOT, default run and `--interpret` byte-identical.
- Time `tests/decimal_perf_witness.jet` as an AOT build before and after. It must be ≥5x faster with identical output.
- `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry csvtransform`: the AOT row shows Jet/Rust ≤ 1.05 and Jet/{Go,Zig,Python,Node} < 1.00.

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime`: Prelude numeric runtime and tier parity.

## Dependencies
None blocking. #2862 owns the run-tier deopt.

cards.title: Web target first result is 3.1-3.6x behind hand-written JS and Rust wasm (web-app, web-widget)
cards.body: On gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl (full matrix, release compiler, gauntlet/results/2026-09-03.json) the web entries measure first_result_s: web-app Jet 70 ms vs JS 23 ms / Node 21 ms (3.3x, 3.1x); web-widget Jet 77 ms vs JS 22 ms / Rust wasm 23 ms / Node 22 ms (3.4-3.6x). artifact_bytes was not captured for any rail (harness prints '-'), so size is unmeasured. Cells webfront.app and webfront.widget lose to every peer.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Make Jet's web target win time-to-first-result and artifact size on the web-app and web-widget gauntlet entries. The target is Jet/JS < 1.00, Jet/Node < 1.00 and Jet/Rust <= 1.05 on first_result_s, and a Jet wasm no larger than the Rust wasm.

## Evidence
Gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl measured web-app at Jet 70 ms against JS 23 ms and Node 21 ms (3.3x, 3.1x), and web-widget at Jet 77 ms against JS 22 ms, Rust wasm 23 ms and Node 22 ms (3.4-3.6x). Cells webfront.app and webfront.widget lose to every peer.

## Current state
- Harness capture is done: `Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs:1631-1633,2352-2370` reports artifact_bytes/wasm_bytes per web rail.
- Streaming instantiate is done: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/DomRuntime.js:2475-2508` uses instantiateStreaming when the content-type is application/wasm.
- Remaining startup cost: the module preamble in `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Web/JavaScript.jet:246-293` builds every import object eagerly and awaits `jetDom.instantiateWasm` (`:263`) before any DOM work. It always includes testing-history imports and bind (`:257-258,277`), and optional font, data, model and game bootstraps (`:279-293`) run synchronously before the first paint.
- The rest of the emitter is in `Emit/Web/Prelude.jet` and `Program.jet`.

## Changes
1. Attribute first. Run `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry web-app` and `--entry web-widget` with the browser trace (`crates/jet-devserver/src/BrowserTrace.rs`). Split first_result into wasm fetch+instantiate, bridge bootstrap, runtime init and first paint, and record the four numbers on the card.
2. `Emit/Web/JavaScript.jet`:
   - emit import groups only for capabilities the program reaches (testing history only under test harnesses);
   - defer game devtools fetch, font binding and data type registration until after the first DOM write;
   - start the wasm fetch at module top so it overlaps bridge setup.
3. `Emit/Web/Prelude.jet`: include only reached prelude pieces (dead-prelude elimination), which shrinks the wasm and glue.
4. Check that `crates/jet-devserver/src/WebHost.rs` serves application/wasm for built artifacts.
5. A wasm-opt-class external tool is a new dependency and needs a ballot first. It is out of scope here.
6. Add a Jet <= Rust wasm size assertion to the harness report. Do not touch entry sources.

## Proof
- `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry web-app` and `--entry web-widget`, on one matched run, report first_result_s Jet/JS < 1.00, Jet/Node < 1.00 and Jet/Rust <= 1.05. artifact_bytes is present for every rail, with Jet wasm <= Rust wasm.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=web/ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` and `cargo test --test web_browser` stay green (I9: DOM and output unchanged).

## Batch
batch-jetc-back: the changes are in the self-hosted web emitter. The measurement follows the same build.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: Process pipeline (procpipe) is 30 ms behind Rust and Go: spawn and pipe plumbing overhead
cards.body: files.orchestration (procpipe) on gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl (full matrix, release compiler, gauntlet/results/2026-09-03.json): Jet 367 ms vs Rust 339 ms (1.08x), Go 336 ms (1.09x), Python 355 ms (1.03x), Node 366 ms (1.00x, loss by the strict rule). The workload is dominated by the child processes, so the whole gap is Jet's own spawn, pipe, and wait plumbing (about 30 ms across the pipeline).
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Remove Jet's fixed spawn, pipe, and wait overhead so that `procpipe` AOT meets the strict gate (Jet/Rust ≤ 1.05, Jet/{Go,Python,Node} < 1.00) and per-process overhead is under 0.2 ms. The process API, timeouts, sandbox law, and diagnostics stay unchanged.

**Evidence**
Gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl measured Jet 367 ms, Rust 339 ms (1.08x), Go 336 ms (1.09x), Python 355 ms (1.03x), and Node 366 ms (1.00x, a loss under the strict rule). The children dominate the workload, so the roughly 30 ms gap is Jet's own plumbing.

**Current state**
- Spawning lives in `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Process.rs`.
  - `:292` builds a `std::process::Command` per spawn.
  - `:340-342` uses `process_group(0)` so ordinary children keep posix_spawn.
  - Pipeline children use `jet_process_pipeline_child` (`:1843`), stop/cleanup (`:1879-1926`), and the relay only when the output limit is not the default (`:643`).
  - `ProcessSpec.rs`, `ProcessPolicy.rs`, and `ProcessSandbox.rs` hold per-spawn policy.
- A 2026-09-21 audit listed candidates: default stderr drains, per-child environment rebuild, and per-call receipt allocations. There is no profile or witness yet.
- `Core/process/process.jet` has only a syntax-migration diff in the working tree.
- The workload is `Tools/gauntlet/entries/procpipe/`.

**Changes**
1. Witness: add `Examples/features/process/spawn_witness.jet`, which pipelines 100 `true` children and prints the collected count, plus its `.out` golden.
2. Profile the AOT witness with `perf record`. Remove fixed per-spawn costs in `Process*.rs`: rebuild the environment once per pipeline, skip stderr drain threads when stderr is inherited or null, reuse read buffers, block in `wait` instead of polling, and hoist policy and sandbox checks to once per pipeline. The D-JPK-SANDBOX2 path stays unchanged.
3. `crates/jet-jit/src/Process.rs` marshalling only, if the JIT shares the cost.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=process/spawn_witness cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` gives identical output on AOT, default run, and interpreter.
- `cargo test --test build_sandbox` passes with diagnostics byte-identical.
- `perf stat -r 5 ./spawn_witness` on the AOT binary shows (wall − children) / 100 < 0.2 ms.
- `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry procpipe --jet-bin target/release/jet` shows Jet/Rust ≤ 1.05 and Jet/{go,python,node} < 1.00. Record the ratios and keep any loss open.

**Batch**
`batch-host-runtime`: the Prelude process runtime with tier parity.

**Dependencies**
None.

cards.title: Gauntlet harness and corpus: peer fixture server, batch-steps trace reset, axis zig probe, parallel-grep entry drift
cards.body:
Three harness defects on gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl (full matrix, release compiler, gauntlet/results/2026-09-03.json) mark working Jet tiers as broken:

1. 'spec.peer' fixture servers (http-client: fixtures/peer.py on 18400) are alive only for the AOT measurement; the run and dev tiers then fail with 'panic: GET failed'. Started by hand, 'jet run run.jet -- http://127.0.0.1:18400' prints the expected output.
2. batch-steps entries (taskfile-cli) run the tier-trace invocation without resetting state files, so the trace sees ids 28, 29, 30 in tasks.json and reports 'trace output mismatch' although the run tier is correct.
3. The memory_safety_fuzz axis reports 'zig: zig version probe failed (exit 1)' while the zig rail builds and runs for every entry in the same run, so the axis stays unmeasured.

Also: web rails never capture artifact_bytes (see the web card).
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Finish the gauntlet harness/corpus repair: criteria 1-3 are verified (peer fixture lifetime for http-client, batch-steps trace reset for taskfile-cli, memory_safety_fuzz zig probe). Only criterion 4 remains: parallel-grep compiles on every Jet tier and concurrency.app is measured against Rust (165 ms), Go (328 ms), Node (3.63 s) and Python (9.09 s).

**Current state**
- Criterion 4's source-drift premise is stale: Tools/gauntlet/entries/parallel-grep/jet/run.jet:25-31 already uses the current contract (`counts :: inputs.para_map((input: ScanInput) -> count_lines(input))`, `count :: counts[index]`; no `pair.b`). Card log 2026-09-21 confirms no source patch is needed.
- Last proof (2026-09-20, run 20260920-3291390-mu9dyx7r): all peers complete; Jet cold build exits 101 after 15.189 s — effect grant mismatch, then a generated-Rust `Task<Result<...>>` mismatch ICE. No Tower card owns that ICE.
- Harness moved to Tools/gauntlet/harness/ (run.mjs, memory-safety-fuzz.mjs, *.test.mjs); the card's `gauntlet/` paths are stale. artifact_bytes for web rails stays with #2867.

**Changes**
1. Pip mints the compiler bug card for the ICE (repro: `jet build Tools/gauntlet/entries/parallel-grep/jet/run.jet`); the fix lands in that card's batch, not here. Also confirm whether the effect report is a correct user error (entry's package grants) or part of the same defect; if the entry lacks a needed grant, add it to the entry's inline package policy.
2. After the fix, rebuild and run the entry on every tier; keep expected.out byte-identical.
3. Record concurrency.app ratios per peer; losses are recorded with an owner, not waived.

**Proof**
- `node --test Tools/gauntlet/harness/` passes (run.test.mjs, measurement-manifest.test.mjs, memory-safety-fuzz.test.mjs, status, integrated-gate).
- `Tools/agent/jet-env node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry parallel-grep`: AOT, `jet run`, `jet dev` and `--interpret` print byte-identical output (I9) and the result lists concurrency.app ratios against Rust, Go, Node and Python.

**Dependencies**
The new generated-Rust `Task<Result>` ICE bug card (to be minted).

cards.body: On gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl (full matrix, release compiler, gauntlet/results/2026-09-03.json) every AOT binary is about 0.7-0.8 MB (binparse 1.34x Rust, 47x C; concurrency-service 1.52x Rust) and every AOT process starts at about 14.2 MB peak RSS against 10.5 MB for the C, Rust and Zig peers (1.35x). Both are required metrics under the competitive law and lose on every measured cell regardless of runtime. The size comes from the inlined runtime crate (the whole Prelude is compiled into each program); the RSS from runtime initialisation (allocator, stack-frame and journey bookkeeping, store handles).
cards.plan:
## Goal

cards.title: AOT Reader.take_pattern per frame and per-byte iteration keep embedded-data 24x behind Rust and 7.8x behind C
cards.body: embedded.data (embedded-data) AOT on gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl (full matrix, release compiler, gauntlet/results/2026-09-03.json): Jet 113 ms vs Rust 4.7 ms (24x), Zig 6.6 ms (17x), C 14.6 ms (7.8x); wins Node 0.80x and Python 0.43x. binparse, the sibling Reader entry repaired by #2253, is now 1.29x Rust and 1.19x Zig, so the remaining cost is the shapes #2253 did not cover: 'reader.take_pattern([U8]{"{channel:U8}{flags:U8}{sample:U16le}..."})' once per 12-byte frame (1,000,000 frames) and 'loop byte in data -> checksum += Int.from_u8(byte)' over 12 MB. Both go through Prelude calls per element in the generated Rust; C reads the frame struct in place.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Close the embedded-data AOT loss. Measured on gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl: Jet 113 ms vs Rust 4.7 ms (24x), Zig 6.6 ms (17x), C 14.6 ms (7.8x); Jet wins Node (0.80x) and Python (0.43x). The sibling binparse entry sits at 1.29x Rust. The goal is for fixed-width `reader.take_pattern` and `loop byte in data` to compile to direct slice code, in the self-hosted printer and the shipped binary alike.

## Current state
- Jet lowering: `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Expressions.jet:4857-4875` lowers `.ReaderTakePattern(parts, canonical)` to `MirSemanticOp.ReaderTakePattern(receiver_value, receiver_place, lowered_parts)`. The parts carry `Bits` widths and endianness.
- The Jet Rust printer has no adapter for `ReaderTakePattern` (or for `CursorTakePattern`). `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Operations.jet:2572` prints only `BinaryPatternMatch`. The Reader op falls through to `:2590` ("MIR semantic operation has no Jet source adapter", E0003), so the self-hosted compiler cannot emit this program at all. It only reads captures, at `:2269` and `:2298`.
- The shipped printer already has a fixed-width fast path: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIRRust.rs:23849` `fixed_reader_take_pattern`, used at `:24503`. It does per-frame literal checks and constant-offset loads, then calls `jet_reader_take_pattern_checked`. The general path at `:24538` calls `jet_reader_take_pattern` / `jet_reader_pattern_miss`. The Prelude MatchScan byte-aligned fast path also landed (f84ffca41). The 113 ms figure predates both, so it has to be measured again.
- `Tools/gauntlet/entries/embedded-data/jet/run.jet` has an uncommitted 1-line edit in the working tree.
- Byte loops still go through Prelude cursors per element.
- `tests/reader_witness/` does not exist.

## Changes
1. Jet printer, `Emit/Operations.jet`:
   - Add a native `.ReaderTakePattern` adapter (and `.CursorTakePattern` beside it).
   - Port the MIRRust.rs:23849 rule. When every part is a literal or a fixed-width `Bits` part at a byte-aligned offset, print one tail length check, constant-offset `from_le_bytes`/`from_be_bytes` loads, and one checked advance.
   - Otherwise print the shared `jet_reader_take_pattern` route, with `jet_reader_pattern_miss` on the miss path so the error text is unchanged.
   - Also print captures without the per-field `.clone()` for Copy scalars (`:2298`).
2. Jet lowering, `Codegen/Statements.jet`: lower `loop byte in data` over `[U8]` to a borrowed slice cursor when ownership facts prove the collection is not written in the loop, and widen inline for `Int.from_u8`. Reuse the view machinery owned by #3318 rather than adding a second borrowed cursor.
3. Rust mirror: add the same byte-loop borrow in MIRRust.rs so the shipped binary proves it. The Prelude reader helpers stay host code.
4. Witnesses: add `tests/reader_witness/{frames.jet,checksum.jet}` (1M fixed-width frames; a 12 MB byte checksum) plus a test `reader_witness_fast_paths_agree` in `tests/tir_io_and_ownership.rs`. The test asserts that the emitted Rust has no per-frame matcher call and that output is identical on AOT, `jet run` and `--interpret`, including the miss diagnostic.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test tir_io_and_ownership -- reader_witness`: passes.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=parsing/ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: no drift.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: no new JetCodegen errors, and no E0003 "no Jet source adapter" for ReaderTakePattern.
- Measurement: `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry embedded-data` and `--entry binparse` show AOT Jet/Rust <= 1.05 and Jet/{C,Zig,Python,Node} < 1.00.

## Batch
batch-jetc-back: Jet printer and lowering work, with a MIRRust.rs mirror.

## Dependencies
#3318 (deciding) decides which borrowed iteration seam step 2 should reuse. The take_pattern half does not depend on it. Non-goals: no bin-pattern grammar change (D-BINPAT1). The JIT/run-tier speed of these shapes belongs to #2863.
