cards.title: AOT integer modulo/division stay out-of-line: embedded-sensor-ring is 4.6x behind Rust
cards.body: embedded.kernel (embedded-sensor-ring) AOT on gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl (full matrix, release compiler, gauntlet/results/2026-09-03.json): Jet 4.87 ms vs Rust 1.06 ms (4.6x), C 1.2 ms (4.1x), Zig 1.31 ms (3.7x); wins Node 0.18x, Python 0.11x. 'jet emit --rust' shows nine 'jet_int_mod' calls in the ring loop; #2254 inlined add/sub/mul ('jet_int_add_hot!') but modulo and division still call out with the bigint-promotion check on every operation.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Give exact default Int a real machine-word fast path. Inline operands must do checked i64 arithmetic with no heap allocation, and only overflow, spill or error cases take the cold exact or trap rail. This closes the embedded-sensor-ring loss and unblocks #1436 criterion 4.

## Current state
- Measured AOT: Jet 4.87 ms vs Rust 1.06 ms (4.6x), C 1.2 ms, Zig 1.31 ms.
- The problem is broader than modulo. Every exact-Int op routes through the heap:
  - The Jet emitter maps ops to `jet_int_owned_*` (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Operations.jet:33-45, 347-363`).
  - Those wrap the raw ops (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/CommonTypes.rs:4735-4794`), e.g. `jet_int_add` :4317 and `jet_int_mod` :4498.
  - The raw ops call the "hot" macros (:4162-4300), which simply forward to `jet_int_exact_*`.
  - `jet_int_exact_add` (:5085) and `jet_int_exact_mod` (:5198) build `CtBigInt` from both operands via `jet_std_raw_to_exact` (:5311) and `jet_int_value` → `JetBigInt::from_int` (:4013). That allocates limb Vecs even for small values.
- jet-foundation already has the correct fast path: `JetInt::add` (`crates/jet-foundation/src/Numeric.rs:3160`) checks `is_inline()` (:2993) first.
- A witness exists: `tests/int_ring_witness.jet`, with `tests/int_division.rs:222` `integer_ring_modulo_and_division_preserve_tier_output` expecting `613081333`.

## Changes

cards.body: numerics.float-kernel (nbody) AOT on gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl (full matrix, release compiler, gauntlet/results/2026-09-03.json): default Jet 3.48 ms vs C 2.77 ms (1.25x), Rust 2.35 ms (1.48x), Zig 2.42 ms (1.44x); wins Node 37x and Python. Expert pair: jet-expert 2.2 ms vs c-expert 1.61 ms (1.36x) and rust-expert 1.93 ms (1.14x). The campaign law asks the default kernel to reach at most 1.05x expert C; #2261 (D-SIMD3=B auto-vectorization with #Scalar opt-out) closed on implementation evidence, so this card owns the remaining gap.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Close the nbody numerics.float-kernel AOT gap. Default Jet takes 3.48 ms, against C 2.77 ms (1.25x), Rust 2.35 ms (1.48x) and Zig 2.42 ms (1.44x); Node and Python are already beaten. Expert pair: jet-expert 2.2 ms against c-expert 1.61 ms (1.36x) and rust-expert 1.93 ms (1.14x). Source: gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl. D-SIMD3=B (auto-vectorize by default, `#Scalar` opts out, #2261) is ratified and must not be reopened. This card owns the remaining gap.

## Current state
- Optimizer: `Compiler/JetOptimizer/Source/Facts/LoopVector.jet:33` `mir_pass_derive_loop_and_vector_facts` derives loop shape, trip count, reduction and vector legality. `Facts/Bounds.jet` and `Verification/Legality.jet` hold the index proofs.
- The Jet Rust printer uses none of these facts: `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/` has no vector or unchecked-index path. `Values.jet:958` special-cases only `MirIndexKind.FixedListProof`.
- The 2026-09-21 audit found that no checked vector facts reach native emission for nbody's nested pair-update loops. In the shipped path the proofs are dropped at TIR→MIR, which is #3039 (building).
- Witnesses already exist:
  - `tests/nbody_witness.rs` and `tests/nbody_witness/{standard,scalar}.jet` check output identity only (`-0.169075164`), on JIT and AOT.
  - `tests/simd_witness.rs:216` proves packed MIR for a `[Float#4]` loop and that `#Scalar` opts out.
  - `tests/jit_run.rs:2454` covers resident-JIT nbody.
- Peer identities come from `Tools/gauntlet/entries/nbody/entry.json`, including the Rust `target-cpu=ivybridge` rail.

## Changes
1. Optimizer (`LoopVector.jet`, `Bounds.jet`, `Legality.jet`): prove nbody's nested pair-update and reduction loops, meaning trip counts, disjoint indexed places and eliminated safe indexes. Record the results on the MIR function or loop. Take the facts that #3039 carries instead of inferring them a second time.
2. Jet printer (`Emit/Operations.jet`, `Emit/ControlFlow.jet`, `Emit/Values.jet`):
   - For lanes marked proven, print plain `f64` operators, `f64::sqrt`, and indexing that skips the check because of the proof.
   - For `#Scalar` functions, keep the existing checked shape.
   - Keep reduction order fixed, so Float output is byte-identical.
3. Rust mirror in `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIRRust.rs`: print the same thing from the same MIR facts. Target flags stay in `Source/main.rs::rustc_args_for_target` and `Source/CmdCompile.rs`, matched to the entry's peer ISA. Peer sources are never edited.
4. Add `nbody_default_emits_packed_f64_and_scalar_does_not` to `tests/nbody_witness.rs`. It inspects the generated Rust and the `--emit asm` output: `vmulpd`/`vaddpd` must be present by default and absent under `#Scalar`.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test nbody_witness`: both tests pass, with output identical across tiers and packed f64 only in the default profile.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test simd_witness`: passes, with no regression.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: no new JetOptimizer or JetCodegen errors.
- Measurement: `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry nbody` must show Jet/{C,Zig} < 1.00, Jet/Rust <= 1.05, jet-expert/c-expert < 1.00 and jet-expert/rust-expert <= 1.05. Every loss is recorded.

cards.title: If-expression arm read moves a non-Copy local and exposes rustc E0382
cards.body: Minimal integrated repro: bind a [U8] local, return that local from one if-expression arm into a new binding, then read the original local. AOT emits the arm tail as a move and rustc rejects the later read with E0382. The equivalent direct binding emits a borrow, while default run and forced interpreter preserve the expected value. D-MEM-COPYSEM1 requires a read into a non-view slot to be a semantic copy; sema ownership rewriting is not reaching if-expression arm tails. This is independent of typed empty-list inference in #2818.

log.text: Closed after integrated four-case ownership proof; no codegen cloning or rustc leakage remains.

cards.title: Generic function with scalar read parameters: AOT ICE while jet run and --interpret print the answer
cards.body:
Actual: `fn max_of<T: Comparable>(left: T, right: T) T -> if left > right -> ~left else -> ~right` with `print(max_of(3, 7))`: `jet check` passes, `jet run` prints 7, `jet run --interpret` prints 7, `jet build` and `jet run --release` exit 101 with the generated-Rust ICE banner. Cause: the emitter declares the instantiation as `pub fn __jet_max_of<T: __jet_Comparable + Clone>(__jet_left: &T, __jet_right: &T)` (unmarked read parameters lower to references) while the call site passes `3i64`/`7i64` by value: `__jet_max_of::<i64>(__jet___arg111_0, __jet___arg111_1)` (repro build/g2.rs lines 70860-70870). The shipped example `examples/features/types/traits.jet` (`largest<T: Comparable>(xs: [T])`) passes only because its parameter is a list. Neighbors on the same program family: (a) `max_of(2.5, 1.5)` gives E0905 "`Decimal` isn't `Comparable`" (the float literal defaults to Decimal, which has no Comparable impl); (b) a variant calling `max_of(I64{4}, I64{2})` turns `jet check` into E2104 "Cost projection ... type-parameterized callable has no complete TIR specialization" whose why/fix text is about command input.

Source: video mine 2026-09-03 (Why Rust Can't Replace C++: zero-cost generics), probe R6 and orchestrator repro `~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/main/g2.jet`.

Expected: one program, one meaning on every tier (I9); rustc rejection is never reachable from a program sema accepted (I2, I3).
cards.plan: 1. Decide argument passing for generic calls once in TIR lowering from the parameter mode (unmarked read of a type-parameter value passes the same way in the signature and at every call site) and make the emitter follow that one rule. 2. Give `Decimal` the Comparable protocol (and the other numeric protocols it lacks), or make a float literal in a Comparable context infer `Float` if the numeric-literal law says so; record which. 3. Replace the E2104 path with a registered sema diagnostic naming the generic function and the missing specialization. 4. Add an executable example with scalar generic parameters for Int, Float, and a user #Comparable struct, golden on AOT, jet run, and --interpret.

cards.title: Shipped example operators/spaceship.jet: sort_by with a compare comparator is an AOT ICE, E0956 on jet run, E2201 on --interpret
cards.body:
Actual: `examples/features/operators/spaceship.jet` line 24 `leaderboard.sort_by((left: Player, right: Player) -> left.compare(right))`: `jet build` exits 101 (emits `Ok(jet_trace_err(((*__jet_left)).compare(&((*__jet_right))), ...)?)` — `?` on an `Ordering`, T1_spaceship.rs:71389-71400); `jet run` prints the first two lines then E0956 "`sort_by comparator must return Ordering` isn't supported by the current evaluator yet"; `jet run --interpret` prints the same two lines then E2201 "`jet dev` can't interpret this program yet — it uses `sort_by comparator must return Ordering`". The JIT trace shows the whole program sent to tier0 (`tier plan gate failed: entry_native; ... ClosureMethod:SortByCompare`). 19 of the other 20 sampled examples matched on all three tiers.

Source: video mine 2026-09-03 tier parity sweep T1 (`~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/loops/results.md`). Neighbor card #2861 covers the `sort_by receiver` refusal only.

Expected (I5, I9): the example prints its golden output on every tier.
cards.plan:
## Authority and scope

No board dependency is recorded. The existing checked `SortByCompare` lowering, route, and interpreter kernel are the one mechanism. #2861 owns the separate `sort_by` receiver refusal; do not duplicate that fix here. The `Ordering` comparator is infallible, so lowering must not add an error-propagation operator to its result.

## Owned paths

- `examples/features/operators/spaceship.jet` and `examples/features/expected/operators/spaceship.out`
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/builtins.rs`
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/routes.rs`
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIREval.rs`
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/SortKernel.rs`
- `tests/tir_operators_and_runtime.rs`, `tests/dev_interp_parity.rs`, and `tests/jit_corpus_gate.txt`
- `crates/jet-jit/src/jit/tiers.rs`

## Ordered implementation and cutover

1. Trace the spaceship example’s comparator through `TClosureOp::SortByCompare` in `lower/builtins.rs`, the `core.list.sort_by_compare`/`jet_list_sort_by_compare` routes, the `MIREval` comparator handler, and `SortKernel.rs`. Keep the comparator’s `Ordering` result as the checked closure contract.
2. Remove the erroneous `jet_trace_err(...)?`/fallible wrapper for the infallible `Ordering` result at the lowering seam, while preserving real comparator errors and source diagnostics for other closure shapes.
3. Ensure AOT, resident JIT, and interpreter all reach the existing sort helper and that tier planning does not force this route to tier0 or report E0956/E2201 for a supported comparator. Do not add a second sort kernel or bypass the route table.
4. Update the example golden, operator/runtime parity coverage, and resident-JIT corpus manifest; remove or revise only snapshots whose stale diagnostic is eliminated. Keep #2861’s receiver work separate.
5. Review the exact route/lowering diff, then run the focused example and tier/parity proof after implementation.

## Acceptance and proof

After implementation, build/run/interpret `examples/features/operators/spaceship.jet` against `spaceship.out`, inspect `--trace-tiers`, and exercise the operator/runtime parity and JIT corpus checks. Require exit 0, exact golden output, no tier0-interpreter row caused by `SortByCompare`, and no stale E0956/E2201 comparator diagnostic. This preparation claims no run.

## Dependencies and non-goals

No board dependency is open. #2861 remains a sibling boundary. Do not change spaceship semantics, add a comparator fallback, or mask a real lowering/runtime error.

cards.title: Path dependency, `--locked`, and `--offline` all fail on a fresh `jet new` project (E0603, E1239 hard-link authority, E1250 toolchain channel)
cards.body:
Actual, from two `jet new` projects `demo` and `lib1` (lib1 exports `pub fn double(x: Int) Int -> x * 2`): (1) `deps: { lib1: ../lib1 }` then `jet build` -> E0603, the compiler searched `lib1.jet` and `lib1/lib1/lib1.jet`/`run.jet` under the dependency path; the `./../lib1` spelling behaves the same. (3) On the plain scaffold with a lock present, `jet build --locked` and `jet build --offline` -> E1250 "Toolchain channel `1.0.0` is pinned but not locked ... Run `jet update jet`" although the scaffold and lock were both written by this same jet binary.

cards.title: Loop liveness lints and the foreign `do` teaching text: unreachable after `loop {}`, `loop true`, bare comparison statement, never-reassigned condition
cards.body:
Actual (all `jet check`, zero diagnostics): (1) `loop { print(1) }` with no `break`, followed by `print(2)` — no unreachable-code warning although sema already marks the code as unreachable internally (Diagnostics.rs:495-547). (2) `loop true { break }` — no lint toward the canonical `loop { }`. (3) A bare comparison statement `i < 6` on its own line (a user trying a trailing loop condition) is accepted silently; no unused-value lint. (4) `running := true` used as `loop running { ... break }` and never reassigned — no `::` suggestion. (5) The E0003 fix text for a foreign `do { ... } while cond` is only "Write `loop { … }`" and does not show the body-first shape `loop { …  if !cond { break } }`.

Source: video mine 2026-09-03 (Infinite Loop Problem in Python), probes L1, L3, L4, L5 in `~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/loops/results.md`; ballot D-DO1 on the same card decides whether a body-first loop spelling exists (recommendation: no new keyword, teach the shape).

Expected: one canonical spelling per loop meaning (I8) taught by lints with fix-its; unreachable and no-effect statements never compile in silence.
cards.plan: 1. Lint: unreachable statement after a loop without `break` (reuse the existing definitely-exits fact). 2. Lint: constant-true loop condition -> fix-it to `loop { }`; constant-false -> body never runs. 3. Lint: expression statement with no effect (comparison, arithmetic, bare name) with fix-it. 4. Lint: mutable binding never reassigned -> `::`. 5. E0003 for `do`/`repeat`/`until`: fix text shows the post-test shape with `if !cond { break }`. 6. UI snapshots for each; entries in the lint registry.

log.text: Implementation-only pass: shipped the five loop liveness/teaching source behaviors. Deferred generated snapshots/grammar/examples and validation to #2919 per owner sequencing.

D-DO1 redesign record: A attempt 1, trailing `loop { … } until test` plus existing state-loop header, failed because `until` is new and a trailing header cannot read a body-bound `line`; the existing header pre-tests and skips an empty first line. A attempt 2, `break if test` as the only spelling plus the ratified bottom-break arrow, failed because the former retires general `if test { break }`, while `if test -> break` stays inside the block and `break value ?? fallback` follows a complete loop expression. Why unavoidable: the exit test reads a value produced inside the block; C and Java hoist it, but Jet block scope forbids that move without new grammar. `next` in A skips the bottom test, unlike C do-while; E0003 fix text and proposed L-BODYFIRST must state that. C pays a hoisted-declaration cost (`line := ""` outside the proposed block). E0003 today knows do/while/for/continue, not repeat/until; expansion is proposed.

criteria.text: Source-complete: sema emits registered loop/liveness lints for unreachable post-loop code, constant loop conditions, effect-free discarded expressions, and mutable bindings never reassigned, while parser teaching rewrites foreign do/repeat/until to canonical body-first loops. Snapshots, fixtures, examples, syntax artifacts, and focused proof are deferred to #2919.

cards.title: Canonicalize loop forms and fold constant conditions once in TIR so no tier pays for a spelling (interpreter 2.5x spread today)
cards.body:
Actual: six spellings of the same counter loop (`loop {}`+break, `loop true`, `loop running` with a flag, `loop i < N`, `loop j := 0, j < N`, `loop k in 0..<N`) at N=3,000,000 on `jet run --interpret`: 64.0 s, 74.0 s, 80.9 s, 56.5 s, 87.8 s, 35.8 s — a 2.5x spread for one meaning. `jet run` (JIT, debug compiler): 3.18, 3.12, 3.16, 3.13, 3.58, 2.75 s. AOT folds all six to under 1 ms (rustc turns the emitted `while true` into `loop`). The emitter maps `loop true` to Rust `while true` (L2b_true.rs) and the JIT lowers every `While` as cond+brif with no constant folding (lower_ctx.rs:6612-6683); the evaluator charges fuel per node (eval/stmts.rs:1149-1307). TIR keeps five distinct loop nodes (TIR/mod.rs:3708-3857) and no shared optimization pass exists between tiers.

Source: video mine 2026-09-03 (Infinite Loop Problem in Python: `while 1` vs `while True` cost), probe L2 in `~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/loops/results.md`. cards.title: Exact placement and lock-free control without #Unsafe: size_of/align_of, alignment layout rule, and an atomic value surface
cards.body:
Actual: the C++ replacement bar in the mined video is exact placement and lock-free hot paths (placement new, cache-line-aligned pools, atomics, hazard pointers). Jet today: `#Layout(c)` works (probe R3: `#Layout(c) struct { a: I8; b: I64; c: I8 }` builds and runs on every tier); `size_of`/`align_of` do not exist (E0102 `Nothing named size_of exists here`); `#Align(64)` is E0927 (`Align` isn't a registered applied rule); no user-facing atomic type exists (grep of Prelude/CoreLib and spec finds only Rust-internal `Atomic*`), so a single-producer single-consumer ring must use `channel` (probe R1: 1,000,000 items sum correct on all tiers; AOT 0.20 s, jet run 3.43 s, --interpret 18.65 s). Jet already answers the video's intrusive-structure objection safely with the arena idiom (`Pool<T>/Id<T>`, probe R2b runs on all tiers) and has no GC by default (D-MEM1).

Source: video mine 2026-09-03 (Why Rust Can't Replace C++), probes R1, R3 in `~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/build/results.md`.

Owner gates to raise on this card: (1) layout introspection API names (`size_of`, `align_of`) as Core functions; (2) an alignment rule spelling inside the existing `#Layout` family (for example `#Layout(c, align: 64)`) rather than a new `#Align` marker (I8: one layout mechanism); (3) whether an `Atomic<Int>`-style value with load/store/fetch_add/compare_exchange belongs in Core or stays behind `#Unsafe`, and how it lowers identically on JIT and the interpreter (I9). Each becomes a ballot with current/proposed/in-the-wild code (Rust `std::sync::atomic`, Zig `@sizeOf`/`align(64)`, C++ `alignas`).
cards.plan:
## Authority and scope
D-PLACE1=A, D-ATOMIC-WIDTH1=A, and D-LAYOUT-ALIGN1=A are ratified in Tower. Implement those selected contracts; no owner gate remains on this card. The latest Atomic recommendation supersedes the fixed-reserve proposal: no Atomic-only quota, artificial exhaustion, or immortal-pinning fallback. Implement only the selected contracts and preserve every existing criterion.

## Ordered implementation
1. Freeze the selected Atomic and alignment contracts in the existing syntax/spec/registry. Keep one Atomic family and one compiler-owned layout fact; do not add a second exact-number implementation or target-specific semantic fallback.
2. For Atomic A, replace global numeric mutex/interning and append-only arenas with canonical immutable exact values, growable nonblocking allocation, tracked ownership, and object-granular reclamation. Keep the inline fast path and distinguish I64 wrapping from Int exact arithmetic. A local cache miss requests ordinary admitted storage; it cannot become an Atomic-only allocation failure.
3. Preserve numeric-value CAS across distinct handles, old-value add, one-word publication, SeqCst ordinary operations, release publish/acquire observe, and all failure/ordering rules. Registration, allocator growth, ownership, return values, error carriers, and drop are part of the whole-path progress proof. No stopped participant may own the sole allocation/reclamation path.
4. Prove ownership-count bounds over every real tracked owner, including foreign transfers and temporaries. Remove the old saturation-to-immortal rule; do not substitute wraparound, permanent retention, or hidden load/store failures. Preserve old values while reclaiming unrelated objects and returning unused backing storage.
5. Cut over AOT, JIT, interpretation, and applicable web to the same exact-number/atomic kernel. Remove the bounded-i64 interpreter route and independent arena policies. New try_new/try_add forms use the existing AllocError family and cannot publish on failure.
6. For alignment A, keep ordinary align(N) as an exact minimum under the portable profile intersection; the proposed align(target, N) explicitly selects proved target facts without a second arbitrary Jet ceiling. Natural alignment may make effective alignment larger. The proposed 1 MiB portable baseline is conditional on complete evidence, not established support.
7. Separate type representability, stack placement, global/linker placement, heap allocation, and foreign by-value ABI facts. Sema owns refusal before codegen. Cache identity includes target/profile, execution-mode set, backend/toolchain/linker, allocator-provider digest, and fact version. Never clamp a request or treat --target alone as expert opt-in.
8. Migrate parser/AST/Syntax, sema registration, Foundation layout/target facts, codegen and every consumer in one cutover. Preserve existing layout examples, reflection facts, diagnostics and snapshots. No unsupported tier is silently excluded.

## Owned paths
crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Atomic.rs; CoreLib/JetStd/CommonTypes.rs and the canonical exact-number module; Foundation Layout.rs/TargetMachine.rs/Facts.rs; Sema/CheckerCore/type_assign.rs and Sema/Registration/Items.rs; parser Items/{distinct_units_structs.rs,marker_groups.rs}; AST items/expressions; Syntax/math_layout.rs; existing JIT/MIR/web adapters; examples/features/lowlevel/layout_c.jet and examples/features/comptime/layout_facts.jet.

## Proof and integration ownership
Coordinate the canonical numeric carrier and allocator cutover as one coherent patch. D-LAYOUT-ALIGN1 owns the separate target-capability choice. No source implementation or criterion completion is claimed by this planning pass.

After ratification, rebuild and exercise the exact counter on AOT, default run, interpretation, and applicable web modes. Check 2^62/2^63 boundaries, multi-limb values, numeric CAS across distinct storage, retained old values, ordering, and I64 versus Int arithmetic.

Prove growth beyond the former reserve without failure while ordinary admitted memory is available. Pause a reader, writer, and growth participant; unrelated updates and reclamation must progress without a global epoch, refill dependency, or hidden lock. Check real exhaustion leaves the cell unchanged, ownership counts cannot wrap or pin, and error construction is safe.

Audit the complete allocation/registration/ownership/reclamation path and target-provider premises; stress alone is not a progress proof. Run matched fixed-width, small-Int, and large-Int workloads with every required metric and peer. No performance regression or execution-mode gap becomes a pass.

Ordinary 2097152 must reject even with --target. Exercise align(target, 2097152) on supporting and refusing profiles. Include natural alignment above the request, zero, negatives, non-powers, missing capabilities, and arithmetic overflow.

Agreement means identical effective size, alignment, offsets, and stride, not identical numeric addresses. Wherever storage is materialized, verify address modulo effective alignment equals zero. Check stack, heap, global, array, and supported foreign-by-value and pointer crossings. A logical engine still owes identical facts; if an operation exposes an address or crosses FFI, it owes the physical guarantee too.

Test no-allocator and insufficient-RAM boards separately from type representability. Check normal and fallible heap failure without clamping. Change target, backend/tier set, linker, allocator, and foreign toolchain identity and require cache invalidation. Register and snapshot diagnostics, regenerate grammars, and golden-test the portable/expert pair. Planning claims no runtime or cross-target proof.

questions.answer:
Agreed. A now has two explicit paths inside the same layout rule: ordinary #Layout(c, align(N)) for portable type layouts, and proposed #Layout(c, align(target, N)) for target-specific requirements without a separate arbitrary Jet ceiling. Passing --target alone never weakens the ordinary form.

The portable proposal covers powers of two through 1 MiB. The expert form checks the selected profile’s real representation limits. N is an unclamped minimum; natural field alignment can make the effective alignment larger. Stack, global, heap, array, and foreign-call support are checked separately, so a valid type does not promise that an instance fits a board’s RAM.

“Unbounded” cannot mean infinite hardware. It means no extra Jet policy ceiling in the expert form, with early semantic rejection rather than clamping or a backend error. cards.title: Execution tiers: one implementation per feature or four? Decide the one-lowering architecture (audit + ballot D-TIER-ONEIR1)
cards.body:
Actual: the owner's invariant is "implement once; every tier runs it; tiers differ only in optimization." What ships: a shared front end through TIR, then four hand-written lowerings of language semantics — AOT Rust emission (`Codegen/TIR/emit`, ~19.8k lines), Cranelift (`jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs`, 34.3k lines; crate ~91k), a tree-walking TIR evaluator (`Codegen/TIR/eval`, ~30.5k lines, `HashMap<String, CtValue>` scopes), and a web emitter (`Codegen/Web.rs`, 12.9k lines) — plus three registration tables for every Prelude function (AOT prelude projection, JIT `host_fns!` at jet-jit/lib.rs:74-177, interpreter ambient arms at core_calls.rs:421-455 / ambient_interp.rs). Comments in ambient_interp.rs:2487-2491, 2842-2845, 5422-5425 record features that ran on AOT and JIT and died on the interpreter until an arm was added. Deopt is whole-program and silent (tiers.rs:1236-1450; `jet run --trace-tiers` showed 4 of 20 sampled examples sent to `tier0 interp`). The corpus gate reports zero tier-divergent rows, yet this run found in one afternoon: generic scalar params (AOT ICE / 7 / 7), recursive `?Node` (check ok / AOT ICE), spaceship example (ICE / E0956 / E2201), stdin lines (ok / ok / E2201), scaffold web build (E-WEB-TIR-UNSUPPORTED), and a 2.5x interpreter cost spread across loop spellings.

Deliverable: `docs/audits/tier-parity-architecture-2026-09-03.md` (how each tier works today, why divergence is structural, the target model, options) and ballot D-TIER-ONEIR1 with options A (one shared low-level IR lowered once from TIR; interpreter executes it, Cranelift compiles it, AOT compiles the same IR; Rust emission retired over time), B (keep Rust emission for AOT; unify JIT and interpreter on one lowering; differential tests against AOT), C (status quo plus a mandatory three-tier differential test for every example and every Prelude call row). D-DEVMODE1 already makes dev/release divergence a release blocker; I9 names Prelude as the only home of semantics.

cards.title: Elementwise list loop copies the list: AOT 0.89 s and 473 MiB for 20M adds, JIT 3.5 us/element, interpreter super-linear (2k 4 s, 6k 25 s, 20k 235 s)
cards.body:
Actual: `c[i] = a[i] + b[i]` over Float lists. AOT N=20M: 0.89 s, RSS 473 MiB, dev and release identical; generated loop (`s1_aot_default.rs:70869-70876`) starts with a `Vec<f64>` clone before indexed scalar stores, and L2510 warns "a generic collection representation repeats inside a loop" with fix text "Provide the collection shape proof that selects the direct representation", which no beginner can act on. JIT N=2M: 7.3 s (3.5 us per element; AOT is ~45 ns). Interpreter: N=2,000 finishes in 3.7 s (1.4 s of it is startup), N=20,000 and N=200,000 both exceed 180 s with no output. Ten times the data costs far more than ten times the time, which is the copy-per-iteration signature the L2510 lint itself describes. Same shape in S8 (unmarked and #Scalar) and S2-S4 (reductions, search).

cards.title: Fixed-width pairwise Float reduction: one defined order that every tier reproduces bit-for-bit and AOT vectorizes (ballot candidate D-FRED1)
cards.body:
Actual: S2 Float sum of 20M elements takes 0.43 s; the Int sum takes 0.03 s (14x). The Float release binary has no packed add in the reduction because IEEE addition is not associative and a strictly sequential accumulate cannot be vectorized. Rust and C++ behave the same without fast-math; the video's point that autovectorization only fires on code 'written the right way' is exactly this case.

Idea: instead of leaving the order sequential (slow) or unspecified (results differ by lane width and by tier, breaking one-program-one-meaning), define reductions over Float (`sum`, `fold` with +, `para_fold`) as fixed-width pairwise: K independent accumulators (e.g. K=8) combined in a fixed tree, specified in the language. Every tier computes the same bits because the order is part of the meaning; AOT gets K-wide packed adds; para_fold already needs a defined combine order and gets the same one. Numerically, pairwise summation has better error bounds than sequential. Cost: a specified K is an ABI-like constant; changing it changes results.

This is a language-meaning decision: ballot candidate D-FRED1 with options (A) fixed-width pairwise as defined order; (B) sequential order, explicit opt-in to pairwise via a Core function; (C) unspecified order. Evidence: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/simd/results.md S2.

cards.title: Optimization exists only in the Rust emitter: give TIR one shared pass so inlining and folding reach JIT and interpreter
cards.body:
Actual: every optimization Jet programs receive today happens after the AOT emitter hands Rust to rustc. `#Inline`/`#Inline(Always)` lower to `#[inline]`/`#[inline(always)]` attributes (`emit/functions.rs:807-813`) and nothing else consumes the marker: `crates/jet-jit/src` has no reference to the inline contract, and the interpreter walks the unmodified TIR. The resident JIT is built with `JITBuilder::new(default_libcall_names())` (`runtime_host.rs:3807`), which is Cranelift's default `opt_level=none`; the debug object path sets `opt_level none` explicitly (`api_debug.rs:76`). The only pre-tier pass in TIR lowering, `canonicalize_pre_tier_expr` (`lower/expressions.rs:1103`), erases user tags and does no folding. Measured effect: the six loop spellings differ by 2.5x on the interpreter and 0x on AOT because rustc folds `while true` and Jet does not (#2886); JIT runs 1 us per loop iteration (#2863). The owner's model is that tiers are the same program at different optimization levels; today the lower two tiers receive zero optimization and the top tier receives rustc's, none of it Jet's.

Source: video mine 2026-09-03, owner comment on the initial prompt; facts from this run's context maps and probes (`~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/`).

Expected: a small set of Jet-owned TIR passes (constant-condition folding, loop-form canonicalization, contract-driven inlining of `#Inline(Always)` bodies, dead-branch removal) that run once after lowering and before any back end, so all four back ends see the same optimized TIR. Cranelift `opt_level=speed` for the resident JIT once the parity gate is green on it. Which passes belong at the shared seam and which stay per-tier is the decision D-TIER-ONEIR1 frames.
cards.plan: 1. Inventory what rustc currently folds for Jet output that the interpreter and JIT do not (start from the six #2886 spellings and the `#Inline(Always)` corpus). 2. Add a `TIR/opt` module with the folding and canonicalization passes from #2886 and inline expansion for `#Inline(Always)` (the checked promise already bounds body size via E0919, so expansion is total). 3. Run the passes once in `lower_*_program` so eval, JIT, web, and emit all consume the result; the emitter keeps emitting the Rust attribute as well. 4. Measure `opt_level=speed` on the JIT corpus gate; adopt if no parity regression. 5. Golden: the six loop spellings within 10% of each other on the interpreter and on the JIT.

cards.title: Transient AoS to SoA transposition for proven vector kernels: cost-gated, AOT-only, visible in jet inspect (ballot candidate D-AUTOSOA1)
cards.body:
Owner ask: when SIMD-shaped work runs over a list of structs, the compiler should be able to use a shallow SoA copy rather than require the user to declare `#Layout(columnar)` or restructure the program. Actual: Jet has exactly two layouts a user can pick by hand (`#Layout(c)`, `#Layout(columnar)`), the vector proof (`CheckerKernel.rs:52-320`) accepts only flat `[Float]`/`[Float#N]` lists, and no pass transposes. The SIMD video's own measurements motivate the ask: SoA is the shape the hardware wants and AoS is the shape the program wants. But a transient copy is only a win when the kernel touches few fields of many elements and runs long enough to amortize the transposition (roughly N x touched-fields x 8 bytes written twice); for the O(N^2) gravity probe (#2889) N=2000 amortizes trivially, for a one-pass N=20M add it never does (#2890 shows a single clone already costs 473 MiB).

Source: video mine 2026-09-03, owner comment on the initial prompt; facts from this run's context maps and probes (`~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/`).

Expected: a design decision (ballot) on whether AOT may introduce a transient columnar copy for a kernel the proof already accepts, under three conditions that keep it explainable: the kernel is proven side-effect free, the cost model shows amortization at the static or profiled trip count, and `jet inspect` reports the transposition with the reason. Behavior must be identical on every tier (a copy is unobservable), so this is an optimization choice, not a semantic one, and does not conflict with I9.
cards.plan: 1. First make the declared layout fast (#2889); an automatic transposition that lands on today's `JetColumnList::cell` accessors would be 15x slower, not faster. 2. Extend the kernel proof to record per-field access sets on struct-element loops (shared with the widen-the-net card). 3. Write D-AUTOSOA1 with options: A never transpose (user declares layout); B transpose when cost model amortizes, AOT only, reported in inspect; C transpose on request via a `#Columnar` loop marker. 4. Prototype B on the #2889 gravity probe and measure against manual SoA.

cards.title: Default multithreading for proven-independent kernels alongside or instead of SIMD: cost-gated auto-parallel (ballot candidate D-AUTOPAR1)
cards.body:
Owner ask: squeeze multithreading gains out by default, alongside SIMD and also where SIMD is impossible, instead of requiring an expert to rearchitect for `para_*`. Actual: parallelism in Jet is opt-in only (`para_map/filter/partition/fold`, 64-item chunks), and nothing decides for the user. The vector proof already establishes the property auto-parallel needs, iteration independence (no aliasing writes, no calls, no early exit), so the analysis exists and is consumed by one back end for one purpose. The SIMD video's numbers are the case for combining: SIMD gives 4-8x per core, threads give N-core x, and the two multiply until memory bandwidth caps them; a loop the proof rejects for SIMD (irregular control, calls) can still be thread-parallel if the iteration-independence half of the proof holds. Risks the video and its audience name: thread startup dwarfs small loops, bandwidth-bound loops gain nothing, and nondeterministic reduction order changes Float results (which is why #2891 wants one defined order first).

Source: video mine 2026-09-03, owner comment on the initial prompt; facts from this run's context maps and probes (`~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/`).

Expected: a ballot on whether the compiler may run a proven-independent `loop` body across threads by default when a cost model says the trip count amortizes spawn cost, with `#Serial` (or the existing `#Scalar`) as the opt-out and `jet inspect` naming the decision. Result must be bit-identical to the serial program on every tier; reductions are excluded until D-FRED1 gives them a defined order.

cards.title: Widen the vector proof: struct-field access, conditional accumulate, early-exit search, and reductions are rejected today
cards.body:
Owner ask: widen the set of loops the compiler can recognize so that shapes other compilers skip still vectorize in Jet. Actual (context map + probes): `CheckerKernel.rs:52-320` accepts elementwise loops over flat `[Float]`/`[Float#N]` with no calls, no control flow, no early exit, and no aliasing; it rejects (a) any struct field read (`p.x`), which is why the AoS gravity probe (#2889) vectorizes only through rustc's autovectorizer and the columnar one not at all; (b) `if cond { acc += x }` conditional accumulate, which is a masked add on every ISA the video shows; (c) `loop ... { if x == needle { break } }` early-exit search, which the video's string-search example vectorizes with a compare-and-movemask; (d) all reductions, because Float fold order is strict (#2891). The SIMD video's central claim is that these four shapes are the common ones and that relying on autovectorization for them is a black box; Jet's proof is the explainable alternative but currently covers the least common shape.

Source: video mine 2026-09-03, owner comment on the initial prompt; facts from this run's context maps and probes (`~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/`).

Expected: the proof accepts each of the four shapes with a named rule, emits the packed form (masked accumulate, compare+movemask+first-set, per-field gather or columnar direct load), and `jet inspect` names the accepted rule or the exact rejecting statement.
cards.plan: 1. Add per-field access sets to the proof so `p.x` over `[Particle]` and over `#Layout(columnar)` both pass; emit direct column loads for columnar (depends on #2889) and strided loads for AoS. 2. Conditional accumulate: prove the condition is side-effect free, emit select/mask. 3. Early exit: prove the body before `break` is side-effect free, emit chunked compare with scalar tail. 4. Reductions after D-FRED1. 5. Each new rule gets a golden probe on AOT with disassembly check and identical output on JIT and interpreter.

cards.title: Read-until-sentinel loop is one line in Python and three in Jet: the state-loop header runs its initializer once (ballot candidate D-LOOPREAD1)
cards.body:
Owner ask: take every UX/DX win Python offers, weighted by frequency. The Python video's walrus idiom `while (line := input()) != "":` is the most common interactive loop shape in the video and its comments; the video presents it as the correct modern replacement for both `while True: ... break` and do-while. Actual in Jet (probe L6, loops lane): `loop line := io.readline(), line != "" { ... }` type-checks and runs on every tier but evaluates the initializer once, so the loop reads one line and then spins or exits; the working form is `loop { line := io.readline() ; if line == "" { break } ; ... }`, three statements for the single most common input loop. The state-loop form (D-LOOP2, two slots) was designed for `loop i := 0, i < n` where once-only init is what you want, and E0376 retired the third slot that would have carried the per-turn step. No diagnostic warns that the header binding is loop-invariant.

Source: video mine 2026-09-03, owner comment on the initial prompt; facts from this run's context maps and probes (`~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/`).

Expected: an owner decision, because every option touches `Syntax.rs` or the reader's model of `loop`. Options: A keep the shape, add a lint when the state-loop binding is never reassigned in the body and the condition depends on it (it is then a one-shot loop by construction), and teach the three-line form in E0003's `do`/`while` fix text; B a `loop name := expr, cond` variant where the initializer re-runs each turn when it is a call (rejected in advance: same spelling, two meanings, breaks reasoning); C a dedicated iterator so the common case is `loop line in io.stdin().lines()` (already exists, D4 shows the interpreter refuses it: #2881) plus `lines_until(sentinel)`.
cards.plan: 1. Fix #2881 first so `loop line in io.stdin().lines()` runs on every tier; that already makes the common case one line. 2. Add the one-shot-loop lint from option A (binding never reassigned, condition reads it). 3. Draft D-LOOPREAD1 with A+C as the recommendation and B as the recorded rejection. 4. Update E0003's fix text for `while`/`do` to show the iterator form and the body-first form.

cards.title: Build metadata has three unrelated version fields and no manifest schema version: declare the forward/backward compatibility policy (owner gate)
cards.body:
Owner ask: does the build system capture all metadata Jet will need indefinitely, is it extensible, and can it preserve forward and backward compatibility across Jet versions? Actual (context map MapBuild + code): `package.jet` has a `jet:` compiler-version field and strict unknown-key rejection (E1206) but no schema version of its own, so a future key is an error to every older compiler and an older manifest has no marker a newer compiler can branch on; `.jet/lock` carries `version: 1` and `Lock.rs:1934-1938` rejects any other value outright ("unsupported lock version") with no migration path; the store is `jet.store.v1` as a magic prefix (`jet-store/lib.rs:17-26`); build records are `jet.build-record/v1` (`lib.rs:387`); receipts are v2 by a separate counter. Editions 2026-2028 exist for language semantics. Five independent version counters, none of them related by a stated rule, and the greenfield rule means no compatibility promise is currently in force at all. Strict rejection is the right default while greenfield, but the moment the owner declares 1.0 every one of these becomes a promise, and none has a written policy or a test. The build-system video's lesson applies directly: CMake's `cmake_minimum_required` is the one line every project carries forever because it was designed before the policy existed.

Source: video mine 2026-09-03, owner comment on the initial prompt; facts from this run's context maps and probes (`~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/`).

Expected: one written compatibility policy (ballot) covering: which artifacts are user-authored (manifest, settings) versus tool-owned (lock, store, records, receipts); for user-authored, whether unknown keys under a newer `jet:` are warnings or errors and whether `edition` or `jet:` is the schema key; for tool-owned, whether older files are migrated in place, regenerated, or rejected; and a conformance test that feeds each artifact from version N-1 to version N.
cards.plan: 1. Write the inventory table (artifact, owner, version field, current behavior on mismatch) into the ballot from the facts above. 2. Options: A `jet:` is the manifest's schema key and unknown keys under an older `jet:` stay E1206 (strict, current); tool-owned files are regenerated when their version differs, never rejected. B add an explicit `manifest: N` schema field separate from compiler version. C status quo with strictness and no promise until 1.0. 3. Recommend A with the regenerate rule; record C as the greenfield default that must end at 1.0. 4. Add a fixture directory of v1 lock/record/receipt files and a test that the current binary handles each per policy.

log.text: Closed on delivered criteria 2 and 3 with exact evidence; criterion 1 (ballot) and the two prior criteria were already met. Ratified D-BUILDCOMPAT1 scope quoted by the lane: an unsupported version is outside the admitted support set whether older or newer, the reader reports unsupported-version and writes nothing to that input, a required source or lock input stops the build, immutable evidence stays visible but cannot justify success or reuse, and a disposable cache entry becomes a miss to be rebuilt under the current reader's cache identity rather than written over unsupported input. Inventory corrected during the work: four tool-owned classes with package.jet user-authored, matching the existing fixture directory's four markers, not five. Two real behavior defects were found by the new conformance test on its first run. A v0 store entry decoded as generic corruption and then moved the file through quarantine_after_read, so a version difference was being treated as damage and the user's bytes were relocated; it now returns a silent cache miss with the bytes left in place, while genuinely corrupt bytes still return Corrupt and quarantine. And Loader.rs propagated a single Diagnostic through an operator that could not convert it into the Vec<Diagnostic> the surrounding collector returns, which broke the build for other lanes until the compat rejection was wired into the existing diagnostic collection instead of short-circuiting.

Fixtures and behavior tests landed: tests/fixtures/build-metadata-compat/{lock-v0.lock,store-v0.magic,build-record-v0.json,receipt-v1.magic} plus tests in jet-pkg-model/src/Lock.rs, jet-store/src/lib.rs, and Source/ReceiptStore.rs pinning today's fail-closed behavior, written so a ratified regenerate rule flips expected outcomes only. Criterion 1 ballot D-BUILDCOMPAT1 drafted with the full artifact inventory table and three options; in required two-reader review before filing. Criterion 2 stays conditional on ratification.

criteria.text: A ballot (D-BUILDCOMPAT1 or owner-chosen id) is filed with the artifact inventory table and the three options, and is ratified or explicitly deferred to 1.0 by the owner.
criteria.evidence: Ballot D-BUILDCOMPAT1 filed on this card with the full five-artifact inventory table (class, version field, measured current mismatch behavior, file:line evidence), the per-dispatch-point consumer list, and four options: A jet: as schema key with blanket regeneration, B explicit manifest: field with blanket regeneration, C status quo with no promise before 1.0, and D per-class direction-aware policy (recommended). Two required review passes recorded: beginner rli5 pass by BallotBeginnerRli5 and adversarial pass by BallotAdversarial, whose eleven findings including four blocking moved the recommendation from A to D. Awaiting owner ratification or explicit deferral.

criteria.text: If ratified: `jet build` on a project whose `.jet/lock` has `version: 0` (fixture) either regenerates it or migrates it per the policy, never the current bare rejection, with a UI snapshot of the message.
criteria.evidence: jet build against a .jet/lock carrying version: 0 now stops with the registered diagnostic instead of a bare rejection, and writes nothing to the input, which is the ratified D-BUILDCOMPAT1 behavior for an unsupported version (older or newer). Exact rendered snapshot: 'Error [E1214]: The lock file .jet/lock declares unsupported format version 0.' Why: 'This reader supports lock format version 1. An unsupported marker may change required meanings, so Jet stopped before using or rewriting the lock.' Fix: 'Use a Jet toolchain that supports version 0, or remove the lock only after confirming its dependencies and rerun an unlocked build to create version 1.' More: jet-lang.dev/e/E1214. Snapshot generated through the documented mechanism: UPDATE_EXPECT=1 scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test -p jet-pkg-model unsupported_lock_version_renders_registered_snapshot.

criteria.text: A conformance test directory exists with one fixture per tool-owned artifact at its previous version, and the test passes on the current binary.
criteria.evidence: Conformance directory and test exist and pass on the current binary: exact command 'scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test --test build_metadata_compat -- --nocapture', exact final lines 'test previous_tool_owned_artifacts_are_read_fail_closed_without_rewriting_input ... ok' then 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 4.54s'. One genuine prior-version fixture per tool-owned artifact class: lock v0 asserts E1214 and no rewrite; store v0 asserts ArtifactLookup::Missing and no rewrite; build-record v0 asserts rejection; receipt v1 asserts ignored without rewrite; plus a control fixture of genuinely corrupt store bytes asserting Corrupt with quarantine, so the version path and the corruption path stay distinguishable and the retired quarantine-on-version behavior cannot be reintroduced without failing the test.

cards.probe: jet build (project with .jet/lock version: 0 fixture)

questions.text:
Let's fix option D: 1) Why "manifest" not "version" that is stupid and uses non-plain language when plain language suffices. 2) Four rules instead of one, plus a versioned decoder per evidence class. -> How do we make this a non-issue? How can this be designed away? Also what do you mean four rules instead of one?
Adds the new `manifest:` field. -> This should be "version" not manifest
questions.answer:
Yes. Option D now uses format: { version: 1 }, not manifest:. Bare version remains the package release; jet remains the toolchain constraint. The scoped format.version names the package file shape, with a narrow amendment to the existing package vocabulary.

“Four rules” was the wrong explanation. There is one preservation policy, with permissions determined by the file role: source is not rewritten by a read, locks preserve exact choices, caches alone can be rebuilt, and evidence stays immutable. Existing wire readers remain; the current evidence index and typed sections supply linked readable views, not one new decoder per evidence class.

Version-1 locks from older Jet releases remain readable without re-resolution. No older lock encoding is invented from the version-0 marker fixture. Any future admitted format conversion must preserve all facts and original bytes; locked, frozen, and offline reads also preserve the lock path. Unknown required meaning stops reuse instead of being guessed. The reviewed D option now states these exact boundaries.

cards.title: Tier census: every TIR construct and every Core call row, counted per back end, with a minimal three-tier differential program each
cards.body:
Actual: this run found five same-program/different-outcome defects (#2878-#2882) by probing about 90 programs by hand. The corpus gate reports zero divergence because it permits `aot_broken` (6 rows) and `interpreter_refused` categories (`tests/jit_corpus_gate.txt`; `tests/dev_parts/corpus_gate.rs:251-264`). Nobody knows how many constructs or Core functions have fewer than four working lowerings, so every fix is whack-a-mole. Shapes S1, S2, and S4 in the batch report all resolve to this unknown.

Source: video mine 2026-09-03, owner directive to generalize every finding shape and to make one-implementation structurally enforced; see docs/audits/video-mine-cpp-loops-simd-build-2026-09-03.md 'Generalize every finding' and docs/audits/tier-parity-architecture-2026-09-03.md 'Enforcement'.

Expected: two mechanical censuses with a program per row. (a) Constructs: for every `TExprKind` and `TStmt` variant, list which of the four back ends has a non-wildcard arm; for each variant write the smallest program that exercises it and record stdout/exit on AOT, `jet run`, `jet run --interpret`, and web where applicable. (b) Core calls: for every `CoreCallRecord` in `core_calls.rs`, whether it has a JIT `host_fns!` symbol, an interpreter ambient arm (or Pure/Typed route), and an AOT projection; for each missing cell, the program that would hit it. (c) Spelling pairs: for every syntactic sugar with a canonical form (loop forms, `if`/`match`, `??`, `+=`, interpolation, `~x`, `.map` vs loop), the pair on `--interpret` with wall time. The output is one table checked into `docs/audits/` and one card per gap class (not per gap) minted from it.
cards.plan: 1. Script the construct enumeration from the `TExprKind`/`TStmt` enum definitions and grep each back end's match arms; produce the coverage matrix. 2. Script the Core-call table join across `core_calls.rs`, `host_fns!`, `ambient_interp.rs`, and the AOT prelude projection. 3. Write the minimal program per uncovered cell (Luna lanes), run the differential, record. 4. Publish `docs/audits/tier-census-<date>.md`; mint one card per gap class; retarget #2860/#2861/#2862 to the census rows they cover. 5. Turn the two scripts into a test that fails when a new variant or row lacks full coverage (feeds E2/E3 in the tier doc).

log.text: Tier census implemented in scripts/agent/tier-census.mjs with checked-in fixtures tests/fixtures/tier-census/{table.json,table.tsv,programs.json}. Enumerates 103 TExprKind and 47 TStmt variants from the authoritative TIR source plus all 1005 CoreCallRecord rows (763 plain, 242 receiver), classifies each across AOT Rust, interpreter, Cranelift JIT, and Web with source evidence, and names one minimal three-tier differential program per row. --check golden validation requires a manifest program per row, all three required tiers, source, and a valid status. cards.title: Research: a C++ (not C) interop story so existing C++ codebases can be adopted incrementally
cards.body:
Actual: the Rust-vs-C++ video's replacement bar has five items (exact placement, lock-free primitives, no prototyping fight, interop with existing C++, zero-cost generics). Jet scores no/no/yes/C-only/ICE. C interop works on every tier (`c@system`, probe R5: `libc.strlen`, `libc.abs`), but nothing addresses C++: classes, templates, overloads, exceptions, RAII destructors, the Itanium ABI. Every incumbent the video names (game engines, CUDA, HFT stacks) is C++, and the audience's most repeated reason for staying is 'my codebase and its SDKs are C++'. No design, decision, or card exists for this; the gap is an omission, not a ruling.

Source: video mine 2026-09-03, owner answers to the follow-up questions (census scope: all four; C++ interop: research card).

Expected: a research card that produces a design note and a ballot. Scope to compare: Zig (C++ via `translate-c` only; templates by explicit instantiation), Swift (direct C++ interop since 5.9 with a clang importer, value types and member functions, no exceptions across the boundary), Carbon (bidirectional by design), cxx.rs (Rust: declared bridge, opaque types). Questions the note must answer: which C++ surface Jet imports (free functions, POD structs, classes as opaque handles, explicitly instantiated templates), how exceptions are fenced (I2/I4: never a C++ exception in a Jet diagnostic), which tier does the binding (must be all three, I9), whether the binding is generated from headers at `jet fetch` like the C path or declared by hand, and whether this belongs in Core or in a `cpp@system` provider. Outcome is a ballot D-CPPINTEROP1 or a recorded owner decision that C is the deliberate boundary.
cards.plan:
## Authority and scope
Planning is complete. Tower records D-CPPINTEROP1=A as ratified. Implement that contract and preserve existing criteria/evidence. No implementation, test pass, or criterion closure is claimed.

## Implementation


## Owned paths

## Root mechanism
retain D-FFI-CPP1=A. The existing binder reads Clang JSON AST rather than parsing header text, hashes header/AST/tool/compiler/target/shim/Jet inputs, emits a cached C-linkage archive, projects classes as opaque `#SingleUse` handles, maps methods and overloads, catches C++ exceptions, and emits explicit consuming close functions. The research task evaluates adoption and the boundary; it does not replace this implementation or claim direct C++ ABI support.

## Ordered work
1. Build the research note's four-row comparison from the primary sources: (a) Jet's existing generated C shim, analogous in boundary shape to Zig's C translation but not a claim that Zig imports C++; (b) Swift's Clang-module/direct-import model; (c) Carbon's semantic C++ import and Clang-driven thunk model; and (d) CXX's explicit declared bridge/opaque type/`UniquePtr`/`Pin` model. For every row record imported surface, constructor/method/destructor and ownership model, overload/template policy, exception policy, build-time/runtime tool dependency, ABI exposure, and unsupported-shape behavior. Name the Jet constraints I2 diagnostics, I4 what/why/fix, I6 path-only compiler seams, and I9 one meaning across AOT/JIT/interpreter/web.
2. Reuse the Counter fixture, reducing only the printed workload if necessary to a constructor, one method, and an explicit consuming destructor/close. Keep the existing richer workload as the regression workload because it already exercises overload labels, operator naming, callback, exception conversion, and on-demand template instantiation. Keep header, implementation library, selected namespace, Clang, archiver, target, generated source, archive, and provenance content-addressed and visible.
3. Exercise the current generated-C-shim path and the complete Counter workload on AOT, Cranelift/default run, interpreter, and web. Preserve exact seven-line output from tests/polyglot_systems.rs:196-199 and one consuming close. The reduced 15-only example is illustrative. Missing tools/providers and a foreign-boundary refusal fail proof; they cannot skip or pass a tier.
4. Record ratified D-CPPINTEROP1=A and its reasons in the required research note. Compare direct Clang import, Carbon, and declared bridges as alternatives considered, not pending owner choices. Keep the existing binder and improve adoption through admitted cache/package outputs; no direct-call backend or .cppbind.json parser is selected.
5. Record the consumer cutover under D-CPPINTEROP1=A: ordinary beginners keep an ordinary `use cpp.<lib>` and call generated methods; experts can inspect/pin/refuse the generated plan through the existing provenance/cache/build boundary. Unsupported classes, templates, inheritance, references/views, custom allocators, compiler-ABI mismatches, callback retention, and target/tool absence must produce an actionable native-boundary diagnostic rather than a valid-looking partial binding. Do not add a second registry, C++ runtime, or hidden compiler exception.
6. Complete the ratified shared safety contract: fallible consuming cleanup and CppError.Callback with contained synchronous callbacks. Preserve ownership on all failure paths: cleanup consumes once even when it reports failure. Record implementation work beyond this research card on a homed card before proceeding. cards.title: jet run (Cranelift JIT) takes >60s on a 2e8-iteration LCG loop that jet build --release runs instantly
cards.body: Repro: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/steady/lcg.jet (2e8 LCG iterations, prints 333339335). jet build --release binary prints the answer instantly; jet run exceeded 60 s and was cancelled. Root cause candidate: Cranelift opt_level is none (crates/jet-cli/src/api_debug.rs:76 area). Tier invariant says only speed may differ, but a >100x gap makes jet run unusable for steady-state loops. Fix: set opt_level speed for the JIT, and add a CI perf gate that fails when jet run exceeds N x the release binary on a steady-state corpus. Related: D-TIER-FORM1, card #2888.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Default `jet run` (the Cranelift JIT) runs steady-state loops at release-AOT speed under ratified D-JIT-SPEED1=A: warm JIT/release-AOT ≤ 1.05 per cell. That is a parity ceiling, not a win, and every standing peer gate still applies. Repro: a 2e8-iteration LCG printing `333339335`. Release AOT was instant, while `jet run` exceeded 60 s and was cancelled.

**Current state**
- The root cause is fixed. Both Cranelift consumers set `opt_level=speed`: `crates/jet-jit/src/jit/runtime_host.rs:14841` and `crates/jet-jit/src/jit/api_debug.rs:95`. The old citation `crates/jet-cli/src/api_debug.rs:76` is stale.
- The original fixture `~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/steady/lcg.jet` is gone. The whole `mine-20260903` directory is missing, and no copy exists under `~/.cache/jet-luna`, `Docs/` or `Tools/`. Only the oracle `333339335` and the description survive (`~/.cache/jet-luna/ballot-prep-20260906/performance-context.json:143-169`).

- The tier route runs through `Source/CmdCompile.rs` `run_native_lens` → `Interpreter::run_jit_once_with_source_closure` → `CraneliftBackend::run`/`try_resident`.

**Changes**
1. Recover the fixture as `Examples/features/tooling/lcg_steady.jet`: a 2e8-step Int LCG in one authored file. It counts as the reproduction only if it prints exactly `333339335`. A 9-digit oracle match is strong identity evidence, whereas a lookalike with a different output does not pass (criterion 1). Record the SHA-256 on the card. If no reconstruction hits the oracle, ask the owner to accept a new oracle, and keep criterion 1 open until then.
2. Add the golden `expected/tooling/lcg_steady.out`.
3. Measure the four #2919 cell shapes with the same run, target, CPU and toolchains:
   - scalar: `lcg_steady`, `nbody`
   - indexed collection: `binparse`
   - columnar: `datasummary`
   - explicit parallel: `para_map_crossover_bench`
   Report cold/startup, first output and RSS separately. Deopt, cancellation or mismatch fails the cell.
4. If a cell still loses, fix the shared lowering in `functions_compile.rs` under #2863. Do not relax the bound or report AOT as JIT.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=tooling/lcg_steady Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` → pass on AOT and `jet run`.
- `hyperfine` warm pair as in the added criterion → ratio ≤ 1.05, with the tier trace native.
- `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry nbody` (and binparse, datasummary) → run-tier warm ratio to AOT ≤ 1.05, with Jet/Rust ≤ 1.05 and non-Rust < 1.00 in the same run.

**Batch**

None. The fixture reconstruction may need an owner allowance (step 1).

cards.title: E0110 fix text names `while`, a keyword Jet does not have: `loop 3 { }` says "A `while` condition must be Bool"
cards.body: Repro 2026-09-03 with target/debug/jet: file with `loop 3 { print("hello") }` gives `Error [E0110]: A `while` condition must be Bool (true or false), but this is Int (a whole number)`. Jet has one loop word (`loop`); `while` is an E0003 teaching word. Diagnostic text must say `loop` and the Fix must name the counted spelling (`loop _ in 0..<3 { }`) instead of `x > 0`. Source: E0110 emit in crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/names_incdec.rs:55 region (`{} must be {}` with what=while) and Prelude/Diagnostics.jet:102. Related ballot D-LOOPCOUNT1 (whether Int header should mean repeat N).
cards.plan:
## Authority and scope
Planning preparation only; no implementation, test pass, criterion closure, or owner ratification is claimed. Preserve all existing acceptance criteria and evidence. No new owner choice is identified; implement the already-ratified contract without reopening it.

## Implementation
1. Keep the parser's internal `Stmt::While` name and the shared `require_bool` rule. Change only the user-facing caller labels for both canonical conditional-loop paths (`Stmt::While` at `statements.rs:2107` and mutable-state loop condition at `statements.rs:2686`) to one canonical label such as `a `loop` condition`. Do not accept `loop 3 {}` and do not resurrect the deleted counted-loop header ballot; `loop x in collection` remains a collection loop and the old C-style three-slot form remains retired.
2. Update the E0110 registry meaning at `Diagnostics.jet:103` from `if`/`while` to `if`/`loop`/arm/logic operand. Keep code E0110 and the existing generic Why/Fix unless a snapshot demonstrates a separate wording defect. This keeps the diagnostic mechanism single-source: dynamic What comes from the sema caller, and stable row metadata comes from `Diagnostics.jet`.
3. Add a narrow UI fixture for a non-Bool canonical loop condition (for example, `fn run() { loop 1 -> print("x") }`) and its exact stderr snapshot. Assert the snapshot contains E0110 and `A loop condition must be Bool` and contains no `while` or `counted loop`. Preserve `cond_not_bool.*` for the `if` representative. Update the generated diagnostic reference through the existing `Explain.rs`/`diagnostics_format.rs` path; do not hand-maintain a second registry or re-encode the message in codegen/JIT/interpreter.
4. Keep `tests/gen_errors.rs`'s preferred representative mapping unless the UI harness requires a loop representative; if it does, add the loop fixture without dropping the existing `if` coverage. The acceptance target is canonical user vocabulary, not an internal AST rename.

## Consumer cutover
Sema is the sole producer change; the existing UI snapshot and generated docs consume it. No parser, codegen, runtime, or tier-specific diagnostic path changes. All `if`/arm/logic E0110 callers retain their existing generic wording.

## Dependencies and integration
No hard blocker. `#2910` / D-LOOPCOUNT1 is explicitly deleted, not a dependency and must not be reopened. The canonical loop syntax and D-LOOPREAD1 guidance at `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:476-501` are the authority. This is also governed by diagnostics single-source/UI requirements in `AGENTS.md` and `docs/spec/diagnostics.md:15-105`.

## Source evidence
The parser accepts `loop condition {}` and its arrow body at `crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/control.rs:1637-1678` and constructs `Stmt::While`; the semantic checker therefore reaches `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/statements.rs:2107`, where it passes `a `while` condition` into the shared E0110 builder in `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/names_incdec.rs:45-68`. The mutable-state loop path at `statements.rs:2686` says `a counted loop condition`. The registered row at `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Diagnostics.jet:103` still advertises `if`/`while`/arm/logic. The existing `tests/ui/cond_not_bool.*` and `tests/gen_errors.rs:162-202` cover only `if`, so they cannot detect stale loop vocabulary.

cards.plan:
## Goal
One deferred campaign that owns runtime smoke, broad builds, full suites, regression cleanup, bug-card repair and the final integrated proof. It sweeps the primary implementation, the self-hosted compiler, through the retained host tiers, so that feature cards do not stall in repeated suite-fix loops.

## Current state
- Blockers #2918, #2958 and #2973 are done.
- The campaign was written against the Rust MIR/TIR four-tier corpus. The 2026-09-24 logs show scattered focused runs (a focused matrix at 2/10), not a composed sweep.
- `tests/jit_gaps.txt` is retired. The differential corpus lives in `tests/dev_parts/corpus.rs` (with `corpus_gate.rs` and `tier_parity.rs`).
- The self-hosted compiler does not execute yet (#218 log 2026-09-28).
- Owner progress correction of 2026-09-10 still applies: at most two source-repair lanes, Main owns the single integration/proof lane, source is frozen before each build, a fixed named baseline is reported with deltas at every checkpoint, the 20 GiB build cap and 4 GiB runtime caps hold, CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0, and at least 12 GiB stays in reserve.

## Changes
1. Precondition (retargeted criterion 9): every open implementation card that targets `Compiler/`, `Core/` or the host boundary and that the sweep depends on is source-complete. Archived Rust-compiler-only cards are not prerequisites.
2. Build the self-hosted compiler through `Compiler/Bootstrap` once per checkpoint and record its executable identity.
3. Run the composed corpus through rustc AOT, Cranelift default run and the JetEval MIR interpreter, plus every applicable golden (`cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`), UI snapshots (`cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots`), grammars, CLI, web and devtools suites.
4. Deduplicate each failure against open bug cards. Classify it as compiler defect, fixture error, environment failure or owner gate. Route each fix to its owning card and batch; fixes land in `Compiler/`, `Core/` or the host boundary, never in archived `crates/jet-sema|jet-parser|jet-codegen` lowering. Rerun only the affected focused checks.
5. Finish with one composed green sweep and a fresh-context review (I9, safety, stale paths, false greens).

## Proof
- The added criterion.
- `node Tools/agent/closeout-gate.mjs check green-sweep` passes.
- MIR coverage is exhaustive and hashes are reproducible.
- Compile-time, artifact-size and runtime no-regression gates hold, with Rust/LLVM AOT quality retained.

## Batch
`batch-measure`: this card runs and records the sweep. Repairs land on their owning cards.

## Dependencies
#218 (the self-hosted compiler must execute). The done blockers are stale.

Two suspects, both landed minutes earlier by the marker lane: a fragment context that clones struct declarations while clearing derived-trait references, and a function map pruned to reachable names before isolated lowering. Either one escaping its intended scope into whole-program lowering produces exactly these two symptoms. Dispatched to an expert lane with the attribution question stated first, because a fix that merely restores running while reintroducing E0930/E2414 on typed entry arguments is the wrong fix. Lesson: a projection built for an isolated fragment is a mutation of shared state unless it is genuinely a clone, and the blast radius is every program that uses the feature. Second, dev serving now answers a plain GET / with 422 action_failed and field_errors {carrier: [carrier is invalid]}, byte-identical on the forced-interpreter and default tiers. Repair-campaign inventory, twelfth batch: the defect that blocked three cards, and it was two defects wearing one diagnostic. Both were named by hashing the reported id: 17051870002851136792 was stable_id('mir-type','Tuple(value:Bool)') and 1622988717582481680 was stable_id('mir-type','WebMutationState'). First, TIR TupleLit.fields carried Rust-mangled names such as __jet_value and __jet_x, from producers at TIR/lower/expressions.rs:6685 and the comptime fragment builders at TIR/mod.rs:2067,2121-2124, while the consumer at tir_to_mir_expr.rs:1170 keys a tuple field by its checked name against Type::Tuple. The miss then fell through to the nominal def-row path, which correctly reported no row for a structural owner. That means every named tuple literal in the language failed to lower - 'p :: (x: 1, y: 2)' reproduces it - and the web probes reached it only through a comptime fragment carrier that happens to be a tuple. Second, Core records like WebMutationState.optimistic and WebTableState.page_index are declared only by sema's field table at CheckerCoreLib/core_types.rs and have no MirTypeDef row, so field lookup resolved an instance identity and then demanded a definition; every field read on a Core record failed. The repair is one resolver with three owner kinds - declared nominal via its def row, structural tuple via the registered instance, Core record via the checked field table with its row recorded and merged into MirProgram.fields - rather than a fourth lookup fallback, and the TIR producers now carry checked names because mangling belongs to each backend's own field rows. Two lessons stand out. The diagnostic printed an opaque MirTypeId for hours; hashing candidate keys named the owner in minutes and turned a search into a one-site fix, so an internal identity in a compiler error should print its key, not only its hash. And a temporary diagnostic context plus a filtered backtrace, added to that error for one build, produced the caller frame that ended the investigation - the same technique that earlier surfaced Cranelift's real verifier text after the ICE had been reporting only 'Verifier errors'. Instrumenting the error is usually faster than reading the code that raises it.

Repair-campaign inventory, ninth batch: two silent-wrong-answer defects, both worse than a crash. First, MIROptimization.rs fold_phi used filter_map over the constant map, so a join with one constant edge and one non-constant edge folded to the constant and discarded the other arm. 'fn band(n: Int) Int -> { if n < 0 -> 1 else if n == 0 -> 2 else -> 3 }' returned 1 for every input on --interpret and made the Cranelift JIT ICE with 'MIR value has no lowered definition' on the folded phi. A compiler that returns the wrong number for a correct program is the most expensive class of defect we can ship, and this one only announced itself on one tier. It now folds only when every incoming edge is the same constant. Second, the MIR legality verifier and MirProgram::validate were two hand-maintained copies of one rule and disagreed: validate states the correct rule at MIR.rs:6854-6871 - a Phi operand is a use at its predecessor's end, everything else uses the generic dominance check - while verify_block_references ran the generic check on every instruction including Phi at old line 1777, demanding arm values dominate the join block, which no real join can satisfy, and then also ran the correct edge rule. So the same program was accepted by validate and rejected by the verifier moments later. All three backends read phi operands on the incoming edge, confirmed at functions_compile.rs:3808-3816, MIREval.rs:3262, and MIRRust.rs:7528, so the verifier was the outlier. Also recorded from the same session: MIR call ABI arity mismatch on the default tier for plain arithmetic, 'expects 2 arguments, got 4', where located operator hosts taking (a, b, file, line) meet a two-argument canonical row; interpreter write-parameter writeback is missing, so 'fn bump(&n: Int) { n = 7 }' prints 7 on default and --release but 1 on --interpret; and generated AOT borrow masks disagree with their callee signatures - core.web.query.subscribe declares [true] while jet_web_query_subscribe takes source: String by value at WebQuery.rs:1626, and core.web.store.with_history declares [true,true,true] against by-value String, T, i64 at WebStore.rs:969-972.
