Milestone, second working-binary session: a local binding compiles and prints on all three execution tiers. 'fn run() { x :: 3; print(x) }' now prints exactly 3 on default jet run (Cranelift JIT), on --interpret, and on --release (AOT through rustc), from one program with one meaning. Getting there took five distinct defects, each a different mechanism, all of which presented as 'print is broken'. First, MIR legality correctly rejected every immutable let because its place row was created with access Read and then written; the fix gives each local one place row per access mode instead of overwriting a single row with whatever access the last use requested. Second, the JIT keyed stack slots by place id, so once a local legitimately had several rows the write and the read got different slots and the read returned uninitialized stack: that, not Display, produced the 93825225728072 output for print(3) and the empty output for print of a string, and it is also the likely explanation for the 'orders' value another lane saw from a Web query print, which means the golden that lane corrected should be re-verified. Third, MIR Print carried a raw typed value while the canonical row is jet_term_write_stdout_line(text: &str, flush), so AOT emitted a &i64 and the JIT read the integer as a string handle; Print now lowers a non-String payload through the single Display route that string interpolation already used. Fourth, that Display route existed only on AOT: the JIT had no jet_fmt_display host and the interpreter's runtime adapter had a hand-maintained list of pure-forwardable Core namespaces that omitted core.text.fmt, so every fmt call fell through to an unsupported branch. Fifth, a program whose only I/O is print recorded no Core usage and therefore stayed in RuntimeLayer::Core, where MIRRust types String as &'static str and panics that interpolation requires an allocation layer, so string interpolation had never worked on --release at all. Two lessons outrank the fixes. The Cranelift ICE reported only 'Compilation error: Verifier errors' and discarded the backend's own per-instruction explanation; once a checked wrapper surfaced the real text, 'invalid reference to entry block block0' made a night-long mystery into a single run, and the cause was that canonical MIR sorts blocks by id so the entry block was not first while the JIT laid blocks out in list order. And the reason five defects in the most basic operation in the language survived a full night of parallel work is that the tier smoke program was print of a string literal with no variables, no arithmetic, and no branches: it could not fail.

Repair-campaign inventory, eighth batch. A total regression and its root cause, found and diagnosed inside the campaign. Symptom: any local binding failed to compile on all three tiers. 'fn run() { x :: 3; print(x) }' ICEd with 'canonical MIR optimization failed: MIR pass legality-verification rejected the program: function ... writes through invalid place ... at 13..14' on default jet run, --interpret, and --release, while a binding-free program still ran correctly on all three. Root cause, from MIROptimization.rs:3791-3798: an invalid place is a WritePlace whose target MirPlace row carries access == Read. An immutable let creates its place row with access Read at mir.rs:4540, then the let write emits WritePlace into that row at tir_to_mir_stmt.rs:77-84. Compounding it, place_for_local at mir.rs:5045 overwrites a local's single place row with whatever access the last use requested, so any later read downgrades an already-initialized or assigned local back to Read. The durable lesson is about detection, not the bug: this survived a night of parallel work because the tier smoke program was 'fn run() { print("...") }' with no variables in it, so every tier check passed while the language could not compile a variable. A smoke program that does not bind, branch, or call with a value proves almost nothing; the suite also had no test asserting that a local binding compiles. Two further defects recorded in the same pass. Multiline typed literals hit 'E0003 Expected } to close typed literal, found ;': a synthetic statement terminator is inserted inside an incomplete expression, reproduced in examples/features/basics/comprehension_forms.jet and tests/compiled_workloads/adapters/jet/cli-archive-filter.jet, and suspected across a large share of 51 census probe failures. And core.text.fmt.display was implemented on AOT only, so string interpolation of a computed value ICEd as unregistered on the Cranelift JIT and E0956 on the interpreter, which is the same one-tier-only implementation pattern as the missing web Core routes.

Repair-campaign inventory, seventh batch. Three defects found while proving tier parity, all in the default execution path. First and most serious: MIR Print lowering passes a raw Int to jet_jit_term_write_stdout_line, which unconditionally clones a heap string handle, so the JIT reinterprets an integer as a handle. Printing the integer 1 emitted the unrelated live string 'orders'. That is type confusion in the tier every user hits first, not a formatting bug, and any program printing an integer on jet run can surface unrelated heap contents. A second lane independently hit print(0) failing on AOT and worked around it by writing print("0"), so the primitive display path is suspect on more than one tier. It survived because no test asserted printed bytes for a non-String primitive; an exit-status test passes while the tier prints unrelated memory. Second: the default Cranelift JIT cannot compile an ordinary branch. A file whose body is only 'if true { print(...) }' exits 101 with 'Cranelift cannot execute MIR function: Compilation error: Verifier errors' while --interpret and --release both exit 0 with correct output. It was first misattributed to a #DebugOnly scope regression; the attribute-free if reproduces it, so Jet is emitting invalid IR for basic control flow. The ICE also discarded Cranelift's per-instruction verifier text, so the backend's own explanation was invisible until a lane routed every define_function site through a checked wrapper. Third: parser starts_expr at crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Expressions/providers.rs:162-179 included KwTrue and omitted KwFalse, so '?? return false' failed with E0003 at the literal while '?? return true' would have parsed. One missing token in a hand-maintained duplicate of the grammar's own knowledge, presenting as a bizarre return-specific rejection. Also recorded: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/DataPlan.rs classify_data_call and DataPlanBuilder are an abandoned typed-plan migration with zero consumers, while infer_core_call, lower/core_calls.rs, and DataPipeline.rs carry the live legacy Table/Series/LazyFrame typing. Someone stopped a replacement midway and left both shapes on disk. The recurring lesson across all four is the same: every one is a fact duplicated in two places where nothing forces the copies to agree.

Repair-campaign inventory, sixth batch: a surface-reachability divergence between the Core export table and the sema checker's module-item list, found while proving demand-driven Arrow inclusion. crates/jet-foundation/src/CoreModuleExports.rs exports items that crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/module_items.rs does not list, and vice versa, which means a module can be exported and still unnameable, or listed in the checker while absent from exports. Member-level divergences: core.args is missing decode and merge; core.email is missing all twenty exported members; core.mem is missing AllocError, Pin, Ptr, address_of, from_addr, pin, volatile_read, and volatile_write; core.web is missing storage; core.web.forms is missing typed_set_async_validator; core.web.query is missing mutation_signal and state_signal. In the other direction the checker lists items the export table does not: WrappedVaultKey, KeyUnlock, and KeyWrapError under core.crypto; CBORError and CBORErrorKind under core.encoding.cbor; XMLError and XMLReason under core.encoding.xml; JobQueueState and JobQueueDeliveryPolicy under core.jobs; eight TUI types under core.tui; and under core.data the whole transform family table, rows, series, values, missing_count, lazy, lazy_filter, lazy_sort_by, collect, plan, filter, sort_by, group_count, group_sum, and group_mean. The durable lesson is that these two tables encode the same fact - what the standard library exposes - in two places with no census tying them together, which is the same one-fact-two-places pattern behind most of tonight's defects; a census that fails closed on any divergence would have caught every item above the day it landed.

Milestone: all three execution tiers run for the first time tonight, with one meaning across them. On a freshly built binary, jet run (Cranelift JIT), jet run --interpret, and jet run --release (AOT through rustc) each print exactly 'first build of the night' and exit 0 for the same two-line program, and lane-check.sh reports CHECK OK for the whole workspace. The interpreter tier is additionally proven on a value-returning program printing 42. Getting AOT there took two more fixes beyond the per-tier ICEs: a missing-symbol family and an extraction family. Missing symbols were real omissions rather than emit bugs - Prelude/Core/FieldError.rs was not in CORELIB_KERNEL_PARTS so the canonical jet_field_error_kernel_show never reached the flattened jet_std scope; derive(Clone) on the Arc/Rc-backed query carriers DataQueryPlan, DataQueryRows, DataQueryOperation, DataQuerySource, and DataQuery imposed a false T: Clone bound and now have unconstrained manual impls; JetParallelReceipt::new omitted the newly added partial_result_discarded field, which must initialize false because record_failure, record_cancellation, and finish are the paths that set it true; the AOT full-closure path bypassed package-aware edition emission so __JET_PACKAGE_EDITION was never defined; and a plain run emitted the test-harness prologue because its artifact was kind=Coverage with no selected tests, so seven jet_test_* helpers and JetTestOutcome were referenced by a program that has no tests. The extraction family was the durable one: the generated program flattens many Prelude sources into one Rust module, so every private helper and import shares one namespace, which produced duplicate use statements for PhantomData, Ordering, AtomicBool, and AtomicU64, a hex_digit collision between Devtools.rs and TypedText.rs, jet_foundation:: paths surviving into a crate that cannot see that dependency, pub(super) items at the wrong rewrite depth, and unreachable quote_json and RuntimeDiagnosticCore. That is now deduplicated by binding name in the assembly rather than patched per instance. Two further defects were fixed on the way: canonical Err needed its single Rust spelling in Context::root_prelude_rust_type_name, and generated symbol mangling only sanitized dots, so canonical identities carrying :: and / produced invalid Rust identifiers - mangling is now injective with distinct escapes and a pairwise collision test.

Repair-campaign inventory, fifth batch, from the first working-binary session. Compile is green workspace-wide (lane-check.sh CHECK OK) and the Cranelift JIT tier now runs a program end to end for the first time tonight: jet run on a print program emits 'first build of the night'. Getting there required five shared-path fixes plus three per-tier fixes, and every one was an identity or backend-agreement defect rather than a logic bug, which is the signature of a wave that never executed as it landed. The shared path had module identity derived two ways (loader alias or file stem hashed into MirFunction.module_id at TIR lowering, versus the name ledger's checked package::path identity that the verifier's module registry was built from), the same defect again for row-embedded types resolved by a new RowTypeCanonicalizer, a FunctionRegistry by_name fallback for alias-qualified call names, a verify_core_call invariant that still encoded pre-cutover coupling before the table gained 28 pure+Ambient rows and 7 sema-only receiver rows, and an artifact planner that implemented only the Output-const entry convention while never recording the zero-arg run convention every tier now reads. Per tier: the JIT assumed every Prelude host call returns a value, so a zero-return Unit host like jet_term_write_stdout_line produced 'MIR Prelude call returned no value'; it also needed a canonical Ok(()) result handle for fallible Unit returns. The interpreter held an ACTIVE_CONTEXT RefCell borrow across the callback at seven dispatch sites, and behind that panic sat a real routing defect: eval_core_call_binding unconditionally took the comptime non-ambient door, so runtime print was checked as a Tier-2 comptime effect demanding an #Impure gate. AOT could not resolve the Err carrier's Rust spelling, and behind that a generated symbol carried :: and / separators straight into a Rust identifier because generated_path only sanitized dots. Two new defects were found in passing and are not yet fixed: a sema ICE at crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/fallible.rs:1074 'non-result fallback cannot expose err' reproduced by a program using values.get(0) ?? 0, and 17 failing tests in crates/jet-parser's library suite. Also recorded as a design question rather than a bug: the checked identity for a single-file program embeds the absolute source path, which reaches generated Rust symbol names and would make artifacts non-reproducible across machines.

cards.body: Correction (2026-09-03 23:5x): the first version of this card blamed the ratified layout-fact feature for an ICE on `jet build examples/features/comptime/layout_facts.jet`. Re-probing showed `jet build` ICEs for EVERY program in the current working tree, including `T1_hello.jet` and the L6 iterator loop that built cleanly this morning (loops/results.md rows L6/T1). rustc on the generated file reports `__jet___add_at/__sub_at/__mul_at/__div_at is not a member of trait __jet_Add/...` (E0407) and four E0637 lifetime errors in the prelude. The tree is HEAD 4df728d30 plus 633 uncommitted files (+58k/-19k) touching crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/emit/*, so the breakage belongs to that in-flight change, not to layout facts. What still stands: `jet run` and `jet run --interpret` print the c-layout row (`c:x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu:8:8:0:0:c:count`). Expected: rebuild the compiler at a clean HEAD (or after the in-flight change lands) and run the three-tier probe; close this card if AOT matches, or re-file with the real rustc error if it does not. Source: D-PLACE1 rework probes, ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/place/ and loops/build/L8_arrow_break.rs.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Close the attribution question. The 2026-09-03 `jet build` ICE on `layout_facts` came from an in-flight dirty tree, not from the ratified layout-fact feature. Prove this with a three-tier run on the current, clean-source binary.

## Current state
- The 2026-09-03 dirty tree (HEAD 4df728d30 plus 633 uncommitted files touching `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/emit/*`) made `jet build` fail for every program, including T1 hello and L6. The rustc errors were E0407 (`__jet___add_at` is not a member of `__jet_Add`) and E0637. That tree no longer exists.
- The example and its golden exist: `Examples/features/comptime/layout_facts.jet` and `Examples/features/expected/comptime/layout_facts.out`.
- `tests/jit_corpus_gate.txt:184` lists `comptime/layout_facts` under `resident_jit`, so the three-tier corpus gate already covers it. Criterion 2 is effectively met.
- The 2026-09-21 Tower log found no live layout-facts ICE, only a stale rustc log. #2921 and #2887, the layout owners, are done.

## Changes
No code change is planned. This is evidence only.
1. Build the current binary once in the shared batch pass and record its path and SHA (`Tools/agent/jet-env which jet`).
2. For `comptime/layout_facts`, a T1 hello and the L6 iterator loop, run `jet build` then the binary, then `jet run`, then `jet run --interpret`. Record exit, stdout and stderr under `~/.cache/jet-luna/2920/`.
3. Route the result:
   - All pass: close as dirty-tree attribution, keeping the existing corpus row.
   - Only layout fails: file a new layout-fact folding defect with the evidence. Do not reopen #2921 or #2887; they are done.
   - Every program fails on AOT: file an emitter defect naming the generated-Rust path and the rejected item.

No layout implementation, syntax change or spec edit lands on this card. The stale `examples/` and `scripts/agent` paths in the old plan become `Examples/` and `Tools/agent`.

## Proof
- `JET_THREE_WAY_STEM=comptime/layout_facts cargo test --test dev_corpus cranelift_three_way_differential_battery`: ok.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=comptime/layout_facts cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: ok.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet build Examples/features/comptime/layout_facts.jet`, then run the produced binary: exit 0 and stdout byte-equal to `layout_facts.out`.

## Batch
`batch-measure`: this is a run-only verification with no code change.

## Dependencies
None. The original dirty tree is gone, so no clean-worktree reconstruction is needed.

cards.title: A plain @-binding cannot read the ratified layout fact: @size :: Ring.@layout.size is E0956 'unbound Ring' on every tier, and the Fix says use jet build while running jet build
cards.body: Actual (2026-09-03, live probe): `#Layout(c) struct Ring { slots: [Int#1024]; head: Int; tail: Int }` then top-level `@ring_size :: Ring.@layout.size` -> E0956 "unbound Ring isn't supported by the current evaluator yet", Fix: "use jet build for the full evaluator" - identical on jet build, jet run, and --interpret, so the fix text is wrong on the tier it names. Inside `fn run`, `size :: Ring.@layout.size` is E0302 (compile-time only) whose Fix says "move the read into an @ binding", which then fails as above. The only working spelling is a `::` binding inside a `derive T.X { }` body (the shipped example). Expected: the documented fact (`T.@layout` size/alignment/stride, D-LAYOUT-FACTS1=B, spec syntax-decisions.md:2773-2783) is readable from an ordinary @-binding in any file; E0956 never tells a jet build user to run jet build; the E0302 fix shows the exact spelling. Source: D-PLACE1 rework probe, ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/place/p1_layout.jet.
cards.plan:
## Authority and scope
Planning preparation only; no implementation, test pass, criterion closure, or owner ratification is claimed. Preserve all existing acceptance criteria and evidence. No new owner choice is identified; implement the already-ratified contract without reopening it.

## Implementation
1. Extend only `Comptime::Reflect::fact_read_value_with_registry` (`Reflect.rs:1773-1901`) for the exact direct type projections `T.@layout`, `T.@name`, and `T.@fields`. Resolve the `Expr::Ident` type subject with the existing `reflect_type_value_with_target_and_graph_and_facts`/struct TypeInfo builder (the same path used by `.reflect()`), using the current `build_facts.target_triple`, fact registry, item graph, and checked source facts. Return the requested TypeInfo projection. Do not create a second layout/name/fields model, aliases, or a runtime reflection object.
2. Leave the outer field-path fold unchanged: once `T.@layout` is materialized, existing traversal folds `.size`, `.alignment`, and other supported fields. Preserve target-aware optional bytes and E0959 behavior for layouts without Jet-owned physical bytes; do not turn unavailable byte facts into fake zero values.
3. Preserve `CheckerInfer::fold_fact_read`'s intentional `None` behavior for `Layout`/`Name`/`Fields` when sema is already handling a TypeInfo projection (`expr.rs:793-896,1144-1208`). The runtime prohibition remains: a local `size :: Ring.@layout.size` must report compile-time-only E0302; only an `@` binding/comptime block may materialize the value.
4. Keep the early-evaluation path canonical. `eval_comptime_items` must pass the same registry/target/graph into the resolver before full type registration; do not special-case top-level globals or defer them to codegen. This makes a standalone top-level `@` read and a derive read two consumers of one fact mechanism.
5. Add a standalone probe/fixture defining the packet's `Ring { slots: [Int#1024]; head: Int; tail: Int }`, binding at least `@ring_size :: Ring.@layout.size` and `@ring_alignment :: Ring.@layout.alignment`, and printing them. Preserve the shipped derive fixture. Add three-tier exact output coverage (AOT/default JIT/interpreter) so a fold that works only inside derive or only in one evaluator cannot pass.
6. Repair diagnostics only where they describe the now-supported boundary. E0956's registered row at `Diagnostics.jet:575` must not tell users to use `jet build` for a construct that should fold in the canonical evaluator. Keep that fallback only for a genuinely unsupported remaining construct, and add/update its UI snapshot so the suggested command is evidence-backed. For the non-comptime E0302 path, retain the compile-time-only rule but make the Fix contain the literal spelling `@size :: Ring.@layout.size` (or the exact binding name from the fixture), not only “move into an @ binding.” Do not replace E0302 with E0956 or emit a tier-specific diagnostic.
7. Update generated diagnostic docs/snapshots through the existing registry producer and UI harness. Keep `T.@layout` exactly the ratified syntax; no new ballot is needed.

## Consumer cutover
The one changed consumer is early comptime global evaluation via `Comptime::mod.rs` and `Sema::Registration::Items`; sema projection and derive code continue to call the same resolver. Generated code receives only the folded literal/TypeInfo-derived value, never a runtime `@layout` call. AOT/JIT/interpreter all consume the same folded value. Diagnostics remain registry-backed and tier-neutral.

## Dependencies and integration
No hard blocker. `#2887` is the related layout probe/reference. `#2920` must not be treated as a blocker unless its clean run independently proves an AOT failure after this fix; its current dirty generated-code ICE is a separate attribution issue. The shared authority is D-LAYOUT-FACTS1=B and D-PLACE1 (`docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:2763-2767,2819-2829` plus the `@` binding decision at `2739-2757`).

## Source evidence
The shipped derive path in `examples/features/comptime/layout_facts.jet:1-43` and `tests/corelib_parts/derives.rs:790-843` reads `info :: T.@layout` inside a derive body and succeeds. The canonical TypeInfo builder at `crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Reflect.rs:1592-1757` already computes struct layout with target/fact context, and direct subject resolution exists at `Reflect.rs:1760-1824`. However, `Reflect.rs:1825-1901` dispatches `FactRead::Layout | Name | Fields => None` at lines 1898-1900. The early top-level `@` path is `Comptime/mod.rs:771-913` through `fold_build_facts`, reached from `Sema/Registration/Items.rs:474-590` before/around registration (`Sema/Bundle/Pipeline.rs:940-969`). Thus `@ring_size :: Ring.@layout.size` fails before registration with the observed E0956 “unbound Ring isn't supported by current evaluator yet”, while a non-comptime local read reaches `CheckerInfer/expr.rs:875-880`/`1144-1208` and correctly receives E0302 as compile-time-only. This is a missing canonical evaluator projection, not a missing compiler command.

cards.title: para_map/para_fold run 2.3x slower than serial map/fold on a 4M-item cheap kernel (S7): the explicit parallel family has no measured gate, only a fixed 64-item chunk floor
cards.body: Actual (2026-09-03, SIMD lane S7, release AOT, hyperfine medians): serial map+fold 0.01156 s; para_map+para_fold 0.02690 s, RSS 49.7 MiB vs 68.1 MiB, identical output (3999999 then 4000000000000). The spec (spec.md:2691-2701) says small inputs stay serial and points users at a crossover bench; at N=4,000,000 the input is not small and the parallel path still loses, because the kernel is bandwidth-bound and the engine's per-item cost dominates. Expected: the para_* family decides at run time from a measured sample (first chunk serial, per-item cost vs once-per-process spawn cost and bandwidth floor, go parallel only with a projected gain >= 2x), so an explicit para_map is never slower than the serial spelling by more than one clock read. The same gate is the one D-ACCEL1 proposes for automatic acceleration; build it once for both. Source: ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/mine-20260903/simd/results.md S7, s7_para.jet, s7_serial.jet.

cards.title: jet run drains all of stdin before `loop line in io.stdin().lines()` runs; AOT pulls one line per turn (tier behavior difference)
cards.body:
Actual: crates/jet-jit/src/IO.rs jet_jit_stdin_lines ("Materialize stdin lines into a string list") reads stdin.lock().lines() to EOF into a Vec before the loop body runs its first turn. AOT (crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/emit/statements.rs ~4350-4382) pulls with BufRead::lines one line per turn. Observable differences: (1) interactive read-until-sentinel loop prints nothing on jet run until stdin closes, prints each line immediately on jet build; (2) after `if line == "" { break }`, a following io.readline() sees the next unread line on AOT but EOF on jet run because the JIT already consumed it; (3) unbounded memory on jet run for a long stream. Interpreter is #2881 (E2201). Source: D-LOOPREAD1 rework 2026-09-03, evidence IO.rs:1127-1141.

Expected (owner tier invariant, D-TIER-ONEIR1=A): one lazy line-pull implementation shared by every run mode; jet run and jet build read exactly the same lines in the same order and leave stdin at the same position after break.

Proof: golden `loop line in io.stdin().lines() { if line == "" { break } print(line) }; print(io.readline())` fed "a\nb\n\nc\n" prints a, b, c on jet build, jet run, and jet run --interpret; a pty test shows the first echo before stdin closes on all three.
cards.plan:
## Authority and scope
Planning preparation only; no implementation, test pass, criterion closure, or owner ratification is claimed. Preserve all existing acceptance criteria and evidence. No new owner choice is identified; implement the already-ratified contract without reopening it.

## Implementation
1. Preserve the ratified D-TIER-ONEIR1=A contract: one lazy line-pull implementation, identical order/values, and identical stdin position after `break`. Keep `MirLoopSourceKind::LinesStdin`/`JetLoopSourceKind::LinesStdin` as the single semantic protocol and retain the existing AOT Prelude and interpreter one-line readers.
2. Inventory all references to `jet_jit_stdin_lines`. If the only uses are the definition and the host-table registration at `IO.rs:1387-1392`, delete both the Vec materializer and its stale registration; do not leave a deprecated alias. If an active legacy lowering path still emits that host symbol, cut that path over to the existing `jet_jit_loop_iter_init` + `JetLoopLineReader` cursor/source-kind route, then delete the old symbol. No route may collect all stdin before loop execution.
3. Audit the JIT/AOT/interpreter stdin handoff, not just the loop cursor. `io.readline()` after a broken loop must see the next unread line, and a loop must not prefetch beyond the current line. Route internal reads through one process-level logical stdin reader/cursor per tier (or an equivalent ownership handoff) while retaining the existing public `io.stdin().lines()` and `io.readline()` surface and `Term.rs` CR/LF trimming/IO.Read faults. Do not assume separate `BufReader`/raw-stdin objects preserve position; prove it with the sentinel stream. If making this handoff changes the public `readline` contract, stop and raise an owner ballot rather than silently changing it.
4. Keep `.lines()` lowering and MIR wire format unchanged. The consumer cutover is from any old host materializer to `LinesStdin`; generated AOT code, JIT cursor, and interpreter ambient handle must all execute one line pull per `next`, block for the first available line, and leave unread bytes after `break`.
5. Add a golden sentinel program using D-LOOPREAD1 and input `a\nb\n\nc\n`: loop prints `a`, `b`, breaks on blank, then `print(io.readline())` prints `c`. Compare exact stdout/stderr/exit for AOT build, default run, and forced interpreter. Keep `examples/features/io/stdin_filter.jet` and its existing corpus row; convert the current test that expects a default-dev JIT gap into an exact parity assertion.
6. Add a focused interactive/liveness check using a child/PTY per tier: write `a\n` without closing stdin and require `a` to appear before EOF/close; then send the blank line and `c\n`, close input, and require the post-break read to print `c`. This detects both all-input materialization and accidental prefetch/blocking. Do not rely only on the current helper that feeds all bytes and closes stdin.
7. Keep the existing shared terminal trimming and `IO.Read` fault path. Do not add a dependency, public stream type, syntax form, or tier-specific exception. Remove the stale gap manifest/acceptance only where the exact parity proof demonstrates the gap is gone; the generated corpus manifest remains source/golden-driven.

## Consumer cutover
`jet-jit::IO` legacy host registration is removed or redirected to the already-existing lazy JIT cursor. The MIR source-kind/lowering contract, AOT Prelude adapter, and interpreter ambient handle remain the consumers of one `LinesStdin` meaning. `io.readline` must share the tier's logical stdin ownership so break-position semantics are preserved; this is an internal cutover unless an implementation changes the public contract.

## Dependencies and integration
No hard blocker. D-TIER-ONEIR1=A is the ratified authority; `#2881` explains the existing interpreter boundary but is not permission to retain a JIT gap. The current `tests/dev_parts/routine.rs:1-27` gap assertion is an obsolete consumer expectation to cut over, not a blocker. The MIR/lowering/source-kind files listed above are shared contracts; do not create a second explanation or duplicate source-kind mechanism.

## Source evidence
The packet's observed behavior is authoritative: JIT `jet run` prints nothing until stdin closes, consumes all input before a blank-line break, and leaves a later `io.readline` at EOF; AOT reads one line per turn and leaves the next line available. The direct old JIT route at `crates/jet-jit/src/IO.rs:1133-1147` materializes `stdin.lock().lines()` into a Vec, and `IO.rs:1387-1392` registers it as `stdin_lines`. In contrast, the canonical AOT by-value source at `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/CollectionIoSources.rs:71-98` is lazy, and the current JIT implementation already has a lazy `JetLoopLineReader`/cursor at `crates/jet-jit/src/Collections.rs:756-813,1193-1295,1381-1539`. MIR uses one target-neutral `LinesStdin` source kind (`crates/jet-foundation/src/MIR.rs:4038-4075`; lowering at `tir_to_mir_stmt.rs:1283-1324`). The interpreter uses the same one-line ambient reader (`crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/ambient_interp.rs:221-273,365-518` and `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIREval.rs:1903-2018,4033-4080`). The stale Vec route is therefore a duplicate/legacy path, not a reason to create another loop implementation.

cards.title: Compiler assurance: mechanized semantic contract and proof-boundary experiment
cards.body: Foundations-and-trust research found no captured end-to-end semantic-preservation theorem for Jet. Source registries, .jproof artifacts, and the hardening rig do not establish one. CompCert, CakeML, Alive2, Affect, and the modal-effects papers show complementary proof methods with explicit boundaries. This card owns a bounded research deliverable and the owner choice about the compiler assurance contract. It does not own the existing hardening rig, MIR implementation, current build repair, or production changes during this investigation. Deduplicated against #1127, #2334-#2343, #2644, #2888, and #2919. Reports: docs/research/jet-foundations-and-trust-2026-09-04/04-trust.md and 02-frontier.md.
cards.plan:
## Authority and scope
Planning preparation only; no implementation, test pass, criterion closure, or owner ratification is claimed. Preserve all existing acceptance criteria and evidence. Ratified choices remain binding: D-COMPILER-PROOF1=A. No new owner choice is identified; implement the already-ratified contract without reopening it.

## Implementation
1. Preserve the full ratified D-COMPILER-PROOF1=A denominator: parsing, checking, compile-time evaluation, shared lowering, optimization, every applicable tier adapter, and Jet-owned Prelude/Core implementation. Missing required preservation arguments block 1.0; there is no new promotion ballot or bounded-search substitute. Foreign compiler suffixes remain named, separately tested assumptions.
2. Write the explicit source-to-execution claim, premises, observable results/mutation/effects/rejection/failure, resource laws, and trusted components into the existing proof/compiler contract. Inventory every construct and boundary; attach each uncovered obligation to its existing live owner without duplicating #2898, #2335, or #2919.
3. Complete one nontrivial real-implementation vertical slice covering results, mutation, comptime, rejection, and failure. Use a ratified binding route: verified construction, direct implementation verification, or a sound translation checker/certificate. A detached model theorem, finite agreeing witnesses, source digest, or two JavaScript evaluators does not establish implementation correspondence.
4. Use #2934’s pinned Lean 4 replay for the preservation argument and #2945’s checked derivation record for evidence. State exactly what the mechanized claim covers. Keep bounded search, differential agreement, model validity, and foreign assumptions distinct; unknown, timeout, missing correspondence, and invalid oracle remain non-proofs.
5. Integrate the claim/obligation record into the existing release evidence gate under the already-ratified law. Keep all uncovered stages live until proved; completing the first slice cannot imply an end-to-end theorem. Ordinary Jet installation needs no proof assistant.
Owned paths: proof/compiler/semantics/{contract.json,model.mjs,implementation.mjs,check.mjs,generate-obligations.mjs}, proof/compiler/obligations.json, and the actual compiler/Prelude slice being bound. #2934 owns checker/toolchain replay; #2945 owns the common evidence record.

cards.plan:
## Outcome

Make current release, version, readiness, and feature-complete claims truthful under the owner’s pre-1.0 mandate while preserving ratified future policy and historical decisions. Use one bounded census; do not create version-migration machinery or a second claim registry.

## Authority and dependencies

1. 2. The dated readiness evidence docs/audits/jet-foundations-and-trust-2026-09-04/07-readiness.md:57-69 records the deleted versioning excerpt and explicitly says #2927 is a truth-labeling/census card, not a release-policy amendment. It is evidence, not a file to recreate.
3. No owner ballot is needed for exact banner wording: use the current owner mandate and the executable Manifest/version authority; ask for a new ballot only if implementation discovers a genuinely new external contract, not for editorial correction.

## Work

1. Build one bounded inventory across current docs, Source, manifests/metadata, CLI help, installation/release pages, and release tests. Start from Source/CmdInspect.rs:4943-5103 (`inspect claims --json`), Source/main.rs:6648-6649 (`version`), crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Manifest.rs:103-115 (`version_banner`), Source/CmdReport.rs:1-17 (local-only report), tests/release_gates.rs:283-292, and tests/release/version_banner.txt. Classify each row as current capability, planned target, historical ratified decision, or unsupported/stale claim.
2. Correct stale current claims at their canonical source and update every generated/report/help/metadata/docs consumer in the same cutover. Use `jet inspect claims --json` as the release-claim projection; do not mislabel `jet report`, which is a local telemetry bundle and has no release-census semantics.
3. Keep current Jet pre-1.0, breaking changes open, and no present Jet-version migration support. Preserve the Ada/Pascal binder-only and C/C++ unavailable boundaries; never infer readiness from a version banner or import-command acceptance.
4. If a claim has no authority plus current evidence owner, classify it stale/unsupported rather than invent a readiness claim. Keep one inventory in this card and the existing evidence; do not add a parser, migration tier, compatibility alias, or permanent registry.
5. Record the corrected claim source/evidence links in the existing release-gate fixtures and docs without rewriting D-REL1–D-REL5 or deleting the dated readiness rationale.

## Proof

Planned proof only; run after implementation through scripts/agent/jet-env. Compare `full jet version` and `full jet --version` with the canonical Manifest banner and release fixture under the owner’s prerelease law; query `full jet inspect claims --json` and compare each disposition with the bounded census; then run the focused release_gates version/claim fixture. Expected proof retains historical decisions, current prerelease state, and binder-only import wording, with no present “v1.0 shipped/post-v1.0 compatibility” claim unless the owner changes the law.

## Scope

No new release decision, version parser, migration machinery, compatibility promise, or owner ballot for editorial/banner wording. Historical audit evidence remains immutable.

cards.title: Compiler proof: pinned checker toolchain and implementation-bound replay
cards.body:
## Actual

D-COMPILER-PROOF1=A requires checked arguments for every Jet-controlled stage. The captured campaign contains no qualified compiler theorem or checked implementation correspondence.

## Expected

A reproducible offline proof construction and replay path binds each checked claim to the exact modeled implementation and produced compiler artifact. The owner selects one proof toolchain; ordinary Jet users need no proof assistant installed.

## Scope and authority

D-COMPILER-PROOF1, D-RECORD1, I6, I9. Owner choice: D-COMPILER-PROOF-TOOLS1. Do not implement the unratified choice.

This is a concrete delivery card, not evidence that the feature works today. No production implementation, fresh compiler build, or project suite was run during this design campaign. No cyber work, AI mode, current Jet-version migration machinery, or protected-record writes.

Original questions: Q1, Q3, Q6, Q7, Q19, Q20, Q23, Q24, Q25, Q30. Proposals: N01.

Report: docs/audits/jet-foundations-and-trust-2026-09-04/08-new-capabilities.md
cards.plan:
## Authority and scope
Planning preparation only; no implementation, test pass, criterion closure, or owner ratification is claimed. Preserve all existing acceptance criteria and evidence. Ratified choices remain binding: D-COMPILER-PROOF-TOOLS1=A. No new owner choice is identified; implement the already-ratified contract without reopening it.

## Implementation
1. Use Lean 4, already ratified by D-COMPILER-PROOF-TOOLS1=A, as the canonical kernel checker. Preserve the current fail-closed unavailable state until a real checked artifact and implementation correspondence exist. Do not introduce another checker, owner gate, or compiler dependency.
2. Pin the development-only Lean executable, version, distribution/store closure, model/generator inputs, and exact proof artifacts. Aeneas may produce supported input but its translation is not automatically a checked binding. Reconstruct and replay offline without fetching or substituting an unpinned system tool.
3. Invoke the actual pinned Lean checker and verify the exact proposition and accepted implementation-binding route. Source scanning, theorem names, digest equality, and an attached .olean file alone are insufficient. Bind source/configuration, model, checked implementation/certificate, and produced compiler artifact under #2925’s relation.
4. Retain all existing negative-fixture evidence and extend it where the real kernel/correspondence route introduces an uncovered boundary. Reject false claims, valid proofs for the wrong proposition/source/candidate, admitted or detached proofs, stale identities, unsupported translations, missing tools, and exhausted budgets.
5. Emit the same #2945 claim record and consume the already-ratified 1.0 gate: a missing required argument blocks release. This card does not need a second owner vote to enforce that law. Ordinary users remain free of proof-assistant installation; compiler and seam dependencies remain path-only.
Owned paths: scripts/agent/compiler-proof.mjs, proof/compiler/toolchain/{manifest.json,fixtures}, the admitted Lean artifacts and development-environment pin. Consume #2925’s claim and #2945’s record; do not duplicate either.

## Source evidence
Packet: `~/.cache/jet-luna/ballot-prep-20260906/assurance-context.json:570-648`. Ratified `D-COMPILER-PROOF1` requires checked arguments for every Jet-controlled stage and implementation-bound replay; ratified `D-COMPILER-PROOF-TOOLS1` selects the pinned proof-toolchain path. `scripts/agent/compiler-proof.mjs:1-320,679-1097` contains the replay/check CLI and pinned-toolchain validation. `proof/compiler/toolchain/manifest.json:1-240` records the exact Lean package/store/executable and hashes. `proof/compiler/obligations.json:1-50`, `proof/compiler/semantics/contract.json:1-180`, and `proof/compiler/semantics/check.mjs:1-717` define the obligation relation, contract identity, and verdict checks.
cards.checkSteps:
Planned proof only; not run during preparation. Rebuild before compiler/runtime smoke. Run repository commands through scripts/agent/jet-env. Use exact narrow criterion evidence; broad suites remain milestone-gated.

`scripts/agent/jet-env full node scripts/agent/compiler-proof.mjs <record>` using the repository’s proof record must first validate the pinned manifest and identities, then invoke `proof/compiler/semantics/check.mjs`. Observable success is an offline replay whose output includes the pinned checker/toolchain identity, contract/implementation/artifact hashes, and bounded checked verdicts. Change one identity/hash in a throwaway copy: observable result is rejection before a proof claim. Remove or make unavailable the pinned executable: observable result is `unavailable`/failure, never pass. Confirm the persisted artifact is accepted by existing evidence ingestion without installing a checker for ordinary users.

Run scripts/agent/jet-env full node scripts/agent/compiler-proof.mjs --replay in a clean offline admitted environment. Observe actual pinned Lean kernel replay and exact implementation correspondence, not merely a valid manifest with result unavailable. Re-run --hostile-fixtures --json and retain the existing negative evidence. Inspect dependency and installation closure to confirm Lean remains development-only.

Planning refreshed from current source and ratified authority. Owned paths, ordered cutover, dependencies, owner gates, and focused proof are recorded. No implementation, new test pass, criterion closure, or owner ratification is claimed.

Criteria 1 and 4 remain open on live evidence: the pinned Lean 4.29.1 store output is not realized in this environment, so --check-toolchain and --replay return status unavailable exit 3 at toolchain.executable and the checked-in fixture records unavailable rather than fabricated proof. Replay is implementation-bound: candidate.commit pins HEAD 5382a5b20 and will fail closed after the integration commit until the record is regenerated against the new compiler commit, which is the intended identity behavior. cards.title: Compiler proof: executable Jet semantics and complete observation contract
cards.body:
## Actual

The research defines a conditional preservation claim but does not provide a complete executable formal model of current ratified Jet.

## Expected

One executable formal semantics covers the ratified language and Jet-owned Core behavior, including acceptance, rejection, effects, failures, resources, and permitted schedules. Its rules are checked against the published language rather than copied from one engine.

## Scope and authority

D-COMPILER-PROOF1, D-TIER-ONEIR1, I1, I2, I3, I4, I5, I9. No new owner choice: implement the cited law and this contract.

This is a concrete delivery card, not evidence that the feature works today. No production implementation, fresh compiler build, or project suite was run during this design campaign. No cyber work, AI mode, current Jet-version migration machinery, or protected-record writes.

Original questions: Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q7, Q19, Q20, Q26, Q28, Q29. Proposals: N01, N02.

Report: docs/audits/jet-foundations-and-trust-2026-09-04/08-new-capabilities.md
cards.plan:
## Owned paths
- proof/compiler/semantics/ (new)
- crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs (read authority)
- docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md (read authority)
- docs/spec/architecture.md (read authority)
- proof/compiler/obligations.json (new generated relation)
- tests/dev_parts/corpus_gate.rs
- tests/fuzz/sema/differential/
- examples/features/

## Implementation
1. Derive the denominator from canonical syntax, typed operations, Core surface and receiver inventories, and applicable target descriptors. Give every construct and boundary an obligation row and live proof owner; unsupported is an open obligation, never an exclusion invented for closure.
2. Define source states, values, bindings, ownership, stores, tasks, foreign interactions, compile-time behavior, and observable transitions. Include result values, mutations, consumed input, externally visible event order, typed failure, cancellation, termination, and promised progress.
3. State configuration, arithmetic, scheduling, stack/allocation/fuel, and foreign-contract premises. Preserve defined failures; do not copy CompCert C undefined-behavior refinement into safe Jet. A target-only exhaustion result is allowed only under the existing ratified resource law.
4. Connect each formal rule to exact current law and executable examples. Reconcile a wrong model against authority; any genuinely unspecified user-visible behavior becomes a named owner gate rather than a silent model choice.
5. Run the same semantic witnesses and hostile boundary cases through the formal evaluator and the canonical Jet corpus after the compiler baseline is restored. Differences in the specification, model, or implementation receive distinct diagnoses.
6. Define the Rust, Cranelift, and web-output models needed by the real correspondence arguments. Do not treat a generated mathematical function or foreign-tool model as a verified implementation bridge. Jet-owned unsafe/runtime behavior remains in scope; foreign implementations remain named premises.

## Focused proof
After implementation: scripts/agent/jet-env full node scripts/agent/compiler-proof.mjs --stage semantics; run the model-validity witness set against the fresh compiler on AOT, default run, interpreter, and applicable web targets.

## Integration contract
Reuse the named existing mechanisms. Migrate every affected producer, consumer, example, generated artifact, and touched documentation together. ## Actual

Current facts, semantic operations, proof rows, and recorded events exist, but the research proposal lacks a single implementation contract connecting a claim to its premises and current validity.

## Expected

A consumer can ask what a claim means, what established it, which premises it uses, and whether it still applies. CLI, editors, review, teaching, and optimization consume the same compiler-owned records.

## Root mechanism and consumer cutover
1. Implement D-EXPLANATION-RECORD1=A as an extension of existing facts, proof records, semantic index, EvidenceReport, and RecordIndex contracts. No second fact plane, evidence semantics, or artifact container.
2. A record links subject, claim, producer/method, rule, premise IDs, source origin, source/build/run/target identity, assumptions, disposition, and optional event/counterexample reference. Preserve distinct static derivation, formal proof, recorded execution, sampled agreement, and external-assumption evidence classes.
3. Produce the link at the authoritative checker, lowering, or recorded operation. Renderers may shorten/expand but cannot invent a reason, attach another source, execute effects, or run another interpreter.
4. Invalidate dependent claims when source, configuration, target, implementation, or run identity changes. Keep stale, expired, redacted, unavailable, unsupported, and budget-exhausted states explicit; missing runtime values stay unknown.
5. Intern repeated references, share nodes, obey D-RECORD1 capture/retention/consent, and avoid full proof-tree copies per consumer. No AI or external service.
6. Migrate CLI/prove/inspect/review/LSP consumers to the shared record. #2899, #2946, and #2947 consume this contract; none creates a competing explanation relation.
7. Use one source-backed witness through `jet inspect`, `jet prove`, `jet review`, editor, and learn, then edit a premise and repeat. Negative controls cover false reason, wrong source, fabricated counterexample, sampled-as-proof, missing/redacted observation, and budget exhaustion.

cards.title: Jet Learn: prediction, counterexample, change, and transfer interactions
cards.body:
## Actual

Source/CmdLearn.rs currently defines three repair exercises with fixed prompts and expected output. #2926’s broad census does not implement the proposed learning interaction.

## Expected

The existing offline jet learn runner teaches a model through prediction, observed evidence, a minimal counterexample or explanation, a controlled change, and a structurally different transfer task.

## Scope and authority

D-LEARN1, D-TEACH-FOREIGN1, D-REPORT-EDITOR1, D-RECORD1. Owner choice: D-LEARN-FEEDBACK1. Do not implement the unratified choice.

This is a concrete delivery card, not evidence that the feature works today. No production implementation, fresh compiler build, or project suite was run during this design campaign. No cyber work, AI mode, current Jet-version migration machinery, or protected-record writes.

Original questions: Q12, Q14, Q15, Q16, Q17, Q18. Proposals: N04, N05.

## Authority and scope
Planning preparation only; no implementation, test pass, criterion closure, or owner ratification is claimed. Preserve all existing acceptance criteria and evidence. Ratified choices remain binding: D-LEARN-FEEDBACK1=A. No new owner choice is identified; implement the already-ratified contract without reopening it. Preserve existing blockers: #2945, #2926.

## Implementation


## Owned paths
- `Source/CmdLearn.rs`: extend the existing runner/task model and progression state; retain watch, one-shot, check, JSON, quiet, and color flags.
- `examples/learn/`: package the four retained end-to-end task families (loop, state/lifetime, effect boundary, foreign boundary), source identities, controlled edits, wrong models, counterexamples, transfer fixtures, and accessibility alternatives.
- `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs`: metadata only where needed to describe existing `jet learn` options; no new command or syntax.
- `editors/vscode/`: project the same task/evidence identity through existing editor actions; ordinary editing does not launch quizzes.
- `tests/learn.rs`: add focused interaction/state tests; do not replace current offline/watch coverage.

## Root mechanism and consumer cutover
1. Consume #2926’s capability-derived task relation and #2945’s shared explanation/record identity. Replace the hard-coded three-entry-only assumption with tasks carrying concept, prerequisite, prompt, plausible wrong model, source/input identity, deterministic oracle, reveal policy, controlled edit, transfer task, and accessibility alternative.
2. Implement ratified D-LEARN-FEEDBACK1=A in the existing runner: minimum prerequisite, prediction or explicit `I do not know`, identified execution/evidence, focused reason or valid counterexample, controlled change, structurally different transfer. Unknown help is immediate; there is no forced delay or penalty. Expert skip records `unmeasured`, never `completed`.
3. Use real compiler facts and identified execution. A wrong prediction gets a distinguishing witness; no persuasive generated prose, second interpreter, AI, external service, or Studio.
4. Keep the first path understandable without jargon while exposing raw premises/evidence to experts. Existing `show_problems`/`jet explain` remains a route, not a replacement for the new task record.
5. Persist progress against curriculum/task/source/oracle identities. Preserve user edits across interruption/resume. A changed lesson/oracle/source revision invalidates affected completion evidence. Distinguish task completion from transfer evidence.
6. Project the same task IDs, evidence, states, and revision rules to ordinary editor and JSON paths; keep watch/one-shot/cancelled/stale/unavailable behavior honest.
7. Add focused fixtures/tests for all four task families and an owner-reviewed learning runbook. Do not claim human learning effectiveness from agent/model completion.

- Exact blockers: #2945 (`c07pex5n`) and #2926 (`c0rpr1gc`).
- Ratified authority: D-LEARN1, D-TEACH-FOREIGN1, D-REPORT-EDITOR1, D-RECORD1; owner choice D-LEARN-FEEDBACK1=A ratified 2026-09-05.

cards.body:

cards.title: Shared state: atomic snapshots and stale-result rejection
cards.body:
## Actual

Pool/Id already protects reused resource slots, and Shared/#Transact already owns shared mutation. The proposed delayed-result guard lacks a reusable, fully specified shared-state interface.

## Expected

A delayed computation can publish only against the same committed state it observed. The chosen interface preserves existing ownership and transactions, rejects ABA and wrong-owner tickets, and never retries effects silently.

## Scope and authority

D-CONC-SHARE1, D-SHARED-API1, D-ROLLBACK-TRAIT, D-POOLID-API1, D-MEM-COPYSEM1, D-FACT-LAW1, I1, I9. Owner choice: D-SHARED-REVISION1. Do not implement the unratified choice.

This is a concrete delivery card, not evidence that the feature works today. No production implementation, fresh compiler build, or project suite was run during this design campaign. No cyber work, AI mode, current Jet-version migration machinery, or protected-record writes.

Original questions: Q4, Q5, Q6, Q7, Q26, Q27, Q28, Q29. Proposals: N07.

Report: docs/audits/jet-foundations-and-trust-2026-09-04/08-new-capabilities.md
cards.plan:
## Authority and scope
Planning preparation only; no implementation, test pass, criterion closure, or owner ratification is claimed. Preserve all existing acceptance criteria and evidence. Ratified choices remain binding: D-SHARED-REVISION1=A. No new owner choice is identified; implement the already-ratified contract without reopening it.

## Implementation


## Root mechanism
Keep the existing `Shared<T>` cell and its owner-bound, opaque snapshot protocol. Add no second epoch, lock, transaction, or pool mechanism.

## Owned paths
`jet-foundation` Shared protocol types; native Prelude Shared routes; `jet-sema` ownership checks; TIR route tables; MIR evaluator transaction scope; JIT and Web adapters; concurrency examples; core-library docs.

## Ordered steps
1. Keep the ratified `capture()` and `try_replace(snapshot, value)` contract. The snapshot must carry the value/revision pair and an unforgeable owner-bound ticket. A stale, wrong-owner, replayed, or exhausted ticket must return the existing typed failure or `false` result. It must never write.
2. Keep one `u64` revision law in every adapter. Every committed write advances the revision, including an equal write and `A → B → A`. Do not retry or wrap on exhaustion.
3. Finish the MIR active-STM carrier. When lowered `TLocal::stm` enters an STM transaction, bind the evaluator frame to the existing `shared_protocol::JetSharedTransaction` lifetime. Make `capture_txn` register the same snapshot with that transaction. Commit must publish through the ordinary Shared lock and revision law. Abort must invalidate the ticket without changing the cell. Nested transactions must use the existing STM nesting rules.
4. Keep the fail-closed error outside an active transaction. Do not keep the current error inside a valid active transaction. Do not add a MIR-only transaction table.
5. Route all tiers through the existing `SharedRoutes` and TIR registry. Reuse the current clone/pure capture checks. Remove any caller that reads a value, stores a separate revision, and later writes without the canonical ticket.
6. Update the concurrency examples, generated declarations, goldens, and core-library documentation. State the wrong-owner, replay, exhaustion, commit, abort, and nested rules once.

## Consumer cutover
Migrate native, JIT, Web, MIR, interpreter, and examples to `capture`/`try_replace`. Keep `Pool` and `Id` as separate APIs. Do not add aliases for the old manual read/compare/write sequence.

## Source evidence
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/MathTaskMem.rs:1147-1214,1226-1391` has the native cell, revision, capture, transaction-capture, and `try_replace` paths.
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Shared.js:1-190` has the Web opaque snapshot and `BigInt` revision path.
- `crates/jet-jit/src/Memory.rs:1053-1292` has JIT capture, transaction registration, owner, revision, and typed result handling.
- `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerOwnership.rs:6181-6315` checks cloneable/pure captures and exact snapshot sources.
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIREval.rs:7239-7453`, especially `:7450-7453`, explicitly reports that `Shared.capture_txn` is unavailable without an active transaction.
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIREval.rs:12098-12358`, `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/tir_to_mir_expr.rs:4030-4069`, and `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/method_calls.rs:6854-6905` show the MIR storage and the lowered STM-local path.
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/SharedRoutes.rs:61-111` and `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/routes.rs:3993-4055` are the existing route surfaces.
- `docs/spec/reference/core-library.md:2972-3022` states the cross-tier Shared API and must not claim parity before the MIR transaction path is complete.
cards.checkSteps:
Planned proof only; not run during preparation. Rebuild before compiler/runtime smoke. Run repository commands through scripts/agent/jet-env. Use exact narrow criterion evidence; broad suites remain milestone-gated.

Invoke the focused Shared concurrency and transaction fixtures through `scripts/agent/jet-env` for native/AOT, default interpreter, MIR, JIT, and Web. Expect exactly one winner for two competing publications; stale, ABA, wrong-owner, replay, and exhaustion cases must not overwrite. Expect equal writes and `A → B → A` to produce distinct revisions. Expect commit to publish, abort to leave the prior value, nested behavior to follow the existing STM rule, and `capture_txn` to work only inside an active transaction.

- Race two snapshots against one cell. Observe one successful publication and one stale rejection.
- Reuse a consumed or wrong-owner ticket. Observe a typed failure or `false`; observe no value or revision change.
- Publish equal values and the ABA sequence. Observe a new revision for each committed write.
- Run plain write, committed transaction, aborted transaction, and nested transaction paths. Observe the ratified revision law.
- Run the same scenarios in native/AOT, interpreter/MIR, JIT, and Web. Observe the same result and error class.

cards.title: Core Testing: reproducible two-implementation comparison with honest outcomes
cards.body:
## Actual

core.testing exposes corpus, fixtures, fake clocks, and test suites, but no first-party two-implementation comparison API. Adopters and experiment authors must assemble comparison and failure reporting themselves.

## Expected

One existing test mechanism compares two implementations on the same declared cases and observation relation, retains a useful counterexample, and never calls empty or inconclusive agreement a proof.

## Scope and authority

D-TESTKIT1, D-RECORD1, D-ADOPT-TIER1, I6, I9. Owner choice: D-TEST-COMPARE1. Do not implement the unratified choice.

This is a concrete delivery card, not evidence that the feature works today. No production implementation, fresh compiler build, or project suite was run during this design campaign. No cyber work, AI mode, current Jet-version migration machinery, or protected-record writes.

Original questions: Q3, Q6, Q8, Q19, Q20, Q21, Q22, Q23, Q24, Q26, Q27, Q28, Q29. Proposals: N09.

Report: docs/audits/jet-foundations-and-trust-2026-09-04/08-new-capabilities.md
cards.plan:
## Authority and scope
Planning preparation only; no implementation, test pass, criterion closure, or owner ratification is claimed. Preserve all existing acceptance criteria and evidence. Ratified choices remain binding: D-TEST-COMPARE1=A. No new owner choice is identified; implement the already-ratified contract without reopening it.

## Implementation
Keep Foundation `TestingComparison` as the one semantic engine. Complete the consumer cutover across AOT, resident JIT, interpreter, and `jet test-compare`: every tier must marshal the same identity, cases, reference/candidate observations, relation, first difference, and verdict record. The carrier may call only the two checked callables; it must not derive a verdict from empty output, a test exit code, or one implementation’s internal state. A finite matched corpus is an honest matched result, never a universal proof. Empty, discarded-only, unsupported, unavailable, timeout, cancellation, invalid oracle, and contamination states must remain non-success. `#2973` supplies typed histories/schedules; this card consumes their artifacts and compares the declared observation relation, without adding a history generator or second schema.

Bring the Core export table, sema member table, generated carrier, canonical call registry, JIT symbols, interpreter route, and CLI JSON parser/rendering into one parity check. If the current `Core.jet` rows and generated `core_calls.rs` rows differ, regenerate/cut over the canonical registry rather than adding a hand-written alias. Keep generated code non-unwinding at host boundaries as required by the ratified decision.

## Dependencies and integration
Authority: `D-TEST-COMPARE1`, `D-RECORD1`, `D-ADOPT-TIER1`, `I6`, `I9`, and Foundation `TestingComparison`. Dependency: `#2973` supplies histories; do not make #2973 implement comparison semantics. Remaining owner gate: accept the final public exposure/CLI record shape and the evidence that all execution tiers route to the Foundation verdict; no new comparison policy is required.

## Source evidence
Packet: `~/.cache/jet-luna/ballot-prep-20260906/assurance-context.json:819-891`. Ratified authority is `D-TEST-COMPARE1`, with `D-RECORD1`, `D-ADOPT-TIER1`, `I6`, and `I9`. The Foundation engine at `crates/jet-foundation/src/TestingComparison.rs:1-183,180-472` owns `ComparisonIdentity`, observation relations, canonical statuses, first mismatch, empty/unsupported/unavailable/timeout/cancelled/invalid-oracle/contaminated outcomes, and JSON records. The carrier at `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/TestingComparison.rs:1-115` invokes the two callables; the JetStd adapter is at `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/TestingComparison.rs:1-100`. `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.jet:88,279-281` declares the exports/dispatcher rows, while the inspected canonical registry block `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/core_calls.rs:1633-1642` contains the neighboring testing rows and must be parity-checked for the comparison rows. The example is `examples/features/tooling/test_compare/run.jet:1-14`; the CLI consumer is `Source/CmdTest.rs:1-243`.

Integration guard: the existing JIT callback-parity receipt remains evidence and its met criterion is not reset. Consolidate any remaining JIT verdict policy into the Foundation engine; hosts only invoke checked callables and marshal observations. The two stateful/foreign scenarios must use explicit isolated environments and real consumer observations. Ordinary CLI/editor replay must resolve the same mismatch artifact and relation; source-table equality alone is not runtime proof.

Mismatch case: same command on core-testing-mismatch.json exits 1 and renders 'status=mismatch relation=typed_equality samples=1 reason=first differing observation is case case-0' with the replay case, input, source, tool, and target plus reference=same/candidate=different. criteria.evidence: All non-pass outcomes are reported honestly rather than collapsed into a pass, each proven on a real run against clean binary md5 adc47ab3125e with 'jet test-compare --json' and each exiting 1: empty -> status=empty samples=0 universal_proof=false; unavailable -> status=unavailable; timeout -> status=timeout; cancelled -> status=cancelled; invalid -> status=invalid_oracle. Every one renders 'reason=recorded runner outcome is <status>'. Only the genuinely matched fixture exits 0. Fixtures at ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/core-testing-{empty,unavailable,timeout,cancelled,invalid}.json. This is the substance of the card: an unavailable peer, a crashed run, or a discarded output cannot be averaged into a green result.

criteria.evidence: Comparison semantics are now declared in exactly one place, which was the defect this card existed to fix. The JIT host at crates/jet-jit/src/jit/runtime_host.rs previously derived status and equality locally at lines 8531-8652 alongside Foundation's canonical compare_samples; jet_jit_testing_compare now calls Foundation compare_samples and the histories host uses the Foundation HistoryRunner through the same carrier, so hosts marshal and Foundation decides. The JIT history parser uses the existing canonical crate::Encoding::json_rt::parse_datatree rather than a second decode path. Proof: 'scripts/agent/lane-check.sh -p jet-jit' -> CHECK OK; '-p jet-foundation' -> CHECK OK; '-p jet-codegen' -> CHECK OK.

criteria.text: The same Core behavior and failure meaning reach AOT, default run/dev, interpreter, and applicable web modes through one Prelude implementation, with no external dependency or second test runner.
criteria.evidence: JIT parity closed by the callback-parity lane. Root cause of the previous fail-closed unavailable: JitCallableSlot carried fn_ptr/env/has_env with no signature, and callback enrolment went through a hand-maintained (module, member) string table consulted only on call_core's explicit jit_symbol path, so every sema_web_call row including core.testing.compare took the Prelude route with raw handles and arrived with raw_unary None. Fix: enrolment is now type-driven. Any CoreCall argument whose checked MIR type is a function type of at most two params with Cranelift-ABI params and return gets a universal thunk generated and bound at the call site on both paths; hosts consume it through jit_callable_parts plus invoke_universal_unary/pair with raw i64 words. More than two params or a convention mismatch is a lowering error so the function deopts rather than leaking a raw handle. jet_jit_testing_compare is reimplemented over that mechanism with typed DataTree equality, case ids, first_difference, seed, proper Option<Int> and Bool carriers, and the canonical status vocabulary; unavailable is now reachable only on a recorded defect or a callback stop. No new unsafe was added; the existing transmute and invoke sites are argued sound with exactly-one-pointer and not-rebound guards, non-unwinding generated code with catch_unwind at host boundaries, trap polling after each invoke, and depth-counted per-thread runtime borrow released before any invoke.

cards.title: Optimization experiments: checked laws, rejected counterexamples, and whole-job cost
cards.body:
## Actual

The research identifies equality search, abstract facts, specialization, fusion, scheduling, and layout opportunities. Existing implementation cards do not supply a reproducible experiment protocol for evaluating each proposed optimization under Jet meaning.

## Expected

Every retained optimization candidate has a machine-semantic law, artifact-bound legality evidence or explicit non-proof, falsifying inputs, and same-job cost evidence before production adoption.

## Scope and authority

D-COMPILER-PROOF1, D-TIER-ONEIR1, D-ACCEL1, D-PLACE1, D-LOOPREAD1, I9. No new owner choice: implement the cited law and this contract.

This is a concrete delivery card, not evidence that the feature works today. No production implementation, fresh compiler build, or project suite was run during this design campaign. No cyber work, AI mode, current Jet-version migration machinery, or protected-record writes.

Original questions: Q1, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q19, Q20, Q21, Q23, Q28, Q29. Proposals: N06, N10.

Report: docs/audits/jet-foundations-and-trust-2026-09-04/08-new-capabilities.md
cards.plan:
## Owned paths
- tools/agent-eval/optimization/ (new bounded experiments)
- proof/compiler/optimization/ (shared obligation definitions)
- gauntlet/ (existing corpus and result integration only)
- crates/jet-foundation/src/ (shared operation/fact interfaces read and consumed)
- docs/audits/jet-foundations-and-trust-2026-09-04/02-frontier.md

## Implementation
1. Implement five executable experiment families: checked arithmetic and floating rewrites; range/alias facts for loop fusion and vectorization; specialization and compile-time staging; layout without semantic copies; and conditional parallel scheduling. Use the current shared operation route, not an experimental second compiler.
2. For each rule, state the exact machine domain, preconditions, value/failure/effect/input/identity/resource observations, proof or checker boundary, and falsifying control. Reject real-number identities used as unrestricted floating-point laws.
3. Separate legality from profitability. A valid but slower transform loses the cost comparison; an invalid fast transform is ineligible. Existing explicit reject/override and inspect output expose the selected plan, rejected alternatives, copies, scheduling, and assumptions.
4. Compare the same source/workload against the unchanged valid path and required peers, including compile latency, warm/cold run behavior, memory, and applicable execution modes. Do not average away a cell loss or promote a research result into a release receipt.
5. Publish each family’s raw result, reduced counterexample, adopted or rejected rule, and concrete production owner. New semantic changes return to the owner; finalized D-ACCEL1/D-PLACE1/D-LOOPREAD1 and already-filed defects remain untouched.

## Focused proof
After implementation: run each bounded experiment and its rejecting controls; use the existing gauntlet for same-job measurements after the fresh candidate is available. This card authorizes no present build retry or full suite.

## Integration contract
Reuse the named existing mechanisms. Migrate every affected producer, consumer, example, generated artifact, and touched documentation together. Tests defend observable behavior and plausible defects, not wiring or wording. Language/Core behavior requires every applicable I9 mode through the same semantics. Close only on integrated criterion evidence; this planning publication claims no implementation completion.

cards.title: Test economics: preserve unique defect detection while removing redundant cost
cards.body:
## Actual

Test counts and registration coverage cannot establish detection value. The research has no consumed per-obligation account proving that proposed suite cuts retain distinct detection.

## Expected

The existing test and hardening portfolio identifies which behavioral defects each test can detect, what it costs, and what evidence a removal would lose. Selection cannot hide mandatory obligations.

## Scope and authority

D-HARDENING-GATE1, D-RECORD1, I4, I5, I9. No new owner choice: implement the cited law and this contract.

This is a concrete delivery card, not evidence that the feature works today. No production implementation, fresh compiler build, or project suite was run during this design campaign. No cyber work, AI mode, current Jet-version migration machinery, or protected-record writes.

Original questions: Q9, Q10, Q11, Q19, Q20, Q22, Q23, Q24, Q25, Q30. Proposals: N10.

Report: docs/audits/jet-foundations-and-trust-2026-09-04/08-new-capabilities.md
cards.plan:
## Owned paths
- tools/agent-eval/test-economics/ (new analysis over existing results)
- scripts/agent/ (existing focused selection and hardening entry points)
- tests/ (only justified consolidation/removal after evidence)
- gauntlet/ (existing test/build latency evidence)
- docs/audits/jet-foundations-and-trust-2026-09-04/04-trust.md

## Implementation
1. Join the canonical callable/construct/mode denominator to existing behavioral oracles, mutation outcomes, historical defects, run identities, wall time, memory, and flake/availability state. Consume current hardening records rather than building another runner.
2. Retain independent oracles for shared implementation paths. Add false-green controls for bound-and-discard outputs, zero valid inputs, all exclusions, broken reference code, wrong candidate identity, and harness failure reported as success.
3. Compute an inspectable candidate selection using distinct detected defect shapes and mandatory obligations before cost. Deterministic tie-breaking may select cheaper duplicate evidence, but one surviving unique detector or required mode cannot disappear.
4. Remove wording-only, wiring-only, mock-echo, and genuinely redundant tests only after a retained consumer contract or independent detector covers every still-required behavior. Keep useful historical minimal regressions when their failure shape is not covered elsewhere.
5. Run selected and omitted relevant controls against the same frozen candidate during the existing closeout window. A selector miss reopens its selection rule and owning obligation; do not weaken D-HARDENING-GATE1 quotas or #2420.

## Focused proof
After implementation: replay the existing oracle and selector controls on one identified candidate, then compare retained/removed detection and measured cost. Broad closeout runs require the existing token; this card does not create a second gate.

## Integration contract
Reuse the named existing mechanisms. Migrate every affected producer, consumer, example, generated artifact, and touched documentation together. Tests defend observable behavior and plausible defects, not wiring or wording. Language/Core behavior requires every applicable I9 mode through the same semantics. Close only on integrated criterion evidence; this planning publication claims no implementation completion.

cards.title: Foreign reasoning: one boundary contract from binding through accepted replacement
cards.body:
## Actual

Existing binder, adoption, conversion, and build-host cards cover individual mechanisms. The report’s complete reasoning chain across ownership, errors, callbacks, cost, and replacement evidence lacks one consumed cross-boundary contract.

## Expected

A user can inspect a foreign call, identify every assumption and conversion, debug through it, compare an explicit replacement, and retain foreign source authority until accepting that replacement.

## Scope and authority

D-FFI-CPP1, D-FFI-UNIFY1, D-ADOPT-TIER1, D-MIGRATE-SRC1, D-TEACH-FOREIGN1, I6, I9. No new owner choice: implement the cited law and this contract.

This is a concrete delivery card, not evidence that the feature works today. No production implementation, fresh compiler build, or project suite was run during this design campaign. No cyber work, AI mode, current Jet-version migration machinery, or protected-record writes.

## Implementation
1. Join existing binder descriptors to shared semantic and explanation identities. Cover ABI, layout/width/alignment, owner/borrow/close rules, encoding, nullable and error mapping, exception behavior, callbacks, task/thread crossing, target availability, and copy/conversion costs.
2. Honor D-FFI-CPP1: clang-based binding, cached C shims, opaque owned handles, consuming cleanup, normal methods, caught C++ exceptions, on-demand templates, labels, named operators, and checked overlays. Do not reopen the archived ruling or promise whole-C++ source translation.
3. Implement source-linked inspection and mixed debugging for C/C++, Python, Java, C#, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Go through their existing adapters. COM/VBA, Ada, and Pascal remain their stated adapter/binder classifications; unsupported cases say why.
4. Use the ratified narrow source-import subset and the comparison API to qualify a replacement on explicit contracts and recorded inputs. A mismatch, unsupported construct, unmodeled foreign effect, or unknown equivalence preserves the original foreign source as authoritative.
5. Exercise native export and CMake/Gradle/Bazel/MSBuild invocation through existing owners. Changing header, overlay, toolchain, target, or foreign implementation invalidates dependent generated artifacts and claims. No current Jet-version migration layer or AI mode is added.

## Focused proof

## Integration contract
Reuse the named existing mechanisms. Migrate every affected producer, consumer, example, generated artifact, and touched documentation together. cards.title: Frontier hypotheses: falsifiable same-job experiments and independent replication
cards.body:
## Actual

The four research hypotheses are reasoned proposals and bounded models, not measured Jet advances or scientific breakthroughs.

## Expected

Each hypothesis has an executable intervention, a comparable baseline, a result that could refute it, and independent replication on identified whole jobs. Novelty is claimed only when the evidence and prior-art comparison support it.

## Scope and authority

D-COMPILER-PROOF1, D-TIER-ONEIR1, D-FACTMODEL1, D-HARDENING-GATE1. No new owner choice: implement the cited law and this contract.

This is a concrete delivery card, not evidence that the feature works today. No production implementation, fresh compiler build, or project suite was run during this design campaign. No cyber work, AI mode, current Jet-version migration machinery, or protected-record writes.

Original questions: Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q9, Q10, Q11, Q12, Q15, Q16, Q18, Q21, Q26, Q27, Q28, Q29, Q30. Proposals: N07, N10, N11.
