- examples/learn/ (existing transfer tasks)
- proof/compiler/ (existing proof obligations)

## Implementation
1. Run four controlled studies: one semantic contract across routes; temporal identity across stale publications and resource reuse; conditional optimization with preserved meaning; and evidence-backed explanations with unfamiliar transfer tasks. Record baseline and intervention without substituting different jobs.
2. Use the exact falsifiers in the research report. A legitimate operation needing a second meaning, stale accepted fact, changed defined observation, or invented explanation refutes its corresponding implementation claim.
3. Cover the eight mission areas through the existing gauntlet and domain workload owners. Measure correct output/failure, resource and latency costs, supported environment, repair actionability, context size, and determinism where relevant.
4. Separate bounded model output, fresh executable results, formal evidence, simulated learner friction, and actual human transfer. Human claims require real participant evidence and consent; no invented survey or uptake percentage.
5. Have an independent reader replay the retained raw artifacts and compare the strongest named prior work. Report reject, supported-with-scope, or unresolved for each hypothesis; every observed defect joins an exact owner, not a generic research backlog.

## Focused proof
After implementation and restored candidate: execute the four studies, retain the real raw observations, and obtain independent replay. Actual human transfer and foreign-environment claims require their named evidence, not a simulated reader.

## Integration contract
Reuse the named existing mechanisms. Migrate every affected producer, consumer, example, generated artifact, and touched documentation together. Tests defend observable behavior and plausible defects, not wiring or wording. Language/Core behavior requires every applicable I9 mode through the same semantics. Close only on integrated criterion evidence; this planning publication claims no implementation completion.

cards.body:

The bootstrap portfolio already has owner gates and port cards. The research does not establish whether current Jet supports readable, correct, efficient compiler-shaped work well enough to justify a port.

A concrete workload evaluation informs #217 without treating self-compilation as correctness or silently making a compiler port a 1.0 requirement.

## Scope and authority

D-TIER-ONEIR1, D-COMPILER-PROOF1, D-HARDENING-GATE1. No new owner choice: implement the cited law and this contract.

This is a concrete delivery card, not evidence that the feature works today. No production implementation, fresh compiler build, or project suite was run during this design campaign. No cyber work, AI mode, current Jet-version migration machinery, or protected-record writes.

## Focused proof

cards.title: Derive endpoint contracts from typed handlers
cards.body:
Should one typed handler define its request, response, schema, and generated client?

Sam exposes an order lookup. The path contains a positive order number. A browser client must send the right request and understand the response.

Source-backed design finding F01; proposed public behavior, not a fresh runtime defect. The owner’s fresh-compiler construction failure remains accepted ground truth. This audit did not retry the compiler or full suite.

Extend D-SHAPE-ONE1, D-SHAPE-PROJECT1, and D-WEBAPP-SERVE1. Do not create another app graph or server. Generated clients consume the checked descriptor, not documentation text. A descriptor mismatch rejects before unsafe decoding. Every in-repo manual description replaced by the new owner is removed in one cutover.
cards.plan:
## Authority and scope
Planning preparation only; no implementation, test pass, criterion closure, or owner ratification is claimed. Preserve all existing acceptance criteria and evidence. Ratified choices remain binding: D-ENDPOINT-SHAPE1=A. No new owner choice is identified; implement the already-ratified contract without reopening it.

## Implementation


## Root mechanism
Define one sema-owned, checked endpoint descriptor. The descriptor is the only source for handler request/response shape, path/query/body binding, codecs, privacy, publication, and explicit transport policy. Do not build a second app graph or server.

## Owned paths
`jet-sema/Sema/App.rs`; shared `HTTPRoute` and OpenAPI models; TIR route lowering; HTTP server dispatch; WebRouter; generated clients; endpoint examples, declarations, and goldens.

## Ordered steps
1. Extend the existing `derive_route_inputs` result into the canonical descriptor. Store the route pattern, exact path fields, remainder query fields, explicit body fields, duplicate-source result, request/response types, Codable codec identity, public/private field facts, and explicit auth/status policy.
2. Use the existing `HTTPRoutePattern` grammar and `JetOpenApiRouteInput` checked model. Do not infer a body from “every lambda parameter that is not `HTTPRequest`.” Require the ratified explicit body declaration and reject an omitted or ambiguous source.
3. Emit sema diagnostics for wrong path names, wrong types, duplicate path/query/body sources, missing required fields, and handler return mismatches. Reject before unsafe decode and before handler invocation.
4. Pass the descriptor through the existing `THandleOp::HTTPRouterRegister` route. Make registration fail if the descriptor is absent or incomplete. Delete `unwrap_or_default()` and the manual `route_handler_contract` fallback.
5. Make HTTP server dispatch match the path, decode path/search/body with the descriptor's checked codec, and return the existing field-error contract before calling the handler. Keep auth and status policy explicit. Never auto-publish private fields.
6. Generate clients and OpenAPI from the same descriptor. Remove manual endpoint descriptions and any docs-text parser. Ensure generated clients send the exact checked request and decode the exact checked result/error.
7. Migrate every endpoint example, client declaration, route registration, and golden. Remove old contract metadata and aliases.

## Consumer cutover
`App.rs` produces the descriptor; TIR and `HTTPServer` consume it; OpenAPI and generated clients consume the same serialized facts. `WebRouter` reuses the descriptor rather than re-deriving fields. No second server graph and no empty-contract fallback.

cards.body:
Should data calculations share one typed query and return ordinary lists?

Mina groups ticket durations by team. Later she reads another source without rewriting the calculation or losing the key and amount types.

Source-backed design finding F02; proposed public behavior, not a fresh runtime defect. The owner’s fresh-compiler construction failure remains accepted ground truth. This audit did not retry the compiler or full suite.

Explicitly amend the public data-container design under D-DATAFRAME1 and D-DATA-SURFACE1. Keep D-SQL-SURFACE1 and D-CORE-EAGER1/2. Stable order, validation, failure order, effects, units, and numerical rules constrain optimization. A dropped column cannot hide a required source-validation error. Migrate plot adapters and every in-repo consumer; no legacy wrappers remain.

## Root mechanism
Make `Query<T>` the only typed query carrier. A query collects to ordinary typed `[T]`; `DataStream` remains one-shot, fallible, and explicit. Keep `DataPivotCell` distinct from grouped data.

## Owned paths

cards.title: Maintain eligible typed queries from source changes
cards.body:
Should a watched query update its answer from edits without a second handwritten algorithm?

A sale changes from 125 to 175 cents. Sam wants the regional total to rise by 50 without maintaining a separate update routine.

Source-backed design finding F03; proposed public behavior, not a fresh runtime defect. The owner’s fresh-compiler construction failure remains accepted ground truth. This audit did not retry the compiler or full suite.

Reuse D-LIVEQUERY1 and D-SHARED-REVISION1. Required-incremental policy rejects any recomputation; ordinary watch discloses it. Budgets name retained indexes and fail rather than silently dropping rows. The standalone BigInt model passed 7056 bounded transitions and rejected two mutants. Its Float counterexample forbids an unjustified generalization; it is not Jet runtime proof.
cards.plan:
## Authority and scope
Planning only; no implementation, new test pass, criterion closure, or owner ratification is claimed. Preserve existing criteria and evidence. Ratified choices remain binding: D-QUERY-LIVE1=A. No new owner gate is identified; do not reopen the selected contract.

## Implementation


## Root mechanism
Add the ratified tracked-source API on top of #2963's typed Query and the existing `LiveQuery` lifecycle. Use `Shared<T>.capture`/`try_replace` for atomic publication. Do not create a second generation or epoch system.

## Owned paths
typed data source and Query types; sema method signatures and Core exports; TIR lowering; native/JIT/MIR/Web carriers; `LiveQuery` lifecycle; bounded retained-state accounting; status/plot consumers; examples and generated declarations.

## Ordered steps
1. Add the checked tracked source with the ratified key function, unique-key rule, source revision, and owner-bound mutation handle. Expose distinct `insert`, `replace`, and `remove` operations. Duplicate keys, missing keys, wrong owners, stale revisions, and invalid values must fail with typed data errors.
2. Add `data.track(initial, key: ...)` and `data.query(...).watch()` to sema, Core exports, TIR, and all adapters. Reuse the #2963 `Query<T>` and `Group<K,V>` types.
3. Build one incremental kernel for eligible operations: filter, map, sum, count, min/max, join, and stable sort. Preserve source order and stable tie rules. Maintain key indexes and grouped state. Keep effects out of replay.
4. For a pure operation that cannot be maintained, use the ratified ordinary-watch recompute path with visible status. In required-incremental mode, refuse with a typed capability error. Reject effectful queries rather than replaying effects or silently changing semantics.
5. Publish each successful result through `Shared` capture/`try_replace`, then use existing LiveQuery generation, cancellation, drop, and close behavior. A stale computation must never replace a newer result.
6. Enforce retained-state ceilings with `DataLimits`. Keep indexes or fail with a typed budget error; do not silently spill or silently drop state. Expose incremental, recomputed, and refused status.
7. Add the same carrier and status behavior to AOT/comptime, JIT, MIR, and Web. Update plots, status views, examples, and generated declarations.
8. Add the BigInt transition model and the Float counterexample as focused fixtures. The Float result must prevent an unsafe general incremental generalization.

## Consumer cutover
#2963 supplies all typed query/list/group values. `LiveQuery` supplies lifecycle and publication. `Shared` supplies atomic revision rejection. Remove any new local invalidation table, duplicate source epoch, or ad-hoc watcher.

## Dependencies
- Ratified authority: `D-QUERY-LIVE1` option A.
- Dependency: #2963 owns the typed Query surface; #2964 must consume it.
- Reuse: `D-LIVEQUERY1` and `D-SHARED-REVISION1`.
- The BigInt transition record and Float counterexample are required evidence, not a new product choice.

cards.title: Typed coordinate spaces and checked transform composition
cards.body:
Should geometry types distinguish world, screen, camera, and device spaces?

Mina converts a mouse position into a game-world position. A camera or viewport change must not make a numerically valid calculation silently use the wrong space.

Source-backed design finding F04; proposed public behavior, not a fresh runtime defect. The owner’s fresh-compiler construction failure remains accepted ground truth. This audit did not retry the compiler or full suite.

Do not modify protected placement or acceleration decisions. No unchecked UnknownSpace default is introduced. A space type identifies a convention, not every runtime scene instance. Stock constructors and aliases are real domain names, not compatibility shims. Conversion failures and stale frame identity need registered diagnostics or typed runtime errors.
cards.plan:
## Authority and scope
Planning only; no implementation, new test pass, criterion closure, or owner ratification is claimed. Preserve existing criteria and evidence. Ratified choices remain binding: D-SPACE-GEOMETRY1=A. No new owner gate is identified; do not reopen the selected contract.

## Implementation


## Root mechanism
Reuse existing geometry carriers, static knowledge, units, `Point`, `Delta`, `Transform`, and provenance. Static tags erase. Dynamic values carry the smallest required frame-owner identity. Do not add `UnknownSpace` defaults or compatibility shims.

## Owned paths
sema geometry typing and diagnostics; native `LinalgFns`; Web `Ui.js`; JIT `Math.rs`; comptime/MIR/reflection; constructors and stock aliases; UI/game examples and docs.

## Ordered steps
1. Keep sema checks for wrong static spaces and the existing E2520/E2521 diagnostic family. Make the operation table explicit: point plus delta returns a point only for the same frame; point minus point returns a delta only for the same frame; delta operations require matching frames where the operation is defined.
2. Add dynamic frame-owner checks to native, Web, and JIT coordinate add/sub. Do not keep the current behavior that preserves the left frame while ignoring the right frame. Return the established typed conversion/frame error.
3. Make `Transform.then` require destination/source equality and produce the composed source/destination pair. Make inverse fallible for singular transforms with the established typed error.
4. Implement the ratified perspective contract. Depth must affect projection/picking or the ray path; it cannot be finite-only validation followed by ignored depth. Preserve the defined perspective/ray result and error cases.
5. Require a declared frame for dynamic constructors. Use real stock constructor and alias names. Do not default to `UnknownSpace`, and do not add aliases that hide the new contract.
6. Carry static erasure and dynamic identity through comptime/interpreter, reflection, AOT/native, JIT, and Web. Keep static paths allocation-free unless the existing carrier requires an allocation. Measure and disclose dynamic identity cost in the existing geometry evidence.
7. Update UI/game/docs/examples and all target-mode goldens. Do not change protected placement or acceleration decisions.

## Consumer cutover
Every geometry consumer uses the checked point/delta/transform/ray contract. Remove unchecked generic carrier arithmetic and stale constructor aliases. Reflection reports the same source/destination and runtime identity facts.

## Dependencies
- Ratified authority: `D-SPACE-GEOMETRY1` option A.
- Preserve existing placement and acceleration decisions. No new `UnknownSpace` or alias decision is allowed.
- Existing diagnostic authority: E2520/E2521 and the geometry diagnostic rows.

## Source evidence
- `docs/audits/jet-refounding-2026-09-05/02-language-and-core.md:314-394` defines coordinate-space semantics, composition, runtime identity, and ratified A.
- `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/type_assign.rs:486-523` recognizes generic Point2/Delta2/Transform/Transform2/Ray2 forms.
- `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_types.rs:363-368` lists recognized geometry names and stock aliases.
- `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/math_layout.rs:472-522,534-613,631-685,728-744` defines geometry layouts, space extraction, returns, and affine forms.
- `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/binary.rs:2164-2173` and `method_calls.rs:5925` contain geometry diagnostics E2520/E2521.
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/LinalgFns.rs:403-488,526-608` has native carriers, frame checks, composition, inverse, constructors, and unchecked add/sub behavior.
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Ui.js:1355-1470` has Web carrier checks, unchecked add/sub, finite-only depth handling, and ray behavior.
- `crates/jet-jit/src/Math.rs:1464-1622` has the JIT unchecked dynamic add/sub path, transform/inverse, point/depth, and ray behavior.
- `examples/features/ui/coordinate_spaces.jet:1-50` is the existing user-facing example.

Use `examples/features/ui/coordinate_spaces.jet` and focused geometry diagnostics through `scripts/agent/jet-env`. Expect valid world/view/screen composition, singular-inverse errors, perspective depth/ray behavior, and dynamic-frame mismatch errors. Compare static allocation behavior and dynamic identity behavior across native, JIT, interpreter/comptime, and Web.

- Add points/deltas from different dynamic frame owners. Observe a typed mismatch error on native, JIT, and Web.
- Subtract points in one frame. Observe a delta with that frame; attempt different frames and observe rejection.
- Compose `world → view` with `view → screen`. Observe `world → screen`; compose a mismatched transform and observe rejection.
- Invert a singular transform. Observe a typed failure.

cards.title: Scoped deterministic execution worlds
cards.body:
Should tests control time and scheduling without changing production function signatures?

Sam tests a task that completes after forty milliseconds. The test should finish quickly and reliably without a longer sleep or a global clock replacement.

Source-backed design finding F05; proposed public behavior, not a fresh runtime defect. The owner’s fresh-compiler construction failure remains accepted ground truth. This audit did not retry the compiler or full suite.

This is not permission to use undeclared effects. Fixed wall-clock origin and monotonic time are separate. Concurrent worlds are isolated. Ambiguous nested schedulers reject; child scopes share the parent scheduler. AOT, JIT, interpreter, and applicable web calls use the same controlled Prelude providers. No I9 exception is requested.
cards.plan:
## Authority and scope
Planning only; no implementation, new test pass, criterion closure, or owner ratification is claimed. Preserve existing criteria and evidence. Ratified choices remain binding: D-TEST-WORLD1=A. No new owner gate is identified; do not reopen the selected contract.

## Implementation


## Root mechanism
Carry one `JetDeterministicWorld` through the existing task context and effect-provider boundaries. Keep the existing scheduler. Do not add a second scheduler or process-global override.

## Owned paths
native scheduler/world, Web deterministic world, JIT random adapter, MIR/Web routes, clock/date/random/sleep/network/foreign effect boundaries, sema effect checks, docs/examples, and mode goldens.

## Ordered steps
1. Keep wall-clock origin separate from monotonic virtual time. Preserve negative-before-deadline, equal-time, timeout, and cancellation ordering. World waits must never call a real sleep.
2. Carry the active world into every spawned task through the existing scheduler task inheritance. A child shares the parent's scheduler/world state as ratified. Scope exit must account for descendants.
3. Complete provider selection at every controlled effect boundary: wall/monotonic time, date, RNG, scheduler sleep, network, foreign calls, and any external clock/random source. Under an active world, require the recorded/controlled provider. If absent, return a typed “missing controlled provider” error; never fall back to the host.
4. Route JIT random calls to the existing world RNG hooks. Remove the current `None`/host-thread fallback when a world is active.
5. Bring Web timer and task state to native parity. `advance` must release due timers in stable order. `wait_idle` must drain runnable work and virtual timers or return the same explicit refusal/status as the native contract; it cannot remain a checked no-op.
6. Keep nested world creation as an explicit fatal/rejection path. Keep the budget and history semantics stable. Stop a world when the budget is exhausted; do not allow a spin loop.
7. Update MIR, Web, JIT, native, examples, docs, and goldens. Do not add an I9 exception for uncontrolled effects.

## Consumer cutover
Time, random, sleep, network, foreign, and scheduler consumers ask the active provider boundary. They do not read a global override or host fallback. The existing world/task handles remain the public seam.

## Dependencies
- Ratified authority: `D-TEST-WORLD1` option A.
- Preserve the existing I9 no-undeclared-effects rule. Do not add an exception for testing worlds.
- No second scheduler or process-global override is permitted.

cards.title: Derive frame resource schedules from checked accesses
cards.body:
Should frame scheduling derive dependencies from the calls that read and write resources?

Mina simulates positions, draws a scene, and composites its image. The schedule must preserve those dependencies and keep images alive until device work completes.

Source-backed design finding F06; proposed public behavior, not a fresh runtime defect. The owner’s fresh-compiler construction failure remains accepted ground truth. This audit did not retry the compiler or full suite.

Do not reopen or write D-PLACE1 or D-ACCEL1. The new public frame API is the gated increment. Resource regions, layout, device, access, and completion identity constrain reuse. The existing explanation record shows dependencies, transfers, refused choices, and costs. A headless schedule does not qualify physical driver behavior.

## Implementation


## Root mechanism
Consume the one checked derivation record owned by #2945. That record is the source for accesses, dependencies, transfers, reuse, retention, completion, and explanation. Do not create a second explanation or schedule derivation.

2. Store the typed record or canonical record ID in `LambdaMeta` beside the explanation projection. Remove the explanation-only runtime re-derivation. #2967 must consume the #2945 record, not explain the same facts again.
3. Carry the record through the existing `GameSceneOnFrame` TIR route and callback lowering. Do not add a new route or scheduler.
4. Make foreign primitives declare complete read/write/overlap access and actual completion. If an async primitive has no completion token, reject physical async scheduling with a typed error. Never guess completion from a callback or frame end.
5. Make runtime callback registration and the frame loop consume the schedule. Respect dependency order. Delay reuse/release until the actual completion token. Preserve source/effect order when optimizing. Permit parallel execution only when the existing checked schedule proves it safe.
6. Keep headless mode as model proof only. Do not claim a physical-driver proof from a headless run. Update the example and conflict fixture to show the schedule and refusal cases.

cards.title: Typed ownership over the Arrow C data interface
cards.body:
Should Jet share compatible foreign columnar buffers through one checked owner?

Sam receives sales from a foreign analytics tool. He wants to query them without serializing a CSV copy or risking use after the producer releases memory.

Source-backed design finding F07a; proposed public behavior, not a fresh runtime defect. The owner’s fresh-compiler construction failure remains accepted ground truth. This audit did not retry the compiler or full suite.

The Arrow C ABI itself needs no Arrow software dependency. New external format or runtime libraries require their separate ballots. Do not treat Arrow C as Arrow IPC or Parquet support. Native, interpreter, JIT, and applicable web consumers use one semantic adapter contract. Semantic units and nominal identities require explicit metadata or conversion, not layout guessing.
cards.plan:
## Authority
Planning only; preserve criteria/evidence and ratified D-COLUMNAR-BOUNDARY1=A. No new owner gate or implementation claim.

## Implementation


## Owned paths
`crates/jet-foundation/src/ArrowData.rs` for the lifecycle and typed contract; `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/DataFlow.rs` for query adaptation; the existing ArrowData tests for lifecycle evidence; docs/spec/refounding records for the public contract. `ArrowFileReader.rs` is the consumed provider ABI, not a place to move #2969's provider implementation. #2969 owns only `Prelude/Parquet.rs` and its official reader closure.

## Root mechanism
one checked `ArrowImported<Row>` owner over an Arrow C schema/array pair. Safe callers see immutable typed schema/report/row operations. Only `unsafe import_c` accepts foreign pointers; it requires release callbacks, claims top-level pointers, validates the complete representable tree before exposure, and uses one Arc owner. The producer's base callback owns recursive child release; Foundation never independently invokes child callbacks. Copy, shared, and no-copy modes have distinct, truthful reports; incompatible no-copy conversions return E4305.

## Ordered work
1. Freeze and publish the supported schema matrix: names, primitive physical types, UTF-8/binary widths and offsets, nullability, dictionaries, slices/offsets, children, row/column/count/buffer ceilings, and expected `ArrowRow` fields. State Arrow C versus Arrow IPC/Parquet explicitly.
2. Keep error meanings stable: E4301 UnsupportedSchema, E4302 MalformedLayout, E4303 Ownership, E4304 Limit, E4305 CopyRefused, E4306 ProducerFailure. Diagnostics must give operation, reason, and actionable unsupported/copy/refusal information.
3. Complete lifecycle witnesses using producer callback counters: normal drop, cloned handles, move, alias/duplicate import, producer failure, malformed schema/layout cleanup, repeated release, and child release delegated to the producer. Assert one top-level callback per claimed base and no safe view after failed validation.
4. Complete storage witnesses: shared/no-copy retains the producer buffers and reports retained bytes; copy owns independent bytes and reports copied bytes; incompatible no-copy refuses rather than silently converting. Match report bytes to actual buffer traversal.
5. Keep the consumer cutover in `DataFlow`: decode each row through `ArrowRow`, then hand the resulting rows to the ordinary deferred query carrier. Do not add an Arrow-specific aggregator, scheduler, foreign-lifetime policy, or raw-pointer API.
6. Run the same semantic fixture through every applicable AOT, interpreter, JIT, and web path. If a target cannot carry the exact provider/ABI, record the target and registered reason rather than substituting CSV, JSON, or a fabricated empty batch.
7. Document the contract and examples as normal typed query code; expert no-copy/copy choices remain explicit settings and do not change the beginner-safe owner default.

## Consumer cutover
#2969 returns a bounded provider pair to `ArrowFileReader::read`; Foundation validates and owns it; DataFlow consumes only `ColumnBatch<Row>`. Remove/avoid any parallel raw Arrow owner or query implementation. Parquet decoding and external format dependencies stay in #2969; Arrow C ownership stays here.

## Dependencies
- **D-COLUMNAR-BOUNDARY1=A:** ratified owner/lifetime decision; no new Arrow ABI ballot.
- **#2969 / D-DATA-READER1:** provider is a downstream consumer; it must return the pair through `ArrowFileReader` and must not duplicate ownership.
- **#2035:** existing analytics card does not redefine this ABI or add Parquet; keep its excluded scope intact.
- **D-FFI-CAP1 / existing foreign ownership laws:** preserve explicit ownership transfer and foreign trust labels.

## Sources
- Packet contract/criteria: `~/.cache/jet-luna/ballot-prep-20260906/interop-context.json:76-149`; ratified decision D-COLUMNAR-BOUNDARY1 at `:152-287`.
- Arrow C ABI and errors: `crates/jet-foundation/src/ArrowData.rs:1-10,25-54,56-83,87-151`.
- Typed owner/report/row hook: `ArrowData.rs:318-415` (`ArrowCopyDisposition`, `ArrowImportReport`, immutable `ArrowImported<Row>`, `ColumnBatch<Row>`, `ArrowRow`).
- Foreign import/lifecycle: `ArrowData.rs:750-842` (`from_spec`, sole unsafe `import_c`, claims, validation, copy drop); `:845-912` (Arc owner, one base release each, producer-owned child release rule, duplicate pointer claims).
- Validation/copy/limits: `ArrowData.rs:914-1084` and the continuation through `:1308` (schema names/types/nullability, children, offsets, dictionaries, buffers, limits, copy refusal/accounting).
- Provider boundary consumed by #2969: `crates/jet-foundation/src/ArrowFileReader.rs:1-21,44-119,121-190,193-221`; Foundation owns provider contract, bounds, error mapping, and `ArrowImported`; Parquet/Arrow C are explicit separate format codes and Arrow IPC is rejected.
- Query consumer: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/DataFlow.rs:2496-2540`; rows go through `ArrowRow` into ordinary `jet_data_query`, with no independent grouping/aggregation/lifetime policy.
- Existing focused tests: `ArrowData.rs:1815-1930,1950-2017,2128-2130` (copy/shared accounting, malformed offsets, no-copy refusal, dictionary/limit checks, one C-owner release, malformed cleanup).
- Official primary source: `https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/CDataInterface.html` says the C definitions are a small stable ABI that can be copied without an Arrow software dependency, supports zero-copy and release callbacks, and is not storage/IPC.

cards.title: Use the official Arrow Rust reader behind the format boundary
cards.body:
Should the native Parquet reader reuse Arrow Rust behind Jet’s checked data boundary?

Mina runs the same sales query on sales.parquet. A format name that returns an unavailable-bridge error does not finish that job.

Source-backed design finding F07b; proposed public behavior, not a fresh runtime defect. The owner’s fresh-compiler construction failure remains accepted ground truth. This audit did not retry the compiler or full suite.

This is an explicit stdlib dependency decision. The retrieved official documentation identifies parquet 59.3.0. Pin its resolved closure and license/provenance through Jetpack before implementation. No automatic future version or arbitrary codec plugin is approved. F07a remains a separate ABI-only choice. Card #2035 is not redefined or reopened to pretend it included this reader.

## Authority
Planning only; preserve criteria/evidence and ratified D-DATA-READER1=A. No new owner gate or implementation claim.

## Implementation


## Owned paths
`crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Prelude/Parquet.rs` for the provider implementation; the package manifest/Jetpack lock/provenance inputs that select `parquet 59.3.0`; provider-focused tests and independent-writer fixtures; existing DataFlow/query callers for cutover verification. `crates/jet-foundation/src/ArrowFileReader.rs` and `ArrowData.rs` are consumed boundaries owned by #2968, not implementation locations for the reader.

## Root mechanism
a bounded byte slice enters one registered provider. `ParquetRecordBatchReaderBuilder` decodes actual Parquet metadata, schema, compression, row groups, and values. The provider enforces input/rows/columns/children/dictionary/total-byte bounds and supported logical/physical types, catches panics, maps failures to stable provider statuses, and transfers one Arrow C schema/array tree. Foundation then validates and owns the pair. There is no JSON canonical blob, serialize-and-reparse path, Arrow IPC alias, arbitrary codec plugin, network fetch, or compiler-crate dependency.

## Ordered work
1. Freeze `parquet 59.3.0`, its exact resolved Arrow/codec/features closure, licenses, source/revision/provenance, and target support through Jetpack. Add the exact docs.rs URL and dependency evidence to the plan/provenance; do not say merely “official Arrow.”
2. Define a real independent-writer corpus: files produced by at least two independent Parquet writers, with supported primitive/logical types, nullability, dictionaries, slices/offsets, compression codecs in the selected feature matrix, nested structures within the declared depth, empty/one/multiple row groups, and the exact expected query values.
3. Route every file through `ArrowFileReader::read(FORMAT_PARQUET, ...)`, not a JSON side channel. Verify provider registration, repeated same-provider registration, replacement refusal, panic containment, output-pointer nulling on failure, and Foundation handoff to `ArrowImported`.
4. Exercise malformed metadata, invalid offsets, unsupported compression, unsupported type/nesting, oversized input/rows/columns/dictionaries/buffers, truncated bytes, and allocation/concatenation overflow. Map each to a bounded provider status and then to the registered Foundation error; never loop or allocate without the configured ceilings.
5. Cut every Parquet caller over to the typed source/query path and remove any obsolete JSON bridge or unavailable-format path. Keep #2035's historical scope intact; do not claim that its CSV/SQL work supplied a Parquet reader.
6. Qualify native AOT, `jet run`, interpreter, and every applicable web byte-source path with the same typed values and errors. If a target cannot host this provider, record the exact blocked target and reason; do not fallback to CSV, JSON, another decoder, or a fabricated result.
7. Publish the closure/codec/license/target/provenance record and the supported-shape matrix. Any codec/provider/target expansion is a new decision, not an implicit upgrade.

## Consumer cutover
provider output enters #2968's single Foundation owner. DataFlow and ordinary query code consume rows, not Parquet-specific arrays or JSON. The provider never owns release policy, row semantics, or an independent aggregation engine.

## Dependencies
- **D-DATA-READER1=A:** ratified official reader selection; no second reader ballot.
- **D-COLUMNAR-BOUNDARY1=A / #2968:** owns the Arrow C ABI, validation, copy policy, and release lifetime; #2969 returns only the provider pair.
- **#2035:** historical CSV/SQL analytics scope explicitly excluded Parquet; do not reopen or claim it as the reader owner.
- **Jetpack closure/I6:** external format closure must be pinned through Jetpack; compiler/sema crates remain path-only.

cards.title: Models as typed, versioned packages
cards.body:
Should model applications load a checked package instead of rebuilding model contracts around raw arrays?

Sam embeds documents for search. Replacing the model must not silently query an old index whose vectors happen to have the same length.

Source-backed design finding F08a; proposed public behavior, not a fresh runtime defect. The owner’s fresh-compiler construction failure remains accepted ground truth. This audit did not retry the compiler or full suite.

Reuse Jetpack, typed shapes, existing placement/acceleration controls, and the Prelude boundary. Do not write protected decisions. A model signature is not a new tensor language. Package identity changes invalidate incompatible indexes without automatic reinterpretation. The backend provider and its foreign dependency are decided separately in D-MODEL-BACKEND1.
cards.plan:
## Authority
Planning only; preserve criteria/evidence and ratified D-MODEL-PACKAGE1=A. No new owner gate or implementation claim.

## Implementation


## Owned paths
`crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Model.rs` for package facts, tensor contract, identity, artifact verification, index compatibility, and provider seam; package fixtures/examples for a real `.Model` output and index; diagnostics/spec docs for E-MODEL-SIGNATURE, E-MODEL-PROVENANCE, and E-MODEL-LOAD. `OnnxRuntimeProvider.rs` is #2971's provider consumer; do not move runtime policy into `Model.rs` or create a second model registry/loader.

## Root mechanism
select one ordinary `PackageFacts::outputs` entry whose kind is `.Model`, parse required graph/weights/tokenizer/optional adapter artifacts and typed tensor input/output specs, build one canonical model identity digest, verify every declared artifact through the no-follow authority resolver, and expose one `ModelProvider` seam. Dynamic dimensions are bounded inclusive ranges; concrete TensorData is checked at execution; embedding index identity includes model digest, final dimension, metric, and normalization. Sessions own loaded weights/resources; model package owns contract/errors; provider owns execution only.

## Ordered work
1. Write the complete package field table and fixture: package name/version/license; graph, weights, tokenizer, optional adapter paths and SHA-256; named tensor inputs/outputs, dtype, rank, static/dynamic bounds; provider identity; preprocessing, pooling, normalization, output meaning, metric; custom-operator flag; context/batch/buffer limits.
2. Validate the ordinary `.Model` output and artifact closure. Reject missing/wrong kind/duplicate/malformed fields, traversal/symlink, absent bytes, hash mismatch, undeclared side files, and any network/download attempt with registered model/package errors.
3. Canonicalize and test identity digest. A changed weight/tokenizer/preprocessing/pooling/normalization/output meaning/metric/package version/license must change identity; same final dimension alone must never admit index reuse.
4. Check input/output tensor names, dtype, rank, and concrete dimensions against bounded declarations. Preserve provider neutrality: this card defines the contract and does not choose ONNX or a Jet-owned engine.
5. Expose resource/cancellation/custom-operator/buffer errors through the package/session contract. Keep placement and acceleration authority with D-ACCEL1; do not introduce a tensor language or hidden provider fallback.
6. Cut model consumers to `ModelPackage::load`/`open_with` and `embedding_index_identity`/`check_index_compatibility`. #2971 implements the selected provider behind this seam; no second package identity, loader, registry, or index tagger is allowed.
7. Exercise one real pinned embedding package through native and applicable web provider paths once #2971's fixture exists. Compare the same output policy and preserve visible transfer/conversion/trust boundaries; if the model/provider or web host is unavailable, record the typed failure rather than claiming model execution.

## Consumer cutover
callers stop assembling raw graph/weights/tokenizer/tensor/index metadata independently. They load the ordinary package and pass it to a provider. Existing tensors and acceleration controls remain; no AI dependency is introduced into Jet development itself.

## Dependencies
- **D-MODEL-PACKAGE1=A:** ratified package choice; do not reopen raw-wrapper versus typed-package semantics.
- **#2971 / D-MODEL-BACKEND1=A:** consumes package identity/tensor contract and supplies only execution.
- **D-ACCEL1:** retains placement/provider-selection authority; this card must not add a competing device policy.
- **Jetpack ordinary package/lock authority:** artifacts are declared package inputs, not provider-fetched bytes.

- Prelude/package examples: `examples/features/packages/model_package/package.jet:1-4` and `run.jet:1-4` are examples of package output, not evidence of runtime inference.

cards.title: ONNX Runtime as a pinned model-package provider
cards.body:
Should the model package use pinned ONNX Runtime before adding another owned inference engine?

Mina loads a supported ONNX model and chooses an available execution provider. Unsupported operators must report a real error, not return fabricated outputs.

Source-backed design finding F08b; proposed public behavior, not a fresh runtime defect. The owner’s fresh-compiler construction failure remains accepted ground truth. This audit did not retry the compiler or full suite.

The official release API reported ONNX Runtime v1.29.0, published 2026-08-12. Approval covers this pinned provider and required package closure, not arbitrary upgrades. Compiler seams remain path-only. CPU and device numeric behavior must match the declared exact/approximate policy. Existing D-ACCEL1 retains all provider-selection authority.
cards.plan:
## Authority
Planning only; preserve criteria/evidence and ratified D-MODEL-BACKEND1=A. No new owner gate or implementation claim.

## Implementation


## Owned paths
`crates/jet-pkg-model/src/OnnxRuntimeProvider.rs` for the provider adapter, policy, native dynamic C bridge, web host seam, typed marshalling, provenance, cancellation, and measurement; provider fixture/tests; Jetpack package/lock provenance for the runtime artifact. `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Model.rs` and D-MODEL-PACKAGE1 remain #2970's package identity/tensor owners. Compiler/sema crates remain path-only under I6.

## Root mechanism
one `ModelProvider` implementation consumes an already checked `ModelPackage`. Native mode validates a RuntimePin (exact version 1.29.0, lowercase SHA-256, MIT license, regular non-symlink file) before dynamic C-API loading and selects only CPUExecutionProvider. Web mode receives the same package bytes/policy through an explicit `WebRuntime` host; unavailable host returns a typed load/backend error. Policy is offline, operator closure is explicit and nonempty, custom code is denied, and no runtime/model download or fallback is permitted. TensorData checks concrete shape/dtype/byte count, sessions check input/output signatures and bounds, cancellation is shared, and measurements report only observed load/warm/transfer/peak/output data.

## Ordered work
1. Pin the exact release and cite the official release URL and C API URL in the provenance/spec record. Record runtime artifact hash, license, package/model/artifact hashes, enabled operators, selected provider, custom-code policy, output policy, and offline/download policy. Do not leave the release version/date supported only by an unlinked ballot sentence.
2. Validate `RuntimePin`, `OnnxRuntimePolicy`, and package closure before opening a session. Require provider identity `onnxruntime@1.29.0`, graph/weights/tokenizer/optional adapter closure, exact artifact hashes, CPU provider, nonempty operator closure, and denied custom code.
3. Keep native C API loading/marshalling in the provider adapter. Validate every input/output TensorData name/dtype/shape/byte count and package limits before/after the foreign call. Map unsupported operator/provider, shape, load, runtime, resource, buffer, and cancellation outcomes to declared `ModelError`; never fabricate an output or silently fall back to CPU/another provider.
4. Keep web execution explicit: inject a supported `WebRuntime`/`WebSessionHandle`, pass the same package bytes and policy, validate returned tensors with the same package contract, and return typed unavailable/unsupported errors when no host exists. Do not hide web as native or use another engine.
5. Add a real pinned ONNX fixture and run the same package/workload through native and applicable web provider paths. Record exact versus approximate numeric policy; exact means output digest equality, approximate means a declared domain tolerance, never an omitted comparison.
6. Use `measure`/`compare_same_run` for load time, warm inference observations, input/output transfer bytes, real sampled peak memory or explicit `None`, workload digest, output policy/digest, and full provenance. Do not synthesize peak memory or average away a tier/trust loss.
7. Cut callers to `ModelPackage::open_with` and this one provider; do not create a second model registry, loader, identity, runtime selector, or compiler dependency. Any new execution provider (CUDA/WebGPU/etc.) is a separate owner decision.

cards.title: Let jet run request project preparation from Jetpack
cards.body:
Should jet run prepare a declared missing environment through Jetpack before executing?

Sam checks out a project and runs its main file. The declared locked environment is not realized on this machine yet.

Source-backed design finding F09; proposed public behavior, not a fresh runtime defect. The owner’s fresh-compiler construction failure remains accepted ground truth. This audit did not retry the compiler or full suite.

Explicit amendment to D-VERDICT-2188-1 and D-ACCEPT-2189. D-ENVFLAG1 remains unchanged. The proposed --no-prepare flag is an owner-gated CLI surface; register it in the canonical command table. Never activate from merely browsing an editor folder. Locked hash mismatches, unavailable offline content, and missing trust fail before execution.
cards.plan:
## Authority
Planning only; preserve criteria/evidence and ratified D-RUN-PREPARE1=A. No new owner gate or implementation claim.

## Implementation


## Owned paths
`Source/CmdCompile.rs` and `Source/main.rs` remain the canonical Jet-side coordinator; `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs` and `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/package_files.rs` remain the single command/flag registry; `crates/jetpack/src/CLI/run_enter_dev.rs` and its existing realize/trust/lock modules remain the Jetpack owner; `crates/jet-driver/src/Loader.rs` remains pure lookup/refusal; `docs/spec/diagnostics.md`, completion/help snapshots, examples, and the stale refounding tooling note must be migrated together. Do not implement a second resolver, shell activation mechanism, or Jetpack-side interpretation of `--no-prepare`.

## Root mechanism
`project_environment_requirement` first proves that the source actually imports a declared package and that the matching environment is inactive. Core-only/local programs run directly; browsing a directory does not activate anything. For `run`, `require_project_environment` calls `prepare_project_environment`; that function rejects `--no-prepare` only before the `--` program-argument separator, locates the current Jet binary/Jetpack engine, forwards only Jetpack-owned environment flags to `jetpack env`, appends `--`, and forwards the original Jet argv to the child. The child runs under the verified marker. Non-`run` verbs remain refusal-only E1355. Jetpack owns plan selection, locked-channel replay, trust admission, realization, concurrency, warm reuse, lifecycle, and visible command execution.

## Ordered work
1. Treat the ratified packet decision as authority and update stale docs that call `--no-prepare` proposed. Keep D-ENVFLAG1 unchanged; `--env`, lock, offline/online, trust, flake, pure, and target selection retain their existing owners.
2. Verify the command table/help/completion path has one `run [<file.jet|dir>] [--no-prepare] [-- <args>]` spelling. Ensure `--no-prepare` is parsed by the Jet parent and is not reinterpreted as a Jetpack environment flag after delegation.
3. Verify source admission: declared environment plus actual package import is required; an editor folder, nearby `env.jet`, or package-independent source does not trigger Jetpack. Already active matching environments reuse their identity without recursive delegation.
4. Verify refusal/delegation: non-`run` commands emit E1355; `jet run --no-prepare` emits E1355 before invoking Jetpack or mutating the lock/store; missing Jetpack/current executable emits E1356; normal `jet run` dispatches exactly once to Jetpack.
5. Verify the `--` boundary specifically. The parent scans only arguments before `--`; only Jetpack-owned flags (`--offline`, `--online`, `--trust`, `--flake`, `--pure`, `--yes`, `--json`, `--no-color`, `--fixtures`, `--env`, `--preset`) go to Jetpack. The original raw argv, including compiler flags and program arguments, goes to the child. A literal `--no-prepare` after `--` must remain a program argument, not trigger parent refusal.
6. Verify Jetpack's existing locked/trust/offline behavior: exact lock/hash mismatch fails before execution; offline missing data names the missing object and makes no network request; untrusted input is denied or asks through the existing trust gate; no lock rewrite, undeclared install, shell hook, or guessed entrypoint occurs. Preserve warm receipt reuse, environment selection, concurrent realization locks, interruption cleanup, and target identity.
7. Exercise fresh admitted, warm, already-active, core-only, missing/offline, mismatch, untrusted, no-prepare, and separator cases in native/interpret/applicable web run paths. Record exact output, diagnostic, child invocation, and store/lock diff. Migrate docs/examples/retired setup instructions only after the command behavior is proved.

## Consumer cutover
users move from the manual `jetpack env --prep` + shell-entry ritual to ordinary `jet run` for declared project environments. `jetpack env --prep` remains the explicit no-execution preparation command. Compiler/package resolution remains pure for build/check/non-run paths. No duplicate dependency resolver or shell activation path is introduced.

## Dependencies
- **D-RUN-PREPARE1=A:** ratified amendment; no new run-preparation ballot.
- **D-VERDICT-2188-1 and D-VERDICT-2189-1:** existing Jet/Jetpack responsibility and environment/preparation authorities explicitly amended by D-RUN-PREPARE1.

- Actual root delegation implementation: `Source/CmdCompile.rs:2156-2166` (declared package import and active environment detection), `:2174-2247` (Jet-owned source/target, Jetpack-owned resolution/lock/trust/realization/concurrency, no-prepare check before `--`, E1355/E1356, dispatch), `:2249-2284` (only Jetpack-owned flags forwarded before separator), `:2287-2305` (run delegates; other verbs remain refusal-only). Call sites include `Source/CmdCompile.rs:2820-2823`, `Source/main.rs:4544-4547,4868-4871`.
- Jetpack realization/trust/lifecycle/warm path: `crates/jetpack/src/CLI/run_enter_dev.rs:1-44,149-246,1963-2013`; parser/flags at `crates/jetpack/src/CLI/parse.rs:200-250`; explicit prep at `run_enter_dev.rs:1662-1671` and warm reuse at `:1963-2007`.

- Stale documentation requiring correction: `docs/audits/jet-refounding-2026-09-05/03-tools-and-systems.md:250-295` still says `--no-prepare` is proposed at `:289`, although D-RUN-PREPARE1 is ratified.

cards.title: Generate and shrink typed operation histories
cards.body:
Should tests generate event sequences and reduce failures to a small replayable history?

Mina tests a booking service against a small reference model. A failure involving reserve, cancel, timeout, and retry should become a short reproducer.

Source-backed design finding F10; proposed public behavior, not a fresh runtime defect. The owner’s fresh-compiler construction failure remains accepted ground truth. This audit did not retry the compiler or full suite.

Do not create a second comparison schema or scheduler. The model cannot call production logic for the behavior being checked. Persist a failing schedule and artifact identity with typed operations. A seed alone is insufficient across changed artifacts. Discard rates and vacuous preconditions are reported; no silent claim of broad exploration.
cards.plan:
## Authority
Planning only; preserve criteria/evidence and ratified D-TEST-HISTORY1=A. No new owner gate or implementation claim.

## Implementation
1. Implement the already-ratified generic testing.histories<Command>(seed, cases, model, actual, observe) interface. No new API ballot is needed. Foundation TestingHistory is the sole generator/shrinker, using D-TEST-COMPARE1 observations and existing controlled-world/replay laws.
2. Derive only type-valid values. Resources, preconditions, distributions, and schedules require declared strategies. The booking campaign is a fixture using this public interface, not its implementation. Support a second operation type to expose accidental specialization.
3. Compare independently obtained public observations. Reject direct/transitive production calls from the oracle; unknown opaque dependencies cannot certify independence. Discarded, unsupported, unavailable, timed-out, cancelled, and invalid campaigns remain non-pass outcomes.
4. Shrink while preserving handle lifetimes, preconditions, event/task dependencies, schedule, and the same failure observation. Record concrete operations/type schema, seed, bounds, distributions, discards, relation, and source/tool/target/artifact identity. Redact secrets without destroying replay; seed alone is insufficient.
5. Expose one contract through Core.jet, sema, generated registration, Prelude, JIT/interpreter/web adapters, and ordinary test/editor output. Remove booking-only public routing or duplicate schema/generator policy. #2950 consumes this artifact and relation, not a second generator.
6. Exercise reserve/cancel/timeout/retry through ordinary Jet code, inject an observable defect, and independently replay the valid minimized counterexample. A private Rust helper cannot meet the public criterion.

## Owned paths
crates/jet-foundation/src/TestingHistory.rs; Core.jet and generated core_calls.rs; Prelude/CoreLib/Top/TestingHistory.rs and the existing checked callback/tier routes. Coordinate the shared Core registry/TestingComparison boundary with #2950. Preserve current met evidence; no second scheduler or test runner.

D-TEST-STRATEGY1=A ratified 2026-09-07. Add optional per-test HistoryStrategy<Command>; omission derives and explicit strategy replaces. Implement the exact five fields and canonical history projections through all tiers, with public resource-lifetime/precondition examples. Main integrates and closes source-only before #2919. cards.title: Boundary census: retain semantic types through adapters and collections
cards.body: Generalize E02, E06, E08, and E10. Mechanically enumerate public boundaries where a known key, unit, shape, nominal identity, nullability, or ownership fact becomes an unqualified String, Float, array, handle, or dynamic record. Classify necessary representation conversion separately from accidental information loss. This is source research, not a claim that every conversion is a bug.
cards.plan:
## Scope
Inspect canonical Core declarations and generated consumers, public data/query aggregates, web request/client descriptions, geometry and tensor bridges, and foreign columnar/model adapters. Use Source/Core.jet, crates/jet-foundation/src/, crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/, and the public reference/example corpus. Reuse #2898 for registration/I9 census; do not duplicate it.

## Method
Generate the public-boundary denominator from the current declaration registry. For each candidate, record the incoming fact, outgoing representation, existing authority, explicit conversion or missing fact, consumers, and evidence. Classify faithful erasure, intentional conversion, required runtime validation, or genuine gap. Retain clean rows so an empty result is auditable. Link F01/F02/F04/F07/F08 owners rather than minting instance cards. File only deduplicated new shapes.

## Acceptance proof
Run the source inventory, inspect its full denominator and unresolved rows, then exercise each claimed runtime defect only with a fresh build when that gate is available. Never infer a runtime bug from a type name or a stale binary.

cards.title: Lifecycle census: dependency, completion, and stale publication rules
cards.body: Generalize E03–E04 and E06–E07. Enumerate stateful dependency and completion mechanisms across computed fields, reactive observers, live queries, tasks, device work, caches, Pool handles, and editor publication. Similar names do not establish identical meaning. Identify exactly where an overlapping rule is reimplemented and where distinct identities must stay distinct.
cards.plan:
## Scope
Inspect computed-field dependencies, ReactiveEventWatch, Top/LiveQuery, MathTaskMem Pool generation, Core/Host.js adapters, task cancellation/completion, game/compute resource lifetimes, RunCache/jet-store, and existing query-service publication. Coordinate with #2949 and #2898; do not replace their implementation work.

## Method
Mechanically enumerate fields and transitions for owner identity, generation, revision, completion, cancellation, dependency membership, and invalidation. For each path, identify the authoritative state, mutation point, publication/use gate, stale outcome, and cleanup obligation. Compare actual transition contracts, not field names. Classify identity differences as intentional or overlapping duplicated policy. Map gaps to F03/F05/F06/F12 and existing owners.

## Acceptance proof
Produce the complete source transition table and a minimal event history for each alleged mismatch. Later runtime proofs use fresh matching artifacts and retain replayed histories. No fresh compiler construction or broad suite is part of this census publication.

1. Every selected lifecycle has an explicit owner, state-transition table, use/publication gate, completion definition, and cleanup rule.
2. Revision, generation, lifetime, clock time, device completion, and semantic cache identity stay separate unless evidence proves an identical contract.
3. Each claimed mismatch has a replayable event sequence and a single structural owner; source-only predictions are labeled and not promoted to runtime failures.
4. The census reuses #2949/#2898 and adopted state/effect mechanisms; no universal context, second scheduler, second reactive engine, or duplicate cache law is proposed.

cards.plan:
## Owned scope
Correct the Errors and results and introductory failure-handling prose in docs/spec/reference/core-library.md. Inspect matching first-hour examples and references for the same retired claim. Do not change semantics or ratified decisions.

## Change
Teach the ordinary implicit propagation path first. Then show explicit fallback, pattern handling, contextual failure information, and application-owned conversion declarations as the expert choices they are. Distinguish the default Err route from typed-target orphan rules. Remove contradictory blanket statements rather than adding another caveat section.

cards.title: Compound-assignment gauntlet pair is noise-dominated: benefit unproven either way
cards.body:
Three honest measurements of the same pair, on three cleanly built binaries, straddle the strict comparator's 1.00 line -- so the current cell cannot resolve whether compound assignment beats the plain spelling it replaces. It is not evidence of a loss and not evidence of a win.

Measurements (100000-element reduction, 3 warmups, 9 trials, fresh process per trial, identical checked stdout both sides):
- binary a3a41a... (Finished dev ... 2m 10s): surface=2230.891ms plain=2188.131ms ratio=1.0195417916 verdict=loss
- binary adc47ab3125e (Finished dev ... 1m 35s): surface=2269.144ms plain=2317.280ms ratio=0.9792273700 verdict=win
- binary e731d4467544 (Finished dev ... 3m 49s): surface=2223.980ms plain=2229.577ms ratio=0.9974896584 verdict=inconclusive

The verdict flipped across changes that touch neither arithmetic nor assignment lowering (a sema is_extern effect guard, a compiler-owned type row). Spread explains it: surface trials on the third run range 618.078ms with IQR 315.974 (raw [2747.927, 2797.9, 2208.975, 2181.694, 2179.822, 2185.474, 2223.98, 2251.189, 2249.756]) while plain ranges 73.488 with IQR 30.671. The surface arm's first two trials are ~25% high, so warmup is not settling within 3 iterations for that arm.

Two consequences, and the second is the bigger one:
1. This specific cell needs either a workload where the two spellings can actually differ, or enough trials plus outlier handling that a confidence interval excludes 1.00.
2. The standing rule ratified as D-PERF-SURFACE-WIN1 will pass or fail every future surface by noise until the harness's pair-measurement design is fixed. The gate machinery is correct and fails closed; the measurement protocol underneath it is not yet trustworthy at the few-percent scale where these deltas live.

Corroboration from an independent lane: tier-census spelling pairs measured on the same binary all sit between 1.7% and 6.2% delta (if_else 1.73%, fallback 2.4%, compound 2.48%, explicit_copy 2.82%, expr_arrow 6.17%), i.e. the same band in which this pair reversed sign twice.

Evidence: gauntlet/performance-surface-evidence.json (SHA256 8db541eed32a2b8c93860f3a3bcf6ddd4a98eb91e1c6b162a8ded82f77fbfe8b) plus dated historical receipts gauntlet/performance-surface-evidence-20260906T154128Z.json and -20260906T155749Z.json. Gate output: 'latest real-data surface gate fails closed: compound_assign_vs_binary_assign surface=2223.98ms plain=2229.577ms ratio=0.9974896583522345 verdict=inconclusive; findings=inconclusive'.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Resolve only the `compound_assign_vs_binary_assign` performance-surface cell with a reproducible win, loss or inconclusive receipt. Language meaning, workload, tier and the strict D-PERF-SURFACE-WIN1=A gate stay unchanged.

## Current state (evidence work landed)
- `Tools/gauntlet/harness/performance-surface.mjs:29-42`: TRIALS=100, ORDER_SEED=2977, BOOTSTRAP_RESAMPLES=10000, BOOTSTRAP_SEED=2977. `:269-273` hold the strict verdicts: a win needs ratio < 1 and upper95 < 1; lower95 >= 1 is a loss; an interval crossing 1 is inconclusive.
- `Tools/gauntlet/performance-surface-evidence.json` `.pairs[0]`: 100 trial pairs, ratio 0.99604, `confidence.ratio_lower95` 0.99094, `ratio_upper95` 1.00526, verdict **inconclusive**, method `paired_index_bootstrap`, 10000 resamples.
- Historical receipts `...-20260906T154128Z.json`, `...155749Z.json` and `...160409Z.json` are present, plus the 20260921 snapshots.
- Pair identity: surface `total += i`, plain `total = total + i`, range `0..<100000`, output `performance-surface:compound_assign_vs_binary_assign:4999950000`, target `jet run --interpret`, metric `wall_time_ms`.
- Since 0e4796f90, compound read-modify-write shares `binary_route` with plain assignment, so identical lowering makes a strict win unreachable by construction.

## Changes
No code change is expected. Verify criteria 1-8 against the landed runner and receipt and meet them with evidence. If a validator fixture is missing (criterion 8: missing or overlapping CI, stale pair identity, wrong ratio, wrong output, missing samples, unpaired rows), add it to `Tools/gauntlet/harness/performance-surface.test.mjs`. The inconclusive result is a valid outcome of this card; the bug stays visible in the manifest (`bug_card: "#2977"`) until the policy question below is answered.

## Proof
- `node --test Tools/gauntlet/harness/performance-surface.test.mjs Tools/gauntlet/harness/measurement-manifest.test.mjs Tools/gauntlet/harness/integrated-gate.test.mjs` is green.
- `jq '.pairs[0] | {trial_pairs, verdict, c: .confidence.ratio_upper95}' Tools/gauntlet/performance-surface-evidence.json` shows 100 pairs, `inconclusive`, and an upper bound above 1.
- `sha256sum` of the three 20260906 receipts matches the hashes recorded in the manifest's historical links (criterion 1).

## Batch
batch-measure. Evidence verification only.

## Dependencies
None. Separate owner policy question, not a blocker for this card: whether D-PERF-SURFACE-WIN1 should accept identical-MIR proof plus an inconclusive receipt as parity for pure-sugar surfaces. Triage recommends A. If it is ratified, file it as its own decision; this card does not change the gate.
cards.checkSteps:
Preparation only; do not run these steps during planning. Run them after implementation in a clean detached checkout.

1. `scripts/agent/jet-env cargo build --bin jet` — record the exact revision, toolchain, host, CPU affinity, and `target/debug/jet` digest.
2. `JET_TEST_SCRATCH_DIR="$HOME/.cache/jet-luna/perf-surface-pair" TMPDIR="$HOME/.cache/jet-luna/perf-surface-pair" scripts/agent/jet-env node gauntlet/harness/performance-surface.mjs` — expect one receipt containing ten balanced warmups, 100 paired trials, raw vectors, order labels, exact output checks, and the paired-bootstrap interval.
3. `node --test gauntlet/harness/measurement-manifest.test.mjs` — expect fixtures to reject absent or overlapping confidence evidence, stale identity, wrong ratio, wrong output, missing samples, and unpaired rows; accept only a strict proven win.
4. `node gauntlet/harness/integrated-gate.mjs --check --json --commit "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"` — inspect `performance_surface_pairs.pairs` and `findings`; unrelated required-cell failures do not change this card's pair result.
5. Compare the three immutable dated receipts and the preserved fourth observation by digest. Confirm the new receipt names the exact pair, target, metric, source digests, artifact, host, raw samples, statistics, and verdict. A point estimate below `1` without an interval wholly below `1` must remain non-passing.

cards.plan:
## Authority and scope

No board dependency is recorded. `ReactiveEventWatch.rs` is the canonical AOT async-event state machine; JIT and interpreter adapters must invoke the same policy, queue, scope, failure, close, and join semantics. The current JIT bridge and `EventLite` boundary are known seams, not independent semantics. - `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower/method_calls.rs` and `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/routes.rs` (constructor/method route)
- `tests/corelib_parts/runtime.rs`, `tests/event_observations.rs`, `tests/event_hooks.rs`, and `tests/dev_interp_parity.rs`

## Ordered implementation and cutover

1. Build a deterministic real-program reproduction around the existing async-event API: scoped listeners, bounded capacity and overflow, delayed handler failure, `once`/priority, close, and awaited task completion. Define the expected state transitions and dispatch reports from the canonical AOT contract before changing adapters.
2. Trace constructor validation, `on`/`once`/`on_priority`, emit, close, count, and join from TIR lowering/routes through JIT `Reactive.rs`, AOT `ReactiveEventWatch.rs`, and interpreter `MIREval.rs`/`EventLite.rs`. Keep one adapter seam and remove the current synchronous/zero-count/identity shortcuts.
3. Make JIT and interpreter preserve scope lifetime, queue capacity/overflow, failure policy, running/blocked/queued counts, close/cancel transitions, and actual joined task completion while retaining safe callback ownership. Do not weaken the canonical AOT state machine to match an adapter.
4. Preserve the shared constructor ABI and route every checked handle method to the repaired adapter. `once` must remain once-only and priority must affect dispatch order; neither may collapse to plain `on`.
5. Add focused AOT/JIT/interpreter parity and failure/close/queue observations, then review for a missing route or tier-specific semantic branch. Keep existing runtime/event observation coverage and update only stale expectations.

## Acceptance and proof

After implementation, run the deterministic real-program reproduction and focused runtime/event parity surfaces on AOT, default JIT, and interpreter. Require identical scoped lifetime, queue overflow, failure report, close, running/blocked/queued counts, dispatch order, and joined-completion transitions; a callback that outlives its scope, a dropped failure, an identity join, or a synchronous/zero-count adapter fails proof. This preparation claims no run.

## Dependencies and non-goals

No board dependency or owner ballot is open. The canonical AOT contract is the authority. Do not invent a second event implementation, alter unrelated task semantics, or hide unsupported behavior with a fallback.

cards.title: Reconcile the directory-walk example type and authority contract
cards.body:
The previous audit binary reports E0302 for entry.is_dir at lines 18, 19, and 25 of grep_scan.jet, plus E1220 for Time.Wait authority. It never reaches the sequential/parallel comparison. The latest source build failed independently. Do not assume the fixture, field API, type inference, or authority metadata is the cause before checking the canonical contract.

Source and reproduction evidence belongs to the 2026-09-09 playlist audit #2989. This card is not a completion claim.
Identified earlier binary SHA-256: ef7c0fcc8a697038a42558272a015fbb104915fa4bc347234f78a94207de182a. Recheck with the repaired fresh build before deciding whether code changes remain necessary.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Make the Jet Core `WalkEntry` the canonical checked record (`path`, `relative`, `is_dir`, `depth`), identical on every tier, so the directory-walk example type-checks and runs with only FS.Read authority.

## Current state
- Criteria 1, 3 and 4 are met. Criterion 2 is open.
- Core/files/files.jet:58-61 declares `WalkEntry { path, is_dir }` only. `walk_rec` (:644-658) builds `WalkEntry{path, is_dir}` without `relative` or `depth`, and `walk_impl` (:661-676) reads the ignore file through the same selector for all three entry points. `walk`, `walk_parallel` (same walk, no thread pool) and `walk_files` start at :679. Their `ignore: String?` has no default.
- Examples/features/io/grep_scan.jet:14-15 calls `fs.walk(root)` with one argument and reads `entry.relative` (:18-19, :27). Its golden is Examples/features/expected/io/grep_scan.out.
- The host record already has all four fields (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/CommonTypes.rs:580-585, `depth: i64`). The registry signature is Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreHostSignatures.jet:77 (`[path, String?] -> [WalkEntry] IOError!`).
- A 2026-09-15 log shows AOT E0308 `Option<JetInt>` versus `i64` for `WalkEntry.depth`.

## Changes
1. files.jet: `pub struct WalkEntry { pub path: String; pub relative: String; pub is_dir: Bool; pub depth: Int }`. `walk_rec` fills `relative` with `relative_impl(path, root)` (:602) and threads `depth` (root children = 1). Give the ignore parameter `String?{None}` so that one-argument calls type-check, and keep CoreHostSignatures.jet:77 consistent with that.
2. If AOT still maps `depth` to `Option<JetInt>`, fix the field typing at the emitter (Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit), not in the fixture. The host kernel (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/FSWalk.rs) keeps `depth` as a plain Int.
3. Authority: the walk and the reads need FS.Read only. Grant no blanket Time.Wait.
4. grep_scan.jet prints `{entry.relative}:{entry.is_dir}:{entry.depth}` so that every field is read. Update the .out.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=io/grep_scan cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes (AOT and default run).
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/io/grep_scan.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/io/grep_scan.out` prints nothing.
- The output ends with `walks agree: true`, and the nested entries show depth 2.

## Batch
batch-core-files: one Core/files record plus at most one emitter field-typing fix.

## Dependencies
None. #2990 is done.

cards.title: Reconcile progress iterator errors and authority with its example
cards.body:
The previous audit binary reports E2402 for ParseError propagation in progress.jet line 75 and E1220 for Time.Wait authority. It does not exercise the progress lifecycle. cards.plan:
**Goal.** Make the canonical `Examples/features/io/progress.jet` run through the one lazy D-COREIO1=A adapter `io.progress(source: Iter<T>, description, template) -> Iter<T>` on every tier. That covers:
- real source-pull counts, with no fabricated totals
- ParseError propagation through `try_collect`
- the checked `Time.Wait` authority
- no frames in machine output

**Current state.**
- `Core/term/term.jet:117` declares only `pub fn progress(label: String) IOError! -[IO, Time.Wait]>`.
- `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreHostSignatures.jet:121` types `progress` as `[String] -> Unit IOError!` only.
- `CoreCallRows.jet:101-102` carries `progress` (max arity 3 → `jet_std_io_progress`) plus a `progress_iter` host route (`jet_std_io_progress_iter`, `[false, true, true]`).
- `Examples/features/io/progress.jet:7-83` uses the 3-argument Iter form. Frozen snapshot5 reported E0104 "progress expects 1 argument, got 3" and E0112. The old E2402/E1220 binary (SHA ef7c0fcc…) is historical only.
- The label form is still used by `Examples/features/io/terminal_parity.jet:38` and `tests/conformance/corpus/core/term/progress.jet:6`.
- Core has no same-name overloads (0 duplicate `pub fn` names across Core/*.jet) and no default parameters. So the two shapes cannot both be Jet-source declarations. They stay one registry-typed host member with arity-selected routes until a ratified variadic/overload surface exists.
- Retained host adapter: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs` and `Prelude/Core/HumanOutput.rs` (frames, counts, drop cleanup).
- #2990 is done.

**Changes.**
1. `CoreHostSignatures.jet`: type `progress` for arity 1 (`String -> Unit IOError!`) and arity 3 (`Iter<T>, String, String -> Iter<T>`, routing to `progress_iter`). Mirror this in the Rust sema signature table so the shipped binary accepts the example. Drop the source-owned `pub fn progress` from `term.jet` and keep a doc comment naming both forms, so the host row is the single declaration.
2. `Time.Wait`: follow the checked record in `CoreCalls.jet:184-186`, with no effect exception.
3. `Compiler/JetEval/Source/Routes/Core.jet`: add the interpreter route for `progress_iter`, including `filter`/`filter_map` callback evaluation and ParseError propagation through `try_collect`. Fix the matching JIT/MIR seam so an error stops the lazy pull with its real value (no panic, no MIR ICE).
4. Host adapter: finish exactly once on exhaustion, break or drop. Count actual pulls. An unknown total renders as unknown. No frames when output is non-TTY or machine/JSON.
5. Rerun the example on a real PTY and on non-TTY capture, and record both in the receipt (c3).

**Proof.** The commands in add_criteria, plus the PTY and non-TTY run of `target/debug/jet run Examples/features/io/progress.jet` recorded on the card.

**Batch.** `batch-host-runtime`: registry signature, JIT/interpreter routes and the retained Prelude adapter, proven by a tier-parity golden after one build.

**Dependencies.** None. #2990 is done.

cards.title: Add bounded source-hotspot evidence to the existing profiler
cards.body:
The root-of-all-evil talk argues for measured execution concentration, not universal percentages or a ban on early optimization. Jet already has .jettrace identities, domain spans, source maps, and cost facts. The inspected schema lacks weighted source-frequency rows with method and coverage semantics. Source facts are not runtime hotness. Public capture scope needs an owner choice; current runtime proof is blocked by the compiler build.

Source and reproduction evidence belongs to the 2026-09-09 playlist audit #2989. This card is not a completion claim.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Close criterion 4 of the ratified source-hotspot profiler (D-PROFILE-DETAIL1=A, D-PROFILE-METHOD1=A). Repeated `jet perf run` captures must have identical source-profile identity with no spurious `no_samples`, and capture overhead (wall vs CPU) must be measured under the performance policy.

## Current state
- Criteria 1-3 and 5 are met: one `.jettrace` recorder, source rows plus derived function totals, and explicit no-sample, unsupported and truncated states (`Source/CmdPerf.rs:1011` `no_samples`).
- The 2026-09-28 ProfilerOverhead run failed repeated-run identity. The periodic observe writer publishes every 100 ms (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Observe.rs:787-789`), while the host polls every 25 ms (`Source/CmdPerf.rs:217, 242`). Overhead measured wall +15% and CPU +35% on hello/wordcount, with about 90 ms fixed.
- In-tree repair: the exit seam publishes synchronously (`Observe.rs:834-843`), and `child_exited` (`CmdPerf.rs:1929`) observes the unreaped zombie so the exit snapshot stays readable. `tests/jet_perf_trace_parts/capture_run.rs:159` `perf_run_short_program_has_repeatable_source_attribution` checks 3 runs.
- Remaining cost: `poll_observe_snapshot` (`CmdPerf.rs:1885`) walks the tree through `process_children` (`:1939`). When `/proc/<pid>/task/*/children` is unreadable it rescans all of `/proc` (`:1961`) on every 25 ms tick.

## Changes
1. `Source/CmdPerf.rs`: resolve the program pid once and cache the discovered pid set. Rescan children only when no snapshot is found, and rate-limit the rescan. Drop the full `/proc` walk when the `children` files are readable. Read the exit snapshot before reaping.
2. Profile the roughly 90 ms fixed host overhead with a wall/CPU split and remove avoidable work in the capture path. Add no new recorder and no second export truth.
3. Keep sample-by-default and explicit-count semantics unchanged.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test jet_perf_trace_capture_run -- perf_run_short_program_has_repeatable_source_attribution` passes.
- Paired measurement under the `Tools/perf/dashboard.sh` policy: 1 warmup + 20 samples per arm, `jet run X` vs `jet perf run X --out <scratch>.jettrace`, for `Examples/features/basics/hello.jet`, `Examples/features/collections/wordcount.jet` and `Examples/features/basics/pattern_matching.jet`. Pass: all 20 profile identities are equal per program with 0 `no_samples`, and wall/CPU overhead medians are recorded on the card. This criterion measures and does not set a threshold. Any performance-motivated surface remains gated on a paired cell.

## Batch
`batch-host-cli`: perf/inspect host tooling.

## Dependencies
None open.

log.text: Overnight proof 2026-09-29: PASS. Fixed overhead is about 200 ms wall and 130-140 ms CPU per capture. Before the fix it was +15%/+35% on hello, with no_samples. One hello capture sample was a 15.5 s outlier (p90) under machine load. The criterion measures and sets no threshold.
Phase 0b plan build-out (2026-09-29, Opus 5.5): plan rewritten for the self-hosted direction with a runnable proof and batch key batch-host-cli.

Phase 0 triage 2026-09-28 (misc1b, Opus 5.5): E_BUILD. Profiler source evidence implemented (crit 1-3,5 met); crit 4 measured 2026-09-28 and FAILED repeated-run identity: short programs race the 100 ms observe publication against the 25 ms poll, and host overhead is ~90 ms fixed plus /proc rescans. Evidence: Card log 2026-09-28 (ProfilerOverhead): Source/CmdPerf.rs:1799-1882 polling; overhead wall +15%/CPU +35% on hello/wordcount

Crit 4 measured 2026-09-28 (ProfilerOverhead, Opus 5.5; debug snapshot of de1e1da15; 1 warmup plus 20 samples per arm under the dashboard.sh policy; data in ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/ProfilerOverhead/). Capture overhead: wordcount wall +15.3% and CPU +37.6%; pattern_matching wall +1.3% and CPU +25.3%; hello wall +15.5% and CPU +35.5%. Nearly all of it is host-side: a fixed ~90 ms plus polling that rescans /proc when the child has no children (CmdPerf.rs:1799-1882). Repeated-run identity FAILS. Short programs race the 100 ms observe publication against the 25 ms poll, so the same run gives no_samples one time and captured the next (CmdPerf.rs:215-239). fn_locations_from_source ignores comments (JetTrace.rs:305), and its range covers only the fn header (323-324). Every sample is attributed to the entry fn (CmdPerf.rs:889-976). Trace CPU covers the whole process, including compile time. overhead_status is always not_measured. The ratified --profile-method=sample|count flag is missing. Criterion stays open; fix follows.

Removed automatic reruns and any second recording trigger. Remaining losses are source information size and explicit counter overhead. D-PROFILE-DETAIL1 and D-PROFILE-METHOD1 are complete short ballots, not ratifications.

cards.title: Expose evidence-backed architecture advice through existing inspection
cards.body:
The de-slop video demonstrates one ordering policy split between optimistic UI and persistence. Two individually simple helpers can disagree. Audit probe optimistic_rank(x)=x+1 versus persisted_rank(x)=x+2 gave all cognitive scores zero and printed false on the identified previous binary. Complexity is not an architecture score. Decide whether Jet should expose bounded architectural candidates through existing inspection or keep this as operator review.

Source and reproduction evidence belongs to the 2026-09-09 playlist audit #2989. This card is not a completion claim.
cards.plan:
## Ratified implementation scope
