cards.title: Preserve canonical typed JSON errors through HTTP
cards.body:
Preserve canonical typed JSON errors through HTTP.

The HTTP helper discards path/reason data already produced by the canonical decoder and labels it InvalidFraming. Consumers lose the field-level repair cause.

Retain the canonical accumulated FieldError values through request/response JSON projection. Prefer the proposed HTTPError.Decode(errors: [FieldError]) case after owner approval. Keep one decoder and no message parsing.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-script-f01. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-SCRIPT-HTTP-DECODE1=A: `HTTPError.Decode(errors: [FieldError])` carries the canonical decoder's field errors through HTTP JSON helpers. Framing failures stay `InvalidFraming`, and nothing is decoded twice.

## Current state
- Core/http/http.jet:29-51: `HTTPError` has no Decode case. Response and request framing checks return `.InvalidFraming` (:476-497, :511-549).
- The typed JSON body decode lives in the Rust bridge, which collapses InvalidData into `JetHTTPBridgeError::InvalidFraming` (crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Prelude/HTTP.rs:2057-2058). The card log also points at HTTPMessage.rs:765-785.
- Server JSON output is `json<T: Encode>` (Core/http/server.jet:53-55). The `[FieldError]` carrier precedent is Core/db/db.jet:87.
- #3665 (ready) is moving the HTTP client semantics from the Rust Prelude into Core/http Jet and will delete the bridge above.
- Research: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-script-f01.

## Changes
1. http.jet: add `Decode(errors: [FieldError])` to `HTTPError`.
2. In the Jet body path that #3665 creates, the response and request `json<T>()` helpers call `json.decode<T>` once. `[FieldError]` maps to `.Decode(errors)`, and a JSON syntax error becomes `.Decode` with one FieldError (path "", the syntax reason and offset). Transport framing failures stay `.InvalidFraming`. There is no message parsing and no second validator.
3. Keep the body caps (C_MAX_BODY_BYTES), one-shot consumption (`BodyConsumed`) and privacy redaction unchanged.
4. Update every exhaustive `HTTPError` match in Core/, Examples/ and Jetpack/.

## Proof
- New test `cargo test --test http_client_law -- http_json_decode_errors_stay_typed`, over a loopback server, returning in turn malformed JSON, valid JSON with a wrong field type, and a bad Content-Length. It asserts `.Decode` with a syntax FieldError, `.Decode` with the path `user.age`, and `.InvalidFraming`, on default run, `--interpret` and AOT.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=net/http_client cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` still passes.

## Batch
batch-core-net: Core/http error surface. It lands in the same build as the #3665 port.

## Dependencies
#3665 (the Jet HTTP client body path).

4. A stable-source focused receipt covers native/default/interpreter and applicable web projections; source reading alone is not closure.

cards.title: Give a loaded plugin an explicit safe release lifecycle
cards.body:
Give a loaded plugin an explicit safe release lifecycle.

The inspected runtime can remove a plugin instance, but the scoped public inventory exposes load and named calls without a Close route. Long-running hosts need to release completed extensions without retaining every loaded instance.

Prefer Plugin support for existing Close, using ordinary ownership/borrows. Preserve the frozen Component, Authority and execution limits. Do not add another runtime or a dynamic eval API.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-script-f03. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Under D-SCRIPT-PLUGIN-CLOSE1=A, give a loaded `Plugin` the existing nominal `Close` lifecycle: `close(^plugin)`. The release is exactly once, stale handles fail before store access, and there is no plugin-only lifecycle, second runtime or eval API.

## Current state
- `Core/plugin/plugin.jet` (17 lines) declares only the intrinsic `core.plugin.load` boundary. There is no Close.
- Language close: `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Statements.jet:2287-2300` requires `close(^x)` with the move marker and a nominal `Close` implementation (E0104/E0201).
- The host already has release: `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Prelude/Plugin.rs:1242` `jet_plugin_close(handle: u64) -> bool` rejects a nested close during an active call (owner-thread, call-boundary scoped). The generated carrier is `JetPlugin { handle: u64 }`, which is `Copy` (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/HandlesRaylib.rs:245-268`). Load goes through the `jet_plugin_bridge!` macro, and there is no close bridge.
- Witness: `Examples/features/packages/sandbox_mathkit` (a plugin fixture with a frozen `.api`).

## Changes
1. `Core/plugin/plugin.jet`: declare `Close` for `Plugin` forwarding to a `core.plugin.close` provider intrinsic, so the checked source is the single owner. The Copy u64 stays an internal carrier and never becomes a source handle.
2. `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCallRows.jet` plus the Rust `core_calls.rs` mirror: add the `Plugin.close` receiver row. In `Compiler/JetSema`, treat `Plugin` as a move-only resource: use after `close(^p)` is the existing use-after-move error, and a close while a borrowed alias, bound function or owned task capture is live is the existing borrow error.
3. Add `jet_plugin_close` to the `jet_plugin_bridge!` macro (AOT) and route the JIT and interpreter to the same bridge symbol. A stale or closed handle in a later dynamic call returns a typed plugin error before touching the store. A close during an active call is refused, as `Plugin.rs:1242` already does.
4. Document the lifecycle in `Docs/spec` core.plugin.

## Proof
- Extend `Examples/features/packages/sandbox_mathkit` to load, call, `close(^p)`, load again, call, then close after a failed call. `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=packages/sandbox_mathkit Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes, and `jet run` and `jet run --interpret` output diffs empty against the golden.
- Add UI fixtures `tests/ui/plugin_use_after_close.jet` and `tests/ui/plugin_close_while_borrowed.jet`. `JET_UI_FILTER=plugin_ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots` passes.

## Batch
batch-host-runtime: the core of the work is host bridge wiring (`Plugin.rs`/`HandlesRaylib.rs`) plus tier parity.

## Dependencies
None. #3253 (the ABI/unload contract statement) consumes this card's result.

1. Main checks ratified lifecycle decisions before treating this as a new choice.
2. The selected public law explains internal Copy handles, aliases, bound functions, active calls, owned task captures and exactly-once release.
3. Use-after-close is rejected under existing checked ownership; stale dynamic host handles fail before store access.
4. Repeated load/call/close, failure then close and attempted outstanding-borrow close have consumer-visible stable-source receipts.
5. No new ownership mechanism is silently introduced; if existing rules cannot express the law, return the precise change to the owner.

cards.title: Cut plugin examples over to named sandbox exports
cards.body:
Cut plugin examples over to named sandbox exports

Both migrate the same named-export sandbox walkthroughs and capability-import law, removing retired target/plugin and dynamic-call teaching while preserving historical captures.

SCRIPT-F02: A user following the current sandbox example is taught call/call_int/call_bool/call_text and dynamic export lookup that current sema expressly retires with E1257.
Migrate affected plugin examples and teaching text to frozen named exports under the existing Component interface law. Remove the impossible missing-export fallback rather than retaining an alias.
Evidence: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-script-f02

SCRIPT-F35: The zero-import walkthrough and authority-checked host import source teach different trust boundaries.
Use D-EMBED2=C, ratified after D-EMBED1, to correct the stale zero-import walkthrough. Align typed host imports and named-export examples with the canonical authority contract and prove registered versus unregistered imports.
Evidence: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-script-f35

Historical source and frozen-executable evidence retain their recorded identity and uncertainty; this research handoff is not a current-tree proof.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Finish the cutover of the sandbox walkthroughs to frozen named exports and the D-EMBED2=C capability-import law. This single home covers SCRIPT-F02 and SCRIPT-F35. No `.call*` or dynamic lookup, and no `target: plugin` alias. Registered typed imports must work, and absent, wrong-type or ungranted imports must fail before guest side effects.

**Current state**
- The source migration has landed. `Examples/features/packages/sandbox_mathkit/run.jet:1-23` calls the named exports `scale`, `hypot`, `gcd`, `is_enabled` and `greet` under a D-EMBED2=C header. `library_loadable/component_host.jet:1-4` also uses named exports.
- Sema retires dynamic calls in both compilers. `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Plugin.jet:132-134` sends `call`, `call_int`, `call_bool` and `call_text` to E1257 "`Plugin.{method}` is retired" (:111). The Rust mirror is `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/plugin_checks.rs:134`. No UI fixture pins the retired-call diagnostic.
- Goldens: `Examples/features/expected/packages/sandbox_mathkit.out` is run by the golden harness. `library_loadable.out` and `library_loadable_cpp.out` are run by `tests/library_outputs.rs` (`native_and_component_exports_share_one_typed_surface` :115, `component_build_load_and_foreign_call_are_one_surface` :616).
- Stale spec prose remains: `Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:3159` (D-PLUGIN1 "`target: plugin` compiles to…") and :3187 ("application `target: plugin` / `core.plugin`"). The amendment D-ONCE-SANDBOX1=A is at :6814.

**Changes**
1. Update `syntax-decisions.md:3159` and :3187 to name `target: sandbox`, with a pointer to D-ONCE-SANDBOX1. Preserve the D-PLUGIN1 decision history.
2. Add `tests/ui/sandbox_retired_dynamic_call.jet` with `.stderr` (E1257 on `mathkit.call_int("scale", …)`).
3. If no test yet shows an ungranted or absent import failing before guest side effects, add one negative case to `tests/library_outputs.rs` next to `guest_import_rejects_invalid_signature_and_duplicate_native_symbol` (:701).

**Proof**

- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test library_outputs -- native_and_component_exports_share_one_typed_surface component_build_load_and_foreign_call_are_one_surface guest_import_rejects_invalid_signature_and_duplicate_native_symbol` passes.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=sandbox_retired_dynamic_call Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots` passes.
- `rg -n 'target: plugin' Docs/spec Examples` returns only the D-ONCE-SANDBOX1 retirement line.

**Batch**

**Dependencies**
None.

cards.body:
Deliver the existing typed form path without an internal lowering failure.

An ordinary typed form produces no HTML and stops before application execution in every attempted command route.

Repair the existing entry/lowering contract under its existing law, then rerun exact NEST-P001 and a real browser form on an identified current build.

cards.plan:

1. Read the exact law, captured contract and witness at docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-form-entry-lowering. Preserve the recorded date, source identity and any source-integrity correction.
2. Repair the existing entry/lowering contract under its existing law, then rerun exact NEST-P001 and a real browser form on an identified current build.
3. Exercise each contract below on an identified integrated source and executable when execution is part of this deliverable. For an investigation, return the actual supported, unsupported and unknown cells before proposing implementation.
   - Exact input hash72facb9077dbb3168de2278f426ef4ae4df4b48dd19ee03931b829463984772e reaches form output on the named build.

cards.title: Export the App HTTP contract from its existing checked facts
cards.body:
Export the App HTTP contract from its existing checked facts.

Current inspected openapi accepts HTTPRouter, while App already owns typed actions/forms. Manual parallel registrations can drift.

Choose App input to web.openapi or an explicit App.http_router projection; recommend direct App input. Preserve checked HTTP/OpenAPI model and existing router callers.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-app-openapi-projection. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Implement D-WEB-OPENAPI-APP1=A. `web.openapi` accepts the App, and its document comes from the checked App HTTP operation descriptors (AppGraph/server-function facts) through the existing OpenAPI renderer. There is no `App.http_router()`, no copied DTO and no second projection store.

**Current state**
- Core/web/web.jet:90-92: `pub fn openapi(router: HTTPRouter) -> String` → host `core.web.openapi`. crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/OpenAPI.rs:1657 `jet_web_openapi(router)` rejects routes without an HTTP contract. :1245/:1254 `jet_web_openapi_route_facts`/`document_from_routes` take `JetOpenApiRouteInput`.
- web.jet:31-34: the `App{name, pages, live, sessions}` struct has no actions or forms. The checked facts live in Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/MIR/MIR.jet:3504-3544 (`MirAppFormFact` with input/output/error types, endpoint, method, csrf, effects, middleware, and `MirAppGraph{routes, actions, forms, …}`). crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/WebServerFn.rs:159 `JetWebServerFnSpec` is the runtime spec.
- #2962 (endpoint derivation) is done. Examples/features/net/backend_battery/run.jet:71-93 proves the router path.

**Changes**
1. Once #3701 fixes which module owns `App`, add the App overload of `openapi` in that module. Under recommendation C that is `app`, and core.web keeps the HTTPRouter form. Two entry points share one renderer, which is allowed under D-WEB-OPENAPI-APP1.
2. Lowering: project `MirAppGraph.actions`/`forms` (public ones only: capability, middleware, CSRF, status, input/success/failure types) into `JetOpenApiRouteInput` rows. Do this in Compiler/JetCodegen at the point where AppGraph is already emitted, and hand them to `jet_web_openapi_document_from_routes`. Visual WebRouter pages, internal resources and `StoredOrder`-style private fields are excluded. The live descriptor is never weakened.
3. No listener starts and nothing is published. Existing HTTPRouter callers are unchanged.
4. Add Examples/features/web/app_openapi.jet plus its golden: one App with a create action (typed input, typed error, auth capability), a visual page and an internal resource, printing `openapi(app)` and the router-form document for the same handler.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=web/app_openapi Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: passes.
- `for m in --release '' --interpret; do Tools/agent/jet-env jet run $m Examples/features/web/app_openapi.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/web/app_openapi.out; done`: empty.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=net/backend_battery Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: the router callers still pass.

**Batch**
batch-core-ui (web family): Core app/web plus the AppGraph projection feeding the existing OpenAPI host renderer.

**Dependencies**
#3701 (App owner module, open ballot).

3. Internal resources and visual-only routes never become public endpoints.
4. Schema/client edits are derived artifacts, not manually maintained DTO copies.

cards.title: Prove request authority, deadline and transaction continuity
cards.body:
Prove request authority, deadline and transaction continuity.

Source has request context and DB resources, but no cross-request isolation/transaction proof was captured.

Use explicit existing context/resource values; verify concurrent principals cannot leak, invalid input cannot write, and cancelled/deadline-expired work cannot be blindly retried. No DI scope system.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-operation-request-lifetime. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Capture an executed receipt that request authority, deadlines and transactions stay separate across interleaved requests, using explicit existing context and resource values. No DI scope system is added. Research finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-operation-request-lifetime` (the card cites the stale lowercase docs/ path).

## Current state
- The request context and headers live in the HTTP server leaf (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/HTTPServer.rs`). Middleware isolation is proven at the Rust level by `tests/http_server_lifecycle.rs:4162` `middleware_orders_short_circuits_contains_panics_and_isolates_requests`.
- DB transactions: `Core/db/db.jet:91` `transaction(scope, name, steps) -[DB, Time.Wait]>` and pool `Core/db/db.jet:28`.
- No Jet-level receipt interleaves two principals over one pool, and none distinguishes commit, rollback and lost reply.

## Changes
1. Write `Examples/features/net/request_continuity.jet`. It binds a server with one shared pool and two routes that read the principal from a request header. Two client tasks interleave through a channel handshake, so the order is deterministic. It prints each principal's own transaction outcome:
   - commit, rollback on invalid input with no row written, and a handler whose reply is dropped after commit (reported as committed-reply-lost, never as rollback);
   - a request whose deadline expires before dispatch, which prints no mutation.
2. Pool and application lifetimes stay distinct: the pool is created once, before bind, and no per-request graph is allocated.
3. Record each criterion as supported, unsupported or unknown on the card. Any unsupported cell becomes its own build card; this card only captures proof.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=net/request_continuity Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes on AOT and default run, and `jet run --interpret` gives the same output.
- The golden shows two distinct principals with distinct outcomes, rollback leaving the row count unchanged, lost reply reported as committed, and the expired deadline leaving the row count unchanged.

## Batch
batch-measure: evidence capture on the current binary. A defect found here is filed separately.

## Dependencies
None. It pairs naturally with #3078's lifecycle example.
cards.checkSteps:
1. Two interleaved requests retain separate principals and transaction outcomes.
2. Commit/rollback and lost-reply outcomes are distinguished.
3. Deadline/cancel before dispatch prevents mutation; cancellation after commit does not report a false rollback.
4. Pool and application lifetimes remain distinct; no per-request graph allocation is required by the design.

cards.title: Prove browser action security on the real dispatch path
cards.body:
Prove browser action security on the real dispatch path.

CSRF/capability fields and strict token machinery do not prove policy ran before mutation.

Exercise existing auth/authorization/CSRF/input-limit rules on one native form and one scripted call; align codec policy with CorelibAstra rather than add a validator.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-browser-action-security. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove on the real dispatch path that auth, capability, CSRF and input-limit policy run before a browser action's mutation, for one native form action and one scripted server-function call. Fix the existing dispatcher if they do not. Do not add a validator.

## Current state
- Policy lives in the Rust CoreLib server-function layer: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/WebServerFn.rs:372-374` (Csrf/Unauthorized/Forbidden), `:418-420` (403/401/403), `:778` (reads `x-csrf-token`), `:888-895` (capability check: no subject gives Unauthorized, a missing capability gives Forbidden).
- The Jet App surface declares the policy: `Examples/features/web/web_app.jet:16-17` (`.action("save", save)`, `.mount("/api", api_mount, "Net", "csrf")`). `Core/web/forms.jet` has only action error helpers. The App harness lane is `tests/web_app.rs` with `Examples/features/expected/web/*.harness.out`.
- The finding lives at `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-browser-action-security` (the card cites lowercase docs/). Campaign #3070 is done; its boundary rules still apply.

## Changes
1. Add `Examples/features/web/action_security.jet`: one form action and one scripted server function that both increment a shared mutation counter, with a declared capability and CSRF policy.
2. Add a `tests/web_app.rs` case that serves it on loopback and sends: malformed body, oversized body, missing/wrong CSRF token, no session, a session without the capability, and a valid call. It records status, error code and the counter after each. Expected: 400/413/403/401/403 with the counter unchanged, then 2xx with the counter at +1. Store the transcript as `expected/web/action_security.harness.out`.
3. If any rejection lands after decode side effects or the handler, move the check ahead of the handler in the WebServerFn dispatch. This is a legitimate Rust fix here because WebServerFn is today's owner; its Jet ownership moves under #3690.
4. Unknown/duplicate JSON members: record the behavior of the actual codec (Core/encoding/json strict parse plus typed decode) for both UI and wire paths, and make them agree. Document it in the web actions section of Docs/spec.
5. Assert that no response body or diagnostic contains the CSRF token, the session id or a submitted secret. Record proxy trust as unsupported and route it to #3305's owner gate.

## Proof
`Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test web_app -- action_security_policy_runs_before_mutation` passes and matches the harness golden. Unauthenticated (401) and authenticated-but-forbidden (403) differ.

## Batch
batch-core-ui: Core/web App actions, proven by the web_app harness.

## Dependencies
None.

4. Responses and diagnostics contain no secret values; proxy trust is tested at its deployment boundary.

cards.title: Expose source-linked App and request-stage facts through existing tools
cards.body:
Expose source-linked App and request-stage facts through existing tools.

Nest already visualizes bootstrap graphs; the observed Jet lowering error has no useful source span.

Project App route/policy/resource facts into existing semantic-index/reasoning views. Keep check readiness separate from server readiness and use real endpoint receipts.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-app-diagnostic-facts. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Project App route, policy and resource facts, with source links, into the existing semantic-index and reasoning views, so a failed route, context or operation check names its source construct and causal dependency. Check readiness stays separate from server readiness, and endpoint claims use real receipts. No new graph store or public debug endpoint.

## Current state
- Jet sema already builds a complete per-route endpoint contract at registration. `sema_http_route_contract` (`Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/HttpRouting.jet:773-833`) records method, pattern, path/query params with schemas, request body, responses, operation id and `provenance` "file:line". It is attached to `THandleOp.HTTPRouterRegister` (:942) inside `sema_call_try_http_router` (:839). Route errors use E2805 (:851, 857, 926, 938, 947).
- The semantic index (`Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/SemanticIndex.jet`) projects arithmetic policy (`sema_compiler_index_arithmetic_fact`, :334-343), callable-policy and output facts, but no route or App facts. The Rust `crates/jet-semindex/src/Types.rs:139` likewise has callable policies only.
- The original finding: Nest visualizes bootstrap graphs, while the observed Jet lowering error had no useful span (`Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-app-diagnostic-facts`).
- App surface: `Core/app/app.jet` and `Core/web/router.jet`. Examples: `Examples/features/web/web_app.jet` and `app_hello.jet`.

## Changes
1. `SemanticIndex.jet`: add `CompilerRoute` rows built from the same checked contract (reuse its record; no JSON re-parse). Each row carries method, pattern, handler symbol id, the registration span and handler span, the schemas, the effect row and the policy/resource facts (authority, `Net` effect) from the call-site facts.
2. `HttpRouting.jet`: each E2805 site attaches the route pattern and the dependency that failed (handler symbol, missing response constructor or duplicate field) as structured fields, so machine-readable facts match the human text without prose parsing.
3. Host projection: `Source/CmdInspect.rs` shows the new rows when the single checked-fact owner (#3186) lands. Until then the facts stay in the Jet index only, with no Rust-side duplicate.
4. Record emit/check/repair/check fidelity, latency, context size and repair choice on 3 bounded edits in the card log (criterion 4).

## Proof
- The added criterion.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/http_route_missing_response.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` shows the construct and cause.
- A server started from `web_app.jet` answers each indexed route (a real endpoint receipt), and the check result makes no claim that the server is ready.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-sema`: index projection and diagnostic facts are sema work.

## Dependencies
Runtime and inspect proof on the self-hosted path needs #218. It coordinates with #3186, which consumes the facts, but is not blocked by it.

cards.title: Make TCP call and event completion states explicit
cards.body:
Make TCP call and event completion states explicit.

A cold request/reply operation and a published event do not share completion semantics. Exact Jet transport coverage is unknown.

Inventory existing TCP transport against send/emit/timeout semantics, then prove one success and one lost reply through the canonical operation state. Record absence before proposing a new API/dependency.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-tcp-rpc-completion. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
State honestly what Jet's TCP surface promises about send, reply and publication completion. Prove the send and timeout cells on the existing raw surface. Record that no request/reply or event-publish transport exists instead of inventing one. Research finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-tcp-rpc-completion`.

## Current state
- The only transport is raw TCP: `Core/net/net.jet:154` `send(stream, text)`, plus the stream methods `write_all(bytes, deadline:)`, `read_text(n, deadline:)` and `ready(interest, deadline:)`, as used by `Examples/features/net/http_readiness.jet:72-134`.
- There is no request/reply, emit or publish API in Core/net, Core/service or Core/event, so criterion 3 (event publication does not fabricate a handler result) holds by absence.

## Changes
1. Write `Examples/features/net/tcp_completion.jet`, all with deadlines:
   - success: `write_all` returns only after the bytes are handed to the socket, and the peer's reply is read;
   - lost reply: the peer reads and applies the request (increments a shared counter) and then closes without replying. The client's `read_text(deadline:)` reports a timeout or closed error, printed as `outcome=unknown-after-send`. The shared counter shows the mutation did happen, so the client may not assume it did not.
2. On the card, record that no event-publish or request/reply transport exists. A typed transport with explicit completion states is a new public API and needs its own ballot if the owner wants one. This card does not add it.

## Proof
`JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=net/tcp_completion Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes on AOT and default run. It shows `sent`, `replied`, and `outcome=unknown-after-send` with `server_applied=1`.

## Batch
batch-measure: a proof receipt on the existing surface. No code change is expected.

## Dependencies
None. Note for the owner: if a typed TCP RPC or event transport is wanted, open a separate ballot. This card closes on absence plus the raw-surface receipt.

1. Request is sent exactly when the public API says it is.
2. Timeout/lost reply after possible mutation reports uncertainty.
3. Event publication does not fabricate a handler result.

cards.body:

It incorporates #3130; that source becomes a frozen historical redirect, not completed implementation. No first-party Jet service package or facade is promised.

Historical captured problem, retained for evidence rather than delivery instructions:
Separate RabbitMQ acknowledgement from business commit.

An unacknowledged message may return after disconnect; handler success alone does not prove durable completion.

Check one RabbitMQ consumer with manual acknowledgement and a forced disconnect after commit. Record current support before adding a dependency.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-rabbitmq-ack-outcome. cards.plan:
**Goal**
Deliver one real RabbitMQ binding under ratified D-NEST-UPSTREAM1=A. The binding must prove manual acknowledgement separate from business commit, redelivery after an unacknowledged disconnect, and duplicate handling. It absorbs the former #3130 distribution work (#3130 criteria 1-4 map to criteria 4-7 here). There is no first-party Jet facade, provider registry or fallback.

**Current state**
- D-NEST-UPSTREAM1=A and D-UPSTREAM-SCOPE1=A are ratified. D-NEST-RABBIT1 and D-NEST-RABBIT-API1 are immutable history. #3397 (policy handoff) is done.
- No AMQP or RabbitMQ module exists in Core/ or Jetpack/.
- The ratified binding route already exists. `Examples/interop/python/run.jet:1` (`use py.ops as ops`) runs an application-owned Python module as a supervised sidecar, and `tests/ffi_python.rs:31` (`python_sidecar_binds_runs_and_launders_failure`) proves bind, run and failure laundering. Option A's own ballot example uses this `use py.<module>` shape.
- Criterion 6 requires a separate exact adoption ballot for any external library. None exists yet.

**Changes**
1. Main files the vendor ballot D-NEST-RABBIT-DEP1. The recommended option is an application-owned Python module over the pinned `pika` client (BSD-3-Clause) through the existing `py` sidecar. The alternative is the C `rabbitmq-c` library through the D-CBIND-UPSTREAM1 Clang extractor. The ballot records version, hash, license and targets.
2. Add `Examples/interop/rabbitmq/{run.jet,orders_amqp.py,expected.out}`. The consumer commits an order to an idempotency ledger, is killed before ack, reconnects, sees `redelivered=true`, and skips the duplicate by order key. It declares queue durability and ack mode explicitly (criterion 3). The Jet side uses `T?` and `E!` results only, with no retry of ambiguous side effects.
3. Any missing binder capability goes to the existing FFI owner. Do not patch around it here.

**Proof**
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test ffi_python -- python_rabbitmq_unacked_disconnect_redelivers`: this new test starts `rabbitmq-server` in scratch and asserts the redelivery and idempotency lines. It must fail, not skip, when the broker is missing.
- `jet run`, `jet run --interpret`, and `jet build` plus the binary each match `Examples/interop/rabbitmq/expected.out` byte for byte.
- No first-party battery ships, so no required gauntlet cell is created (AGENTS.md performance gate). Record the round-trip latency as evidence only.

**Batch**
`batch-host-runtime`: the proof is a Python-sidecar interop run with tier parity. No compiler change is expected.

**Dependencies**
Owner ratification of the vendor ballot (D-NEST-RABBIT-DEP1, to be filed). #3397 is done and is no longer a gate.

Prove durable jobs, meaning persistence across restart, bounded shutdown, retry and duplicate outcomes, on the existing core.jobs contract. Add an upstream broker-store binding only if the owner wants one beyond D-DX-QUEUE1=A. This card absorbs #3099 (#3099 criteria 1-5 map to criteria 4-8 here).

**Current state**
- D-NEST-UPSTREAM1=A, D-NEST-REMOTEQUEUE1=A and -API1=A are ratified, and #3397 is done. D-DX-QUEUE1=A/#2457 fixes bundled SQLite by default, an explicit database-provider override, and one Prelude lifecycle (Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md:1938).
- The durable queue exists today. `Examples/features/concurrency/job_queue.jet:10-49` sets `JET_JOB_QUEUE_DB`, then runs enqueue/claim/heartbeat/acknowledge/fail/cancel/dead_letter/recover_expired/pause/resume. The Prelude runtime is `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/ServiceAuthority.rs:3175` (`JetJobQueueStore`), `:5643` (`recover_expired`), and the JIT DB store at `crates/jet-jit/src/DB.rs:380-460`.

**Changes**
1. Stage A needs no owner choice. Add `Examples/features/concurrency/job_queue_restart/run.jet`. Worker process 1 claims job A with a short lease and exits without ack. Process 2 opens the same DB and runs `recover_expired`, reclaims A (attempts=2), acks it, and drains B on bounded shutdown without acknowledging unfinished work. Print states for criteria 1-3 and 7, then add its golden.
2. Stage B is the recommended ballot outcome. Close the integration on the SQLite store plus the existing explicit provider override. Only if the owner asks for a broker store, file D-NEST-REMOTEQUEUE-DEP1 naming an exact upstream client behind the existing `JetJobQueueStoreProvider`. **Batch**
`batch-host-runtime`: the queue store and lease logic are Prelude CoreLib Rust and the JIT DB host, and the proof is a tier golden.

**Dependencies**
The owner answers whether Stage A closes the card (recommended) or whether a broker-store ballot follows. Stage A can proceed now.

cards.title: Validate typed configuration before readiness
cards.body:
Validate typed configuration before readiness.

Environment strings and source precedence need an explicit startup policy; no configuration/readiness receipt was captured.

Inventory EnvConfig and typed App/CLI entry separately. Prove each existing documented precedence and secret-safe validation before readiness. D-CONFIG-ENV1 is an open import, so do not treat a new .env/file merge policy or external secret provider as ratified.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-config-readiness. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Missing or invalid required configuration fails before any request is admitted, with the redacted E2416 field path. Criteria 1 (precedence) and 3 (redaction) are already met.

## Current state
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:1727` `JetApp::serve` reads `JET_APP_PORT` and binds; it has no configuration or readiness hook. `Core/app/app.jet` has no config/readiness slot, and HTTP admission has no readiness predicate (card log 2026-09-22).
- D-CONFIG-ENV1 is open as a spec-only import: no new .env/file merge policy or secret provider is ratified.
- Finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-config-readiness`.

## Owner question (blocks the choice)
Option A (recommended): the app graph gains a typed readiness slot that `serve` runs before binding. Option B: no framework hook; document calling `env.decode` in `run` before `serve`. Option C: defer to a full D-CONFIG-ENV1 ballot. This plan is written for A.

## Changes (option A)
1. `Core/app/app.jet`: add a builder method such as `.ready(check: fn() -> () ConfigError!)`. It stores one readiness check on the app graph and rejects a second one.
2. Self-hosted compiler: JetFoundation registry row/signature for the builder method, and `HandleMethods.jet` routing for the App handle.
3. `Prelude/App.rs` `serve` runs the check before bind. On Err it prints the canonical E2416 report (field path only, never the value) and exits non-zero without opening a socket.
4. Add `Examples/features/web/app_config_readiness.jet` with a required typed field read through `env.decode`. Its golden runs with the variable missing and gives an `.err.out` containing E2416 and the path, with no listening line.
5. Docs/spec: the App readiness contract.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=web/app_config_readiness Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes (`.err.out`).
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test web_app -- config_failure_prevents_bind` asserts the port never accepts a connection and the secret value is absent from stderr.

## Batch
batch-core-ui: Core/app/web App surface and its Prelude leaf.

## Dependencies
Owner choice among A/B/C. With B the change reduces to the documented pattern plus the golden.

cards.title: Deliver upstream shared cache integration with its full contract
cards.body:
Current delivery law: D-NEST-UPSTREAM1=A. This card is the single active owner for shared cache binding, distribution and protocol/lifecycle evidence. It incorporates #3100; that source becomes a frozen historical redirect, not completed implementation. No first-party Jet service package or facade is promised.

Historical captured problem, retained for evidence rather than delivery instructions:
Keep cache miss distinct from stored falsy values.

Cache absence, expiration and Query revalidation are distinct from value truthiness and HTTP response caching.

Reuse existing cache/Query mechanisms; prove absence and invalidation semantics without a parallel web cache store.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-cache-absence-policy. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. cards.plan:
**Goal**
Bind one real shared cache store under D-NEST-UPSTREAM1=A so that two service instances keep a stored `false`, `0` or empty text as a hit (not a miss), expire it on an explicit TTL boundary, invalidate it after an order change, and recover from a store failure. This absorbs #3100 (#3100 criteria 1-4 map to criteria 4-7 here).

**Current state**
- D-NEST-UPSTREAM1=A, D-NEST-REMOTECACHE1=A and -API1=A are ratified, and #3397 is done.
- The local cache exists as the Prelude `JetCache` LRU (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs:38-45`, `jet_lru_has` at :691). No shared or multi-instance store binding exists in Core/ or Jetpack/.
- The binding route exists: the Python sidecar (`Examples/interop/python/run.jet:1`, `tests/ffi_python.rs:31`). The D-NEST-UPSTREAM1 option A example is literally `use py.cache_ops as cache` returning `false`.
- Criterion 6 requires a separate vendor adoption ballot, and none exists yet.

**Changes**
1. Main files D-NEST-REMOTECACHE-DEP1. The recommended option is an application-owned `cache_ops.py` over pinned `redis-py` (MIT) against a Valkey/Redis server through `use py.`. The alternative is a C client through D-CBIND-UPSTREAM1.
2. Add `Examples/interop/shared_cache/{run.jet,cache_ops.py,expected.out}`. Two instances share one store. The lookup returns `Bool?`, so absence is `None` and a stored `false` is `Val(false)`. The example sets TTL in explicit seconds and shows invalidation on an order update. When the store is killed it reports a typed `E!` failure, never a miss.
3. Leave HTTP response caching and Query state untouched (criterion 3). No second cache model.

**Proof**
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test ffi_python -- python_shared_cache_falsy_hit_ttl_invalidate` (new) starts `valkey-server` or `redis-server` in scratch. It asserts `hit:false`, `hit:0`, `hit:""`, `miss` after the TTL boundary, the invalidation, and the typed store-down error, and it fails when the server is absent.
- `jet run`, `jet run --interpret` and the AOT binary each match `expected.out`.
- No first-party battery ships, so there is no required gauntlet cell.

**Batch**
`batch-host-runtime`: a sidecar interop run with tier parity.

**Dependencies**
The owner ratifies the vendor ballot (to be filed).

cards.body:
Current delivery law: D-NEST-UPSTREAM1=A. This card is the single active owner for telemetry exporter binding, distribution and protocol/lifecycle evidence. Expose useful telemetry without hidden authority or disclosure.

Best-tooling Nest supplies semantic traces and agent context, but external disclosure and cross-service propagation still require policy.

Reuse the core.log set_sink/otlp_file/span/trace source floor and ratified observation contract; prove application propagation/redaction/exporter failure. Observe/telemetry-panel locators were unavailable without retained bytes, so do not infer their implementation. Do not propose a new trace store or exporter primitive; added remote adapter placement follows D-NEST-EXPORTER1.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-observability-context-export. cards.plan:
**Goal**
Export redacted telemetry from a Jet service through one real upstream exporter under D-NEST-UPSTREAM1=A. Trace identity must cross one permitted boundary without becoming a principal, and exporter loss or failure must be observable without blocking requests. This absorbs #3101 (#3101 criteria 1-4 map to criteria 5-8 here).

**Current state**
- D-NEST-UPSTREAM1=A, D-NEST-EXPORTER1=A and -API1=A are ratified, and #3397 is done.
- The local floor exists in `Core/log/log.jet`: `redact` (:71), `span`/`enter`/`close` (:75-79), `set_sink` (:81), `sample_every` (:90), `otlp_file` (:96) and `set_trace_id` (:105). These are exported via `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.jet:1271-1273`.
- No remote OTLP exporter binding exists. The file exporter must not be relabeled as OTLP (plan item 5 in the original card).
- The binding route is the Python sidecar (`Examples/interop/python/run.jet:1`). Criterion 7 requires a vendor ballot, and none exists.

**Changes**
1. Main files D-NEST-EXPORTER-DEP1. The recommended option is an application-owned module over pinned `opentelemetry-sdk` plus `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp` (Apache-2.0) through `use py.`, fed from the `core.log` JSON sink. The alternative is to close propagation and redaction on the `otlp_file` floor and leave remote export open.
2. Add `Examples/interop/telemetry_export/{run.jet,exporter.py,expected.out}`. Service A sets a trace id, calls service B over `core.http`, and B logs with the same trace id. It never derives a principal from the header (criterion 2). Secrets use `log.redact` and must not appear in the export (criterion 3). A killed collector yields a counted dropped-span fact while requests still succeed (criterion 4).

**Proof**
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test ffi_python -- python_otlp_export_redacts_and_survives_collector_loss` (new) runs `otelcol` or the SDK's in-process test receiver. It asserts one trace id on both spans, no secret bytes in the export, and `dropped>0` plus request success after the collector is killed.
- `jet run`, `jet run --interpret` and the AOT binary each match `expected.out`.

**Batch**
`batch-host-runtime`: sidecar interop plus `core.log` Prelude sinks, with tier parity.

**Dependencies**
The owner ratifies the exporter vendor ballot (to be filed).

cards.title: Treat package compatibility as part of backend capability
cards.body:
Treat package compatibility as part of backend capability.

Current Nest core and current official integration names are not automatically a compatible installed set. Throttler6.5.0 declares Nest peers only through11.

cards.title: Prove service tests and live HTTP share the same policy path
cards.body:
Prove service tests and live HTTP share the same policy path.

A direct handler test can bypass extraction, auth and serialization.

Use the existing in-process client or real loopback server and explicit dependency values; compare one isolated service check with a real HTTP denial and success. Do not copy Nest testing-container machinery.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-http-test-seam. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Show that an isolated service check and a live HTTP request go through the same boundary policy (extraction, auth, serialization). A test that swaps the DB value must not bypass that policy. Do not copy Nest testing-container machinery.

## Current state
- Core has no in-process test client (grep over Core/http, Core/web, Core/service, Core/app finds no test_client/in_process). The server surface is `Core/http/server.jet:11-47` (`mux`, `bind`, `serve`, `serve_once_listener`).
- `Examples/features/net/backend_battery/run.jet:101-147` already uses the real loopback pattern: `bind("127.0.0.1:0", mux, deadline: 2s)`, `task { bound.serve() }`, `bound.shutdown(100ms)`, `serving.join()`. It is the model for the proof. [INFERENCE] Neither net/backend_battery nor web/battery has an `Examples/features/expected/*.out` golden, although `tests/golden.rs:855-886` requires one for every project `run.jet`.
- `Core/service/service.jet` is the service owner. The finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-http-test-seam`.

## Changes
1. Add `Examples/features/net/service_http_seam/run.jet` (with package.jet). It defines an order service whose DB dependency is an explicit value parameter (a real temp sqlite versus a fake in-memory value), plus one boundary function `admit(req) -> Order HTTPError!` that does extraction, auth and decode.
2. The isolated check calls `admit` and then the service with the fake DB. The live check binds on loopback and sends a denied request (no auth → 401, malformed body → 400, service never invoked) and a successful request (201). Both paths print the same policy verdicts.
3. Cleanup: shut down the server and join the task, then assert the temp DB and listener are released and no global mux/route registration survives (a second bind on the same address succeeds).
4. Add the missing `expected/net/backend_battery.out` so the existing battery is golden-covered.

## Proof
`JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=net/service_http_seam Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes on AOT and `jet run`, showing identical isolated and live verdicts, and service call count 0 for the denied cases. `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=net/backend_battery Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.

## Batch
batch-core-net: http server surface plus examples, proven by net goldens.

## Dependencies
None.

2. Malformed input and denied authority cannot invoke the service.

cards.plan:
**Goal**
Prove that `jet check`, watched `jet dev`, `jet build` and `jet test` agree on one source identity after an input-shape edit, so fast transpilation can never publish stale metadata or a service while checking fails. Investigation first; no web-specific compiler or command.

**Current state**
- Finding and witness: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-checked-build-watch-parity (anchor at line 23368; the card's `docs/research/` path is now `Docs/research/`). No Jet loop receipt exists.
- Commands: `jet check`/`jet build` in Source/CmdCompile.rs, `jet dev` in Source/CmdDevTools.rs; D-DX-GENERATE1=A says source-writing generation runs only when explicitly invoked, never during build or test.
- Campaign #3070 (done) shared-boundary rules still apply.

**Changes** (evidence; code only if a cell fails, filed as a bug card)
1. Read the finding; keep its date, source identity and corrections.
2. In ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/3091/ build a small App endpoint program with a codec'd request type and a generated client/schema produced by the explicit generation step.
3. Make one bounded invalid input-shape edit (rename a request field without updating the handler). Run `jet check`, `jet dev` (watch), `jet build`, `jet test` on a fresh binary.

- Receipt table with exact commands, exit codes and diagnostics: invalid edit → `jet check` non-zero, `jet dev` keeps the last-good revision and shows the error, `jet build`/`jet test` fail with the same code; no source file written during build/test (compare `git status --porcelain` of the scratch project before/after).

cards.title: Verify password and encryption composition without a web crypto wrapper
cards.body:
Verify password and encryption composition without a web crypto wrapper.

Current core.auth register_user/password_login and session/OAuth/magic-link APIs are source-located under #506; this campaign has not established password-storage or encryption safety at runtime.

Inventory existing Core crypto and authentication support, then exercise password verify/mismatch and secret-safe failure. Do not adopt bcrypt or a new wrapper without a separate named dependency ballot.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-password-crypto-boundary. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Identify and exercise the real password-storage and verification path behind core.auth. Prove that a wrong password fails without leaking the password, hash, key or token, and that encryption examples state nonce/key ownership. No bcrypt and no new wrapper.

## Current state
- `Core/crypto/crypto.jet:573-600`: `password_hash` (Argon2id PHC `$argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=1$`, 16-byte random salt) and `password_verify`. `Core/crypto/expert.jet:684-687`: bounded `argon2id` parameters. The conformance corpus has `tests/conformance/corpus/core/crypto/password_hash.jet` and `password_verify.jet`.
- `Core/auth/auth.jet:154-171`: `register_user` and `password_login` hand the plaintext to the native `core.auth.register_user`/login provider after `valid_password_hash` (`:482-484`). That helper only checks the plaintext's shape (8-4096 chars, no controls), so it is misnamed. Which hash the provider stores is unverified.
- `Examples/features/net/backend_battery/run.jet:65-66` registers the password `"argon2id:demo"`, which reads like a stored hash.
- Finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-password-crypto-boundary`.

## Changes
1. Trace the core.auth provider's register/login and record the algorithm, parameter storage and verify path on the card. If it does not use the Core Argon2id PHC path, make `Core/auth/auth.jet` hash with `crypto.password_hash` and check with `crypto.password_verify` in Jet, and keep only row storage as the provider leaf.
2. Rename the private `valid_password_hash` to `valid_password_text`.
3. Add `Examples/features/crypto/password_auth.jet`: register; correct login succeeds; wrong login gives `AuthError.Rejected`; the printed error and its Display contain neither the password, the PHC string, the salt nor a session token (the example checks with `contains` and prints booleans). Also `password_verify` of a wrong password returns false.
4. Audit the AEAD examples (`Examples/features/crypto/crypto_envelope.jet`, `typed_crypto.jet`, `crypto_suite.jet`). A fixed nonce either becomes a random nonce with key ownership stated in the example, or is labeled as a test vector.
5. Replace the battery's `"argon2id:demo"` password with a plain passphrase.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=crypto/password_auth Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes on AOT and `jet run`.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev_tier_parity -- crypto_auth_and_vault_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot` stays green.

## Batch
batch-core-crypto: Core/auth and Core/crypto only.

## Dependencies
None.

1. Identify the actual password-hash algorithm, parameter storage and verification path.
2. Wrong password fails without leaking password, hash, key or token.
3. Encryption examples identify nonce/key ownership; no deterministic sample nonce is a production pattern.

cards.title: Prove migration and transaction ownership in the backend battery
cards.body:
Prove migration and transaction ownership in the backend battery.

Pool capacity alone does not establish migration, rollback, nested transaction or session cleanup behavior.

Exercise the existing database/battery path with a failed migration and one committed/rolled-back unit of work. Compare savepoint/session capabilities as explicit supported or unsupported behavior, not automatic ORM adoption.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-database-migration-proof. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove migration and transaction ownership on the real core.db path: a failed migration cannot advance the schema version, connections are released after commit and after rollback failure, and nested/savepoint behavior is recorded exactly. No ORM adoption.

## Current state
- `Core/db/db.jet:91-97`: `transaction(scope, name, steps)` and `migrate(scope, name, steps)` take `[SQL]` batches and delegate to the native `core.db` provider. There is no savepoint or nested-transaction surface.
- Existing examples: `Examples/features/io/db.jet:12,32-35` (migrate plus begin/rollback), `io/db_pool.jet`, `io/db_policy.jet:9`. `Examples/features/web/battery/run.jet:98` calls `battery.migrate_orders`.
- Finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-database-migration-proof`.

## Changes
1. Add `Examples/features/io/db_migration_proof.jet` on a temp sqlite file:
   - migrate `v1` succeeds;
   - migrate `v2` with a failing second step returns Err, the applied-migration record still shows only `v1`, and the table from v2's first step is absent;
   - a `transaction` with a failing step leaves rows unchanged; a successful one commits;
   - after each, the pool reports its idle/available count through `db_pool`'s existing surface (or the missing surface is printed as unsupported);
   - a nested begin inside a transaction prints its exact error or behavior.
2. If the provider advances the version or leaks a connection, fix it in the core.db provider leaf and keep the policy (version bookkeeping, all-or-nothing) in `Core/db/db.jet`.
3. Criterion 4: record that OpenAPI and route contracts come only from explicit route types. Grep the web/openapi projection for any entity-to-schema path and cite the result on the card.
4. Document the supported and unsupported savepoint cells in the core.db section of Docs/spec.

## Proof
`JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=io/db_migration_proof Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes on AOT and `jet run`. The golden shows version `v1` after the failed `v2`, unchanged rows after rollback, released connections, and the nested-transaction verdict.

## Batch
batch-core-data: core.db source and provider leaf, proven by an io golden.

## Dependencies
None.
cards.checkSteps:
1. A failed migration cannot leave a falsely advanced schema version.
2. Connection release follows both commit and rollback failure.
3. Nested/savepoint behavior is recorded precisely, including unsupported cases.
4. No database entity automatically becomes a public endpoint schema.

cards.title: Prove local timer and cron scheduling without durable-job claims
cards.body:
Prove local timer and cron scheduling without durable-job claims.

A process-local schedule has clock/overlap/restart semantics different from a persisted queue.

Use existing task/time and App lifetime surfaces; assess cron expressiveness without adding another executor.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-local-schedule-contract. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Close criterion 2: overlap and cancellation of process-local timer and interval schedules must not silently outlive cancellation or App shutdown. Criterion 1 (clock, zone and missed tick) and the restart half of criterion 3 were proven on 2026-09-22 by `tests/dev.rs` `schedule_clock_records_window_and_missed_tick_behavior` and `tests/dev_schedule_wave_a` `local_schedule_restart_does_not_replay_a_missed_window`.

## Current state
- `Core/tasks/tasks.jet:114-120` `after`/`interval` go to host `core.tasks`. `cancel(rx)` (:175-178) only closes the receiver, and the producer keeps running.
- The producers are detached threads: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Scheduler.rs` (per the 2026-09-22 audit, around :3889-3907; `jet_scheduler` spawns detached at :4246-4252) and `CoreLib/JetStd/MathTaskMem.rs:937-973`. JIT `Concurrency.rs:2138-2215` discards join ownership.
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:1727-1777` `serve`/`serve_on`/`serve_port` have no scheduler scope or shutdown hook. `jet_scheduler_drain` (Scheduler.rs:4424) exists for tests.
- Task groups and HTTP shutdown already cancel and join their own children.

## Changes (recommended option: owned producers, no new public API)
1. `Scheduler.rs`: timer and interval producers register in the current scheduler world with a cancel flag. The producer exits on its next tick, or at once, when its receiver is closed, so `tasks.cancel` stops it. Mirror this in `MathTaskMem.rs` and JIT `Concurrency.rs` so every tier shares one meaning. Keep the join handle.
2. `App.rs`: on the existing graceful serve stop (SIGINT/SIGTERM), cancel every timer producer the app world owns, then join them within a bound. A job overrunning that bound is reported on stderr as `schedule job <name> still running at shutdown`, never silently dropped.
3. Non-overlap: an interval whose previous consumer run is still active does not queue a second tick. Record this as a missed tick, which is already the proven criterion-1 policy.
4. If the owner prefers an explicit 'unsupported at shutdown' contract instead, that needs a ballot. None exists today, so this plan implements the fix.

## Proof
- Add `tests/dev.rs::schedule_cancel_stops_producer_and_app_shutdown_joins`. It starts an interval, cancels it, and asserts no further ticks and a producer count of 0. It also starts an App with a long-running scheduled job, sends SIGTERM, and asserts the job is cancelled or reported. `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev -- schedule_` passes on default run and the interpreter.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=concurrency/cancel_cleanup Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` still passes.

## Batch
batch-host-runtime: Prelude scheduler, App host and JIT concurrency parity.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.plan:
**Goal**
Measure the complete authenticated backend workload (report section 11 create/list protocol) against best-tooling Nest12/Fastify after correctness is proven. No latency, throughput, startup, memory or package-cost superiority is measured today.

**Current state**

1. Read the finding; keep date, source identity and pins.

cards.body:
Choose Socket.IO compatibility distribution.

The selected peer capability includes package/adaptor ownership, not only endpoint syntax. Current Jet interoperability and distribution are not established for this added scope.

Submit D-NEST-SOCKETIO1 before adding this capability to CoreLib, creating a first-party package or treating an external integration as stock. Keep the semantic proof card separate.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-socketio-distribution. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. cards.plan:
**Goal**
Provide Socket.IO protocol compatibility through one real upstream implementation under D-NEST-UPSTREAM1=A. A Socket.IO client must connect, exchange a message with acknowledgement, and disconnect with cleanup. Raw-WebSocket substitution, a first-party facade and implicit fallback are all forbidden.

**Current state**
- D-NEST-UPSTREAM1=A is ratified. D-NEST-SOCKETIO1=A and -API1=A are immutable history. #3397 is done.
- Core provides only native WebSocket (`Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/NetworkHandles.jet:150-181`, `WsConn`). That surface stays separate and unchanged.
- No Socket.IO binding exists. The semantic socket-lifetime proof stays on #3303 (planning).
- The binding route is the Python sidecar (`Examples/interop/python/run.jet:1`, `tests/ffi_python.rs:31`). Criterion 3 requires a vendor ballot, and none exists.

**Changes**
1. Main files D-NEST-SOCKETIO-DEP1. The recommended option is an application-owned module over pinned `python-socketio` (MIT) through `use py.`. The ballot records its Engine.IO protocol version, license, hash and targets.
2. Add `Examples/interop/socketio/{run.jet,sio_server.py,expected.out}`. The Jet program hosts the Socket.IO server through the sidecar. An independent reference client (`socket.io-client` for Node, or `python-socketio` as client) connects, emits `order` with an ack callback, receives the ack payload, and disconnects. The server reports the disconnect cleanup exactly once. Callback lifetime and cancellation go through typed `E!` results.

cards.title: Complete the reproducible script workflow through the existing lock
cards.body:
Complete the reproducible script workflow through the existing lock.

A manifest-less script is not reproducible merely because it names a version. Jet already has inline source hashing/locks, while uv demonstrates environment preparation and Lua native modules show compatibility obligations.

Prove and teach one local-source/lock/lift-to-manifest workflow. State external executable, system-library, runtime and target requirements. Do not add a second resolver or silently fetch a different dependency.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-script-f05. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove and teach one reproducible script workflow: local source → `jet fetch --lock` → clean run → `jet init <script>` lift into `package.jet`, with dependency identity preserved end to end and no second resolver.

## Current state
- Identity and fail-closed resolution are ported: `Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Scripts/InlineDeps.jet:104` `pkg_inline_deps_cache_identity`, `:155` resolve, `:284-296` E1253, `:300` L0203. Rust landed in bf2325ebe.
- The shipped host already has all three steps. `tests/inline_deps.rs` covers `jet fetch --lock` sidecars (`jet_lock_writes_sidecar` :158, `jet_lock_unresolved_dep_is_e1253` :197) and the lift (`jet_init_lifts_uses_into_package_jet` :218).
- The lift has a gap. `Source/main.rs:7312` `lift_inline_deps_into_manifest` copies only the selector (`"1.4"`), not the resolved version or content hash from `stats.jet.lock`, and its doc comment (`:7075-7078`) says it silently skips parse problems. Lifting therefore does not preserve identity, which fails criterion 3.
- UI fixture `tests/ui/inline_dep_unresolved.jet` pins the E1253 text.

## Changes
1. `InlineDeps.jet`: add `pkg_inline_deps_lift(script, lock?)`. It returns the manifest deps plus lock seed rows `(name, selector, resolved, content_hash)`, reusing `ScriptDependencyIdentity` (`:51-55`).
2. `Source/main.rs` `lift_inline_deps_into_manifest` (the shipped mirror): when `<script>.lock` exists, seed the project lock with the same resolved version and content hash through the existing lock writer and the comment-preserving `jet add` editor. A script that does not parse is an error, not a silent skip. With no sidecar, lift selectors only and print that `jet fetch --lock` was not run.
3. Teach the workflow in `Docs/spec/packaging/` (script section). State external executable, system-library, runtime and target requirements. Keep lua-cjson 2.1.0 explicitly unestablished against Lua 5.4.8.
4. If the lift cannot seed the lock through existing commands, file an owner ballot instead of adding a command.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test inline_deps`: all green, including a new `jet_init_lift_preserves_locked_identity`. After `jet fetch --lock stats.jet` and `jet init stats.jet`, the project lock carries `resolved = "1.4.2"` and the same `content_hash`. Deleting `.jet/inline-deps/textkit` then fails with E1253 and no registry fallback.
- `JETPACK_WORKER=scr Tools/agent/jet-env bash Jetpack/Bootstrap/check.sh --area PackageModel --tests` prints JETPACK CHECK OK with a new `InlineScriptDeps.jet` lift claim.

## Batch
batch-host-cli: the user-visible proof is the shipped `jet` binary; the Jet mirror rides the PackageModel unit.

## Dependencies
None open. #3655 (Jetpack CLI run/enter port) inherits this behavior later.

cards.title: Prove SQL value binding, scope, rollback and cleanup
cards.body:
Prove SQL value binding, scope, rollback and cleanup.

SQL behavior is independent of JSON decoding and deserves its own consumer proof.

Exercise the existing SQL/DBScope route with injection-shaped values, denied rows, rollback and close; no new SQL API.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-script-f11. cards.plan:
**Goal**
Prove the existing SQL/DBScope route: an interpolation hole stays a bound value (never an identifier or syntax), the selected row policy holds through query, transaction and failure, a failed transaction rolls back, and close releases the connection. No new SQL API.

**Current state**
- Core/db/db.jet:32-58 `policy` accepts only `true` and `owner == user`. :91-97 `transaction`/`migrate`. :60 `policy_audit`.
- Examples/features/io/db_checked_sql.jet: `{id}`/`{name}` holes (:12, :15), a failed transaction (:14), `close` (:24). Its policy is `true`, so no row is denied.
- Examples/features/io/db_policy.jet: `owner == user` scope for alice. It inserts a row with owner `bob` and prints `rows:1` (expected/io/db_policy.out:2), because the host silently rewrites the insert's owner bind to the scope user (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/DBPluginWire.rs:947-961). SELECT gets `owner = ?` appended (:1005-1012), and joins/subqueries fail closed (:554-558).
- Missing: an injection-shaped value witness, and a second user whose rows are actually denied.
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-script-f11.

**Changes**
1. Witness Examples/features/io/db_bound_values.jet. Insert `name = "x'); DROP TABLE person; --"` through a hole and read it back verbatim with the table intact. A hole in a table-name position is rejected. Two scopes (alice, bob) under `owner == user`: each sees only its own rows. An UPDATE that changes owner is refused (DBPluginWire.rs:971-975). A failed policy-scoped transaction leaves the count unchanged. A query after `close()` returns an error.
2. Classify the silent owner-rewrite on INSERT against the D-DBPOLICY-BIND1 law in this card's evidence. If the law expects rejection, file a bug; do not change it here.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=io/db_bound_values Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> literal injection text round-trips, row counts per user are isolated, rollback holds and use-after-close errors. Identical on every tier the harness runs.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=io/db_checked_sql Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` and `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=io/db_policy ...` -> unchanged.

**Batch**
batch-core-data (core.db family).

**Dependencies**
None. Related: #3308, #3669.

cards.title: Measure and close bounded streaming data paths
cards.body:
Measure and close bounded streaming data paths.

A whole-file allocation can erase the practical value of an otherwise concise script.

Trace existing reader/stream/codec/client composition for one large bounded JSON/CSV task; measure retained memory, copies and cancellation release against selected streaming peers.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-script-f15. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
For one large, bounded JSON/CSV task, trace and measure Jet's reader, stream, codec and client composition: retained memory, copies, early stop and cancellation release, against selected streaming peers. Any missing streaming API or parser dependency is balloted separately. No speculative zero-copy claims.

## Current state
- The Core source readers take whole text. `Core/encoding/csv.jet:96-99` `reader(text)` parses every row up front. `json.jet:94-95` says the reader 'materializes the value'. The same holds for `jsonl.jet:54` and `xml.jet:161-163`. `Core/data/loader.jet:125` streams over a materialized payload. `files.read_lines` (`Core/files/files.jet:915-917`) reads the whole file, and `write_lines` (:921-924) builds by repeated concatenation.
- A second, file-backed path exists on the provider side: `tests/encoding_parity.rs` uses `json.reader(^input, encoding.EncodingLimits.safe())` (:1947) and `fmt.writer(^output, limits)` streams for jsonl/csv/xml/cbor (:1656-1780), with limits such as `max_total_bytes`. This path is not declared in the Core `.jet` sources.
- The measurement tool `Tools/perf/stream_bench.py` (creation, pull, early_close, memory versus Python) exists.
- The finding is at `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-script-f15`.

## Changes (evidence only)
1. Workload: a 200 MB generated CSV and JSONL under `~/.cache/jet-luna/stream-probe/`, taking the first 10 matching rows and stopping, plus a malformed row at 150 MB and an oversize row.
2. Measure peak RSS (`/usr/bin/time -v`), wall time and copies for: the String `csv.reader`, the file-backed `json.reader(^input, limits)` and jsonl streams, `files.read_lines`, and Python `csv`/`ijson` as peers. Run on AOT and `jet run`.
3. Record whether early stop releases the file handle, and whether a malformed or oversize row stops predictably with a typed `EncodingError` at a stated offset.
4. Post the cell table. Flag the source-versus-provider split (Core `.jet` declares only String readers) as a correctness item for the encoding owner. Ballot any byte-source streaming reader for CSV/XML separately.

## Proof
- The card log holds a table of RSS, time and early-stop results per tier, plus the exact commands.
- `python3 Tools/perf/stream_bench.py` with `JET_STREAM_BENCH_COMMAND='Tools/agent/jet-env target/debug/jet'` produces JSON output that is attached to the card.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test encoding_parity -- jsonl_csv_xml_cbor_streams_match_aot_and_default_dev` passes.

## Batch
batch-measure: measurement only.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: Prove text, byte, locale and index conversion boundaries
cards.body:
Prove text, byte, locale and index conversion boundaries.

Unicode, non-Unicode OS arguments, binary strings and indexing conventions create concrete data-loss risks at script/native boundaries.

Exercise existing String/Bytes/UTF-8 and argument/path conversions; document units and conversion failures without adding another indexing origin.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-script-f17. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove that text-versus-bytes, locale and index conversions stay explicit and lossless-or-typed at the file, subprocess and guest boundaries, with identical typed outcomes on AOT, `jet run` and the interpreter. No second index convention may be introduced.

## Current state
- The encoding witness matrix was integrated in 83aca71bd. Witnesses with goldens: `Examples/features/strings/from_bytes.jet`, `Examples/features/io/stdout_bytes.jet` and `Examples/features/serde/encoding*.jet`. Cross-tier tests: `tests/encoding_parity.rs` (e.g. `malformed_text_codec_errors_match_aot_default_dev_and_interpreter` :626, `json_quoted_unicode_and_duplicate_key_errors_match_all_tiers` :690), `tests/text_unicode.rs`, `tests/checked_text_crossings.rs`.
- Units: `core.text` exports `byte_count`, `scalar_count`, `graphemes`, `char_indices` and `byte_views` (`CoreCallRows.jet:1980`).
- Not yet exercised: invalid UTF-8 read as text from a file, child stdout lines containing invalid UTF-8, and guest string crossing. Non-UTF-8 argv and env are owned by #3373.
- The finding is at `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-script-f17`.

## Changes
1. Add `Examples/features/strings/text_byte_boundaries.jet` with a golden. It covers:
   - writing `[U8]{0x61, 0xFF, 0x62}` to a temp file, then `files.read` as text (a typed UTF8/IO error, never U+FFFD) and reading bytes (exact)
   - a child `printf 'a\377b\n'` read through `lines()` (typed error or declared policy)
   - `String.from_bytes` on invalid input giving None
   - `"é👍🏽"` with `byte_count`/`scalar_count`/grapheme count, and `char_indices` offsets printed with their unit
2. If a boundary silently substitutes U+FFFD, fix it in the owning Core `.jet` or its provider leaf, following the declared strict policy (`ascii_lower` strict-UTF-8 work, #3569 log).
3. The guest boundary cell comes from the `Examples/features/packages/sandbox_mathkit` string call. Record it.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=strings/ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run Examples/features/strings/text_byte_boundaries.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/strings/text_byte_boundaries.out` and the `--interpret` form both diff empty.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test encoding_parity -- malformed_text_codec_errors_match_aot_default_dev_and_interpreter` passes.

## Batch
batch-core-text: a text-family witness plus any strict-decode fix, retested with the strings goldens.

## Dependencies
None. The argv and env cells are delegated to #3373.
