cards.title: Choose whether API authors can require forward-compatible matching
cards.body:
Choose whether API authors can require forward-compatible matching.

Rust non_exhaustive, Swift unknown-case handling and Zig non-exhaustive integers address different evolution boundaries. Jet already permits an explicit else but has no captured public non-exhaustive-author contract.

Route D-ENUM-EVOLUTION1: retain the closed enum law and caller-selected else (recommended), or add an explicit publisher marker requiring downstream fallback. Keep wire unknown values separate; do not reopen D-UNIONTYPE1 accidentally.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f19-public-evolution-policy. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
1. Read the exact law, captured contract and witness at docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f19-public-evolution-policy. Preserve the recorded date, source identity and any source-integrity correction.
2. Route D-ENUM-EVOLUTION1: retain the closed enum law and caller-selected else (recommended), or add an explicit publisher marker requiring downstream fallback. Keep wire unknown values separate; do not reopen D-UNIONTYPE1 accidentally.
3. Exercise each contract below on an identified integrated source and executable when execution is part of this deliverable. For an investigation, return the actual supported, unsupported and unknown cells before proposing implementation.
   - Owner ratifies one policy with source-compatibility, downstream exhaustiveness and same-module behavior spelled out.
   - If added, the public marker has a full ballot and negative/positive examples; if retained, document why manual else differs from publisher enforcement.
   - No arbitrary foreign integer or unknown wire payload becomes a valid declared case as a side effect.
4. Attach exact input/output/error and applicability evidence to this card. Retain losing or unavailable cells. Any public change beyond the named ballot requires its own complete owner decision.

## 2026-09-12 streamlining handoff — #3396

The decisions below are already ratified A. This is contract-preserving design guidance, not runtime proof. Do not repeat an approval already supplied by the named decision.

### D-ENUM-EVOLUTION1

Under D-ENUM-EVOLUTION1=A, use the existing approved contract. Do not add an open-enum mechanism; use existing exhaustive matching and explicit else where a caller wants future-case tolerance. Reuse EnumDef groups/variants and existing match/exhaustiveness checks; publisher docs/version metadata are ordinary existing surfaces. Do not reopen this same API/profile/marker decision merely because its implementation is not shipped.

- User path: Do not add an open-enum mechanism; use existing exhaustive matching and explicit else where a caller wants future-case tolerance.
- Shared mechanism and types: Reuse EnumDef groups/variants and existing match/exhaustiveness checks; publisher docs/version metadata are ordinary existing surfaces.
- Compile-time facts versus runtime state: Compatibility policy belongs to API/documentation metadata; runtime values remain closed enum cases and errors stay explicit.
- Keep explicit: Keep missing-case errors useful, avoid synthesized unknown cases/markers, and do not weaken exhaustiveness or wire decoding.

Use one checked source of facts and the existing error, ownership and effect rules. No new public wrapper, registry, grammar or dependency follows from this note. Any real change beyond the selected contract requires its own owner choice. Preserve the exact existing criteria and required runtime/I9/performance evidence.

cards.title: Choose the public checked numeric enum conversion surface
cards.body:
Choose the public checked numeric enum conversion surface.

Existing D-SHAPE-CONVERT1=A already fixes enum conversion direction and fallible narrowing. Automatic declaration-derived membership lookup remains a separate unproved Core API addition.

Route D-ENUM-INGRESS1 for generated checked lookup only. Preserve Target.from_int and the ordinary fallible conversion result; never introduce from_discriminant, an optional narrowing result, or a duplicate error family.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f20-checked-ingress-api. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-ENUM-INGRESS1=A (ratified, which settles criteria 1 and 3). Generate a destination-owned `Enum.from_int(raw: Int) -> Enum String!` for payload-free enums whose cases all have explicit, unique integer codes. A declared code returns the case; a nonmember returns the existing checked-conversion error. There is no payload, no implicit cast, no source-order ordinal, no `from_discriminant`, no optional result and no new error family. Caller-written code parsers are replaced by the generated lookup; protocol aliases stay explicit. Source: ENUM-F20, which absorbs #3131.

## Current state
- `from_int` exists only for built-in numerics and precise types: `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/BuiltinStatics.jet:162,165` (Decimal/Fraction) and `:216-220` (numeric sources). It also exists for Distinct and range types (`Examples/features/types/range_types.jet`, `distinct_types.jet`).
- `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Static.jet:274-280` admits built-in owners through the `BuiltinStaticRow` table. There is no enum path, and nothing in `Compiler/` or `crates/` matches `EnumFromInt`/`enum_from_int`.
- Declared codes are already in the AST: `Compiler/JetAst/Source/AST/Items.jet:962-963` (`discriminant: Int?`, `discriminant_expr`).
- Criterion 4: #3131 (the proof sibling for range, membership and ingress) is done. Reconcile its receipts and do not redo range/Distinct proof.

## Changes
1. **JetSema.** In `Calls/Static.jet`, resolve `E.from_int` when `E` is a declared enum. Require every case to be payload-free with an explicit `discriminant` and unique values; otherwise emit the registered errors. The result type is `E String!`, the same shape as the Distinct/range `from_int`.
2. **JetCodegen.** Lower the call to a generated code-to-case table sourced from `EnumDef.variants` (in `Expressions.jet`), plus the matching JetEval evaluation. Other numeric inputs first go through their existing checked Int conversion.
3. **Retained host.** Add the Rust bootstrap sema/lowering mirror so the shipped binary proves the feature. Emission uses a plain `match` with no Prelude helper.
4. **Callers.** Replace hand-written code-to-enum parsers in `Examples/` and `Core/` with the generated call. Find them by grepping for enum `if raw ==` ladders that return `E?`, then review each hit. Protocol alias mappings stay explicit.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=types/enum_from_int cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: pass.
- `JET_THREE_WAY_STEM=types/enum_from_int cargo test --test dev_corpus cranelift_three_way_differential_battery`: tiers agree.
- The two UI fixtures above.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=types/range_types cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: unchanged.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: exit 0.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-sema`: a checked static resolution with a generated table; there is no runtime surface.

## Dependencies
None. #3131 is done.

cards.title: Choose adjacent enum tag/content envelopes in existing Codable
cards.body:
Choose adjacent enum tag/content envelopes in existing Codable.

Serde’s adjacent representation and protocol-shaped envelopes are broadly useful. Jet’s captured enum forms name external, internal and untagged modes; no executed adjacent derive path is established.

Route D-ENUM-ADJACENT1: add a tag+content option to the existing discriminator mechanism in stock Codable, or keep an explicit wrapper DTO/custom conversion. Do not add another enum serializer package.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f22-adjacent-wire-tags. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-ENUM-ADJACENT1=A (ratified, so criterion 1 is effectively met). The existing `Discriminant` marker takes an optional `content:` key, `#[Codable, Discriminant("kind", content: "body")]`, and then every payload sits under that field:
- Named payloads stay objects, and single payloads keep their value shape.
- A unit case omits content when encoding. On decode it accepts absent content or `content: null` and rejects non-null content.
- DenyUnknownFields does not reject the recognized null content field.
- Without `content:`, the current internal-tag behavior is unchanged.

This extends stock Codable. There is no new serializer or wrapper DTO. Source: ENUM-F22.

## Current state
- Serde attributes carry one optional string: `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Registration/Checked.jet:136-146` (`Discriminant`/`Tag` becomes `Tag`, with `value` from `sema_checked_marker_text`), `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/TIR/TIR.jet:1605-1616` (`TSerdeAttributeKind`: RenameAll, Tag, Untagged, DenyUnknownFields; `value: String?`), and the MIR lowering at `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Functions.jet:277-286`.
- The host rejects anything else: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIRRust.rs:7058-7070` panics on unexpected payloads, and `crates/jet-jit/src/jit/runtime_host.rs:1650-1664` reads only tag, untagged and deny-unknown.
- No example uses `Discriminant` today.

## Changes
1. **TIR and MIR.** Add `content: String?` to `TSerdeAttribute` and `MirSerdeAttribute`, populated only for Tag. The MIR digest (`Digest.jet`) includes it.
2. **JetSema.** In `Checked.jet`, read the `content:` labelled argument (`sema_checked_marker_text_label`) and check collisions with the tag key, and with payload field names where relevant, before codegen. In `Serde.jet`, apply the unit and DenyUnknownFields rules.
3. **JetCodegen.** Emit the adjacent encode/decode in the enum serde lowering path (`Functions.jet`), plus JetEval.
4. **Retained host.** In `MIRRust.rs`, accept `Tag` with content and emit adjacent codecs. The `runtime_host.rs` JIT descriptor gains `serde_content`. Update the Prelude DataTree codec routes (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/`, the Codable encode/decode) and the Rust bootstrap sema mirror.
5. Update `Docs/spec/reference/core-library.md` (Codable enum representations).

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/enum_adjacent cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: pass.
- `JET_THREE_WAY_STEM=serde/enum_adjacent cargo test --test dev_corpus cranelift_three_way_differential_battery`: tiers agree.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/enum_adjacent_content_collides.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`: pass.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/ cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: unchanged.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: exit 0.

## Batch
`batch-core-encoding`: a Codable enum wire extension, batched with #3149, #3150, #3233, #3238 and #3299. These cards touch the same serde attribute path, so one implementer should own the #3148/#3149/#3150 sequence.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: Choose typed preservation of unknown enum wire variants
cards.body:
Choose typed preservation of unknown enum wire variants.

Ignoring unknown object fields is not the same as accepting an unknown enum tag. Useful forwarding must retain the original tag and parsed payload, and must not hide malformed known cases.

Route D-ENUM-UNKNOWN1: keep strict derived decoding by default and add an explicit unknown-preserving case backed by an opaque stock encoding value, or leave preservation to a raw DataTree/application envelope. The proposal must make round-trip and construction invariants explicit.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f23-unknown-wire-preservation. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-ENUM-UNKNOWN1=A (ratified, so criterion 1 is effectively met). Add one opt-in `#Unknown` case whose payload is the opaque stock type `UnknownVariant<Self>`, from `core.encoding`. Only checked decoding can create it; Encode re-emits the stored parsed tree, so Encode stays total. The marker applies only to tagged representations. Strict decoding stays the default, known tags with malformed payloads are still errors, and untagged ambiguity is never reclassified as unknown. There is no general open enum, no raw-byte guarantee and no trial decoding. Source: ENUM-F23.

## Current state
- There is no `UnknownVariant` type and no `#Unknown` marker anywhere in `Core/encoding`, `Compiler/` or `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude`.
- Serde attribute handling: `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Registration/Checked.jet:136-146`. Variant markers are `serde_markers` at `Compiler/JetAst/Source/AST/Items.jet:964`.
- `Core/encoding/json.jet` exposes only DataTree decoding.
- Enum serde lowering: `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Functions.jet:277-286`. Host: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIRRust.rs:7058-7070` and `crates/jet-jit/src/jit/runtime_host.rs:1650-1664`.

## Changes
1. **Core.** Declare `pub struct UnknownVariant<T>` once in `Core/encoding/encoding.jet`, holding a private tag and a `DataTree` payload. It has no public constructor, and read-only accessors `tag()` and `payload()`.
2. **JetParser and JetSema.** Accept the variant marker `#Unknown` in `DeclarationMarkers.jet`. Check that the enum is tagged (`Discriminant` or default external), that there is at most one such case, that its payload is exactly `UnknownVariant<Self>`, and that user code never constructs one. Register the diagnostics.
3. **JetCodegen, JetEval and the host.** Decode dispatch tries known tags first. An unknown tag builds `Retained(UnknownVariant{…})` from the parsed tree. A known tag with a bad payload still errors. Encode writes the stored tree back under the owner's tagging. Mirror this in `MIRRust.rs` and `runtime_host.rs`, and in the Prelude codec and the Rust bootstrap sema.
4. **Composition.** Compose with #3148's adjacent form: the content field is preserved in the tree.

cards.title: Choose decode-only aliases for durable enum wire names
cards.body:
Choose decode-only aliases for durable enum wire names.

A canonical rename freezes one spelling; reading older spellings while emitting only one current name is a separate migration capability. Source-name renaming and semantic case aliases must remain distinct.

Route D-ENUM-WIREALIAS1: add explicit decode-only aliases to existing Codable case markers, or keep per-version DTO conversion. This is an existing-CoreLib functionality addition, not a new serializer or duplicate enum case mechanism.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f24-decode-only-case-aliases. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-ENUM-WIREALIAS1=A (ratified, so criterion 1 is effectively met). Add the case marker `#DecodeAliases("old", …)`. Decode accepts those names plus the canonical name. Encode writes only the canonical `Rename`/`RenameAll` name. Collisions are rejected before codegen. Case identity, `T.cases` and metadata do not change. There is no per-call strict opt-out; removing an alias is an input-compatibility change. Source: ENUM-F24.

## Current state
- There is no `DecodeAliases` marker in `Compiler/`, `crates/` or `Core/`.
- Variant wire names come from `Rename`/`RenameAll`: `Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/DeclarationMarkers.jet:18` routes serde markers, and `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Registration/Checked.jet:106-146` resolves shape names and serde attributes.
- `TSerdeAttributeKind` (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/TIR/TIR.jet:1605-1616`) has no alias carrier.
- Codegen and host decode paths: `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Functions.jet:277-286`, `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIRRust.rs:7058-7070` and `crates/jet-jit/src/jit/runtime_host.rs:1650-1664`.

## Changes
1. **JetParser.** Add `"DecodeAliases"` to the serde marker set (`DeclarationMarkers.jet:18`), valid on enum cases only.
2. **JetSema.** Fold the aliases into the variant's wire-name metadata as `decode_aliases: [String]` in the TIR/MIR variant rows. Check that canonical names and all aliases are unique across cases after `RenameAll`, and register the collision diagnostic. Aliases never create values or `T.cases` entries.
3. **JetCodegen and JetEval.** Decode compares the input against the canonical name and then the aliases, returning the canonical case. Encode is untouched.
4. **Retained host.** Make the same comparison in the `MIRRust.rs` enum decoder, the `runtime_host.rs` descriptor and the Prelude codec, and add the Rust bootstrap sema mirror.
5. Document the marker in `Docs/spec/reference/core-library.md` and state the input-compatibility consequence there.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/enum_decode_aliases cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: pass.
- `JET_THREE_WAY_STEM=serde/enum_decode_aliases cargo test --test dev_corpus cranelift_three_way_differential_battery`: tiers agree.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/enum_decode_alias_collision.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`: pass.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: exit 0.

## Batch
`batch-core-encoding`: Codable enum decode, batched with #3148 and #3149 in one implementer's sequence.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.body:
Measure canonical enum codec forms on the same wire workload.

Wire tags, field names, payload shapes and parsers influence size and throughput. The corpus provides features and examples, not comparable end-to-end measurements.

Create one codec benchmark card for current external/internal/untagged representations and any separately ratified adjacent form. Compare established Serde/Glaze or peer equivalents using the same protocol data and correctness fixtures.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f26-codec-representation-cost. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. cards.plan:
**Goal**
Run the existing enum-codec harness against the canonical Jet codec and a pinned Serde peer on the same wire workload, and record bytes, allocations, encode/decode medians and malformed-input behavior per representation.

**Current state**
- Tools/perf/enum_codec_bench.py (the card cites the stale path tools/perf) defines `FORMS = external, internal, untagged, adjacent` (:68), `CASES = payload, evolution, unknown, malformed` (:69) and fixture wire payloads (:107-133). Form markers: none, `#Discriminant("type")`, `#Untagged` (:134-150). Entry point: `core.encoding.json.to_string`/`decode<T>`.
- Static mode only. `--run` needs an external `--command` adapter (header :14-34), and none is checked in. `peer_comparison.status = not_run` (:993-998). Card log 2026-09-22: static checks only.

**Changes**
1. Add Tools/perf/enum_codec/adapter.jet, a Jet program using the canonical `core.encoding.json` codec with one `Command` enum per form (the adjacent form is used only if already ratified; otherwise that cell stays unavailable). It implements the harness protocol (`--operation`, `--form`, `--case`, `--input`, `--output`, `--metrics`, `--rounds`) and writes `codec_ns` and `allocation_count` when the runtime exposes them. Add Tools/perf/enum_codec/jet-adapter.sh, which builds it once with `jet build --release` and execs the binary.
2. Add Tools/perf/enum_codec/serde-adapter.sh, which builds a pinned `serde`/`serde_json` peer (versions recorded, `--release`) from a small Cargo project under Tools/perf/enum_codec/serde_peer with the same enum shapes, and speaks the same protocol. This measures the peer only. No dependency enters Jet (criterion 3).
3. Run both on the same machine and settings. Keep the reports side by side and apply the strict comparator per cell. Record losing cells on this card and make no win claim without one.

cards.title: Measure enum dispatch and visitor structure on a real state machine
cards.body:
Measure enum dispatch and visitor structure on a real state machine.

Match, visitor, virtual method and table dispatch trade code shape and work distribution. Source compactness alone does not establish branch or cache cost.

Create a finite-state/parser dispatch comparison card with equal transitions and payload processing using Jet named enums and the best appropriate C++/Rust/Zig/Java/C# approaches.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f27-tagged-dispatch-cost. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Measure enum dispatch and visitor structure on a real finite-state parser with equal transitions and payload processing. Compare Jet named-enum matches with the best C++, Rust, Zig, Java and C# designs, keeping closed-set and open/extensible guarantees equal. Source compactness is not evidence of branch or cache cost.

## Current state
- `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen` owns enum match lowering, and `Tools/perf/constructs/match-{1,2,4}.jet` (the `large-matches` family in `Tools/perf/construct-scale.tsv`) already covers compile-side scaling of large matches.
- No runtime state-machine dispatch entry exists in `Tools/gauntlet/entries/`. `binparse` and `logreport` parse inputs, but they do not isolate dispatch shape.
- #218 (log 2026-09-28): the self-hosted codegen cannot run programs yet.
- The finding is `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f27-tagged-dispatch-cost` (the card cites the stale `docs/` path). The performance-admission-before-new-option chain applies.

## Changes
1. Add `Tools/gauntlet/entries/enum-state-machine/`. It is a tokenizer/state machine over a fixed 8 MB input, run in two variants: a balanced case distribution and a skewed one (90% one state).
   - The Jet source uses named enums with payloads and one `if state == { … }` table.
   - The peers use switch/match, a visitor, virtual dispatch and table dispatch, each labeled as a closed or open design.
   - Every program prints the token count and a checksum.
2. First confirm that outputs are identical for both distributions, then record end-to-end medians, code size of the dispatch function and branch-miss counts (`perf stat -e branches,branch-misses` where available). An isolated empty switch is not an admissible result.
3. Record the self-hosted Jet generated code for the match once #218 runs. Any lowering change is filed as a JetCodegen card with a paired performance cell.

## Proof
- `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry enum-state-machine --runs 11`. Checksums match across all languages and both distributions, and results record medians, code size and branch data (or "unavailable" per peer).
- The card log keeps the closed-vs-open labeling next to each number.

## Batch
`batch-measure`: evidence only.

## Dependencies
#218 (self-hosted codegen must execute).

cards.title: Measure generic enum and visitor compile/rebuild cost
cards.body:
Measure generic enum and visitor compile/rebuild cost.

Template/generic expansion and generated codec/match code can move cost from runtime to builds and diagnostics. The current packet contains no compile-time result.

Create a pinned compiler-workload card generating a bounded family of equivalent generic sums, visitors and codecs, then changing one case and rebuilding. Compare cold and incremental behavior and diagnostic size.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f28-compile-and-rebuild-cost. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Measure compile and rebuild cost for a bounded family of equivalent generic sums, visitors and codecs, including a rebuild after adding one case. Separate front end/typechecking, code generation and linking where tooling permits. This workload supports no whole-language speed claim.

## Current state
- The compile-side harness exists. `Tools/perf/dashboard.sh --construct-scale-json` measures the `generic-instantiations`, `large-matches` and `derives-reflection` families at scale points 1/2/4 (`Tools/perf/construct-scale.tsv`, `Tools/perf/constructs/`). cards.title: Measure exhaustive functions versus enum-keyed tables
cards.body:
Measure exhaustive functions versus enum-keyed tables.

Finite static mapping is not set membership. Odin’s enum-indexed arrays and ordinary enum-keyed maps suggest a useful job, but no new Jet enum-array syntax is required without evidence.

Create a static mapping card comparing an exhaustive function, Map<Enum,T> and an explicit dense table behind ordinary code. Include sparse discriminants, missing entries and adding a case.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f29-total-case-tables. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Compare three ways to hold a total static mapping over an enum: an exhaustive function, `[Enum: T]`, and an explicit dense table behind ordinary code. Show where each one detects an omitted case (at compile time or at lookup), and what it costs to initialize, store and look up. Keep D-MAP-KEY1 and ordinary collections; a new syntax, type or table API needs its own ballot.

## Current state
- Compile-time omission is live in both compilers. The self-hosted checker emits E0307 in `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Coverage.jet:144-163`, which covers else-less tables (`:163`) and multi-head functions (`:160`). The row is registered at `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet:3415`, and the shipped binary also emits E0307.
- The triage note "E0307 not emitted" is stale. #3140 covers structured repairs and fix-its, which this measurement does not need.
- The cost cells need generated code from the primary path, which is blocked on #218 (log 2026-09-28).
- The finding is `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f29-total-case-tables` (the card cites the stale `docs/` path). The performance-admission-before-new-option chain applies.

## Changes
1. Add `Examples/features/types/enum_total_mapping.jet` with its golden. It declares an enum with sparse explicit discriminants and maps it three ways. It prints a lookup of every case and the observed behaviour for a missing map entry and a missing dense-table slot.
2. Add `tests/ui/enum_total_mapping_missing_case.jet`. After a case is added to the enum, the exhaustive function reports E0307 while the map and table compile, and the snapshot records that difference.
3. Add `Tools/gauntlet/entries/enum-total-mapping/` with Jet, Rust, C and Odin sources for the same total mapping (sparse numeric codes included). Measure initialization, storage bytes and lookup medians over black-boxed keys.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=types/enum_total_mapping.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes, and `jet run --interpret` prints the same missing-entry behaviour.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/enum_total_mapping_missing_case.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` shows E0307 only on the function form.
- `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry enum-total-mapping --runs 11` gives equal checksums and records the init, storage and lookup columns.

## Batch
`batch-measure`: evidence only.

## Dependencies
#218 for the Jet cost cells on the primary path. #3140 is not a prerequisite, because E0307 already exists.

cards.title: Derive shape and enum consumers from checked declarations
cards.body:
Prove built-in enum catalog, completion and reflection agree.

The Rust-side core enum catalog feeds known builtin variants but is not itself the public enum value/metadata API. Drift between catalog, docs and consumers would mislead users and agents.

Create a bounded consistency card for the captured core_enum_variants catalog: enumerate its consumers and compare declaration/type identities, completion labels, diagnostic case lists and any reflection path. Preserve one source of truth.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f30-core-catalog-consistency. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Under D-ONE-SHAPE1=A, checked declarations are the single source for built-in enum cases and shapes in the self-hosted compiler. Completion, construction, missing-case diagnostics, reflection, emission and JetEval all read the same checked declaration and ShapeProjection. No handwritten catalog is ported.

## Current state
- The drift the card targets lives in archived Rust. crates/jet-foundation/src/CoreModuleExports.rs:930 `core_enum_variants` feeds crates/jet-sema core_types.rs:613 and CheckerItems.rs:2280. The MIRRust and MIREval shape traversals are also archived.
- Compiler/ has no `core_enum_variants` (grep). JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCallRows.jet:2001-2005 carries only export names (`type_exports`), with no case lists.
- Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Comptime/Reflection.jet:665-669 builds enum layout from the checked definition.
- Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/CoreUsage.jet:452-457 `sema_core_has_source_package` exposes only `core.archive` as Core source. Every other built-in enum is still a compiler seam, so the Jet compiler has no declaration for it yet.
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f30-core-catalog-consistency.

## Changes
1. Receipt: list each consumer of built-in enum cases in Compiler/ (Patterns.jet missing-case, SemanticIndex.jet completion, Reflection.jet, JetCodegen Emit shape mapping, JetEval ReflectionMethods.jet). For each, record the source it reads today.
2. CoreUsage.jet: widen `sema_core_has_source_package` so that Core packages declaring enums (starting with core.web.query's `WebQueryStatus`) load as checked source. Register their enums through the normal registration graph.
3. Point every consumer at the registered declaration, removing any residual name list. JetCodegen Emit and JetEval derive shape mapping from ShapeProjection. Rename, skip, computed, default and field order follow the checked shape, and historical schema snapshots stay unchanged.
4. Add no public API. #3147, #3233 and #3238 keep their exposure, evolution and export proofs.

## Proof
- `rg -n "core_enum_variants" Compiler` prints nothing.
- tests/ui/core_enum_missing_case.jet (a non-exhaustive `WebQueryStatus` match) snapshots the declared cases: `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/core_enum_missing_case cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`. On the shipped binary this pins today's user-visible case list; it becomes Jet-compiler proof when the snapshot runs through the self-hosted route.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/ cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes (rename, skip and default round-trips unchanged).
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0. The self-hosted route waits for #218.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: this is Core-source registration plus consumer rewiring in JetSema, retested with one UI and serde golden pass.

## Dependencies
None blocking. Coordinate with #3147, #3233 and #3238 through the same declaration owner.

cards.title: Measure typed case iteration and derivation cost after its gate
cards.body:
Measure typed case iteration and derivation cost after its gate.

A generated case iterator could avoid hand-maintained lists, but heap freedom, compile-time generation cost and stable order are unmeasured.

Create a post-decision measurement card dependent on D-ENUM-CASEVALUES1: compare the ratified value surface with an explicit list and peer Enum.GetValues/CaseIterable/enum_values equivalents. If the owner retains lists, measure and document that route instead.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f31-case-iteration-cost. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
After D-ENUM-CASEVALUES1=A ships `T.@values`, measure it against a hand-maintained explicit list and peer equivalents: C# `Enum.GetValues`, Swift `CaseIterable` and Rust `strum`/const arrays. Record order, allocation, cold and steady-state cost, and derive/compile cost. Payload enumeration is not claimed, and iteration reuses ordinary Iter adapters.

## Current state
- D-ENUM-CASEVALUES1 is ratified A (one typed catalog of payload-free enum values), and implementation is #3132 (ready). No `@values` handling exists anywhere; a grep over `Compiler/`, `Core/` and `Examples/` finds nothing.
- The primary compiler cannot run programs yet (#218, log 2026-09-28).

2. Add `Tools/gauntlet/entries/enum-case-values/`. Jet (`@values` and explicit list), C#, Swift and Rust iterate a 256-case enum 10M times through an ordinary `map`/`fold`. Record construction and storage allocation plus cold and steady-state medians.
3. Record the compile/derive cost for the 256-case enum with the dashboard phase split. Compare the `@values` source against the explicit list in the same run.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=types/enum_case_values.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes, and `jet run --interpret` prints the identical ordered list.
- `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry enum-case-values --runs 11` records allocation counts (zero heap allocations expected for `@values`, which is catalog data) and cold and steady-state medians with equal checksums.

## Batch

cards.title: Prove enum rename, navigation and case completion
cards.body:
Prove enum rename, navigation and case completion.

Audience comments distinguish identifier-based cases from string unions for rename/refactor support. Language semantics do not prove editor behavior.

Create a focused LSP/editor card for rename, definition/references and context-sensitive case completion on unit/payload/generic enums and relative case syntax. Separate source renames from frozen #Rename wire names.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f33-editor-symbol-operations. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Renaming an enum variant through the real LSP changes every source reference across sibling modules, including leading-dot and bare `Enum.Variant` patterns. Unrelated same-spelled cases and frozen `#Rename` wire names stay unchanged.

## Current state
- Criteria 2 and 3 (completion, add/remove consistency) are met: `tests/lsp.rs:4610` `lsp_enum_variant_navigation_completion_and_rename`.
- The LSP (`Source/LSP/Server.rs:385,2937` `rename_response`) builds its SymbolDB from `crates/jet-semindex/src/Build.rs:1333` `build_symbol_db`. That builder pushes refs for identifiers, fields, impls and derives (`:1078,3297,3367`) but never walks patterns, so sibling-module pattern variants are missing. This is the 2026-09-21 blocker.
- In the self-hosted compiler, variant constructors record a `SemaNameReferenceFact` of kind `variant` (`Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Expressions/Constructors.jet:238`). `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Patterns.jet` records none, so the Jet semantic index (`SemanticIndex.jet:1616-1620`) also misses pattern references.

## Changes
1. JetSema `Patterns.jet`: when a pattern resolves to an enum variant (leading-dot `.Val(x)` against the subject type, or qualified `Enum.Variant`), push `SemaNameReferenceFact{kind: variant}` with the variant symbol from the owning module. This makes the compiler index complete.
2. LSP host (`crates/jet-semindex/src/Build.rs`, retained LSP tooling): walk match and if-table patterns and emit a `scoped_ref` whose target anchor is the variant declaration, resolved through the subject type. The anchor comes from the enum's declaration, not from the spelling.
3. `rename_response`/`lsp_rename_semantic_op`: restrict edits to refs whose anchor identity matches. Never touch string literals or `#Rename(...)` arguments.

## Proof
- Extend `tests/lsp.rs` with `lsp_enum_variant_rename_crosses_sibling_modules`. Module a declares `enum Mode { Fast Slow }`; module b matches `.Fast` and `Mode.Slow`, and has an unrelated `enum Speed { Fast }` plus `#Rename("Fast")`. Renaming `Mode.Fast` edits a's declaration and b's `.Fast` only. Run `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test lsp -- lsp_enum_variant` (both tests pass).
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.

## Batch
batch-host-cli: the observable proof is the LSP surface. The Jet sema reference row lands in the same build.

## Dependencies
None. #813 is done.

cards.title: Investigate type-indexed variant results on a concrete typed AST
cards.body:
Investigate type-indexed variant results on a concrete typed AST.

The selected audience raises Haskell/OCaml GADTs as a capability omitted by a simple enum ranking. That comment is a hypothesis, not verified language behavior or proof that Jet needs GADTs.

Create a bounded typed-AST investigation: express integer and boolean expression nodes and an evaluator whose result type follows the node type using current Jet generic enums, constraints and ordinary wrappers. Retrieve primary peer evidence only for this job; if a real gap survives, return a dedicated full ballot rather than importing a broad type-system feature.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f34-indexed-variant-usecase. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Decide from executed evidence whether current Jet can express a typed expression AST whose evaluator result type follows the node type (the GADT use case). If it cannot, return one precise owner ballot. The audience's GADT remark is a hypothesis, not proof, and this card does not open a dependent-type campaign.

## Current state
- Generic enums and applied types already exist: `Type.Named` and `Type.Apply` in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Types/Types.jet:4-18`. Related examples are `Examples/features/types/generic_types.jet`, `recursive_enum.jet` and `typestate.jet`, which uses phantom-state wrappers.
- No shipped example encodes a typed expression tree. `Examples/features/generics/` holds only `typed_lambda_inference.jet`.
- The finding is `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f34-indexed-variant-usecase`. The card text still cites the stale `docs/` path.

## Changes
1. Add `Examples/features/generics/typed_ast.jet`, using the new spelling only. It encodes integer and boolean nodes (`Lit`, `Add`, `Eq`, `If`) three ways: (a) one enum per result type with typed constructors; (b) a phantom-typed `Expr<T>` wrapper with smart constructors over one untyped enum; (c) an evaluator bounded by a trait. It evaluates one fixed program and prints the results. Add a golden under `Examples/features/expected/generics/`.
2. Add `tests/ui/typed_ast_ill_typed.jet` with ill-typed nodes for each encoding: `Add` over `Bool`, `If` with an `Int` condition, and mismatched branches. The snapshot records which of them are rejected at check time and under which registered code.
3. On the card, record a table of encoding × {rejected before runtime, evaluator needs an unreachable runtime arm or cast, source size}. Compare it with the same job in pinned primary sources: the GHC GADTs user-guide section and the OCaml manual's GADT chapter.
4. Close with one of two outcomes. Either the existing mechanisms are adequate (cite the cells), or write one owner ballot with same-program alternatives. If the ballot is ratified, the fix belongs in `Compiler/JetSema` (constructor typing of generic enums).

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=generics/typed_ast.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes, and `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/generics/typed_ast.jet` prints the same output.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/typed_ast_ill_typed.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` passes. Every rejected node carries a registered code, and every accepted ill-typed node appears in the card table.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-sema`. The deliverable is a check-time property of generic enum typing, and any gap is fixed in JetSema.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: Choose first-class payload constructor values
cards.body:
Choose first-class payload constructor values.

Rust exposes payload variant constructors as callable values. Jet’s direct construction receipts do not establish whether a qualified constructor can be passed to an ordinary higher-order function without a wrapper.

Route D-ENUM-CONSTRUCTORCALL1 after the exact current callable lookup is inventoried: treat qualified payload constructors as ordinary capture-free callable values, or retain explicit lambdas. Preserve existing S30 labels/effects/inference rules and leave unit cases as values.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f36-constructor-callable-values. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Deliver D-ENUM-CONSTRUCTORCALL1=A (ratified). A qualified payload constructor such as `Message.Text` is an ordinary capture-free callable value, derived from its checked signature, so it can be passed to a higher-order function without a wrapper lambda. Unit cases stay values. Signatures that ordinary function values cannot express are refused, not erased.

## Current state
- Neither compiler treats a qualified payload constructor as a callable value (grep for CONSTRUCTORCALL/constructor_value in Compiler/ and crates/: none). The Rust recovery 0732a643 is partial and archived.
- Evidence: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f36-constructor-callable-values`.
- The callable value shape is `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Types/Types.jet:15` `Type.Fn(params, ret, effect_bound, param_contract, call_metadata, return_view_provenance)`, with `FunctionCallMetadata.conventions` at `:263-269`. The MIR closure is at `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/MIR/MIR.jet:1782`. Direct constructor calls go through `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Expressions/Constructors.jet`.

## Changes
1. JetSema (name resolution of `Enum.Variant` in value position, `Expressions/Constructors.jet`): when a payload variant is used without a call, build its `Type.Fn` from the checked payload signature (labels into `param_contract`, conventions into `call_metadata`, no effects, infallible). Label, ownership and provenance rules follow S30/S47. Generic enums instantiate through ordinary callable inference.
2. Refuse, with the existing registered diagnostics, any constructor whose payload needs move/write/view conventions or labels that a function value cannot carry (tie-in with #3143's access slots). Do not claim every named or owning constructor is first-class.
3. JetCodegen: lower the value to one capture-free function (a generated thunk per variant) that every tier consumes. Direct calls and D-CALLVALUE1=B routing are unchanged. Add no constructor protocol and no reflection invocation.
4. Rust mirror (so the shipped binary runs the golden): the same derivation in crates/jet-sema's value-position path.
5. Add `Examples/features/types/constructor_values.jet` + `.out` (`items.map(Message.Text)` versus `items.map(s -> Message.Text(s))`, a generic `Box.Some`-style case, a unit case used as a value). Add `tests/ui/constructor_value_{view_payload,labelled_payload}.jet`.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=types/constructor_values Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes, and `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/types/constructor_values.jet` matches.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/constructor_value_ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` passes.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: value-position resolution and the Fn type live in JetSema. The thunk lowering and Rust mirror ride the same build.

## Dependencies
None blocking. Share the callable-contract changes with #3143 in the same batch.

cards.title: Investigate native database enums and migration safety
cards.body:
Investigate native database enums and migration safety.

The full captured audience adds PostgreSQL native enums. This is a useful persistence question, but no PostgreSQL primary source or Jet database enum-binding proof was captured.

Create a bounded database-boundary investigation under the existing core.db/Driver work. Compare parameterized bindings of a closed Jet enum to a portable wire name and to a native PostgreSQL enum. Examine adding/renaming cases, database ordering and mixed-version readers. A new connector capability or default requires a separate complete owner ballot.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f38-database-enum-boundary. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
A bounded investigation of closed Jet enums at the database boundary: how they bind today (portable wire name vs native PostgreSQL enum), plus case addition/rename, database ordering and mixed-version readers. It closes with existing coverage or precise, independently decidable additions. No new driver is imported silently.

**Current state**
- Core/db/db.jet has no enum path. Values cross as `DBValue` (row_int/float/text/bool, :64-82), typed rows go through `decode<T: Decode>` (:87, compiler lowering), and SQL holes bind values.
- The only engine is SQLite (rusqlite 0.31 bundled, crates/jet-jit/Cargo.toml:39-40, D-DEP-DB1). No PostgreSQL client exists in the tree, so a native-enum cell cannot run today.
- Related decisions to read first: D-DBMIGRATE1 (Examples/features/io/db_checked_sql.jet:1), D-DBPOLICY-BIND1, D-FOUND-COREAPI1. Related cards: #3308, #3669.
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f38-database-enum-boundary.

**Changes**
1. Witness Examples/features/io/db_enum_binding.jet (SQLite). Bind a fieldless `#Codable` enum through an SQL hole and store its canonical wire name as TEXT. Read it back through `db.decode<T>` with an unknown stored name rejected as `[FieldError]`. Show an added case readable by a new reader, and an old reader rejecting it. Show that `ORDER BY` sorts by text, not declaration order. A CHECK constraint lists the allowed names.
2. PostgreSQL cell from pinned primary docs (PostgreSQL 17: CREATE TYPE ... AS ENUM, ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE / RENAME VALUE, declaration-order sorting, no value removal) recorded as not runnable (no driver). A native-enum capability becomes a separate ballot only if a PostgreSQL provider is admitted under #3308.
3. Record the closure on the card: SQLite TEXT plus a CHECK constraint is the existing coverage, and native enums need a driver decision first.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=io/db_enum_binding Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> round trip, unknown-case rejection, added-case behavior and text ordering. Identical on every tier the harness runs.

**Batch**
batch-core-data (core.db family).

**Dependencies**
None for the SQLite witness. The PostgreSQL native cell waits on a provider decision tracked by #3308 (not a blocker for closing this investigation).

cards.title: Prove text parsing keeps case, wire and display names distinct
cards.body:
Prove text parsing keeps case, wire and display names distinct.

The peer APIs provide checked name lookup, but no current Jet enum parse generator was established. An application should not need JSON quoting merely to validate a command-line choice.

Create a bounded current-surface and ergonomics card under D-SHAPE-CONVERT1. Locate and exercise enum Target.parse or the best existing parser; compare canonical source names, grouped names, case sensitivity, wire Rename and unknown text. If a new generated parser is useful and absent, prepare its own complete Core API ballot rather than smuggling it into numeric ingress.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f42-enum-text-parsing. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Establish, by execution, how a Jet program turns text such as a CLI choice into a payload-free enum today, and whether case, wire and display names stay distinct. If a generated parser is missing and useful, prepare its own complete Core API ballot. Do not smuggle one into numeric ingress, and add no alias, string-enum family or optional package.

## Current state
- Evidence: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-enum-f42-enum-text-parsing`, under D-SHAPE-CONVERT1 (ratified A).
- No generated enum text parser exists: no `Target.parse`, `from_name` or `from_str` generation in `Compiler/JetSema`, `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/AutoDerives.jet`, or `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/BuiltinStatics.jet`, whose parse rows cover only Int/Float/F64/PasswordHash (lines 133-186). The only current routes are the Codable/JSON decode path (quoting required) and hand-written `if text == { "north" -> ... }` matches.
- D-SHAPE-ONE1 and D-ONE-SHAPE1 (ratified A) keep source names and shape/wire projections distinct.
- Triage's recommended ballot (not yet created): should every payload-free enum get a generated checked text decoder (`Target.parse(text) -> Target String!`) that matches exact source case names only, with wire renames left to Codable? Options: A generates a source-name, case-sensitive parse (reusing the D-ENUM-INGRESS1 generator from #3146); B has no generator and documents the Codable route; C generates a parse through the shape projection. Recommendation: A.

## Changes
No compiler change on this card.
1. Create the probe directory `~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/enum-text/` with its own `package.jet` granting the effects it needs (`authority: { holds: { allow: [IO, Mem.Alloc] } }`; the scratch root no longer has a shared package.jet), and write `probe.jet` there: a payload-free `enum Target` with plain cases, one variant group (D-TAG1 spelling as in `Examples/features/types/`), and one case carrying the Codable wire-rename marker. Parse it via (a) Codable/JSON decode of a quoted name and (b) a hand-written text match. Run known, unknown, grouped, wrong-case, source-name-of-renamed and wire-name inputs.
2. Record the exact entry points, the fallible error contract and the observed outputs. Compare against Java `valueOf`, Python `Enum[...]` and .NET `Enum.Parse` on the same inputs (documented behaviour).
3. Reconcile the retired work receipts named in the finding. Do not redo verified cells.
4. If the gap is confirmed, draft the D-ENUM-PARSE ballot with the three options above (same-program alternatives, edge cases, and beginner and expert paths) and link it from this card. Implementation goes on a new card after ratification.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/enum-text/probe.jet` output is attached to the card for every input row. Expected: the JSON route decodes only quoted source names, and the manual match handles only what it spells.
- The ballot draft exists in Tower (`node Tools/tower/tower.mjs decision show D-ENUM-PARSE1`) or the card states why none is needed.

## Batch
batch-measure: evidence only, with no code change.

## Dependencies
None. A later implementation card would depend on the ballot and reuse #3146's generator.

cards.plan:
**Goal**
Prove `Tally<Enum>` counted-multiset behavior under D-TAG1 with the existing API only: one, repeated and removed occurrences, removal of an absent member, and an explicit `any` predicate over a variant group.

```jet
active.remove(Damage.Fire.Burn)
print("burn after 2 removes: {active.count(Damage.Fire.Burn)}")
```

cards.title: Offer an optional local callable summary over existing checked facts
cards.body:
Offer an optional local callable summary over existing checked facts.

Readers currently have source-backed reasoning, effect, rights and callable projections. The proposal organizes those same facts around one selected callable, so a reader can inspect failure, write access and effects without reconstructing a cross-view explanation.

After owner choice, add an opt-in summary-first presentation through existing jet.reasoning/editor machinery. Keep stable semantic identity and one SemIndex/checked-contract source. Show explicit unknown/stale/truncated states. Preserve expert detail and provenance. Do not add source syntax, a command family, an effect store, a readability score or mandatory lint.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-read-f01. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove the optional callable summary in `jet.reasoning` (D-READ-LOCAL1=A). It is one collapsible local answer projected from the existing SemIndex derivations, showing failure, write access, effects and checked records, with explicit unknown, stale and truncated states.

## Current state (implemented, integrated 2a724d5ac, untested)
- `Source/LSP/Features.rs:410-460`: selection anchored by checked callable identity or derivation, not by name text, with unavailable states. `:454` `callable_summary_json` returns an `unavailable` status plus reason when nothing is selected.
- `:625` emits status, callable, declaration_source, failure, write_access_parameters, effects, returned_views, policies, metadata_producer_status, checked_records, limits and runtime_observation.
- `:1015` embeds the summary in `jet.reasoning/v1`.
- `Source/LSP/Server.rs:606,2312-2359` handles executeCommand.
- `Tools/editors/vscode/extension.js:352,552,817` shows the result.
- No test mentions `jet.reasoning` (grep `tests/` finds nothing). `tests/lsp.rs:1847` `lsp_execute_command_impact_returns_report` is the executeCommand transcript pattern to copy.
- Ownership: identity comes from the existing CallBinder (#3398). D-CALLVALUE2=A is ratified, and #3399 owns the invocation cutover. Reuse the BigCodeAstra identity, references and rename work (criterion 8).

## Changes
1. Add `lsp_reasoning_callable_summary_contrast` to `tests/lsp.rs`, using the `run_transcript` / executeCommand pattern. The fixture:
   ```jet
   #Error
   enum SaveError {
       Full
   }
   fn save(items: &[Int]) -[IO]> Int SaveError! {
       &items.push(1)
       print("saved")
       return items.len()
   }
   fn pure_len(items: [Int]) -> Int { return items.len() }
   fn run() {
       buf := [Int]{}
       n :: save(&buf) ?? 0
       print(pure_len(buf) + n)
   }
   ```
   Assertions:
   - `save`: `failure` names SaveError with its declaration source; `write_access_parameters` lists `items`, labelled as a declaration fact rather than an observed write; `effects` contains IO (criteria 1-3).
   - `pure_len`: no purity claim is derived from the absence of `&` (criterion 3).
   - After a `didChange` that breaks the file, the summary's status is `stale` or `unavailable`, never empty facts (criterion 4).
   - `limits` and provenance are present (criterion 5).
2. Criterion 6's current-tables contrast: request the same selection through the existing lenses and the summary, and assert that both carry the same identity.
3. Criterion 7: a counterbalanced explain-predict-modify-repair trial through `Tools/agent-eval/run-cold-context.mjs` (a human beginner/expert pair if the owner supplies one), recorded in `Docs/audits/callable-summary-trial-<date>.md` with no productivity claim.

cards.title: Measure context-sensitive local readability instead of enforcing metrics
cards.body:
Measure context-sensitive local readability instead of enforcing metrics.

The sources identify real tensions—familiar idioms, live mutable state, helper boundaries and invariant comments—but provide no controlled basis for a universal readability threshold.

Run a bounded counterbalanced beginner/expert explain-predict-modify study on the already selected corpus. Use the result to support or reject contextual guidance, not to pre-authorize a style linter.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-read-f09. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Run a bounded, counterbalanced beginner/expert explain-predict-modify study on the selected local-readability corpus. The result supports or rejects contextual guidance. It never pre-authorizes a style linter or metric threshold.

**Current state**
- No study receipts exist. Criteria 3-4 require recorded participant strata and human prediction and modification errors, which agents cannot supply.
- Criterion 6 forbids any participant contact until the owner approves recruitment and outreach.
- The 2026-09-28 learnability report already drove the P0 learnability cards. The protocol and receipt formats to reuse are BIG-F07/#2858 (criterion 5).
- Source: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-read-f09.

**Changes** (after owner approval)
1. Predeclare paired tasks, each with identical observable contracts (values, input mutation, order, errors, cleanup): early guard versus positive branch, named selection versus manual loop, deep interface versus shallow helper split, and WHY/invariant comments versus HOW narration. Use the C pointer rewrite only as a negative control.
2. Record prior-language familiarity and beginner/expert stratum, and counterbalance task order.
3. Measure prediction and modification errors, context needed, retries and time, with uncertainty. Do not use line counts or preference as a proxy.
4. Publish bounded findings, including negative results, as a new report under Docs/research/.

**Proof**
A committed protocol file and anonymized receipts under `Docs/research/`, listed with `rg -n 'READ-F09' Docs/research`. Per-pair error and time tables with intervals. No linter change in the diff.

**Batch**
`batch-deferred`: a human study, deferred until the owner approves participants.

**Dependencies**
The owner decides on participant and outreach approval (criterion 6). The recommendation is to keep this at P3, parked until a real study is feasible. No code prerequisite.

cards.title: Prove message-to-source lookup using existing structured logging
cards.body:
Prove message-to-source lookup using existing structured logging.

core.log already has structured fields, redaction, trace IDs, text/JSON sinks and telemetry source identity. That is not proof that a composed, translated or redacted message can be located in the correct program source. Existing telemetry constants identify core.log implementation sites, while Python documents caller-frame attribution.

Exercise a finite lookup capsule with existing log.info_fields/log.field/redact, source maps and stable author-supplied event keys. Keep output search, event identity, source identity and trace correlation separate. Measure the remaining source-navigation gap without first inventing another logging or localization library.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-read-f11. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal.** Measure how well existing structured logging locates the emitting source (READ-F11; research: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-read-f11`). The capsule is a finite one: an author-supplied stable event key with `info_fields`/`field`/`redact`. Keep output search, event identity, source identity and trace correlation separate, and invent no new library.

**Current state.**
- `Core/log/log.jet`:
  - `info_fields` (:49) and `field`/`int`/`float`/`bool` (:55-69)
  - `redact(key)` (:71): the value is never supplied and renders `[redacted]`
  - `record`/`formatter`/`format` (:352-368), giving deterministic text/JSON rendering to a String
  - `set_trace_id` (:105) and the `otlp_file` bridge (:96)
- Telemetry source identity currently names `core.log` implementation sites, not the user's call site. Do not read the Prelude metadata as the Jet call site (c4).
- READ-F17/D-READ-LOGSITE1 separately governs any call-site metadata addition (c5).
- Goldens exist for `io/log_structured` and `io/log`.

**Changes.**
1. Add `Examples/features/io/log_source_lookup.jet` and its `.out`. Cover the five cases in add_criteria (c1). The language fixture is a plain `[String:String]` map, not shipped localization.
2. The lookup receipt goes on the card, not in the tree. For each record:
   - take the `event` value, search the source for the unique `field("event", "<key>")` site, and record file:line
   - record the source file's SHA-256 before and after, so navigation verifies content identity (c4)
   - mark each hit "developer-supplied key", not compiler-verified identity (c2)
   - show that the wrapper case lands on the wrapper call site only because the key is passed through
3. Check the text, JSON and OTLP-file views for the redacted field: the marker is present and the value is absent. An absent payload is not treated as proof (c3). Coordinate the sink, bounds and observer-cost notes with #3250 (CORE-F023).
4. Record the remaining gap as a measured finding, with no defect claim (c5): no compiler-verified call site, and a key that is not checked for uniqueness. No new CoreLib, event-ID registry, localization engine, source-map kind or command is added (c6).

**Proof.** The command in add_criteria, plus the lookup receipt on the card.

**Batch.** `batch-core-files`: a log witness golden, retested with the files/term/log pass. No code change.

**Dependencies.** None. D-READ-LOGSITE1 is independent.

2. Show whether the existing stable event field locates the correct source after message composition/translation/redaction and across a wrapper; distinguish a developer-supplied key from compiler-verified source identity.
3. Verify field values/redaction through existing text, JSON and telemetry views without leaking the redacted value or treating absent payload as empty proof. Keep sink/protocol/bounds/observer-cost work coordinated with CORE-F023.
4. A source lookup must verify source content identity before navigating. Do not reinterpret the current fixed Prelude source metadata as the original Jet call site.
5. Do not claim a logging runtime defect from the source inventory alone. READ-F17/D-READ-LOGSITE1 separately governs the proposed call-site metadata addition; this capsule also remains useful if that choice is rejected.
6. No new CoreLib, exporter dependency, event-ID registry, localization engine, source-map artifact kind or command family is authorized by this proof card.

cards.title: Make existing examples teach their local contracts explicitly
cards.body:
Make existing examples teach their local contracts explicitly.

Names and short code do not reveal input mutation, deferred evaluation, failure exits, cleanup or external invariants by themselves. The initial report left this teaching value in prose.

Audit the existing four-workload examples/reference passages and fill only missing or misleading explanations. Reuse current docs/examples rather than create a second style guide or impose naming/comment rules.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-read-f12. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Make the selected teaching examples state their local contracts explicitly: what each one reads, changes, returns, delays and requires on every exit. Fix only missing or misleading explanations, and run the examples to prove it.

**Current state**

**Changes**
1. Write a criterion map as a card log. For each of criteria 1-7, give the file:line that teaches it, or mark it "already sufficient" with the line. For the C assignment/post-increment control (criterion 6), point at `lowlevel/unsafe_obligations.jet` and confirm it separates copied bytes and NUL from final pointer state, without claiming an unobserved program.
2. Patch only lines the map shows missing or misleading, and keep WHY/units/invariant comments. Link IteratorAstra, BigCodeAstra and READ-F08 (#3173) instead of restating them.

cards.title: Prove combined deferred-close, guard and exit-handler ordering
cards.body:
Prove combined deferred-close, guard and exit-handler ordering.

The captured law defines resource-only deferred close and its ordering relative to guards and exit handlers. The initial guard probe does not prove consumption, once-only cleanup or combined cancellation/panic/stop behavior.

Close the finite resource-close/guard/atexit conformance matrix under D-SHAPE-RESOURCE1/2 and D-FAIL-EXIT1. Reuse the current mechanisms and repair violations at their owning boundary; do not infer this contract from guard-only success.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-read-f14. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Close the finite cleanup-ordering conformance matrix under D-SHAPE-RESOURCE1/2 and D-FAIL-EXIT1: deferred close, scope guards and `atexit` across every exit path, each in an isolated subprocess. Research finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-read-f14`.

## Current state
- The law is in `Docs/spec/reference/core-library.md:1346-1354`:
  - deferred closes run in reverse declaration order, then guards in reverse registration order, then `atexit` in registration order;
  - `process.exit`/`os.stop` share the explicit exit boundary;
  - a host kill or abort can skip cleanup.
- Existing single-path goldens: `Examples/features/io/process_exit_cleanup.jet:1-24` (with `.out`), `os_stop_cleanup.jet`, `scope_guard.jet`. Parser support for `defer close(^x)` is at `Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/Statements.jet:506`. Guards are in `Core/mem/scope`.
- No matrix covers typed error, panic unwind or cancellation at a wait point, and none checks once-only close or second-close rejection.

## Changes
1. Write `Examples/features/io/cleanup_matrix.jet`. It relaunches itself per case through `core.process` with an argument, so each path runs in a fresh subprocess: normal return, typed error, panic, cancel at `time.sleep` inside a task group, `process.exit(0)`, and `os.stop(3)`. Each child declares two resources, two guards and two atexit handlers, then prints its trace. The parent prints each child's trace and exit code.
2. Add `tests/ui/defer_close_twice.jet` (second close or use after consuming close is a compile error) and a finish/flush failure case showing that the fallible close result is not hidden by automatic cleanup.
3. Any violation found is fixed at its owner (codegen defer lowering, Core/mem/scope, or the exit boundary in the runtime), not in the test.
4. Guard lifetime overlap goes to READ-F05. File, HTTP and task domain lifecycles stay with CORE-F010/F011/F012/F021.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=io/cleanup_matrix Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes on AOT and default run, and `jet run --interpret` gives the same output. Every case shows closes once in reverse order, then guards in reverse, then atexit in order where the exit law applies. No post-stop statement prints. The exit codes are 0, 1, 101, 0, 0 and 3.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev -- explicit_exit_cleanup_matches_interpreter_jit_and_aot` passes with cleanup_matrix added to its example set.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/defer_close_twice Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` passes.

## Batch
batch-core-files: process and exit boundary with scope and resource Core, proven by one golden.

## Dependencies
None.

3. Observe each deferred close exactly once in reverse declaration order, then guards in reverse registration order, then atexit handlers in registration order where the governing exit law applies.
4. Verify immediate versus scheduled consuming close, later-use/second-close rejection, and that finish/commit/flush/shutdown failures are not hidden by infallible automatic cleanup.

cards.title: Prove finite task, channel, join and fail-fast behavior
cards.body:
Prove finite task, channel, join and fail-fast behavior.

The selected corpus contains bounded channels/workers, joins and task.all failure/cancellation examples, but source text and printed labels do not prove scheduling bounds, failure ownership or cleanup.

Run and close a finite source-matched conformance capsule for the captured task/channel jobs under existing concurrency law. Use deterministic coordination and bounded timeouts; do not add a scheduler or another concurrency API.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-read-f15. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Run a finite, source-matched conformance capsule for tasks, channels, joins and fail-fast under the ratified law: D-CONC-SPAWN1=D, D-CONC-FAIL1=A, D-CONC-JOIN1=A, D-CONC-CHAN1=A, D-CONC-CHAN2=D and D-CANCELMODEL1=C, none re-balloted. Coordination is deterministic, with no new scheduler or API. Research finding: READ-F15 (`Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md:24279`).

## Current state
- Examples exist in `Examples/features/concurrency/`: bounded_workers, task_all, cancel_cleanup, shield_commit, tasks_join_all, task_group and select_channel all have goldens. `all_failfast.jet:1-33` and `task_panic.jet` are expected-failure examples (`.err.out` convention) with no `.out`.
- The surface is `Core/tasks/tasks.jet` and `Core/sync/sync.jet`.
- The existing goldens print labels such as a worker limit. They do not observe state transitions, so capacity-one backpressure and the two-worker limit are asserted by text, not proven.

## Changes
1. Write `Examples/features/concurrency/conformance_capsule.jet`, with each cell a function printing observed transitions:
   - capacity-one channel: the second send blocks until a receive happens (observed through a handshake channel, not sleeps);
   - two-worker limit: a shared max-in-flight counter never exceeds 2;
   - explicit join and scope-owned join; a bound Task must be joined, used or detached (UI fixture `tests/ui/task_unjoined.jet`);
   - `task.all` first failure keeps the winner's error identity; panic becomes TaskFailure.Panicked; siblings are cancelled at a documented wait point; a shielded commit is deferred until after cancellation.
2. Run the same capsule on every tier. Record any evaluator or host-bridge gap as an open cell with its exact error; never substitute another path and claim equivalence.
3. Cancellation cleanup order is checked through #3179 (READ-F14), and guard fixes through READ-F05.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=concurrency/ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes, including the new capsule, and `jet run --interpret` of the capsule matches byte for byte.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev -- concurrency_and_game_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot` passes with the capsule added to its example set.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/task_unjoined Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` passes.

## Batch
batch-core-tasks: tasks, channels and scheduler behaviour, proven by one golden run.

## Dependencies
None. Cleanup order is shared with #3179, which does not block this card.

3. Prove explicit and scope-owned joins, the obligation to join/use/detach a bound Task, and documented channel wait/readiness behavior without importing foreign loop syntax.
4. Exercise task.all first failure, panic-to-TaskFailure, cancelled-member behavior, sibling cancellation at documented wait points and shield deferral; preserve the intended winner/error identity.
5. Verify cancellation cleanup via READ-F14 and guard fixes via READ-F05. Record evaluator/host-bridge gaps honestly instead of substituting another path and claiming equivalence.
