cards.title: Design checked workgroup storage and barriers
cards.body:
Design checked workgroup storage and barriers.

W2/W6 cannot be represented by a scalar zip-map alone.

Prepare the bounded design and proof under the accompanying complete scope ballot; implementation remains gated by exact API/semantic approval.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-gpu-f09. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

Exact source proof boundary: Proposed investigation/design/measurement; no implementation or runtime proof claimed.

Owner boundary: {'decision_id': 'D-GPU-GROUP-SCOPE1', 'choice': 'Should checked kernels expose workgroup arrays and barriers?', 'kind': 'Complete exact public/semantic choice; unratified author draft.'}
cards.plan:
## Goal
Settle D-GPU-GROUP-SCOPE1 (checked workgroup storage and barriers), then build or record the chosen route for the W2/W6 cells, which a scalar zip-map cannot express. This card is the single home; do not create a duplicate.

## Owner gate (open)
D-GPU-GROUP-SCOPE1 is open (draft).
- Option A exposes `workgroup_array(at, length, fill)` plus `workgroup_barrier(at)`, with Invocation facts and launch control. The ballot author recommends A, but A is blocked by its own missing matched pair and the strict candidate/plain win (the AGENTS.md performance gate).
- Option B keeps authored workgroup storage out and uses the existing tensor operations.
- Recommendation: B until authored kernels execute (#3026) and A's matched F32 sum-of-squares programs (both yield 5559680) show a strict win; then revisit A. This plan is written for B, with the A delta below.

## Current state
- Kernel checks live in `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/ComputeValidation.jet` (181 lines) and `Sema/Ownership/Crossings.jet:358-388`.

`batch-core-ui` (core.compute/gpu family). The B route and the A surface both land in Core/compute, with sema checks only under A.

Owner ballot D-GPU-GROUP-SCOPE1. Under A, also #3026.

cards.plan:
## Goal
Settle D-GPU-SUBGROUP-SCOPE1: does lane-to-lane exchange stay a compiler-internal optimization behind ordinary checked resource access (A), or become an explicit checked `subgroup_shuffle` with Invocation facts and `subgroup_size` launch control (B)? Assuming 32 lanes or CUDA scheduling would break portable code.

## Owner gate (open)
- D-GPU-SUBGROUP-SCOPE1 is open (draft). Both the ballot author and triage recommend A, which adds no public surface.
- Option B is also blocked by its own missing matched-program strict win.
- This plan is written for A.

## Current state
- Kernel validation is `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/ComputeValidation.jet`. Lowering is `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Functions.jet:1124-1139` (`jet_codegen_lower_kernel_proof`, `.Parallel` only). `Compiler/JetOptimizer` has no subgroup pass.
- Authored kernels do not launch yet (#3026 ready), and the self-hosted sema never fills `kernel_proof` (`CheckProgram.jet:801`).
- The finding is `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-gpu-f10` (the card cites the stale `docs/` path).

## Changes (A)
1. Add `Examples/features/tooling/compute_neighbor_square.jet`. The complete 32-value neighbor-square program uses ordinary indexed source (`at.index ± 1` reads of a checked View). It prints the 32 results.
2. On devices where it is available, record queried 32-lane and 64-lane behaviour. Keep unavailable cells explicit. Other widths use explicit supported controls and are never implicitly remapped.
3. Record the active-lane participation, width and mask contracts, and the exact unsupported-feature failure before launch.
4. Measure whether internal lowering (a JetOptimizer shuffle rewrite, if any) serves the workload. Any such rewrite must preserve the checked semantics and ship with a paired two-program cell.

## B delta (only if ratified)
- A public `subgroup_shuffle` in `Core/compute/compute.jet`, plus Invocation `subgroup_size` facts and a launch control.
- Width checks in `ComputeValidation.jet`, and UI negatives for undeclared widths.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=tooling/compute_neighbor_square.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` prints the 32 expected values, `jet run --interpret` matches, and a GPU-provider run is recorded, or labeled unavailable.
- Measurement: `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry tensor-map-4k --runs 11` has no regression after any internal rewrite.

## Batch
`batch-core-ui` (compute/gpu family).

## Dependencies
Owner ballot D-GPU-SUBGROUP-SCOPE1 and #3026 (authored kernels must execute).

cards.title: Decide checked atomics for contended GPU algorithms
cards.body:
Decide checked atomics for contended GPU algorithms.

Histogram/scatter workloads need a policy for contended updates,not a false disjoint-write proof.

Prepare the bounded design and proof under the accompanying complete scope ballot; implementation remains gated by exact API/semantic approval.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-gpu-f11. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

Exact source proof boundary: Proposed investigation/design/measurement; no implementation or runtime proof claimed.

Owner boundary: {'decision_id': 'D-GPU-ATOMIC-SCOPE1', 'choice': 'Should kernels use existing atomic cells or avoid contended writes?', 'kind': 'Complete exact public/semantic choice; unratified author draft.'}
cards.plan:
## Goal
Settle D-GPU-ATOMIC-SCOPE1, the policy for contended GPU updates such as histogram and scatter. The choice is between moving existing `Atomic<U32>` cells into an owning tensor (A) and a non-contending per-bucket scan over the same checked `U32` launch (B). A false disjoint-write proof is never acceptable.

## Owner gate (open)
- D-GPU-ATOMIC-SCOPE1 is open (draft). The ballot author recommends A, but A is blocked by its missing matched pair and strict candidate/plain win.
- Triage recommends B for now: it adds no public surface and runs once #3026 lands. Revisit A after authored-kernel matched programs exist.
- This plan is written for B.

## Current state
- Kernel checks live in `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/ComputeValidation.jet`, and the host compute providers in `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Compute.rs`.
- No authored kernel launches yet (#3026).
- Existing `AtomicU64` source is not device-layout evidence, and relaxed `atomicAdd` is not sufficient.
- The finding is `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-gpu-f11` (the card cites the stale `docs/` path).

## Changes (B)
1. Add `Examples/features/tooling/compute_histogram.jet`. It builds a per-bucket non-contending scan over the checked `U32` launch and prints `counts [1,3]` from input `[1,0,1,1]`. It also covers repeated indices, initialization, bounds and exact totals.
2. Add `tests/ui/gpu_contended_store.jet`, a contended write through an ordinary exclusive `ViewMut`, which must be rejected. Add `tests/ui/gpu_float_atomic_reproducible.jet`, where nondeterministic float accumulation is rejected under F32Strict+Reproducible.
3. Preserve D-PLACE1 and D-ATOMIC-WIDTH1: one family, sequential consistency, no order argument, no relaxed operation, and no hidden lock or weakened progress claim. Unsupported GPU semantics reject. The source input-visit counts are algorithm facts, not timing evidence.

## A delta (only if ratified)
- Move initialized `Atomic<U32>` cells into `Tensor<Atomic<U32>>` and consume that owner on readback. Prove that no host loan, copied cell identity or host atomic reference to device bytes survives.
- Prove the one-word layout, target size/alignment, transfer encoding, sequential consistency, linearizability, nonblocking progress and device-loss consumption.
- No numeric tensor may be reinterpreted as atomic storage.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=tooling/compute_histogram.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` prints `[1,3]`, and `jet run --interpret` matches.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/gpu_ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` shows both rejections with registered codes.

## Batch
`batch-core-ui` (compute/gpu family).

## Dependencies
Owner ballot D-GPU-ATOMIC-SCOPE1 and #3026 (authored-kernel launch).
cards.checkSteps:
1. Use an integer histogram with repeated indices. Verify initialization,bounds,exact totals and the hardware scope needed to preserve existing Atomic ordering.
2. Do not classify contended atomic writes as ordinary exclusive ViewMut stores.
3. Do not admit nondeterministic floating atomic addition under F32Strict+Reproducible; preserve named recorded policy rules.
4. Preserve D-PLACE1/D-ATOMIC-WIDTH1:one family,ordinary sequential consistency,publish/observe,no order argument or relaxed operation,no hidden lock or weakened progress claim. Unsupported GPU semantics reject.
5. Ratify the exact owning Atomic<U32> tensor construction, launch and readback in D-GPU-ATOMIC-SCOPE1, or the complete per-bucket noncontending alternative. No numeric tensor may be reinterpreted as atomic storage.
6. Move initialized Atomic<U32> cells into Tensor<Atomic<U32>> and consume that owner on readback. Prove no surviving host loan, copied cell identity or host atomic reference to device bytes.
7. Prove the selected one-word layout, target-visible size/alignment, transfer encoding, sequential consistency, linearizability, nonblocking progress and device-loss consumption. Current AtomicU64 source is not device-layout evidence; relaxed atomicAdd is not sufficient.
8. Both alternatives produce parity counts[1,3] from[1,0,1,1]. The source input-visit counts are algorithm facts, not timing evidence.

cards.body:
Decide tile acceleration as public Core capability or internal lowering.

Tile/matrix hardware may accelerate useful fused kernels,but public vendor-shaped APIs impose lasting cost.

Prepare the bounded design and proof under the accompanying complete scope ballot; implementation remains gated by exact API/semantic approval.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-gpu-f12. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

Exact source proof boundary: Proposed investigation/design/measurement; no implementation or runtime proof claimed.

Owner boundary: {'decision_id': 'D-GPU-TILE-SCOPE1', 'choice': 'Should tile optimization stay internal or become an explicit checked kernel value?', 'kind': 'Complete exact public/semantic choice; unratified author draft.'}
cards.plan:
## Goal
Decide D-GPU-TILE-SCOPE1 on evidence: tile acceleration either stays an internal lowering of existing tensor operations (A, recommended) or becomes a public `Tile<F32>` value with five collectives (B). The plan below is written for A. No public API is implied by internal optimization.

## Current state
- `Core/compute/compute.jet:235` `maximum`, `:244` `matmul` (`matmul_blocked(a, b, 8, …)`), `:251` `matmul_f32_tile` (separate existing operation). A fused matmul+bias+clamp runs as three separate ops today.
- D-GPU-TILE-SCOPE1 is open (A: optimize existing ops internally; B: public Tile<F32> plus five collectives). The #3398 handoff says to use the checked kernel/resource facts under #3026-#3028 (#3026 ready).
- Finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-gpu-f12`.

## Changes (evidence first, then A)
1. Measure (criteria 1-3): a Tools/perf cell for the complete 2x2 bias/clamp case and the larger canonical candidate/plain matrix. Compare matched dtype/layout: unfused `matmul`→`add`→`maximum`, `matmul_f32_tile`, and cuTile/CubeCL/Burn peers where available. Record precision, accumulation order, rounding, alignment, tile extent, target capability, compile and warm-cache cost, and end-to-end time. No fast-math and no silent narrowing.
2. If A wins: add an internal fused path in `Core/compute/compute.jet` (a private helper selected when a matmul result feeds add/maximum in one expression, or via the existing blocked kernel). cards.body:
Decide authored U32 kernels and typed Tensor support.

The exact W1/W2 graphics/data workloads use U32; F32 launch proof does not establish integer GPU behavior.

Prepare the bounded design and proof under the accompanying complete scope ballot; implementation remains gated by exact API/semantic approval.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-gpu-f13. Owner boundary: {'decision_id': 'D-GPU-U32-SCOPE1', 'choice': 'Should the existing authored launch admit physical U32 data?', 'kind': 'Complete exact public/semantic choice; unratified author draft.'}
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Settle D-GPU-U32-SCOPE1 and deliver the chosen route: either authored kernels and Tensor admit physical U32 with explicit wrapping, or U32 workloads stay CPU-only with honest unsupported cells. There is no F32 relabel and no new precision default.

**Owner ballot (open: D-GPU-U32-SCOPE1)**
(A) Admit U32 storage and kernels with a U32 dtype and explicit wrapping ops. (B) Keep U32 CPU-only and record GPU U32 as unsupported. (C) Defer until #3028. Recommendation: B now, and revisit A once #3028's matrix proves cross-target integer dispatch, because integer GPU semantics differ per backend. This plan is written for B, with the A delta noted.

**Current state**
- Core/compute/compute.jet:41-46: `Tensor.data: [Float]`, `numeric_profile` limited to the F64/F32 constructors (around :93-140). :814 and :827 serialization accepts only `c_profile_f64`/`c_profile_f32`. Non-CPU paths return `ComputeError.Unsupported` (:155, :602, :744, :812).
- Kernels: `#Kernel(.parallel)` (Examples/features/tooling/compute_kernel.jet:12) runs on CPU. The sema lives in Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/ComputeValidation.jet.
- tests/fixtures/compute_gpu_evidence_matrix.json: W1, W2 and W4 are U32.

**Changes (option B)**
1. Add Examples/features/tooling/compute_u32.jet: the exact 257-element W1 over `[U32]` with `wrapping_add`/`wrapping_mul` on CPU (no Float or F64 conversion), a checked-overflow negative returning a typed error, and `on_device(…, device_cuda())` → `ComputeError.Unsupported` for U32 work.
2. Numeric width inventory: print I8…I64, U8…U64, F32 and F64 as supported or unsupported per kernel and Tensor. Add none implicitly.
3. ComputeValidation.jet: reject a `#Kernel` whose parameters are U32 buffers when placement is non-CPU, with a registered diagnostic, its what/why/fix text, and tests/ui/compute_u32_gpu_placement.jet.
4. Option A delta: a `Tensor` dtype field and a U32 constructor, with an exact spelling in the ballot.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=tooling/compute_u32 Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: passes.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=compute_u32_gpu_placement Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`: the snapshot matches.

**Batch**
batch-core-ui (gpu family).

**Dependencies**
Owner ballot D-GPU-U32-SCOPE1.

cards.plan:
## Goal
Settle D-GPU-RANKED-SCOPE1 for checked kernel resources beyond the 1D amendment. Option A keeps ranked coordinates through `at.coord(axis)` and the existing ranked View brackets. Option B stays 1D with explicit flatten/reshape at the boundary. Images and matrices must not need hidden flattening copies or a second resource type. This card owns only the higher-rank, coordinate and layout extension; 1D strided views belong to D-GPU-INDEXED-RESOURCE1.

## Owner gate (open)
- D-GPU-RANKED-SCOPE1 is open (draft). The ballot author recommends A, but A is blocked by its missing matched pair and strict win.
- Triage recommends deferring: ratify D-GPU-INDEXED-RESOURCE1 (also open) first, then use B until A's matched strict-win programs exist.
- This plan is written for B.

## Current state
- Kernel resource checks are `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/ComputeValidation.jet`. Core tensors (`Core/compute/compute.jet`) already carry `shape` and strides (`sum_axis` at `:264`).

1. Add `Examples/features/tooling/compute_row_exchange.jet`. The complete 2x3 row exchange uses explicit flatten/reshape with existing syntax and prints `[4,5,6,1,2,3]`.
2. Add a transposed/subview matrix case with nontrivial strides. Validate shape and byte-size overflow and provider alignment, and allow no implicit broadcast, reshape-copy, narrowing or new buffer family.
3. Add UI negatives `tests/ui/gpu_shape_overflow.jet` and `gpu_stride_misaligned.jet`.
4. Keep the fixed matrix/vector arithmetic and `core.linalg` that are always available, and use no different index grammar.

## A delta (only if ratified)
- `Invocation.coord(axis)` and ranked View brackets inside `#Kernel` bodies.
- Rank and stride facts in `ComputeValidation.jet`.
- The same 2x3 program without a flatten.

## Proof

Owner ballots D-GPU-INDEXED-RESOURCE1, then D-GPU-RANKED-SCOPE1. Also #3026 (authored-kernel launch).

cards.title: Design proved helpers and bounded control flow in kernels
cards.body:
Design proved helpers and bounded control flow in kernels.

Useful generic kernels need a precise ordinary-language subset; cargo familiarity alone does not settle allocator,panic,dyn or recursion behavior.

Prepare the bounded design and proof under the accompanying complete scope ballot; implementation remains gated by exact API/semantic approval.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-gpu-f15. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

Exact source proof boundary: Proposed investigation/design/measurement; no implementation or runtime proof claimed.

Owner boundary: {'decision_id': 'D-GPU-HELPER-SCOPE1', 'choice': 'Should device eligibility follow the kernel call or require a helper marker?', 'kind': 'Complete exact public/semantic choice; unratified author draft.'}
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-GPU-HELPER-SCOPE1=A (ratified): one reachability-aware kernel checker proves the ordinary helpers and bounded loops reachable from a `#Kernel(.parallel)` body. Library authors never annotate helpers; there is no second marker, helper checker, owner family or launch engine.

## Current state
- AST: `KernelProof{mode, bounds, alias_free, captures, race_free, barriers_uniform, control_flow}` at `Compiler/JetAst/Source/AST/Items.jet:618-626`, carried on the marker at `:631`, and `TFunc.kernel_proof` at `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/TIR/TIR.jet:1928`.
- The self-hosted sema never builds that proof: `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/CheckProgram.jet:801` hardcodes `kernel_proof: None`.
- Kernel-related checks exist only at crossings (`Sema/Ownership/Crossings.jet:358-388`).
- Codegen lowers only `.Parallel` (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Functions.jet:1124-1139`).
- The archived reference is `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerKernel.rs:676-906` (`check_kernel_marker`, E1102). It proves the body only, not reachable helpers.
- The shipped example is a single expression (`Examples/features/tooling/compute_kernel.jet:12`).
- Recovery scaffold 593a5690f was never integrated.
- The finding is `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-gpu-f15` (the card cites the stale `docs/` path).

## Changes
1. JetSema: add `Sema/KernelProof.jet`.
   - Port `check_kernel_marker` and set `kernel_proof` in `CheckProgram.jet:801`.
   - Walk the call graph from each kernel and prove every reachable body for bounds, aliasing, captures, races, uniform barriers, finite loops (a constant or parameter-bounded `loop` with a proved bound) and control flow.
   - Reject dynamic dispatch, opaque or foreign calls, unproved recursion, forbidden captures or effects, allocation, panic and divergent barriers. Each rejection is E1102 with a span on the helper plus a note naming the kernel call path.
2. Specialization and cache identity include the checked body, types, policies and capabilities of every reachable helper (`Functions.jet` lowering keys).
3. Mirror the reachability walk in `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerKernel.rs` so the shipped binary proves the same rows.
4. On the card, record the inventory table: calls, generics/traits, closures, captures, loops, recursion, dyn, allocation and panic, each marked supported, rejected or unknown against the captured device languages.

## Proof
- `Examples/features/tooling/compute_helper_loop.jet`: one helper called by two kernels plus one bounded loop, printing `[31,47]`. `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=tooling/compute_helper_loop.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes, and `jet run --interpret` matches.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/kernel_helper_ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` covers a helper that allocates, recursion, a dyn call, an unbounded loop and a host effect. Each has a source-level explanation.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` shows no new diagnostics in the touched JetSema files, compared with the pre-change receipt.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-sema`. This is kernel-proof checking.

## Dependencies
None to build the checker. Device execution of the helper programs belongs to #3026.

3. No second frontend/checker or provider-owned meaning; specialization/cache identity includes checked body,types,policies and capabilities.
4. Ratify A reachable helper proof or B the exact #Kernel(.helper) marker in D-GPU-HELPER-SCOPE1. Both complete helper/loop programs yield[31,47]; rejected host effects keep source-level explanations.

cards.title: Measure host overlap without changing completed launch
cards.body:
Measure host overlap without changing completed launch.

D-GPU-COMPUTE-LAUNCH1 returns a completed Tensor; vendor async streams are not evidence that Jet exposes equivalent host overlap.

Measure whether existing ordinary host concurrency plus completed compute.launch can overlap useful work and preserve resource ownership. Do not introduce another result token by inference.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-gpu-f16. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

Exact source proof boundary: Proposed investigation/design/measurement; no implementation or runtime proof claimed.

Owner boundary: No independent owner choice asserted by this finding; preserve its exact scoped investigation and existing law.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Measure whether ordinary host concurrency (`spawn`/channels, D-ASYNCRT1) plus the completed `compute.launch` (D-GPU-COMPUTE-LAUNCH1=A) overlaps useful host work, without inventing an async result token.

**Current state**
- `compute.launch` does not exist yet: there is no `launch` in Core/compute/compute.jet and no compute_launch in Compiler/ or Compute.rs. #3026 owns it.
- tests/fixtures/compute_gpu_evidence_matrix.json `overlap`: witness W4, stage order host_prepare→transfer_in→compute_submit→compute_complete→transfer_out→host_consume, the required fields, and comparison lanes (CUDA/HIP events, cuTile DeviceOp, existing Jet concurrency).
- The host concurrency spelling is in Examples/features/concurrency/scheduler_spawn.jet and task_group_parameter.jet (`spawn` plus `channel<T>`). The harness pattern is Tools/perf/corelib_compare.py.

**Changes**
1. After #3026, add Tools/perf/compute_overlap_bench.py plus Tools/perf/compute_overlap/overlap.jet. The Jet arm runs W4 host work in a `spawn`ed task concurrently with a completed `compute.launch` in another task and timestamps each stage. The baseline arm runs the same stages sequentially.
2. Peer lanes: a CUDA event recipe and a cuTile DeviceOp recipe, run only when a real device and toolchain exist. Otherwise they are `unavailable` with the reason, never zero.
3. Record each required field separately. Cancellation is a task cancel before launch completes, and the result must report the completed-call semantics.
4. If overlap requires an async Core return or a transfer API, write a separate amendment ballot to D-GPU-COMPUTE-LAUNCH1. No code for it on this card.

**Proof**
- `python3 Tools/perf/compute_overlap_bench.py --samples 5 --json ~/.cache/jet-luna/perf/compute_overlap.json`: exit 0, all cells populated or unavailable.
- The receipt is attached with commit, toolchain and machine.

**Batch**
batch-measure: a harness and a run, with no compiler or Core change.

**Dependencies**
#3026 (completed `compute.launch`). The W4 dtype follows #3216; run W4 as specified if U32 GPU is admitted, else record it as unsupported and measure the F32 W0 pipeline.

cards.title: Decide GPU toolchain packaging and audit dependency candidates
cards.body:
Decide GPU toolchain packaging and audit dependency candidates.

Nightly/toolchain/driver chains and first-launch JIT cost affect first-use success and distribution weight.

Inventory current Jet codegen/runtime dependencies and compare the two packaging policies in D-GPU-PACKAGING1. Prepare individual named dependency-adoption ballots only after exact versions,licenses,roles and costs are known.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-gpu-f17. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

Exact source proof boundary: Proposed investigation/design/measurement; no implementation or runtime proof claimed.

Owner boundary: {'decision_id': 'D-GPU-PACKAGING1', 'choice': 'Stock source/checking with optional provider toolchain components versus bundling selected compiler components; no named adoption authorized.', 'kind': 'Distribution scope'}
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Apply D-GPU-PACKAGING1=A. Stock Jet ships Core source plus the checker, and physical device compilers are optional external components acquired through Jetpack fetch, lock and audit. Deliver the component inventory and the actionable missing-component result for non-CPU devices.

**Current state**
- Core/compute/compute.jet:80-85 names the device constructors (CPU/Auto/CUDA/Metal/Vulkan/WebGPU). :787-790 `select_device` returns the name. :152-157 and :742-756 return a bare `ComputeError.Unsupported` for non-CPU devices, with no component named and no remedy (`ComputeError` :23-34).
- There is no rust-gpu, Naga, wgpu or CUDA dependency in Cargo.toml or crates/*/Cargo.toml, and no device-compiler provider in Compiler/JetCodegen.
- Examples/features/tooling/compute_capabilities.jet with its golden reports capabilities.
- Criterion 4 is already met.

**Changes**
1. Inventory: add Docs/research/gpu-toolchain-inventory-2026-09.md with current components (from Cargo.lock and the Jetpack provider manifests) and candidate components (rust-gpu, Rust-CUDA, cuTile, CubeCL, Naga, wgpu, vendor SDKs), each with version, license, security, footprint, cache and upgrade facts. It is evidence only and selects nothing; each adoption is its own later ballot.
2. Missing-component result: when a non-CPU device is selected and its provider component is absent, return the result D-GPU-PACKAGING1=A specifies. That means a typed compute error that names the component, the Jetpack acquisition command and the capability layer that failed (source-check, device-compile, driver or hardware). Use the spelling in the ratified decision text. If the decision gives none, raise a spelling-only ballot before editing `ComputeError`. There are no implicit downloads, license acceptance or driver installs.
3. Extend compute_capabilities.jet so it prints the five capability layers separately, and update its golden.
4. Offline toolchains keep Core source and verified metadata (D-CORE-SOURCE-AUTHORITY1). #3028 keeps vendor coverage.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=tooling/compute_capabilities Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: passes.
- `for m in --release '' --interpret; do Tools/agent/jet-env jet run $m Examples/features/tooling/compute_capabilities.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/tooling/compute_capabilities.out; done`: empty.

**Batch**

**Dependencies**
None.

cards.title: Prove the GPU authoring and diagnostic repair loop
cards.body:
Prove the GPU authoring and diagnostic repair loop.

The observed invalid Debug suggestion,authority denial and interpreter flag failure show real edit-run friction; quantities remain unmeasured.

Build one honest current GPU getting-started/repair workflow after the owning execution fixes. Measure the ten micro categories and five agent-loop quantities against matched peer tasks.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-gpu-f18. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

Exact source proof boundary: Proposed investigation/design/measurement; no implementation or runtime proof claimed.

Owner boundary: No independent owner choice asserted by this finding; preserve its exact scoped investigation and existing law.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Measure one GPU getting-started → diagnostic → repair workflow on the current tree (GPU-F18). Record the ten micro categories and the five agent-loop quantities against a matched peer task. Fix only existing help, docs and diagnostics.

## Current state
- Finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md:24935` (GPU-F18; the old `docs/research` path moved). Observed friction: an invalid Debug suggestion, an authority denial and an interpreter-flag failure. None of it has been measured yet.
- The compute evidence matrix landed in a0fb3b3dc (card log 2026-09-21).
- Examples: `Examples/features/tooling/compute_{kernel,device,cuda,vulkan_webgpu,metal,capabilities,tensor,ndarray,...}.jet`, with goldens in `Examples/features/expected/tooling/compute_*.out`. Core surface: `Core/compute/compute.jet`.
- Host providers serve built-in operations only: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Compute.rs:1602` (libcuda dlopen) and `:2756` (libvulkan dlopen). User-authored kernels are #3026.

## Changes (measurement; no new API)
1. Choose one bounded, realistic task (for example, scale then reduce an F32 buffer) and run it in three legs: (a) a CPU example, (b) a built-in provider call through `core.compute`, (c) a user-authored kernel (#3026). Use current, source-equated CLI, help and authority recipes (criterion 1).
2. Run each leg from a cold agent context: `jet help` / `jet explain`, author, `jet check`, `jet run`, `jet run --interpret`, then repair the diagnostics. Record each of the ten categories as supported, unsupported or unknown: safety stage, types, resource ownership, transfer/copy visibility, discovery, formatting, diagnostics, shape, capability, code search (criterion 2).
3. For every step, record verdict fidelity, verdict latency (wall ms), actionability (whether the fix line led to a passing edit), context economy (bytes of source, diagnostics and help read) and repair determinism (the same repair on a rerun). Also record tool/action counts and the actual repair results. Run the matched peer task using the peer recorded in the finding (criterion 3).
4. Correct help or diagnostic text only where it is proven wrong, such as the invalid Debug suggestion. A new command, Core API or telemetry requires an owner ballot (criterion 4).
5. Write `Docs/audits/gpu-authoring-loop-<date>.md` and keep the raw logs in `~/.cache/jet-luna/gpu-f18/`.

## Proof
- Baseline: `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=tooling/compute_kernel cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- The audit has one row per leg × quantity with observed numbers, plus all ten category cells. Losing and unavailable cells stay in the table. Pass = all five quantities recorded for all three legs.

## Batch
batch-measure. This is evidence only; any help or diagnostic text fix rides in the same pass.

## Dependencies
#3026 (user-authored kernels) for leg (c). Legs (a) and (b) can run now.

3. Measure all five declared quantities:verdict fidelity,verdict latency,verdict actionability,context economy and repair determinism. Retain context bytes,tool/action counts,elapsed stages and actual repair results as observations,not invented savings.
4. Do not add a new command,Core API or telemetry system unless results justify it and an exact owner ballot approves it; fix existing documentation/help where contracts already exist.

cards.body:
Prove GPU source-to-provider debugging and profiling.

The ability to launch is not enough to explain a device failure or locate a copy/allocation bottleneck.

Inventory existing Jet inspect/receipt/debug/profiler routes and map an authored source span/program identity to the provider artifact and resource/timing evidence. Use existing mechanisms first.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-gpu-f19. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

Exact source proof boundary: Proposed investigation/proof; not executed.

Owner boundary: This investigation selects no new API/dependency/policy. Any concrete addition requires a complete exact owner ballot before implementation.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Trace one authored kernel from source, proof and cache identity to the actual provider program and its resource and timing evidence using existing inspect and receipt mechanisms, with CPU and source debugging kept distinct from real-device evidence.

**Current state**
- tests/fixtures/compute_gpu_evidence_matrix.json (a0fb3b3dc) `trace` names the witness (W1), the required fields (source_path … unsupported_reason), the identity chain, and the debug boundary (never claim source-level GPU stepping). No test consumes the fixture.
- `#Kernel(.parallel)` (Examples/features/tooling/compute_kernel.jet) runs on CPU only. Provider launch and dispatch belong to #3026 and #3028.
- Existing surfaces to reuse before adding anything: `jet inspect` facts, build receipts and the compute capability report (Examples/features/tooling/compute_capabilities.jet with its golden).

**Changes**
1. Inventory: map each required trace field to an existing producer (inspect facts, receipts, Compute.rs placement) or mark it missing, recorded in the fixture's `trace.source_anchors`.
2. Add tests/compute_parity.rs `kernel_trace_cpu`, which compiles compute_kernel.jet, reads the kernel's source span, sha and proof/cache identity from existing inspect output, runs it, and asserts the record fields with measured instrumentation overhead. `kernel_trace_provider` does the same on one real provider after #3026 and #3028. Use the W1 witness if #3216 admits U32; otherwise use the F32 W0 witness and note the substitution.
3. Failure witnesses: a kernel source error (existing diagnostic, typed span) and a provider/device failure (invalid device index) that keeps typed `ComputeError` context.
4. Any missing field that needs a new command, API or capture dependency becomes an owner ballot. There is no new telemetry subsystem.

**Proof**

cards.title: Prove authored-kernel and gradient composition
cards.body:
Prove authored-kernel and gradient composition.

Library usefulness includes custom operations composed with differentiation,not only forward kernel output.

Build one bounded value-and-gradient workflow under the existing compute transform law,using the same authored operation and placement on CPU and a real provider. First establish whether the existing route admits it.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-gpu-f20. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

Exact source proof boundary: Proposed investigation/proof; not executed.

Owner boundary: This investigation selects no new API/dependency/policy. Any concrete addition requires a complete exact owner ballot before implementation.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Prove that an authored operation composes with the ratified differentiation transforms (gradient, value_and_gradient, jvp, vjp): sum(x*x) at [1, 2, 3] → value 14 and gradient [2, 4, 6], on CPU and one real provider, with the same operation and placement.

**Current state**
- The transform over functions exists. Examples/features/tooling/compute_autodiff.jet:10-30 runs `compute.gradient(loss, w, x)`, `compute.gradient(loss)` (a transform) and a second-order `gradient(d_loss)`, all on CPU with a golden.
- Core/compute/compute.jet:332-355: the value-level `value_and_gradient(pred, target)`, `vjp` and `gradient(pred, target)` are MSE-specific helpers. `jvp` checks shape, device and profile.
- `#Kernel(.parallel)` exists (Examples/features/tooling/compute_kernel.jet:12), but authored kernel launch on a provider is #3026's job. Device paths return `Unsupported` (:155).

**Changes**
1. Runnable now on CPU: add Examples/features/tooling/compute_kernel_gradient.jet. It declares `#Kernel(.parallel) fn square(x: Float) -> Float` and `fn loss(x: Tensor) -> Tensor` = sum of `square` over x, then prints `compute.value_and_gradient(loss)`, `vjp` and `jvp` at [1, 2, 3]. Record derivative ownership (derived by the transform, no second definition), shape and effect checks, seed and pull, and residency.
2. Negative rows: a mutating kernel and data-dependent control flow must fail as source or typed errors. Add a tests/ui fixture for the source error with its snapshot.
3. After #3026 and #3028, add tests/compute_parity.rs `kernel_gradient_provider`, running the same program with provider placement. There is no hidden host fallback.
4. If the transform cannot admit authored kernels, return an exact kernel-transform admission ballot and keep the names.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=tooling/compute_kernel_gradient Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test compute_parity -- kernel_gradient_provider`: passes or reports a typed unsupported cell.

**Batch**
batch-core-ui (gpu family).

**Dependencies**
#3026 (authored kernels on providers) and #3028 (a real provider), only for the provider half. The CPU half (step 1-2) can land now.

**Current state.**
- `Core/files/files.jet` (107 public fns) has:

  - `temp_dir`/`temp_file` (:755/:758) and `lock` (:761), which are provider leaves
  - `read_at`, `symlink`, `read_link`, `copy2`
- `Core/files/path.jet` (75 fns) is pure lexical `Path`, and FS effects are separate (c4). D-PATH-CONTAINMENT1=A lexical `is_within` has a witness in `Examples/features/io/path_within.jet`.

**Changes.**
1. Add `Examples/features/io/files_rooted_lifecycle.jet` and its `.out` with the cases in add_criteria. Use only existing APIs. Everything runs under a `temp_dir`, so it is hermetic.
2. Document the observed symlink, metadata-preservation (`copy2`) and lock semantics in the doc comments of `files.jet` `symlink`/`copy2`/`lock` (c5).
3. If a case fails, fix it at the root in the Core source or provider leaf within this card. A missing API (e.g. an `openat`-style rooted open that defeats replacement races) is recorded as a new owner-gated card and marked unsupported in the receipt, not inferred (c6).
4. Record the supported, unsupported and unknown matrix (Linux; macOS/Windows marked unknown) on the card.

**Proof.**

**Dependencies.** None. #3078/#3398 lifecycle ownership still governs the close semantics.

cards.title: Prove HTTP client and shared-body lifecycle
cards.body:
Prove HTTP client and shared-body lifecycle

Both findings exercise the same HTTP client/body owner, phase/idle/total deadlines, trust settings, cancellation and connection reuse on controlled local responses.

CORE-F011: Exercise ordinary and streaming HTTP through one body owner and existing client policy, compared with HTTPX/Asio/Glaze.
Exercise ordinary and streaming HTTP through one body owner and existing client policy, compared with HTTPX/Asio/Glaze.
Evidence: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f011

SCRIPT-F07: A five-second inactivity timeout is not a total deadline, and TLS encryption or SNI is not certificate authentication. Jet already names phase/total limits and trust policy; the common scripting path must honor them.
Exercise the existing client against controlled local slow/status/oversize responses and a private local certificate fixture. Preserve bounded body and cancellation cleanup.
Evidence: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-script-f07

Historical source and frozen-executable evidence retain their recorded identity and uncertainty; this research handoff is not a current-tree proof.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove the HTTP client and shared-body lifecycle against the Jet owner once #3665 lands: consumption, cancellation, the separate phase, idle and total deadlines, redirect and credential policy, trust, and actual resource release.

## Current state
- Phase, total and trust timeouts live in the Rust bridge today: `resolve_request_phase_timeouts` and `compose_total_deadline` (crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Prelude/HTTP.rs:53, :307-340, :2106-2163) and crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/HTTPClient.rs:94-97, :203-209.
- In the Jet client: `Session.timeout_ms` (Core/http/client.jet:35, :95, :117-121), `RedirectPolicy {Disabled, Limited, All}` (:26-29), `redirect_limit` (:244-250), a body cap check (:181, :282), and `HTTPError.Timeout(phase)`, `Cancelled` and `BodyConsumed` (Core/http/http.jet:34-42).
- Existing loopback law tests in tests/http_client_law.rs: `public_client_policy_exposes_pool_cookie_timeouts_and_facts` (:721), `post_307_replays_streamed_body_under_redirect_tee_cap` (:1682), `https_to_http_redirect_denied_unless_allow_http_downgrade` (:2557), `ambient_context_deadline_upper_bounds_client_total_timeout` (:2814), `unreplayable_307_closes_redirect_body` (:2942), `follow_same_origin_credentials_strips_authorization_on_redirect` (:3123), `cross_origin_redirect_strips_request_credentials_and_rejects_proxy_auth` (:3187) and `request_first_byte_timeout_overrides_client_phase_budget` (:3280).

## Changes (after #3665)
1. Add loopback tests to tests/http_client_law.rs: `http_body_second_consumption_is_body_consumed`; `http_early_drop_releases_pooled_connection` (a pool reuse count after the drop); `http_cancel_during_read_and_upload_releases_socket`; `http_slow_active_stream_idle_vs_total_deadline` (a trickling body passes the idle timeout and fails the total one with `Timeout("total")`); and `http_status_size_json_schema_errors_are_distinct`.
2. Add `https_default_trust_rejects_expired_wrong_name_untrusted` with a custom-trust variant that relaxes only the named policy (tests/http_server_tls.rs fixtures, no external network).
3. Fix any failure in the Jet owner (Core/http/client.jet or http.jet), not in a Rust shim.

## Proof
- `cargo test --test http_client_law -- http_body_second_consumption_is_body_consumed http_early_drop_releases_pooled_connection http_cancel_during_read_and_upload_releases_socket http_slow_active_stream_idle_vs_total_deadline http_status_size_json_schema_errors_are_distinct` passes.
- `cargo test --test http_client_law -- https_default_trust_rejects_expired_wrong_name_untrusted` passes.
- The eight existing law tests named above still pass.

## Batch
batch-core-net: an HTTP client proof in the same retest as #3665.

## Dependencies
#3665 (the Jet HTTP client port). Running the proof earlier would only have to be redone.

cards.title: Prove raw socket, DNS and network-resource lifecycle
cards.body:
Prove raw socket, DNS and network-resource lifecycle

Both use canonical non-HTTP socket/DNS ownership, partial I/O, structured errors, close and cancellation; URL, MIME and email remain separate.

CORE-F032: Compare DNS/TCP/UDP/TLS and ordinary file/pipe/OS-handle operations beyond HTTP against selected peer families.
Compare DNS/TCP/UDP/TLS and ordinary file/pipe/OS-handle operations beyond HTTP against selected peer families.
Evidence: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f032

SCRIPT-F30: Typed TCP/UDP/Unix/DNS/TLS already share one byte-stream/deadline/error law; the scripting workflow lacks focused execution receipts.
Exercise existing socket/DNS/readiness/cancellation operations through one ordinary bounded local transfer, including partial IO, half-close, truncation and earliest deadline.
Evidence: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-script-f30

Historical source and frozen-executable evidence retain their recorded identity and uncertainty; this research handoff is not a current-tree proof.
cards.plan:
**Goal.** Produce a current-tree execution receipt and a target matrix for non-HTTP networking (CORE-F032 and SCRIPT-F30; research: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f032`, `#finding-script-f30`). Scope:
- TCP/UDP/Unix/TLS under the shared positive-limit, partial-write and EOF law
- UDP truncation metadata
- host DNS versus wire resolver
- cancellation, earliest deadline, half-close and misuse after close

URL, MIME, email and FTP stay on separate cards.

**Current state.**
- `Core/net/net.jet` (583 lines) has:
  - `tcp_connect_timeout` (:131) and `set_timeout`/`set_read_timeout`/`set_write_timeout` (:228-243)
  - UDP bind, send and receive with `limit` validation (:270-304) and packet accessors, including `udp_packet_original_len`/`udp_packet_truncated` (:306-310)
  - Unix listen/accept/connect/read/write/`unix_shutdown(how: NetShutdown)`/close (:312-355)
- `Core/net/tls.jet` is the TLS client.
- Goldens exist for `net/socket_echo`, `net/dns_lookup` and `net/tls_peer_identity`.
- `Examples/features/net/network_core_contract.jet` (16 lines) covers IP/CIDR and MIME only (tested by `tests/network_core_contract.rs`). It is not a socket witness, so socket cases must not be added to it.

**Changes.**
1. Add `Examples/features/net/socket_lifecycle.jet` and its `.out` (loopback and a temp Unix path only; no external network) with the cases in add_criteria (c4, c5, c6).
2. DNS: extend `dns_lookup` only if host resolution versus the explicit wire resolver is not already distinguished in its output (c5).

cards.title: Prove one typed and streaming CSV contract
cards.body:
Prove one typed and streaming CSV contract

Both compare one canonical CSV reader/writer and typed-row contract for quoting, headers, dialects, malformed rows and bounded streaming.

CORE-F049: Compare existing CSV typed/row/column/headerless/delimiter/rectangular/quoted-field jobs with selected peers.
Compare existing CSV typed/row/column/headerless/delimiter/rectangular/quoted-field jobs with selected peers.
Evidence: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f049

SCRIPT-F16: CSV dialect, quoting and header behavior is a distinct format contract, not automatically covered by a JSON proof.
Compare the captured Python csv reader/writer/DictReader/DictWriter capabilities with Jet canonical CSV typed decode and current options.
Evidence: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-script-f16

Historical source and frozen-executable evidence retain their recorded identity and uncertainty; this research handoff is not a current-tree proof.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove one typed and streaming CSV contract: RFC 4180 quoting, a declared result for every row shape, bounded streaming with a proper close, and dialect options mapped explicitly.

## Current state
- Core/encoding/csv.jet:30-39 treats RFC 4180 rows as text cells and lifts them into `DataTree` arrays (`parse` :79). Typed `decode<T>` is compiler lowering over header-named columns.
- Defect: `rows(text, header: Bool{false}, skip_blank)` ignores `header` (`_ :: header`, :72-74).
- Defect: `dict_rows` (:293-314) pads short rows with "" and silently drops the extra fields of long rows. No rectangularity error exists.
- The Jet `reader(text)` (:96-99) parses the whole text. The streaming route that actually ships is the host `jet_enc_csv_reader(input: FileReader, limits, delimiter, ...)` (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/EncodingStream.rs:2413; dispatcher crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.jet:753), used by Examples/features/serde/encoding_csv_stream.jet:28.
- Law: Docs/spec/encoding-decisions.md:116-147 (reader over `^files.FileReader` plus limits) and :173-174 (CSVRow, RFC 4180 including quoted newlines).
- Goldens exist for serde/csv, csv_typed and encoding_csv_stream.

## Changes
1. csv.jet: `dict_rows` returns an `EncodingError` (Syntax, with line and column, reason `row N has M fields; the header has K`) for a ragged row instead of padding or truncating. Delete the dead `header` parameter of `rows` and migrate its callers.
2. New Examples/features/serde/csv_shapes.jet with its .out. It covers an embedded quote (`""`), a quoted delimiter, a quoted CRLF newline, an empty field versus an empty quoted field, a missing final newline, short and long rows through `dict_rows` and typed `decode<T>` (a type error with row and column), header mapping by name, a bare quote in an unquoted field (Syntax), and an unterminated quote at EOF (Truncated).
3. Extend encoding_csv_stream.jet with a file larger than `buffer_bytes: 64`, read row by row; an early drop of the reader mid-file (closed by RAII); and a row over `max_item_bytes` (Limit). Any defect found in the host reader is fixed there, since it remains the shipped route until #3690.
4. Map dialect options to the current API in the CSV section of encoding-decisions.md: delimiter is supported; quote and escape character, BOM, non-UTF-8 input, comment lines and skip-initial-space are explicit unsupported cells. Note that column transposition allocates (criterion 3). Any new option or default is a ballot first (criterion 7).

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/csv_shapes cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/encoding_csv_stream cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `for f in csv csv_typed csv_shapes; do Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/serde/$f.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/serde/$f.out; done` prints nothing.

## Batch
batch-core-encoding: csv.jet plus goldens. A host-reader fix, if needed, is a retained-boundary mirror.

## Dependencies
None.

6. Dialect/encoding/streaming options are mapped to current APIs; unsupported cells are explicit.
7. New CSV defaults or options are independently owner-balloted before implementation.

cards.title: Prove explicit App construction and service lifetimes
cards.body:
Prove explicit App construction and service lifetimes

Both prove ordinary App construction and explicit resource lifetimes against service-locator/provider composition. No dependency container is introduced.

CORE-F082: Map the selected MVVM Ioc and DI access job to existing App dependency ownership instead of importing a global service locator.
Map the selected MVVM Ioc and DI access job to existing App dependency ownership instead of importing a global service locator.
Evidence: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f082

nestjs-composition-availability-proof: Explicit functions are a benefit only if missing, duplicate and cyclic dependencies remain diagnosable without a runtime lookup container.
Exercise existing App/module/resource composition with shared values, factories, optional resources and one source-local invalid dependency. No new DI system.
Evidence: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-composition-availability-proof

Historical source and frozen-executable evidence retain their recorded identity and uncertainty; this research handoff is not a current-tree proof.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Show that ordinary App construction with explicit values covers what service locators and DI containers do: a shared app-scoped resource, a causal error for a missing dependency before serving, and test substitution without global mutation. No dependency container or second registration surface is added. This absorbs CORE-F082 (MVVM Ioc/DI access mapped to App ownership) and `nestjs-composition-availability-proof`. Findings: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f082` and the nestjs composition finding (the card cites the stale lowercase docs/ path).

## Current state
- There is no container or provider API.
  - `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/App.rs:940-2065` exposes only the JetApp builder (route, page, loader, mount, serve), used as `web.app().route(..).loader(..)` in `Examples/features/web/web_app.jet:14-22`.
  - `Core/app/app.jet:21-150` holds auth, live and sync helpers.
  - `Core/service/service.jet:18-48` holds supervision trees and restart policies.
- Handlers already capture constructed values: `Examples/features/net/backend_battery/run.jet:101-105` shares `Shared<Metrics>` across routes.

## Changes
1. Write `Examples/features/net/app_composition.jet`:
   - `fn build(store: OrderStore, clock: Clock) -> HTTPMux` constructs every handler from explicit values;
   - `run()` opens the real store once (`open_store(path) ?? ...`), and a missing store path returns a typed error naming the constructor before `bind`, printed with its source location;
   - the same `build` gets an in-memory fake store in a second mux, and dispatching `http.dispatch(mux, req)` for one request shows different observable output with no global state;
   - a request counter proves the store was constructed once across three requests.
2. Add no Core API. If a real gap appears (for example, a handler cannot capture a resource value), file it for a ballot. Do not work around it.
3. Route the Nest measurement comparison to #3096.

## Proof
`JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=net/app_composition Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes on AOT and default run. It prints: `store constructed once` across three requests; the missing-store error with its source line before any `serving` line; and different real and fake outputs from the same `build`.

## Batch
batch-core-net: an HTTP composition witness in Examples. No compiler change.

## Dependencies
None. Measurement belongs to #3096.

cards.title: Measure algorithm obligations on matched collection jobs
cards.body:
Measure algorithm obligations on matched collection jobs.

Run the existing competitive gate for sort/search/transform and eager/lazy collection jobs with the selected peer libraries.

Run the existing competitive gate for sort/search/transform and eager/lazy collection jobs with the selected peer libraries.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f002. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Add matched sort/search/transform and eager/lazy collection-job cells to the existing gauntlet, then measure them against the selected peer libraries (CORE-F002). Record losing cells; don't average them away.

## Current state
- Finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md:20266` (CORE-F002).
- The "existing competitive gate" has no collection cells: `Tools/gauntlet/entries/` holds 24 entries (binparse, csvtransform, wordfreq, ...) and none of them is a sort, search or transform job. `Tools/perf/corelib_compare.py:204-236` measures `runtime_only_ns` only.
- Jet surface: `Core/collections/collections.jet`, plus sema/lowering in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:239-260,843-885`.
- Entry layout: `entry.json`, `expected.out`, `jet/` and one directory per peer (`rust`, `c`, `zig`, `go`, `python`, `node`), registered in `Tools/gauntlet/matrix.json` and `Tools/gauntlet/measurement-manifest.json`.

## Changes
1. Add `Tools/gauntlet/entries/collections-jobs/` with fixed-seed inputs covering stable sort by key with ties, binary search / partition point, a map-filter-group transform, and the same pipeline eager versus lazy. Each peer uses its standard library (Rust std/itertools, Python stdlib, JS Array, Go `slices`/`sort`, C `qsort`, Zig std.sort).
2. Every implementation matches mutation (in place or copy), stability, tie order, error policy and the exact result bytes against one `expected.out` (criterion 1).
3. Add a source metric per cell: count of imports, callbacks, temporaries and hidden facts, recorded in the entry's source-metric row (criterion 2).
4. Register the entry in `matrix.json` and `measurement-manifest.json`. Each loss is a separate row with a bug card (criterion 3).

## Proof
- `node --test Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.test.mjs Tools/gauntlet/harness/measurement-manifest.test.mjs` is green.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry collections-jobs` shows every language matching `expected.out` on every tier (AOT, run, interpreter), with per-cell verdicts under the AGENTS.md comparator and losing cells listed individually.

## Batch
batch-measure. Harness corpus plus a run; no compiler change.

## Dependencies
None. The iterator-contract-before-adapters and performance-admission conditional chains (#3070) still govern any follow-on implementation.

cards.title: Close typed-number behavior across execution modes
cards.body:
Close typed-number behavior across execution modes.

Trace and exercise the public typed JSON path on one frozen native/interpreter/Web identity, including the captured native/Web integer-helper discrepancy.

Trace and exercise the public typed JSON path on one frozen native/interpreter/Web identity, including the captured native/Web integer-helper discrepancy.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f003. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Typed JSON numbers mean the same thing on AOT, default run, the evaluator and the web target, including the captured native/web integer-helper discrepancy. Exact integers and decimals are preserved as the target needs. Overflow and nonfinite values give typed errors with no silent string coercion or suppression. Finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f003`.

## Current state
- `Core/data/data.jet:549-552` `json<T: Decode>` forwards to the intrinsic `core.data.json<T>`, which has no Jet body.
- `Core/encoding/json.jet:71-76` parses JSON into `DataTree` in Jet. DataTree is a host type with `Int(i64)` (`crates/jet-foundation/src/DataTree.rs:9-12`), but `Int` is exact and unbounded (D-INTBIG1), so large integers are a real overflow and precision cell.
- `Compiler/JetEval/Source/Routes/Core.jet` has no core.data or json route (grep).
- The last attempt, `cargo test --test encoding_parity exact_typed_json_numbers_match_aot_default_run_and_interpreter`, failed with E0956 on the archived forced interpreter.
- The corpus has `tests/conformance/corpus/core/encoding/json/*.jet` (decode, parse, loads and others), but no typed-number fixture.

## Changes
1. Give `json<T>` a Jet body: `encoding.json.parse(text)` followed by the typed `Decode` lowering (JetSema/JetCodegen Decode derive), so every tier runs the same source. Delete the `core.data.json` intrinsic rows.
2. The number path in json.jet keeps the lexeme's integer and fraction information: integers go to exact `Int`, including beyond i64 where DataTree must carry them, and decimals become Float only when the target is Float.
   - A quoted number to an Int target is a typed Decode error, not a coercion.
   - Fractional to Int is an error.
   - Beyond a fixed-width target (U8, I32) is an overflow error.
   - NaN or Inf text is rejected.
3. Web emitter (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Web`): use the same compiled Jet path rather than a JS integer helper. Remove the JS helper once nothing reaches it.
4. JetEval needs no new route when the body is Jet. Otherwise add one in `Routes/Core.jet` delegating to the same body.

## Proof
- New `Examples/features/serde/json_typed_numbers.jet` covers exact, big-int, quoted, fractional, overflow, nonfinite and nested-struct targets, printing value or typed error. `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/json_typed_numbers Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes on AOT and default run.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev -- data_pipelines_and_parsing_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot` includes the example and passes.
- The web build of the same example gives byte-identical output (`cargo test --test web_browser -- json_typed_numbers`).

## Batch
batch-core-data: the data/encoding typed-decode path.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove CORE-F004 (`Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f004`) on the current binary. Exercise the existing field-metadata law end to end: grouped Codable/DenyUnknownFields markers, Flatten combinations, custom Decode precedence, required/default/optional fields and PublishedSchema retention. ## Current state
- The markers are implemented in the self-hosted compiler:
  - `Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/DeclarationMarkers.jet:18` routes `RenameAll`, `DenyUnknownFields`, `Tag`, `Untagged`, `Rename`, `Skip`, `Default` and `Flatten` to the serde list.
  - `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Registration/Checked.jet:141` maps DenyUnknownFields, and `:1901` sets `published_schema`.
- Registered rows in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet`:
  - E2408, Flatten needs a struct (`:13671`)
  - E2410, missing required field (`:13703`)
  - E2412, unknown field under DenyUnknownFields (`:13735`)
- Existing goldens cover PublishedSchema and migrations (`Examples/features/serde/decode_migration.jet:10`, `migrations/run.jet`, `migrations2/run.jet`), plus `serde_derive.jet`, `codable_default.jet` and `user_derive.jet`. No example exercises DenyUnknownFields, Flatten or missing/null/invalid-type decoding.
- Round-tripping retained unknown fields in their original order (criterion 3) has no known mechanism. It is probably unsupported.

## Changes
1. Add `Examples/features/serde/field_metadata.jet` and its `.out`. Use only the current spelling (`T?`, `-> T E!`, `??`). It should cover:
   - `#[Codable, DenyUnknownFields]` rejecting an extra key with the E2412 FieldError.
   - The lenient default dropping the same key.
   - `#Flatten` of a nested `#Codable` struct, including Flatten combined with DenyUnknownFields.
   - A hand-written `Decode` taking precedence over the derived codec.
   - A required field missing (E2410), an optional `T?` field absent versus explicit `null`, a declaration-default field, and a wrong-type value, each printing a distinct error.
2. Keep the existing E2408 fixture `tests/ui/serde_flatten_not_struct.jet` as the compile-time Flatten witness.
3. Criterion 3: if retained-unknown round-trip is unsupported, record it as an unsupported cell with its evidence, and ask Main to open a separate owner ballot. Do not build a second metadata model here.
4. Use #3155 for the checked declaration and shape projections. Computed fields and skipped fields must stay distinguishable.

cards.title: Choose duplicate-key admission for JSON input
cards.body:
Choose duplicate-key admission for JSON input.

Ratify the default and a typed public control for duplicate object names in JSON-input readers; do not conflate this with unknown fields.

Ratify the default and a typed public control for duplicate object names in JSON-input readers; do not conflate this with unknown fields.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f005. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Complete D-CORE-JSON-DUP1=A. Ordinary JSON `parse`, `decode<T>` and `reader` reject duplicate object names on every tier, with key and location. Explicitly named Allow siblings keep later-value resolution. Reader events keep every occurrence. Duplicate tracking is bounded by the existing limits.

**Current state**
- The Jet Core parser already rejects: Core/encoding/json.jet:438-443 (`duplicate object key` with path, line, column). The Core reader (:95, :473-486) materializes through the same Parser.
- The shipped host path does not: `json.parse` is a dispatcher row (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.jet:729 -> MathRandomTime.rs:1659 `jet_std_json_parse` -> JSONDataTree.rs:100-101 `parse_json(text, false)`). Typed decode is JSONDataTree.rs:107-108 `parse_json_typed(text, false)`. JSONCodec.rs:3 is `false`. Comptime is JSONInterp.rs:163/169/175 `false` and AppLite.rs:221 `false`. With false, crates/jet-foundation/src/EncodingJson.rs:366-369 keeps the later value. So Jet source and the executed tiers disagree (I9).
- No Allow control exists.
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f005.

**Changes**
1. Host mirror (needed so the shipped binary proves the fix): pass `true` at JSONDataTree.rs:101 and :108, JSONCodec.rs:3 (then fold `parse_json_strict` :6-8 into it), JSONInterp.rs:163/169/175 and AppLite.rs:221. Apply the same policy in the host reader `jet_enc_json_reader` (Top/EncodingStream.rs:534).
2. Core/encoding/json.jet: give `Parser` an `allow_duplicates` flag. Add named siblings `parse_allow_duplicates`, `decode_allow_duplicates<T>` and `reader_allow_duplicates` (operation-variant law in Docs/spec/stdlib-api-laws.md; the decision leaves the exact spelling open). Allowed whole-value parsing keeps the later value. The Allow reader emits every occurrence as events instead of materializing first.
3. Duplicate-key state is charged to `EncodingLimits.max_item_bytes`/depth. Typed decode reports `[FieldError]` with the path. parse/reader report `EncodingError` with path, line and column.
4. Register the siblings in Prelude/Core.jet (:94-95 plus dispatcher rows), run `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs`, update core-library.md.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/json_duplicate_keys Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> on `{"count":2,"count":3}`: parse, decode<CountRecord> and reader each report `/count` with line/column; the Allow siblings return 3 and the Allow reader shows both events. Identical on AOT, default `jet run` and the interpreter.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/json Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` and `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/json_typed ...` -> unchanged.

**Batch**
batch-core-encoding.

**Dependencies**
None. The decision is ratified.

2. Reject reports the key/location.
3. explicit Allow retains documented value resolution.
4. raw event occurrence semantics are explicit.
5. limits bound duplicate tracking.

cards.title: Add checked JSON Pointer selection to the existing data model
cards.body:
Add checked JSON Pointer selection to the existing data model.

Ballot a standard pointer selection operation over DataTree, preserving the existing field/at operations for their distinct literal-key/index jobs.

Ballot a standard pointer selection operation over DataTree, preserving the existing field/at operations for their distinct literal-key/index jobs.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f008. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Implement D-CORE-JSON-POINTER1=A: `DataTree.pointer(path: String) -> DataTree EncodingError!` with RFC 6901 selection. Empty pointer = root; `/` = the empty-name member; `~0`/`~1` escapes are checked; array segments are canonical nonnegative indices (no `-`); null is a value, not absence; errors name the failing segment. No ancestor is cloned; only the final result is owned. It is not mutation, query or a borrowed-view API.

**Current state**
- DataTree accessors are handle ops: JetSema Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Data.jet:84-88 (`field`, `at`, `int`, `text` contracts), TIR Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/TIR/TIR.jet:1099-1102 (`THandleOp.DataTreeField`...), codegen Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Data.jet:503-515 -> host `jet_datatree_field`/`jet_datatree_at` (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/DataTree.rs:218-235).
- Core/encoding/json.jet public API (:71-100) has no pointer. No application pointer parser exists in Core.
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f008.

**Changes** (Jet first)
1. Core/encoding/json.jet: add one Jet kernel, `pub fn pointer(tree: DataTree, path: String) -> DataTree EncodingError!`, plus a private segment parser `pointer_segments(path) -> [String] EncodingError!`. #3278/#3279/#3296 reuse the parser. Traversal matches `.Object`/`.Array` by reference and copies only the returned subtree. EncodingError carries the `path` prefix up to the failing segment and a reason (missing member, index out of range, non-canonical index, bad escape, not a container).
2. Method surface: add a `pointer` contract in Sema/Calls/Data.jet beside :85 with `THandleOp.DataTreePointer`. Codegen Data.jet lowers it to the Jet source function, not a new Rust twin. The JSON alias form follows the same row.
3. Register the export in Prelude/Core.jet :94-95, run `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs`, add the core-library.md row next to `field`/`at`.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/json_pointer Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> cases "", "/", "/a~1b", "/m~0n", "/arr/0", "/arr/01" (error), "/arr/-" (error), "/arr/9" (error), "/x" on a null member (null) vs "/absent" (located error). Identical on AOT, default `jet run` and the interpreter.
- `target/debug/jet inspect audit copies --json Examples/features/serde/json_pointer.jet` -> no DataTree copy inside the traversal loop; the only copy is the returned value.

**Batch**
batch-core-encoding.

**Dependencies**
None. Lands first in this batch because #3278 and #3279 reuse its segment parser.

cards.title: Export JSON Schema from canonical Codable metadata
cards.body:
Export JSON Schema from canonical Codable metadata.

Ballot general data-schema export independently of the already ratified HTTP route OpenAPI projection.

Ballot general data-schema export independently of the already ratified HTTP route OpenAPI projection.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f009. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-CORE-JSON-SCHEMA1=A (ratified): `json.schema<T>() -> DataTree EncodingError!` emits JSON Schema draft 2020-12 from the canonical Codable/Encode/Decode metadata. The codec keeps owning requiredness, nullability, renames, defaults, validation, enums and variants. Recursion uses bounded `$ref`s. Unsupported custom codecs report their type and path. There are no fabricated constraints, no second validator, and no new syntax or marker. HTTP OpenAPI and CLI schema keep their existing owners. Source: CORE-F009.

## Current state
- Nothing exports a schema: `Core/encoding/json.jet`, `Compiler/JetSema` and the Prelude have no `json.schema` symbol.
- The typed-decode intrinsics live in `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Data.jet:487-510` (`sema_data_core_decode_contract`; json `decode` at `:491-492`).
- Serde metadata is checked in `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Serde.jet` and `Registration/Checked.jet:140-141`. The markers are parsed at `Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/DeclarationMarkers.jet:18`.
- #3155 ("Derive shape and enum consumers from checked declarations", P2, ready) owns the shared checked shape projection. Its plan says not to make it an unconditional blocker.

## Changes
1. **JetSema.** Add `json.schema<T>()` as a type-argument intrinsic beside the decode contract in `Calls/Data.jet`, resolved against the checked declaration facts: fields, `T?`, declaration defaults, Rename/RenameAll, Skip, Flatten, Tag/Untagged, validate blocks and enum variants. A type whose codec is hand-written, or has no compiler-known wire shape, turns the call into a runtime `EncodingError` with type and path. It is not a compile error, because the ratified signature is fallible.
2. **JetCodegen.** Lower to one Core call that builds the `DataTree` from a compile-time schema table. There is no runtime reflection walk.
3. **Core.** Add `pub fn schema` in `Core/encoding/json.jet`, with the Core call row in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCallRows.jet`, and emit `"$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"`.
4. **Retained host.** Add the Rust bootstrap sema/lowering mirror so the shipped binary proves it, plus a JetEval route.
5. Reuse #3155's projection if it has landed first; otherwise build from the same checked facts and leave one shared function for #3155 to adopt.

cards.title: Map executor and buffer control without another runtime
cards.body:
Map executor and buffer control without another runtime.

Determine which Asio/Tokio expert controls are already expressible through Jet task/IO owners and which useful controls lack a public route.

Determine which Asio/Tokio expert controls are already expressible through Jet task/IO owners and which useful controls lack a public route.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f013. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Map Asio/Tokio expert controls (affinity and serialization, blocking offload, admission and backpressure, caller buffers, allocation policy, cancellation association) onto Jet's existing task and IO owners, without adding another runtime. Each missing control becomes its own owner gate, and costs are measured wherever they are claimed.

## Current state
- `Core/tasks/tasks.jet`: `after`/`interval` (:114-120) use host `core.tasks`. `cancel` (:175-178) closes only the receiver, since producers are detached (see #3095). `waitany` (:106) uses deterministic first-arm selection. `TaskState` channel, lock and notify (:27-90) are pure source values.
- The host is `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Scheduler.rs`: an M:N pool, `blocking_wait` state (:3704, :3822), and IO pollers (epoll/IOCP) at :2699-2862. `TaskGroup.rs` holds cancel, deadline and `#Shield`. The IO owner is `Core/io/io.jet`.
- Existing witnesses: `Examples/features/concurrency/{bounded_workers,bounded_spsc_atomic,job_queue,scheduler_spawn,deterministic_world,deadline_context,parallel_iter}.jet`.
- The finding is at `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f013`. The #3398 handoff says to reuse #3078 lifecycle operations.

## Changes (evidence only)
1. Record one cell per control with the Jet spelling or 'none':
   - strand or serial executor: a single-consumer channel
   - `spawn_blocking`: the scheduler `blocking_wait` reserve
   - bounded admission: channel capacity or `bounded_workers`
   - caller-provided read buffers: whether `io` reads into `&[U8]`
   - allocator or arena per task: `core.mem.Arena`
   - cancellation token association: task-group scope
2. Run the listed witnesses on AOT and `jet run`. Measure the cost of blocking offload and bounded admission with a throwaway bench under `~/.cache/jet-luna/executor-map/` (throughput and p99 latency at 1/8/64 tasks).
3. Post the table and open one gate card per real missing control. No new runtime.

## Proof
- The card log holds the cell table, bench numbers with exact commands, and per-tier transcripts.
- `for f in bounded_workers deadline_context; do Tools/agent/jet-env jet run Examples/features/concurrency/$f.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/concurrency/$f.out; done` gives empty diffs. job_queue.jet has no golden, so it is recorded from its run transcript only.

## Batch
batch-measure: evidence and cost measurement only.

## Dependencies
None. The cancellation-association cell depends on #3095's producer ownership fix; record the current behavior.
