cards.title: Choose the direct ArgsSpec completion artifact
cards.body:
Choose the direct ArgsSpec completion artifact.

Ballot whether the direct completion method emits an installable shell script through the same checked command metadata instead of the captured label-and-words string.

Ballot whether the direct completion method emits an installable shell script through the same checked command metadata instead of the captured label-and-words string.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f014. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Implement ratified D-CORE-ARGS-COMPLETION1=A. `ArgsSpec.completion(shell)` returns an installable Bash/Zsh/Fish/PowerShell script built from the same checked command facts as the existing non-executing embedded-schema completion (D-SHAPE-CLI-COMPLETE1). It replaces the placeholder word list. There is one renderer, no second parser or registry, and extraction never executes the target.

**Current state**
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Args.rs:527-546` `jet_args_completion` returns `"<shell> completion: --help --version ..."`, a placeholder.
- The method is routed from `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/ProcessHandles.jet:61`, `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/HandleMethods.jet:1180`, and the Rust mirror (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/routes.rs:2927`, `subset/handles.rs:355`, `crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/ArgsLite.rs:451`).
- The real script renderer is `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:2759` `completions_for_program(shell, command_name, &CLICommandSchema)`. It covers bash, zsh, fish, and powershell, with `shell_single_quote` escaping and a hostile-name test at `:3124`.
- `Args.rs` is shared by `include!`/`include_str!` into emitted programs (`Codegen/mod.rs:3270,4012`), the JIT (`crates/jet-jit/src/Args.rs:23`), and comptime.

**Changes**
1. Move the shell-script bodies out of `completions_for_program` into a dependency-free `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/CompletionScript.rs`. It takes the program name, root words, per-command `(name, words)` pairs, and input specs as plain slices, and owns the escaping.
2. `CLI.rs::completions_for_program` becomes a thin adapter from `CLICommandSchema` to that input and `include!`s the file.
3. `Args.rs` `jet_args_completion` projects `JetArgsSpec` entries (flags, options with short forms, nested subcommands, positionals) into the same input and calls the same renderer. The Prelude part list at `Codegen/mod.rs:3269-3273` and `:4011-4015` adds `CompletionScript.rs`.
4. An unknown shell returns the existing Env-effect error path, not a string.

**Proof**
- New golden `Examples/features/cli/args_completion.jet`, whose spec has a quoted name and nested subcommand flags, printing all four scripts: `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=cli/args_completion cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` shows identical output on AOT, default run, and interpreter.
- `cargo test -p jet-cli -- external_completion_rejects_hostile_program_names` still passes.
- New `cargo test --test cli_surface -- args_completion_scripts_load_in_shells`: `bash -n` and `zsh -n` accept the emitted scripts, and `fish --no-execute` does too when fish is installed.

**Batch**
`batch-host-runtime`: the Prelude CoreLib Rust with tier parity.

**Dependencies**
None. The decision is ratified.

cards.title: Close observable state and generated-property parity
cards.body:
Close observable state and generated-property parity.

Map MVVM observable property/recipient and source-generation jobs onto existing reactive/UI state and compiler metadata.

Map MVVM observable property/recipient and source-generation jobs onto existing reactive/UI state and compiler metadata.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f016. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Map MVVM observable-property and source-generation jobs onto Jet's existing reactive/UI state and compiler metadata. Prove unchanged-value notification, derived updates and owner disposal on the provider path, and account for generated-member diagnostics and AOT limits. Any missing state API gets its own ballot. No ObservableObject hierarchy.

## Current state
- `Core/reactive/reactive.jet:16-34` has the carriers `Signal`/`Computed`/`Derived {value, version}` and `Effect {last, active}`. The comment at :13-15 says the runtime provider replaces constructors with dependency-tracked cells. Source ops: `set_if_changed` (:61, `Int` only), `effect_run_if` (:74), `unsubscribe` (:50).
- Defect candidate: `set` (:56-58) and `computed_set` (:89-91) return the old signal unchanged once `version >= 2147483646`. After about 2^31 writes, new values would be silently dropped on the source path. `Int` is unbounded (D-INTBIG1), so the cap is unjustified.
- Web mapping: `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Web/JavaScriptOps.jet:53-55` (JetSignal new/get/set).
- Witnesses: `Examples/features/ui/reactive.jet`, `reactive_scope.jet`, `ui_tui_reactive.jet` and `Examples/features/web/ui_web_reactive.jet`.
- The finding is at `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f016`.

## Changes
1. Add `Examples/features/ui/reactive_observable.jet` with a golden. It covers: set to the same value (does an effect re-run?), a derived chain update order, disposal through `unsubscribe` and scope exit (no further runs), a generic `set_if_changed` on a `String` signal (expected to be a compile error today), and the version-cap behavior.
2. Fix the silent version-cap drop in `reactive.jet` `set`/`computed_set` (remove the cap; `Int` is exact), because it violates the no-lost-update invariant. Everything else is evidence only.
3. Record cells for generated members: are there accessor diagnostics for a `#Codable`-style generated property? Does AOT reject reflection-only paths? Open a ballot for generic `set_if_changed` if it is missing.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=ui/reactive Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run Examples/features/ui/reactive_observable.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/ui/reactive_observable.out` and the `--interpret` form both diff empty.

## Batch
batch-core-ui: Core/reactive witnesses and one in-owner fix, retested with the ui goldens.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: Prove stock availability without unused activation
cards.body:
Prove stock availability without unused activation.

After import closure, measure distribution, checking, linked sections, initialization and per-call allocation separately for selected Core batteries.

After import closure, measure distribution, checking, linked sections, initialization and per-call allocation separately for selected Core batteries.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f018. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Show that importing a stock Core battery costs nothing when it is unused (CORE-F018). After import closure, measure distribution, checking, linked sections, initialization and per-call allocation separately, using control/import/use arms.

## Current state
- Finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md:20735` (CORE-F018).
- No harness measures import arms. `Tools/perf/corelib_compare.py:204` reports `runtime_only_ns` only. `Tools/gauntlet/harness/performance-surface.mjs` measures paired spelling surfaces, not linked sections or startup.
- Core batteries live in `Core/<module>/*.jet`, for example `Core/text`, `Core/encoding`, `Core/http`, `Core/data`, `Core/regex`.

## Changes
1. Add `Tools/perf/core-activation.mjs`. For each selected battery (json, regex, http client, data frame, time), generate three programs: **control** (no import), **import** (import, no use) and **use** (one call). Keep compiler, source and toolchain frozen; record the candidate commit and binary sha (criterion 1).
2. For each arm and target (host AOT release, plus `jet run`), measure:
   - check time;
   - AOT binary size and linked sections (`size -A`, symbol count from `nm --defined-only`);
   - reachable-dependency closure from the build receipt;
   - startup to `run()` (hyperfine-style, 20 samples);
   - per-call allocations for the use arm (`JET_ALLOC_STATS=1` if present, otherwise `heaptrack`/`valgrind --tool=massif` counts).

   Report import-vs-control deltas (criterion 2).
3. Report unavoidable compile-time costs (parse and check of the imported module) separately from runtime and binary cost (criterion 3).
4. A zero-cost claim needs a measured zero delta in sections, startup and allocations. Dead-code elimination in source alone is not evidence (criterion 4).
5. Write the results to `Docs/audits/core-activation-<date>.md` and register the cells in `Tools/gauntlet/measurement-manifest.json`, so this stays inside the existing gate rather than becoming a second registry.

## Proof
`node Tools/perf/core-activation.mjs --jet target/release/jet --out ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/core-activation.json` exits 0 with a row per battery × arm × target × metric. The audit lists every nonzero import delta as a finding with a card. Pass = all cells measured or explicitly `unavailable`.

## Batch
batch-measure.

## Dependencies
None.

1. Use frozen compiler/source/toolchain and control/import/use arms.
2. measure target-specific reachable dependencies and startup.
3. report unavoidable compile costs separately.
4. do not claim zero cost from dead-code elimination alone.

cards.title: Preserve diagnostic causes and bounded failure behavior
cards.body:
Preserve diagnostic causes and bounded failure behavior.

Close error contracts for the selected data/IO/task operations, including source location, cause, limit and cancellation without panic/empty-value substitution.

Close error contracts for the selected data/IO/task operations, including source location, cause, limit and cancellation without panic/empty-value substitution.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f021. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Remove the silent empty-value substitutions from Core failure paths, and prove repairable, redacted and correctly ordered diagnostics across the failure cells.

## Current state
- Law: Core/archive/archive.jet:20-21 says decoders return a typed `ArchiveError` and an empty list is a valid value, never a sentinel. Docs/spec/stdlib-api-laws.md:77-78 and F2 (:220) ban sentinels, and F3 requires every failure to say what, why and how to fix it.
- Violations in archive.jet: `deflate(data) -> [U8] Never!` returns `[U8]{}` above `C_MAX_OUTPUT` (64 MiB, :34, :89-90); `compress` does the same (:178-179); `tar_add` returns `[U8]{}` or the unchanged archive on oversize data, an invalid name or an oversize name (:279-292); and the internal `zip_from_files` uses `[U8]{}` as a sentinel (:460-529).
- Violations in JSON and hex: json.jet `JSONWriter.to_string` (:121) and the renderers (:583, :589) use `String.from_bytes(out) ?? ""`, and so does `bytes_to_hex` (Core/encoding/encoding.jet:81).
- IOError values are not yet inspectable or renderable (#3582, ready). Criterion 4 reuses the READ-F14 ordering contract (#3179; D-SHAPE-RESOURCE1/2, D-FAIL-EXIT1).

## Changes
1. archive.jet: `deflate`, `compress` and `tar_add` return `[U8] ArchiveError!`. Size limits give `Unsupported` and an invalid name gives `Malformed`, and `zip_from_files` becomes fallible internally. Migrate every caller (Core/archive/gzip.jet, zstd.jet, Examples/, tests/conformance/corpus/core/archive). If the bare `ArchiveError` enum cannot meet F3 (what, why, fix), draft a ballot for payload-carrying cases. That ballot does not block removing the sentinels.
2. json.jet :121, :583, :589 and encoding.jet:81: build output that cannot fail (validated text pieces), or treat the unreachable case as an internal invariant failure. Never return "".
3. New Examples/features/errors/core_failure_paths.jet with Examples/features/expected/errors/core_failure_paths.out. Cells: malformed (`archive.inflate` on a bad block, `json.parse`); EOF and absence (`files.read` on a missing path, a truncated `jsonl` record); limits (`tar_add` with an invalid name, a zip over `C_MAX_ENTRIES`); IO (reading a directory as a file); cancel (a cancelled task reports Cancelled); unsupported target; a secret-bearing error printed redacted; and one failing Core call inside a function with `defer`, a guard and an exit handler, printing the ordered cleanup trace under the READ-F14 law.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=errors/core_failure_paths cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/errors/core_failure_paths.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/errors/core_failure_paths.out` prints nothing.
- A grep for `return \[U8\]\{\}` and `?? ""` in Core/archive/archive.jet and Core/encoding/json.jet finds no failure-path hits.

## Batch
batch-core-encoding: archive and JSON codec failure paths plus one errors golden.

## Dependencies
#3582, for the IO cell's inspectable IOError rendering. The archive and JSON fixes can land before it.

cards.plan:
## Goal
Measure how well a cold agent discovers Core workflows and repairs them, using the existing runner and inventory (CORE-F022). Record verdict fidelity, latency, actionability, context economy and repair determinism. No second registry or runner.

## Current state
- Finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md:20855` (CORE-F022).
- Runner: `Tools/agent-eval/run-cold-context.mjs:90-116`, with `--tasks`, `--output`, `--jet-bin`, `--mode capsule|control|both`, `--record-baseline` and `--check-baseline`.
- Fixed tasks: `Tools/agent-eval/tasks/tasks.json` (hello, cli, data-transform, http). Source-derived inventory: `Tools/agent-eval/dx/manifest.json`.
- No current task covers the imports, error and lifecycle concepts.

## Changes
1. Add one or two tasks to the existing `Tools/agent-eval/tasks/tasks.json` that force importing a Core module, handling a typed failure (`-> T E!` with `?`/`??`), and resource lifecycle (open, use, close through scope). Build their oracles from `dx/manifest.json` entries (criterion 2).
2. Run both modes (`capsule`, `control`). For each task, record verdict fidelity (the verdict matches the oracle), latency, actionability (the first diagnostic's fix leads to a passing edit), context bytes and repair determinism across two reruns (criterion 1).
3. Keep the E0999 correction as one labelled witness row, not a benchmark result (criterion 3).
4. Put everything in the runner's existing output schema; add no new registry or runner (criterion 4).

## Proof
`node Tools/agent-eval/test-cold-context.mjs` is green with the new tasks. Then `node Tools/agent-eval/run-cold-context.mjs --tasks Tools/agent-eval/tasks/tasks.json --mode both --output ~/.cache/jet-luna/agent-eval/core-f022.json --jet-bin target/debug/jet` exits 0. Its scoreboard has all five quantities for every task, including the imports/error/lifecycle task, and the E0999 witness row. Losing cells are kept.

## Batch

## Dependencies
None.

cards.plan:
**Goal.** Finish CORE-F023 (research: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f023`). Map the Glaze time-trace (Chrome `traceEvents`) and data-recorder jobs, plus baseline logging/profiling, to their existing owners:
- `core.log` spans/fields/redaction with the OTLP file bridge (runtime, application telemetry)
- `jet perf trace`/`export` (tooling, profiling)

Then demonstrate one finite exported-trace job with bounded buffers and preserved source identity. Any new Core export is a separate ballot.

**Current state.**
- `Core/log/log.jet:16-20` has typed fields, `redact` and spans, and says "This is not a tracing SDK; OTLP file export is the one optional bridge."
- The spans are `span`/`enter`/`close` (:75-79), with `otlp_file(path)` (:96), `sample_every` (:90) and `set_trace_id` (:105).
- Existing witnesses: `Examples/features/io/log_structured.jet` (golden, span+trace id) and `io/log_projection.jet` (no golden, `otlp_file`).
- Tooling: `jet perf export <trace> --chrome` emits `"traceEvents":[` (`tests/jet_perf_trace_parts/views.rs:103-113`). That covers the Glaze time-trace format for profiling, not for application telemetry.
- There is no data recorder or replay in Core.
- #2782 (building) fixes the default-evaluator `set_trace_id` arm (E0956).

**Changes.**
1. Add `Examples/features/io/log_trace_export.jet` and its `.out` (cases in add_criteria) (c2).
2. Record the formats on the card (c1):
   - OTLP-file JSON record shape as emitted: span/trace ids, attributes, redaction marker
   - the `jet.trace` schema, and the Chrome projection from `jet perf export`
3. c3 bounds: document and exercise the host sink buffer limit and the `sample_every` behaviour. Measure observer cost once with a throwaway 10k-event loop (with and without the sink) through `Tools/agent/jet-env`, and record wall time on the card. This is not a performance claim.
4. c4: check that exported records keep the user's span names and trace id, and that source identity is not replaced by the `core.log` implementation site. This is coordinated with #3176.
5. The recorded-value/replay recorder is absent. Record it as a missing capability to be proposed as its own ballot.

**Proof.** The command in add_criteria.

**Batch.** `batch-core-files`: a log witness plus a measurement note. No code change is expected.

**Dependencies.** None hard. If the interpreter tier still hits E0956 on `set_trace_id`, #2782 must land first for the interpreter cell.

cards.body:
Investigate explicit multi-file configuration inclusion.

Recover the selected JSON Include contract and compare safe explicit file-resolution composition with existing config/files/codec owners.

Recover the selected JSON Include contract and compare safe explicit file-resolution composition with existing config/files/codec owners.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f024. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Implement ratified D-CORE-CONFIG-LAYERS1=A: one explicit, rooted, bounded JSON configuration-layer loader in core.args that reuses decode/merge and rooted file access. Pure decoding stays IO-free.

**Current state**
- Core/args/args.jet:124 `merge(base, overlay)` overlays objects (arrays and scalars replace). :49/:54 `decode`/`decode_argv`. No include or layer loader exists anywhere in Core.
- Core/files/files.jet:132 `read_bytes`, :338 `canonicalize`, :824 `is_symlink`; `Path.is_within` exists (Examples/features/io/path_within.jet). There is no native rooted open (openat/O_NOFOLLOW).
- Core/encoding/json.jet:71 `parse` is strict and IO-free.
- Ratified contract (A): `load_json_layers<T>(paths: [Path], root: Path, include_key: String, limits: ConfigLimits = ConfigLimits.safe()) -> T` on the ordinary fallible rail with structured [FieldError]/EncodingError/IOError causes. `ConfigLimits` wraps EncodingLimits.safe() with max_files=64, max_include_depth=32, max_total_source_bytes=67108864. No core.config tree, no env interpolation, no global cache.
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f024.

**Changes**

cards.body:
Investigate bounded runtime template rendering.

Recover the selected Stencil/Mustache body/export contract and determine the useful runtime-template job beyond ordinary interpolation.

Recover the selected Stencil/Mustache body/export contract and determine the useful runtime-template job beyond ordinary interpolation.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f025. cards.plan:
**Goal**
Ship the ratified D-CORE-TEMPLATE1=A bounded runtime template renderer in Core/text: compile once, render through the encoded field view, and keep the renderer opaque and immutable.

**Current state**
- No template renderer exists in Core: no `Template` or mustache symbol under Core/.
- Existing owners to reuse: Core/text/html.jet (`escape`, `attr_escape`, `text_escape`), Core/encoding/encoding.jet (`DataTree`, `EncodingLimits`), the `__jet_Encode`/DataTree scalar and container traversal, and core.text token handling.
- Ratified contract (#3396 handoff): delete per-application Mustache/Stencil parsers and arbitrary getter dispatch. Keep HTML vs text escaping, raw triple braces, the safety-context limitation, missing-field spans, and explicit limits. No eval, include, filesystem, or global cache.

**Changes**
1. Add a Core/text/template.jet module (declared in text.jet beside `module html`) with an opaque immutable `Template`, `compile(source: String, limits: TemplateLimits) -> Template TemplateError!` and `render<T: Encode>(t: Template, value: T) -> String TemplateError!`. Render walks the Encode field view directly, with no JSON stringify/parse round trip, so renames, omissions and exact scalar formatting are preserved.
2. Grammar: `{{name}}` (escaped by the template's context), `{{{name}}}` raw, `{{#section}}`/`{{^inverted}}`/`{{/section}}` over Bool, Optional and List containers, and dotted paths. No partials, lambdas or includes. Recursion is bounded by `max_depth`.
3. `TemplateError` carries kind (`MissingField`, `MalformedTag`, `Limit`) and a byte span plus line and column. Limits are depth, output bytes and render steps.
4. Add the module to the CoreModuleExportNames row in Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCallRows.jet and to the Prelude Core.jet module table. Jet-owned: no host route.
5. Add Examples/features/text/template_render.jet plus its golden. Add a paired perf cell (reused-template render vs `"{…}"` interpolation, and a dormant-import build) in the canonical perf manifest.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=text/template_render Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: passes.
- `for m in --release '' --interpret; do Tools/agent/jet-env jet run $m Examples/features/text/template_render.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/text/template_render.out; done`: empty.
- The perf pair is recorded through Tools/perf with a same-run receipt. No speed claim without it.

**Batch**
batch-core-text: a new Core/text module plus its registry export row, proved by one golden.

**Dependencies**
None. Criterion 4 is satisfied by D-CORE-TEMPLATE1=A; partials or any other grammar beyond it need a new ballot.

cards.plan:
## Goal
State the ABI, version, type, ownership, error and unload contracts of Jet's only plugin boundary, the WASM Component loader. Account the Glaze Interfaces/REPE plugin and shared-library capabilities and baseline FFI against it. Any native-dylib or ABI addition is routed to its own ballot.

## Current state
- `Core/plugin/plugin.jet:12-17`: `core.plugin.load` takes a literal artifact, and sema attaches a frozen Component interface. The provider keeps authority and error checks.
- Host: `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Prelude/Plugin.rs` (`jet_plugin_load_declared` :1110, `jet_plugin_load` :1232, `jet_plugin_close` :1242, `jet_plugin_call` :1258, wire strings `O:`/`E:`). The carrier is `JetPlugin { handle: u64 }` in `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/HandlesRaylib.rs:245`.
- Witnesses: `Examples/features/packages/sandbox_mathkit`, `Examples/features/foundations/capabilities` (guest), UI fixtures `tests/ui/plugin_e1257_version_mismatch` and `plugin_e1260_unsupported_shape`.
- Native FFI is a separate audited boundary (`tests/cffi.rs`, jet-ffi-descriptor-v1). There is no native shared-library plugin API. The native-dylib ask is #3598.
- The finding is at `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f026`.

## Changes (evidence only)
1. Run the plugin witnesses and UI fixtures, and record per-contract cells:
   - ABI: the component model and WIT-typed values.
   - Version: E1257.
   - Type shape: E1260.
   - Ownership: the Copy handle today, `Close` after #3072.
   - Error: typed wire errors, no panic.
   - Unload: `jet_plugin_close` semantics and the nested-close refusal.
2. Confirm that no raw-pointer safety is inferred anywhere on the path.
3. Post a table comparing Glaze/REPE capabilities (typed interface discovery, RPC, shared-library load) as supported, unsupported or unknown. Route native dylib to #3598, and open a ballot only for a genuine gap.

cards.title: Retain RPC interoperability without a second codec
cards.body:
Retain RPC interoperability without a second codec.

Map Glaze JSON-RPC/REPE registry, buffers and conversion jobs to the application transport owner with exact foundational data/task dependencies.

Map Glaze JSON-RPC/REPE registry, buffers and conversion jobs to the application transport owner with exact foundational data/task dependencies.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f027. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Keep JSON-RPC/REPE-style interoperability possible without a second codec or scheduler. Recommended option A: protocol adapters are packages over core.http/core.net.ws plus the typed codec, and this card becomes the package witness that proves it. The plan is written for A.

## Current state
- No JSON-RPC/REPE adapter exists (grep over Core/, Compiler/, Examples/ and the Prelude finds none). The transport owners are `Core/http/server.jet` and `Core/net/ws.jet`; the codec is `Core/encoding/json.jet` (DataTree parse/to_string). Typed codec sharing is #3236 (ready, not a prerequisite).
- Owner question: A = package over Core transport plus codec; B = a Core battery `core.rpc` with framing/ID/error/notification/cancel law.
- Finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f027`.

## Changes (option A)
1. Add `Examples/features/net/jsonrpc/` (run.jet, package.jet, `rpc.jet` module): a JSON-RPC 2.0 adapter over a loopback `core.http.server` POST endpoint and a `core.net.ws` session.
2. Record exact behavior (criterion 1):
   - framing: one object or a batch array;
   - IDs: string, number or null, echoed exactly;
   - errors: -32700/-32600/-32601/-32602/-32603 with data;
   - notifications: no id, no response;
   - cancellation: the `$/cancelRequest` convention cancels the handler task through existing task cancellation, or is printed as unsupported.
3. Criterion 2: a maximum body/message size enforced before parse, and auth through the existing header/session check before dispatch.
4. Criterion 3: unknown members and unknown result bodies pass through as DataTree unchanged.
5. The adapter uses only the Core codec and tasks: no reflection model and no scheduler (criterion 4).

## Proof
`JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=net/jsonrpc Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes on AOT and `jet run`, printing each framing/ID/error/notification/cancel/limit cell.

## Batch
batch-core-net: example package over http/ws, proven by a net golden.

## Dependencies
Owner choice A/B. B would instead add `Core/rpc` and needs its own API ballot.

cards.body:
Close shared data-model losslessness boundaries.

Determine exactly which peer map keys, tags, binary values, numeric widths and typed variants the canonical DataTree/codec path preserves or rejects.

Determine exactly which peer map keys, tags, binary values, numeric widths and typed variants the canonical DataTree/codec path preserves or rejects.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f029. cards.plan:
## Goal
Publish one executable losslessness table for the shared `DataTree` across every Core format. It must separate typed-codec fidelity from dynamic-tree fidelity, and any algebra expansion goes to a ballot rather than into a parallel tree.

## Current state
- The public Jet `DataTree` has seven variants: Null, Bool, Int, Float, Text, Array and Object (Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet:4127). The host carrier additionally holds Number, TypedText and Bytes (crates/jet-foundation/src/DataTree.rs:9-22).
- Docs/spec/encoding-decisions.md:390-392 forbids a `DataTree.Bytes` variant. :876-885 maps Codable `[U8]` to CBOR major type 2 on typed paths but rejects bstr in `parse` (D-ENC-DYN1), along with tags, non-text keys and bignums. :158-160 lets exact-token Number travel only as a Prelude carrier.
- Core/encoding/cbor.jet:29-37 and :166 reject bstr, :198 rejects non-text keys and :199 rejects duplicate keys. The TOML root is `[String:DataTree]` (toml.jet:34), and TOML datetimes stay text (toml.jet:5).

## Changes
1. New witness Examples/features/serde/datatree_losslessness.jet with its .out. Per format (json, cbor, toml, yaml, xml, csv), it feeds exact wire fixtures and prints either the parsed tree or the exact `EncodingError` kind and reason. The fixtures cover a non-string key (CBOR int key, YAML `? 2. Add a `DataTree losslessness` table to Docs/spec/encoding-decisions.md beside :390, with rows format x category and cells preserved, typed-only or Unsupported plus the reason. It points at the golden and replaces nothing ratified.
3. Fix only a codec that silently coerces instead of preserving or rejecting, inside that codec's file.
4. Any cell that needs a new public variant (for example Bytes) or a public profile expansion becomes a Tower ballot. Do not add a second value tree.

cards.body:
Close common cryptographic primitive coverage.

Map selected standard-library hashes/MAC/secure randomness and current algorithm additions to existing crypto owners and approved dependencies.

Map selected standard-library hashes/MAC/secure randomness and current algorithm additions to existing crypto owners and approved dependencies.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f030. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Map the selected standard-library hash/MAC/KDF/secure-randomness jobs to the existing core.crypto owners. For each algorithm record version, key/nonce, error, target availability and secret lifetime. List the real gaps, and send any new algorithm or dependency to its own scoped owner vote.

**Current state**
- Core/crypto/crypto.jet `pub fn`s: `digest`/`new`/`update`, sha1, sha224, sha256, sha384, sha512, sha3_224..sha3_512, blake3, hmac_sha256, hkdf_sha256, pbkdf2_hmac, constant_time_equal(_bytes), seal/open, file_seal/file_open, sign/verify (Ed25519), x25519(_public/_shared), wrap/unwrap, password_hash(_with_salt)/password_verify. Types: CryptoError, Digest256/512, Hasher, Secret, SigningKey/VerifyKey, Sealed, PasswordHash (:46-150). Core/crypto/expert.jet (#Unsafe raw): aes256gcm, xchacha20poly1305, argon2id, hkdf_sha256_raw, ed25519_verify_strict (:699).
- Legacy-named exports `generatekey`, `privateencrypt`, `privatedecrypt`, `publicencrypt`, `publicdecrypt` exist in crypto.jet and need classification (alias vs real algorithm).
- The CSPRNG/simulation split already exists: Core/crypto/random.jet (fail-closed `bytes`, `token_*`, unbiased `int_range`, :45-61) vs Core/math/random.jet (seeded `rng`, but also `bytes`, `randbytes`, `getrandbits`). The simulation byte producers are the confusable cell.
- Overlaps #3667 (Core-in-Jet crypto one meaning) and #3597 (Ed25519 seed/verify).
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f030.

**Changes**
1. Witness Examples/features/crypto/primitive_matrix.jet: known-answer vectors (FIPS 180-4/202, RFC 4231 HMAC, RFC 5869 HKDF, RFC 8018 PBKDF2, BLAKE3 reference) for every exported primitive, plus typed CryptoError on wrong key/nonce length.
2. Add a table in Docs/spec/reference/core-library.md (crypto section): algorithm, spec version, key/nonce sizes, error, target availability (native/web/no-OS), secret zeroization/lifetime, owner module. Add a line stating that core.math.random bytes are never cryptographic.
3. Gap list on the card, one owner vote each, no implementation here: HMAC/HKDF over SHA-512, ECDSA P-256/RSA verification (JOSE interop), scrypt, and the classification of the legacy-named exports.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=crypto/primitive_matrix Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> all vectors match on AOT, default `jet run` and the interpreter.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=crypto/random_api_split Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> the existing CSPRNG/simulation split golden still passes.

**Batch**
batch-core-crypto.

**Dependencies**
None. Coordinate with #3667, which may move primitive bodies; this card only adds vectors and docs.

cards.title: Close UI async-command lifecycle behavior
cards.body:
Close UI async-command lifecycle behavior.

Compare MVVM command enablement, overlapping execution, cancellation, observable status and failure against existing UI actions and tasks.

Compare MVVM command enablement, overlapping execution, cancellation, observable status and failure against existing UI actions and tasks.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f033. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Measure the MVVM async-command lifecycle against Jet's existing UI action and task paths: enablement, duplicate or overlapping activation, cancellation, observable status, domain failure and owner teardown. Any missing command abstraction gets its own ballot. Errors must never be lost in a detached task.

## Current state
- `Core/ui/ui.jet` (168 lines) has nodes, backends, previews, `key_event`, `reactive_render` (:140) and a11y roles. It has no command or action type.
- `Core/tasks/tasks.jet`: `TaskFailure { message, raised }` (:35). `cancel(rx)` (:175-178) only closes the receiver, and `recv` returns the `-1` sentinel on close (:128-131). The host task control plane is `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/TaskGroup.rs` (Cancelled/DeadlineBlown/Panicked, `#Shield`).
- Reactive state is in `Core/reactive/reactive.jet` (Signal/Effect).
- Witnesses: `Examples/features/ui/reactive_scope.jet`, `ui_tui_reactive.jet`, `Examples/features/concurrency/{task_group,race_cancel,cancel_cleanup,detached_task}.jet`.
- #3403 (omitted-viewport choice) is open but does not gate this card. The finding is at `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f033`.

## Changes
1. Add `Examples/features/ui/async_command.jet` with a golden. It models a 'Save' command as a Signal-held status (Idle/Running/Failed/Done) plus a task-group-spawned job, and covers:
   - `can_execute=false` blocks activation
   - a second click while Running is ignored or queued, per explicit code
   - cancellation through the task group reaches the job
   - a domain `Err` surfaces as Failed with its message, not as a panic
   - scope teardown cancels and joins the job before exit
   Run it on the null backend so it is deterministic.
2. Record cells for what needs hand-written glue (status signal, duplicate guard) versus what the existing task, error and teardown contract gives for free. If the glue is general, draft one ballot for a command helper over the existing task group. Do not copy RelayCommand.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=ui/async_command Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run Examples/features/ui/async_command.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/ui/async_command.out` and the `--interpret` form both diff empty.

## Batch
batch-core-ui: a Core ui/tasks witness, retested with the ui goldens.

## Dependencies
None. #3239 (task outcome and TaskFailure owner) informs the Failed-versus-panic cell.

2. report domain errors without detached-task loss.
3. UI commands use the existing task error, cancellation and owner-teardown contract at the application UI boundary.
4. gate any missing command abstraction.

cards.plan:
## Goal
Measure typed messaging and subscription lifecycle on `core.event`: weak versus strong registration, token channels, request/reply, duplicate registration and reply, missing-response errors, unsubscribe and disposal, and concurrent send. No global message bus or service locator is added by default.

## Current state
- `Core/event/event.jet:20-46` forwards `scope`, `new<T>`, `with_policy`, `hook<T,R>`, `decision_hook<T,E>`, `policy_sync` and `async_result<T,E>` to provider-owned state (D-EVENT1/2, comment :14-18). There is no typed request/reply or messenger.
- `Examples/features/ui/events.jet:31-58` already shows `on`/`once`/`emit`/`summary`/`unsubscribe`, `scope.active_count`, async `emit_async().join()`, `close`, decision hooks and `scope.cancel()`. Tests: `tests/event_hooks.rs` and `tests/event_observations.rs`.
- The card log's Rust `ReactiveEventWatch.rs:540-804` is reference only. The finding is at `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f034`.

## Changes
1. Add `Examples/features/ui/event_lifecycle.jet` with a golden. It covers:
   - registering the same handler twice (count reported by `summary`)
   - a handler whose owning scope is cancelled while the event lives, to show retained-recipient lifetime
   - `unsubscribe` then `emit`
   - `emit_async` from two tasks with the delivery order and report
   - request/reply modelled as `decision_hook` returning a value, with the no-handler outcome (fallback) and a two-responder outcome (policy-selected)
2. Record cells covering weak registration (no weak form exists: recipient lifetime is scope-owned), token channels (typed `Event<T>` instances act as tokens), missing-response error and duplicate reply. Draft a ballot only for a real missing job such as a typed request/reply with a missing-reply error. No global bus.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=ui/event Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes, covering events.jet and event_lifecycle.jet.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run Examples/features/ui/event_lifecycle.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/ui/event_lifecycle.out` and the `--interpret` form both diff empty.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test event_hooks` passes.

## Batch
batch-core-ui: a Core/event witness, retested with the ui goldens.

## Dependencies
None.

Compare observable grouped-collection jobs (group, key and item mutation, read-only views, comparer order, remove-empty-group, observer cleanup) with Jet's existing collection and reactive composition, and ballot a new type only if nothing equivalent exists. Keep iterator collection destinations separate from UI notification semantics.

## Current state
- `Core/reactive/reactive.jet:16-34` has immutable `Signal`/`Computed`/`Derived`/`Effect` carriers with version counters. `Core/reactive/loadable.jet` holds loadable state. There is no observable collection.
- `Core/collections/collections.jet:23-49` has no grouping type. Grouping comes from iterator `groupby` (`Core/math/combinatorics.jet`, the `core.math.combinatorics` export list) and map building. `core.web.table` (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCallRows.jet:1410-1414`, 2008) owns keyed row, sort and filter state for web UI.
- The #3398 handoff says to use #3325's operation facts and to keep encounter order, key identity and collection state rather than inferring them from traversal names.
- The finding is at `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f036`.

## Changes (evidence only)
1. Write a throwaway probe under `~/.cache/jet-luna/grouped-obs/` that builds `Signal<[String: [Item]]>` grouped by key. It covers:
   - moving an item to a new key, so its group changes
   - removing the last item, then deciding whether the empty group is removed
   - a missing-group lookup
   - a duplicate item
   - comparer order through `sort_by` versus insertion order
   - effect unsubscribe cleanup
   Run it on AOT, `jet run` and `jet run --interpret`.
2. Compare with `core.web.table` keyed rows for the UI case.
3. Post a supported/unsupported/unknown table. Recommend a ballot only if a signal over a map, or web.table, cannot express a job without O(n) rebuild or lost notifications.

## Proof
- The card log holds the probe source, per-tier outputs and the table.
- `for f in reactive reactive_scope; do Tools/agent/jet-env jet run Examples/features/ui/$f.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/ui/$f.out; done` gives empty diffs.

## Batch
batch-measure: evidence only.

## Dependencies
None. #3325 supplies operation-fact vocabulary but does not gate this card.

cards.title: Investigate closed-send and zero-capacity channel outcomes
cards.body:
Investigate closed-send and zero-capacity channel outcomes.

Trace the public sender and bounded-channel constructor before classifying the captured discarded boolean and capacity clamp as user-visible behavior.

Trace the public sender and bounded-channel constructor before classifying the captured discarded boolean and capacity clamp as user-visible behavior.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f037. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Run every closed-send, no-receiver, full, cancel and capacity-0/1 channel outcome on the current tree. Classify each as rendezvous or minimum-one buffering, and as delivered or silently dropped, against the ratified concurrency law. Any change to a public result or default goes to a ballot.

**Current state**
- crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Scheduler.rs:3017-3023 `JetSchedulerChannel::bounded` uses `Some(capacity.max(1))`. Capacity 0 silently becomes a 1-slot buffer, so there is no rendezvous.
- crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/MathTaskMem.rs:1052-1054 `JetSender::send` does `let _ = self.tx.send(value)`. A send after close or with no receiver is dropped with no signal.
- Core/tasks/tasks.jet:40-43 `channel(capacity)` clamps negative capacity to 0 (0 means unbounded in `put`). :46-48 `put` returns the unchanged state when closed or full, with no signal. :126-130 `recv` maps a closed channel to the sentinel -1.
- Builtin surface: `channel<T>(capacity: n)` returns (tx, rx), as in Examples/features/concurrency/channel_builtin_1560.jet.
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f037. #3343 (nonblocking drain, ready) depends on this finding.

**Changes**
1. Add witness Examples/features/concurrency/channel_outcomes.jet with golden output. Cover capacity 0 and 1 (does a send block until a receiver arrives?), send on full (block vs drop), send after `tx.close()`, send after the receiver is dropped, a send blocked when its task is cancelled, and `recv` after close for the builtin and for core.tasks `recv`/`put`/`channel(-1)`.
2. Add a table to this card: observed vs ratified law (Docs/spec concurrency sections, D-CONC-CHAN1), noting each silent drop or sentinel.
3. File one ballot for the changed public results: capacity 0 as rendezvous or a rejected argument; `send` returning a closed/fallible result instead of discarding it; core.tasks `recv` sentinel -1 vs an optional. No runtime change before ratification.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=concurrency/channel_outcomes Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> identical recorded outcomes on AOT, default `jet run` and the interpreter. Any tier divergence is itself a finding and is filed as a bug.

**Batch**
batch-host-runtime: the behavior lives in the host scheduler and the proof is a three-tier golden.

**Dependencies**
None. #3343 and #3180 consume this finding.

2. distinguish rendezvous from minimum-one buffering and delivery from dropped values.
3. resolve against exact ratified concurrency law.
4. any changed public result/default needs a ballot.

cards.title: Prove archive and compression safety profiles
cards.body:
Prove archive and compression safety profiles.

Close existing archive/compression capabilities after import build closure, including hostile archive resource and path cases.

Close existing archive/compression capabilities after import build closure, including hostile archive resource and path cases.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f039. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove the archive and compression safety profile on hostile inputs, and fix the losing cell: an encoder that silently returns an empty or unchanged buffer. Each codec, version and target is distinguished, and there is no claim about compressed-size-only memory. Finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f039`.

## Current state
- `core.archive` is Jet source (`Core/archive/archive.jet`) with `C_MAX_OUTPUT` 64 MiB and `C_MAX_ENTRIES` 4096 (`:34-36`). Inflate, zip and tar readers enforce them with typed `ArchiveError.Unsupported/Malformed/Checksum` (`:142,255-256,329-334,594-596`), and tar_get validates padding and end markers.
- Losing cells, where failure is silent:
  - `deflate` returns `[U8]{}` above the cap (`:89-90`), and so does `compress` (`:178-179`);
  - `tar_add` returns the archive unchanged on a bad name or oversize input (`:279-291`);
  - `zip_from_files` returns `[U8]{}` on invalid input (`:460-473,529`);
  - `Core/archive/gzip.jet:16-17` and `zstd.jet:26-27` `compress` return `[U8]{}` above 64 MiB.
- The API is in-memory, so filesystem traversal, symlink and overwrite-permission cells are not applicable until #3596's streaming tar reader carries mode, type and link headers. Record them as N/A-pending-#3596.
- Goldens: `Examples/features/io/archive.jet`, `compress_gzip.jet` and `compress_zstd.jet` all have `.out` files.

## Changes
1. Make every silent-empty encoder fallible, returning `-> [U8] ArchiveError!` (or `GzipFileError`/`ZstdFileError`) with `Unsupported` on oversize input. `tar_add` returns `Malformed` for an invalid name and `Unsupported` for oversize. Migrate the callers (Examples, Jetpack, Core) and the export rows in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCallRows.jet:1898-1900`. This changes existing signatures; the #3263 criteria require typed errors, and D-CORE-COMPRESS1 already defines the error enums.
2. Write `Examples/features/io/archive_hostile.jet`. Each case prints its typed error:
   - truncated deflate, gzip and zstd;
   - bad gzip CRC and bad zstd checksum;
   - an inflate bomb crossing `C_MAX_OUTPUT` (built from repeated stored blocks, not a 64 MiB literal);
   - a zip with 4,097 entries;
   - zip and tar names with `../` and absolute paths (rejected by `archive_name_valid`/`zip_name_valid`);
   - tar with a bad checksum and a missing end marker.
3. Per codec, record whether the memory bound is on output size (decompressed) and never on input size.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=io/archive Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` covers archive, archive_hostile, compress_gzip and compress_zstd on AOT and default run. Every hostile case prints a typed error and none prints an empty buffer.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test archive` passes.

## Batch
batch-core-encoding: Core/archive codecs. This family sits with encoding; no separate archive key exists.

## Dependencies
None. Filesystem cells follow #3596.

cards.title: Close exact numeric and simulation-RNG breadth
cards.body:
Close exact numeric and simulation-RNG breadth.

Map fixed/big/decimal/rational/complex, checked/wrapping/saturating operations, statistics and repeatable simulation randomness within the declared baseline scope.

Map fixed/big/decimal/rational/complex, checked/wrapping/saturating operations, statistics and repeatable simulation randomness within the declared baseline scope.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f040. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Produce an executed map of Jet's exact numeric and simulation-RNG surface. It covers the Int, Float, Decimal, Fraction and fixed-width types; checked, wrapping and saturating operations; stats; and repeatable RNG. Record the rounding, overflow, NaN and conversion policy per cell. Missing types or operations become individual owner gates. No claim may rest on a name alone.

## Current state
- `Int` is exact and arbitrary precision (D-INTBIG1=A, `Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:1172`). So `Core/math/math.jet:205-209` `checked_add/sub/mul` always return `Val`, and `saturating_add/sub/mul` (:252-256) are plain `+ - *`. Whether those names are meaningful for `Int` or only for fixed widths (`I8`…`U64`) is exactly an open cell.
- Fraction and Decimal are compiler-known numeric types (`Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Core.jet:394`; D-NUMTYPE1=A ratified Complex and Fraction). Complex and Measurement use precise builtins in `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Expressions.jet:561-562`.
- Stats are in `Core/math/stats.jet` (878 lines). Repeatable RNG is in `Core/math/random.jet:45-105` (seeded `Rng`, split).
- Witnesses: `Examples/features/math/{fraction,fraction_exact,exact_rational_math,int_from_u64_extreme,random_audit,random_extremes}.jet` with goldens.
- The finding is at `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f040`. Related cards: #1464 (core.math gaps) and #2866 (Decimal perf).

## Changes (evidence only)
1. Run the existing math witnesses on AOT, `jet run` and `jet run --interpret`, and record the outputs.
2. Write throwaway probes under `~/.cache/jet-luna/numeric-map/` for these cells:
   - fixed-width overflow (trap or wrap per type)
   - Float NaN/inf ordering and `cmp`
   - Decimal rounding mode and scale
   - Fraction reduction and zero denominator
   - Int to Float, Float to Int and Decimal to Float conversion loss
   - `saturating_*`/`checked_*` on fixed widths versus Int
   - seed replay across tiers and after `split`
3. Keep hardware SIMD vectors separate from GPU kernels (`Core/compute`).
4. Post the cell table (supported/unsupported/unknown, with the exact input and output) on the card. Open one gate card per missing type or operation. Flag the Int `saturating_*` names as a candidate ballot (retire them or restrict them to fixed widths).

## Proof
- The card log holds the cell table and the per-tier transcripts.

cards.plan:
## Goal
Inventory Core's build, package and debug provenance: export discovery, dependencies and features, build graph, and diagnostics. Compare it with current Jet commands and generated Core metadata, keeping exact executable and source identities. Do not create a second registry, and do not infer a clean build from archived receipts.

## Current state

- The compiler side is `Compiler/JetEval/Source/CompilerServices.jet`. Generated Core metadata lives in `crates/jet-foundation/src/CoreModuleExports.rs` and `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCallRows.jet` (`CoreModuleExportNames`).

3. Post a supported/unsupported/unknown table for each finding row. Link existing package, flash and build-query cards rather than duplicating them. Open a gate only for a real missing capability.

cards.title: Choose stock BSON interoperability
cards.body:
Choose stock BSON interoperability.

Ballot a BSON1.1 adapter under the existing encoding/data model for ordinary document interchange, rather than a parallel object runtime.

Ballot a BSON1.1 adapter under the existing encoding/data model for ordinary document interchange, rather than a parallel object runtime.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f043. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Implement ratified D-CORE-BSON1=A (stock `core.encoding.bson`), D-CORE-BSON-ADOPT1=A (maintenance policy, no vendor code) and D-CORE-BSON-PROFILE1=A (full BSON 1.1 wire/API profile). The codec sits on the shared typed codec, reader/writer, limits and errors. Native values are module-local records, not new DataTree variants. Serialized JavaScript is never executed.

**Current state**
- Core/encoding/ has no bson.jet. The binary codec precedent is Core/encoding/cbor.jet (reader row at crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.jet:755). Format rows live at Core.jet:243-248. The DataTree variants are closed (Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:1291-1293; D-ENCBIN1).
- Ratified profile: `decode<T: Decode>(bytes: [U8]) -> T [FieldError]!`, `encode<T: Encode>(value: T) -> [U8] EncodingError!`, `parse(bytes) -> DataTree EncodingError!`, reader/writer on the FileReader/FileWriter lifecycle with an EncodingLimits.safe default. int32/int64 map to exact Int with checked bounds and double to Float. Native records: Binary{subtype: U8, bytes}, ObjectId{bytes (12)}, Timestamp{seconds: U32, increment: U32}, Regex{pattern, options}, JavaScript{source}, JavaScriptScope<T>{source, scope}, Decimal128{bytes (16)}. DateTime maps to Instant only when exact. MinKey/MaxKey/Undefined/DBPointer return Unsupported. Duplicate names are rejected before overwrite, and lengths, terminators, UTF-8 and array ordinal keys are checked before allocation.
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f043.

**Changes**
1. New Core/encoding/bson.jet: the byte reader/writer, the document/element grammar, the native records with `#Codable` customization, typed errors carrying the byte offset and path, and limits charged for skipped subtrees too.
2. Register it: `format_row BSON core.encoding.bson BSON` at Core.jet:243-248, module and source_module rows, then `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs`. Add a core-library.md section naming ADOPT1 maintenance ownership.
3. Add no dependency, no MongoDB client and no DataTree variant.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/bson Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> COUNT-BSON-1.1 hex `1000000010636f756e74000200000000` decodes to count=2 and re-encodes to the same bytes. `16000000075f696400000102030405060708090a0b00` gives ObjectId bytes 00..0b. Wrong total length, truncation, trailing bytes, a missing cstring NUL, bad UTF-8, a non-ordinal array key, a duplicate name, depth/size limits, MinKey -> Unsupported, and JavaScript returned as inert text. Identical on AOT, default `jet run` and the interpreter.
- Before the golden is blessed, each fixture's bytes are cross-checked by hand against the BSON 1.1 grammar and recorded on the card.

**Batch**
batch-core-encoding.

**Dependencies**
None. All three decisions are ratified.

cards.title: Investigate SQLite JSONB ownership and interchange
cards.body:
Investigate SQLite JSONB ownership and interchange.

Determine whether existing SQLite operations close the selected JSONB read/write/set/conversion job or a standalone format adapter is useful.

Determine whether existing SQLite operations close the selected JSONB read/write/set/conversion job or a standalone format adapter is useful.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f045. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Close D-CORE-JSONB1=A: SQLite JSONB stays an opaque value at the database boundary. Stock typed JSON plus SQLite's own `jsonb()`/`json()` handle the job, with no Jet JSONB codec, no EncodingFormat row and no DataTree variant. The proof is a versioned boundary witness.

**Current state**
- The witness is already in the working tree, untracked: Examples/features/io/db_jsonb_boundary.jet (header cites D-CORE-JSONB1=A). It prints `sqlite_version()`, stores `jsonb(json.to_string(record))`, prints `typeof`/`hex(body)`/`json(body)`, decodes with `json.decode<Reading>`, checks exact big integer 9007199254740993, and converts the external COUNT-JSONB blob `X'8c57636f756e741332'` through SQLite.
- There is no Examples/features/expected/io/db_jsonb_boundary.out yet.
- The engine is bundled SQLite via rusqlite 0.31 / libsqlite3-sys (crates/jet-jit/Cargo.toml:39-40). JSONB needs SQLite >= 3.45.0, and the printed version pins the identity.
- Criterion 6 (option B byte cross-read) is moot under A. Criterion 8 is met by making no speed claim.

**Changes**
1. Extend the witness so criterion 1 covers every selected element category: null, true/false, float, a big integer beyond i64 (as text), nested array/object, and text needing escapes. Print hex per category and the round-trip result.
2. Keep the opaque-format warning and the not-PostgreSQL note in the header, and add the same note to the core.db section of Docs/spec/reference/core-library.md.
3. Create the golden once and review it by hand: `JET_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=io/db_jsonb_boundary Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=io/db_jsonb_boundary Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> passes with the reviewed .out (sqlite_version line, hex per category, `round trip identical: true`, `big exact: true`, `external blob: {"count":2}`) on every tier the harness runs.

**Batch**
batch-core-data (core.db boundary; no codec).

**Dependencies**
None.
cards.checkSteps:
1. Use versioned SQLite/Glaze byte fixtures for all selected element categories and exact numbers.
2. compare direct DB operations with external buffers.
3. do not call an internal storage format a stable general interchange standard.
4. ballot any added codec/placement after this evidence.
5. If A wins, preserve stock typed JSON and test the existing SQLite conversion boundary for this exact blob; add no standalone JSONB surface.
6. If B wins, cross-read/write minimal/nonminimal headers, all text/numeric forms and reserved/truncated/overlong inputs.
7. Keep SQLite version/source identity and opaque-format warning visible; do not claim PostgreSQL interchange.
8. Measure whether avoiding conversion actually benefits a matched workload before any speed claim.

cards.title: Investigate BEVE interoperability and bounded costs
cards.body:
Investigate BEVE interoperability and bounded costs.

Assess the selected BEVE sizing/header-peek/typed-array/partial-operation jobs against existing binary encoding and a concrete C++ interchange workload.

Assess the selected BEVE sizing/header-peek/typed-array/partial-operation jobs against existing binary encoding and a concrete C++ interchange workload.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f046. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Ship `core.encoding.beve` as D-CORE-BEVE1=A ratified: the exact BEVE Version2 wire profile with checked typed projection, bounded decode and explicit `Unsupported` for categories the shared tree cannot hold.

## Current state
- No BEVE code exists. Core/encoding/ holds base32, base64, binary, cbor, csv, encoding, hex, ini, json, jsonl, toml, xml and yaml; the module list is Core/encoding/encoding.jet:32-52.
- Shared carriers to reuse: `DataTree` (public variants Null/Bool/Int/Float/Text/Array/Object, Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet:4127; no public Bytes case, Docs/spec/encoding-decisions.md:390-392), plus `EncodingError`, `EncodingErrorKind` and `EncodingLimits`, used the way Core/encoding/cbor.jet:1-26 uses them.
- D-CORE-BEVE1=A: wire is little-endian with low-3-bit base tags, compressed counts (2-bit size selector, value shifted by 2), headerless typed keys and elements, UTF-8 strings, zero reserved bits and Version2 extension IDs. Ordinary encode emits Version2 only. Extension1 is reserved for legacy Version1 tags and is never emitted. Version1 reads go only through an explicitly identified typed operation with the required enum schema, never a silent fallback.
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f046 and the derived-binary-fixtures capture (#capture-f560efbdd688). Those bytes are analyst derivations from wire rules, not encoder output.

## Changes
1. New Core/encoding/beve.jet with `parse(bytes: [U8]) -> DataTree EncodingError!`, typed `decode<T>` and `encode<T>`, `reader`/`writer`, and header inspection that peeks tag and count without materializing. Everything goes through the shared limits and error rails, with module-local handles only.
2. The decoder rejects nonzero reserved bits, unknown tags, compressed-count overflow, counts larger than the remaining bytes, invalid UTF-8, depth/item/total overruns and trailing bytes. Each error carries a byte offset.
3. Typed arrays keep their declared width on typed paths. `DataTree` projection is exact (Int or Float) or `Unsupported` (byte arrays, extensions, complex values). Nothing is approximated.
4. Version1 is reachable only through the ratified explicit typed operation. If the ratified text does not fix its exact public name, stop that slice and ballot the name.
5. Register the module: add `module beve` to encoding.jet, run `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --write` (this regenerates crates/jet-foundation/src/CoreModuleExports.rs, RingLayer.rs and Syntax/core_calls.rs), and add the export row in Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCallRows.jet (beside core.encoding.ini at :1934) and the dependency row in Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Rings/RingLayer.jet:51-55.
6. New witness Examples/features/serde/encoding_beve.jet with Examples/features/expected/serde/encoding_beve.out. It covers the signed-int32 count fixture; Version2 typed-array, string and object boundaries; reserved bits and tags; compressed-size boundaries; padding; length overflow; malformed and trailing input; typed versus `Unsupported` projection; and the encoded size next to `cbor.to_bytes` on the same value.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/encoding_beve cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/serde/encoding_beve.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/serde/encoding_beve.out` prints nothing.
- `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --check` exits 0.
- Criterion 2: `Tools/agent/jet-env jet perf run Examples/features/serde/encoding_beve.jet` records time and allocations for the matched BEVE and CBOR fixtures. Sizes are already pinned in the golden.
- Criterion 4 is satisfied by the ratified D-CORE-BEVE1=A. No dependency is added.

## Batch
batch-core-encoding: one new Core/encoding module plus regenerated registry views, proven by a serde golden.

## Dependencies
None open. D-CORE-BEVE1 is ratified A.

cards.title: Close independent ETF JSON-view and typed-codec contracts
cards.body:
Investigate EETF applicability and dependency boundary.

Retain the selected optional EETF reader/writer/converter and Erlang dependency as a bounded interoperability investigation.

Retain the selected optional EETF reader/writer/converter and Erlang dependency as a bounded interoperability investigation.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f047. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Ship `core.encoding.eetf` with its two independently ratified operations: the one-way checked JSON view (D-CORE-EETF1=A) and the typed ETF codec (D-CORE-ETF-CODEC1=A). Both cover standalone ETF version131 as documented for OTP 29.0.6 and need no Erlang runtime.

## Current state
- No ETF code exists in Core/encoding/ (the module list is encoding.jet:32-52). Criterion 4 is met because both ballots are ratified A.
- D-CORE-EETF1=A defines `to_json(bytes: [U8], limits: EncodingLimits{EncodingLimits.safe()}) -> String EncodingError!`, which fully validates one term and rejects trailing bytes. Its rules: integers and bignums stay exact, and finite floats use the current JSON writer. Atoms `true`/`false` become booleans; other atoms become text. Proper lists, NIL and tuples become arrays. STRING_EXT is the same byte-list value as LIST_EXT, so both project to an integer array. Binaries become Base64 text, and non-byte-aligned bitstrings are `Unsupported`. Map keys may be atoms, UTF-8 binaries or proper Unicode-scalar lists converted to strings; any other key, or a collision after conversion, is rejected. Key text decoding is strict. Process, port and reference identities are rejected.
- D-CORE-ETF-CODEC1=A defines `decode<T: Decode>(bytes, layout: Layout{.Map}, strings: StringEncoding{.Utf8Binary}, byte_arrays: ByteEncoding{.Binary}, limits)` on the FieldError rail and `encode<T: Encode>` returning owned `[U8] EncodingError!`. Reader, writer and caller-buffer operations reuse the same adapter. Layout is Map or Proplist, and record keys are UTF-8 atoms taken from the known field names.
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f047 and #finding-core-f089 (the COUNT-ETF-131-ATOM fixture and the native-header capture).

## Changes
1. New Core/encoding/eetf.jet with one bounded term reader: version byte 131; SMALL_INTEGER, INTEGER, SMALL/LARGE_BIG, NEW_FLOAT (tag 70), the atom tags, STRING, LIST (proper and improper), NIL, SMALL/LARGE_TUPLE, MAP, BINARY and BIT_BINARY; and COMPRESSED (tag 80), whose declared size is checked against the limits before inflating with the existing core.archive inflate (Core/archive/archive.jet). Distribution headers, fragments and LOCAL_EXT are `Unsupported`.
2. `to_json` projects that reader under the EETF1 rules. Typed `decode`/`encode` use the same reader and writer, with the `Layout`, `StringEncoding` and `ByteEncoding` controls. A caller buffer that is too small fails without partial success.
3. Limits apply equally to skipped values, compressed expansion, every arity and allocation, and both owned and caller buffers. There is no parallel Term tree and no guessed variant discriminant.
4. Register the module as for the other codecs: `module eetf` in encoding.jet, `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --write`, plus rows in Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCallRows.jet and Rings/RingLayer.jet.
5. New Examples/features/serde/encoding_eetf.jet with its .out, covering criteria 5-12: the COUNT-ETF-131-ATOM JSON result, map versus proplist, atom/string/byte-list/binary, tuple loss, embedded NUL and UTF-8, exact bignums, fixed-buffer shortage, malformed and trailing data, duplicate normalized keys, improper lists, opaque identities, compressed-bomb bounds, and the byte-70 float.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/encoding_eetf cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/serde/encoding_eetf.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/serde/encoding_eetf.out` prints nothing.
- `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --check` exits 0.
- No Erlang runtime is needed: the golden runs on a host without erl. Criterion 13 is recorded from the two ratified A outcomes.

## Batch
batch-core-encoding: one Core/encoding module and its golden.

## Dependencies
None open. It uses the existing core.archive inflate.

cards.title: Close YAML version, trailing input and resource behavior
cards.body:
Close YAML version, trailing input and resource behavior.

Compare the selected YAML1.2 scalar/collection/document/flow/block profiles and current Glaze fixes against the actual Core implementation.

Compare the selected YAML1.2 scalar/collection/document/flow/block profiles and current Glaze fixes against the actual Core implementation.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f051. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Make Core YAML fail closed for every construct it does not support, report real error locations, bound nesting, and measure (and then fix) render linearity.

## Current state
- Core/encoding/yaml.jet:17-21 declares the profile: JSON-compatible YAML 1.2 plus block maps and lists, `|`/`>` scalars and `#` comments, with a claim that unknown syntax fails closed. JSON-looking input goes to json.parse (:26-31).
- The fail-closed claim does not hold. `parse_scalar` (:240) is `Never!`, so anchors (`&a`), aliases (`*a`), tags (`!!int`, `!x`), flow collections and document markers (`---`, `...`) are never rejected. They become Text or map rows.
- Every syntax error reports offset 0, line 1, column 1 (:47, :54, :151, :154, :156, :157, :195, :198), so the location is lost.
- There is no depth limit. `parse_block` recurses through `join_lines` re-splitting (:176, :218), which re-scans nested text at each level.
- Rendering and scalar building concatenate in loops (`out = "{out}..."` at :107-114, :276, :282, :341-346, :423-424, :431), which is quadratic in output size.
- Research: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f051.

## Changes
1. `parse_scalar` becomes fallible. It rejects a leading `&`, `*`, `!`, `{` or `[` outside the JSON fast path, plus `%` directives, `---` after content and `...`, each as an `EncodingError` of kind Unsupported with a reason naming the feature. A single leading `---` is accepted.
2. Carry each row's line number and byte offset through `parse_block`, `parse_map` and `parse_list`, so that every error reports its true line, column and offset.
3. Enforce `EncodingLimits.safe().max_depth` for nesting, and parse child blocks by index range instead of `join_lines` re-splitting.
4. Render into one `[U8]` buffer (the json.jet `write_*` pattern) instead of string concatenation, in the render, quote and spaces helpers.
5. New Examples/features/serde/yaml_profile.jet with its .out. It covers a 1 MB single-line scalar, trailing content after the root, a second document, an anchor, an alias and a tag (each Unsupported), a duplicate key with its real line, nesting 257 deep, the number forms (`0x1F`, `1e3`, `.inf`, `-0`), and a round trip.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/yaml_profile cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/serde/yaml_profile.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/serde/yaml_profile.out` prints nothing.
- The existing `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/yaml.jet cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` still passes.
- Criterion 3: `Tools/agent/jet-env jet perf run` on a scratch program that renders 10k and 100k-entry maps shows a time ratio of about 10x (linear), not 100x. Record the before and after numbers on the card.
- Criterion 4: no profile or dependency is added.

## Batch
batch-core-encoding: Core/encoding/yaml.jet plus its golden.

## Dependencies
None.

4. gate any added profile/dependency.

cards.title: Prove JSONL and multi-value stream boundaries
cards.body:
Prove JSONL and multi-value stream boundaries.

Close NDJSON/JSONL and multi-root reading/writing through current streaming owners, including early exit and partial records.

Close NDJSON/JSONL and multi-root reading/writing through current streaming owners, including early exit and partial records.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f052. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove the JSONL record boundaries: one complete value per non-empty record, per-record locations, arbitrary multi-root JSON rejected, bounded incremental reading, and no claim of streaming where the whole text is materialized.

## Current state
- Core/encoding/jsonl.jet:1-6 says blank lines are skipped and each non-empty line goes through `json.parse`.
- `parse(text)` (:11-18) builds every row. The Jet `reader(text)` (:54) splits the whole text into `rows: [String]` up front, and `JSONLReader.next` (:31-39) parses one row at a time.
- Errors come from `json.parse(line)`, so line and offset are row-local (line 1). The record's stream line and offset are lost.
- The bounded route that ships is the host `jet_enc_jsonl_reader(input: FileReader, limits)` (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/EncodingStream.rs:1618; dispatcher crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.jet:751), used by Examples/features/serde/encoding_jsonl_stream.jet:28, which has a golden.
- Law: Docs/spec/encoding-decisions.md:116-147 (reader over `^files.FileReader` with `EncodingLimits`) and :171-172 (`next` returns `DataTree?`; each non-empty record contains one complete value).

## Changes
1. jsonl.jet: `parse` and `next` rewrite a record error to carry the record's stream line, the byte offset (record start plus inner offset) and the path `[N]`. The header states that `parse` and `reader(text)` are whole-text operations and that bounded streaming is the `reader(^FileReader, limits)` route.
2. Host reader (the retained route until #3690 ports it): verify, and fix where needed, that a record over `max_item_bytes` is a Limit error; that a final record without a newline is accepted when complete and Truncated when not; that two roots on one line (`{} {}`) are a Syntax error; that CRLF is handled; and that locations are per record.
3. Extend encoding_jsonl_stream.jet (and its .out) with: blank lines, CRLF, a partial final record, a multi-root line, a record over `EncodingLimits{max_item_bytes: 32}`, an early `break` after the first record (the reader is dropped and closed), and printed error locations. The same text through `jsonl.parse` shows the same outcomes and locations.
4. Record the incremental-buffer cell as supported on the host reader route and whole-text on the Jet `reader(text)` route. The Jet cutover is #3690's work.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/encoding_jsonl_stream cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/serde/encoding_jsonl_stream.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/serde/encoding_jsonl_stream.out` prints nothing.

## Batch
batch-core-encoding: jsonl.jet plus the retained host reader, proven by one serde golden.

## Dependencies
None. #3690 later removes the host reader, and this golden then guards the Jet port.
