cards.title: Close binary text encodings and fixed-buffer contracts
cards.body:
Close binary text encodings and fixed-buffer contracts.

Map base64/hex/binary conversion and fixed-buffer read/write/sizing jobs to existing Core encoding and memory controls.

Map base64/hex/binary conversion and fixed-buffer read/write/sizing jobs to existing Core encoding and memory controls.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f053. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove the malformed and noncanonical behavior of the base encodings. Then put the missing fixed-buffer controls (exact required size, caller-owned output, borrowed view) through individual owner ballots instead of inventing them.

## Current state
- Base64 (Core/encoding/base64.jet) is canonical by design (:3-5). It rejects `=` outside the tail (:152), more than two pad characters (:150), wrong padding for the final quantum (:162-163), any pad in the URL alphabet (:149, :161), bytes outside the alphabet (:153) and nonzero unused bits (from :165). `decode_padded` is just `decode` (:212).
- Base32 (base32.jet), hex (hex.jet, plus root `hex_to_bytes` at encoding.jet:85-99, which rejects odd length and bad digits) and binary.jet (`BinaryError` Range/Format/Values at :22-26) cover the rest.
- No `encode_into`, `decode_into`, `encoded_len`, `decoded_len` or required-size API exists anywhere under Core/ (confirmed by grep). Every encoder returns a newly owned `String` or `[U8]`.
- Existing witnesses are Examples/features/serde/encoding_base.jet and encoding_base_expert/, with goldens.

## Changes
1. New Examples/features/serde/encoding_base_hostile.jet with its .out. It covers, for base64, base64url, base32, base32hex and hex: missing, extra and interior padding; nonzero trailing bits (`Zh==` against `Zg==`); mixed alphabets; whitespace; odd hex length; a non-ASCII byte; empty input; and, for binary.jet, pack and unpack overflow and truncation (`unpack_u32le` on 3 bytes, `pack_u8(256)`, and a `sign_extend` width outside its range). Each case prints the exact error reason or the value. The encoded length is printed next to the documented formula (4*ceil(n/3), 8*ceil(n/5), 2n) to pin the required size.
2. Fix only any case found to repair input silently instead of rejecting it.
3. Draft the Tower ballots for the missing controls, one decision each with same-program alternatives: (a) required-size queries `encoded_len`/`decoded_len`; (b) caller-buffer `encode_into(data, out: &[U8])` that reports shortage without a partial write; (c) a borrowed byte view versus owning conversion. Show the beginner and expert paths. Implementation waits for ratification and lands on this card's follow-up criteria.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/encoding_base_hostile cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/serde/encoding_base_hostile.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/serde/encoding_base_hostile.out` prints nothing.
- The existing `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/encoding_base cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` still passes.
- Criterion 4: `node Tools/tower/tower.mjs decision list --card 3275` shows the three drafted ballots.

## Batch
batch-core-encoding: a witness over Core/encoding alphabets. Any fix stays in those files.

## Dependencies
None to start. Criteria 2 and 3 (caller ownership, view versus owning) resolve through the ballots this card drafts.

cards.title: Investigate object identity, cycles and typed graph coding
cards.body:
Investigate object identity, cycles and typed graph coding.

Account Jackson identity/back-reference/polymorphic metadata and Serde/Glaze graph limits against the canonical data/typed-codec model.

Account Jackson identity/back-reference/polymorphic metadata and Serde/Glaze graph limits against the canonical data/typed-codec model.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f054. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Record how Jet's canonical data and typed-codec model handles object identity, cycles, back-references and polymorphic metadata, against Jackson (`@JsonIdentityInfo`, `@JsonBackReference`, `@JsonTypeInfo`) and Serde/Glaze graph limits. The deliverable is a fixture-backed receipt. Any graph profile or API addition needs its own ballot, not a parallel serializer. Finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f054`.

## Current state
- The DataTree value tree (`Core/encoding/encoding.jet`, host `crates/jet-foundation/src/DataTree.rs`) has no identity, reference or type-tag node. Typed Decode reconstructs values structurally, so implicit object-graph reconstruction and polymorphic type instantiation from input are structurally absent.
- CBOR rejects all tags, including shared-reference tags 28/29, as `Unsupported` (`Core/encoding/cbor.jet:29-37`).

## Changes (investigation, fixtures only)
1. Write `Examples/features/serde/graph_identity.jet`:
   - an explicit-ID graph (`struct Node{id: Int, parent: Int?}` in a list) round-trips through JSON with identity preserved by the IDs;
   - two references to the same value encode as two copies (alias not preserved; stated in output);
   - a JSON payload with a type-discriminator field decodes only into the enum variant the target type names, never into an arbitrary type chosen by the input, so unsafe code instantiation is rejected;
   - CBOR tag 28/29 input returns `Unsupported`.
2. Record the supported, unsupported and unknown cells on the card, with the alias/cycle profile stated explicitly as “explicit IDs only”.
3. If the owner wants an identity or cycle profile, draft a ballot. No code beyond the fixture on this card.

## Proof
`JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/graph_identity Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes on AOT and default run and shows each cell.

## Batch
batch-core-encoding: codec investigation with a fixture.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: Investigate standards-query compatibility before adoption
cards.body:
Investigate standards-query compatibility before adoption.

Assess the actual captured JMESPath subset and a concrete runtime-selector workload against existing typed collection/query operations.

Assess the actual captured JMESPath subset and a concrete runtime-selector workload against existing typed collection/query operations.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f055. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Implement D-CORE-JMESPATH1=A: a named, bounded, standard JMESPath adapter at `core.data.jmespath`, with `compile(expr, limits) -> Expression JmesPathError!` (opaque, reusable) and `search(expr, tree, limits) -> DataTree JmesPathError!`. It passes the full official conformance corpus (all 26 built-ins) and has no IO. Nothing narrower is ever labelled full JMESPath.

**Current state**
- No JMESPath or query-string evaluator exists in Core (Core/data holds data.jet, loader, stream, arrow, plot, sketch). DataTree is the only dynamic value (Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:1291-1293). Typed List/Iter/Query operators (group_by, count_by: Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:239) are the static-predicate path and stay unchanged.
- Ratified defaults: expression bytes 65536, nesting 128, visited/output nodes 1000000, retained/output bytes 16777216, work units 10000000, charging traversals, comparisons, sorts, and string/number work. Duplicate-name objects are rejected. No implicit conversions. Unspecified object order is not promised.
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f055.

**Changes**
1. New Core/data/jmespath.jet: lexer and Pratt parser to an opaque `Expression` AST, and an evaluator over DataTree (projections with null omission, filters, pipes, multiselect list/hash, slices with zero-step error, expression references, `&` sort_by/max_by/min_by, all 26 functions). Typed `JmesPathError{kind: Syntax|InvalidType|InvalidValue|InvalidArity|UnknownFunction|Limit, span, data_path}`. `JmesPathLimits` with the defaults above.
2. Register the module in Prelude/Core.jet, run `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs`, add a core-library.md section.
3. Vendor the pinned jmespath.test compliance JSON under tests/fixtures/jmespath/ with its license and version.

**Proof**
- New `tests/corelib_parts/jmespath.rs` included by tests/corelib_encoding_surface.rs: `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test corelib_encoding_surface -- jmespath_conformance_corpus` runs every fixture case through a Jet driver on AOT, default `jet run` and the interpreter -> all pass, with the per-suite count printed.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=tooling/jmespath_limits Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> pathological nested/sort/filter expressions stop with Limit errors, a compiled Expression is reused across searches, and a duplicate-name object is rejected.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=tooling/typed_query Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> unchanged (SQL/row queries and iterator methods untouched).

**Batch**
batch-core-data: the ratified home is core.data.

**Dependencies**
None. Uses the #3234 duplicate policy for input trees but does not wait for it (it rejects duplicates itself).

cards.title: Add JSON Patch over canonical data with atomic failure
cards.body:
Add JSON Patch over canonical data with atomic failure.

Ballot the six standard JSON Patch operations as one checked data transformation, not arbitrary mutation callbacks or another record model.

Ballot the six standard JSON Patch operations as one checked data transformation, not arbitrary mutation callbacks or another record model.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f056. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Implement D-CORE-JSON-PATCH1=A: `json.patch(doc: DataTree, ops: DataTree) -> DataTree EncodingError!` applying a validated RFC 6902 operation array (add/remove/replace/move/copy/test). It includes root paths, array insertion and `-`, required `value`/`from`, move-into-descendant rejection and precise op-index/path errors. The input is unchanged on every error. It is bounded, with an explicit-limits sibling.

**Current state**
- No patch applier exists: Core/encoding/json.jet public API :71-100 has parse/decode/to_string/canonical/reader/events/writer only. DataTree access is only `field`/`at` (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/DataTree.rs:218-235). `equal_unordered` (:218 trait) supplies JSON equality for `test`.
- Exact numbers: typed parse keeps big numbers as `DataTree::Number` text (crates/jet-foundation/src/EncodingJson.rs:23-33 tests).
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f056.

**Changes**
1. Core/encoding/json.jet: add `pub fn patch(doc, ops)` and `pub fn patch_with_limits(doc, ops, limits: EncodingLimits)`. Validate the whole op array first (shape, op name, required fields, pointer syntax via #3237's `pointer_segments`), then apply to a working copy and return it only on success, so the source is never mutated. Errors carry `/ops/{i}` and the target path. `test` uses JSON equality (numbers compared exactly, objects unordered). Bound op count, depth, produced bytes and copies with EncodingLimits (safe_limits :60). No create-intermediate or nonatomic mode, and no diff (that is #3296).
2. Register in Prelude/Core.jet :94-95, run `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs`, add a core-library.md row.
3. Typed re-entry is shown in the example via `json.decode<T>` of `json.to_string(result)`, reusing Decode validation.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/json_patch Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> RFC 6902 appendix A cases: escaped paths, array insert and `-`, remove, move-descendant error, copy, test failure leaving the original unchanged, big-number exactness, a limit error, and a typed re-entry failure as `[FieldError]`. Identical on AOT, default `jet run` and the interpreter.

**Batch**
batch-core-encoding.

**Dependencies**
Lands in the same batch after #3237 (shared segment parser). It is not a Tower blocker because both are ready and land together. #3296 depends on this card.

cards.title: Add JSON Merge Patch with explicit null deletion
cards.body:
Add JSON Merge Patch with explicit null deletion.

Ballot JSON Merge Patch as a distinct standard wire transformation rather than calling PublishedSchema merge an equivalent.

Ballot JSON Merge Patch as a distinct standard wire transformation rather than calling PublishedSchema merge an equivalent.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f057. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Implement D-CORE-JSON-MERGE1=A: `json.merge_patch(target: DataTree, patch: DataTree) -> DataTree EncodingError!` with RFC 7386 semantics. Object members recurse; null members delete; arrays and non-object patches replace, including a null root. Absent differs from null. The original is unchanged on failure. It is bounded by existing limits and is not routed through JSON Patch.

**Current state**
- No merge patch exists in Core/encoding. The nearest is Core/args/args.jet:122-146 `merge(base, overlay)` (CLI/config overlay: arrays and scalars replace, no null deletion). That is a different job and stays unchanged.
- Core/encoding/json.jet:71-100 public API has no merge. `DataTree.Object` keeps insertion order (encoding.jet:27-28), so the result keeps target order with new members appended.
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f057.

**Changes**
1. Core/encoding/json.jet: `pub fn merge_patch(target, patch)` and `merge_patch_with_limits(target, patch, limits)`. There is one recursive copy-on-write traversal: only rebuilt objects on the patched path are new and untouched subtrees are moved or shared, never deep-cloned. Depth, size and allocations are charged to EncodingLimits. Share traversal helpers with #3278, but the semantics stay merge-specific.
2. Register in Prelude/Core.jet :94-95, run `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs`, add a core-library.md row that states the difference from `args.merge`.
3. Typed re-entry in the example: `json.decode<T>` on the merged result reports `[FieldError]`.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/json_merge_patch Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> all RFC 7386 appendix A cases (null delete, array replace, non-object root replace, null root, absent vs null), a depth-limit error with the original unchanged, and a typed re-entry error. Identical on AOT, default `jet run` and the interpreter.

**Batch**
batch-core-encoding.

**Dependencies**
None. #3297 depends on this card.

cards.plan:
**Goal**
Map the requested collection families (sequence, map, set, queue, heap, ordered, immutable, concurrent) to the Jet types that actually ship, record each family's ordering, equality/hash, mutation/invalidation, snapshot/borrow and allocation contract, and send each useful missing family to its own scope ballot.

**Current state** (corrects the triage: generic families already ship as compiler builtins)
- Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:4-18 `SemaCollectionKind`: List, FixedList, Iter, ViewIter, View, Map, Set, Rank, Bits, Tally, Cache, Queue, PriorityQueue. Mutating methods per kind are at :285-293.
- Docs/spec/reference/core-library.md:276-287 documents `[T]`, ordered `[K:V]`, hash `Set<T>`, ordered-set `Rank<T>`, `Queue<T>`, `PriorityQueue<T>`, bounded `Cache<K,V>`, `Tally<T>`, `Bits`, `Bytes`. :289-293 pins stable sort/partition and last-equal `min_by`/`max_by`. Map keys are limited by E0502 (:264).
- Core/collections/collections.jet:23-49 adds String-only Counter/Deque/OrderedMap/Layer/Chain plus Int heap helpers (`nsmallest` :577, `nlargest` :606). Core/collections/set.jet:5 `StringSet`. These are Python-compatible duplicates of Tally/Queue/[K:V]/Set.
- There is no immutable/persistent family and no concurrent (shared or lock-free) map/queue family. Channels are the only concurrent queue.
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f060.

**Changes**
1. Add witness Examples/features/collections/collection_contracts.jet. Per family, show iteration order, equality (Set vs Rank), a copy vs move boundary, Cache eviction and Queue capacity, and View reads after allowed disjoint writes.
2. Add a contract table beside core-library.md:276 with order, equality/hash, invalidation, borrow and allocation per family. Keep type families separate from iterator producers (`lazy`, Iter, ViewIter) and collect destinations (`to_list`, `to_set`, `collect`).
3. Record the Core/collections duplication as a finding. Retiring it needs its own card.
4. For immutable/persistent collections, concurrent map/queue and a sorted map, file one short Tower scope ballot each. Do not build a generic collection tree.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/collection_contracts Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> passes on every tier the harness runs.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/list_loop_mutate.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` -> the existing mutation-during-traversal snapshot is unchanged.

None. Related: #3231, #3372, #3325 (the iterator-contract-before-adapters chain).

cards.plan:
## Goal
Pin the XML and markup data-parser profile Core actually ships with a fixture per cell, and route the ratified-but-unimplemented D-ENCXML1 cells (namespaces, C14N) to one owning card.

## Current state
- Core/encoding/xml.jet:43-53 defines the profile: well-formed XML 1.0 without DTDs. DTDs, parameter entities, XInclude and namespace rewriting are rejected. Only the five predefined entities and numeric references decode, and there is no external IO. A DOCTYPE fails with `DTDs are forbidden in Core XML` (:295-296). Depth, node and attribute limits (`XMLLimits` :71-80, safe values :30-41) are enforced in `parse_with` (:139-150) and `parse_element` (:345-350). The `XMLReason` cases are Syntax, Truncated, ForbiddenDtd and UnknownEntity (:54-59).
- Gap against ratified law: Docs/spec/encoding-decisions.md:252-257 and :317-335 (D-ENCXML1=A) specify namespace resolution (`XMLName{raw, prefix, local, namespace_uri}`), a tagged `$xml` tree (:390-414), and `xml.canonical(doc, XMLCanonical)` with the modes `Inclusive11` and `Exclusive10`. The Jet source instead has `XMLCanonicalMode {Inclusive, Exclusive}` (:82-85) and `canonical(text)`, which just re-renders (`to_string(parse_xml(text))`, :159).
- Examples/features/serde/encoding_canonical.jet calls the ratified spelling (`XMLCanonical{mode: .Inclusive11}`, `XMLParseOptions.safe()`, `parse_with(text, options)`), so it has no golden.
- Core/text/html.jet:14-16 provides escaping and bounded entity decode only; tag stripping is a span operation, not a parser. There is no HTML parser, and the GUI renderer is out of scope.

## Changes
1. New Examples/features/serde/xml_profile.jet with its .out. It covers: a DOCTYPE document (Syntax, `DTDs are forbidden`); an `&unknown;` entity; the five predefined and decimal/hex numeric references; a prefixed element `<a:b xmlns:a="u"/>` (record the actual name and namespace output); nesting 257 deep (the bounded Limit error); an attribute count over the limit; an unclosed tag (Truncated); a `<!ENTITY` bomb (rejected with no expansion); XInclude (no IO); and `html.escape`/`unescape` beside `html.strip_tags` to show the span-only behavior.
2. Write the supported/unsupported/unknown table into the XML section of encoding-decisions.md next to :252. Mark namespaces, C14N and the tagged tree as ratified-but-unimplemented rather than unsupported.
3. Create one Tower card (or attach to an existing one) to implement D-ENCXML1 namespaces, C14N and the tagged tree in Core/encoding/xml.jet, and to repair encoding_canonical.jet with its golden. That work does not happen here.
4. Criterion 4: an HTML parse profile has no ratified decision, so draft a ballot.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/xml_profile cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/serde/xml_profile.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/serde/xml_profile.out` prints nothing.
- The existing `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/encoding_xml cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` still passes.

## Batch
batch-core-encoding: a witness and doc table over Core/encoding/xml.jet.

## Dependencies
None. The D-ENCXML1 implementation is recorded as a new card, not a prerequisite for this evidence card.

cards.plan:
## Goal
Cut Core/encoding/ini.jet over to the ratified D-CORE-INI1=A profile: strict raw parsing onto the shared `DataTree`/Codable rails, explicit interpolation operations, and bounded expansion.

## Current state
- Core/encoding/ini.jet exists, but its header at :12-17 says the last duplicate key wins, `DEFAULT` is not magic, and there is no interpolation.
- It defines its own tree and error type, which the ratified text forbids (`no IniTree`): `INIError{line, reason}` at :18-28, `Pair`/`Section`/`Ini` at :31-43, and `parse(text) -> Ini INIError!` at :47.
- The getters `get_int`/`get_bool`/`get_float` at :122-140 guess types after parsing. `strip_comment` at :217 removes inline comments, which the ratified profile does not allow.
- The exports are listed at Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCallRows.jet:1934, and conformance seeds in tests/conformance/corpus/core/encoding/ini/*.jet construct `Ini{}`.
- D-CORE-INI1=A: `parse` returns an Object of section Objects with Text values, keeping spelling and order. Sections must be named. Delimiters are `=` or `:`. Comments are whole-line `#`/`;` only, with no inline comments. Multiline values are indentation-based, and valueless options are not allowed. Duplicate section or option names, malformed continuations and invalid UTF-8 are rejected. Names are case-sensitive. `DEFAULT` is inherited at lookup and typed decode without mutating the raw sections. Typed decode is Int (exact signed decimal), Float (finite decimal), Bool (1/yes/true/on and 0/no/false/off, case-insensitive) or String. `decode_interpolated` handles `%(name)s`/`%%`, and `decode_interpolated_extended` handles `${section:key}`/`$$`. Cycle, missing-key and syntax errors keep the key path. Explicit `IniLimits` fields wrap `EncodingLimits` with depth 32 and 8388608 produced bytes. The writer is deterministic and makes no comment-preservation claim. There is no environment or file lookup.

## Changes
1. Rewrite ini.jet: `parse(text) -> DataTree EncodingError!` (format INI), `to_string(value: DataTree) -> String`, typed `decode<T>`, `decode_interpolated` and `decode_interpolated_extended`, and `IniLimits`. Delete `Ini`, `Section`, `Pair`, `INIError`, the guessing getters, `set`/`remove_*` and inline-comment stripping in the same cutover.
2. Add the INI format to `EncodingFormat` in Core/encoding/encoding.jet if it is missing.
3. Regenerate the views with `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --write`, update the CoreCallRows.jet:1934 export row, and rewrite every tests/conformance/corpus/core/encoding/ini/*.jet seed to the new surface.
4. New Examples/features/serde/encoding_ini.jet with its .out, covering criteria 4-7: case and duplicate rejection, DEFAULT inheritance without mutation, raw versus Basic versus Extended output on the same input, a cycle and depth-33 failure, an expansion-byte overrun, a round trip of values and order with comments dropped (and reported as dropped), and a rejected valueless option.
5. Criterion 7: the codec is pure (text in). Reading a missing file stays an IOError at the caller, and the example shows that.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/encoding_ini cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/serde/encoding_ini.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/serde/encoding_ini.out` prints nothing.
- `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --check` exits 0, and `node Tools/agent/core-conformance.mjs` accepts the rewritten ini seeds.

## Batch
batch-core-encoding: a single Core/encoding module cutover with its golden.

## Dependencies
None open. D-CORE-INI1 is ratified A.

cards.body:
Investigate plist and platform data interchange.

Determine the useful property-list/platform configuration job in the captured baseline and whether current Core facilities satisfy it.

Determine the useful property-list/platform configuration job in the captured baseline and whether current Core facilities satisfy it.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f063. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Ship `core.encoding.plist` per D-CORE-PLIST1=A: typed XML and binary property lists over the existing XML kernel and the shared codec rails.

## Current state
- No plist code exists in Core/encoding/.
- The XML kernel to reuse is Core/encoding/xml.jet: `parse_with(text, limits: XMLLimits)` at :139, `XMLLimits` at :71-80 with safe values at :30-41, and depth enforcement at :345-347. It never defines named entities (:43-53), and it rejects any DOCTYPE at :295-296.
- Real Apple XML plists carry `<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC ...>`. The ratified fixture (`<?xml ...?><plist version="1.0"><dict><key>count</key><integer>2</integer></dict></plist>`) does not.
- D-CORE-PLIST1=A: `to_string` produces XML and `encode` produces binary bytes. Typed decode accepts the explicit String/XML input or byte input (XML or binary). Byte input recognizes only the documented signatures (`bplist00`, `<?xml`/`<plist`) and never falls back to another parser. Typed values are String, Bool, Int, Float, lists, string-key records/maps, `[U8]`, `Instant` (absolute UTC) and a module-local `PlistUID` wrapping U64 (range 0..2^64-1; XML output of a UID is `Unsupported`). Numeric width is checked before output. Untyped `parse` returns `DataTree` only for representable categories; `data`, `date` and UID are `Unsupported` there. The byte grammar and boundary corpus are attached before any implementation claim.
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f063 and #capture-f560efbdd688.

## Changes
1. New Core/encoding/plist.jet with an XML path built on the xml.jet kernel (bounded, no external IO, no entity definitions) and a binary `bplist00` reader and writer. The binary side covers the trailer (offset size, object-ref size, object count, top object, offset-table offset), rejects out-of-range offsets and refs, rejects cycles through a visited set, checks integer width and the UID range, and rejects trailing or overlapping data.
2. Typed `decode<T>`/`encode<T>`, `to_string`, and untyped `parse` returning `DataTree` or `Unsupported`.
3. DOCTYPE: accept only the exact Apple plist DOCTYPE literal, stripped before the kernel and never processed. Any other DOCTYPE remains a Syntax error. If the owner reads the ratified text as excluding this, stop the slice and ballot it.
4. Register the module (`module plist` in encoding.jet, `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --write`, rows in CoreCallRows.jet and Rings/RingLayer.jet).
5. New Examples/features/serde/encoding_plist.jet with its .out. It cross-reads and writes the count fixture as XML and binary, covers collections and native types, preserves bytes, date and UID on typed paths, shows `Unsupported` on untyped projection, and exercises the binary integer and UID limits, malformed offsets, a ref cycle, hostile XML (billion-laughs DOCTYPE, deep nesting), and the root-buffer size it measures.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/encoding_plist cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/serde/encoding_plist.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/serde/encoding_plist.out` prints nothing.
- `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --check` exits 0.
- Criterion 7: `Tools/agent/jet-env jet perf run Examples/features/serde/encoding_plist.jet` records peak allocation for a whole-root read. No incremental-parsing claim is made.

## Batch
batch-core-encoding: one Core/encoding module and its golden.

## Dependencies
None open. D-CORE-PLIST1 is ratified A.

cards.title: Investigate mail/MIME and mailbox data helpers
cards.body:
Investigate mail/MIME and mailbox data helpers.

Map selected mail/MIME/message encoding and mailbox capabilities to existing network/data owners and application adapters.

Map selected mail/MIME/message encoding and mailbox capabilities to existing network/data owners and application adapters.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f064. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Close the mail/MIME and mailbox data gap. Parsing and formatting are separate from sending and authentication. Hostile headers, encodings, limits and attachment streaming are covered. Parsing has no credential or network side effect. Each missing library/API/placement choice is gated on its own.

**Current state**
- Core/email/email.jet builds and sends: Address/Attachment/Envelope/Message types (:59-148), builders (:181-249, `serialize` :249), and SMTP send (:290-306). There is no RFC 5322/MIME parse and no mbox/Maildir reader.
- Core/net/mime.jet:8-15 handles media types only (#3125 proves it).
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f064.

**Owner question (open; plan written for recommendation A)**
Should core.email gain bounded RFC 5322/MIME parsing, and do mailbox formats belong in Core? A) add `parse` as the inverse of `serialize` in core.email with hostile-header limits, and mailbox formats go to packages; B) both parse and mailbox in Core; C) neither. Recommendation: A.

**Changes** (A)
1. Core/email/email.jet: `pub fn parse(bytes: [U8]) -> Message EmailError!` and `parse_with_limits(bytes, limits: EmailLimits)`. The signature is pure, with no `-[Net]>`/`-[FS]>` effect row, so the compiler enforces no network or credential access. It handles header unfolding, RFC 2047 encoded-words, multipart with boundary validation, nesting-depth/part-count/header-count/header-byte limits, and base64/quoted-printable bodies. Hostile inputs (CR/LF injection, NUL, overlong lines, boundary collisions) produce typed errors.
2. Attachment streaming: `parse_reader(reader: FileReader, limits)` yields parts without buffering whole attachments, reusing the existing FileReader lifecycle.
3. The round-trip law `parse(serialize(m)) == m` holds for messages that `serialize` accepts.
4. Mailbox formats: note the package placement in core-library.md. Nothing is added to Core.
5. Register in Prelude/Core.jet, run `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs`, add core-library.md rows.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=net/email_parse Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> round trip, encoded-words, nested multipart, streamed attachment and hostile-header rejections. Identical on AOT, default `jet run` and the interpreter.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/email_parse_net_effect.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` -> calling the network from a parse callback context is an effect error.

**Batch**
batch-core-net.

**Dependencies**
The owner ballot above. Related: #3126 (send proof), #3125 (media types).

1. Separate parsing/formatting from sending/authentication.
2. cover hostile headers, encodings, limits and attachment streaming.
3. no credential/network side effect during parse.
4. gate missing library/API/placement choices individually.

cards.title: Investigate basic asset audio container IO
cards.body:
Investigate basic asset audio container IO.

Retain the captured baseline wave-file opportunity only as ordinary bounded asset/container IO, not specialist audio-signal analysis.

Retain the captured baseline wave-file opportunity only as ordinary bounded asset/container IO, not specialist audio-signal analysis.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f067. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Decide whether Core reads basic PCM audio containers as ordinary bounded asset IO. If yes, implement the minimal WAV/RIFF path that feeds game sound assets, with no DSP.

## Current state
- Audio exists only as the raylib provider: `RaylibSound{path}` (Core/game/raylib.jet:30-32), and `load_sound`/`play_sound` (:100-106), which keep audio state provider-owned (:5-7).
- No WAV or RIFF parsing exists under Core/ (grep for wav and riff finds nothing).
- Byte helpers to reuse are in Core/encoding/binary.jet (`unpack_u16le`/`unpack_u32le`, `BinaryError` at :22-26).
- `scene.assets.sound` is the ratified sound entry point (D-GAME-ASSET1=A; see #238). Examples/features/game/battery/assets/jump.wav is an existing fixture.
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f067. The job is ordinary container IO, not audio analysis.

## Owner question (open; this is why the phase is deciding)
Options: A) a bounded WAV reader and writer in Jet under core.game assets; B) provider-only through raylib `load_sound`; C) a package, not Core. Recommended: A, minimal. The games critical area needs a tier-independent asset path, and A reuses binary.jet. The ballot must show the same program under A, B and C.

## Changes (written for option A)
1. Core/game/wav.jet (module `core.game.wav`): `read(bytes: [U8], limits: WavLimits{WavLimits.safe()}) -> WavClip WavError!` and `write(clip: WavClip) -> [U8] WavError!`. It supports RIFF/WAVE with `fmt ` PCM 8/16/24/32-bit, IEEE float32 and WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE wrapping those. It skips unknown chunks with bounds and pad bytes. It rejects compressed formats (Unsupported), a truncated or oversized `data` chunk, channel or rate overflow, and trailing garbage past the RIFF size. `chunks(size)` streams frames without materializing the whole clip.
2. The #238 sound import path uses `wav.read` to produce the checked import fact (kind, channels, rate, frames). The raylib provider still plays it.
3. Register with `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --write`.
4. New Examples/features/game/game_wav.jet with its .out, covering the PCM16 and float32 fixtures, jump.wav, extensible format, unknown chunks, and each malformed case.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=game/game_wav cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/game/game_wav.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/game/game_wav.out` prints nothing.

## Batch
batch-core-ui: a Core/game asset module.

## Dependencies
The owner ballot above (not yet filed; draft it with the three options). #238 consumes the result but does not block the reader.

cards.title: Investigate locale and message-catalog composition
cards.body:
Investigate locale and message-catalog composition.

Account gettext/locale/pluralized message jobs with existing text/format ownership and ReadableAstra source identity work.

Account gettext/locale/pluralized message jobs with existing text/format ownership and ReadableAstra source identity work.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f069. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-CORE-CATALOG1=A: one checked, object-local GNU `.mo` message-catalog parser in `core.text`, with a caller-supplied fallback order. It supports context and plural forms and has no ambient locale, filesystem or global state. Source translation IDs stay separate from locale data, and there is no second interpolation grammar.

## Current state
- There is no catalog, gettext or `.mo` support anywhere in Core (`Core/text/`: combinators, fmt, html, parse, string, text, wrap). D-CORE-CATALOG1=A is ratified with these terms: Catalog is opaque and local; it reuses core.text strings and collections, shared limits and typed error/cause conventions; keys, locale order and plural selection are runtime values; and it keeps GNU `.mo` version, charset and plural compatibility, missing-source behavior, malformed errors, and immutable ordered fallback explicit.
- Interpolation already has one grammar (`core.text.fmt` and `{…}` string interpolation). Placeholders in translated text must go through it.
- The finding is at `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f069`.

## Changes
1. `Core/text/catalog.jet`:
   - `Catalog` (opaque) and `CatalogError` (Truncated, BadMagic, BadVersion, OffsetOutOfRange, BadCharset, BadPluralForms, LimitExceeded) with causes.
   - `catalog.parse(bytes: [U8], limits: CatalogLimits{…}) -> Catalog CatalogError!`, which handles both endians and revision 0/1, requires UTF-8, and parses the `Plural-Forms` header with a bounded expression evaluator.
   - `catalog.chain([Catalog])` for immutable ordered fallback.
   - `get(msgid)`, `get_ctx(context, msgid)`, and `plural(msgid, msgid_plural, n)`/`plural_ctx`. A missing entry returns the source `msgid`/plural per the GNU rule, with a typed `found: Bool` available.
   - No file IO: the caller reads the bytes.
2. Registry rows for core.text.catalog and the Rust mirror if the shipped binary needs it. Document the module in `Docs/spec` core.text.

## Proof
- Add `Examples/features/text/message_catalog.jet` with a golden. It embeds two small `.mo` byte fixtures (de, fr) and covers context, a three-form plural (e.g. `ru` or `pl` formula), fallback order, two concurrent Catalog objects, and malformed cases (truncated, bad offset, bad charset, bad plural formula, oversize).
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=text/message_catalog Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `jet run` and `jet run --interpret` output diffs empty against the golden.
- A search of `Core/text/catalog.jet` for `files.`/`sys.get` finds nothing (no ambient access).

## Batch
batch-core-text: a new Core text module.

## Dependencies
None. The decision is ratified.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f074. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Implement ratified D-CORE-CLI-MENU1=A: `ArgsSpec.prompt(input, output)`, with a stdin/stdout convenience form. It walks the canonical command schema interactively, validates through the same parser, and returns `ParsedArgs?` on the ordinary fallible rail.
- None means an explicit cancel or a clean EOF before a complete selection.
- A malformed answer returns a structured ArgsError; IO failure keeps IOError.
- A non-TTY or unsupported target is an explicit capability failure.
- It returns one selection per call, and the caller dispatches. It never runs handlers, never starts a scheduler, and never clears the screen.

**Current state**
- Guided field filling exists: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Args.rs:555` `jet_args_parse_guided` calls `jet_args_parse_mode(.., allow_missing=true)`, plus guided field validation and argv building at `Args.rs:1053-1260`.
- The TUI/line prompts and `jet_args_guided_accessible` are at `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/ArgsProjection.rs:221-350`.
- There is no command-selection menu and no public `prompt` method: `ProcessHandles.jet` has no `prompt` op.

cards.title: Investigate matrix and extension-type codec adapters
cards.body:
Investigate matrix and extension-type codec adapters.

Account Glaze Eigen and documented extension adapters as typed data interoperability, not a selected numerical-computing framework.

Account Glaze Eigen and documented extension adapters as typed data interoperability, not a selected numerical-computing framework.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f075. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Record how matrix and tensor values cross Jet's typed codecs: shape, layout (row/column-major), scalar type and tag fidelity. Treat Glaze's Eigen adapters and documented extension adapters as typed data interoperability, not as a chosen numerical framework. Codec glue stays separate from external-library inclusion, and any adapter or dependency needs a ballot. Finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f075`.

## Current state
- `Core/compute/compute.jet:41-46` defines `Tensor{shape: [Int], data: [Float], device, numeric_profile}`, row-major by construction.
- Tensor has its own ad-hoc text format, `serialize`/`deserialize` (`:647,672`), outside the canonical Encode/Decode model. That is a parallel serializer, the thing criterion 2 warns about.
- CBOR rejects tags, which includes the RFC 8746 typed-array and multi-dimensional-array tags, and half/single floats (`Core/encoding/cbor.jet:29-37`).

## Changes (investigation, fixtures only)
1. Write `Examples/features/serde/tensor_codec.jet`:
   - a 2x3 Tensor through `json` (via its Decode/Encode derive if present, else record absent) and through `compute.serialize`;
   - print shape, element order and profile after a round trip;
   - an F32 tensor shows whether the scalar type survives;
   - a CBOR RFC 8746 tagged array returns `Unsupported`.
2. On the card, record which path preserves shape, layout, scalar type and tag, and which does not.
3. Recommend retiring `compute.serialize`/`deserialize` in favour of canonical Encode/Decode if Tensor derives them. That retirement, and any RFC 8746 tag support, is a follow-on ballot or card. Nothing ships on this card beyond the fixture.

## Proof
`JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/tensor_codec Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes on AOT and default run and shows each fidelity cell.

## Batch
batch-core-encoding: codec investigation with a fixture.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: Investigate bounded JSON Patch generation
cards.body:
Investigate bounded JSON Patch generation.

Assess generating a patch from two values separately from applying a supplied patch, including Glaze diff and its reserved options.

Assess generating a patch from two values separately from applying a supplied patch, including Glaze diff and its reserved options.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f076. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Implement D-CORE-JSON-DIFF1=A: `json.diff(before: DataTree, after: DataTree) -> DataTree EncodingError!` returns a deterministic RFC 6902 operation array with `patch(before, diff(before, after)) == after`. It does not promise minimal output, move/copy detection or LCS. It is bounded, and it is gated separately from D-CORE-JSON-PATCH1.

**Current state**
- No diff exists in Core/encoding/json.jet (:71-100). The applier it must reuse does not exist yet (#3278, ready). DataTree equality is `equal_unordered` (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/DataTree.rs:218 trait; EncodingTraits.rs:577-581).
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f076 (Glaze diff and its reserved options).

**Changes**
1. Core/encoding/json.jet: `pub fn diff(before, after)` and `diff_with_limits`. Objects are traversed in `before` insertion order and then new `after` keys in order. Changed scalars emit `replace`, missing keys `remove` and new keys `add`. Arrays: a common prefix and suffix compare element-wise, and the rest is replaced whole (documented; no LCS). Paths are built with RFC 6901 escaping, shared with #3237. Visited nodes, comparisons, emitted bytes and allocations are bounded, and limit exhaustion is an ordinary EncodingError, never a silent whole-document replace. Non-finite floats are rejected.
2. Register in Prelude/Core.jet :94-95, run `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs`, add a core-library.md row with the ordering and non-minimality note.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/json_diff Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> for each fixture pair, prints the ops and `patch(before, diff) == after: true`. Covers key order, nested objects, prefix/suffix arrays, escaped keys, non-finite rejection and a limit error. Identical on AOT, default `jet run` and the interpreter.

**Batch**
batch-core-encoding (lands after #3278 in the same batch).

**Dependencies**
#3278 (patch applier; ratified DIFF1 requires reusing it).

cards.title: Investigate merge-diff representability
cards.body:
Investigate merge-diff representability.

Retain merge-diff generation as a separate useful operation while rejecting the unsupported claim that every target is representable.

Retain merge-diff generation as a separate useful operation while rejecting the unsupported claim that every target is representable.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f077. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Implement D-CORE-JSON-MERGEDIFF1=A: `json.merge_diff(before: DataTree, after: DataTree) -> DataTree EncodingError!` returns an RFC 7386 merge document only when applying it yields exactly `after`. Otherwise it returns `EncodingErrorKind.Unsupported` with the member path, never lossy output, and never silently switches to JSON Patch.

**Current state**
- No merge diff exists. The merge applier it must reuse does not exist yet (#3279, ready). `EncodingErrorKind.Unsupported` already exists (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/EncodingTypes.rs:54-60). DataTree equality is `equal_unordered` (JetStd/DataTree.rs:218 trait).
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f077.

**Changes**
1. Core/encoding/json.jet: `pub fn merge_diff(before, after)` and `merge_diff_with_limits`, sharing #3279's traversal helpers. Rules: a removed member emits `null`. A changed or added member whose target value is `null` is unrepresentable (Unsupported at `/path`). An unchanged null member is omitted (representable). A null root replacement is representable (root patch `null`). Arrays replace whole. Non-object roots replace. Comparison, output and depth are bounded. No minimality or universal round-trip claim.
2. Self-check in debug examples only: `merge_patch(before, result) == after`. No runtime double-apply in the shipped path.
3. Register in Prelude/Core.jet :94-95, run `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs`, add a core-library.md row pointing to `json.diff` (#3296) as the separate JSON Patch job.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/json_merge_diff Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> cases: absent->null and value->null member (Unsupported with path), unchanged null (omitted), null root (representable), nested object change, array replace, a limit error, and `merge_patch(before, merge_diff(before, after)) == after: true` for every representable pair. Identical on AOT, default `jet run` and the interpreter.

**Batch**
batch-core-encoding (lands after #3279 in the same batch).

**Dependencies**
#3279 (merge applier; ratified MERGEDIFF1 requires reusing it).

cards.title: Investigate selected-field serialization
cards.body:
Investigate selected-field serialization.

Compare Glaze partial-write/path-selection with existing generated Encode and output streaming for a bounded projection job.

Compare Glaze partial-write/path-selection with existing generated Encode and output streaming for a bounded projection job.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f078. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Produce the executed projection cells and the strict candidate/plain measurement that D-CORE-JSON-SELECT1 (open; recommendation A `json.to_string_selected(value, paths)`) requires before it can be ratified. No public API lands on this card.

**Current state**
- Core/encoding/json.jet:81 `to_string(value: DataTree)` renders a whole tree; `render_json`/`write_json` (:580, :650-707) visit every member. No path selection or partial write exists anywhere in Core/encoding.
- Typed records reach JSON through the generated Encode route (`json.to_string(record)`, e.g. Examples/features/io/db_jsonb_boundary.jet:32).
- D-CORE-JSON-SELECT1 is open and performance-gated: A cannot be ratified before a registered candidate/plain pair proves a strict win. Tools/gauntlet/measurement-manifest.json `performance_surface_pairs` holds only `compound_assign_vs_binary_assign`, and Tools/gauntlet/harness/performance-surface.mjs measures only that pair.
- Related: #3306 (top-level exclusions, deciding), #3236 (shared codec values), #3299 (partial updates), #3237 (RFC 6901 pointer parser that option A must share).
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f078 (Glaze v8.3.0 partial-write).

**Changes**
1. Add Tools/gauntlet/entries/json-projection/ (Jet and Rust arms, expected.out). Record with a large unselected field, nested object, array, renamed, skipped and custom-codec fields. Plain arm = hand-written DTO + `json.to_string`. Candidate arm = a gauntlet-private selected encoder over the generated Encode walker (no Core export).

cards.title: Investigate partial updates to existing typed records
cards.body:
Investigate partial updates to existing typed records.

Compare Glaze direct partial reads and struct merge behavior with current complete Decode, config merge and the proposed standard data patches.

Compare Glaze direct partial reads and struct merge behavior with current complete Decode, config merge and the proposed standard data patches.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f079. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-CORE-TYPED-UPDATE1=A (ratified): `json.update<T>(existing: T, patch: DataTree) -> T [FieldError]!`. It is a nonmutating, atomic update driven by a compiler-generated field plan:
- Omitted fields keep their values, and explicit null follows the target field's nullability.
- Names, unknown fields, Flatten and validation keep their existing law.
- Unchanged fields are not rebuilt through a lossy wire round-trip.
- Custom mappings with no lawful update path return an explicit unsupported `FieldError` before any change.
- There is no `Partial<T>`, no new marker, and ordinary decode does not change.

Source: CORE-F079. The card title's "Investigate" is superseded by the ratified decision.

## Current state
- No typed update or patch-into-record API exists in `Core/encoding/json.jet`, `Compiler/` or the Prelude.
- Typed decode is the model to follow: `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Data.jet:487-510` (`sema_data_core_decode_contract`, json at `:491-492`, result `Result<T, [FieldError]>`).
- Field metadata comes from `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Serde.jet` and `Registration/Checked.jet`. E2410 and E2412 are registered at `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet:13703,13735`.
- The decision names reuse of struct decode metadata, `StructDef.validate_block`, `jet_datatree_unproject` and `FieldError`.

## Changes
1. **JetSema.** Add `json.update<T>(existing, patch)` next to `decode` in `Calls/Data.jet`. `T` must have a compiler-derived codec; a hand-written Decode means the call returns the unsupported `FieldError` at runtime. `existing` is taken by read access, and the result is a fresh owned `T`.
2. **JetCodegen.** Generate a per-type update plan. For each field present in the patch, decode it through the field's existing decoder; for each absent field, copy it from `existing`. Apply Flatten, Rename and DenyUnknownFields exactly as decode does, then run the validate block on the assembled value. Return `Err` with the full `FieldError` list and no partial value.
3. **Core.** Add `pub fn update` in `Core/encoding/json.jet` and its Core call row.
4. **Retained host.** Add the Prelude `jet_datatree_unproject` reuse and the Rust bootstrap mirror so the shipped binary proves it, plus a JetEval route.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/json_update cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: pass.
- `JET_THREE_WAY_STEM=serde/json_update cargo test --test dev_corpus cranelift_three_way_differential_battery`: tiers agree.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/json_typed cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: ordinary decode is unchanged.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: exit 0.

## Batch
`batch-core-encoding`: a Codable/encoding surface batched with #3233 and #3238.

## Dependencies
None. Criterion 4 ("independently ballot any new typed update API") is satisfied by D-CORE-TYPED-UPDATE1=A.

cards.title: Investigate explicit JSON-with-comments support
cards.body:
Investigate explicit JSON-with-comments support.

Retain the selected JSONC convenience as an explicit configuration-dialect investigation rather than weakening ordinary JSON parsing.

Retain the selected JSONC convenience as an explicit configuration-dialect investigation rather than weakening ordinary JSON parsing.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f080. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Implement D-CORE-JSONC1=A: an explicit `core.encoding.jsonc` codec that accepts `//` line and `/* */` block comments, rejects trailing commas, and keeps exact numbers, UTF-8, duplicate/field policy, limits and original source offsets. `to_string` emits ordinary JSON. There is no CST, round trip, include or eval, and ordinary `core.encoding.json` is unchanged.

**Current state**
- Core/encoding/json.jet is strict: `skip_ws` (:181) accepts only JSON whitespace, and trailing commas are rejected at :417 and :458. No comment mode exists.
- Format rows live in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.jet:243-248 (`format_row JSON core.encoding.json JSON` ...), and they drive the shared EncodingFormat carrier.
- Typed decode wrappers follow the Core/db/db.jet:87 pattern (`pub fn decode<T: Decode>(...) -> T [FieldError]!`).
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f080.

**Changes**
1. New Core/encoding/jsonc.jet. `parse(text)`, `decode<T>(text)` and `reader(text)` run one comment-blanking pass: bytes inside comments become spaces, newlines are kept, and string literals and escapes are respected. The result then goes to `json.parse`/`json.decode<T>`/`json.reader`, so there is one JSON parser and line/column/offset stay identical to the source. An unterminated block comment is `Truncated` at its offset. Errors are re-tagged with `EncodingFormat.JSONC`. `to_string`/`to_string_pretty` delegate to json.
2. Add `format_row JSONC core.encoding.jsonc JSONC` at Core.jet:243-248, module and source_module rows beside :94-97, run `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs`, add a core-library.md section stating that JSONC is not wire-equivalent to TOML/YAML and that comments are not preserved.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/jsonc Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> line/block comments accepted; `//` inside strings kept; trailing comma rejected with the same line/column as json; unterminated comment -> Truncated; big-number exactness; duplicate key rejected (#3234 policy); typed decode; to_string output with no comments. Identical on AOT, default `jet run` and the interpreter.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/json Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` -> strict JSON still rejects comments.

**Batch**
batch-core-encoding.

**Dependencies**
None. The decision is ratified.

cards.title: Prove JSON text projection and canonicalization
cards.body:
Prove JSON text projection and canonicalization.

Compare ordinary, pretty and canonical output through the existing JSON owner, with byte-sensitive canonical output kept distinct from cosmetic formatting.

Compare ordinary, pretty and canonical output through the existing JSON owner, with byte-sensitive canonical output kept distinct from cosmetic formatting.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f081. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Make Jet's `json.canonical` the exact RFC 8785 contract that D-JSONCANON1=A ratified, and pin it with exact-byte fixtures. The Jet source currently disagrees with both the spec and the host implementation.

## Current state
- Core/encoding/json.jet:90-91 declares `canonical(value: DataTree) -> String` as infallible, with object keys sorted by UTF-8. `render_canonical` (:586-590) swallows failure with `?? ""`. `write_canonical` (:592-632) runs an O(n^2) selection sort with the byte-order comparator `cmp_utf8` (:634-648), writes Int raw (`{n}`, :599), and writes Float through the ordinary `write_json_float` (:600).
- Law, Docs/spec/encoding-decisions.md:730-807 (D-JSONCANON1=A): sort by unsigned UTF-16 code units (:777); use the ECMAScript `Number::toString` shortest round-trip binary64 serializer (:778-780); `-0.0` emits `0`; NaN and infinities are `Unsupported` (`JCS cannot encode a non-finite Float`); an Int is admitted only when binary64 represents it exactly (9007199254740992 yes, 9007199254740993 no; :783-788); duplicate keys are Syntax (`JCS requires unique object keys`); there is no locale, normalization or external crate; one semantic writer serves `json.writer(canonical: true)` as well (:145).
- The host already sorts by UTF-16 (`jet_json_jcs_key_cmp`, crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/EncodingStream.rs:271-273; JIT `jet_jit_json_canonical_checked`, crates/jet-jit/src/Encoding.rs:2843). So the tiers can disagree (I9).
- The named witness Examples/features/serde/encoding_canonical.jet covers CBOR and XML, not JSON, and uses XML APIs Core lacks (see #3282), so it has no golden.

## Changes
1. json.jet: `canonical(value: DataTree) -> String EncodingError!` implementing D-JSONCANON1 exactly. That means a UTF-16 code-unit key comparator with an O(n log n) sort, the JCS number serializer, the Int admission check, non-finite and duplicate-key rejection, and no `?? ""`. Migrate every `json.canonical` caller found by grep across Core/, Examples/, tests/ and Jetpack/.
2. Edition clause: encoding-decisions.md:795-801 keeps 2026 prototype bytes. AGENTS.md greenfield cutover allows that only as an owner-named exception. Ship one form, and ask Main before carrying a 2026 branch.
3. New Examples/features/serde/json_canonical.jet with its .out. It covers the RFC 8785 Appendix B number vectors; keys whose UTF-8 and UTF-16 orders differ (U+E000 against U+1F600); -0.0; 2^53 admitted and 2^53+1 rejected; NaN rejected; nesting; the round trip `parse(canonical(x)) == x`; and `canonical` differing from `to_string_pretty`.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/json_canonical cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/serde/json_canonical.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/serde/json_canonical.out` prints nothing, which is byte parity with the host JCS route.
- Criteria 3 and 4 hold by construction: pretty and compact output are not canonical, and no profile change is made beyond the ratified one.

## Batch
batch-core-encoding: one json.jet function plus its golden.

## Dependencies
None. The encoding_canonical.jet repair belongs to the XML C14N work that #3282 routes.

1. Pin canonical profile, key ordering, duplicate admission and numeric/Unicode representation.
2. exercise exact byte fixtures and round-trip.
3. never treat pretty/minified output as canonical or promise original lexical preservation.
4. gate profile changes.

cards.title: Cover route overlap and ordering across existing HTTP projections
cards.body:
Cover route overlap and ordering across existing HTTP projections.

Jet already detects duplicate route shapes; broader overlap/order consistency is unproved, and Nest12 already supplies conflict/specificity controls.

Contrast static/dynamic/typed route overlaps in App and canonical HTTP router under actual adapters. Fix the existing matcher/diagnostic, not a second routing API.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-http-route-conflict-parity. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Make route conflict and precedence one law across the canonical HTTP mux/router and the web App router: accepted routes pick the same handler on every adapter, and conflicting or ambiguous routes get a deterministic, source-linked diagnostic. Fix the existing matcher and E2804; do not add a second routing API.

## Current state
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/HTTPServer.rs:704` (E2804 contract conflict), `:1216` and `:7014` (E2804 exact duplicate method+pattern at mux/router registration). `CoreLib/Top/WebRouter.rs:932-933` rejects only an exact `pattern_text` duplicate. E2807 covers builder-versus-convention collisions in App (`tests/ui/web_app_route_collision.stderr`). The E2804 row is at `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet:14446`.
- Overlaps such as `/items/{id}` versus `/items/new`, or a typed param versus an untyped param, have no specified verdict. HEAD handling and typed-path failure (404 or 400) are unrecorded.
- Finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-http-route-conflict-parity`.

## Changes
1. Record first: `Examples/features/net/route_overlap.jet` registers static, param, typed-param and wildcard routes on `http.router()`, the server mux, and an App. It probes each path over loopback (plus HEAD, and a typed param given a non-integer) and prints the chosen handler and status per adapter.
2. Adopt one precedence law per segment: static > typed param > param > wildcard, taking the App route facts' existing `precedence` field as the source of truth. Apply it in the HTTPServer mux/router matcher and WebRouter.
3. Registration-time E2804 covers ambiguous overlaps too: the same method with the same specificity at every segment and a shared matching path. Both spans are reported, as E2807 does. Update the DiagnosticRows.jet text and the Prelude Diagnostics row together, plus Docs/spec/diagnostics.md.
4. A UI fixture for the ambiguous case.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=net/route_overlap Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes: every adapter prints the same handler for every probe, and HEAD and typed-failure behavior are shown.
- UI fixture `tests/ui/http_route_ambiguous_overlap.jet` with its `.stderr` shows E2804 with both spans: `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots`.

## Batch
batch-core-net: HTTP router/mux matcher and diagnostics, proven by a net golden and a UI snapshot.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: Preserve socket context, acknowledgement and cleanup
cards.body:
Preserve socket context, acknowledgement and cleanup.

Nest12 already supports per-connection request-scoped providers. Jet cannot claim a win from an obsolete restriction.

Check Jet socket coverage against two connections, repeated messages, disconnect cleanup and bounded output; preserve native WS versus Socket.IO acknowledgement differences.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-websocket-connection-lifetime. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove WebSocket connection lifetime on the existing surface: isolated per-connection context, repeated messages on the right connection, disconnect cleanup, explicit bounds, and acknowledgements that mean only their documented stage. Nest 12 already has per-connection providers, so Jet claims no win from an obsolete restriction. Socket.IO stays with #3098. Research finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-websocket-connection-lifetime`.

## Current state
- `Core/net/ws.jet:18` has `connect`, `:29` `upgrade(request)`, and `WsError.MessageTooLarge(limit)` (`:12`) as the only explicit bound.
- The HTTP upgrade runs in the server leaf `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/HTTPServer.rs`.
- `Examples/features/net/ws_echo.jet:1-33` covers one connection and one message (golden `ws_echo.out`). Nothing covers two connections, repeated messages, disconnect or backpressure.

## Changes
1. Write `Examples/features/net/ws_lifetime.jet`:
   - two clients upgrade, and each handler keeps a connection-local counter;
   - each client sends three messages and the replies carry `{client}:{n}`, proving isolation;
   - client A disconnects, and A's handler loop ends with a closed error and prints `a-cleanup`, while B continues;
   - an oversize message returns `MessageTooLarge(limit)`;
   - `send_text` returning Ok is printed as `queued`, not `delivered`, so an acknowledgement means only its documented stage.
2. If a disconnect leaves the handler task alive, or no send-queue bound exists, fix it in the server leaf (HTTPServer.rs upgrade path) or in Core/net/ws.jet. Name the bound in the Core doc comment.

## Proof
`JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=net/ws_lifetime Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes on AOT and default run: isolated counters, `a-cleanup` before server shutdown, the MessageTooLarge line, and `queued` wording.

## Batch
batch-core-net: Core/net/ws plus its server leaf.

## Dependencies
None. Socket.IO acknowledgement semantics are #3098.
cards.checkSteps:
1. Two sockets have isolated contexts and repeated messages reuse the correct connection context.
2. Disconnect ends connection-owned work and releases resources.
3. Backpressure/queue bounds are explicit; an acknowledgement means only its documented stage.
4. CORE-F028 streaming upgrade, close, cancellation and body/output limit failures retain one socket/body owner; raw WS and Socket.IO acknowledgements are not equated.

cards.title: Prove HTTP policy ordering outside browser form actions
cards.body:
Prove HTTP policy ordering outside browser form actions.

CORS, headers, trust-proxy and rate identity are not validated by a form CSRF check.

Inventory and exercise existing HTTP policy on preflight, raw HTTP client and trusted/untrusted proxy cases. Missing capability becomes a named owner gate before adding any CoreLib API.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-http-policy-order-proof. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Inventory and exercise HTTP policy outside browser form actions (CORS preflight, security headers, forwarded identity, body limits) on a raw HTTP client over loopback. Record each missing capability as a named owner gate before adding any CoreLib API.

## Current state
- `Core/http/server.jet:77-83` `cors_policy`/`cors` delegate to the native provider; `:89` `request_id`. Grep over Core finds no trust-proxy, rate-limit or security-header function. `bind(..., deadline)` (`:15`) is the only transport bound exposed.
- The Rust CoreLib owner is `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/HTTPServer.rs`.
- Finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-nestjs-http-policy-order-proof`.

## Changes
1. Add `Examples/features/net/http_policy_order.jet` (loopback bind, serve task, shutdown, as in `net/backend_battery/run.jet:101-147`). It sends:
   - OPTIONS preflight from an allowed and a disallowed origin;
   - a disallowed-origin POST without auth: CORS does not authorize, and the handler's auth check still returns 401;
   - a normal response and an error response (404, handler Err): print the headers each carries;
   - an oversized and a malformed body: rejected (413/400) before the handler, with the mutation counter unchanged;
   - a request with `X-Forwarded-For` from the untrusted loopback peer: the access-log identity and any auth decision use the socket peer.
2. Where behavior is wrong (for example a limit enforced after the handler), fix it in HTTPServer.rs dispatch order.
3. For every unsupported cell (trust-proxy configuration, security-header policy, rate identity), open one owner ballot card each and link it here. No API is added in this card.
4. Criterion 5 / CORE-F028: document the body/transport limits in Docs/spec, distinct from TLS.

## Proof
`JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=net/http_policy_order Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes on AOT and `jet run`. The golden shows preflight verdicts, 401 despite CORS, headers on both success and error responses, a 413/400 with counter 0, and peer-based identity.

## Batch
batch-core-net: http server policy, proven by a net golden.

## Dependencies
None. Follow-up API work waits on the ballots this card files.

4. Malformed/oversized input is rejected before mutation; declared error mapping remains stable after headers are sent.
5. CORE-F028 transport/body limits reject malformed or oversized input before handler mutation; TLS/body/transport meaning remains distinct from Nest adapter policy order.

cards.title: Serialize explicit top-level exclusions
cards.body:
Serialize explicit top-level exclusions.

Exclusion is useful when most fields should be retained. It is not equivalent to a safe published allowlist: a newly added field is included unless existing Encode metadata omits it.

Should JSON encoding support an explicit top-level exclusion operation?

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f083. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Decide and, if A is ratified, implement D-CORE-JSON-EXCLUDE1: `json.to_string_excluding(value, keys)` through the same encoder. The docs must teach that exclusion is not a safe published allowlist, because a newly added field is emitted unless Encode metadata omits it.

## Current state
- `Core/encoding/json.jet:81` `to_string`, `:88` `to_string_pretty`, `:91` `canonical`; there is no exclusion operation.
- D-CORE-JSON-EXCLUDE1 is open (A: `to_string_excluding(value, keys)`; B: no stock operation, users project with an application struct or Encode-omitted fields). The recommendation is A, conditional on the allocation cell beating the projection.
- Finding: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f083`.

## Changes (option A)
1. `Core/encoding/json.jet`: `pub fn to_string_excluding<T: Encode>(value: T, keys: [String]) -> String EncodingError!`. It encodes top-level fields in declared order and skips the named ones. Empty and duplicate keys are a no-op; an unknown key returns an error naming it; excluding every field gives `{}`. Renamed fields match on the wire name. Numbers are emitted exactly, with no DataTree round trip.
2. JetFoundation registry row, signature and export for the new member.
3. `Examples/features/encoding/json_exclude.jet` plus golden covering the empty, duplicate, unknown, all-field, renamed, Encode-omitted and newly-added-field cases (criteria 1-3).
4. Criterion 4: a Tools/perf allocation cell comparing this against an equivalent application projection struct, and a Docs/spec note on the allowlist distinction.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=encoding/json_exclude Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes on AOT and `jet run`.
- The allocation measurement is recorded on the card.

## Batch
batch-core-encoding: one Core/encoding member.

## Dependencies
Owner ratification of D-CORE-JSON-EXCLUDE1.

cards.title: Close locale-sensitive formatting and parsing
cards.body:
Close locale-sensitive formatting and parsing.

Recover locale/facet/culture numeric, monetary, date/calendar and collation contracts from the declared C++/Python/Java/.NET indexes; compare existing core.text.fmt/time defaults before proposing a locale API or dataset.

Recover locale/facet/culture numeric, monetary, date/calendar and collation contracts from the declared C++/Python/Java/.NET indexes; compare existing core.text.fmt/time defaults before proposing a locale API or dataset.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f084. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal.** Decide whether Core gains locale-sensitive number/date formatting and parsing, then build that decision. Today every Core format is invariant.

**Current state.**
- `Core/time/calendar.jet:2-6` says "without locale tables … Names are English and fixed; there is no locale override". `day_name` is at :116, `month_name` at :146, `formatmonth` at :201.
- `Core/time/time.jet:602` `strftime` uses hard-coded English `days`/`months_short` arrays. `parse` (:238), `parse_time` (:249) and `parse_rfc3339` (:272) accept ISO grammar only.
- `Core/text/fmt.jet` (306 lines) has `number` (:4, grouped with `,`), `grouped`/`decimal`/`percent` (:34-36) and `sci` (:37). None of them takes a locale.
- A grep for `locale` over Core/ finds only the calendar comment.
- Research source: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f084` (the old path was `docs/research/`).
- Siblings: #3289 covers locale/message-catalog composition and #3310 covers catalog extraction. Both are open and neither is a prerequisite.

**Owner ballot (open, blocks only this card).** D-CORE-LOCALE1:
- A) No locale in Core. Document invariant formatting and leave locale to packages.
- B) `core.text.locale` with an explicit `Locale` value passed per call (no process-global default) and a bundled CLDR subset as Jet constant tables.
- C) A provider leaf over OS/ICU data.

Recommended: **B**. Start with numbers and dates. Collation stays behind its own later gate. The plan below assumes B.

**Changes (option B).**
1. New `Core/text/locale.jet`:
   - `Locale` value: tag, decimal/group separators, grouping sizes, month/day names, date patterns.

cards.body:
Close stock database and persistence contracts.

Map SQLite/dbm/JDBC/database/sql/ADO persistence jobs to existing core.db and file owners, independently of JSONB byte encoding.
