cards.title: Prove concrete collection iterator bounds and projections
cards.body:
Prove concrete collection iterator bounds and projections.

Hash, ordered-tree, heap, deque and linked-list iterators carry different order/exact/reverse and ownership contracts. A List proxy does not preserve every one.

Complete the per-family owned/shared/mutable/key/value/range capability map under CORE-F060 and the common iterator protocol.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f061. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove the per-family iterator capability map (hash, ordered/Rank, heap/PriorityQueue, deque/Queue, List) for owned, shared, key, value and range projections. Each family must keep only the order, exact-size and reverse guarantees it truly has, and no view may mutate a key.

## Current state
- Per-family method tables are in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:145-216`:
  - Set (`values`, `first`, `sort`);
  - Rank (`first`, `last`, `to_list`);
  - Queue (`peek_front`, `peek_back`, `reverse`);
  - PriorityQueue (`peek`, `pop`, `to_sorted_list`);
  - Map (`keys`, `values`, `slice`, `top_n`).
- `Map.keys` and `Map.values` and `Set.values` return a plain `Iter` (`:458-459,471`) and carry no order or exactness facts. The runtime is `jet_map_keys` and `jet_map_values` in `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.rs`.
- No example pins hash order as unspecified, heap iteration as unsorted, or set-operation results as carrying no inherited reverse or exact traits.
- The finding is at Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f061 (CORE-F060). Operation facts come from #3325.

## Changes
1. Add `Examples/features/collections/family_iter_capabilities.jet` and its `.out` with these cells:
   - Set and Map iteration printed only after `sort()`, so the output is deterministic; a comment states that hash order is unspecified.
   - Rank iteration and `first`/`last`, printed in comparator order.
   - PriorityQueue: `peek`/`pop` order versus `to_sorted_list`. Do not print the raw iteration order, and state that it is not promised to be sorted.
   - Queue front and back reads.
   - `Map.keys().len()` next to `filter(…).len()`: exact size is lost after filter.
   - A Set `union`, then `to_list().sort()`.
2. Add `tests/ui/iter_family_mutable_key.jet` and `.stderr`: an attempt to mutate a Map key or a Set element through iteration is rejected with the existing ownership/key-invariant diagnostic. If no diagnostic fires, the finding is a sema bug. Fix it in `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Ownership` first, then in the Rust mirror.
3. Put the capability table on the card, with unknown cells kept.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/family_iter_capabilities Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `jet run` and `jet run --interpret` of the example, each diffed against `Examples/features/expected/collections/family_iter_capabilities.out`, produce empty diffs.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/iter_family_mutable_key.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` passes.

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime`: the proof is a three-tier golden. The UI snapshot rides the same build.

## Dependencies
None.
cards.checkSteps:
1. Hash iteration does not gain sorted or repeatable order; ordered ranges preserve comparator semantics.
2. Set operations do not inherit reverse/exact traits merely because their inputs have them.
3. Heap iteration is not falsely promised sorted; range cardinality may be unknown even for an exact-size collection.
4. No mutable key or mutable set-element view can invalidate ordering/hash invariants.

Prove path and filesystem iterator source contracts.

Path components/ancestors and ReadDir are not generic text split or sorted directory lists. Their error and ordering behavior is source-specific.

Map stable path/filesystem producer and remainder operations through existing rooted-file/path owners.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f063. cards.plan:
**Goal.** Produce a current-tree receipt for path and filesystem producer contracts (ITER-F063; research: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f063`; row map in `target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json`). Contracts:
- roots, empty paths, separators and platform prefixes keep path semantics
- ReadDir per-item errors are distinct from constructor errors, with no invented order
- borrowed remaining-path projections

**Current state.**
- The shared lexical Path normalization repair was retained on 2026-09-15.
- `Core/files/path.jet` (438 lines):
  - `parts` (:150) is `files.split_slash(~path.raw)`, a generic text split. It is the case the card warns about, and may drop the root component.
  - `drive` (:159) recognizes only `X:`, not UNC `//server/share`.
  - `root`/`anchor` (:171/:181), `parents` (:84) and `is_empty` (:192) treat `""` and `.` as empty.
  - `iterdir` (:399) and `walk` (:407) return eager `[Path] IOError!`, so a per-item error cannot be represented apart from the constructor error.
- There is no borrowed "remaining path" projection (c3).
- Goldens exist for `io/path`, `io/path_within`, `io/walk_files`, `io/files_depth` and `io/dir_entry`.
- The old blocker (generated-Rust unsafe gate around `SetConsoleCtrlHandler`, log 2026-09-15) must be rechecked. The goldens passing on AOT shows whether it cleared.

**Changes.**
1. Add `Examples/features/io/path_components.jet` and its `.out` (cases in add_criteria).
2. Fix `parts` to follow the pathlib component law that `core.files.path` mirrors: the anchor (`/`, `C:\`, `//srv/share/`) is the first component, repeated and trailing separators collapse, and `""`/`.` give `[]`. Teach `drive` UNC prefixes. Both are lexical and pure (#3224 c4).
3. c2: record that per-item ReadDir errors are currently folded into the list constructor. A lazy `ReadDir` producer with per-item `IOError` items is new public API. Raise it as its own ballot on the generic iterator protocol (chain iterator-contract-before-adapters) and do not add it here.
4. c3: record "unsupported" with the peer references (Rust `Components::as_path`, Python has none). Any projection needs its own ballot.
5. Attach the supported, unsupported and unknown matrix to the card.

**Proof.**
- The command in add_criteria.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=io/path cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` and `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=io/walk_files cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: pass on AOT, which rechecks the unsafe gate.

**Batch.** `batch-core-files`: path source fix plus a files-family golden.

**Dependencies.** None. The ReadDir producer and the remaining-path projection become separate owner-gated cards if wanted.

cards.body:
Expose borrowed remainder projections from capable sources.

as_slice/as_str/as_path, char offset and exact-chunk remainder APIs expose unconsumed storage, not a new traversal. The bounded Jet inventory does not prove these generic projections.

Add remainder observation through existing View/ViewMut/provenance on capable iterator sources.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f065. cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-ITER-REMAINDER1=A with these rules:
- Sources that have an honest contiguous remainder (slice/list view iterators, String byte and char iterators, Path components, exact-chunk producers) expose `remaining()`, a shared `View` of the unread storage. With exclusive access they expose `into_remaining()`, which follows the ViewMut loan rules.
- The char offset is `offset()` in UTF-8 bytes.
- The exact-chunk remainder is the incomplete edge, not the full remaining input.
- Filters and other transformed sources never expose a remainder.
- A shared remainder rooted in immutable external storage may coexist with cursor advancement. A view into iterator-owned or mutable storage blocks conflicting advancement.

## Current state
- The only `remaining` is `Reader.remaining -> Int` (`Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/StreamHandles.jet:177`).
- There are no `remaining`, `as_slice` or `into_remaining` rows in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet`.
- `ViewIter` exists as a kind (`Collections.jet:139`) but carries no source position fact.
- The capability must stay separate from exact-size, reverse and fused (per #3398, which uses the #3325 facts).
- The finding is at Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f065.

## Changes
1. Jet compiler:
   - `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet`: add `remaining` (Read, returning `View<T>`/`StrView`) and `into_remaining` (Move) rows, gated on a `contiguous_remainder` source fact.
   - Set that fact only for list/View iterators that have not been adapted, and for String/Path iterators. `map`, `filter` and the other adapters clear it.
   - `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Ownership`: provenance ties the remainder view to the source owner, and a live exclusive remainder blocks `&it.next()`.
   - Add codegen and JetEval routes.
2. Host: `JetIter` sources over slices track their position (`jet_iter_remaining`, `jet_iter_offset`) in `Prelude/Core/Collections.rs` and `crates/jet-jit/src/Collections.rs`, plus the Rust mirror.
3. Add the example and the UI fixtures named in the criteria, plus a mixed front/back cell once #3335 lands. If #3335 is not ratified, record that cell as unsupported.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/iter_remaining Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `jet run` and `jet run --interpret` produce empty diffs.
- The UI snapshots pass.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-sema`: this is provenance and loan checking.

## Dependencies
#3315 (a held, resumable cursor). The mixed-end cell of criterion 1 is conditional on #3335, which is deciding.

## Goal
Pin the fixed behavior: a writable, held, user-defined Iterator cursor yields successive items on every tier, an immutable one reports E0202, and a malformed `next` is rejected by sema. Finding: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f066.

## Current state
- Triage 2026-09-28 on jet-debug-snapshot5: probe ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/TriageTypes2b/held.jet (`cur := BagIter{..}; cur.next()` twice) prints `10 20`. held_imm.jet (`cur ::`) reports E0202 `Cannot write to cur ... Fix: Declare cur := ...`. The lowering ICE is gone.
- Examples/features/collections/iter_hook.jet:11-20 has the BagIter Iterator impl but no held-cursor golden.
- Criterion 3 was not probed. Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Registration/Checked.jet:2137 emits E0913 `implementation method ... does not match its trait method`, which is the expected frontend owner.

## Changes
1. Add Examples/features/collections/held_cursor.jet, in new syntax:
```jet
struct BagIter { items: [Int], at: Int }
impl BagIter.Iterator {
    fn next(&self) -> Int? { ... }
}
fn run() {
    cur := BagIter{items: [Int]{10, 20}, at: 0}
    a :: &cur.next()
    b :: &cur.next()
    print("{a ?? 0} {b ?? 0}")
}
```
Add its golden under Examples/features/expected/collections/.
2. Add tests/ui/iter_cursor_immutable_binding.jet (E0202) and tests/ui/iter_impl_bad_next_signature.jet (`fn next(self) -> String`) with snapshots.
3. If the bad-signature fixture reaches codegen or reports anything other than a registered sema diagnostic, fix Registration/Checked.jet so E0913 fires before lowering. The Jet codegen must not rebuild an Iterator identity from the method spelling.

## Proof

- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/iter_cursor_immutable_binding.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` and the same for iter_impl_bad_next_signature.jet pass.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0 if Checked.jet changed.

cards.title: Interleave sources with an explicit end policy
cards.body:
Interleave sources with an explicit end policy.

Alternating/interleaved sources are distinct from concatenation, sorted merge and readiness merge. itertools exposes longest and shortest termination variants.

Add alternating source composition to existing Iter with explicit shortest versus drain-remainder forms.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f067. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-ITER-INTERLEAVE1=A (ratified): alternating composition on `Iter` with an explicit end policy. `a.interleave(b)` drains the longer source after the shorter ends, and `a.interleave_shortest(b)` stops when either source ends. Pulls are left-first and per-source order is kept. Alternation is distinct from `concat`, sorted merge and asynchronous readiness merge, which is a separate Stream operation. No fairness guarantee is attached.

## Current state
- A grep for `interleave` over `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet` and `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude` finds nothing but unrelated comments.
- Existing two-source adapters to copy are `zip`, `zip_short` and `zip_pad` (`Examples/features/collections/zip_family.jet`; JIT `jet_jit_iter_zip_family`, `crates/jet-jit/src/Collections.rs:11573`).
- The shared mechanism reuses canonical Iter source composition, held positions, the failure carrier, fused normalization only when declared, and borrowed-remainder handling. Non-fused behaviour is not silently normalized.
- The finding is `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f067` (the card cites the stale `docs/` path).

## Changes
1. Jet compiler, in `Collections.jet`:
   - Add `interleave` and `interleave_shortest` rows: arity 1 with an argument of the same element type, result `Iter<T>` via `sema_collection_output_iter`, iter receiver moved.
   - Add `TBuiltinOp.Interleave(shortest: Bool)` in `TIR.jet`, routed in `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/BuiltinMethods.jet` next to `.Intersperse` (`:575`).
2. Host mirror:
   - `crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs` and the TIR lowering and routes.
   - Prelude `jet_iter_interleave(a, b, shortest)`: an explicit turn flag; after one side ends, either drain the other or stop without probing the other side again. Source failure propagates in pull order.
   - The JIT row and the MIREval arm.
3. Docs: `Docs/spec/reference/core-library.md`, stating the exact pull trace for empty, non-fused and failing sources.

## Proof
- New `Examples/features/collections/interleave.jet`. With `[1,3,5]` and `[2,4]` it prints `1,2,3,4,5` (drain) and `1,2,3,4` (shortest). It also covers an empty left source, a source that fails on its second pull (pull trace printed), and a `by_ref`-borrowed remainder still readable afterwards once #3317 lands.
  - `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/interleave.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
  - `JET_1216_STEM=collections/interleave Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev_tier_parity collections_memory_and_streams_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot` passes.

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime` (iter-adapter cluster).

## Dependencies
None. The borrowed-remainder row relies on #3317's `by_ref`; until that lands it is recorded as pending.

cards.title: Investigate sort-key evaluation and stable versus unstable tradeoffs
cards.body:
Investigate sort-key evaluation and stable versus unstable tradeoffs.

The selected sorted_by_cached_key and unstable variants expose useful cost/ordering questions, but current capture lacks full per-method guarantees and no measurements ran.

Compare existing Jet sort/key/comparator contracts and the approved top-k/statistics work before adding spellings.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f068. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Pin down the existing sort-key contract before anyone adds a `sorted_by_cached_key`, unstable or ThenBy variant. The contract covers stability, key-callback count and order, failure order, and descending and secondary keys. It also shows how the existing compound-comparator composition expresses each case.

## Current state
- `sort_by` works by key, by comparator (`TClosureOp.SortByCompare`) or fallibly (`TrySortBy`). `sort_by_desc`, `min_by` and `max_by` also exist (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:242-243,406-410,854-858,870-871`).
- `sort_by` is List-only with write access, so it sorts in place.
- LAST-tie extrema are pinned by #2298 (done) and covered by `Examples/features/collections/max_by_tie.jet`.
- `Examples/features/collections/sort_by_key.jet` exists but prints no callback counts. No cached-key or unstable variant exists.
- The finding is at Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f068.

## Changes
1. Add `Examples/features/collections/sort_key_contract.jet` and its `.out` with these cells:
   - (a) stable order: records with equal keys keep their input order;
   - (b) a key function that prints each call, so the golden records the exact number and order of calls for a five-element list;
   - (c) a fallible key through `sort_by` returning `Result`, failing on the third key, with the list state printed afterwards;
   - (d) a descending primary key plus an ascending secondary key through one comparator closure returning `Ordering`, keeping the stable primary groups;
   - (e) `max_by` LAST tie next to stable sort, printed separately.
2. Record the observed callback count on the card. If it varies between tiers, fix the kernel (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs` `jet_list_sort_by*`, and the Jet route in `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/ClosureMethods.jet`) so all tiers agree.
3. Any cached-key or unstable API needs a matched performance pair registered in `Tools/gauntlet/measurement-manifest.json` `performance_surface_pairs` before an owner ballot. None is proposed here.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/sort_key_contract Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `jet run` and `jet run --interpret` of the example, diffed against the `.out`, produce empty diffs. The key-count lines are identical across all three tiers.

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime`: an existing-kernel tier-parity proof.

## Dependencies
None.

1. Stable order and LAST extrema ties remain separate policies.
2. Count key callback evaluations and preserve effect/failure order; caching is not assumed safe for an effectful callback.
3. If a new API only improves performance, provide matched evidence before an owner ballot; otherwise document the existing composition.
4. Secondary and descending keys preserve stable primary groups; use an existing compound comparator before adding ThenBy aliases.

cards.title: Provide Cartesian product sources without implicit replay of resources
cards.body:
Provide Cartesian product sources without implicit replay of resources.

C++ views and itertools/Python products supply parameter-grid traversal. Nested generators can express some cases but task-backed generators may have different borrowing/cost properties.

Add a Cartesian source on existing Iter with explicit replay eligibility for the reused dimensions.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f069. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Provide a lazy Cartesian product source on Iter whose reused dimensions must be replayable, or materialized explicitly. Written for option A of D-ITER-CARTESIAN1 (open ballot attached to this card): `cartesian(other)` plus a finite-dimension `product` constructor, rightmost dimension fastest. Finding: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f069.

## Current state
- Core/math/combinatorics.jet:38-61 has only eager `product(items: [Int], repeat)` and `cartesian(left, right) -> [[Int]]`, both over Int lists.
- There is no lazy product on Iter in Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet.

## Changes
1. JetFoundation Collections.jet: register `cartesian` on Iter/List (arity 1) with output `Iter<(A, B)>`, plus a k-dimension `Iter.product([...])` constructor. Only the leftmost dimension may be one-shot (Iter/Stream). Every reused dimension must be a replayable source (List, FixedList, View, Range) or an explicit `.to_list()`.
2. JetSema: reject a one-shot reused dimension with a new registered diagnostic (row in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Diagnostics.jet, regenerate Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet with `node Compiler/Bootstrap/generate-diagnostic-rows.mjs`). The fix text is `call .to_list() on it`. Borrowed View dimensions yield borrowed items under the existing view-loan rules.
3. JetCodegen lowering and the retained host adapter in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs (odometer over replayable dimensions, no hidden cache), with the JIT twin.
4. Core/math/combinatorics.jet keeps its eager Int helpers, or they are removed in the same cutover if the ballot says so.
5. Mirror typing in stage-zero Rust only as far as the shipped `jet` needs to run the golden.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/cartesian cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes. `jet run --interpret` on the same file matches.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/cartesian_one_shot_dimension.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: checked collection surface plus a new sema rejection.

## Dependencies
Owner ballot D-ITER-CARTESIAN1 (recommendation A). With B, record the finding and close.

cards.body:
Choose Rayon reuse without silently adding another scheduler.

Rayon1.12 indexed/parallel contracts are useful evidence, but a separate worker pool is not automatically compatible with Jet task ownership and cancellation.

Decide whether to retain existing para_* implementation, evaluate an internal bridge that satisfies existing scheduler law, or explicitly amend that law for optional native integration.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f071. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Close the Rayon reuse choice under ratified D-ITER-RAYONDEP1=A ("keep stock implementation independent"). No Jet parallel iteration may run on a hidden Rayon pool, and capture and cancellation law stays with the `para_*` cards.

**Current state**
- D-ITER-RAYONDEP1=A is ratified. No workspace manifest names rayon.
- The `para_*` family runs on `std::thread::scope` (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/ParallelKernel.rs:68,103`) with measured planning (`ParallelPlan.rs:694-698,1351-1353`).
- **Correction to the triage:** `Cargo.lock:2139` does contain rayon 1.12.0. It enters transitively through wasmtime 25 (`Cargo.lock:3067`), whose default `parallel-compilation` feature compiles guest components. wasmtime is pulled in by `crates/jet-jit/Cargo.toml:43` and `crates/jetpack-bin/Cargo.toml:16` (`features = ["component-model"]`, default features on). That pool compiles guest wasm and never runs Jet user work, so it is outside criteria 1-2's `para_*` scope. The "count = 0" proof in the triage is wrong.
- Capture and cancellation law is owned by #2922, #3672 and #3344.

**Changes**
1. Record in the card log that `para_*` is Rayon-free, citing file:line.
2. Record the wasmtime transitive rayon with exact provenance as a host compile-time detail outside D-ITER-RAYONDEP1. If Main wants the stricter reading ("no hidden pool anywhere in `jet`"), set `default-features = false` on both wasmtime entries and re-add the needed features (at least `cranelift`, `component-model`, `runtime`). Prove it with `cargo tree -i rayon -p jet-jit`, which must report nothing, and a sandbox golden such as `packages/sandbox_mathkit`.
3. Close criteria 1-3 as moot under outcome A and point them at #2922, #3672 and #3344.

**Proof**
- `rg -n '^\s*rayon' Cargo.toml crates/*/Cargo.toml` finds no match.
- `rg -n 'rayon' crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude` finds no match.
- `Cargo.lock` shows rayon only under wasmtime.

**Batch**
`batch-measure`: evidence closure. The optional feature trim would move to `batch-host-runtime`.

**Dependencies**
None.

cards.body:
Choose tokio-stream leverage without an accidental Tokio runtime dependency.

tokio-stream0.1.19 wraps concrete channels/timers/sockets/filesystem resources and has a different StreamExt set from futures. Its wrapper names alone do not justify another runtime.

Decide whether existing resource+Stream adapters should remain native or gain an explicitly scoped foreign Tokio bridge.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f073. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
**Goal.** Close ITER-F073 (research: `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f073`) under the ratified D-ITER-TOKIODEP1=A. Channel, timer and reader streams stay native, each with its own wait/end/error contract. There is no second Tokio runtime, hidden task authority or duplicate resource ownership. A future foreign bridge must bind at the existing readiness/error/cancel boundary.

**Current state.**
- D-ITER-TOKIODEP1=A is ratified. The #3396 handoff says not to reopen it.
- `Cargo.lock` has no `tokio` package, as checked.
- Native sources:
  - `Core/tasks/tasks.jet:118` `interval(period) -[Time]> Receiver<Int>` and `after` (:114)
  - `channel<T>(n)` with sender close
  - `files.open(path).lines()`
- The witness `Examples/features/concurrency/native_resource_streams.jet` (49 lines) is in the working tree, uncommitted and in flight. It covers:
  - a channel producer that closes, so the loop ends
  - `tasks.interval(1ms)` bounded by the consumer, since it never ends
  - a file reader counting lines and surfacing a typed `IOError` for a missing path

  It has no `Examples/features/expected/concurrency/native_resource_streams.out` yet.

**Changes.**
1. Finish the in-flight witness. Replace the hard-coded `/tmp` path with `files.temp_dir("jet_native_streams")` so the golden is hermetic. Add the golden `.out`.
2. c3 needs no dependency ballot: under option A nothing is adopted. Record on the card that the dependency features, target support, binary/cost impact and cancellation limits of tokio-stream 0.1.19 would apply only to a future bridge proposal.
3. Record the supported, unsupported and unknown cells on the card:
   - channel end
   - timer unbounded
   - reader error
   - cancellation of an in-progress `interval` loop through the task group (covered by `task.group` exit)

**Proof.** The command in add_criteria.

**Batch.** `batch-core-tasks`: a tasks/channels witness golden, retested in the tasks pass. No code change is expected.

**Dependencies.** None.
cards.checkSteps:
1. A channel, timer and fallible reader prototype preserve source-specific wait/end/error contracts.

cards.title: Add demanded separator factories while preserving existing intersperse
cards.body:
Add demanded separator factories while preserving existing intersperse.

Jet already documents intersperse. The distinct captured candidate is intersperse_with: a separator factory can have effects or fail. Existing constant insertion also needs demand proof under F008.

Add a separator-factory sibling to existing stock Iter and retain the existing constant form. Ratify factory timing only; do not re-ballot basic intersperse.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f074. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-ITER-SEPARATOR1=A (ratified): `intersperse_with(factory)` next to the existing constant `intersperse`. The factory runs only at demanded boundaries, meaning after the adapter knows another source item exists. Each call creates a distinct owned value, and the factory owns its failure. The constant form keeps the lawful repeated-ownership requirement. Only factory timing is ratified here; basic `intersperse` is not re-balloted.

## Current state
- Only the constant form exists. It has arity 1 and a separator of the element type (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:270-273`, `:414`, `:627`, `:665`), with op `TBuiltinOp.Intersperse` (`:890`). Codegen routes it at `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/BuiltinMethods.jet:474,575`.
- The runtime clones one separator: `jet_iter_intersperse<T: Clone>` and `jet_list_intersperse<T: Clone>` (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs:941,2314`). The JIT row is `crates/jet-jit/src/Collections.rs:11572`.
- `intersperse_with` appears only in `Docs/spec/reference/surfaces/rust-surface.json:290`.
- The existing constant form also needs the F008 demand proof.
- The finding is `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f074` (the card cites the stale `docs/` path).

## Changes
1. Jet compiler:
   - `Collections.jet`: add `intersperse_with` with arity 1, argument type `Fn() -> T` (a fallible factory keeps its failure effect) and result `Iter<T>`.
   - Add `TClosureOp.IntersperseWith` in `TIR.jet`, with its route in `ClosureMethods.jet`.
2. Host mirror:
   - `crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs` and the TIR lowering and routes.
   - Prelude `jet_iter_intersperse_with`, which reuses the existing adapter's one-item lookahead: no factory call before the first item or after the last, and a pending source item is kept across a factory failure. No eager separator allocation.
   - The JIT row and the MIREval arm.
3. Docs: `Docs/spec/reference/core-library.md:308-312` lists the family, and says the constant form requires a clonable separator.

## Proof
- New `Examples/features/collections/intersperse_with.jet`. It shows:
  - empty and singleton sources emitting no separators, with the factory count printed as 0;
  - `take(3)` over `[a,b,c]` running the factory once;
  - a factory that increments a counter and returns distinct values;
  - a factory that fails on its second call, with the pending item still observable.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/intersperse_with.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `JET_1216_STEM=collections/intersperse_with Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev_tier_parity collections_memory_and_streams_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot` passes.

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime` (iter-adapter cluster).

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: Investigate minimum-length padding without truncating long input
cards.body:
Investigate minimum-length padding without truncating long input.

pad_using differs from take(n) after chaining fillers: it must preserve an input already longer than the requested minimum. Exact peer factory timing needs a focused contract read.

Prove the job with existing source/generator mechanisms and bounded demand before selecting any new helper.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f075. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Show that minimum-length padding (`pad_using`) can be built from existing mechanisms: short input gains only the missing positions, long input is never truncated, and factory indices, failure and early stop are exact. Add no helper and no silent default filler.

## Current state
- No `pad_using` exists.
- These building blocks exist:
  - `take`, `repeat`, `cycle` and `concat` (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:257,270,627`);
  - `indexed` (`:635`);
  - the zip family including a pad policy (`Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Expressions/Zip.jet:100-160`);
  - Stream generators (`Examples/features/streams/generators.jet:14-20`).
- `cycle(n)` and `repeat(n)` materialize their input (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs:2684-2702`).
- The finding is at Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f075.

## Changes
1. Add `Examples/features/collections/pad_minimum.jet` and its `.out`. A generator `fn pad_min(items: Stream<Int>, min: Int, fill: (Int) -> Int) -> Stream<Int>` yields each input item and counts it, then yields `fill(i)` for each index `i` from the count up to `min`. Cells:
   - (a) `[1,2]` with min 5: the filler runs for indices 2, 3 and 4 only, and prints each index;
   - (b) `[1..7]` with min 3: all seven items come through untouched and the filler never runs;
   - (c) early stop: `take(3)` on (a) shows the filler ran for index 2 only;
   - (d) a fallible filler failing at index 3 propagates the error after items 1, 2 and filler(2);
   - (e) the same job through `zip` with the pad policy, if it expresses it, printed side by side.
2. Record on the card that the composition exists. Any stock helper is a separate ballot.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/pad_minimum Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `jet run` and `jet run --interpret` of the example, diffed against `Examples/features/expected/collections/pad_minimum.out`, produce empty diffs.

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime`: an example-only three-tier proof.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: Investigate alternate-association folds separately from left folds
cards.body:
Investigate alternate-association folds separately from left folds.

tree_reduce/tree_fold1 and parallel reductions may change association. Floating values, error order and tree-building results can therefore differ from a left fold.

Capture exact peer association contracts and compare existing fold/parallel laws before proposing a tree-fold API.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f076. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove the association law of every existing reduction path: `fold` and `reduce` are left folds, Float `sum` and add-fold use the D-FRED1=A fixed lane tree, and `para_fold` may reassociate. Show that no compiler path reassociates an ordinary `reduce` for speed. Add no tree-fold API.

## Current state
- `reduce` and `fold` are left-fold closure operations (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:245-246,859-862`).
- Float `sum` and scalar add-fold use the eight-lane fixed tree (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs:205-221`; `FloatAddFold` in `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/ClosureMethods.jet:153-157`).
- `para_fold` and `FloatAddParaFold` route to `jet_list_para_fold*` (`ClosureMethods.jet:158-166`).
- The finding is at Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f076.

## Changes
1. Add `Examples/features/collections/fold_association.jet` and its `.out` with these cells:
   - (a) a String tree-building reducer `(a, b) -> "({a}{b})"` over `["a","b","c","d"]` through `reduce` and `fold`, which must print `(((ab)c)d)`;
   - (b) non-associative Int subtraction through `fold`;
   - (c) an empty and a singleton `reduce` (absent value, then the item itself);
   - (d) a fallible reducer failing on the third item, showing that items 1 and 2 were combined first;
   - (e) Float `sum` over values chosen so that left-fold and lane-tree results differ, with a comment citing D-FRED1=A;
   - (f) `para_fold` with the String reducer, printing its grouping only if it is deterministic by contract. Otherwise print a canonicalized result and state that the grouping is unspecified.
2. Where the Float fast path could fire, check that `fold` with a non-add closure never picks `FloatAddFold`. If it does, fix the selection in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet` operation selection, then in its Rust mirror.
3. A tree-fold API or an opt-in association policy needs its own ballot. It is not proposed here.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/fold_association Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `jet run` and `jet run --interpret` of the example, diffed against `Examples/features/expected/collections/fold_association.out`, produce empty diffs.

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime`: parity across the existing reduction kernels.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: Investigate shuffle and sampling with explicit random state
cards.body:
Investigate shuffle and sampling with explicit random state.

Jet already documents shuffle with a fixed demo seed and directs users to Rng for real shuffling. The .NET candidate is not evidence of a missing shuffle method. Explicit random-state and streaming/sample behavior still require proof.

Verify the existing shuffle/Rng contract and distinguish full permutation from bounded sampling. Keep any proposed default change owner-gated after exact source/probe evidence.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f078. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove bounded sampling with an explicit random state, keeping it separate from full-permutation shuffle. That shuffle half belongs to #3392 under D-ITER-RNG1=A. Seed ownership and replay must be explicit, and endless input can never yield a 'final' full shuffle.

## Current state
- `Core/math/random.jet:176` `shuffle(items: &[Int]) -[Rand]>` (Fisher–Yates), :192 `sample(items, n)`, :253 `choice` and :258 `choices` all use the ambient `-[Rand]` source and are monomorphic `[Int]`. The explicit `Rng` (seeded, split) is at :45-105.
- `Core/data/sketch/reservoir.jet:26` `add(res, item, rand: Int)` takes caller-supplied randomness, and :52 `sample(res)` is a bounded reservoir over `String`.
- The demo LCG `jet_iter_shuffle` (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs:2714-2717`, seed 0xC0FFEE42) is retired by #3392.
- The finding is at `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f078`.

## Changes
1. Add `Examples/features/math/random_sampling.jet` with a golden. It covers a seeded `Rng` sample of k from n with replay (same seed gives the same output, successive draws advance), `split` independence, and a reservoir over a bounded `loop` source of 10,000 items feeding `reservoir.add` with `rng.int` draws. It also shows that an unbounded source must be bounded by an explicit `take_n` before a full shuffle.
2. Record cells for: ambient `-[Rand]` versus explicit `Rng`, `[Int]`-only monomorphism, and reservoir `String`-only. Each gap becomes an owner gate (generic sample, `Rng.sample`), with no silent default change.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=math/random_sampling Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run Examples/features/math/random_sampling.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/math/random_sampling.out` and the `--interpret` form both diff empty, so seed replay holds on every tier.

## Batch

## Dependencies
#3392 (explicit random-state owner for shuffle).

cards.title: Prove typed selection without importing unchecked runtime casts
cards.body:
Prove typed selection without importing unchecked runtime casts.

LINQ Cast/OfType and Python dynamic filtering address heterogeneous sources. Jet should use its existing tagged/typed/foreign-value contracts rather than inherit runtime casting by name.

Demonstrate tagged-case selection and checked foreign downcast, with the enum/type owners, before deciding any helper is missing.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f079. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Show that Jet's typed selection (tagged-case patterns plus `filter_map` over fallible callbacks) covers the LINQ `OfType`/`Cast` and dynamic-filter jobs without runtime casts, and classify checked foreign downcast as absent rather than inventing it.

**Current state**
- Tagged-case selection is ordinary pattern matching (`if v == { .Case(x) -> … }`, `loop … ->`). Pattern sema is in Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Patterns.jet, and the examples are Examples/features/patterns/{list_destructure,refutable_test_bind,struct_destructure}.jet.
- `filter_map`: Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Collections.jet:84-91 accepts only a `Result` callback (E0108 otherwise), and Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:607-613 maps the success type, unwrapping an inner Option. The iterator builtins are at :864-867.
- No downcast, `try_as` or `as?` exists anywhere in Core, Compiler/JetSema or Examples.

**Changes**
1. Add Examples/features/patterns/typed_selection.jet over `enum Shape { Circle(r: Float) Rect(w: Float, h: Float) Label(text: String) }`. It covers (a) selection by `loop s in shapes -> if s == { .Circle(r) -> … else -> {} }` (drop), (b) `shapes.filter_map((s) -> if s == { .Circle(r) -> Ok(r) else -> Err("skip") })` (drop failures), (c) propagating the first rejection with `?`-style early return (propagate), and (d) a borrowed loop that reads `.Label(text)` without copying (the loan is kept). Each row prints its keep, drop or propagate verdict.
2. Add tests/ui/typed_selection_payload_escape.jet, where a borrowed `.Label(text)` payload escapes the loop and hits the existing loan diagnostic, plus its snapshot (criterion 1).
3. Record foreign downcast as an absent capability. Polyglot and FFI values arrive through typed binders, so there is no erased value to downcast. Add no RTTI or erasure feature (criterion 3). Any later helper (for example, an `of_case` adapter) needs its own ballot.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=patterns/typed_selection Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: passes.
- `for m in --release '' --interpret; do Tools/agent/jet-env jet run $m Examples/features/patterns/typed_selection.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/patterns/typed_selection.out; done`: empty.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=typed_selection_payload_escape Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`: the snapshot matches.

**Batch**
batch-jetc-sema: pattern, loan and filter_map checking are sema facts. Any defect the example exposes is fixed there.

**Dependencies**
None.

cards.title: Provide keyed lazy set operations without a second collection model
cards.body:
Provide keyed lazy set operations without a second collection model.

LINQ UnionBy/IntersectBy/ExceptBy and Rust set iterators expose set algebra over sources. Adjacent dedup does not supply cross-source membership behavior.

Add keyed lazy set operations using existing Set equality/hash policy and explicit finite-side requirements.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f080. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-ITER-SETOPS1=A (ratified). Add `union_by`, `intersection_by` and `difference_by` on the stock `Iter`, reusing the existing Set eligibility, equality and hash policy. There is no iterator hasher and no second collection model. Source: ITER-F080.

## Current state
- Set algebra exists only eagerly:
  - Set/Rank `union`, `intersection` and `difference` at `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:151,158,469,507,728-731`.
  - List `union`/`intersection`/`difference` at `:270,415,911-913`.
- There is no `union_by`/`intersection_by`/`difference_by` in `Compiler/` or `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude`. Triage named them `intersect_by`/`except_by`, but the ratified spelling is `intersection_by`/`difference_by`.
- The ratified contract:
  - Union emits first occurrences from the left, then right items not yet seen.
  - Intersection and difference first build the finite right-side key set, then emit at most the first left representative per key, in left order.
  - An infinite or failing right side prevents the first output, and the plan does not hide that boundary.
  - Each source keeps its own errors and ownership. No mutable indexed keys.
- #3398 handoff: use #3325's operation facts. Keep this card's encounter order, key identity and collection-state contract.

## Changes
1. **JetFoundation.** In `Collections.jet`, add arity rows for the three methods: arg 0 is `Iter<T>`, arg 1 is a key callable `T -> K`. Callback param typing, output `Iter<T>` and `TClosureOp.UnionBy`/`IntersectionBy`/`DifferenceBy` go at the existing closure-method sites (`:239-241,388-411,627,865-868`).
2. **JetSema.** Require `K` to satisfy the existing Set key eligibility (reuse the Set element check). The key callable follows the existing callable effect rules.
3. **JetCodegen.** In `ClosureMethods.jet`, route to `core.iter` `union_by`/`intersection_by`/`difference_by`, which map to `jet_iter_*_by`.
4. **JetEval.** Implement the same lazy semantics.
5. **Retained host.**
   - Prelude `Collections.rs` and `.js` use a `HashSet<K>` for seen keys. Union streams lazily; intersection and difference drain the right side on first demand.
   - Add the `MIREval` route and the Rust bootstrap sema mirror.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/iter_set_ops cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: pass.
- `JET_THREE_WAY_STEM=collections/iter_set_ops cargo test --test dev_corpus cranelift_three_way_differential_battery`: tiers agree.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/set cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: eager Set operations are unchanged.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: exit 0.

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime`: new Prelude lazy adapters with three-tier parity, batched with the core-iter-adapter cards.

## Dependencies
None blocking. #3325 (planning) owns the shared operation-fact contract. Reuse its facts if they have landed; otherwise use the existing closure-route facts and do not wait for it.

3. Second-source error, unbounded membership side and early output stop have explicit outcomes.
4. Borrowed and owned results preserve provenance and cannot mutate keys while indexed.

cards.plan:
## Goal
Finish the retired `.view(range)` cutover (D-DYNARRAY1 followed by the bracket-range place rule). The public entry is `values[range]`, `&values[range]` or `~values[range]` (no-copy, write and copy respectively). Every reachable `.view(...)` is rejected with the teaching diagnostic, and no retired alias stays in a lookup table.

## Current state
- Law: `Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:562-566` retires `.view(a..b)`.
- The Rust bootstrap rejects it: E0214 "`.view(a..b)` is now a bare range place" in `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/calls/method_calls.rs:1214-1218`. The UI fixture `tests/ui/view_method_retired_e0214.{jet,stderr}` passes on the shipped binary.

The E0214 intercept makes it unreachable from source. It is a retained alias row that criterion 2 asks us to classify.
- The Jet compiler has the E0214 registry row (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet`, code "E0214") but no emission site in `Compiler/JetSema` or `Compiler/JetParser`. On the Jet path, `.view(range)` falls through to a generic unknown-method error, and the retired spelling is not taught.

## Changes
1. `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Collections.jet`: before ordinary method lookup on List, String, fixed-list and View receivers, a `view` call with a range argument emits E0214 using the registry text, with a machine fix rewriting `x.view(a..b)` to `x[a..b]`. Place checks are unchanged.
2. Remove the unreachable `("view", 2)` row from `crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs`, since it is a retired public alias. The UI fixture proves E0214 still fires first. Record in the card log that no internal metadata name depended on it.

cards.title: Use one explicit random-state owner for sequence shuffling
cards.body:
Use one explicit random-state owner for sequence shuffling.

The captured Iter shuffle materializes a List and resets a private demo LCG each call, while Rng.shuffle already uses the seeded handle kernel. This is source evidence, not an observed random sequence.

Retire the demo-only List/Iter shuffle route in favor of the existing explicit Rng.shuffle operation, subject to a distinct owner choice.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f082. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-ITER-RNG1=A (ratified). Retire the zero-argument List/Iter `shuffle()` and its private demo LCG. The one random-state owner is `random.rng(seed)` with `rng.shuffle(&list)`. A finite source is collected explicitly before an in-place shuffle. No ambient entropy, no cryptographic claim, no second Rng. Source: ITER-F082.

## Current state
- The demo route is still live:
  - `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:263-264` (arity), `:627` (Iter output), `:818` (`ListShuffle`) and `:920` (`IterShuffle`).
  - `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/BuiltinMethods.jet:579` routes to `jet_iter_shuffle`.
  - The runtime is `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs:2714-2717`, a fixed `0xC0FF_EE42` LCG. Its copies are in `crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Builtins.rs:2061` and `CollectionEval.rs:985`.
- The explicit path exists: `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/TimeHandles.jet:199-245` (`rng.shuffle(&items)` with E0202 for a missing `&`), `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/HandleMethods.jet:1082` (`jet_rng_shuffle`) and `Core/math/random.jet:176`.
- Callers: `Examples/features/collections/iter_adapters.jet:77-78` (`nums.lazy().shuffle()`).
- The same LCG also serves `Set.shuffle()` (`Collections.rs:626-627`, `BuiltinMethods.jet:158-161`), which is ratified under D-SET-DECLINE1 and used at `Examples/features/collections/set.jet:77`, and `List.random()` (`Collections.rs:2892`). D-ITER-RNG1 names only List/Iter.

## Changes
1. **JetFoundation and JetSema.** Delete the List/Iter `shuffle` rows (`:263-264,627,818,920`) and the `ListShuffle`/`IterShuffle` ops. A call now gets one registered error pointing at `random.rng(seed)` / `rng.shuffle(&items)`, with no alias.
2. **JetCodegen and JetEval.** Remove the `iter_shuffle` route and any evaluator case.
3. **Retained host.** Delete `jet_iter_shuffle` from the Prelude `Collections.rs`/`.js` and the comptime copies, and mirror the removal in the Rust bootstrap sema.
4. **Callers.** Migrate `iter_adapters.jet` and its `.out`, and every other caller found by `grep '\.shuffle()'`. Update `Docs/spec/reference/core-library.md` where it lists List/Iter shuffle.
5. **Set.shuffle and List.random.** They are ratified separately and out of this decision's scope. Keep their surface. They need a private deterministic helper, or their own owner ballot to take an Rng. Raise this to Main; do not change them silently.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/iter_adapters cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: pass.
- `JET_THREE_WAY_STEM=collections/iter_adapters cargo test --test dev_corpus cranelift_three_way_differential_battery`: tiers agree.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/list_shuffle_retired.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`: the error is registered.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/set cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: unchanged.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: exit 0.

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime`: Prelude route removal and a golden migration, batched with the core-iter-adapter cards.

## Dependencies
None. D-ITER-RNG1 is ratified A. The Set.shuffle/List.random question is a follow-up, not a blocker.

cards.title: Collect explicit borrowed results without the default read-view copy
cards.body:
Collect explicit borrowed results without the default read-view copy.

D-MEM-COPYSEM1 makes ordinary read-view storage a semantic copy. The selected top-k prototype separately preserves explicit borrowed [View<T>] results. Generic borrowed iterator collection needs the same explicit ownership choice, not an assumed no-copy to_list.

Add an explicit borrowed materializer through existing View and aggregate-provenance rules while preserving ordinary to_list semantics.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f083. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Add one explicit borrowed materializer for Iter that returns `[View<T>]` (view headers only, source owners kept live), while `to_list` keeps the D-MEM-COPYSEM1 semantic copy. Written for option A of D-ITER-VIEWCOLLECT1 (open ballot). Finding: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f083.

## Current state
- Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:7-9,122-125: ViewIter/View kinds exist. There is no borrowed materializer; `to_list` copies read-view items (D-MEM-COPYSEM1).
- The selected top-k prototype already preserves explicit `[View<T>]` results; this generalizes it.

## Changes
1. JetFoundation Collections.jet: on ViewIter receivers only, register `to_views()` (name per the ballot's option A) returning `[View<T>]`.
2. JetSema/Sema/Ownership: the result's provenance is the union of the source owners. Items that are not rooted in live external storage (a `.map` temporary) are rejected with a registered code. Mutation, reorder or resize of a source while the result is live is rejected across wrappers and returned aggregates, using the existing aggregate-provenance rules. ViewMut collection needs the existing disjointness proof and is otherwise rejected.
3. JetCodegen lowering stores view headers in normal List storage, with no payload copy; mirror in the retained host Prelude Collections.rs.
4. Default `to_list` is unchanged.
5. Mirror typing in stage-zero Rust only as far as the shipped `jet` needs for the golden.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/borrowed_collect cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes. `jet run --interpret` matches.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/view_collect_temporary.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`, and the same for view_collect_mutation.jet.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: ownership/provenance checking is the substance.

## Dependencies
Owner ballot D-ITER-VIEWCOLLECT1 (recommendation A). Builds on #3318's loan machinery (same batch).

cards.title: Copy capable iterator progress through the existing copy spelling
cards.body:
Copy capable iterator progress through the existing copy spelling.

Stable concrete iterator types have118 Clone rows, while &mut I is explicitly not Clone. Copying a cursor is distinct from repeating its outputs, buffering tee branches, or copying every yielded payload.

Extend the existing explicit copy operation to sources whose iterator-state copy contract is lawful; preserve consume-once ownership of each resulting cursor.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f084. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-ITER-COPY1=A: the existing explicit copy `~it` copies lawful iterator cursor state, meaning the position plus the declared captured state. Each copy is then consumed once and advances independently. Copying does not tee or buffer output, and it does not clone every payload. Shared external state stays shared. Exclusive `by_ref` loans and one-shot resource sources (Stream, file lines, channels) are not copyable.

## Current state
- `copy` exists only on Set, Bits and List (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:149,167,231`). There is no `~` on Iter kinds.
- The runtime `JetIter<T>(Box<dyn Iterator<Item = T>>)` (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs:1304`) cannot be cloned.
- There is no built-in `next` yet (#3315).
- The finding is at Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f084. This card feeds #3350 (fork investigation) and #3316 (lazy cycle replay).

## Changes
1. Jet compiler, in `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema` copy capability checking:
   - An `Iter`/`ViewIter` type is copyable only when its source-kind fact is replayable (a List/View slice, a range, or a lazy chain whose adapters capture only copyable state).
   - Stream, Reader, file/dir lines, channel receivers and `by_ref` projections are ineligible. They get the existing not-copyable diagnostic, with the iterator reason in the note.
   - `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet`: record the replayable fact per producer and adapter.
   - Add the `Compiler/JetCodegen` copy lowering for Iter.
2. Host:
   - `JetIter` gains an optional clone hook: store `Box<dyn JetCloneIter<T>>` for replayable sources, so `jet_iter_copy` clones the state, not the collected output.
   - Update `crates/jet-jit/src/Collections.rs`, plus the Rust mirror.
   - Assignment from `~a` gives clone_from value semantics with no alias. Storage reuse is out of scope for this card.
3. Add the example and UI fixtures named in the criteria. Add an effectful-map cell showing that a copy does not rerun earlier callbacks, and a shared-external-state cell (a map closure reading a mutated `Cell`) that states future values may differ.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/iter_copy Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `jet run` and `jet run --interpret` produce empty diffs.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/iter_copy_one_shot.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-sema`: the copy-capability check is the core of the change.

## Dependencies
#3315 (without `next` there is no advanced cursor to copy).

4. Assignment from an explicit copy supplies clone_from value semantics without adding an alias; possible storage reuse is measured separately.

cards.body:
# Ballot and design streamlining — 2026-09-12

This preparation follows #3070 and the owner’s new request. It reviews the 102 decisions answered A at intake, plus the three ready unanswered ballots. The other 19 unanswered drafts retain their performance gates. No compiler, runtime, SDK or dependency implementation is claimed.

## Published owner-facing changes

- D-ENUM-CASEVALUES1 on #3132 now recommends T.@values as ordinary compile-time [T#N] data. It shares checked enum rows with reflection, but is not an erased description or a mutable cursor. B keeps lists; C exposes the original cases() iterator alternative.
- D-ITER-SIZE1 on #3317 now recommends one runtime size_hint() pair. Equal lower/upper bounds mean exact size. ExactRemaining, remaining_len(), and a runtime @remaining reader are not proposed.
- D-ENUM-CONSTRUCTORCALL1 on #3161 now demonstrates a real higher-order helper and payload result. It permits only signatures ordinary function types can preserve, including labels, ownership, effects and provenance.
- qgu3pklf and qjya7u03 are answered with links to their published revisions. The ballots remain owner choices; answering a question did not select an option.
- D-NEST-UPSTREAM1 on #3397 is one successor choice covering sixteen answered decisions and eight first-party package commitments. Fifteen affected implementation cards retain their prior blockers and also wait on #3397.

## Recommendation: fewer shared mechanisms, not fewer meanings

### Codecs and structured data

Use one checked set of field, variant, wire-name, default and validation facts. Derive schema, typed encode/decode and typed-update plans from it. Keep custom codec precedence and visibility intact.

Use DataTree where a dynamic tree is actually required. Do not force every typed or streaming operation to allocate a whole tree. An eligible derived codec can use a direct reader/writer plan when the same checked facts prove equivalent behavior. Custom codec bodies cannot be bypassed by guessing their schema.

Share limits, path errors, traversal and ordinary ownership. Keep Pointer, Patch, Merge Patch, Diff, Merge Diff, typed update and JMESPath distinct: they have different mutation, null, failure and representability contracts. Native binary-format values stay in their format owner rather than widening every dynamic tree.

### Commands and application metadata

Use the checked command schema for parsing, help, completion, prompts, ReST, YAML, Markdown and man output. A shared projection owns visibility, defaults, ordering and secret suppression. Each renderer owns its escaping and output-specific rules. Generating documentation must not execute a handler.

Feed the checked App HTTP operation graph into the existing OpenAPI renderer. Do not create an App-to-router conversion or a second schema store. Explicit foreign protocol mappings may consume those facts, but reflection does not expose every method as a network endpoint.

### Enums, reflection and constructors

Keep one checked enum declaration owner for matching, discriminants, ingress conversion, wire names, aliases, unknown-case handling and reflection. The enum value catalog and case descriptions ask different questions over those same rows.

Use ordinary function values for eligible constructors. Do not add Constructor<T>, an enum factory protocol or reflection-based invocation. Use compile-time derives when the type is known. Reserve erased runtime Value inspection for jobs that genuinely need it.

Preserve D-ENUM-CASEMETA1’s complete-or-refuse visibility and transitive value-copy rules. Replacing snapshots with borrowed views would change that answered contract; this pass does not do it.

### Iterators, resources and tools

Keep one Iterator/Iterable protocol and one adapter vocabulary. Reuse ordinary read/move/write conventions, views, result/optional values, destination construction and task authority. Do not add TryIter, ExactRemaining or dependency-specific iterator families.

Carry lawful progress, cardinality, permanent-end, loan and effect facts internally. Live remaining size is runtime state. Empty is not closed, Pending is not end, stop is not cancel, and failure is not absence. Required buffering and finite-source assumptions stay visible.

Use the existing semantic index, diagnostic records and source identities for readability, refactoring and review views. Do not add per-tool analyzers, independent hashes or another mutable compiler model. Preserve unknown, stale, incomplete and unobserved results.

## Where reflection and compile-time metadata help

| Subject | Generate or share once | Keep as runtime work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enum declaration | Typed values, case descriptions, conversion tables, wire dispatch and callable signatures | Supplied payloads, ingress values and the active captured case |
| Checked codec | Field/variant plans, schema and direct derived reader/writer code where lawful | Input admission, duplicate keys, dynamic patch/query values and custom codec execution |
| Command schema | Help, completion, documentation, prompt descriptions and validation structure | Keystrokes, entered values, dynamic schemas and command dispatch |
| App HTTP graph | Public operation descriptions and OpenAPI output | Requests, authorization, handler effects and connection lifecycle |
| Foreign binding descriptor | Names, typed projections, ownership/effect declarations, version identity and generated glue | Actual foreign safety, callbacks, cancellation, protocol outcomes and retry behavior |
| Iterator operation | Conservative cardinality/effect/loan propagation | Cursor progress, readiness, unknown future counts and failures |
| Checked program | Source-identified explanations, diagnostic links and refactoring previews | Runtime observation and cleanup execution |
| Compute kernel | Reachable-helper checks, element width, shape constraints and captured-effect checks | Runtime dimensions, provider/device execution and transfer results |

The existing @ mark reads compiler-known facts or demands evaluation of known inputs. It does not make runtime state known. Type.reflect() remains the compile-time aggregate view; runtime reflection remains the existing value operation. A parsed template plan may be built at runtime: calling an operation compile does not grant it a language compile-time exception.

Do not introduce parallel Meta, Schema, Reflect or provider registries. Generate projections from the appropriate checked owner. Keep declared, verified, unknown and executed evidence distinct. Facts do not grant permissions, manufacture types, reveal private payloads or bypass compile-time effect rules.

## Service maintenance boundary

Recommended D-NEST-UPSTREAM1=A uses maintained implementations through existing foreign bindings and bounded application glue. It does not promise eight Jet-specific service facades. Candidate libraries include async-graphql, tonic/prost, rust-rdkafka/librdkafka, lapin, socketioxide and Redis clients. They are candidates, not approved versions or proved bindings.

A Redis client alone is not a JobQueue provider. An OTLP exporter is not the selected custom POST /events sender. An installed SDK is not a lifecycle, protocol, I9 or performance receipt. Missing integration capability stays open rather than producing a hidden first-party fallback.

OpenAPI and local logging retain their current owners. The new ownership choice does not reopen codec or iterator dependency rejections. Provider-specific APIs and occasional foreign runtimes are the explicit cost of avoiding first-party service maintenance.

## Approval accounting

All 102 intake decisions remain ratified history. The integrated review records 75 useful refinements under existing law, 11 choices needing no additional mechanism, and 16 choices affected by the one new service ownership ballot. Main removed 27 redundant requests to re-approve APIs, formats, markers or profiles already covered by their selected A.

Implementation is not proof of approval, and approval is not proof of implementation. Existing criteria, snapshots, I9 and strict matched-performance gates remain unchanged. The 19 performance-gated draft decisions were not made ready or ratified.

## Complete per-decision user-side ledger

Each row below has a specific mechanism/type/metadata handoff on its existing card. Ninety-one card plans cover all 102 decisions. No implementation criterion was marked complete.

| D-ENUM-INGRESS1 / #3146 | Remove declaration-code parsers from callers; generate the lookup from EnumDef, while leaving unrelated protocol aliases/application mappings explicit. | Existing A covers this refinement |

| D-CORE-JSON-POINTER1 / #3237 | Replace application pointer parsers with a single proposed DataTree.pointer operation; copy only the returned subtree, not each ancestor. | Existing A covers this refinement |
| D-CORE-JSON-SCHEMA1 / #3238 | Delete parallel hand-written schema/validator descriptions; derive names, requiredness, nullability, defaults, validation and variants from the existing checked facts. | Existing A covers this refinement |
| D-CORE-JSON-PATCH1 / #3278 | Use one path/operation engine over a working copy; remove caller-side patch interpreters and never mutate the source before validation succeeds. | Existing A covers this refinement |
| D-CORE-JSON-MERGE1 / #3279 | Reuse one DataTree traversal and copy-on-write result path; do not implement a second validator or silently route through JSON Patch. | Existing A covers this refinement |
