6. Read back every write. Prove scope coverage, criterion preservation, dependency integrity and complete open/non-draft ballots; leave existing performance-gated drafts honest. Answer the owner’s four technical questions directly.

## Main technical analysis: types are facts, not separate engines

Conclusion: convention does not justify a separate semantic mechanism. A type name, a type instance, a representation and an execution protocol are different things. Two names can project one parameterized family. One family can still require different instances because ownership, lifetime, error meaning or permitted operations differ. Separate runtime engines do not follow from those distinctions.

The test is substitutability. If replacing one value with the other changes a legal operation, lifetime, effect, evaluation order, authority or observable result, that fact must remain checked. It may be a parameter, qualifier, role or associated fact; it need not become another public concept. Keep efficient specialized representations when their data differ. Do not add a universal object that replaces static checks with tags, runtime checks, copying or allocations.

### Option, Result and failure containers

Yes: optional and fallible values can share one mechanism. The current Prelude already defines JetOutcome<T,E> as Result<T,E>. Its optional view uses JetAbsent; its fallible view carries the error report E. JetOptionalView implements optional operations on that same carrier. The frontend still distinguishes Type::Option and Type::Result for checking and surface meaning. That is not evidence of two runtime engines.

Preserve clean absence versus typed failure as facts, not duplicate implementations. A stream can produce an element, end cleanly, or fail. Flattening those into an undifferentiated missing value loses observable meaning. Likewise, shared storage does not erase nested composition or which operation handles which layer. or_err changes a clean absence into a failure report; that is a semantic conversion, not a reason for another carrier.

A zero-sized absence report alone proves no universal zero-overhead result. A payload using every bit pattern leaves no spare state for absence. Niche and layout claims need type-specific evidence, not the comment’s general wording. No layout or runtime measurement was performed here.

Disposition: retain one carrier and shared sum operations; preserve the checked report/absence facts and surface identity. #3160 owns identity proof; #3325 and #3236 own the already-approved common operation and error boundaries. No new public Outcome name, alias or failure mechanism is proposed. Sources: crates/jet-foundation/src/Outcome.rs:1-22,1952-2018; crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/types.rs:933-961; examples/features/types/optional_result_variants.jet:1-16.
Nested stream and public optional-operation sources: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/EncodingStream.rs:1073-1077; crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs:1844-1860.

### List, View, Iter, ViewIter and Stream

Yes: owned and borrowed collections can be instances of one semantic family. Ownership and lifetime are static facts; separate public names do not require duplicated method policy. But a borrowed View cannot escape its owner or silently become an owned List. Access mode, backing owner, traversal, result ownership and evaluation timing must survive normalization.

The present representations differ: List is materialized; View borrows storage; Iter owns a boxed iterator; ViewIter carries a borrowing lifetime. List.map is eager while iterator mapping is lazy. An effectful callback makes that timing observable. Stream adds pull, end/failure, acknowledgement and cancellation behavior; calling it lazy is not a complete contract.

Disposition: D-ONE-OPERATIONS1=A on #3325 owns one checked operation contract with receiver/result facts and specialized adapters. Share those facts and derivations; do not force all values into one allocation or executor. No implicit materialization, lifetime erasure or new universal collection API is proposed. Sources: crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs:233-287,1517-1565,1717-1817; crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs:1147-1203; crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/Context.rs:3293-3335; crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Stream.rs:123-155,189-301.

### Compile-time facts, runtime metadata and @

Metadata can be ordinary typed data. Knowing a field name at compile time does not require a runtime reflection engine to retrieve it. Jet already reads compiler facts through @ bindings and uses selected results in runtime code. @ marks the compile-time binding/read; it is not a request to a runtime registry.

Static Type.reflect() is currently restricted to compile time. Sema folds it into a ComptimeName carrying the result; a call outside that stage gets E0302. Runtime reflect.of(value) instead builds a value projection with type name, path, display and field projections. The inspected representation stores owned strings and field records. It is not a live reference that automatically follows later mutation, nor a lossless box of arbitrary original values.

Share the checked declaration facts and generate portable metadata projections once. Runtime reflection can add the current value projection. Do not make runtime code carry the whole compiler CtValue universe, checked AST handles, build authority or compile-only functions. A runtime enum projection also cannot reconstruct every declared enum case from one value.

Disposition: #3155/D-ONE-SHAPE1=A owns shared declaration facts; #3186/D-ONE-TOOLS1=A owns checked query context. Keep the current staging contract. A proposal to make Type.reflect() callable at runtime, expose new metadata fields or add a sigil would need a separate ballot; none is proposed here. Sources: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/expr.rs:773-828; crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Reflect.rs:1-119; examples/features/reflection/fact_reads.jet:1-84; examples/features/reflection/reflect-value.jet:1-70.

### DataTree, relational plans, columns and tensors

These need not be unrelated implementation silos, but they are not interchangeable storage contracts. DataTree is a heterogeneous interchange carrier. A relational plan describes deferred typed operations. Columns describe physical field-wise storage. The inspected JetTensor stores Arc<Vec<f64>> with shape, strides, device and placement facts. This is not evidence of arbitrary element-type support. A table with differently typed named columns is not simply a homogeneous numeric matrix.

Share schema, shape, scalar conversion, buffer ownership and device facts where their meanings match. Do not route arithmetic or column access through boxed tree values merely to obtain one nominal type. Conversions may require allocation or copying; no zero-copy or performance win is claimed.

Disposition: retain specialized storage/execution values; reuse checked facts and explicit projections under #3155 and #3236. Existing GPU/device and columnar performance owners keep their exact proof gates. No universal DataTree-backed tensor/table API is proposed. Sources: crates/jet-foundation/src/DataTree.rs:1-66; crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/data_plan.rs:1-208; crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Columns.rs:1-31,111-159; crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Compute.rs:1-31,4013-4032.

### Current schema and historical schema

Old and current are usually values or roles, not a reason for duplicate schema machinery. A shared immutable schema-description projection can serve comparison and serialization. The complete current checked declaration also contains compiler facts that do not belong in a durable snapshot.

The non-negotiable distinction is history: a published snapshot records an earlier contract. Recomputing it from today’s declaration destroys the evidence needed to detect a removed or renamed field. Reusing a record type does not grant publication authority or make old and current contents equal.

Disposition: #3155 owns declaration facts and #3233 owns evolution proof. Use one canonical current projection and preserve immutable historical records and migration meaning. Do not create a second live metadata registry or erase snapshot provenance. Sources: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Schema.rs:1-88,134-223; crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/SchemaMigration.rs:1-27; examples/features/serde/migrations/.jet/cache/schema/UserRecord.snapshot:1-5.

### Task, Job, Stream and Service

Share existing lifecycle operations; do not infer identical protocols from similar verbs. A scoped task can borrow under its owner. A durable queue item needs serializable state and acknowledgement across process failure. A stream has repeated pull/end behavior. A service has supervision and mailbox rules. A #Job declaration alone is not proof that an invocation is durable; direct calls and durable queue submission are different cases.

A qualified family could encode these roles statically, but merely renaming them Activity would remove no machinery. A local join must not stand in for durable acknowledgement. Do not add another scheduler or generic lifecycle framework around the existing primitives.

Disposition: #3078/D-ONE-LIFECYCLE1=A owns common operations with distinct policies; #3239 retains task/cancellation proof. Sources: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/TaskGroup.rs:1-90,198-396; crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Job.rs:1-18,84-177; crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/JobQueueTypes.rs:1-28; crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Services.rs:92-183,882-975.
Borrowed-spawn source: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/MathTaskMem.rs:546-570.

### Diagnostics, status, reports, evidence, proof, replay and LSP

Common field shapes justify shared construction, validation, serialization and projection code. They do not make these records equal claims. A successful command status is not proof that a criterion was exercised. A replay describes recorded events, not necessarily the current program. An editor diagnostic is a projection with source/version identity, not the original compiler object.

Keep their wire contracts, provenance, authority and invariants checked. A common carrier may sit underneath constrained records; do not replace them with an unrestricted map and scattered runtime checks. Share representation only where it preserves the exact allowed values and conversion meaning.

Disposition: #3186/D-ONE-TOOLS1=A owns checked source identity and query projections; existing report/evidence/replay contracts remain unchanged. No new universal report envelope is proposed. Sources: crates/jet-foundation/src/Diagnostics.rs:67-73,172-223; crates/jet-foundation/src/Report.rs:287-400,590-705; crates/jet-foundation/src/Evidence.rs:157-248,318-350; crates/jet-cli/src/Recording.rs:57-118,381-535; Source/LSP/Server.rs:798-835,850-881.

### Foreign descriptors, ABI facts and handles

Use one foreign declaration contract and share its checked projections. A descriptor, an application binary interface contract, a generated stub and a live owned handle still have different contents and authority. [INFERENCE] A common tagged inspection projection could display these records, but would not make every artifact valid for every call boundary. No such universal inspection type is claimed to be shipped.

Preserve scalar width, layout, ownership, thread/callback policy, target identity and lifetime obligations. Do not infer ABI validity from a generated declaration or provider status. A generic record that drops these facts is not unification.

Disposition: retain the existing descriptor contract and per-language ABI leaves. #3401/D-CBIND-UPSTREAM1=A covers C extraction, not permission to erase other foreign obligations. #3402 separately fixes native Nixpkgs translation into Jet’s package model; Nix implementation reuse is prohibited by the owner. Sources: crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/ffi.rs:6-47,76-296,1064-1088,1171-1188; crates/jet-driver/src/Foreign.rs:1-23.

### Syntax convenience versus mechanisms

A familiar spelling can project an existing mechanism without creating a second implementation. Conversely, the same word can hide different timing or ownership. Judge checked meaning, not punctuation. D-CALLVALUE2=A now chooses ordinary adjacent invocation of returned functions through the existing call machinery; this preparation did not implement it. The @ staging contract remains unchanged.
Authority evidence: the owner ratified D-CALLVALUE2=A on #3399, read back at Tower revision 55842. The eight-row type capture does not supply invocation runtime proof.

Ballot disposition: the eight type-family questions and this syntax question are analyzed above against the nine ratified ballots and existing contracts. No additional public type, API, syntax, authority exception or runtime mechanism is proposed. Do not manufacture a new owner choice for routine internal factoring or re-ballot an unchanged law. If a future implementation requires a real contract change, expose that exact choice before coding.

Evidence scope: Luna-max collected exact source and checked-in expectations; Main wrote this analysis and every decision. These are source-backed conclusions and explicit design recommendations, not runtime, layout, provider, performance or cross-engine completion proof. No implementation was performed.

### Type-analysis disposition

The eight type-family questions and syntax-versus-mechanism question have source-backed answers in the technical analysis above. They reuse the ratified operation, shape, codec, query, lifecycle and invocation contracts. Retained distinctions are justified by observable facts, not convention. Internal factoring with unchanged public behavior is not another owner ballot. No new public type, API, sigil, authority exception or runtime engine is proposed.

### Licensing and native Nixpkgs direction

Owner licensing choice: Jet/Jetpack code is MIT. Compatible permissive dependencies may retain their licenses and notices. Managed package payloads may use other licenses and retain their original terms. This is not permission to relicense third-party code. Independently, the Nixpkgs adapter must not depend on Nix implementation executables, libraries, daemons, services or storage.

Nixpkgs repository recipes are MIT-licensed separately from the packages they build. Package metadata and distribution permissions must survive translation. Primary references: https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/b5aa0fbd538984f6e3d201be0005b4463d8b09f8/README.md and https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/b5aa0fbd538984f6e3d201be0005b4463d8b09f8/COPYING . cards.title: Choose ordinary invocation for returned callable expressions
cards.body: Owner-requested simplification choice D-CALLVALUE2. The complete ballot owns the proposed alternatives; current law remains until ratification. This card is the coherent implementation/policy home for that choice, not a claim that proposed behavior exists.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement ratified D-CALLVALUE2=A: postfix invocation on any expression whose checked type is callable (`make_adder(1)(2)`, `get()()`, grouped and method-returned callables), in one cutover that removes the synthetic function-value `.call(...)` route. A user-declared method named `call` stays an ordinary method.

## Current state
- Jet parser: every postfix call on a non-name callee already builds `Expr.CallValue` (`Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/Expressions.jet:922`). Jet sema checks it through `sema_call_check_value_owned` / `sema_call_value_checked_from_type`, which produce `TExprKind.IndirectCall` (`Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Values.jet:40-150`).
- Old law still taught in the Jet compiler: registry row `E-CALL-VALUE` ("use `.call(…)`", D-CALLVALUE1=B) at `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet:8598-8613`.
- Shipped Rust bootstrap: the parser rejects `)(` with E-CALL-VALUE (`crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Expressions/postfix.rs:336`, test in `crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/mod.rs:2324`). The sema maps `.call` on `Type::Fn` to `INTERNAL_CALL_VALUE` (`crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerInfer/calls/method_calls.rs:3601`; `crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs:522-525`).
- Callers: `Examples/features/functions/returned_function_call.jet:7-8`, `tests/ui/E-CALL-VALUE_call_result_not_called.{jet,fixed.jet,stderr}`, the E0803 advice in `tests/ui/call_non_function.stderr` and `todo_call_e0803.stderr`, `tests/corpus_policy.{rs,tsv}` and `tests/support/fmt_lossless.rs:7` (fixture references), `Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:383-385` and `Docs/spec/spec.md:681`. The `c.call(...)` uses in the cffi UI fixtures are user FFI functions and stay.

## Changes
1. Jet compiler: delete the `E-CALL-VALUE` row. Remove any Fn-typed `.call` projection in `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Methods.jet`, so `.call` on a function value is an ordinary unknown-method error. Rewrite the E0803 text: "only a callable value can be invoked; call it with `(…)`".
2. Rust bootstrap mirror, so the corpus still parses and runs: remove the E-CALL-VALUE branch in `postfix.rs` and build the value call; remove `INTERNAL_CALL_VALUE` and its method_calls arm; delete the parser unit test.
3. Fix the captured-`base` defect (#1427) on whichever tier loses it: returned closures keep their captures through `IndirectCall`.
4. Migrate: the example to `make_adder(1)(2)`, the fixtures, the corpus_policy/fmt_lossless references, the docs, `Syntax.rs` and a syntax-decisions entry for D-CALLVALUE2=A. Regenerate `jet devtools grammars` and re-bless snapshots.

## Proof
- The two added criteria.
- A Jet slice check (`Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`) is clean for `Compiler/JetParser` and `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls`.
- `cargo test -p jet-parser` passes.
- A new golden covers `f()()()`, `(pick(true))(3)`, `obj.get_fn()(1)` and argument side-effect order.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-front`: a parser/call-surface cutover plus the Rust parser and sema mirror.

## Dependencies
None. D-CALLVALUE2 is ratified A, so Main can mark criterion 1 met.

cards.plan:
**Goal**
Record the ratified D-UPSTREAM-SCOPE1=A policy: which optional-integration decisions and cards inherit the upstream-first preference, and each one's concrete owner home. The preference itself never approves a provider, API or dependency.

**Current state**
- D-UPSTREAM-SCOPE1=A is ratified (Tower), so criterion 1 is satisfied by the vote. Option A extends upstream-first evaluation to compatibility interpreters, header extraction, domain tooling and optional ecosystem integrations. It keeps first-party Core contracts and existing ratified bindings until a named cutover.
- No card except #3400 references D-UPSTREAM-SCOPE1, and neither it nor D-NEST-UPSTREAM1 appears anywhere in Docs/.
- The concrete homes already exist:

cards.body: Owner-requested simplification choice D-CBIND-UPSTREAM1. The complete ballot owns the proposed alternatives; current law remains until ratification. This card is the coherent implementation/policy home for that choice, not a claim that proposed behavior exists.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-CBIND-UPSTREAM1=A (ratified): C bindings use the shared Clang declaration extractor that C++ already uses, and the focused C parser is removed.

## Current state
- The decision is ratified with outcome A: share the existing Clang extractor for C and C++. Criterion 1's owner outcome therefore exists; D-CBIND3 remains an unratified historical import.
- The Jet port still uses the focused parser: Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Foreign/C/HeaderBinder.jet:4 says there is no bindgen and no libclang. The bind hash is at :47-50 and the sidecar writer at :73.
- Rust: crates/jet-pkg-model/src/CBind.rs:25-34 hashes header plus cflags. The C++ extractor at CppBind.rs:565-585 runs `clang -std=c++17 -Xclang -ast-dump=json`.
- Empty cflags reach the bind hash at CFFI.rs:2747 and :2874, and at Source/CmdDevTools.rs:4904-4905 (`pass "" for now`).
- The approved toolchain comes from Jetpack/Provider/Source/Toolchain/CcToolchainDescriptor.jet, and the sandbox from Jetpack/Foundation/Source/NativeSandbox.jet:97.

## Changes
1. Jet, in Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Foreign/C:
   - Replace the HeaderParser path with Clang C-mode AST extraction that follows the CppBind process and provenance pattern: `-x c`, no C++ shim, the resolved descriptor's clang, and runs inside the native sandbox.
   - Delete HeaderParser.jet and its claims.
   - Keep the inspect command, the generated cache and the handwritten overlay boundary.
   - The bind hash covers target, compiler identity, flags, header include closure and overlay.
2. Jet still checks ownership, close/thread/link facts, supported value and callback types, ABI layout and unsupported declarations. Nothing guessed passes.
3. Rust mirror, needed so the shipped `jet inspect bind` and `jet build` prove the fix: in CFFI.rs and CmdDevTools.rs, thread the real cflags and target through `compute_bind_hash`, and route C extraction through the CppBind extractor in C mode. Remove the C focused parser from CBind.rs and add no fallback.
4. A missing provider or sandbox fails closed with a registered diagnostic.

## Proof
- The added criterion.
- A linked-execution fixture: a C library with a record, a pointer/count pair, a callback and a macro constant, bound, built and run. `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=ffi/c_clang_bind cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` prints the expected output on AOT, `jet run` and the interpreter.

## Batch
batch-jetpack-pkgmodel: the Jet cutover lives in PackageModel. The small Rust mirror rides the same build.

## Dependencies

cards.title: Choose one explicit cross-backend default viewport policy
cards.body: Owner-requested simplification choice D-UI-VIEWPORT1. The complete ballot owns the proposed alternatives; current law remains until ratification. This card is the coherent implementation/policy home for that choice, not a claim that proposed behavior exists.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement the ratified D-UI-VIEWPORT1=A (2026-09-13). An omitted root constraint uses the attached host's own coordinate frame: browser/native logical space or terminal cells. It follows host resize, and with no host attached it keeps the declared virtual layout. Explicit constraints keep their exact meaning. There is no new public viewport API, no new unit family, and no universal pixel-to-cell factor.

## Current state
- Criterion 1 is satisfied by the ratification. D-UI-VIEWPORT1=A explicitly amends the D-UI-MOUNT1=A default. D-STYLEUNIT1=A has syntax/source provenance only, with no captured board decision.
- Backends still hard-code their defaults:
  - `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Ui.rs:1409-1410` defines `DEFAULT_MOUNT_COLS/ROWS = 80/24`, used by `mount_node_default` at `:1579-1583` and `:1817-1820` and by the TUI constraint at `:1016`.
  - `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/UiGtk.rs:1382-1383` uses 320×240, and `:975` sets the window default size.
  - `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/DomRuntime.js:1864-1869` uses 80×24.
- There is no per-layout-transaction viewport capture. `Core/ui/ui.jet:120-133` has preview viewports only.
- `tests/dom_runtime_parity.rs:94-133` pins the two 80×24 literals against each other. That is a source-text test and must be deleted in the cutover.

## Changes
1. `Ui.rs`: replace `DEFAULT_MOUNT_*` in `mount_node_default` with a host-frame query captured once per layout transaction. TUI uses the current terminal size in cells and re-lays out on the existing resize event. Null/headless has no attached host, so it uses the declared virtual viewport, which stays documented. Paint waits for allocation without blocking the synchronous mount API.
2. `UiGtk.rs`: an omitted root uses the window's allocated logical size and re-lays out on allocation change. Keep the explicit `gtk_window_set_default_size` only as the initial window hint.
3. `DomRuntime.js`: an omitted root uses the container's client box and follows a ResizeObserver.
4. Delete the literal-drift test in `tests/dom_runtime_parity.rs:94-133`. Update docs and examples that describe 80×24 or 320×240 as the default.

## Proof
Run `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test ui_viewport` (new file, registered in `tests/suites.txt`):
- `tui_omitted_root_fills_pty_and_follows_resize` uses a pty at 120×40 resized to 100×30, and layout and hit-test follow the resize.
- `explicit_constraint_is_stable_across_host_resize`.
- `null_backend_uses_declared_virtual_viewport`.
- `dom_omitted_root_follows_container_resize` runs through the Chromium CDP driver at two sizes.

For GTK, record visual plus geometry evidence of initial allocation and resize on a real Linux display. Unavailable hosts are reported as unavailable, not as a pass.

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime`: Prelude UI hosts (TUI/GTK/DOM runtime).

## Dependencies
None (ballot ratified).

cards.title: Measure paired AoC whole-solution performance and ergonomics
cards.body:
## Outcome

Run the complete frozen corpus through matched performance and source-effort measurements. Report whole-solution outcomes, not isolated language-runtime superiority.

## Shared stream contract

This card owns its Outcome, implementation plan, and criteria. The rules below are shared context for the complete idea stream. Sibling cards own the other portions; they are not duplicate acceptance work on this card.

- Thirty diverse preselected puzzles, both parts; correctness, ergonomics, and speed; puzzle evidence does not replace real-workload gates.
- Best correct natural solution per language; different algorithms allowed. Label measured results whole-solution outcomes, not isolated runtime/compiler speed or proven global optima.
- Use existing applicable gauntlet peer rails and strict comparison rules. Keep losses and uncertainty visible.
- Controlled agent authoring: three fresh-context attempts per puzzle per applicable comparison language, equal model/tools/docs/limits; preserve failures; never call agent evidence human beginner evidence.
- Freeze selection before Jet measurements; reproducible inputs and independent expected answers; one meaning on applicable Jet execution tiers.

## Origin and authority

Consider advent of code solutions in jet as evaluation metric/benchmark

cards.title: Complete LSP semantic coverage across Jet constructs
cards.body:
## Outcome

Implement every Jet-applicable semantic LSP 3.18 capability across all applicable registered Jet constructs, not merely one successful example per method.

## Shared stream contract

This card owns its Outcome, implementation plan, and criteria. The rules below are shared context for the complete idea stream. Sibling cards own the other portions; they are not duplicate acceptance work on this card.

- All current stable LSP 3.18 Jet-applicable capabilities crossed with every applicable Jet construct. Explicit reason for each inapplicable item; no advertised empty/no-op implementations.
- Real end-to-end VS Code, Zed, Neovim acceptance; protocol harness also required. No notebook visual or Canvas-node redesign.

## Origin and authority

Source idea `bhg7rahc`, recorded 2026-09-12T19:16:49.469Z:

Inspect LSP standard to ensure 100% jet support
cards.plan:
## Goal
Every Jet-applicable semantic capability in LSP 3.18 works across every applicable registered Jet construct through the real server. Each cell has a consumer-observable witness or a reasoned N/A, and no capability is an advertised no-op. The editor acceptance runs in VS Code, Zed and Neovim belong to sibling #3413; this card owns the semantic cells and the protocol-harness proof.

## Current state
- The semantic providers live in the retained host: Source/LSP/Features.rs (hover, identity, definition, references, rename, semantic tokens, refactors from :2863), Source/LSP/Completion.rs (keyword, type, member and compiler-fact completion, and D-LSP5 auto-import at :730-780), Source/LSP/Check.rs (overlay check, diagnostics, fixes) and Source/LSP/Server.rs (dispatch). The old plan's crates/jet-codegen/src/Source/LSP paths are stale.
- tests/lsp.rs already has named tests: `lsp_initialize_capabilities_have_named_test_coverage` (:765), navigation (:2714), prepare-rename/call hierarchy (:2798), type hierarchy (:2904), semantic tokens (:4212), inlay hints (:4439), references (:4569) and enum variants (:4610).
- Today the semantic facts come from the shipped checker's index. When #3186 lands they come from the Jet checked-fact owner (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/SemanticIndex.jet:1570). Providers must read that one index, never text search or a second checker.

## Changes
1. Inventory, pinned to a source commit: cross the 3.18 capability list (from #3410's protocol inventory) with the construct registries (JetFoundation/Source/Registry, Syntax). The constructs are declarations, scopes, imports, generics, traits, effects, patterns, enums, raw and interpolated strings, entry forms, generated origins and incomplete edits. Commit the matrix as tests/lsp/semantic_matrix.json with a reason for each N/A.
2. Fill each missing cell in its canonical provider (Features.rs or Completion.rs) from checked identities: completion and resolve, hover, signatures, definition/declaration/type/implementation, references, rename, symbols, diagnostics, tokens, inlay hints, actions, folding and selection, links, lens, and call/type hierarchy. Keep wire `#Rename` data names separate from source identifiers.
3. Reuse #3158 (enum rename/navigation/completion) and #3191 (checked relationship projections) rather than duplicating them. Only Main edits Server.rs dispatch.
4. Edge cases: non-ASCII positions, shadowing, same-spelled symbols across modules, overloads and generics, broken-code recovery, stale data and cancellation. An edit must still parse and check afterwards.

## Proof
- `cargo test --test lsp -- lsp_semantic_construct_matrix` (new) drives the real `jet self lsp` over each cell in semantic_matrix.json, and passes.
- `cargo test --test lsp -- lsp_initialize_capabilities_have_named_test_coverage` passes: every advertised capability names a matrix row.
- `cargo test --test lsp -- lsp_enum_variant_navigation_completion_and_rename lsp_checked_identity_and_versioned_rename` still pass.

## Batch
batch-host-cli: LSP is a retained host command, proved by one tests/lsp.rs pass.

## Dependencies

cards.title: Make jet dev output minimal with an explicit dashboard focus
cards.body:
## Outcome

Deliver a quiet default dev loop and the complete existing applicable dashboard on demand in the same terminal. Preserve application input and output.

## Shared stream contract

This card owns its Outcome, implementation plan, and criteria. The rules below are shared context for the complete idea stream. Sibling cards own the other portions; they are not duplicate acceptance work on this card.

- Minimal task output plus compact status line: target, state, last meaningful action; distinguish reload from restart/state reset. No routine timing, capture-budget, receipts, action/debug chatter or promotions.
- Expandable full existing applicable dashboard in same terminal, explicit focus only. Preserve scrollback and restore prior output on collapse.
- Ctrl+] enters dashboard; second Ctrl+] exits and passes a literal Ctrl+] to app. Escape exits dashboard without forwarding prefix. Ordinary keys belong to app outside dashboard focus.
- No auto expansion/focus stealing. Plain/non-TTY/NO_COLOR/JSON and application-owned terminal modes need honest fallback; no fake/cut-off panels. Existing panel/session mechanism, no new dashboard domain semantics.
- Actual TTY visual acceptance is owner-only.

## Origin and authority

Source idea `blqrifm6`, recorded 2026-09-14T11:20:45.881Z:

Cleanup all the junk printed to terminal when using jet dev, I did not authorize that user facing ux/ui
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Implement ratified D-DEV-FOCUS2=A. Default `jet dev` shows application output plus one compact status line: target, state, and last meaningful action, with reload and restart/state-reset kept distinct. The full existing dashboard opens only by explicit focus in the same terminal.
- Ctrl+] enters the dashboard.
- A second Ctrl+] exits and forwards one literal Ctrl+] to the app.
- Escape exits without forwarding.
- Nothing auto-expands. Scrollback is preserved and restored.

**Owner quote**
"Cleanup all the junk printed to terminal when using jet dev, I did not authorize that user facing ux/ui."

**Current state**
- `crates/jet-devserver/src/TerminalHost.rs` owns capabilities (TTY, ANSI, NO_COLOR, width), typed focus and input enums, panel navigation, and rendering. It has no Ctrl+] (0x1d) handling anywhere.
- `Source/CmdDevTools.rs` owns dev action parsing, terminal byte mapping, host construction, and the refresh render. (The card's `crates/jet-codegen/src/Source/` paths are stale.)
- Dev dispatch is in `Source/main.rs`. `crates/jet-cli/src/OutputProfile.rs` owns TERM and width selection.
- #3068 only removed one promotion.
- Optional-history notices go through `jet::ReceiptStore::optional_history_notice`, which already exists (see #3416).

**Changes**
1. `Source/CmdDevTools.rs` default render: the application stream plus one status line. Drop routine timings, counters, capture-budget banners, receipt paths, and action chatter.
2. `TerminalHost.rs` gets a focus state machine and routes input bytes:
   - 0x1d enters focus, or exits and forwards 0x1d;
   - ESC exits;
   - other bytes go to the app unless focused.
3. Opening the dashboard saves the output ring and restores it on collapse, reusing the existing panel catalog. The alternate screen is allowed.
4. Fallbacks:
   - with no TTY, JSON, or NO_COLOR there are no panels, and a status line is printed on state change only;
   - when the application owns the TTY (raw mode), Ctrl+] routing still works, and panels render only while focused.

**Proof**
- New `cargo test --test dev -- dev_default_view_is_output_plus_status_line`: PTY run of a printing app shows only the app lines plus one status line matching `^dev: .* · (running|reloaded|restarted)`.
- New `cargo test --test dev -- dev_ctrl_bracket_focus_and_forwarding`: 0x1d opens the dashboard, 0x1d again closes it and the app receives 0x1d, ESC closes without forwarding, and scrollback is restored.
- New `cargo test --test dev -- dev_edit_or_failure_never_steals_focus`.
- The owner accepts the real terminal appearance (criterion 6).

**Batch**
`batch-host-cli`: devtools terminal host.

**Dependencies**
None hard. #3416's notice mechanism is already in the tree, and #3113 reload state is consumed when available.

cards.title: Bound all disposable history with per-project FIFO retention
cards.body:
## Outcome

Replace replay-only/count-limited retention with a consistent 256 MiB per-project byte-only FIFO budget across all disposable histories, while protecting saved and required audit data.

## Shared stream contract

This card owns its Outcome, implementation plan, and criteria. The rules below are shared context for the complete idea stream. Sibling cards own the other portions; they are not duplicate acceptance work on this card.

- Result first; ordinary history is best-effort and cannot turn passed tests into failure. A crash may lose latest unsaved history.
- Mandatory authority/audit records and explicitly requested proof/saved artifacts remain durable and fail closed. No performance shortcut may weaken those.
- FIFO for all disposable unsaved run/build/test/replay histories, keeping reference groups consistent; saved claims and required audit roots protected outside disposable quota.
- 256 MiB per project byte limit, no policy record-count cap; shared-cache location must not cause cross-project eviction. Real disk-full and individual oversized records handled honestly.
- Normal save/eviction is silent. Actual optional persistence failure emits one concise nonfatal notice WITH cause-specific corrective action in the notice; never require external lookup or auto-run a destructive repair.
- No mandatory background daemon merely for receipts; implementation can choose minimal bounded mechanism. Show no persisted artifact claim before persistence.

## Origin and authority

Source idea `bn8w6h9l`, recorded 2026-09-14T12:18:45.476Z:

❯ scripts/agent/jet-env jet test examples/features/tooling/branch_dispatch_bench.jet --measure branch dense: pass branch sparse: pass branch enum: pass branch ordered: pass branch biased: pass 5 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped Error [E2105]: Couldn't finalize test evidence for `examples/features/tooling/branch_dispatch_bench.jet`: could not store evidence record `test:df05f274a6220fd1:1270457:1789388040091365494`: record budget exceeded; no unreferenced unsaved safe replay can be evicted  Why: Jet could not complete the named file, tool, or operating-system operation  Fix: Correct the named problem, then run the command again More: jet-lang.dev/e/E2105                       Should not be failing. Why is there a limited budget? Default behavior should allow users to get the result of their triggered operation with FIFO order. Should not run then fail because it couldnt save a receipt, plus that error happened AFTER it already printed test results... wtf? What is the point of the receipt then? We want everything to be as fast as possible, so holding up completion of the testing op because of a receipt is not ideal. Need to discuss better approach
cards.plan:
**Goal**
All disposable run/build/test/replay history shares one 256 MiB per-project byte-only FIFO. Saved claims and mandatory audit/sensitive roots stay outside the quota and are never evicted. Reference groups stay whole. The old replay-only / 200-record policy is gone. D-HISTORY-LIFECYCLE2 option A (interview-selected) governs.

**Current state** (implemented; proof owed)
- `Source/RecordIndex.rs`:
  - :27 `DEFAULT_RECORD_BUDGET_BYTES = 256 MiB`.
  - :222 `RecordBudget { max_bytes }`, with no record-count field.
  - :1102 `eviction_groups` evicts whole linked disposable groups FIFO.
- Existing tests:
  - :1621 `saved_history_survives_disposable_eviction_after_restart`
  - :1673 `concurrent_update_and_store_preserves_each_row`
  - :1711 `oversized_disposable_update_does_not_corrupt_the_previous_index`

cards.title: Keep optional history off command completion and exit status
cards.body:
## Outcome

Fix the reported passed-test-then-E2105 failure at its ownership boundary. Ordinary history is best effort; required audit and explicitly requested evidence remain durable and fail closed.

## Shared stream contract

This card owns its Outcome, implementation plan, and criteria. The rules below are shared context for the complete idea stream. Sibling cards own the other portions; they are not duplicate acceptance work on this card.

- Result first; ordinary history is best-effort and cannot turn passed tests into failure. A crash may lose latest unsaved history.
- Mandatory authority/audit records and explicitly requested proof/saved artifacts remain durable and fail closed. No performance shortcut may weaken those.
- FIFO for all disposable unsaved run/build/test/replay histories, keeping reference groups consistent; saved claims and required audit roots protected outside disposable quota.
- 256 MiB per project byte limit, no policy record-count cap; shared-cache location must not cause cross-project eviction. Real disk-full and individual oversized records handled honestly.
- Normal save/eviction is silent. Actual optional persistence failure emits one concise nonfatal notice WITH cause-specific corrective action in the notice; never require external lookup or auto-run a destructive repair.
- No mandatory background daemon merely for receipts; implementation can choose minimal bounded mechanism. Show no persisted artifact claim before persistence.

## Origin and authority

Source idea `bn8w6h9l`, recorded 2026-09-14T12:18:45.476Z:

❯ scripts/agent/jet-env jet test examples/features/tooling/branch_dispatch_bench.jet --measure branch dense: pass branch sparse: pass branch enum: pass branch ordered: pass branch biased: pass 5 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped Error [E2105]: Couldn't finalize test evidence for `examples/features/tooling/branch_dispatch_bench.jet`: could not store evidence record `test:df05f274a6220fd1:1270457:1789388040091365494`: record budget exceeded; no unreferenced unsaved safe replay can be evicted  Why: Jet could not complete the named file, tool, or operating-system operation  Fix: Correct the named problem, then run the command again More: jet-lang.dev/e/E2105                       Should not be failing. Why is there a limited budget? Default behavior should allow users to get the result of their triggered operation with FIFO order. Should not run then fail because it couldnt save a receipt, plus that error happened AFTER it already printed test results... wtf? What is the point of the receipt then? We want everything to be as fast as possible, so holding up completion of the testing op because of a receipt is not ideal. Need to discuss better approach

## Distinct ownership

#3415 owns record classification, storage budget, and FIFO/reference lifecycle. This card owns command result computation, completion, persistence-failure routing, and notices. It depends on #3415 and does not duplicate its storage implementation.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Ordinary best-effort history must never change a command's result. The reported `jet test examples/features/tooling/branch_dispatch_bench.jet --measure` pass-then-E2105 must stay a pass. Required authority/audit records and explicit `--record=NAME` or proof saves stay durable and fail closed.

**Shared contract (kept)**
- Result first; a crash may lose the latest unsaved history.
- A normal save or eviction is silent.
- An actual optional failure prints one nonfatal notice that carries its own corrective action.
- No mandatory daemon and no unbounded queue.
- Nothing claims a persisted path before commit.
- #3056 (expected failures) and #3057 (identity) stay separate.

**Current state**
Part of the mechanism is already in HEAD:
- `Source/ReceiptStore.rs:1909` `enqueue_optional_history` is a bounded `try_send` queue. When the queue is full or unavailable, it drops the job and prints a notice.
- `:1253` `optional_history_notice` prints one `history: optional persistence failed while …; fix: …` line.
- `Source/CmdCompile.rs:6363-6376` `finish_test_evidence`: a non-preserved report is persisted through the queue; a preserved report (explicit save) is persisted synchronously, and failure returns `Err`.

Gaps that remain:
- (a) In the fresh path, `Source/CmdCompile.rs:7552-7582` turns any `Err` into E2105 and `evidence_ok = false`. That includes report-assembly IO in `read_or_create_test_evidence_report` (`:6051`) and `append_harness_test_evidence`. `ok = child_ok && doctests_ok && evidence_ok` then fails a passing run.
- (b) The cached path at `:7279-7312` has the same problem.
- (c) In `Source/CmdDevTools.rs:1-156`, dev capture failures print on every revision; they are not coalesced.
- (d) No test covers optional-failure behavior.

**Changes**
1. `finish_test_evidence`: separate the semantic result (test projection, claim floor `floor_met`, expected-failure law, `child_ok`) from any persistence or IO step.
   - When `preserve_report` is false, report-assembly or temp-file IO errors call `optional_history_notice` and return the semantic result.
   - When `preserve_report` is true, keep `Err` leading to E2105 and failure.
   - Never collapse the result to `child_ok` alone.
2. Both call sites (`:7279`, `:7552`): E2105 only for the preserved/required path.
3. `ReceiptStore::optional_history_notice`: coalesce identical `(operation, fix)` pairs once per process. `CmdDevTools` dev capture uses the same notice.
4. Authority receipts (`CmdCompile.rs:1196-1537`) are unchanged and stay fail-closed.

**Proof**
- New `cargo test --test cli_commands -- test_passes_when_optional_history_cannot_persist`: a project with a passing `#Test` and a read-only `.jet/records` (chmod 0555) exits 0, prints the pass summary, and prints exactly one `history: optional persistence failed` line.
- New `cargo test --test cli_commands -- explicit_record_save_still_fails_closed`: the same setup with `--record=keep` exits nonzero with E2105.
- New `cargo test --test cli_commands -- test_json_result_unchanged_on_optional_history_failure`: the `--json` envelope has no notice on stdout.
- Manual: `Tools/agent/jet-env jet test Examples/features/tooling/branch_dispatch_bench.jet --measure` exits 0.

**Batch**
`batch-host-cli`: retained Source/ test/receipt host code.

**Dependencies**
None. #3415 (FIFO retention) is not needed to decouple result from persistence; it only changes which history gets evicted.

Re-run the exact original branch_dispatch_bench --measure command after the fix under the bounded optional-quota failure fixture; do not substitute an easier unmeasured test. ## Outcome

Repair the reported JSON interpolation failure in data_loader using ratified backtick raw strings. Ordinary interpolation keeps its current meaning.

## Shared stream contract

This card owns its Outcome, implementation plan, and criteria. The rules below are shared context for the complete idea stream. Sibling cards own the other portions; they are not duplicate acceptance work on this card.

- Repair data_loader literal JSON using existing ratified raw backtick strings. Preserve ordinary interpolation meaning.
- Verify JSON reader result, exact output and diagnostics guidance to existing raw/escaped forms; no new literal syntax.

## Origin and authority

Source idea `bobs0iri`, recorded 2026-09-14T12:24:49.173Z:

Parser error: ❯ scripts/agent/jet-env jet run examples/features/tooling/data_loader.jet  Error [E0002]: This `{` never gets a matching `}`   --> examples/features/tooling/data_loader.jet:99:30     |  99 |     files.write(json_path, "[{\"service\":\"cache\",\"latency_ms\":2.0}]") ?? panic("write json")     |                              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^  Why: `{` inside quoted text starts an interpolated value and needs a closing `}` before the text ends  Fix: Add a `}` after the value, or write `{{` for a literal brace More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0002  1 problem found run `jet explain E0002` to learn more

cards.title: Make authority approval compact and policy edits explicit
cards.body:
## Outcome

Deliver approval UI only where the current effect-policy contract requires a user choice. #3418 now owns the trusted-default and restricted-mode amendment. Do not restore the older rule that every metadata-free effectful script must prompt.

## Current dependency

This card remains blocked by #3418. Its prompt eligibility, trust scope, and policy selection must consume the canonical resolver. No UI code may infer effects or grant authority through a second mechanism.

The owner wants unchanged implementation source to work under personal and enterprise policies. Switching invocation policy must not silently edit source. A persistent project-policy edit remains a separate explicit action with an exact reviewed target and diff.

## Preserved safety and user-experience contract

- When approval is appropriate, explain the uncovered effects and their source. Keep explicit denies out of approval menus.
- Trusted execution must not repeatedly prompt for effects already covered by the selected authority. Exact trust scope comes from #3418.
- Preserve the compact numbered choices and accessible plain/TTY/JSON/no-TTY behavior. Do not consume application stdin accidentally.
- Exit, Escape, EOF, unavailable input, and invalid input grant nothing. Do not persist a denial merely because the user cancels.
- A project-policy edit requires exact acceptance. Preserve unrelated source, comments, existing denies, and external enterprise restrictions.
- Read-only, stale, malformed, ambiguous, or virtual policy targets fail closed. Incomplete policy/receipt transactions do not launch effects.
- Application effect trust never approves unrelated package/environment/toolchain trust or sensitive provider consent.

D-TRUST-LAUNCH1 is preserved as history. The default-policy amendment is not implemented by this card update. Retain the existing approval and transaction proof obligations, but derive the cases that prompt from the newly ratified upstream contract.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Finish the approval UI requirements that D-SCRIPT-CONFIRM1=A (#3705) doesn't already cover: safe cancellation, exact persistent-policy edits, and fail-closed targets. Consume #3418's trusted/restricted policy contract; never add a second resolver.

**Owner note (deciding)**
Criterion 2 says the default never grants. Ratified D-SCRIPT-CONFIRM1=A (#3705) says Enter or `y` runs a script once. Recommended resolution (A): #3705 owns the one prompt implementation, and this card keeps only the requirements below. EOF, Escape, unknown input, and no-TTY runs still grant nothing. This plan assumes A.

**Current state**
- `Source/CmdCompile.rs:1196` `resolve_application_authority` is the only authority transaction.
- `:953` `authority_prompt_is_interactive` treats JSON, CI, or non-TTY stdin as non-interactive.
- `:1260-1270`: a non-interactive run reports E1803 and exits.
- `:1274-1281` prints `authority required for [...] — choose once, project, or deny`.
- `:1287-1476`: `once`/`1` gives an invocation grant, and `project`/`2` edits the manifest or inline Package block. Any other input, including empty input, falls through to `_` and denies with E1803. Empty input does not persist a deny.
- `project` without a manifest fails at `:1290-1298`.
- Virtual and outside-root sources fail closed at `:1315-1340`.
- `tests/cli_parts/support.rs:380` `run_budget_update_pty` is an existing openpty harness.

**Changes**
1. `Source/CmdCompile.rs` `resolve_application_authority`: after #3705 lands its `[Y/n/always]` prompt, make EOF, Escape, unknown input, and a closed stdin exit 1 without writing any receipt or deny. Only an explicit `n` records `interactive.deny`.
2. Before `always` or project persistence writes anything, show the exact target path and the diff (inline header vs `package.jet` `authority.holds.allow`). Refuse read-only, virtual, stale (source hash changed since the projection), malformed, or ambiguous targets with the existing E1362 or authority-transaction diagnostics. Existing denies, comments, and unrelated fields must survive byte-for-byte.
3. Once #3418 lands, select the restricted-mode prompt eligibility from its resolver output only.
4. Generalize `run_budget_update_pty` into `run_pty(dir, args, answer)` in `tests/cli_parts/support.rs`.

**Proof**
- `cargo test --test cli_surface -- authority_prompt_eof_and_unknown_grant_nothing`: the PTY answers `\x04`, `\x1b\n`, and `maybe\n` each exit 1. No `.jet/receipts/authority.jsonl` row is written, and no effect runs.
- `cargo test --test cli_surface -- authority_always_previews_exact_diff_and_refuses_readonly`: `always` on a read-only script fails closed, and the source is unchanged.
- `cargo test --test cli_surface -- fix_all_inserts_script_inline_authority_block` still passes.

**Batch**
`batch-host-cli`: the prompt lives in retained Source/ CLI host code.

**Dependencies**
- #3705 (the prompt itself).
- #3418 (restricted-mode eligibility only).

Use isolated harmless fixtures. Cover numbered/menu choices, Enter, Escape, EOF, invalid input, NO_COLOR, JSON, no TTY, stdin preservation, read-only/virtual/ambiguous sources, stale revisions, transaction failure, and required receipt failure. Prove canceled or denied operations cause no effect. Preserve existing focused transaction regressions rather than asserting old prompt wording or obsolete default eligibility.

cards.title: Separate execution lint visibility from diagnostic enforcement
cards.body:
## Outcome

Show advisory lints in check/build and editor Problems, but keep ordinary run/dev/test output quiet unless the user explicitly requests advisories.

## Shared stream contract

This card owns its Outcome, implementation plan, and criteria. The rules below are shared context for the complete idea stream. Sibling cards own the other portions; they are not duplicate acceptance work on this card.

- Check/build show ordinary advisory lints. Run/dev/test do not unless explicitly requested.
- Errors, runtime failures, authority denials, and explicitly denied lints remain enforced; no semantic-check suppression.
- Editor advisories visible in Problems and appropriate inline markers; no popups/focus stealing; full what/why/fix on demand.

## Origin and authority

Source idea `brh9sr28`, recorded 2026-09-14T14:11:53.190Z:

Are lints usually printed when running a program/script? I understand errors but having lint stuff is a little annoying/distracting when just trying to test functionality
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Advisory lints show in check/build and in editor Problems, but ordinary run/dev/test output stays quiet unless the user passes the existing `--verbose`/`-v` (before `--`). Errors, runtime failures, authority denials and explicitly denied lints stay enforced. D-LINT-VISIBILITY2 option A: no new `--lints` flag. D-A11YGATE1 and the other opt-in lint categories are unchanged.

**Current state**
- The policy is implemented in `Source/OutputAdapter.rs:73-93` (`advisory_lints_visible` = `verbose || !matches!(self, Run | Dev | Test)`), in commits a4e1fd6dd and 247445f8f. Criterion 6 is met.
- `tests/lint_visibility_wave_a.rs` covers check/build/run (:54) and dev watch-off (:104). There is no `jet test` cell, no enforcement matrix and no JSON cell.
- LSP: `Source/LSP/Server.rs:937` renders diagnostics with severity, code and codeDescription. There is no test for advisory severity or for the absence of showMessage.
- Lint-command filtering lives in `Source/CmdDevTools.rs`. The old citation `crates/jet-codegen/src/Source/CmdDevTools.rs` is stale.

**Changes**
1. No Jet compiler change: this is CLI/LSP presentation only.
2. `tests/lint_visibility_wave_a.rs`:
   - `test_hides_advisories_unless_verbose`: `jet test` with a passing `#Test` hides the advisory by default, shows it with `-v`, and aggregates the pass count unchanged.

3. `tests/lsp.rs`: add `lsp_publishes_advisories_without_show_message`.
4. Fix any failing cell in `OutputAdapter.rs` or `Source/LSP/Server.rs` only. Update the affected diagnostic snapshots and CLI help, and do not re-pin incidental wording.

**Proof**
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test lint_visibility_wave_a` → pass.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test lsp -- lsp_publishes_advisories_without_show_message --exact` → pass.
- Real-editor evidence (criterion 5): one VS Code session screenshot/transcript showing the advisory in Problems with no popup, attached to the card.

**Batch**
batch-host-cli: Source/ output adapter, CLI and LSP.

**Dependencies**
None.

cards.title: Make one authored source the default small-program workflow
cards.body:
## Outcome

Adopt one authored .jet source with inline package facts for suitable examples, scaffolds, dogfood, and benchmarks. Generated lock files remain allowed; real multi-file applications remain real.

## Shared stream contract

This card owns its Outcome, implementation plan, and criteria. The rules below are shared context for the complete idea stream. Sibling cards own the other portions; they are not duplicate acceptance work on this card.

- Disposable generated state goes in platform user cache, separated by canonical project/target identity. Intentionally saved portable project data stays owned by project; no per-input-file .jet debris.
- One authored source file is repository-wide default for suitable examples/scaffolds/dogfood/benchmarks. Put necessary metadata/policy in package {}; generated reproducibility locks allowed. Real multi-file apps stay multi-file.
- Gauntlet workflow matched per cell, standalone default; real package cells put all peers in comparable package workflows. No Jet-only preparation.
- Expose first-use setup, cold/warm build, execution and source-to-result totals separately, retaining per-metric losses. Never average away losses or rewrite historical receipts.
- Current internal operational caches .jet may contain saved/audit/sensitive state: classify before migration, preserve protected roots and links, do not blanket-delete. Existing .jet trees outside owned disposable data are not authorized collateral deletion.

## Origin and authority

Source idea `bsl93wcp`, recorded 2026-09-14T18:24:32.543Z:

Consider cleanup for .jet/ dirs EVERYWHERE in the project. So messy, especially compared to all the other types. We also need to prefer single file jet, not separate package files. We want to evaluate parity between jet and other languages in gauntlet, so having packages estabilished for jet but not other languages is not a direct or fair comparison, pick one.

## Distinct ownership

The matching cards #3421 share original idea provenance, not this outcome. This card owns only the implementation boundary and observable criteria stated above.

## Goal
Make one authored `.jet` source with inline `package {}` facts the default for suitable examples, scaffolds, dogfood and gauntlet benchmarks. Generated locks stay; real multi-file applications stay multi-file.

## Authority
- D-SINGLEFILE-DEFAULT2=A is ratified (triage 2026-09-28).
- Reuse D-ECO-INLINEPACKAGE1 for the metadata; invent no new format.
- Owner idea `bsl93wcp`: prefer single-file Jet, and match gauntlet workflows fairly across languages.
- Shared stream rules: disposable state goes under the selected `.jet` root (#3421, D-GENERATED-STORAGE2=B). Classify protected data before any migration; no blanket deletes.

## Current state
- `git ls-files` counts 105 `Examples/**/package.jet` and 24 `Tools/gauntlet/entries/*/jet/package.jet` (53 tracked files across the gauntlet jet dirs).
- The scaffold points the wrong way. `Source/main.rs:7245-7307` `run_init` writes `package.jet` through `jetpack::JetPin::write_init` (`:7295`), and `lift_inline_deps_into_manifest` (`:7312`) copies the script's inline deps *into* the manifest.
- Inline package facts and authority holds already exist in `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Package/mod.rs:83-253` (PackageFacts, PackagePolicy, PackageAuthority), so #3418 is not needed.
- `Source/ReceiptStore.rs:1384-1621` keys identity on package, workspace, lock and generated roots.

## Changes
1. Inventory the 105 example manifests and 24 gauntlet manifests in `Docs/audits/single-file-inventory-<date>.md`. Classify each as standalone (migrate) or genuinely multi-file (keep), with the concrete reason: imports across files, assets, multiple outputs, workspace members.
2. Migrate the standalone programs: fold `package.jet` facts into an inline `package {}` block with explicit authority, and delete the manifest only when every fact survives inline. Keep `.jet/lock` and saved outputs, and never use `--trust` to make an example pass.
3. Gauntlet: Jet cells become single-file where peers are single-file. Real package cells put every peer in a comparable package workflow (#3423 owns the metrics).
4. Scaffold: `jet init <script>` keeps an inline `package {}` in the script and writes no `package.jet`. The existing multi-file path stays behind an explicit flag. Migrate the Jetpack/ port equivalent in step with #3590.
5. Every migrated executable follows the explicit-entry law (#3122) and writes generated state only under the shared root (#3421).
6. Migrate docs, goldens and automation in the same commit.

## Proof
- `cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes, with the changed set byte-identical on AOT, run and interpreter.
- `cargo test --test pkg` passes.
- A scratch `jet init hello.jet` creates no `package.jet`, and `jet run hello.jet` works.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry wordfreq` still matches `expected.out`.
- The inventory lists every kept multi-file example with its reason.

## Batch
batch-host-cli. The scaffold lives in the CLI host; the examples ride the same golden retest.

## Dependencies
#3122 (explicit entries), #3421 (storage root, building). #3418 is not a prerequisite.

cards.title: Match gauntlet workflows and expose source-to-result costs
cards.body:
## Outcome

Make each gauntlet cell compare equivalent standalone or package workflows and show setup, build, execution, and source-to-result costs separately.

## Shared stream contract

This card owns its Outcome, implementation plan, and criteria. The rules below are shared context for the complete idea stream. Sibling cards own the other portions; they are not duplicate acceptance work on this card.

- Disposable generated state goes in platform user cache, separated by canonical project/target identity. Intentionally saved portable project data stays owned by project; no per-input-file .jet debris.
- One authored source file is repository-wide default for suitable examples/scaffolds/dogfood/benchmarks. Put necessary metadata/policy in package {}; generated reproducibility locks allowed. Real multi-file apps stay multi-file.
- Gauntlet workflow matched per cell, standalone default; real package cells put all peers in comparable package workflows. No Jet-only preparation.
- Expose first-use setup, cold/warm build, execution and source-to-result totals separately, retaining per-metric losses. Never average away losses or rewrite historical receipts.
- Current internal operational caches .jet may contain saved/audit/sensitive state: classify before migration, preserve protected roots and links, do not blanket-delete. Existing .jet trees outside owned disposable data are not authorized collateral deletion.

## Origin and authority

Source idea `bsl93wcp`, recorded 2026-09-14T18:24:32.543Z:

Consider cleanup for .jet/ dirs EVERYWHERE in the project. So messy, especially compared to all the other types. We also need to prefer single file jet, not separate package files. We want to evaluate parity between jet and other languages in gauntlet, so having packages estabilished for jet but not other languages is not a direct or fair comparison, pick one.

## Distinct ownership

The matching cards #3421, #3422 share original idea provenance, not this outcome. This card owns only the implementation boundary and observable criteria stated above.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Make each gauntlet cell compare equivalent standalone or package workflows across all peers, and show first-use setup, cold/warm build, execution and source-to-result costs separately. Source idea `bsl93wcp` (2026-09-14): "…having packages established for jet but not other languages is not a direct or fair comparison, pick one."

**Current state**
- Harness owners (moved from `gauntlet/`): Tools/gauntlet/measurement-manifest.json (24 entries; schema, cells, tiers, verdicts), Tools/gauntlet/matrix.json (rails at :64-67, strict policy), Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs (entry validation, build/run, scoreboard), status.mjs, integrated-gate.mjs (supported tiers aot/run), timer.py (wall_seconds, peak RSS, time-to-first-stdout), live-reload.mjs.
- Cache owners: Source/RunCache.rs (warm run cache in ~/.cache/jet/run), Source/RecordIndex.rs (project .jet/records index), Source/ReceiptStore.rs (target identity roots). Existing .jet trees may hold saved/audit/sensitive state: classify, never blanket-delete.
- Blockers: #3404 (peer rails and one JS identity, ready) and #3422 (single-authored-source default, planning).

**Changes**
1. Consume #3404's rails unchanged. Inventory each cell's source layout, dependency setup, generated locks, cache state, build and launch commands and edit lifecycle.
2. Standalone workflow by default; when the task genuinely needs a package, every applicable peer uses a comparable package workflow. No Jet-only setup, warmup, trust grants or hidden precompilation.
3. Adopt #3422's single-authored-source default with inline `package {}` policy where applicable; real multi-file workloads stay multi-file.
4. Measure first-use setup, cold build, warm build, execution and source-to-result with exact boundaries (plus startup, first-result and edit-to-result for run/dev); distinguish source-only cold state from pre-installed toolchains.
5. Carry these metrics through manifest, runner, raw receipts, status, integrated gate and the Tower gauntlet view; the strict per-metric comparator applies, totals never hide a component loss.
6. Historical receipts stay unchanged and are labelled incomparable where needed.

**Proof**
- `node --test Tools/gauntlet/harness/` passes with new cases: a Jet-only preparation step fails validation; a total that hides a component loss still fails the gate.
- Paired runs `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry wordfreq` (standalone) and one real package entry show the five metrics per peer; then the full affected matrix.

**Batch**
batch-host-cli: gauntlet measurement tooling.

**Dependencies**
#3404 (peer rails), #3422 (single-authored-source default).

cards.title: Ordinary #Transact fails rollback and LIFO hook semantics
cards.body: Fresh shipped examples errors/transact.jet and errors/rollback_trait.jet exit 0 but violate their contracts: commit hooks run 1 then 2 instead of LIFO 2 then 1; failed transactions leave -50/150 and -140/240 instead of restoring 100/0 and 60/40; explicit rollback hook is omitted. Existing Shared-transaction and FFI-undo cards do not own ordinary #Transact lifecycle.
cards.plan: Repair the canonical ordinary transaction snapshot/undo lifecycle and hook stack. Preserve Shared and FFI #Undo semantics. Prove both shipped examples plus failure/success boundaries on default, interpreter, AOT and applicable Web with exact goldens; no alternate transaction mechanism.

log.text: A bounded repair proved the interpreter already produces the exact transact.jet lifecycle: commit hooks LIFO, failed automatic transfer restored to 100/0, and rollback hook fires once. A proposed TransactionSnapshot MIR closure then exposed an incomplete JIT ABI: CoreClosureCall supplied only a handle, while rollback needs place identity plus captured value; a unary host would be a no-op and cannot restore caller-visible state. The entire incomplete TransactionSnapshot cutover was reverted. Final source check is green: `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 scripts/agent/jet-env cargo check -p jet-codegen` finished in 53.67s. All criteria stay open because default/AOT/Web still lack one complete place-aware snapshot mechanism. Anti-loop cutoff applied; no fake registration retained.

criteria.text: Commit hooks run LIFO on success and are discarded on failure; rollback hooks run LIFO only on failure.
criteria.evidence: Compared fresh default/interpreter output with committed transact.out.

criteria.text: Automatic snapshots and Rollback trait state restore caller-visible values exactly after ? failure.
criteria.evidence: Compared fresh automatic/custom rollback balances with committed goldens; focused regression passed.

criteria.text: transact.jet and rollback_trait.jet match exact goldens on default, interpreter, AOT and applicable Web tiers.
criteria.evidence: Independent Main execution observed both direct tiers restore balances to 60/40 and exact dev_tier_parity complete 1 passed, 0 failed with the rollback_trait stem.

D-UNIFYLIT/D-TEXTHEAD require checked HTML holes to compose as markup while untrusted String holes escape exactly once. SQL binding behavior is not the defect.
cards.plan: Preserve the existing checked-text trust fact through sema, TIR, Prelude and JIT/AOT adapters. Use one composition mechanism: trusted HTML holes remain markup, untrusted strings escape once. Prove exact shipped output across tiers without weakening SQL/raw-text safety.

log.text: Closed on explicit trusted-hole metadata propagation, exact checked_text_sql interpreter/JIT/AOT golden parity, SQL safety preservation, and CHECK OK.

Final trusted-hole metadata propagation attempt broke the shared compiler gate (an unupdated SQL TypedTextInterp pattern) before behavior proof. Per the two-cycle anti-loop cap, the full attempt was surgically reverted and the prior compiler-green state restored. Existing exact failure remains: nested checked `<strong>` is escaped; ordinary user text escaping is not accepted as closure.

Integrated focused proof remains red after the binding-type evaluator change: `cargo test --test checked_text html_composition_matches_aot_jit_interpreter_and_web -- --nocapture` failed 1/1. Actual nested composition escapes the already-checked strong node as `<strong>safe</strong>`; expected `safe`. The retained edit did not close composition semantics; criteria remain open and no retry loop was run.

cards.title: Generated interrupt handlers violate the unsafe-region invariant
cards.body: The focused tooling/debug_native golden reaches generated Rust, then tests/golden.rs:568 rejects five interrupt-handler unsafe lines for jet_interrupt_mark, POSIX signal registration, and SetConsoleCtrlHandler outside vetted generated memory/stdlib internals. This is an I1 compiler defect, not an example-output failure.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Generated interrupt/signal code stays inside the vetted Prelude unsafe boundary (I1). The `tooling/debug_native` golden passes unchanged on a freshly rebuilt compiler.

**Current state**
- Criterion 1 is met. The interrupt FFI now lives in the vetted Prelude file `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Interrupt.rs` (the triage cited a path without `Top/`):
  - `jet_interrupt_mark` for unix at :125 and windows at :141.
  - `SetConsoleCtrlHandler` at :199-220.
  - Generated user Rust no longer carries these unsafe lines.
- The golden unsafe-region scanner is in `tests/golden.rs` (baseline check near :568-574) and is not weakened.
- Criterion 2 is open. The 2026-09-15 proof run stopped on `record budget exceeded` (E2105) in the golden harness, which is why #3416 was attached. That failure came from the old 200-record count cap. `Source/RecordIndex.rs:27` now uses a 256 MiB byte-only FIFO with whole-group eviction (`eviction_groups` :1102), and no count cap remains (see #3415). The harness should no longer hit that failure, so #3416 (decoupling the test exit status from optional history) is not a prerequisite for this golden.
- Fixture: `Examples/features/tooling/debug_native.jet` → `Examples/features/expected/tooling/debug_native.out`.

**Changes**
1. None is expected. Rebuild and run the golden.
2. If the golden still fails on an unsafe-region line, move the offending emission into `Interrupt.rs` behind the existing `JET_VETTED_UNSAFE` marker. Never allow-list it in the scanner.
3. If it fails on E2105 again, attach the exact stderr to #3416 and re-add the blocker. Do not raise the budget.
4. The Jet compiler emitter (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit`) must reference only the Prelude helper, with no inline `unsafe` signal code. Confirm this with a grep for `SetConsoleCtrlHandler|sigaction` under `Compiler/`.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=tooling/debug_native Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` → passes, output byte-equal to `expected/tooling/debug_native.out`.
- `node Tools/agent/check-unsafe-ratchet.mjs` → no new unsafe region.
- `Tools/agent/lane-check.sh` on the touched lane → `CHECK OK`.

**Batch**
batch-host-runtime: a Prelude runtime boundary plus an AOT golden.

**Dependencies**

cards.title: Use L1/L2/L3 facts in bounded automatic acceleration
cards.body:
The owner wants automatic CPU-cache-aware optimization without new source ceremony. D-SIMD3 and D-ACCEL1 already approve automatic vectorization and measured, bounded acceleration.

Current source uses a fixed 64 KiB copy block and a measured memory-bandwidth floor. Acceleration inputs and selected-target facts do not describe L1, L2, L3, or their sharing. This is source evidence from 2026-09-16, not a fresh performance result.

Extend the existing acceleration cost model with trustworthy cache information. Do not create another scheduler, optimizer, marker, or public command. Keep current host-native and cross-target compilation behavior.

This is separate from #2874's nbody loss, #2889's columnar loss, #2890's copied loops, and #2922's explicit parallel gate. Their existing homes and acceptance terms remain intact. Preparation only; no implementation or benchmark ran in this session.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Bounded automatic acceleration accounts for the L1/L2/L3 capacity and sharing of the executing CPU, as optimization evidence and never as a language guarantee. It adds no source ceremony, scheduler, marker or command (D-SIMD3, D-ACCEL1).

## Current state
- Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Target/TargetMachine.jet has no cache-level facts.
- Compiler/JetOptimizer/Source/Facts/AccelerationDecisionLedger.jet:192-195 ledger rows have no cache facts.
- The runtime gate in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/ParallelPlan.rs:55-163 costs spawn and bandwidth, with a fixed 64 KiB copy block and a measured bandwidth floor, and no cache model.
- The previous plan owned archived crates/jet-foundation TargetMachine.rs and MIROptimization/Acceleration.rs.

## Changes
1. TargetMachine.jet: internal CacheFacts per level: usable capacity, line size, sharing (private/shared, core set), and status (Known/Unknown/Mixed/Virtualized). Build host and execution target stay distinct; a cross target without trustworthy facts is Unknown, with no invented capacities.
2. JetOptimizer acceleration derivation: use cache facts to judge nested reuse against per-worker storage and shared-cache pressure. Unknown keeps today's conservative plan. The size gate, benefit gate, 1024-item floor, #Scalar/#Local and legality gates still control every candidate. Nothing enlarges the D-ACCEL1 scratch budget or the worker count.
3. AccelerationDecisionLedger.jet: record the cache facts used and the accept/reject reason. Cached decisions are keyed to the execution target.
4. Retained host: platform cache discovery in jet-rt host bindings. ParallelPlan.rs consumes the same facts at run time.
5. Add Tools/gauntlet/entries/cache-locality: the #2889 particle workload with a nested-reuse case and a single-pass rejection control, paired enabled/disabled.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=lowlevel/simd_auto_loop cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` and the same run under `jet run --interpret` are unchanged (same output with facts known or Unknown).
- `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry cache-locality --runs 5` passes under the current per-metric policy. A losing or inconclusive cell leaves criterion 5 open.

## Batch
batch-jetc-back: JetOptimizer decision plus target facts. The host gate rides along.

## Dependencies
#3039 (carried loop/access proof), #2922 (shared ParallelPlan gate), #2889 (particle workload reused by the entry).

cards.title: Prove caller-owned fixed storage across execution modes
cards.body:
The owner wants precise low-level memory control without losing safety. Existing law already covers caller-owned backing, bounded allocation, lifetime checks, alignment, address stability, and fallible allocation. Those choices do not need another ballot.

One narrow proof gap remains in the inspected source. The Fixed.over language fixture runs through generated Rust in tests/allocator_families.rs. The allocator mode comparison uses Fixed.new instead. Fixed.over has no checked-in executable example and shared golden in the inspected examples.

Use the existing 128-byte caller buffer and payload 9 as the concrete control witness. Add the missing executable example and cross-mode lifecycle proof. This is verification debt, not evidence that the implementation is broken.

Do not duplicate completed #1889, #1926, #2887, #3059, or #3424. Do not reactivate #217's deferred bootstrap campaign. Source was inspected on 2026-09-16; no runtime proof ran during preparation.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Prove caller-owned fixed storage with a checked-in example that runs on every execution mode. `Fixed.over` must allocate typed values in a caller buffer, reuse dead storage, report typed exhaustion and close safely, with no heap fallback. This is verification debt, not a new API. Existing law already covers backing, bounds, lifetime, alignment, stability and fallible allocation.

**Current state**
- The only witness is `tests/allocator_families.rs:425-446`: `bytes := [U8#128]{ uninit }`, `fixed :: mem.Fixed.over(&bytes)`, `value :: fixed.alloc(9)`, `print(value)`, `close(^fixed)`. It asserts generated-Rust text `JetFixed::over_uninit_fixed(&mut __jet_bytes)` and runs AOT only, expecting `9\n`.
- The allocator mode comparison uses `Fixed.new` (:448-457), and the borrow-conflict fixture is at :516-520.
- `Examples/features/memory/` has no `fixed_backing*` example and there is no golden. That directory currently carries other uncommitted edits (receiver-mark wave), so touch only the new files.

**Changes**
1. Add `Examples/features/memory/fixed_backing.jet`, using the 128-byte caller buffer and payload 9 as the control witness. It allocates two typed values, lets one die, then reuses its storage (showing the offset is reused). It exhausts with a typed `E!` failure handled by `??`, reports alignment and offsets of drop records from inside the backing range, then calls `close(^fixed)`. Add `Examples/features/expected/memory/fixed_backing.out`.
2. Add UI fixtures for live-view reset or close, conflicting backing access, escape and task crossing, under `tests/ui/fixed_backing_*.jet` with `.stderr`, using the ratified codes. Include one positive last-use-before-reset case.
3. Repair any defect found in the existing sema or runtime path, with a focused regression in `tests/allocator_families.rs`. Do not add a new allocator API.

**Proof**
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=memory/fixed_backing Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes (AOT).
- `JET_CORPUS_GATE_FILTER=memory/fixed_backing Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev_corpus_gate -- example_corpus_strict_jit_aot_differential_gate` passes, with default run equal to AOT and an interpreter row either equal or refused with a recorded code.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=fixed_backing Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test allocator_families` passes.

**Batch**
`batch-host-runtime`: the `JetFixed` runtime with a three-tier golden.

**Dependencies**
None.
