cards.title: Jai vs Jet: interview closeout — callable respell, build model, meta ceiling
cards.body:
Umbrella for the Jai-vs-Jet interview (owner grill 2026-09-16, brief: docs/research/jai-vs-jet-fable-brief-2026-09-16.md). The interview is complete; this card links the ballots and records the settled tree so nothing from the thread is lost. Owner asked for ballots and cards only, no separate report.

## Settled by owner (constraints for every child ballot)

Syntax
- One callable shape: `fn name(params) -> T { }`; `fn name(params) -[E]> T !Err { }`; unit `fn run() { }`; effectful unit `fn announce() -[IO]> { }`. Braces mandatory on named function and method bodies. Function types `fn(Int) -> Int`, `fn(Int) -[IO]> Int`. `struct`/`enum`/`trait`/`impl`/`module` stay items (Column A). Illegal: any second arrow (`-> Int -> { }`, `-> Int -[IO]> { }`, `-[IO]> -> Int`).
- Lambdas: `x -> body`, `(a: Int) -[IO]> { … }`; no written return or error type (amends D-LAMBDA-IFACE1=A). `if` / `loop` / arm one-liners keep `->`.
- Two return values: keep `T !E` plus tuples/structs. `(q, r) :: f()` already ships (`(tx, rx) :: channel<Int>()`), so no unpack card.
- Const generics now (R4): `struct Packet<@N: Int> { data: [U8#@N] }`, use `Packet<64>` / `Packet<@lanes>`; narrow S26 amendment; `Meta.Const` named with it.
- Cutover: one paired law+implementation card; old spellings become teaching diagnostics; no dual period.

Build
- Compile-time work is ordinary functions; `fn build` is a short compile-time main. `b`/`BuildContext` is the plan only: `add_executable`, `generate`, `plan`, `action` (outside executables). `find` / `embed_file` / `fetch(url, sha256:)` are ordinary functions governed by the effect row (`-[Net]>`, `-[!Net]>`, package deny); unpinned compile-time IO stays behind `#Impure`; the lockfile records files and hashes.
- `b.generate("name", value)` takes a typed template value (`generate { items with holes }` -> `Generated`); today's inline block is the same thing written in place; raw source strings refused. In-tree materialization is opt-in per package, still lock-hashed; drift fails the build.
- `b.include(opengl)`: the package's own `fn build` runs with a fresh BuildContext rooted at its package, reads only its own directory and its pinned URLs, and its fragment merges into your plan. Never pass your `b`; never run on import. Helper functions you call see only the values you pass. Amends "dependency entries are checked and never run".
- Root `fn build` lists its ceiling explicitly: `fn build(b: BuildContext) -[FS, Net, Meta.Generate, Meta.Include]> BuildPlan`; unlisted is an error; package policy may deny.

Meta
- Ladder R0-R4 ships: bake (`@x :: f()`), root `fn build` generate/observe/action, helpers + sandboxed include, named sibling derives (`ParticleSoa` as a real file), const generics. Refused: splice into existing code, token/AST macros, types-as-values / use-site type factories, in-place rewrite, a type with no file, ambient `#run`.
- `Meta.Generate` and `Meta.Include` named now; `Meta.Reflect` ungated; `Meta.Const` with const generics; Rewrite/Tokens never named.

Context
- D-CTX1 (`#Context(field: value) { … }`) and D-DEADLINE1 already exist and are the binder. Owner: unclear what more is gained; parked on a frozen child card for later discussion.

## Facts established (do not re-ask)
- `.claude/ballot-arrow-unify.json` is stale: D-ARROW-UNIFY1=B ratified 2026-08-20, superseded by D-ARROW-RESPELL1=A.
- Current law: D-SIG-SHAPE1=B + D-CALLABLE-ONE1=A (`fn double(n: Int) Int -> n * 2`; `fn load(p: String) String -[IO]> { }`), D-EFFECT-ROW2=B fused row, D-FAILURE-FOUNDATION1=A prefix failure roles.
- Tower refuses `short` for `group: syntax`; the three syntax ballots are `full`; the four build/meta ballots are `short`, owner-authorized in chat 2026-09-16.


## Ballots minted (all ballot-ready, 2026-09-16)

| Decision | Card | Mode | Rec |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-SIG-AFTER1 | #3503 | full | A: `fn f(n: Int) -> Int { }`, braces on named bodies |
| D-LAMBDA-IFACE2 | #3504 | full | A: lambdas write params + effect row only |
| D-CONSTGEN1 | #3505 | full | A: `struct Packet<@N: Int>`; option D keeps S26 |
| D-BUILD-IO1 | #3506 | short | A: `find`/`embed_file`/`fetch` are ordinary functions; `b` is the plan only |
| D-BUILD-GENVALUE1 | #3507 | short | A: `b.generate` takes a typed template value |
| D-BUILD-INCLUDE1 | #3508 | short | A: `b.include(pkg)` runs the package build sandboxed with its rights |
| D-META-GATE1 | #3509 | short | A: `Meta.*` capabilities on effect machinery; Tokens/Rewrite refused |

Frozen: #3502 (context: visibility, typed keys, task/FFI edges on top of D-CTX1). Owner: 'not clear what we gain from introducing context'; discuss later.

Review provenance: the three syntax ballots ran beginner and adversarial passes through stateless fresh completions because subagents were over quota; the adversarial pass returned 'recommendation weak' on D-SIG-AFTER1 and D-LAMBDA-IFACE2 and each was repaired (option D `=` bodies and option C anonymous `fn` added as fair alternatives, with why-nots). Short profile for the four build/meta ballots was owner-authorized in chat; the syntax group is code-gated to full ballots, so those three went full regardless.

cards.title: Callable respell: return type after the one arrow, braces on named bodies
cards.body:
Owner gate from the Jai-vs-Jet interview. Today (D-SIG-SHAPE1=B, D-CALLABLE-ONE1=A) the return type sits bare after the parameter list and `->` introduces the body: `fn double(n: Int) Int -> n * 2`, `fn load(p: String) String -[IO]> { … }`. The owner's proposal moves the type to the other side of the one arrow and makes braces mandatory on named function and method bodies: `fn double(n: Int) -> Int { n * 2 }`, `fn load(p: String) -[IO]> String !IOError { … }`. Unit bodies stay `fn run() { }` and `fn announce() -[IO]> { }`. Function types follow: `fn(Int) -> Int`, `fn(Int) -[IO]> Int`. Control one-liners (`if c -> x`, `loop x in xs -> f(x)`, arm tables) and lambdas keep `->` as the body arrow; that is the same glyph in a different position, not a second arrow on a function.

Refused in the interview: any second arrow on a function (`-> Int -> { }`, `-> Int -[IO]> { }`, `-[IO]> -> Int`); the bind form `f :: fn(...)` for named callables (Column B) and the full Jai `Name :: struct` unification; dual spelling "for now".

Cutover (owner, Round 3): one paired card lands law entry, parser, `jet fmt` rewrite, grammars, editor packs, examples, and docs together; the old spellings become teaching diagnostics with no alias; the repository is never in two spellings. D-SIG-SHAPE1 measured 427 declared return types and 34 effect ceilings over 600 examples; this respell touches those plus every named one-liner body.

## Exit criteria (after ratification)
1. Parser accepts only the ratified shape; old shape is a teaching diagnostic with a machine-applicable fix.
2. `jet fmt` rewrites every in-repo `.jet` file in one commit; goldens unchanged.
3. `docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md` entry amends D-SIG-SHAPE1=B and D-CALLABLE-ONE1=A; `docs/spec/reference/syntax-surface.jet` updated.
4. Grammar files, highlighting, LSP completion emit only the new shape.

(or -[Effects]> MyErr!). Keep unit-no-result fn run() {}. Migrate parser, formatter/autofix, Syntax registry and decision rationale, AST/MIR/API signature presentation, diagnostics and UI snapshots, all Core, examples, tests and generated/editor grammar callers in a single greenfield cutover. Normalize exactly one blank line between function declarations; replace chained branch guards with ordered arm tables where semantically equivalent. Do not enable old prefix or arrowless aliases. Focused proof: parser/formatter idempotence, diagnostic snapshot(s), actual default JIT/interpreter/AOT examples and golden outputs. Source and current diagnostic evidence are in the 2026-09-24 log; no syntax cutover is claimed before all paths and tier proof pass.

cards.title: Lambda interface under type-after-arrow: params and effect row only
cards.body:
Companion to D-SIG-AFTER1. D-LAMBDA-IFACE1=A lets a lambda write any suffix of the callable interface: `increment :: (n: Int) Int !LambdaError -[]> Ok(n + 1)`. Once the return type moves after the arrow on named functions, a lambda that writes a type collides with a lambda whose body is a struct literal: `x -> Point{x: 1}` (expression body) versus `x -> Point { block }` (type then block). Owner's call (Round 1 and Round 3): lambdas keep `params -> expr` and `params -> { block }` and may write an effect row with the fused arrow (`(a: Int) -[IO]> { … }`); they do not write a return or error type. Those come from the expected type or from a typed parameter or field (`f: fn(Int) -> Int !E`).

## Exit criteria (after ratification)
1. Parser rejects a written return/error type on a lambda with a teaching diagnostic naming the typed-binding form.
2. `examples/features/callable/lambda_interface.jet` respelled; inference law (D-LAMBDA-INFER1) untouched.
3. Spec entry amends D-LAMBDA-IFACE1=A.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement ratified D-LAMBDA-IFACE2=A under type-after-arrow. A lambda writes `params -> expr`, `params -> { block }`, or with an effect row `params -[IO]> body` (`-[]>` means none; plain `->` adopts the expected row). It never writes a return or error type. Those come from the expected type or a typed binding (`f: fn(Int) -> Int E! :: n -> …`). A written parameter type must equal the expected one, and a written row must fit the expected row (E0747). D-LAMBDA-INFER1 is untouched.

## Current state
- The Jet parser detects a lambda only when `)` is followed by `TOKEN_LAMBDA_ARROW` (`Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/Expressions.jet:679`). `parser_parse_lambda` (:727-753) expects `->` right after the parameters. So `(a: Int) -[IO]> { }` is not recognized as a lambda, and a written result type fails with a generic "`->` after lambda parameters" error.
- The effect row is parsed for named functions in `Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/Items.jet:695-711` (`TOKEN_MINUS` + `TOKEN_LBRACKET` … `]`, then `>`). There is no shared helper.
- The example still teaches the retired full interface: `Examples/features/callable/lambda_interface.jet:1,7` (`increment :: (n: Int) Int LambdaError! -[]> Ok(n + 1)`, citing D-LAMBDA-IFACE1=A).
- Docs: only D-LAMBDA-IFACE1=A is recorded (`Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:7540-7543`), with the `Syntax.rs:273-275` comment "gives lambdas the same interface suffixes". Related UI fixtures exist: `tests/ui/lambda_interface_{result,error,effect}_mismatch.jet`.

## Changes
1. Jet parser: factor the effect-row parse out of `Items.jet` into one helper used by both named functions and lambdas. Lambda lookahead accepts `)` followed by `->` or by an effect row ending in `>`. A type or `E!` between `)` and the arrow gets the teaching diagnostic (new registry row in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet`), with recovery.
2. Jet sema (`Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Expressions/Lambdas.jet`): the lambda result and error come only from the expected type. The written row is checked against the expected row (E0747).
3. Rust bootstrap mirror so the corpus parses: the same lookahead, rejection and row parse in `crates/jet-parser`.
4. Migrate: respell `lambda_interface.jet` and its golden; update or retire the three `lambda_interface_*_mismatch` fixtures (the result and error forms become the new diagnostic; the effect-row mismatch stays E0747). Update `Syntax.rs`, add a syntax-decisions entry for D-LAMBDA-IFACE2=A amending IFACE1, regenerate `jet devtools grammars` and re-bless snapshots.

## Proof
The two added criteria cover the parser (Jet and Rust), sema, example, snapshots and three tiers.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-front`: a lambda surface cutover plus the Rust parser mirror.

## Dependencies
None. D-LAMBDA-IFACE2 is ratified A.

cards.title: Compile-time IO is ordinary functions; BuildContext is the plan only
cards.body:
Owner gate from the Jai-vs-Jet interview. The owner rejected `b.fetch` / `b.find` / `b.embed` as a second IO system next to effects ("The effect system should catch a network request and block it based on project declarations or `-[!Net]>` in the build signature"). Settled: `find`, `embed_file`, `fetch(url, sha256:)` are ordinary functions governed by the effect row and package policy; the lockfile records the exact files and hashes (effects cannot do that job); unpinned compile-time IO stays behind `#Impure`. `b` keeps only the plan: `add_executable` and siblings, `generate`, `plan`, and `action` for an outside executable (a cached graph node). `fn build` is a short compile-time main: read inputs, call helper functions, fill the plan, return. Helper logic lives in ordinary functions called at build time, never inside `b.action` / `b.generate` blocks. Root `fn build` writes its ceiling explicitly, e.g. `fn build(b: BuildContext) -[FS, Net, Meta.Generate, Meta.Include]> BuildPlan`.

## Exit criteria (after ratification)
1. `BuildContext` exposes no IO methods; `find` / `embed_file` / `fetch` are checked as ordinary effectful calls inside the comptime interpreter.
2. Example: sprite atlas built by `find` -> `pack_sprites` (function) -> `b.generate`; a `-[!Net]>` build entry rejects `fetch` at compile time.
3. `docs/spec/reference/metaprogramming.md` updated; law entry recorded.

## Owner scope extension — 2026-09-21

## Outcome

Finish D-BUILD-IO1 under the selected trusted/restricted policy and shared prep model. Reuse ordinary functions for files, search, embedding, network and output; BuildContext retains plan operations, not a parallel IO vocabulary. Wire real output sinks and authority at prep/build entry and helper calls. Record concrete file/URL/tool inputs and hashes separately from effect permission.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime
- crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude
- crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs
- crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Lock.rs

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

Extend build_entry and a sprite-atlas/prep-input witness. Read files, compute data, print, embed bytes and generate a called declaration across relevant phases/tiers. Deny Net/FS at outer and inner ceilings and from a dependency; require no effect occurs. Change input content and verify invalidation; prove stdout is fresh on a pure cache hit.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-BUILD-IO1=A, which the owner has ratified. At compile time, `find`, `embed_file` and `fetch(url, sha256:)` are ordinary effectful functions: the effect row and package policy govern them, and the lock records the exact files and hashes. `BuildContext` keeps only plan operations (`add_executable` and siblings, `generate`, `plan`, `action`). Unpinned compile-time IO stays behind `#Impure`. The root `fn build` states its ceiling, e.g. `fn build(b: BuildContext) -[FS, Net, Meta.Generate, Meta.Include]> BuildPlan`.

Owner quote: "The effect system should catch a network request and block it based on project declarations or `-[!Net]>` in the build signature."

## Current state
- The duplicate IO vocabulary lives only in the archived comptime: `crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build/runtime_bridge.rs:823-843` handles `b.find` and `b.fetch`, and `Methods::eval_net_fetch` backs them.
- The self-hosted stack has no BuildContext executor. `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet:8269` has only the build-entry signature row. `Core/build/build.jet:108-113` `graph` panics outside checked build code.
- The Jet lock model lives in `Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Lock/` (`Record.jet`, `Provenance.jet`, `Write.jet`).
- `Docs/spec/reference/metaprogramming.md` is the reference to update. The old `docs/` path is stale.

## Changes
1. Core: add `find(glob)`, `embed_file(path)` and `fetch(url, sha256:)` as ordinary Core functions with effect rows `FS` and `Net`. They must not be BuildContext methods.
2. Sema (`Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Effects/`): check them in prep and build bodies against the declared ceiling. `-[!Net]>` rejects `fetch` at compile time with a registered what/why/fix row and a UI snapshot.
3. Eval (`Compiler/JetEval/Source/CompilerServices.jet`) together with `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/BodyComptime.jet`:
   - execute these functions under prep and build authority;
   - record every concrete file, URL and tool input with its hash, kept separate from effect permission;
   - invalidate on any input change;
   - keep stdout fresh on a pure cache hit.

   The host CLI process keeps only filesystem and network access and grant enforcement.
4. Lock: write the input records to `Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Lock/Record.jet` and `Write.jet`.
5. Remove `b.find` and `b.fetch` from `runtime_bridge.rs` in the same cutover, with the shipped-path mirror of steps 1-3. Update `Docs/spec/reference/metaprogramming.md`.
6. Example: `Examples/features/comptime/sprite_atlas.jet`, which runs `find` → `pack_sprites` (an ordinary function) → `b.generate`.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=comptime/sprite_atlas Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: passes.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/build_io_net_denied Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`: `fetch` is rejected under `-[!Net]>`.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test build_entry -- build_io_inputs_recorded_and_invalidate`: lock hashes are recorded, an input change forces a rerun, and stdout is fresh on a cache hit.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: the effect-row checking of compile-time IO is the core of this card. The eval, lock and doc changes land in the same build.

## Dependencies
- #3520: metaprogramming contract, building.
- #3521: shared prep execution; owns criterion 4.
- #3418: trust defaults versus policy denies; owns criterion 3.

cards.title: b.generate takes a typed template value; in-tree materialization opt-in
cards.body:
Owner gate from the Jai-vs-Jet interview. Today a generated module is written inline: `b.generate("name") { typed items }`. The owner wants the logic in helpers (`sqlx.client_source(sql)`) and `fn build` to only register the result. Settled: a helper returns a typed template value (`generate { items with holes }` is an expression of type `Generated`, the same hole grammar derive templates already use); `b.generate("db_client", value)` renders it under `.jet/generated` and sema checks it as ordinary items; the inline block stays as the same thing written in place; raw source strings are refused (D-META-CODE1=A, real code with holes). In-tree materialization is opt-in per package, still lock-hashed, and the build fails if the committed file drifts from what generate would emit.

## Exit criteria (after ratification)
1. `generate { … }` expression type-checks in a helper file; slips are reported at the helper's line.
2. `b.generate(name, value)` and the inline block produce identical files.
3. Manifest opt-in materializes in-tree; drift is a build error with the diff path named.

## Owner scope extension — 2026-09-21

## Outcome

Finish D-BUILD-GENVALUE1 using one Generated representation and the selected shared publishing interface. Helpers return typed item templates; AOT BuildContext and shared prep publish the same checked values. Support complete item/member/parameter/value generation needed by the workload cards, with explicit name/binding rules. Preserve package-opted in-tree materialization, output ownership and drift errors. Standard mode refuses source strings and mutation of handwritten code.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-foundation/src/AST
- crates/jet-parser/src/Parser
- crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/mod.rs
- crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build/runtime_bridge.rs
- crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

Extend programmable_build so run actually invokes generated_build_message, not a matching literal. Add a helper-returned Generated value and an inline equivalent; compare their behavior and source maps across tiers. Generate a type, impl, constant and function consumed by handwritten code. Check collisions, invalid holes, bad types and opted-in materialization drift.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-BUILD-GENVALUE1=A (ratified): `generate { items with holes }` is an expression of type `Generated`, using the derive-template hole grammar. A helper such as `sqlx.client_source(sql)` returns it, and `b.generate("db_client", value)` registers it. The inline `b.generate("name") { ... }` is the same thing written in place. Raw source strings are refused (D-META-CODE1=A). In-tree materialization is opt-in per package, lock-hashed, and drift is a build error.

## Current state
- No `generate` expression or `Generated` type in Compiler/JetParser or Compiler/JetSema (triage grep). The only self-hosted pieces are the E35xx build-generation rows, Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet:8349-8367 (shadow/cycle), and the BuildContext signature row at :8221.

Examples/features/tooling/programmable_build/ has a golden.
- The owner extension of 2026-09-21 names archived Rust paths (jet-parser, jet-comptime runtime_bridge.rs, jet-driver).

1. JetParser and JetAst: parse `generate { ... }` as an expression into one Generated node (items with holes). The inline `b.generate(name) { ... }` desugars to `b.generate(name, generate { ... })`.
2. JetSema: type it as `Generated`. Holes are checked at the helper's source line, and rendered items are checked as ordinary items. Shadowing handwritten items or passing a String is rejected with the registered E35xx codes.

AOT BuildContext and shared prep use one representation. The only host piece is the filesystem write through the existing fs boundary.

cards.title: b.include(pkg): a package's own fn build runs sandboxed inside yours
cards.body:
Owner gate from the Jai-vs-Jet interview. Current law: imported dependency build entries are checked and never run. The owner asked whether a package's build could be a hook your own `fn build` calls, keeping everything auditable in one file. Settled: `b.include(opengl)` in your `fn build` runs the package's `fn build` with a fresh BuildContext rooted at that package; it may read only its own package directory and fetch only its pinned URLs (WASI-style root, Nix-style fixed-output fetch); its effect row and lock entries are its own; the returned fragment merges into your plan. Never pass your `b` into a dependency; nothing runs on import; a manifest `enable:` list was rejected in favor of a grep-able call. Helper functions you call from a package (`sqlx.client_source(sql)`) see only the values you pass; they are pure over bytes you read and cacheable by input hash; shipped templates use `embed_file` inside their own package.

## Exit criteria (after ratification)
1. `b.include(pkg)` runs the dependency entry under a package-rooted FS sandbox; a read outside it is a compile error naming the path.
2. Lock records which package's build ran and what it emitted.
3. Example: OpenGL-style bindings package emits generated `.jet` through `b.include`; import alone emits nothing.

## Owner scope extension — 2026-09-21

## Outcome

Finish D-BUILD-INCLUDE1: only an explicit b.include in the AOT build entry runs a dependency build, with its own root/context/authority and validated contributions. Shared prep can call ordinary library helpers or explicitly registered providers without running dependency fn build. Imports alone remain inert. Do not pass root mutable BuildContext or unrestricted compiler authority into a dependency.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build
- crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs
- crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Lock.rs
- crates/jetpack/src

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

Extend the binding-package include witness. Compare import-only, ordinary helper call, explicit AOT include and shared-prep provider registration. Require correct emitted modules and real calls, package-root FS enforcement, pinned input provenance, duplicate/conflicting contributions and import cycles. Confirm no dependency build executes under run/interpreter preparation.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-BUILD-INCLUDE1=A, which is ratified. `b.include(pkg)` inside your `fn build` runs that package's `fn build` with a fresh BuildContext rooted at the package. That build:
- may read only its own directory and fetch only its pinned URLs (a WASI-style root plus Nix-style fixed-output fetch);
- has its own effect row and lock entries;
- returns a plan fragment that merges transactionally into yours.

Imports stay inert, and the caller's `b` is never passed to a dependency. A manifest `enable:` list was rejected in favour of a grep-able call. Helpers called from a package (`sqlx.client_source(sql)`) see only the values passed to them, are pure over bytes you read, and can be cached by input hash.

## Current state
- Nothing is implemented. Current law: dependency build entries are checked and never run.
- `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet:8269` has only the build-entry signature row. Neither `Compiler/JetDriver` nor `Compiler/JetEval` has a BuildPlan executor or `b.include`.
- `Core/build/build.jet:108-113` `graph` is a compiler-owned query.
- `Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Policy/EffectBudget.jet:51` carries the `has_build_entry` fact.
- The Jet lock lives in `Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Lock/`.
- The owned paths on the card (`crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build`, `crates/jet-driver`, `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Lock.rs`, `crates/jetpack`) are archived.

## Changes
1. Add `include(pkg)` to the BuildContext plan surface. It is a plan operation, not IO, and it needs the `Meta.Include` effect.
2. Execute it in `Compiler/JetEval/Source/CompilerServices.jet` and `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/BodyComptime.jet`:
   - build a fresh BuildContext and authority rooted at the dependency's package directory;
   - run its `fn build`;
   - validate the returned fragment and merge it transactionally. A collision or a denied effect leaves no partial publication.

   A read outside the package root is a compile error that names the path, with a registered row and a UI snapshot. The host keeps only the filesystem-root sandbox and the fixed-output fetch leaves.
3. Lock: record which package's build ran, and its producer/input/output identity (`Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Lock/Record.jet`, `Write.jet`).
4. Imports and ordinary helper calls never run a dependency's `fn build` or hooks. Shared prep generation works through ordinary helpers or registered providers on non-AOT tiers, without `fn build`.
5. Mirror the change on the shipped path so the host tests exercise it.
6. Example: an OpenGL-style bindings package under `Examples/features/packages/include_bindings/`. Importing it alone emits nothing; `b.include` emits the generated `.jet`.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=packages/include_bindings Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: passes.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/build_include_read_outside_root Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`: passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test build_entry -- build_include_`: passes. It covers:
  - import-only runs nothing;
  - the lock records the producer;
  - a collision leaves no partial output.

## Batch
batch-jetc-driver: the build-entry execution, sandbox and merge live in the driver and eval.

## Dependencies
- #3506: compile-time IO as ordinary functions.
- #3507: typed `b.generate` templates.
- #3520: metaprogramming contract.
- #3418: effect and policy unification.

cards.title: Complete reflection and explicitly opted-in Jai-level metaprogramming
cards.body:
## Current authority — owner direction 2026-09-21

The latest owner instruction requests BOTH complete standard reflection/generation and full Jai-level metaprogramming. Standard/default mode keeps level 5. Above-level-5 powers require explicit metaprogramming opt-in. This amends the earlier absolute ceiling for opted-in programs only; historical decisions remain immutable evidence.

Requested advanced power includes first-class compile-time types, code values, caller capture, insertion, compiler workspaces/events, signature/type/body rewrites, procedure baking, native-helper boundaries and build control. No capability is silently replaced by scaffolding or deferred to another execution tier. Ordinary checks, explicit Unsafe regions and external enterprise authority remain binding.

The owner also proposed settings declarations such as tls: Bool{true} and api_base: String{"https://api.example.com"}. D-SETTINGS-CTOR2 presents that proposal as a genuine owner choice. It is not recorded as ratified.

This card is the integration parent. #3539 owns the composed closure matrix. Children depend on the public-contract card #3520, never on completion of this parent. No implementation is claimed by this planning pass.

## Delivery map

- #3520 — Complete reflection and metaprogramming public contract
- #3521 — Shared prep execution and explicit runtime boundaries
- #3147 — Complete typed type and enum reflection
- #3522 — Complete callable signatures and captured-state reflection
- #3523 — Complete program, source, package and semantic reflection
- #3524 — Complete demand-driven runtime type and value reflection
- #3525 — Deterministic generator dependencies and typed phase scheduling
- #3526 — Explicit above-level-five metaprogramming authorization
- #3527 — Compiler sessions, workspaces, events and build control
- #3528 — First-class compile-time types and type-producing programs
- #3529 — Code values, lexical capture and scoped source insertion
- #3530 — Transactional code transformations and complete semantic rechecking
- #3531 — Preparation execution, persistent state and native-call boundaries
- #3532 — Metaprogram dependency keys and incremental invalidation
- #3533 — Generated-code navigation diagnostics and metaprogram inspection
- #3534 — Project-defined semantic checkers over complete typed code
- #3535 — Foreign declaration checks and generated binding metadata
- #3536 — Automatic annotated command registry and typed console adapters
- #3537 — Field-derived live inspector serialization and migration workflow
- #3538 — Automatic entity buckets defaults counts and dispatch
- #3539 — Close the complete Jai capability and reflection proof matrix
- #3540 — Use ordinary constructor defaults in typed package settings
- #3505 — Complete standard-mode const generics
- #3506 — Ordinary preparation IO with enforced effects and input provenance
- #3507 — First-class typed Generated values and shared additive publication
- #3508 — Explicit isolated dependency builds and generated contributions
- #3181 — Reconcile semantic-index schema and compiler metadata projections
- #3175 — Expose bounded checked local obligations through the existing semantic index
- #3199 — Prove typed, JSON and Rust compiler-facade fact parity
- #3201 — Align core.compiler source-operation arity across checking and evaluation
- #3202 — Choose structured source origin for public compiler diagnostics
- #3541 — Procedure identity baking and staged specialization

## Integration sequence and ownership

First resolve the six owner ballots. Then deliver the contract and existing schema/facade prerequisites. Complete shared preparation, typed reflection and additive generation before dependent generated applications. Advanced authorization and sessions unlock type/code factories, transformations and specialization. Cache invalidation and tooling follow their checked semantic producers. Each card closes immediately after its own integrated focused proof.

Use one coherent implementer per patch. AST, Reflect, Driver, parser, semantic-index and pipeline edits have overlapping paths. Serialize those mutations; do not dispatch them merely because cards are separate. Independent example consumers may run concurrently after their required interfaces land. Main is the named integration and close owner.

Existing #3418 owns effect and host authority. #3419 owns approval presentation. #3421 owns generated storage and is already active. #3042 owns checked native assembly. This campaign consumes those contracts without overwriting active owners. #2526 remains the separate resource scheduler; #3525 owns semantic producer barriers, not a competing CPU pool.

## Proof and evidence limits

#3539 contains forty finite peer capability families, source locators, evidence limits, delivery owners and behavioral proofs. Its inventory includes capabilities beyond the original clip. A versioned current proprietary Jai SDK inventory remains necessary before an unqualified current full-Jai parity claim. Missing evidence is a blocker, not a removed requirement.

All public reflection fields and operations additionally need typed schema coverage. Tests must distinguish true emptiness from unavailable, denied, stale, invalid and truncated results. Generated examples must perform real calls and state changes. Literal output echoes and source-only inspections do not prove the feature.

Rebuild the integrated compiler before runtime proof. The previously observed stale CoreModuleExports.rs prevents a fresh build; this planning pass neither repairs it nor reuses an older binary as current proof. Implementation must resolve that build prerequisite under its owning source work before claiming behavior.

AOT, default run, interpreter and applicable web preserve one meaning. Exercise dev invalidation where inputs change. AOT artifact launches must not rerun prep. Closing this parent requires every scoped delivery owner done, the exact commit-bound composed matrix, and one fresh review.

## Earlier interview record — historical, superseded only where stated

The following earlier wording is retained for rationale. Any absolute metaprogramming ceiling in it now applies to standard mode only. The current owner instruction above governs opted-in scope.

## Current owner direction

Prep prepares a program for execution under interpreter, JIT, and AOT. AOT preparation happens while producing the prepared artifact; it is not a hook rerun on every application launch. Build is specifically the AOT procedure for producing executables, libraries, and linkable objects. Do not run fn build as a prerequisite for JIT or interpreted execution.

The owner wants useful preparation-time Jet execution, including console output, ordinary helper calls, reflection, and generation. The broader effect model is owned by #3418: infer effects even when unwritten, positive rows are ceilings, trusted development avoids permission fatigue, and restricted policy can require explicit budgets. Record phase and package provenance for all preparation and build effects.

## Existing ratification and amendment boundary

D-META-GATE1 remains immutable history. Its approved Meta.Generate and Meta.Include vocabulary and its use of the existing effect machinery are the starting point. Do not create a separate metaprogram permission engine. Read-only reflection is not the same permission as changing generated program structure.

The new prep/build distinction changes the earlier root-build-centric framing. Generation required by a program must be available to shared preparation or supplied as an explicit prepared input. It cannot depend on secretly executing the AOT build entry under another tier.

The owner confirmed: keep the existing ceiling and use Jet-owned semantics. Controlled public hooks mean read-only observation and additive checked generation, not user-defined automatic wrapping, replacement, or rewriting of existing code. Ordinary wrappers explicitly written by the author remain ordinary Jet. Common implicit transformations belong to bounded Jet-owned semantic contracts, using native markers or ordinary Core APIs as appropriate. This choice approves no new marker spelling or individual native feature. Exact observation/generation events, APIs, ordering, and limits still need specification and ratification. The selected prep/build split, explicit activation, shared effect policy, and effect-preserving caching remain unchanged.

## Open owner gates

- Specify public read-only observation and additive checked generation within the confirmed ceiling: stable events, typed query and output contracts, explicit activation, bounded ordering, and provenance. No user-defined automatic wrappers, existing-body rewrites, shadow replacement, token macros, or grammar extensions. Ballot any genuinely new native semantic feature individually; do not infer approval from the examples.
- Define enterprise controls for any approved hook: provider identity, exact scope, required capabilities, ordering, input and output provenance, limits, generated-code visibility, and ordinary sema checking of outputs.
- Implement effect-preserving preparation caching. The owner clarified that a status print must occur when its step is logically invoked, even if the expensive calculation uses a cache. Reuse valid pure results without dropping, duplicating, reordering, or replaying effects as if newly executed. Cache eligibility and dependency keys must respect this semantic rule.
- Finish the preparation surface and metadata namespace after the execution and trust model is settled. The prep term is selected in the interview; the complete grammar and new public APIs are not ratified by this card text.

## Current evidence

Source inspection only: crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/mod.rs runs the build entry through the interpreter with sink: None. Methods/dispatch.rs requires a sink for ordinary print/eprint. Do not claim ordinary build-entry console output already works. This needs a rebuilt runtime reproduction during implementation.

The existing b.generate(name) typed item block is implemented by Build/runtime_bridge.rs and appears in examples/features/tooling/programmable_build/run.jet. Reuse its canonical typed generation path rather than creating a text-expansion or alternate emitter mechanism.

This P1 card owns the metaprogram phase and capability work. #3418 owns the shared policy contract. No implementation or runtime proof was performed during this interview amendment.

## Worked cache contract

A preparation helper prints Preparing table, calls a pure table calculation, then prints Table ready. On a second logical invocation with unchanged inputs, the table calculation may use a cache. Both prints still occur once, in the same order, from the current invocation. They are not a replayed historical transcript. A changed relevant input invalidates the computed result.

Compiler hooks obey the same rule. A hook promised at a logical preparation event cannot lose its observable effects merely because the compiler reused checked facts or generated values. Define public events by their semantic contract, not accidental cache-miss behavior.

Executing a prepared AOT artifact is not a preparation invocation and does not repeat these prints. No separate effectful-workflow cache that skips bodies is approved by this clarification.

## Hook activation: owner selection

The owner selected explicit feature use or registration. Applying a library rule to a source target counts as opting in. A package-wide hook requires explicit registration. Importing a dependency alone does not activate its declared hooks. Activation is not an extra permission prompt: trusted and restricted execution still use the shared authority policy.

Three practical examples were explained: tracing through wrapping, database transactions through scoped resources, and differentiation through a derived callable. The owner rejected using their writing convenience to justify crossing the existing ceiling and selected Jet-owned semantics. The power boundary is now confirmed: no user-defined automatic wrapping or rewriting of existing code. The examples approve no new marker or duplicate implementation.

## Readability and enterprise reassessment

The assistant withdrew its recommendation to add general user-defined wrappers. The owner then confirmed retention of the existing ceiling. Type checking establishes type rules, effect checking constrains modeled operations, and provenance exposes inputs and outputs. None proves intended business behavior, semantic preservation, or cheap local reasoning. Wrapper order can change authorization, caching, retry, and failure behavior while retaining valid types and the same possible effects. Generated-source visibility helps investigation; it does not remove that cost.

The owner-confirmed direction is to retain read-only observation and additive, addressed, checked generation; use ordinary library calls for ordinary composition; and keep any implicit transformation of existing code under a small, Jet-owned semantic contract. Native markers are not automatically the best spelling for every job: existing compute.gradient is already a callable surface, and the in-memory #Transact contract must not be confused with a database transaction. No new marker spelling or implementation is approved here.

Open safeguards to assess include provider and input identity, bounded deterministic staging, output ownership, source mapping, tier parity, and prevention of bypasses through generated shadow definitions or preparation-time writes to compiler inputs. Enterprise authority restrictions must be enforced, not inferred from audit logs. Additive generation still has build, editor, and review costs. The reference prose promising Jai-class power with none of the costs is an aspiration, not exercised evidence or a guarantee of unrestricted Jai-equivalent mechanisms.

## Confirmed metadata and runtime boundaries

The owner selected all compiler-owned metadata for the @ namespace, including supported facts about declared types and functions, not only ambient source/build facts. Ordinary values and helper functions keep ordinary names. Metadata handles do not grant use-site type creation. Preserve the previously selected grouped compiler roots and ordinary lower-case members; callable subject-query roots are selected below, while metadata schemas remain open.

The owner selected a preparation-phase boundary for the stronger runtime escape. Keep two semantic modes: the weaker mode disables automatic eager evaluation; the stronger mode also forbids explicit preparation-time execution of the marked code. Ordinary compiler optimizations, including pure constant folding, remain allowed. This is not an optimizer barrier or a guarantee that particular runtime work or instructions survive. The later selections below require explicit modes and function/method/block sites. Do not use a NoPrecompute name to promise more than this contract.

The owner selected an explicit generation boundary. prep executes ordinary Jet preparation code, including ordinary if and loop computation. A visible typed generation operation publishes checked declarations for the program. Do not introduce prep if or prep loop as declaration-selection/repetition shorthand. Generated function bodies are not executed merely because their declarations are produced. Exact shared generation API spelling remains open; the illustrative generate name is not ratified. Reuse one canonical typed generation mechanism across the permitted phases, without strings-as-macros or an alternative emitter.

## Latest surface selections before video analysis

The owner selected callable compiler metadata roots, for example @TYPE(User).fields, rather than @TYPE.of(User).fields. Previously selected ambient forms remain grouped facts such as @SOURCE.line. Exact metadata schemas remain subject to their canonical source contracts.

Runtime-mode markers require an explicit mode. The owner rejected a bare #Runtime default: do not accept an omitted mode or introduce a default alias. The two proposed explicit forms are #Runtime(.NoEager) and #Runtime(.Only), carrying the previously selected automatic-evaluation opt-out and application-only phase boundary respectively. Neither is an optimizer barrier.

Runtime-mode markers apply to functions/methods and explicit code blocks, not module-wide defaults. The owner then paused the interview to request a current-implementation comparison against the Jonathan Blow video R6rH8IGtrTI. Do not infer further design choices from that research request.


## Video comparison evidence — 2026-09-21

Source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R6rH8IGtrTI (16:40). The comparison uses the full timestamped automatic English transcript and limited storyboard inspection, not a full-resolution code transcription. The linked original stream was provenance, not an additional audit scope.

Current building blocks include ordinary build functions and helpers, pre-build ProgramInfo, typed type/field reflection, additive derives and user rules, generated Jet modules, a read-only diagnostic extension, typed CLI schemas, and generational Pool/Id storage. These do not prove the complete console/entity workflows demonstrated in the clip.

Function-site user rules already inspect a FunctionInfo target and emit ordinary top-level items (CheckInner.rs:1122-1163). Do not add a second annotation mechanism merely for console commands. The current FunctionInfo projection contains parameter names but not their types, return type, markers, docs, or bodies (Comptime/Reflect.rs:3076-3143,3164-3185). The function-rule effect projection is declared effects, while whole-program solved facts are separate; public metadata must state its phase and completeness. This constrains a straightforward generic signature-driven adapter. #CLI methods and explicit bindings already cover typed argument parsing, #Doc help, and duplicate checks.

ProgramInfo is taken before build-generated modules. Generated import rounds are not an after-all-typed semantic fixed point. Ordinary build helpers can already be colocated with domain code. Add a public scheduling mechanism only for dependencies that ordinary explicit calls cannot express. A general generation design needs complete declared input facts, generation, then final checking; it cannot require successful final checking of consumers before their generated names exist.

The driver already defers pre-build E0102 and retains generated module name/path/digest/source. That is not a producer-aware promised-symbol contract. The post-sema WASM extension exposes entry-module function facts and diagnostic/edit suggestions, not general program mutation or generated artifacts. Keep these distinct seams explicit.

The live game inspector currently ingests host-supplied property facts; no automatic ReflectionField-to-inspector bridge was found. Pool<T> is slots plus a free list, not the video's exact per-type bucket container or an automatic entity registry. Columnar lists are a different layout. C header/declaration checks do not establish agreement with an arbitrary linked binary. Resident JIT JSON migration code also contains explicit unsupported paths (Encoding.rs:2382-2481); this comparison supplies no full migration or tier-parity proof.

The clip's principal products are a fit for read-only metadata plus additive checked generation; this is an architectural conclusion, not an exercised implementation. The clip only references an earlier rewrite plugin and does not establish that unrestricted body rewriting is required for these products. Its run-when-all-typed convention is explicitly project-defined, not a built-in Jai rule. These findings constrain this card's existing metadata and phase work; they do not commission a game inspector, entity system, FFI verifier, or experimental compiler.

Fresh proof command: scripts/agent/jet-env cargo build -p jet --bin jet with CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0. It exits 101 because jet-foundation/build.rs rejects CoreModuleExports.rs as stale relative to Prelude/Core.jet. No regeneration, old-binary run, or tests were used. The source comparison is complete; current-tree runtime equivalence remains unverified.

## Separate experimental variant — feasibility only

The owner asked whether a non-default, broader metaprogramming variant could exist without changing standard Jet. This is a feasibility question, not implementation approval and not an amendment to the confirmed standard ceiling.

A separately selected experimental dialect/toolchain can share checked lowering and execution infrastructure. This is not an existing build-profile switch: current profiles are build facts, not a language branch. Type-producing computation, wider code inspection, body transforms, and compiler-event scheduling would need explicit new contracts, invalidation rules, diagnostics, and source mapping. Candidate generated or transformed programs must pass sema before entering the checked IR; guest-supplied checked facts cannot be trusted.

Keep standard source acceptance, dependency activation, cache/artifact identity, and editor/toolchain identity distinct. Imports must not opt a standard root into the experimental dialect. Metaprogramming power does not authorize bypassing host permissions or provider approvals. Checking a transformed program can preserve type/memory rules but does not prove that it preserves the original business behavior or source contracts; any proposed changes to protected contracts need an explicit owner decision. A separate fork gives stronger operational separation but greater drift. External generation into ordinary Jet is a bounded existing alternative, not a full compiler message-loop/type-factory substitute.

No public syntax, command name, dependency, scope move, safety exception, or experimental implementation is selected by this note. Full Jai parity is not established by this one clip.

## Goal
`core.units.from` becomes a Jet-owned semantic function in `Core/units/units.jet`. Rust keeps only the typed `Measurement` leaf. There is no high-level host dispatcher row, and construction means the same thing on every tier.

## Current state
- `Core/units/units.jet:13-17` already implements `from` in Jet as `measurement(magnitude * unit, uncertainty: 0.0)`. Criteria 1, 2 and 4 are met for the archived path.
- The self-hosted registry still has the host row: `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreHostSignatures.jet:350` (`core.units` / `from`, returning `measurement`). That leaves criterion 5 open.
- The Measurement leaf is routed at `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/HandleMethods.jet:369-377` (`value`, `uncertainty`, `add`/`sub`/`mul`/`div`, `sqrt` go to `jet_std::JetMeasurement::*`).
- `Compiler/JetEval/Source` has no `Measurement` or `core.units` support.
- The three-tier proof (criterion 3) failed on the shipped binary: E0956 on `Measurement.value` in the interpreter (log 2026-09-24) and a MIRRust ICE (log 2026-09-22, `MIRRust.rs:2036`).
- Fixture: `tests/conformance/corpus/core/units/from.jet` (`units.from(12.0, 0.0)`, then `print(result.value())`).
- Criterion 7 asks for "a compiler built from Compiler/". That binary does not exist yet: the bootstrap host is feature-gated (`Cargo.toml:78-81`, #218/#3663). The runnable proof is on the shipped binary, plus a Jet slice check.

## Changes
1. Delete `CoreHostSignatures.jet:350` and any `CoreCallRows` row routing `core.units.from` to a host symbol, so JetSema binds the Jet body. Regenerate the Core projections with the existing generator (`node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs`).
2. JetEval: add the Measurement handle operations (value, uncertainty, add, sub, mul, div, sqrt) in `Compiler/JetEval/Source/Routes` or `EvalValues.jet`, calling the same leaf meaning.
3. Shipped-binary mirror, needed for the user-visible three-tier proof: in `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIREval.rs`, add the `jet_std::JetMeasurement::*` handle route (the E0956). In `MIRRust.rs`, fix the ICE near `:2036` so AOT emits the leaf call. Mirror the removal of the Rust `core.units.from` host row if one still exists.
4. Measurement syntax is unchanged. Migrate every generated consumer, with no shims.

## Proof
- `JET_CORE_CONFORMANCE_FILTER=core/units/from cargo test --test dev_corpus_gate core_conformance_corpus_uses_strict_three_tier_gate`: pass.
- `JET_CORE_CONFORMANCE_FILTER=core/units/ cargo test --test dev_corpus_gate core_conformance_corpus_uses_strict_three_tier_gate`: the other units witnesses stay green.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: exit 0.
- `Tools/agent/lane-check.sh`: `CHECK OK`.

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime`: what remains is tier parity for a Prelude leaf across AOT, JIT and the interpreter. The registry edit is small.

## Dependencies
None blocking this proof. The literal "built from Compiler/" form of criterion 7 waits on #218 (self-hosting), which is tracked separately.

cards.title: Complete callable signatures and captured-state reflection
cards.body:
## Outcome

Unify FunctionInfo, MethodInfo, callable-type and semindex projections over the existing CallableSignatureFact and sema facts. Include parameter types/names/labels/zones/access/defaults/variadic contracts, return/failure/view provenance, type/value parameters, inferred versus declared effects, phase obligations, attributes, documentation, captures and specialization identity. Do not expose private checker stores or describe declared effects as inferred facts.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Reflect.rs
- crates/jet-semindex/src/Types.rs
- crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Captures.rs
- crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/items.rs
- crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/expressions.rs

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

Extend tests/reflect.rs, tests/semindex.rs and a new callable_catalog golden. Query free functions, methods, generic instances, overloaded/trait callables and closures through the same typed interface. Change one label, default, capture or effect and require the corresponding descriptor and generated consumer to change. Invalid/private/unavailable requests have snapshots.

## Deduplication

#3509 owns this campaign. Existing owners #3147, #3175, #3181, #3199, #3201, #3202 and #3505–#3508 are reused, not replaced. #3418, #3419, #3421 and #3042 remain separate prerequisite owners. Shared specification references alone do not make these distinct implementation outcomes duplicates.
cards.plan:
## Goal
FunctionInfo, MethodInfo, callable-type and semantic-index projections are unified over the Jet checker's callable facts. They cover parameter types, names, labels, zones, access, defaults and variadics; return, failure and view provenance; type and value parameters; inferred vs declared effects with distinct provenance; phase obligations; attributes; docs; captures; and specialization identity. Queries use the ordinary `T MetadataError!` contract, and private checker stores stay private.

## Current state
- Nothing has started. The owned paths are archived: crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Reflect.rs, crates/jet-semindex/src/Types.rs, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Captures.rs and crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/{items,expressions}.rs.
- Jet homes:
  - Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Comptime/Reflection.jet:790 `sema_comptime_reflection_method_info` builds MethodInfo from `parameter_texts` strings (:791), not typed records.
  - SemanticIndex.jet:98 `sema_compiler_index_parameter_values` and :1311 `sema_compiler_index_function_signature` stringify signatures.
  - Registration/TypeMetadata.jet; capture classification in Expressions/Lambdas.jet.
  - The public surface is Core/reflect/reflect.jet and Compiler/JetEval/Source/ReflectionMethods.jet.

## Changes
1. Add a typed `SemaCallableFact` in Registration/ built once from the checker (parameters with label, zone, access, typed default expression kept unevaluated, variadic flag; return and failure contract; view provenance; generic parameters; declared vs inferred effects; attributes; doc; captures from Lambdas.jet; specialization identity from #3541).

cards.title: Complete program, source, package and semantic reflection
cards.body:
## Outcome

Expose the checked program graph through the selected metadata roots: packages/modules/imports, declarations, scopes/locals/references/calls, docs/comments/source spans, generated origins, effects/memory/ownership/state facts, target/build facts and effective typed settings with contribution provenance. Reuse semindex and source text/token ownership; do not add another AST walk or schema. Distinguish root-authorized program scope from ordinary source visibility and phase completeness.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-semindex/src/Types.rs
- crates/jet-semindex/src/Build.rs
- crates/jet-semindex/src/Docs.rs
- crates/jet-semindex/src/Symbols.rs
- crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/program_imports.rs
- crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Reflect.rs
- crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Public.rs

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

Extend tests/semindex.rs and tests/compiler_api.rs with a multi-package program_catalog witness, including generated modules, unsaved overlays and a dependency. Compare metadata, inspect JSON, docs and editor identities. Verify comments containing braces and strings, source/caller locations through wrappers, typed settings/default/profile/CLI views and denied scopes.

## Deduplication

#3509 owns this campaign. Existing owners #3147, #3175, #3181, #3199, #3201, #3202 and #3505–#3508 are reused, not replaced. #3418, #3419, #3421 and #3042 remain separate prerequisite owners. Shared specification references alone do not make these distinct implementation outcomes duplicates.

## Goal
Expose the checked program graph through the selected metadata roots: packages, modules and imports; declarations; scopes, locals, references and calls; docs, comments and source spans; generated origins; effect, memory, ownership and state facts; target/build facts; and effective typed settings with their contribution provenance. Reuse the one checked model; no second AST walk or schema.

## Current state
- The Jet side has only the pieces. `Compiler/JetEval/Source/ReflectionMethods.jet` supports `TypeInfo/FieldInfo/MethodInfo` marker and method queries (:11-15). `Compiler/JetEval/Source/CompilerServices.jet:39-42,399` builds `JetCompilerServicesCheckedFacts` (functions and effects). `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/SemanticIndex.jet` projects arithmetic, callable-policy and output facts (for example `sema_compiler_index_arithmetic_fact`, :334-343).
- No program catalog, comment/doc projection or typed settings projection exists in Compiler/. The owned Rust paths (`crates/jet-semindex`, `jet-comptime/Reflect.rs`, `jet-foundation/AST/program_imports.rs`, `jet-pkg-model/Public.rs`) are archived.
- Typed package settings live in the Jet package model under `Jetpack/PackageModel` (#3590).
- Public carriers are in `Core/reflect/reflect.jet`.

## Changes
1. `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/SemanticIndex.jet`: extend the one index with the declaration/scope/reference/call graph, generated origins, and effect/ownership/state facts. Each row carries a stable identity and scope.
2. Comments, documentation and marker arguments come from the lexer token stream (`Compiler/JetLexer`) as distinct row kinds. Lexical source location and explicit caller-source capture are separate fields.
3. `Compiler/JetEval/Source/ReflectionMethods.jet` and `CompilerServices.jet`: program, package and source root queries return typed records or a typed refusal. Whole-program queries report completeness and revision. A pre-generation snapshot never claims later generated declarations.
4. Effective package settings, with type, origin and defaults/profile/CLI provenance, come from `Jetpack/PackageModel` at check time with no runtime manifest access or self-granted permission.
5. `Core/reflect/reflect.jet`: typed carriers. Root spelling follows D-META-ROOT3 (recommended A: `compiler.program()`, `compiler.package_info()`, `compiler.source()`).

## Proof
- The added criterion.
- `cargo test --test semindex` stays green.
- A fixture comment containing braces and strings round-trips exactly.
- A denied scope returns the typed refusal.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-sema`: the fact projection and index are sema work. The eval queries are thin.

## Dependencies
#3520 (metadata contract, building), #3522, #3181, #3175, #3199 and #3202, all open and real. #3201 is done. The runtime proof runs on the self-hosted compiler, so #218 is needed.

## Outcome

Extend the actual typed reflection lowering and shared Prelude values, not the shadowed string-classifier source path. Provide typed erased-value inspection, active enum cases, callable/type identity and an explicitly requested retained type catalog. Keep compile-time metadata separate from runtime retention; use one declaration-owned model and enforce lawful capture/copy/visibility. Runtime stripping must never produce dangling metadata handles.

- crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Reflect.rs

cards.plan:
## Goal
Typed runtime reflection: erased-value inspection, active enum case, callable and type identity, and an explicitly requested retained type catalog. It uses one declaration-owned metadata model, lawful capture, copy and visibility, and never gives a dangling handle after stripping.

## Current state
- Comptime TypeInfo is built in `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Comptime/Reflection.jet`. Enum variants are emitted as `FieldInfo` rows whose `ty` is a display string (`sema_comptime_reflection_enum_variant_info`, :1129-1155). This is the string-typed shape the card forbids for runtime views.
- Lowering and eval support only `TypeInfo.has_marker/implements/has_method` and `FieldInfo/MethodInfo.has_marker` (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/ReflectionMethods.jet:19-22`, `Compiler/JetEval/Source/ReflectionMethods.jet:11-15`).
- The public surface is `Core/reflect/reflect.jet`. Shared runtime values live in the host Prelude `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Reflect.rs`.
- Golden `Examples/features/reflection/reflect-value.jet` exists. Tests `tests/reflect.rs` and `tests/core_reflect_value.rs` exist.

## Changes
1. `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Comptime/Reflection.jet`: one declaration-owned metadata graph with an explicit retention scope. Typed type references replace display strings. The complete-or-refused capture and copy check is transitive over nested graphs.
2. `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/ReflectionMethods.jet`: lower `reflect.of(value)`, the active case (shared with #3147's `value.case()`), callable/type identity and retain/retain_program to calls on the host Prelude values. Emit a metadata table only when retention is requested.
3. `Compiler/JetEval/Source/ReflectionMethods.jet`: the same semantics, calling the same Prelude helpers.
4. `Core/reflect/reflect.jet`: typed carriers. Unavailable, denied or truncated facts return a typed refusal and never empty metadata.
5. `Reflect.rs` changes only where a helper is missing. `crates/jet-jit` and `crates/jet-interpreter` get adapter wiring only. There is no new TIR/MIR lowering in `crates/jet-codegen`.
6. Value and type roots use the D-META-ROOT3 spelling (recommended A: `compiler.value(...)`, `compiler.types()`). Until #3662 cuts over, examples keep the current ratified spelling.

## Proof
- The added criterion (reflect-value golden on AOT, `jet run` and interpreter).
- `cargo test --test core_reflect_value` and `cargo test --test reflect` pass.
- A stripped-metadata case prints a typed refusal.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-back`: most of the work is lowering and eval of reflection methods.

## Dependencies
#3147 (case model), #3522 (callable signatures) and #3523 (program metadata graph), all real. Self-hosted runtime proof needs #218.

cards.title: Deterministic generator dependencies and typed phase scheduling
cards.body:
## Outcome

Replace incidental pre-build ordering with one dependency-aware preparation/generation schedule. Support declared input scopes, multiple generation rounds, waiting for typed facts, late generated inputs and producer-owned promised outputs. Keep ordinary explicit helper calls simple. Typed barriers mean complete declared inputs, not final successful checking of consumers that await generation. Detect cycles, duplicate outputs, stale handles and nontermination.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs
- crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle/Pipeline
- crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build
- crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/program_imports.rs

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

Create staged_registry witness: generator A emits an entity type; generator B consumes its typed descriptor; handwritten run calls B output. Permute module traversal and worker order and repeat warm/cold runs. Negative fixtures cover missing producer, misspelled ordinary name, duplicate generation, a dependency cycle and a hook that never converges.

## Deduplication

#3509 owns this campaign. Existing owners #3147, #3175, #3181, #3199, #3201, #3202 and #3505–#3508 are reused, not replaced. #3418, #3419, #3421 and #3042 remain separate prerequisite owners. Shared specification references alone do not make these distinct implementation outcomes duplicates.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Replace incidental pre-build ordering with one dependency-aware prep/generation schedule in the Jet driver. It supports declared input scopes, multiple generation rounds, waits for typed facts, late generated inputs and producer-owned promised outputs. A typed barrier means "all declared inputs are complete", not "consumers checked". Cycles, duplicate outputs, stale handles and nontermination are detected. Ordinary explicit helper calls stay simple.

## Current state
- Nothing is implemented. The owned paths in the body are archived: crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle/Pipeline, crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build and crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/program_imports.rs.
- Jet homes:
  - Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/BodyComptime.jet: `jet_driver_orchestrate_comptime_bodies` (:155) and `jet_driver_recheck_comptime_bodies` (:308) run body stages in graph order, with no producer/consumer dependency model.
  - Pipeline.jet (2227 lines) sequences the stages.
  - Loader.jet collects sources.
  - Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Comptime/BodyRequests.jet holds the body requests.
  - Compiler/JetAst/Source/AST holds program import facts.
- #3509 owns the campaign.

## Changes
1. JetDriver: add a `JetDriverGenerationGraph` with nodes for generators and declared outputs, and edges for declared inputs and awaited typed facts. BodyComptime.jet runs rounds to a fixed point over this graph instead of module order. Each round publishes its outputs atomically, and a round cap reports nontermination.
2. Loader.jet: admit late generated inputs through the declared input scope only. A generated file that nothing promised is an error.
3. JetSema CheckProgram.jet and Comptime/BodyRequests.jet: a typed barrier waits for its declared producers' outputs, and an unrelated unknown name is not suppressed as a pending promise.
4. Register diagnostics with what/why/fix for a missing producer (naming producer and consumer), duplicate output, cycle, stale handle and nontermination (DiagnosticRows.jet).
5. Write the witness as Examples/features/comptime/staged_registry/: generator A emits an entity type, generator B consumes its typed descriptor, and handwritten run code calls B's output.

## Proof
- Run the staged_registry witness through the self-hosted route under permuted module traversal and worker order, cold and warm. Output and hook-event order are identical each time.
- tests/ui/generator_{missing_producer,misspelled_name,duplicate,cycle,nonterminating}.jet snapshots: `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/generator_ cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.

## Batch
batch-jetc-driver: this is the orchestration change in JetDriver, with its sema barrier.

cards.title: Compiler sessions, workspaces, events and build control
cards.body:
## Outcome

Expose a deliberate typed compiler interface supporting isolated workspaces, source/import admission, compile options and output targets, phase events, diagnostics, debug inspection, source additions, cancellation and completion. Include before-link/write and post-build actions where AOT applies. Share native read-only and opted-in control projections without turning extension v1 diagnostic suggestions into silently applied edits. Host/target and workspace identities are explicit.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-driver/src/lib.rs
- crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs
- crates/jet-driver/src/QueryService.rs
- crates/jet-pkg-model/src/CompilerExtension.rs
- crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build
- Core/compiler

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

Add compiler_workspaces witness: one metaprogram drives two isolated workspaces with different settings/targets, adds generated sources, consumes phase events and builds or runs their outputs. Verify deterministic per-workspace ordering, no cross-workspace names or authority, error/cancel paths and AOT-only linker/write events. Use existing compiler_api and compiler_extension_e2e harnesses.

## Deduplication

#3509 owns this campaign. Existing owners #3147, #3175, #3181, #3199, #3201, #3202 and #3505–#3508 are reused, not replaced. #3418, #3419, #3421 and #3042 remain separate prerequisite owners. Shared specification references alone do not make these distinct implementation outcomes duplicates.
cards.plan:
## Goal
A deliberate typed compiler interface: isolated workspaces, source and import admission, options and targets, phase events, diagnostics, debug inspection, source additions, cancellation and completion, plus before-link/write and post-build actions where AOT applies. Read-only and opted-in control projections share it, and extension v1 suggestions are never silently applied.

## Current state
- Nothing has started, and the blockers are open.
- Owned paths archived: crates/jet-driver/src/{lib.rs, Driver/mod.rs, QueryService.rs}, crates/jet-pkg-model/src/CompilerExtension.rs and crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build.
- Jet homes: Core/compiler/compiler.jet is the public surface. Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet and CompilerQueries.jet do the work, served by Compiler/JetEval/Source/CompilerServices.jet. Extension identity is in Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/CompilerExtension/CompilerExtension.jet. Linking and rustc emission stay on the retained host boundary.

## Changes
1. Core/compiler/compiler.jet: add a `Workspace` handle type with revision and identity, plus typed options, targets, source admission and `events()` yielding typed `CompilerEvent` records (workspace, revision, phase, source identity). Stale or foreign handles return an error.
2. JetDriver: each workspace owns an independent Pipeline state. Events are emitted at existing phase boundaries in deterministic order, and cancellation leaves no partial publication. Builds reuse the existing build machinery, never a second driver.
3. AOT: before-link/write and post-build hooks cross the host linker boundary only for AOT outputs.
4. Backend options cannot disable Jet checks, bypass unsafe law or expose rustc user errors.
5. Add the witness Examples/features/comptime/compiler_workspaces/.

## Proof
- The witness produces the expected output through the self-hosted route, stable across repeated runs.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/workspace_ cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.

## Batch
batch-jetc-driver: this is the driver session and event model behind Core/compiler.

## Dependencies
#3526 (opt-in for control operations), #3525 (scheduling) and #3508 (`b.include` sandboxed builds). The self-hosted run needs #218.
