cards.title: First-class compile-time types and type-producing programs
cards.body:
## Outcome

Add opted-in type values and type-producing computation, not another string type parser. Support construction and selection of complete representable type shapes, recursive references, generic specialization, polymorph-time validation and factory results in type positions. Reuse nominal/declaration identity and generic substitution. Give every constructed type a stable generated origin and checked layout. Keep ordinary const generics in standard mode.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/comptime.rs
- crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/types.rs
- crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime
- crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Registration
- crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle/GenericModules

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

Create type_factory witness that constructs a record/enum and generic container from metadata, uses the returned type in declarations, and calls generated members. Test equal factory inputs, distinct nominal declarations with equal layout, changed arguments, recursion, constraints and effect-dependent input invalidation. Default mode rejects the same type-producing operation; all applicable tiers execute equivalent instances.

## Deduplication

#3509 owns this campaign. Existing owners #3147, #3175, #3181, #3199, #3201, #3202 and #3505–#3508 are reused, not replaced. #3418, #3419, #3421 and #3042 remain separate prerequisite owners. Shared specification references alone do not make these distinct implementation outcomes duplicates.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Opted-in first-class type values and type-producing computation: construct and select complete type shapes, recursive references, generic specialization and polymorph-time validation, with factory results usable in type positions. No string type parser. Ordinary const generics stay in standard mode.

## Current state
- `TComptimeValue` (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/TIR/TIR.jet:443-459`) has no type-value variant. Compile-time values are Int, Float, Bool, Char, String, BigInt, Bytes, List, Map, Struct, Enum, Present, Failed, Unit and Closure.
- Observational TypeInfo is built as a `Struct("TypeInfo", …)` value in `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Comptime/Reflection.jet:1330`. It cannot be used as a type.
- Registration of authored declarations lives in `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Registration/` (`Items.jet`, `Checked.jet`). Generic substitution lives under `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Inference`.

## Changes
1. `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/TIR/TIR.jet`: add `TComptimeValue.Type(ty: Type, origin: TGeneratedOrigin)`. It is distinct from the TypeInfo struct, so observation and construction stay separate (criterion 1). Give `Compiler/JetAst` a type-position node for a factory call.
2. `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Comptime`: builders for record, enum, generic apply and recursive reference. Each constructed type gets a stable generated origin (factory symbol plus normalized inputs) and a checked layout through `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Target/Layout.jet`.
3. `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Registration`: factory results register through the same path as authored declarations. Equal inputs give one identity. Distinct nominal declarations with equal layout stay distinct. Constraint failures, runtime-unknown inputs, stale workspace types and impossible layouts get registered diagnostics with spans.
4. `Compiler/JetEval`: evaluate factories under the opted-in mode. Standard mode rejects type-producing operations with a registered diagnostic. Const generics (D-CONSTGEN2, #3505) are unaffected.
5. Do not edit archived crates.

## Proof
- The added criterion: `Examples/features/comptime/type_factory.jet` builds a record, an enum and a generic container from metadata, uses them in declarations and calls generated members. It covers equal inputs, equal-layout distinct nominals, changed arguments, recursion and a constraint failure. Plus the UI fixture for standard-mode rejection.
- `jet run --interpret` on the same file matches.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-sema`: type construction, identity and registration are sema work.

## Dependencies
#3527 (workspace/session model for stale-type invalidation), #3505 (const generic spelling), #3147 (declaration metadata model). Runtime proof on the self-hosted path needs #218.

cards.title: Code values, lexical capture and scoped source insertion
cards.body:
## Outcome

Extend the canonical typed-code representation to expressions, statements and declarations in opted-in mode. Support code-as-data, quotation/capture, explicit caller-code inspection, hygienic default name binding, explicit lexical capture, scoped insertion and source-text-to-code parsing. Preserve category/type/source information through code-to-tree and tree-to-code conversion. Source text is parsed by the ordinary lexer and never gains trusted generated identifiers or unchecked flags.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/expressions.rs
- crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/comptime.rs
- crates/jet-parser/src/Parser
- crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime
- crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Captures.rs

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

Add code_capture witness with nested/recursive expansion, an intentionally shadowed caller local, explicit capture, injected caller code, expression/body/declaration fragments and source-string insertion. Show correct values and source blame across tiers. Wrong categories, accidental capture, reserved identifiers, noncopyable captures and unavailable caller scope must fail with snapshots.

## Deduplication

#3509 owns this campaign. Existing owners #3147, #3175, #3181, #3199, #3201, #3202 and #3505–#3508 are reused, not replaced. #3418, #3419, #3421 and #3042 remain separate prerequisite owners. Shared specification references alone do not make these distinct implementation outcomes duplicates.
cards.plan:
## Goal
In opted-in mode, extend the canonical typed-code representation to expressions, statements and declarations: code as data, quotation and capture, explicit caller-code inspection, hygienic default binding, explicit lexical capture, scoped insertion, and parsing source text into code. Category, type and source information survive code-to-tree and tree-to-code conversion. Source text goes through the ordinary lexer and parser and never gains trusted identifiers.

## Current state
- Nothing has started, and the blockers are open.
- The owned paths are archived: crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/{expressions,comptime}.rs, crates/jet-parser/src/Parser, crates/jet-comptime and crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Captures.rs.
- Jet homes: Compiler/JetAst/Source/AST/Comptime.jet and Expressions.jet (AST), Compiler/JetParser (text-to-code), Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Comptime and Expressions/Lambdas.jet (hygiene and capture), Compiler/JetEval (evaluation).
- Ballot text: expansion callbacks go through the exact `register_expansion` contract with stable declaration targets, invocation syntax and explicit captures. Caller-code access outside an active authorized callback fails.

## Changes
1. JetAst Comptime.jet: add a `CodeValue` carrying category (expr, stmt, decl), a typed tree, source identity and hygiene marks.
2. JetParser: expose parse-to-CodeValue through the ordinary entry. Parsed identifiers are untrusted.
3. JetSema Comptime: hygiene gives generated names fresh bindings by default. Explicit captures (reusing Lambdas.jet classification) are listed and checked for copy and move. Scoped insertion rechecks the inserted code in the target scope. Caller-code inspection works only inside an authorized `register_expansion` callback.
4. Stored or serialized code is bound to schema, toolchain and inputs, and fully rechecked on load. No payload claims to be trusted checked IR.
5. Standard mode keeps typed additive item templates, and arbitrary insertion needs the #3526 opt-in.
6. Add the witness Examples/features/comptime/code_capture/.

## Proof
- The witness produces the expected output on AOT, `jet run` and `--interpret` through the self-hosted route.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/code_value_ cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: hygiene, capture and recheck are the risky part, and they are JetSema.

## Dependencies
#3527 (sessions), #3507 (typed templates) and #3522 (capture reflection). The self-hosted run needs #218.

cards.title: Transactional code transformations and complete semantic rechecking
cards.body:
## Outcome

Apply the selected advanced edit contract to bodies, declarations, signatures and types. Validate ownership, revision, conflicts and binding identities; publish a complete candidate atomically only after sema. Recompute effects, ownership, layout, overloads and dependent callers. Record changed source contracts explicitly; unchanged source contracts and external policy still bind. Never inherit vetted unsafe provenance for modified code.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-driver/src/QueryService.rs
- crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle
- crates/jet-semindex/src/SemanticOps.rs
- crates/jet-foundation/src/AST
- crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

Create rewrite_contract witness that instruments a function, changes a signature with all callsites, and changes a reflected type consumed by a generator. Compare cold and incremental results. Negative tests introduce type, ownership, phase and effect errors; conflicting edits; forged provenance; stale checked IR; and an unauthorized target. Failed candidates leave the last good program unchanged.

## Deduplication

#3509 owns this campaign. Existing owners #3147, #3175, #3181, #3199, #3201, #3202 and #3505–#3508 are reused, not replaced. #3418, #3419, #3421 and #3042 remain separate prerequisite owners. Shared specification references alone do not make these distinct implementation outcomes duplicates.
cards.plan:
## Goal
In opted-in mode, apply the advanced edit contract to bodies, declarations, signatures and types. A ChangeSet is an explicit mutable operation builder over immutable checked snapshots, consumed and sealed at commit. After full semantic rechecking of every affected consumer (effects, ownership, layout, overloads, dependent callers), the complete candidate is published atomically. Changed source contracts are recorded, while unchanged contracts and external policy still bind. Modified code never inherits vetted unsafe provenance.

## Current state
- Nothing has started, and the blockers are open.
- The owned Rust paths are archived: crates/jet-driver/src/QueryService.rs, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle, crates/jet-semindex/src/SemanticOps.rs, crates/jet-foundation/src/AST and crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR.
- Jet homes: Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/CompilerQueries.jet (query service), Pipeline.jet, Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/CheckProgram.jet, SemanticIndex.jet, Compiler/JetAst/Source/AST and Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/TIR/TIR.jet.

## Changes
1. JetDriver CompilerQueries.jet: add `ChangeSet`, which records operations against a snapshot revision and binding identities. Commit validates ownership and revision, detects conflicts, applies to a copy, runs the full sema pipeline on the affected closure, and publishes only on success. Failure leaves the last good program and emits source- and producer-mapped diagnostics.
2. CheckProgram.jet: recheck dependent callers and recompute effects, ownership and layout. A typechecked input snapshot never blesses modified output.
3. Receipts: structural records list changed signatures, effects, runtime markers and source contracts, and host policy and memory/type obligations stay attached.
4. Safety origin (I1): a generated or rewritten `#Unsafe` region, whether from parsed text, deserialized code or a rewritten marker, is refused with no publish and no host effect. Legitimate user-written audited regions keep their exact scope.
5. Dependency transformations publish only into the authorized workspace snapshot and never mutate shared dependency storage.
6. Generated Rust rejection stays an internal error (exit 101), never a user-error discovery path.

## Proof
- Run the rewrite_contract witness (Examples/features/comptime/rewrite_contract/) through the self-hosted route cold and incrementally with identical output.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/changeset_ cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` passes for every negative variant.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.

## Batch
batch-jetc-driver: this is the transaction engine in the driver's query service with a sema recheck.

## Dependencies
#3527 (compiler sessions and workspaces), #3529 (code values) and #3528 (first-class compile-time types). The self-hosted run needs #218.

cards.title: Preparation execution, persistent state and native-call boundaries
cards.body:
## Outcome

Close arbitrary supported Jet evaluation during preparation, including compiled helper execution where required, nested compile/run sessions, yielded work and explicit prepared-data transfer. Define session-local metaprogram state versus values deliberately embedded in artifacts. Reuse ordinary functions, effects and audited foreign boundaries. Distinguish host native execution from selected target layout and runnable target artifacts; do not infer a Jai FFI guarantee from conflicting sources.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime
- crates/jet-interpreter/src
- crates/jet-jit/src
- crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude
- crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

Extend comptime_diff and phase/native helper witnesses: compute the same value in prep and application, retain explicit prepared state, reset session-only state across fresh builds, execute a generated child program and a permitted native helper, and reject a denied host effect. Cross-target preparation reports target layout while running only compatible host helpers. Cold/warm results and live effects must agree.

## Deduplication

#3509 owns this campaign. Existing owners #3147, #3175, #3181, #3199, #3201, #3202 and #3505–#3508 are reused, not replaced. #3418, #3419, #3421 and #3042 remain separate prerequisite owners. Shared specification references alone do not make these distinct implementation outcomes duplicates.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Preparation (`prep`) can execute any supported Jet workload: compiled helpers, nested compile and run sessions, yielded work and explicit prepared-data transfer. Session-local metaprogram state is separated from values deliberately embedded in artifacts. Host native execution uses ordinary functions, effects and audited foreign boundaries, and stays distinct from target layout and runnable target artifacts. No Jai FFI guarantee is inferred from conflicting sources.

## Current state
- Nothing has started. The owned paths are archived: crates/jet-comptime, crates/jet-interpreter, crates/jet-jit and crates/jet-driver. crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude is retained host runtime.
- Compile-time evaluation now lives in Compiler/JetEval/Source/Evaluator.jet (with CompilerServices.jet and SharedRuntime.jet), Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/BodyComptime.jet and Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Comptime/BodyRequests.jet.
- Existing prep examples: Examples/features/comptime/prep_block.jet, prep_fn.jet, prep_loop.jet and prep_branch.jet.

## Changes
1. JetEval Evaluator.jet: add a prep execution path that runs compiled helpers through the same MIR the application uses. Where native execution is required, it calls the retained JIT host adapter, never a separate semantic evaluator.
2. BodyComptime.jet and Identity.jet: nested compile/run sessions get their own workspace identity. Explicit prepared data (a typed value marked for embedding) is serialized into the artifact, and session-only state is keyed per build and reset on a fresh build.
3. Effects: prep code runs under the package's effect grants (#3526 mode). A denied host effect is diagnosed before execution. Host vs target: prep runs host helpers only when the ABI matches, and reports target layout facts otherwise.
4. Register diagnostics for a host/target mismatch, an unavailable native ABI and application-only execution attempted in prep.
5. Add the witnesses Examples/features/comptime/prep_state/ and prep_native/.

## Proof
- Run both witnesses through the self-hosted route cold and warm. Values agree with the runtime computation, prep prints occur once per logical run, and session state resets on a fresh build.
- tests/ui/prep_{denied_effect,abi_mismatch,app_only}.jet: `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/prep_ cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.

## Batch
batch-jetc-driver: this is driver and evaluator orchestration of prep sessions.

## Dependencies
#3521 (shared prep execution), #3506 (compile-time IO as ordinary functions), #3526 (above-level-five authorization) and #3527 (compiler sessions). The self-hosted run needs #218.

cards.body:
## Outcome

Key reusable computation by compiler/mode/schema/target/provider/input/authority and generated interface identity. Track reflected-fact reads, files, settings, code values, type factories, hook registrations and output ownership. Invalidate affected reverse dependencies and reject cross-revision handles. Preserve every effect of a logical invocation while reusing pure work; no cached transcript replay.

## Proof

Compare exact behavior to fresh compilation, inspect actual reuse receipts and count live print/effect occurrences. Exercise dev revision changes and rejected candidate rollback.

## Goal
Key reusable metaprogram computation by compiler, mode, schema, target, provider, inputs, authority and generated-interface identity. Track reflected-fact reads, files, settings, code values, type factories, hook registrations and output ownership, and invalidate reverse dependencies. Cross-revision handles are rejected. A logical invocation's effects happen afresh, once and in order, even when the pure work is reused; cached transcripts are never replayed.

## Current state
- Nothing has started, and the blockers are open.
- The owned paths are archived: crates/jet-foundation/src/CanonicalAST.rs, crates/jet-driver/src/QueryService.rs, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle.rs, crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build/errors_keys.rs and crates/jet-pkg-model/src/Lock.rs.

## Changes
1. Identity.jet: add a `JetDriverMetaKey` with the fields above, including the frozen mode from #3526.
2. CompilerQueries.jet: record read edges for each metaprogram evaluation (reflected facts, files, settings, code values, type factories, hooks). An edit invalidates the reverse closure, and handles carry a revision that fails when stale.
3. BodyComptime.jet: on a pure-computation hit, reuse the value but re-execute the logical effects (prints, IO) in source order. Receipts separate reused computation from fresh effects.
4. Jetpack Lock: standard and opted-in entries are keyed separately. Editor and dev sessions share the revision-aware identities.
5. Add the witness Examples/features/comptime/meta_incremental/.

## Proof

batch-jetc-driver: this is the driver query graph and identity.

#3530 (transactions), #3531 (prep execution), #3525 (scheduling) and #3541 (specialization identity). The self-hosted run needs #218.

cards.title: Project-defined semantic checkers over complete typed code
cards.body:
## Outcome

Extend read-only checker inputs to complete authorized declarations, typed call expressions, source/docs and solved facts. Reuse the shared metadata model for in-language and isolated extensions. Permit project checks and diagnostics without requiring mutation mode; proposed edits never auto-apply. Core language/safety errors remain sema-owned.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-driver/src/CompilerExtensionHook.rs
- crates/jet-pkg-model/src/CompilerExtension.rs
- crates/jet-semindex/src
- crates/jetpack-bin/tests/compiler_extension_e2e.rs

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

Create checker_suite witness: a project policy rejects a specific typed call/format mismatch, allows a correct call, reports a precise source fix and works across modules/generated code. Test sema-invalid input availability, revoked scope, checker crash/timeout and malformed findings through compiler_extension_e2e. No matching-text-only or mock-echo proof.

## Deduplication

#3509 owns this campaign. Existing owners #3147, #3175, #3181, #3199, #3201, #3202 and #3505–#3508 are reused, not replaced. #3418, #3419, #3421 and #3042 remain separate prerequisite owners. Shared specification references alone do not make these distinct implementation outcomes duplicates.

- Jet homes:

  - Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Comptime/Reflection.jet is the reflection model.
  - Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet sequences the phases.
  - The lint row L1401 compiler_extension is at Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet:3175.

## Changes
1. SemanticIndex.jet and Reflection.jet: add one read-only checker view over the finalized checked result, with the same records reflection uses: declarations, typed call expressions with resolved callee and argument types, source and docs, and solved effects. Visibility follows the checker's authorized scope.
2. Pipeline.jet: add a project-checker phase after sema succeeds. Checkers run only with a clean check or an explicit sema-invalid availability state. cards.body:
## Outcome

Expose existing FFI declarations, target ABI/layout, symbol names/mangling, artifact identities and available header/debug/probe evidence to metaprograms. Build a binding/checker example from actual inputs. Compare only fields supported by the evidence; absent binary signature information is unknown, never verified. Reuse current binding and link machinery; no new external dependency is approved by this plan.

## Goal
Metaprograms can read existing FFI declarations, target ABI and layout, symbol names, artifact identities and whatever header, debug or probe evidence is available. A binding/checker example is built from actual inputs. Only fields the evidence supports are compared: missing binary signature information is `unknown`, never verified. The existing binding and link machinery is reused, and no new external dependency is added.

## Current state
- Nothing has started, and the blockers are open.

- Existing native fixtures: the Compiler/Bootstrap/Tests.rs `build_local_c_provider` (:1794) pattern for local C archives.

## Changes
1. ForeignProviders.jet: publish a typed `ForeignEvidence` record per declaration (declared signature, target layout, symbol, artifact digest, and an evidence source of header, debug info, probe or none) into the reflection model (Comptime/Reflection.jet).
2. Jetpack Foreign BindingPlan.jet: generate bindings from that record, with receipts naming exactly which evidence was checked and binding it to the artifact digest.
3. Mismatch checks run before any unsafe call. Opaque or unavailable evidence yields `unknown` and never passes as verified.
4. Callbacks and exports use the canonical FFI model and existing unsafe and effect law. Cross-platform ABI is not claimed beyond the host that ran it.
5. Add the witness Examples/features/lowlevel/foreign_binding/ with a C source and a stripped variant.

cards.title: Field-derived live inspector serialization and migration workflow
cards.body:
## Outcome

Generate inspector descriptors and checked access adapters from the same canonical field metadata used by codecs. Connect them to the actual live inspector rather than leave host-maintained property lists. Keep serialization exclusions and editor visibility as explicit independent policy. Exercise defaults/version migrations and repair reachable tier drift through shared Prelude semantics, including current resident migration refusals where the contract requires support.

## Owned paths and integration

- examples/features/metaprogramming/reflected_inspector
- crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/GameWorldInspector.rs
- crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/GameDevProtocol.rs
- crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Registration/Serde.rs
- crates/jet-jit/src/Encoding.rs

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

Add/remove/rename a field and observe both actual inspector UI and serialized output update without a manual registry. Edit a supported property and observe the live value; invalid edits leave state unchanged. Decode historical data through a converter and a nonprimitive default on AOT/run/interpreter. Capture actual UI evidence and exact codec goldens.

## Deduplication

#3509 owns this campaign. Existing owners #3147, #3175, #3181, #3199, #3201, #3202 and #3505–#3508 are reused, not replaced. #3418, #3419, #3421 and #3042 remain separate prerequisite owners. Shared specification references alone do not make these distinct implementation outcomes duplicates.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Generate inspector descriptors and checked access adapters from the same canonical field metadata that codecs use, and drive the real live inspector with them instead of host-maintained property lists. Serialization exclusions and editor visibility stay separate policies. Defaults and version migrations behave the same on every tier.

## Current state
- Nothing has started, and the blockers are open.
- Owned paths in the body: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Registration/Serde.rs and crates/jet-jit/src/Encoding.rs are archived. crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/GameWorldInspector.rs and Prelude/CoreLib/Top/GameDevProtocol.rs are retained host runtime and hold the handwritten property catalog this card retires. The old examples/features/metaprogramming path is stale.
- Jet homes: field and serde facts in Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Serde.jet and Registration/, and reflection in Comptime/Reflection.jet. Core UI and game libraries live under Core/.

## Changes
1. Metadata: Reflection.jet exposes, per field, one typed descriptor (name, type, default, source span, serde policy, editor-visibility policy) from the checked declaration. The serde and inspector views are two projections of it, never coupled.
2. Core: add an inspector-descriptor generator (a Core game or UI module) that turns the descriptor into typed get/set adapters with checked edits. An invalid edit returns an error and leaves the value unchanged.
3. Host: GameWorldInspector.rs and GameDevProtocol.rs consume the generated descriptors over the existing protocol, and the handwritten property lists are deleted.
4. Migrations: version converters and nonprimitive defaults decode identically on AOT, JIT and the interpreter. Repair any drift in the shared Prelude code, not per tier.
5. Add the witness Examples/features/game/reflected_inspector.jet (the old examples/features/metaprogramming path is retired) with its expected .out.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=game/reflected_inspector cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `~/.cache/jet-luna/safe-jet.sh run` and `run --interpret` on the witness print identical output.
- Attach a live inspector screenshot or video after a field add and a rename.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.

## Batch
batch-core-ui: the deliverable is the Core inspector generator and its host consumer, retested with one golden and tier pass.

## Dependencies
#3524 (runtime type and value reflection), #3507 (typed generate), #3525 (scheduling) and #3147 (type and enum reflection).

cards.body:
## Outcome

Build the entity-system witness using public type discovery and ordinary safe library containers. Generate per-concrete-type bucket storage, stable typed handles where required, type/count/default tables and dispatch. Include entity types produced by another generator. Do not substitute a manual list or call Pool/SoA equivalent to the demonstrated bucket organization.

## Owned paths and integration

- examples/features/metaprogramming/entity_registry
- crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/MathTaskMem.rs
- crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Game.rs

## Proof

Run the entity_registry program across applicable tiers. Add/remove an entity declaration without touching central tables; verify counts, default creation, iteration and dispatch. cards.plan:
## Goal
Ship an entity-system witness whose per-type buckets, stable typed handles, count/default tables and dispatch are generated from public type discovery and ordinary safe Core containers, including entity types produced by another generator.

## Current state
- There is no `Examples/features/metaprogramming/` tree; compile-time witnesses live in `Examples/features/comptime/` (for example `comptime_table.jet`, `reflect.jet`, `prep_loop.jet`). No entity_registry example exists.
- Type discovery is the comptime TypeInfo built in `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Comptime/Reflection.jet` (`sema_comptime_reflection_type_info_fields`, struct/enum builders around :1330 and :1395). Evaluator access goes through `Compiler/JetEval/Source/ReflectionMethods.jet`. Only `has_marker`, `implements` and `has_method` are typed accessors (`Calls/Reflection.jet:132-155`).
- `Core/game/game.jet` exists. The Rust host Prelude has `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Game.rs`.

## Changes
1. Add `Examples/features/comptime/entity_registry/run.jet` with its golden. Entity types carry a marker. A `prep` generator discovers every marked type through the #3520 metadata path, never a hand-written list. It emits one bucket per concrete type (a `[T]` plus a generation-checked handle), a type/count/default table and a dispatch function. A second generator produces one extra entity type that the first generator must pick up (ordering per #3525).
2. Add any missing safe container support in Jet under `Core/game` or `Core/collections` (for example a generational slot list). Touch `Game.rs` or `MathTaskMem.rs` only if a genuinely missing runtime primitive is found, and record why.
3. Do not add an entity keyword, privileged body rewrite or Pool/SoA alias (criterion 4). Any new diagnostic gets a registry row and a UI fixture.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=comptime/entity_registry cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: counts, default creation, iteration and dispatch match on AOT and default `jet run`.
- The same program covers: adding or removing one entity declaration changes the tables with no central edit; delete then reuse makes a stale handle fail typed; reordered source traversal gives identical output.
- `jet run --interpret Examples/features/comptime/entity_registry/run.jet` prints the same output.
- No performance claim.

## Batch
`batch-core-meta`: the deliverable is a Jet library-plus-example witness over the reflection/prep surface. It lands with the other comptime witnesses.

## Dependencies
#3520 (public type discovery contract), #3525 (generator ordering), #3505 (const generics, if bucket capacities are static) and #3147 (declaration metadata model). Runtime proof on the self-hosted path needs #218. #3536 is a sibling witness, not a prerequisite. Keep the #3509 dedup note: reuse the named owners and never replace them.

## Goal
Close the #3509 Jai-capability and reflection campaign with one executable coverage manifest. Every captured peer family, public reflection family and new operation maps to a passing behavioral witness, or the gap stays open.

## Current state
- Every child card in the blocker list is still open (#3520 and #3421 building; #3521-#3538, #3505-#3508, #3418 planning; #3147, #3175, #3181, #3199, #3202, #3419, #3526, #3540 and #3042 ready). Only #3201 is done.
- No coverage manifest exists. Compile-time witnesses live in `Examples/features/comptime/` and `Examples/features/reflection/` (`reflect-value.jet`, `fact_reads.jet`). There is no `Examples/features/metaprogramming/`.
- The owned paths are stale: `scripts/agent` is now `Tools/agent`. The registry home is the Jet registry `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/`, not `crates/jet-foundation/src/Registry.rs`.
- The finite peer inventory (S1 The Way to Jai at commit 19cb4b7a, S2 the Jai Community wiki, and the rest captured 2026-09-21) is in the card body and stays authoritative.

## Changes
1. Add one manifest, `tests/meta_suite/manifest.json`. cards.title: Procedure identity baking and staged specialization
cards.body:
## Outcome

Complete procedure-of-call identity, compile-time argument baking and partial application through the existing callable/generic specialization path. Support polymorph-time constraints and type adjustment separately from body rewriting. Callable identity includes selected overload, generic/type/value bindings and captured arguments; no runtime string name stands in for identity. New public operations use the advanced control contract; ordinary existing generics stay available without opt-in.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-sema/src
- crates/jet-foundation/src/AST
- crates/jet-comptime/src
- crates/jet-tir/src
- tests/generics.rs
- tests/comptime_diff.rs

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

Add a callable-specialization package that resolves overloads, bakes two arguments, returns a callable and executes it across AOT, run, interpreter and applicable web. Contrast equal and distinct specializations, rejection of an unsatisfied constraint, a capture requiring runtime state, and cache invalidation after the selected overload changes.

## Deduplication

#3509 owns this campaign. Existing owners #3147, #3175, #3181, #3199, #3201, #3202 and #3505–#3508 are reused, not replaced. #3418, #3419, #3421 and #3042 remain separate prerequisite owners. Shared specification references alone do not make these distinct implementation outcomes duplicates.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Complete procedure-of-call identity, compile-time argument baking and partial application through the existing callable and generic specialization path. A callable's identity includes the selected overload, generic, type and value bindings, and captured arguments; no runtime string name stands in for it. Polymorph-time constraints and type adjustment go through the same checker, separate from body rewriting. New public operations need the advanced opt-in, and ordinary generics stay available without it.

## Current state
- Nothing has started, and the blockers are open.
- The owned Rust paths are archived: crates/jet-sema, crates/jet-foundation/src/AST, crates/jet-comptime and crates/jet-tir. The proof tests the body names (tests/generics.rs, tests/comptime_diff.rs) exercise the Rust path.
- Jet homes: generic specialization in Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls (Binder.jet, Resolution.jet, Static.jet) and Inference/ (Solver.jet, Substitution.jet). TIR is Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/TIR/TIR.jet, and evaluation is Compiler/JetEval.

## Changes
1. Calls/Resolution.jet and Inference/: define a `SemaCallableIdentity` (selected overload key, type and value arguments, baked argument digests, capture list). Specialization caches key on it.
2. Baking and partial application: a compile-time-known argument folds into the specialization. The returned callable carries the remaining parameters with their labels, effects and capture lifetimes.
3. `register_specialization` callbacks (ratified ballot text) receive the original type and value arguments, constraints and source. Returned adjustments re-enter the same generic checker, and an unsatisfied constraint cannot be forged.
4. Opt-in gate: new public baking operations need the #3526 mode.
5. Register diagnostics for an unsatisfied constraint, a runtime-state capture in a baked argument, and an ambiguous or absent identity.
6. Add the witness Examples/features/comptime/callable_specialization/.

## Proof
- The witness produces identical output on AOT, `jet run` and `--interpret` through the self-hosted route. Repeated and incremental builds give identical identities.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/specialize_ cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: this is generic resolution and identity in JetSema.

## Dependencies
#3528 (compile-time types), #3522 (callable signatures) and #3529 (code values). The self-hosted run needs #218.

cards.body:
Measure current Core workloads with the existing gauntlet and Core comparison harness. Record exact inputs, output oracles, compiler and host identity, matched peer ratios, and losses. Optimize only a verified hot path; never average away a loss or claim an unmeasured win.

Criteria:
1. At least one frequency-weighted numerics or text workload has a fresh matched Jet/peer receipt.
2. Core source-vs-native comparison records output parity and runtime ratios.
3. Any loss or inconclusive cell remains an explicit blocker with an owner; no strict win is claimed without evidence.
4. The focused measurement commands and outputs are reproducible from disk-backed scratch.

Non-goal: broad suite publication or changing the strict comparator.

log.text: Remaining blockers are explicit. The paired surface cell is inconclusive: 434.419 ms surface vs 436.147 ms plain, ratio 0.996038033, paired 95% interval 0.9909432457..1.0052586690. The Base64 wrapper cell is a loss: source 1.146731x Rust and dispatcher 1.077537x, so it is not a strict win. The sieve numerics cell is also a loss against Rust/C/Zig/Node (19.433474x, 15.127662x, 15.801042x, 3.102871x) despite exact output parity. The integrated gate remains honest and failing: 0/27 cells pass, 2602 findings, with stale conformance/tier evidence and a version-2 compiler baseline missing required version-4 identities. No strict performance win is claimed.

Route audit complete: generated Core metadata owns the moved set, sys.success, time.expiring, web storage constructors, data sketch helpers, units.from, Base64 predicate, process.status_ok, and selected math members. No duplicate dispatcher rows or stale moved set/sys/expiry routes remain; remaining native rows are distinct APIs or comptime helpers. Ledger check remains green.

Correction: the prior log with `2,? ms` placeholders is superseded and must not be used as evidence. Exact medians are 434.419 ms surface and 436.147 ms plain; see the subsequent corrected log and gauntlet/performance-surface-evidence.json.

Fresh paired surface medians are 434.419 ms (surface) and 436.147 ms (plain), ratio 0.996038033. The 95% paired-bootstrap interval is 0.9909432457..1.0052586690, which crosses 1; verdict remains inconclusive. Exact receipt: gauntlet/performance-surface-evidence.json.

Fresh paired surface proof completed with 10 warmups and 100 trials on the current compiler artifact. `compound_assign_vs_binary_assign` point ratio is 0.996038033 (surface median 2,? ms / plain median 2,? ms); paired 95% ratio interval is 0.9909432457..1.0052586690, so verdict is inconclusive and validation correctly fails. Output and identity checks are recorded in `gauntlet/performance-surface-evidence.json`; no strict surface win is claimed. The integrated gate now executes and reports fail (0/27 cells pass, 2602 findings), including stale conformance/tier evidence and the version-2 compiler baseline missing version-4 peer identity. These are explicit proof blockers, not hidden by aggregation.

Optimization applied after correctness closure: `core.collections.set.isdisjoint` now scans the first set and returns false on the first shared item instead of constructing a full temporary intersection. This removes avoidable allocation and work while preserving the same Bool contract. Fresh JIT output was `true`; fresh release AOT output was `true`. cards.title: CoreLib expert idioms and canonical formatting
cards.body: Replace redundant Unit wildcard bindings with calls where failure propagation is preserved; use ordered arm tables when equivalent, not for state-changing or cascading branches; format Core declarations with exactly one empty line between them. Once D-PREP-SURFACE2 is implemented, migrate ordinary Core constants to plain names and reserve @ for compiler-owned metadata. Check call behavior on applicable tiers and measure matched performance before claiming an improvement. Existing L0507/L0514 and the formatter are the canonical tools; do not mint duplicate syntax or bulk-rewrite unchecked code.
cards.plan:
**Goal.** Finish the Core idiom cleanup:
- Unit-validator results are no longer bound to `_`.
- Equivalent multi-way branches become ordered arm tables.
- Module constants follow the current naming ruling.

Every change must be semantics-preserving and done one module at a time.

**Current state.**
- c1 (the formatter keeps exactly one blank line between definitions) is met.
- 228 lines still match `^\s*_ (::|=|:=) ` in Core/**/*.jet. By file: `Core/compute/compute.jet` 78, `Core/encoding/toml.jet` 28, `encoding/xml.jet` 24, `encoding/json.jet` 16, `regex/regex.jet` 12, `args/args.jet` 11, `sync/sync.jet` 10, `web/forms.jet` 10.
- Typical case: validators such as `compute.jet:1229 fn finite_or_error(value: Float) -> Bool ComputeError!` return a constant `Ok(true)`, and callers write `_ :: finite_or_error(value)` (compute.jet:116, :190).
- Not every `_ ::` qualifies:
  - `_ :: checked_numel(shape) ?? return Err(...)` (compute.jet:100) discards a real Int.
  - `_ :: ~timing` (forms.jet:298) is an unused-parameter discard.
- L0507 auto-fix (#3679) is done. The arm-table lint fixture is `tests/ui_lint/prefer_arm_table.jet`.
- c4 is superseded by the owner's ALL_CAPS ruling for module constants (#3584, building). The D-PREP surface it waited for has landed (`Examples/features/comptime/prep_*.jet`).
- The working tree has an uncommitted `!E` → `E!` syntax sweep across 100 Core files. Rebase each module patch on top of it.

**Changes (one module per patch, largest first).**
1. `Core/compute/compute.jet`, then `solve.jet`: turn always-`Ok(true)` validators (`finite_or_error`, `validate_tensor_ref`, …) into unit-fallible `-> ComputeError!`. Callers become bare propagating calls (`finite_or_error(value)?`). Keep discards that throw away a real value.
2. `Core/encoding/{toml,xml,json}.jet`: same treatment for parser `&self.assign(...)`/`&self.bump()` calls whose result is not needed. Where the value is genuinely unused, use `.drop("reason")`, not `_ ::`.
3. `Core/regex/regex.jet`, `Core/args/args.jet`, `Core/sync/sync.jet`, `Core/web/forms.jet`: same rule.
4. In each touched module, convert only the if/else-if chains that L0507/L0514 flag and that have no side effects in conditions. Keep comparison count and fallthrough.
5. c4: constants in touched modules follow #3584 ALL_CAPS. No leading `@`.

**Proof.**
- Per module: `jet fmt --check` and `jet check` are clean (see add_criteria).
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=tooling/compute_ cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: green, with identical success and ComputeError lines.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/ cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` and `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=text/regex cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: green.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui_lint/prefer_arm_table.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots lint_snapshots`: unchanged.
- No performance claim.

**Batch.** `batch-core-encoding`: most of the edits are encoding/regex parsers. The compute and forms modules are Core-only too and ride the same Core retest. No compiler change is needed.

**Dependencies.** None. #3551 and #3521 are not prerequisites, and c4 follows #3584's ruling rather than waiting on it.

cards.title: Choose whether to warn on one-shot mutable selection
cards.body: Core often initializes a mutable value only to replace it once under a condition (for example, Core/compute/compute.jet rhs_cols). Decide whether to advise an immutable if-expression when the initializer and update are adjacent, the value is not observed before the update, and the branch does not change state. Preserve mutable bindings in loops, parsing, and state machines. This is a new lint policy, not a syntax or optimizer change; any diagnostic needs a registry row and UI snapshot after ratification.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Deliver D-ONESHOT-MUT1=A (ratified): an advisory lint for a mutable local that gets a literal default and is then replaced once by the immediately following Boolean `if`. It points to the immutable value-`if` form:
```jet
fn columns(shape: [Int]) -> Int {
    cols :: if shape.len() == 2 -> shape[1] else -> 1
    cols
}
```
It never warns if the name is read between the two statements, reassigned later, captured, passed by mutable reference, or used in a loop. It never rewrites code automatically, and a bare warning does not block building. This is a lint policy, not a syntax or optimizer change.

## Current state
- The motivating site is `Core/compute/compute.jet:494-495`: `rhs_cols := 1` then `if b.shape.len() == 2 -> rhs_cols = b.shape[1]`, then read at :496 and in later loop headers (:502, :555).
- No implementation or registry row exists (grep for one_shot/ONESHOT in Compiler/, crates/ and `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Diagnostics.jet`: none). The card had no plan.
- Self-hosted lint homes: JetSema currently emits only L0101/L0102 advisories (`Ownership/Checks.jet:396-400`). Statement sequencing lives in `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Statements.jet`, and checked write facts come from ownership state.
- Interpretation of "used in a loop" (needs owner confirmation only if wrong): the declaration/replacement pair sits inside a loop body, or the variable is written inside a loop. A later read in a loop header, as at the Core site, does not suppress the warning; otherwise the ratified motivating site could never warn.

## Changes
1. Registry: add `L05xx one_shot_mutable_selection` (advisory, severity warning, no Safe edit; Fix text shows the value-`if` shape using the user's names) to `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Diagnostics.jet`, then run `node Compiler/Bootstrap/generate-diagnostic-rows.mjs`.
2. JetSema `Statements.jet`: after checking a block, scan adjacent statement pairs. A `x := <literal>` binding followed immediately by `if <Bool cond> -> x = <expr>` (no else, one assignment) warns at the binding when checked facts show no read of `x` in `cond`, no later write, no capture by a lambda, no `&x` argument, and the pair is not inside a loop body. Use the whole-scope write facts, not a statement tail (the lesson of #3734's L0528 bug).
3. Rust mirror (so the shipped `jet check` shows it): the same rule beside the Rust stdlib lints.
4. Rewrite `Core/compute/compute.jet:494-495` to `rhs_cols :: if b.shape.len() == 2 -> b.shape[1] else -> 1`, and fix any other in-repo hits the same way (count logged on the card).

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui_lint/one_shot_mut_ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots lint_snapshots` passes.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=tooling/compute_ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes after the Core rewrite (unchanged output; `compute_linalg` exercises the solve path).

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: a statement-sequence lint in JetSema.

## Dependencies
None; D-ONESHOT-MUT1=A is ratified.

cards.title: Choose Core TCP stream handle shape across AOT and resident execution
cards.body: Core/net/net.jet exposes TCPStream as a public fd/host/port record, but the AOT provider owns an opaque JetTCPStream with live socket state. Typed TLS consumes that live stream. Decide one canonical source handle and migration before changing public fields. Preserve ratified D-NETSOCKET1=A and D-NETTLSSTREAM1=A, and prove safety plus AOT/default run/interpreter meaning without recreating sockets from fd.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Cut `core.net` over to the ratified opaque live TCP handle (D-NET-HANDLE-ABI1=A, D-NET-LISTENER-ABI1=A), and make `tls.client` consume a connected stream (D-NETTLSSTREAM1=A, D-NETTLSCONFIG1=A). AOT, default run and the interpreter must agree.

## Current state
- `Core/net/net.jet:31-41`: `TCPStream`/`TCPListener` are still source records `{ fd: Int host: String port: Int }`, with private fields since the forged-record test `tests/core_net_tls.rs:51`. The AOT provider owns the live socket as `JetTCPStream { inner: std::net::TcpStream, … }` (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/NetHTTP.rs:23`). The two carriers disagree.
- `Core/net/tls.jet:38` `client(host, port)` dials its own socket through `net.tcp_connect`. The ratified shape is `tls.client(^tcp, server_name:, config:, deadline:)` (D-NETTLSCONFIG1=A, card #300). `unwrap` (:94) and `peer_port` (:88) are explicit refusals.
- Log evidence (2026-09-24/25): TLS programs failed in generated Rust by cloning a non-Clone TCPStream, and the Reader fixture rejects qualified TCPStream with E0905.
- `Examples/features/net/tls_peer_identity.jet:10` still calls `tls.client("localhost", 0)`.

## Changes
1. `Core/net/net.jet`: make `TCPStream` and `TCPListener` opaque nominal handles (no fd/host/port record). Route every accessor (`local_addr`, `peer_addr`, `read_text`, `write_all`, `close`, `ready`, `set_timeout`, `nodelay`) through the typed provider leaf. Keep NetError conversion.
2. `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry` (CoreCallRows and the core type table) plus the Jet sema/codegen handle mapping: map source `TCPStream`/`TCPListener` directly to the provider carrier in AOT and to the same logical capability in JIT and the interpreter. Never rebuild a socket from an integer.
3. `Core/net/tls.jet`: replace `client(host, port)` with `client(^tcp: TCPStream, server_name: String, config: ClientConfig, deadline: Duration) -[Net, Time.Wait]> TLSStream IOError!`, consuming the stream. Update `connect_host` to connect and then call `client`.
4. `NetHTTP.rs`: take the TLS client from the consumed `JetTCPStream`. Mirror only what the shipped binary needs.
5. Migrate `Examples/features/net/*`, `tests/core_net_tls.rs` and conformance fixtures. No fd alias may remain in `Core/net`.

## Proof
- Add `Examples/features/net/tls_stream_consume.jet` with a golden. It runs local TCP then `tls.client` against an untrusted-cert peer and prints typed success and failure lines.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=net/tls_ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` and `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=net/socket_echo …` pass.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run` and `jet run --interpret` on those examples diff empty against their goldens.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test core_net_tls` passes.
- A search of `Core/net` for `fd:` finds nothing in TCPStream/TCPListener.

## Batch
batch-core-net: Core/net source cutover plus registry rows, retested with the net goldens.

## Dependencies
None open. Criterion 2 (owner ballot) is met.

cards.title: Wordfreq: finish borrowed byte-key map update without changing Core API
cards.body: New follow-up loss since completed #2254. Source-backed 2026-09-21 wordfreq matched entry: AOT Jet/Rust 11.30, Jet/C 9.79, Jet/Zig 25.62; default run Jet/Python 26.25, Jet/Node 13.59; exact outputs verified, partial-entry only. Existing TIR string_bytes_source marks a dead String.from_bytes(token) local, but map write route still selects jet_map_update_string; Prelude already has jet_map_update_string_bytes. Compiler lowering paths are currently dirty from concurrent work; do not overwrite other streams. #2858 owns full gauntlet, #3547 owns Core completion, #3559 owns peer API audit. No public API/syntax change or new benchmark framework.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Close the wordfreq loss by routing the exact shape "dead strict `String.from_bytes(token)` local, then an equivalent map update on that key" to the existing borrowed-byte Prelude helper. No Core API or syntax change, and no new benchmark framework.

## Current state
- Measured 2026-09-21 (source-backed, partial entry, exact outputs verified). AOT Jet/Rust 11.30, Jet/C 9.79, Jet/Zig 25.62. Default run Jet/Python 26.25, Jet/Node 13.59. These are historical failures, not passes.
- Jet compiler: `TLocal.string_bytes_source` exists (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/TIR/TIR.jet:35`) but is never set; every constructor writes `None` (`TIR.jet:43,53,57`, `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Functions.jet:1181`). The map-update route always picks `jet_map_update_string` for `String` keys (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Expressions.jet:733-735`). `Compiler/JetOptimizer/Source/Transforms/` has no bytes-key transform (only DeadValues, FixedReduction, InlineAlways, InlineMapping, ScalarAndCfg).
- Host: the Prelude already has `jet_map_update_string_bytes` (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.rs:3115`) beside `jet_map_update_string` (:2888). The shipped Rust lowering routes only to the string form (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/routes.rs:7940`, `MIRRust.rs:15784`).
- Workload: `Tools/gauntlet/entries/wordfreq/` has entry.json, expected.out and c, go, jet, node, python, rust and zig peers.

## Changes
1. `Compiler/JetOptimizer/Source/Facts`: a fact that marks a strict `String.from_bytes(bytes)` local as dead except as a map key. Set `string_bytes_source` only when the local has no other use, no alias and no escape.
2. `Compiler/JetOptimizer/Source/Transforms/StringBytesKey.jet` (new; add it to `Compiler/Bootstrap/sources.list`): rewrite the exact map increment/update to the borrowed-byte route and reject every other shape. The invalid-UTF-8 failure, fallback and evaluation order must stay identical. `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Expressions.jet` emits `jet_map_update_string_bytes`.
3. Minimal host mirror so the shipped binary proves the fix: the same exact-shape selection in `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR` routes and `MIRRust.rs`. Nothing more.
4. Focused accepted and rejected shape tests beside the optimizer, plus one Rust TIR regression.
5. Peer policy (criterion 6): check the declared peers against the entry.json token rules. Criterion 5 needs the ratified #2858 c15 Go peer in the wordfreq cell.

## Proof
- `cargo test --test tir_collections_and_methods -- wordfreq_bytes_key` covers accepted and rejected shapes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run Tools/gauntlet/entries/wordfreq/jet/run.jet`, its AOT build and `jet run --interpret` all match `expected.out` on the entry's fixture input, plus one invalid-UTF-8 input.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry wordfreq` gives fresh matched receipts with a strict per-metric verdict. Any remaining loss stays open with an owner.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-back`: an optimizer/codegen transform. Its gauntlet run joins the batch's measurement pass.

## Dependencies
None blocking. #2858 owns the full gauntlet and the Go peer, #3547 Core completion and #3559 the peer API audit.

cards.title: Bound one shared Core archive inflater for Core image
cards.body: Ratified D-CORE-IMAGE1=A requires caller-controlled PNG decode bounds. Current Core.archive.decompress inflates up to fixed 64 MiB before core.image can compare an explicit smaller limit. A small input can thus allocate far beyond a caller budget. Extending the public Core.archive API is owner-only; a private second image inflater violates the one-mechanism rule. Source evidence: Core/archive/archive.jet:33-34,119-200 and feature branch Core/image/image.jet:339-348; focused review agent://ImagePngAudit finding P1. Decide the safe common decoder seam before shipping image PNG.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement ratified D-CORE-ARCHIVE-BOUND1=A (2026-09-24): a caller-bounded inflater, so PNG decode (D-CORE-IMAGE1=A) never allocates beyond the caller's budget. The signature is `core.archive.decompress_bounded(data: [U8], max_output_bytes: Int) -> [U8] ArchiveError!` with a positive max and a typed `Limit` on overrun. The existing `decompress` delegates to the same internal inflater and keeps its 64 MiB behaviour. No duplicate DEFLATE parser, hidden provider policy, dependency or larger allocation.

## Current state
- `Core/archive/archive.jet:23-28` `ArchiveError{Malformed Unsupported Checksum NotFound}` has no `Limit`.
- `inflate` (`:120`) and `decompress` (`:191`) hard-code `C_MAX_OUTPUT` checks (`:142`, inner loops `:1103,1136,1331,1385`).
- No `decompress_bounded` exists (grep).
- Exports: `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCallRows.jet:1898`. Registration now goes through the Jet registry rather than hand-edited CoreModuleExports.rs.
- The dirty-path blocker is gone after the 2026-09-27 cleanup.
- `Core/image` is not in this tree; it lives on #3561's feature branch.

## Changes
1. `archive.jet`: add a `Limit` variant to `ArchiveError`. Thread a `max_output` parameter through the private inflate core (stored, fixed and dynamic paths), checking it before appending each decoded byte or copy run. Add `pub fn decompress_bounded(data, max_output_bytes)`: non-positive max returns `Err(Limit)` or `Malformed` per the ballot's positive-max rule, and overrun returns `Err(Limit)`. `decompress` calls the core with `C_MAX_OUTPUT` and still maps overrun to `Unsupported`, so its behaviour is unchanged.
2. Registry: add `decompress_bounded` to the core.archive export row in CoreCallRows.jet and regenerate derived tables.
3. Tests: `tests/archive.rs` cases for stored, fixed, dynamic, checksum, empty, malformed, exact-limit (ok) and limit+1 (Limit).
4. Example: `Examples/features/io/archive_bounded.jet` with a golden.
5. Image: when #3561's `core.image.decode` lands, it passes its checked scanline bound and maps `Limit` to `ImageError.Limit`, keeping malformed and checksum failures distinct.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test archive` passes the new bounded cases.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=io/archive Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` covers archive and archive_bounded on AOT and default run, `jet run --interpret` matches, and the existing archive.out is unchanged.

## Batch
batch-core-encoding: Core/archive codec change.

## Dependencies
None to start. Criterion 3 closes with #3561's image decode; whichever card lands second wires `decode` to `decompress_bounded`.

cards.title: Choose transparent RGBA input behavior for JPEG encode
cards.body: D-CORE-IMAGE1=A authorizes JPEG encode and says JPEG alpha is opaque, but does not say what encode(Image,.JPEG,Limits) does with RGBA pixels whose alpha is below 255. Silently dropping alpha can expose hidden RGB; selecting a matte color changes visible output. Go1.25 jpeg/writer.go:425-447 ignores alpha, while Jet promised one safe explicit image meaning. This is an owner-only user-visible product behavior, not a codec implementation detail. Resolve before JPEG encode while JPEG decode/GIF can continue.
cards.plan:
**Goal.** Build the ratified D-CORE-JPEG-ALPHA1=A rule: JPEG encode rejects any RGBA input with a pixel whose alpha is below 255, returning typed `ImageError.Unsupported` (advise PNG). No hidden RGB leaks, and there is no matte, compositing API or dependency.

**Current state.**
- c1 is met: the owner ratified option A on 2026-09-24.
- There is no `Core/image/` on master. Today JPEG appears only in the MIME rows at `Core/net/mime.jet:75,102`.
- The archived candidate `feat/core-image@b3c898cc7:Core/image/image.jet` has `encode` at :972 and returns `Unsupported` for every JPEG encode. It has no alpha check yet.
- #3561 restores the module and adds baseline JPEG encode.

**Changes.**
1. In `Core/image/image.jet`, as restored by #3561, add a private helper `fn jpeg_requires_opaque(image: Image) ImageError!`. It scans the alpha byte of every pixel and returns `Err(ImageError.Unsupported)` at the first alpha < 255.
2. `encode(image, .JPEG, limits)` calls the helper first, after the `max_output_bytes` pre-check and before any output buffer is allocated.
3. Decoded JPEG stays opaque (alpha 255), so decode → encode round-trips.
4. Document the rule in the `encode` doc comment: "JPEG has no alpha; non-opaque input is `Unsupported`; encode PNG instead".
5. Add the test `core_image_jpeg_alpha_rejects_nonopaque_across_tiers` to `tests/core_image_jpeg.rs`. It covers:
   - fully transparent red → `Unsupported`
   - alpha 254 → `Unsupported`
   - opaque → bytes that decode back with alpha 255
6. Extend `Examples/features/io/image.jet` with one transparent-input line so the golden shows the typed error.

**Proof.**
- `cargo test --test core_image_jpeg -- core_image_jpeg_alpha_rejects_nonopaque_across_tiers`: passes.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=io/image cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run`: identical output on every tier.
- No performance claim.

**Batch.** `batch-core-ui`: same Core image source and retest pass as #3561.

**Dependencies.** #3561. The module and the JPEG encoder must exist first. The plan is small enough to land in the same patch as #3561.

cards.title: Count member imports as uses of their required module namespace
cards.body: Both ratified dotted and grouped imports run31 after #3568, but L0103 falsely calls module alpha unused. Applying the suggested removal breaks dotted form with E0603 and grouped form with E0610. Fresh before/after evidence: index-followup/{mini-results.json,import-no-declaration-results.json}. This is a diagnostic-product defect, not permission to change import grammar.
cards.plan:
## Goal
A selective member import counts as a use of the module namespace it requires: dotted `use alpha.member`, grouped `use alpha.{a, b}` and forward aliases. L0103 (`unused_import`) never calls such a namespace unused, and no Safe fix removes a required dependency. A genuinely unused namespace still warns. This is a diagnostic defect, not permission to change import grammar.

## Current state
- After #3568 both ratified forms run, but L0103 says module `alpha` is unused. Applying the suggested removal breaks the dotted form with E0603 and the grouped form with E0610. Evidence: `index-followup/{mini-results.json,import-no-declaration-results.json}` (card body).
- Archived Rust: `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle/Liveness.rs:129-201` `collect_unused_imports`. The namespace candidate (:140-171) is judged only by `alias_used(ledger, alias)` on the namespace alias, so reads through member bindings (:173-198) never mark the namespace live. Its edit deletes the whole import (:157-160).
- Self-hosted: the L0103 row exists (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet:2583`), but no unused-import pass exists in Compiler/JetSema or JetDriver (grep). Name references are recorded as `SemaNameReferenceFact` (`CheckProgram.jet`, e.g. :868) and aliases are registered in `Calls/Core.jet:50-77`.

## Changes
1. JetSema: add the unused-import pass over the checked module (next to `CheckProgram.jet`'s name-reference collection). The namespace of an import is live when its alias is read or any member binding it introduced is read, including forward aliases resolved through `Calls/Core.jet`. Report L0103 only for a namespace with no live alias and no live member. A member binding with no reads gets its own L0103 whose edit removes only that member. Skip `pub`/package-pub imports and C headers, as the Rust pass does.
2. The Safe edit never deletes an import whose namespace is required by a used member; such an import never becomes a candidate.
3. Rust mirror (the shipped binary must stop the false warning): in `Liveness.rs`, compute namespace liveness as "alias used OR any binding from this import used" before pushing the namespace candidate.
4. #3702 extends the same pass so marker applications also count as uses. Land both together.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui_lint/unused_import_ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots lint_snapshots` passes (three quiet member-import fixtures and one warning fixture). Use directory fixtures if the imported module needs its own file.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run` on each quiet fixture prints its expected output.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: a liveness pass in JetSema. The Rust mirror rides the same build.

## Dependencies
None. #3702 (marker uses) builds on the same pass in the same batch.

cards.title: Run Jet repository dogfood through native Jetpack packages without Nix
cards.body: Owner authorization 2026-09-24 21:00 America/New_York: one additional GPT-6 Astra implementation worker, target usable project dogfood by 2026-09-25 07:00 local. Jetpack-owned nixpkgs adapters must natively convert/realize Jet packages rather than depend on installed Nix; the whole nixpkgs ecosystem remains the eventual target. Deliver the repository environment first; track uncovered conversions and defects in Tower. Self-hosting remains the primary delivery stream. Do not claim full Nix replacement from fixture tests or perform account/security changes.
cards.plan:
## Goal
The owner can enter the Jet repository's `env.compiler` environment through Jetpack-owned native packages, with no installed Nix and no Nix subprocess, and build and smoke-test the compiler inside it.

## Current state
- Criteria c3 and c4 are met: native adapter, lease and closure fixtures pass.
- env.jet:14-30 declares `module env.compiler`. Its documented entry is `Tools/agent/jet-env compiler <command>`. The local mapping catalog crates/jetpack/catalogs/jet-dev pins flake.lock revision 3ed67ec0…; native cache signatures and hashes remain mandatory for the bytes.
- tests/jetpack_dogfood.rs:1125-1160 fabricates shell tools, including a fake cargo, so it is not evidence.
- Open owner question q0oa4sn0 asks for approval to download and execute the 36 exact package selections (about 1.04 GB compressed, 3.95 GB of NAR data). The run would use isolated scratch under ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch, 20 GiB disk and 20 GiB RAM with no swap, no global profile, no persistent trust grant and no Nix fallback. c1 and c2 wait on that answer.
- Portable empty-Hangar import is #3578 and out of scope.
- The Jetpack that ships today is the Rust host binary (crates/jetpack). The Jet port cannot run yet, so this card proves the shipped product.

## Changes
No planned code. After approval:
1. Fresh `cargo build -p jetpack`, alone and within the shared bounded target.
2. Use an isolated HOME and Jetpack roots under ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/dogfood-3576 and a PATH that contains no nix.
3. Run `jetpack env compiler --prep -y`. A missing package must fail explicitly.
4. Inside the environment, run a real `cargo build -p jet` and an exact smoke check.
5. Run a same-Hangar locked replay with the network disabled.
6. Record lock, store and receipt provenance.

Each uncovered conversion or defect found becomes its own Tower card. A code fix is allowed only when it sits in the Jetpack provider or store path the run exercises.

## Proof
- `env -u NIX_PATH PATH=<no-nix> Tools/agent/jet-env compiler cargo build -p jet` exits 0.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env compiler target/debug/jet run Examples/learn/<hello>.jet` prints the golden output.
- An offline replay with the network disabled succeeds without acquisition.
- `command -v nix` inside the environment returns nothing.

## Batch
batch-measure: the remaining work is an evidence run, not a code change.

## Dependencies
Owner answer to q0oa4sn0. The plan is written for approval. On refusal, c1 and c2 stay open and the card parks.

cards.title: Lower checked Result payload range handlers without a compiler crash
cards.body: Fresh main compiler run of an accepted inclusive Result payload range handler exits101: checked result pattern has a non-result subject at41..168. Program fn result()->Int{42}; run matches .Ok(40..50), .Ok(_), .Err(_). Reproduced before and after current critical candidate; this is a preexisting lowering defect, not proven new regression. Source and exact CLI captures in ~/.cache/jet-luna/pip-stabilize-repair-fcq62mw4/index-followup/mir-resource-followup/result-range-{before,after}.*; scratch source pip-result-range-h2ne36pe/run.jet. cards.plan:
## Goal
An accepted range pattern on a checked Result payload lowers without a crash:
```jet
fn result() -> Int { 42 }
fn run() {
    if result() == {
        .Ok(40..50) -> print("range")
        .Ok(_) -> print("other")
        .Err(_) -> print("error")
    }
}
```
This prints `range`. First-arm ordering and owned-carrier semantics hold.

## Current state
- Scratch source ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/pip-result-range-h2ne36pe/run.jet exits 101 with `checked result pattern has a non-result subject`. Captures are in ~/.cache/jet-luna/pip-stabilize-repair-fcq62mw4/index-followup/mir-resource-followup/result-range-{before,after}.*; the recorded command used the retired scripts/agent path, now Tools/agent.
- The message comes from stage zero crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/mir.rs:7345,7692.

1. JetCodegen Expressions.jet: a Variant pattern on a checked Result carrier projects the Ok payload through the carrier's payload projection, then feeds the payload sub-pattern (a range) into lower_guarded_pattern_range. Keep the arm order and do not copy the carrier.
2. Stage zero: the matching carrier-subject handling at mir.rs:7345/7692 so the shipped `jet` proves the fix. There is no syntax restriction and no fallback.

cards.title: Bound native toolchain CAS bundles and support portable large-closure replay
cards.body: Native compiler dogfood metadata exposes existing project CAS defect: Provider persistence exports the full uncompressed closure per package.36 selected packages/40outputs union204objects: compressed1,039,872,339B,NAR3,946,100,296B. Sum of per-package closure sizes12.528GB; largest~1.9GB. Initial export lacks aggregate1GiB cap, but Store/Archive import/decode enforces MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES1GiB, so fresh portable-cold import of larger toolchain bundles cannot work. Current Store replay imports the archive even on the same-Hangar path, so it too is blocked for large bundles until #3576 adds authentic verified warm reuse. That proposed path is not yet exercised and must not count as portable import evidence. Static evidence from AstraJetpack Archive.rs:158-192,251-259,1121-1177,1622,2111-2126 and ~/.cache/jet-luna/astra-jetpack/measure_bundles.py. Estimates are metadata-derived, not measured actual realization.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Make large native toolchain closures (>1 GiB) portable. Export and import them into an empty Hangar under bounded memory and disk, with shared objects stored once and canonical `/nix/store` paths preserved.

## Current state
- Measured (static metadata): 36 packages / 204 objects, compressed 1,039,872,339 B, NAR 3,946,100,296 B. The per-package closure sum is 12.528 GB and the largest is about 1.9 GB (source: `~/.cache/jet-luna/astra-jetpack/measure_bundles.py`).
- The Jet port carries the same cap. `@STORE_MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES :: 1073741824` is at `Jetpack/Store/Source/Archive/HangarArchiveFormat.jet:13`, and `HangarArchive.decode(bytes)` (`:239-240`) decodes the whole archive in memory. `ArchiveTransfer.jet:34-35,46-47,159-160,174-175,956-957` and `NixCasBundle.jet:88-91` all read a whole `[U8]` and reject anything above 1 GiB.
- `NixCasBundle.jet:241` `store_nix_cas_build_unlocked` exports one full closure per package. The Rust reference defect that synthesizes names from CAS digests is at `crates/jetpack/src/Store.rs:1476-1478,1548-1553,1654`.
- Binary streaming file handles are missing from Core (#3593).

## Changes
1. `HangarArchiveFormat.jet`: replace whole-buffer `decode` with a streaming reader over a core.files binary handle, one CAS node or chunk at a time. Keep `@STORE_ARCHIVE_MAX_OBJECTS`, per-object node and field bounds, and add no silent limit. The aggregate size is bounded by the declared disk budget, not by 1 GiB of RAM.
2. `ArchiveTransfer.jet` import, attest and broker paths plus `NixCasBundle.jet` import: stream-verify the HMAC trailer and write objects by content address, skipping objects the Hangar already holds.
3. `NixCasBundle.jet` export and the Provider persistence export: emit one shared object set across packages, with per-package manifests referencing it. Preserve the original canonical `/nix/store` path mappings and per-object transitive references.
4. A new public archive format needs an owner-ratified contract. Prefer extending the existing CAS node encoding.

## Proof
- `JETPACK_WORKER=cas Tools/agent/jet-env bash Jetpack/Bootstrap/check.sh --area Store --tests` prints JETPACK CHECK OK, with `Jetpack/Store/Tests/Archive.jet` claims for a streamed import above the old cap (synthetic sparse objects), dedupe of a shared object across two packages, and tamper, oversize-field and object-count rejection.
- Measurement: cold replay of the real toolchain closure into an empty Hangar with network and host `/nix/store` absent, under `systemd-run --user -p MemoryMax=2G`. Record peak RSS, disk totals and execution of a dynamically linked toolchain binary.

## Batch
batch-jetpack-store: Store-area code and claims.

## Dependencies
#3593 (binary streaming handles), #3627 (archive port and tests land first).
