cards.title: Imported user markers: false unused-import lint, doubled E0927 with stale Why text, and a pub marker error drawn in the wrong file
cards.body:
Observed 2026-09-28 (target/debug/jet 13:07, d4bb652df plus working tree) with routes.jet = `marker Get(path: String, @sites: [.Function])`:

1. `use "routes.jet" as routes` plus `#Get("/users") fn users()` checks and runs, but L0103 says the import is never used. Following the fix (remove the import) turns `#Get` into E0927. The lint must count marker uses (#3571 covers member imports only).
2. `#routes.Get("/users")` reports E0927 twice for one site. Its Why says rules are "a closed, registered vocabulary (I7), not any PascalCase word", which is stale since D-META-USER1=A lets packages declare markers; the fix should name the declaring import.
3. With `pub marker Get(...)` in routes.jet, checking the importer prints E0003 "Expected one of fn, struct ... after a visibility qualifier" with the caret drawn on the importer's line 1 (`use \"routes.jet\"`) instead of routes.jet line 1: a span from one file rendered against another file's text.

Found by the mine-for-jet playlist run (report mine-for-jet-2026-09-28).
cards.plan:
## Goal
User-declared markers from an imported file (D-META-USER1=A) are first-class in diagnostics. A marker application counts as a use of its import (no false L0103). An unknown or qualified marker gives exactly one E0927 whose Why/Fix reflect declared markers and name the declaring import. A parse error inside an imported file renders against that file.

## Current state
- Observed 2026-09-28 (shipped binary) with `routes.jet` = `marker Get(path: String, @sites: [.Function])`:
  1. `use "routes.jet" as routes` + `#Get("/users") fn users()` runs, but L0103 says the import is never used. Removing it turns `#Get` into E0927.
  2. `#routes.Get("/users")` reports E0927 twice for one site. Its Why says rules are "a closed, registered vocabulary (I7), not any PascalCase word", which has been stale since D-META-USER1=A.
  3. With `pub marker Get(...)`, checking the importer prints E0003 "Expected one of fn, struct ... after a visibility qualifier" with the caret on the importer's line 1: a span from one file rendered against another file's text.
- Rust L0103 pass: `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/Bundle/Liveness.rs:129-201` (alias/binding reads only; marker resolution is not counted).
- Self-hosted: the stale Why is at `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/MarkerRules.jet:1076` (`sema_marker_rules_unknown_error`, with a nearest-name edit at :1077). The marker registry is at `ScopeMembers.jet:99-126`. There is no L0103 emitter in Compiler/ (see #3571). Marker declarations parse at `Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/Declarations/Markers.jet:35-87`.

## Changes
1. JetSema `MarkerRules.jet`: emit E0927 once per site (dedupe at the marker-resolution call so the qualified path does not report twice). New Why: "no imported module declares marker `X`". The Fix suggests the import that declares the nearest name, or `marker X(…)`, through `diagnostic_with_edit`. Update the E0927 row text in `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Diagnostics.jet` and run `node Compiler/Bootstrap/generate-diagnostic-rows.mjs`.
2. The unused-import pass (built by #3571) also marks an import live when a marker resolved through `ScopeMembers` came from that import's module.
3. Every parse diagnostic carries its source-file identity. JetDriver `Loader.jet` / the renderer use the file of the span, not the entry file, so an imported file's error shows that file's path, line and text.
4. `pub marker`: D-META-USER1=A covers declared markers, but whether they export with `pub`, and how, is part of the open marker-naming ballot on #3707. Until that is decided, the parse error for `pub marker` stays but is rendered in the right file (item 3). No new spelling on this card.
5. Rust mirror (the shipped binary): the same dedupe/text in the Rust marker path, marker-use liveness in `Liveness.rs`, and file-correct parse-error rendering for imported modules.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=marker_import_ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots` passes (the lint and error directory fixtures listed in the added criterion).
- `JET_UI_FILTER=E0927 Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` passes, with reviewed re-blesses of the Why text only.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: marker resolution and liveness are JetSema. File-correct rendering rides the same build.

## Dependencies
#3571 builds the Jet unused-import pass this extends (same batch; not a hard blocker for items 1 and 3). #3707 holds the ballot for qualified library markers and `pub marker`.

cards.title: Replace print-only browser examples with executable ones
cards.body:
Six shipped examples print API names instead of calling the API, so their goldens prove nothing (I5): Examples/features/net/browser_network.jet, browser_privacy.jet, browser_artifacts.jet, browser_locators.jet, browser_cdp.jet, browser_lifecycle.jet each say `// Live endpoints come from the host. This example only documents the API.` and print strings such as `locators:get_by_role+text+label+placeholder+test_id+css`. browser_agent.jet and browser_matrix.jet follow the same pattern.

An example that prints a claim is a dishonest proof: it keeps passing after the API breaks. Found by the mine-for-jet playlist run (report mine-for-jet-2026-09-28).
cards.plan:
## Goal
Replace the print-only browser examples with ones that call the API against a local deterministic BiDi fixture and print observed results (I5). Add a guard so an example cannot again pass by printing API-name literals.

## Current state
- `Examples/features/net/browser_artifacts.jet:7-8`, `browser_cdp.jet:6-7`, `browser_lifecycle.jet:6-7`, `browser_locators.jet:7-9`, `browser_network.jet:7-8` and `browser_privacy.jet:6-7` each say "This example only documents the API" and print strings such as `locators:get_by_role+text+label+placeholder+test_id+css`. `browser_agent.jet:15-22` and `browser_matrix.jet` print checklist strings.
- `Core/web/browser.jet:144-149` `connect()`/`connect_browser_profile` go to the native provider; `:160-164` `fixture_context`/`fixture_page` are value constructors only. No BiDi test double exists.
- `tests/truthfulness.rs:478-482` already walks examples and goldens.

## Changes
1. Fixture: a deterministic WebDriver BiDi test double written in Jet over `core.http.server` plus `core.net.ws` on 127.0.0.1:0. It serves a fixed page DOM, answers the session/browsingContext/script/network/storage commands the examples use from a recorded table, and rejects unknown commands with the BiDi error shape. Put it in `Core/testing` (test-support module), not in a product namespace. If `connect_profile` cannot target a loopback ws endpoint, add a typed endpoint field to `BrowserProfile` as the only provider change.
2. Rewrite the eight examples to connect to the fixture and call the documented API (locators, actions, network intercept, cookies/storage/screenshot/pdf artifacts, CDP ability probe, lifecycle, privacy cleanup, agent/matrix). Print observed values: element text, intercepted status, cookie names, and the byte length plus sha256 of screenshots. Regenerate goldens.
3. Guard: `tests/truthfulness.rs::examples_do_not_print_only_literals` fails when an example's `fn run` consists only of `print("<literal>")` statements. There is no allowlist.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=net/browser_ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes for all ten browser examples on AOT and `jet run`.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test truthfulness -- examples_do_not_print_only_literals` passes, and fails on a scratch example that only prints literals (checked once by hand, not kept).
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev_tier_parity -- network_http_and_browser_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot` stays green.

## Batch
batch-core-ui: Core/web browser plus the test-support fixture, proven by net goldens.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: Script authority: one default-yes confirmation for scripts with no declared authority
cards.body:
Owner note (2026-09-28, mine-for-jet playlist run): "Have allow by default with a prompt that just asks to confirm the used permissions if none are specified in the package/script/file/CLI command."

Today (observed 2026-09-28, target/debug/jet 13:07): a manifest-less script gets the D-AUTH-AMBIENT1=A floor (IO, arguments, allocation; in practice the whole Exec root, see #3697). Anything else stops. In a terminal the prompt reads `authority required for ["FS","FS.Read"] — choose once, project, or deny [application default]` and waits for a typed word; `project` fails for a script with no package manifest (Source/CmdCompile.rs:1283). Without a terminal the run fails with E1803.

Sema already knows every authority the entry reaches before running, so Jet can ask once, up front, with the call sites. This card holds the owner ballot on the prompt default and the no-terminal behavior. Packages, file grants (#Abilities), and --allow/--deny keep deciding whenever present.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Implement ratified D-SCRIPT-CONFIRM1=A: a script whose reached authority is undecided gets one upfront `Run it? [Y/n/always]` prompt that lists each authority in plain words with its call site.
- Enter or `y` runs the script once.
- `n` exits 1.
- `always` writes the grant into the script.
- With no terminal, the run stops with E1803 and a `Fix: jet run --allow=...` line.

**Owner quote**
"Have allow by default with a prompt that just asks to confirm the used permissions if none are specified in the package/script/file/CLI command."

**Current state**
- `Source/CmdCompile.rs:1196` `resolve_application_authority`.
- `:1240-1259`: when nothing is undecided, it writes delegation receipts and returns without a prompt.
- `:953-957`: interactivity means not JSON, not CI, and a TTY on stdin.
- `:1260-1270`: a non-interactive run emits `application_policy_diagnostic`, whose E1803 Fix names the inline `package { … }` row (`tests/ui/e1803_script_inline_authority.stderr:3`).
- `:1274-1281` prints the raw JSON list `authority required for ["FS","FS.Read"] — choose once, project, or deny`.
- `:1287-1476`: `once`/`project`, with everything else denying. Empty input denies too, which is the opposite of the ratified default.
- `project` without a manifest fails at `:1290-1298`.
- The D-AUTH-AMBIENT1 floor is unchanged.

**Changes**
1. `resolve_application_authority` renders `<file> will:` followed by one row per undecided authority: plain label, callee, and `file:line`, taken from the effect projection's call-site facts (`jet::EffectBudget`, next to `render_effect_projection_line`). Then it asks `Run it? [Y/n/always]`.
2. Empty input, `y`, or `yes` records `interactive.once` in the existing receipt. `n` exits `ExitCodes::USER_ERROR` without persisting a deny. `always` goes through the existing project-approval path. With no manifest, that path writes `authority.holds.allow` into the leading inline `package { … }` block (reuse the `jet fix --all` inserter behind `fix_all_inserts_script_inline_authority_block`); otherwise it writes `package.jet`.
3. Non-interactive runs: change the E1803 Fix to `jet run --allow=<Effects> <file>`, and update `tests/ui/e1803_script_inline_authority.stderr` and `tests/ui/env_config_secret_redacted.stderr`.
4. Add a generalized PTY helper next to `run_budget_update_pty` (`tests/cli_parts/support.rs:380`).

**Proof**
- `cargo test --test cli_surface -- script_authority_prompt_enter_runs_once`: prompt text matches the ballot, exit 0, and the file is written.
- `cargo test --test cli_surface -- script_authority_prompt_n_refuses`: exit 1, nothing written.
- `cargo test --test cli_surface -- script_authority_prompt_always_writes_inline_header`: the source gains a `package` block, and a rerun has no prompt.
- `cargo test --test cli_surface -- script_authority_no_terminal_e1803_fix`: stdin is null and the Fix line holds `--allow=`.
- `cargo test --test cli_surface -- script_authority_no_prompt_when_decided`: package.jet, `#Abilities`, and `--allow` each run without a prompt.
- Snapshots: `cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots` for the two E1803 `.stderr` fixtures.
- AOT path: repeat the Enter case against `jet build` then the built binary launched by `jet run`.

**Batch**
`batch-host-cli`: CLI authority transaction plus CLI tests.

**Dependencies**
None. #3419 folds its remaining UI safety rules in after this lands.

Current code still prints the old 'choose once, project, or deny' prompt with raw effect names; there is no Y/n/always prompt and no inline-header write. cards.title: jet review misclassifies authority changes (lexical < instead of subset; absolute package path in compared value)
cards.body: Found by the #2998 study. Source/CmdReview.rs:961-970 classify_authority_change compares token sets with < (lexical ordering, not a subset test). The compared value also embeds the absolute package.jet path (Source/CmdGates.rs:146-157), so identical authority in two checkouts reads as a change, and the direction follows the path sort order. Repro in ~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/ArchAdviceMeasure/review-defect/: narrowing [FS,IO,Mem] to [IO,Mem] prints widened, and a real widening prints narrowed with verdict reviewable. This is a safety review gap.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Make `jet review` classify authority changes by effect-set relation (widened, narrowed, or changed when the sets are incomparable), never by lexical order or checkout path. An incomparable change must block the `reviewable` verdict. This is a safety review gap.

**Current state**
- The fix is in the working tree, uncommitted (`git status`: `M Source/CmdReview.rs`, `M tests/review.rs`).
- `Source/CmdReview.rs:953-970` strips the writer's source path from the authority clause. `classify_authority_change` at :1010 uses `is_subset` both ways, through :1037, and :1041-1043 maps the incomparable case to `changed`.
- `tests/review.rs:686` `review_classifies_authority_by_effect_set_relation_not_checkout_path` covers identical, narrowed, widened and incomparable authority, with each side in a separate directory.
- The original repro is `~/.cache/jet-test-scratch/ArchAdviceMeasure/review-defect/`: `[FS,IO,Mem]` to `[IO,Mem]` used to print `widened`.

**Changes**
None beyond the in-tree edit. Integrate `Source/CmdReview.rs` and `tests/review.rs`.

**Proof**
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test review -- review_classifies_authority_by_effect_set_relation_not_checkout_path` passes.
- Rerunning the scratch repro prints `narrowed` for `[FS,IO,Mem]` to `[IO,Mem]`, and a real widening prints `widened` without verdict `reviewable`.

**Batch**
`batch-host-cli`: a Source/ CLI review command.

**Dependencies**
None.

cards.title: Library markers named through their module (#web.Get), then an explicit HTTP route exposure surface
cards.body:
Owner note (2026-09-28, mine-for-jet playlist run, FastAPI video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v6G_JJK01zU): "I like the potential idea of nested namespaces for markers like python decorators, where to make a rest api app, you can use @app.get(...), @app.post(...), etc. which is imported, then you can create the api with something like FastAPI(app, ...). Seems like overall very nice ux."

Jet today (observed 2026-09-28, target/debug/jet 13:07):
- D-META-USER1=A lets a package declare `marker Get(path: String, @sites: [.Function])` with a body that adds code, and `#Job` already collects marked functions into program subcommands (D-JOB-SUBCMD1).
- A marker from an imported file resolves only unqualified (`#Get`); `#routes.Get(...)` is E0927; `pub marker` is a parse error (#3702).
- HTTP routes are values: `mux.get("/users/:id", handler)` with `req.param("id")` strings; the shipped serve examples do not check (#3065 log). D-ENDPOINT-SHAPE1=A already derives endpoint contracts from typed handlers; D-SHAPE-EXPOSE1 leaves exposure spelling to a ballot.
- Counter-evidence: the Axum tutorial (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iPNEhKMIqNg, ~31:53) praises a router that is "simply a value" with no decorator or registration ceremony.

This card holds the full owner ballot on how library markers are named and whether HTTP routes use them.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-MARKER-MODULE1=A (ratified): library markers are named through their module (`#web.Get(...)`) and declared `pub marker`. HTTP route exposure is a separate owner ballot that must be ratified before any route-marker surface (criterion 4).

Owner note 2026-09-28 (FastAPI video): wants `@app.get(...)`-style namespaced markers. Counter-evidence: the Axum router is simply a value (~31:53).

## Current state
- Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/MarkerRules.jet:1041-1077 look markers up by bare `marker.name`. An unknown name is E0927 `isn't a known applied rule`. Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/ScopeMembers.jet:262.
- Compiler/JetParser has no qualified-marker grammar, and `pub marker` is a parse error (#3702).
- HTTP routes are values (`mux.get("/users/:id", handler)`). Typed path binding exists (Examples/features/web/battery/run.jet:135).

## Changes
1. JetParser: parse `#ident(.ident)*(args)` into a Marker whose name carries a module path and per-segment spans (JetAst Marker node). Also parse `pub marker Name(...)`. This grammar is registered under I7.
2. JetSema MarkerRules.jet: the registry key becomes (declaring module, name). Resolve `#mod.Name` through the import binding, and `#Name` only for built-in applied rules or an unambiguous local declaration. Registered diagnostics: unknown module member, private marker (not `pub`), ambiguous bare name (fix: qualify it). Fold in #3702: L0103 counts marker uses as import uses, and E0927 is not doubled.
3. Add rows in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Diagnostics.jet and regenerate DiagnosticRows.jet with `node Compiler/Bootstrap/generate-diagnostic-rows.mjs`.
4. Stage-zero Rust parser/sema mirror so the shipped `jet` runs the golden and snapshots (legitimate user-visible mirror).
5. After criterion 1 lands, Pip raises the route-exposure ballot: an explicit root such as http.routes(from: Api), a #HTTP program struct like #CLI, or value routes only. It must cover no package-wide scan, one route descriptor (I8), the existing specificity ordering, `HTTPResponse HTTPError!` handlers, OpenAPI from one representation, and I9 on four tiers. Criteria 2-3 wait for that ballot.

## Proof
- `cargo test --test selfhost_parser generated_jet_call_arguments_match_native_parser_contract` passes with new CASES rows for qualified markers.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=modules/qualified_marker cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/marker_qualified_unknown.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`, and the same for _private and _ambiguous.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.

## Batch
batch-jetc-front: new grammar plus AST, with the parser-slice proof. Sema resolution rides the same build.

## Dependencies
None for criterion 1. Criteria 2-3 need the route-exposure ballot (criterion 4). #3702 overlaps; land them together.

cards.title: Sema keeps the default Err route on functions that cannot fail (D-FAILURE-FOUNDATION1 says it removes it)
cards.body:
D-FAILURE-FOUNDATION1=A: "Every function has the structured Error route by default. Sema removes it when impossible." Observed 2026-09-28 (target/debug/jet 13:07, d4bb652df plus working tree):

```jet
pub fn twice(n: Int) -> Int {
    return n * 2
}
```

`jet inspect expand --facts callable-signature honest.jet` prints `twice ... -> Int effects=[] errors=[Err] failure=Int (implicit default !Err)`. The route is not removed, so callers in infallible contexts reject the call. That is why #3591 had to add `!Never` by hand to pure Core helpers (Core/process, Core/app) and #3693 hit ten errors in `use core.process`.

A signature that claims a failure the body cannot produce is dishonest in the owner's sense, and the ceremony it forces (`!Never` on helpers) is the kind D-FAILURE-FOUNDATION1 was ratified to remove. Found by the mine-for-jet playlist run (report mine-for-jet-2026-09-28).
cards.plan:
## Goal
D-FAILURE-FOUNDATION1=A says "Every function has the structured Error route by default. Sema removes it when impossible." Implement the removal: a function without a written failure contract has its failure set inferred from its body, the way effect rows are inferred (D-EFFECT-OMIT1). A helper that cannot fail is then callable from a `Never!` context without ceremony, and the hand-written `Never!` markers in Core go away. This card owns the sema inference; #3740 owns the ABI/lowering that consumes it.

## Current state
- Observed 2026-09-28: `jet inspect expand --facts callable-signature` on `pub fn twice(n: Int) -> Int { return n * 2 }` prints `errors=[Err] failure=Int (implicit default !Err)`.
- Self-hosted:
  - `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Declarations.jet:23-35` `sema_failure_contract_source` returns "implicit default !Err" whenever no contract is written. `Registration/Checked.jet:173-180` `sema_checked_failure` gives `TFailureCarrier.Result(ty, Err)` for any unannotated return, and `Calls/Resolution.jet:80-84` does the same at call resolution.
  - Failure inference exists only for lambdas/callbacks (`Scopes.jet:338-339`, `Expressions/Lambdas.jet:1567-1568`).
  - The Rust reference is `crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/items.rs:1243-1247`.
- The workaround is visible in Core: `Never!` on pure helpers at `Core/process/process.jet:130,141,146,154,181,240,253,340` and `Core/app/app.jet:183,191,239,249,263` (added by #3591; #3693 hit ten errors in `use core.process`).

## Changes
1. JetSema: add a failure-set solve beside the effect solve (`Effects/Checks.jet` `sema_effect_solve`, reusing its call-edge graph and SCC fixpoint). A function's inferred failure set is the union of failures from reachable `?`/implicit propagation, fallible callee edges and `Err` returns. It is empty when none exist. Function values, trait dispatch and closures contribute their declared or inferred callable type, and an unknown callee is maximal (`Err`).
2. Registration/call resolution: for an unwritten contract, publish the solved set as the checked failure fact (`TFailureCarrier.Infallible` when empty). `sema_failure_contract_source` reports "inferred: none" or "inferred: E1, E2" with provenance. A written contract stays a pin.
3. `jet inspect expand --facts callable-signature` (host) prints the inferred set. The public API summary records the inferred set of exported functions, and a change is reported like an effect-row change (wording per #3742's D-FAIL-PUBSIG1 outcome).
4. Rust mirror (Core compiles with the shipped binary): the same inference in crates/jet-sema.
5. Remove every `Never!` in Core/ that exists only to drop the default route, in one cutover.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet inspect expand --facts callable-signature tests/ui/inferred_failure_pure_helper.jet` prints `errors=[]` for `twice`.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/inferred_failure_ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet check Core/process/process.jet` and `Tools/agent/jet-env jet check Core/app/app.jet` report no problems with the markers removed. `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=io/ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes (process/app users).

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: failure-set inference is a JetSema solve. The Core cleanup and Rust mirror ride the same build.

## Dependencies
None blocking. #3740 builds its plain-return lowering on this fact. The API-summary wording follows the open D-FAIL-PUBSIG1 ballot on #3742, but the inference itself is correct under every option.

cards.title: Honest signatures: name the principle and show every function's full inferred contract, including determinism
cards.body:
Owner note (2026-09-28): "Want to find the video that talks about framing functions as honest/dishonest vs deterministic/nondeterministic. Want to incorporate that idea/philosophy into jet."

Source: Logan Smith, "How to write the perfect function" (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2OMRWPOSw9s, already in Docs/spec/reference/prior-art.md). At 10:49 he defines an honest function as one that touches the outside world only through its signature; mutation of an argument the caller hands over stays honest. At 12:25 he notes that dishonesty is infectious. At 18:20 he says to keep dishonest code at the top of the call tree. At 22:43-25:05 he makes code deterministic by passing a seeded generator instead of reading a global one. Jet mapping: an empty effect row with & parameters is Smith's honest function, an effect row names the dishonesty, and D-DET1's injectable Rng is his seeded-generator fix. (Correction: the first report said the video was not found; it was in prior art all along.)

Jet facts (observed 2026-09-28): effect rows are inferred and may stay unwritten (D-EFFECT-OMIT1); call sites must write & to mutate (E0202); D-FAILURE-FOUNDATION1 promises sema removes the default Err route when impossible, but it does not (#3708); #Pre conditions may have side effects (#3699). `jet inspect expand --facts callable-signature` renders the full inferred contract (`load ... effects=[FS, FS.Read] errors=[Err]`), but LSP hover builds its text from written effect rows only (crates/jet-semindex/src/Build.rs:2863-2877) and appends the whole program's effect line, so an unwritten row hovers like a pure function.

This card holds the owner ballot on naming the principle and the determinism label.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-HONEST-SIG1=A (ratified), "Name it and show it". Owner note (2026-09-28): "Want to find the video that talks about framing functions as honest/dishonest vs deterministic/nondeterministic. Want to incorporate that idea/philosophy into jet."

Every view that shows a signature (hover, `jet doc`, API snapshots, diagnostics) must show the full inferred contract (parameters, result, failure and effects) plus one label:
- `honest` for an empty row. `&` parameters stay honest because the caller grants that access.
- `deterministic` for a row that passes the existing `#Replayable` check.
- Otherwise `dishonest: <first effect>`.

Nothing new is written in source.

The source is Logan Smith, "How to write the perfect function" (youtube 2OMRWPOSw9s, already in `Docs/spec/reference/prior-art.md`), at 10:49, 12:25, 18:20 and 22:43-25:05. In Jet's terms, an empty row is Smith's honest function, a row names the dishonesty, and D-DET1's injectable `Rng` is his seeded-generator fix.

## Current state
- Hover builds the arrow from written rows only: `crates/jet-semindex/src/Build.rs:2863-2877` uses `f.declared_effects`. An unwritten row therefore hovers like a pure function, and the whole-program effect line is appended.
- `jet inspect expand --facts callable-signature` already renders the inferred contract (`load … effects=[FS, FS.Read] errors=[Err]`).
- The `#Replayable` walker is `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Effects/Checks.jet:432-434` (E0725); function headers are at `Sema/FunctionHeaders.jet:57`.
- No "honest" label exists in `Source/LSP`, `Source/CmdDoc.rs` or `Compiler/`.
- D-FAILURE-FOUNDATION1 says sema removes the default Err route when a function cannot fail, but it does not (#3708). Until that lands, "can fail" is wrong.

## Changes
1. JetSema `Effects/Checks.jet`: factor the `#Replayable` reach test into `sema_effect_determinism_label(row) -> honest | deterministic | dishonest(first)`. Expose the label with the inferred row and failure set through `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/CompilerQueries.jet` (callable-signature facts).
2. Host mirror so the shipped tools show it:
   - `crates/jet-semindex/src/Build.rs:2863` reads the checked inferred row and failure set instead of `declared_effects` and appends `can fail: yes|no · <label>`.
   - `Source/LSP/Features.rs` (hover) and `Source/CmdDoc.rs` render the same line. API snapshots and signature notes in diagnostics use the same function.
3. Docs: the `Docs/spec/vocabulary.md` definition is written by the agent. The `Docs/spec/philosophy.md` text is written by the owner, crediting Smith. No duplicated catalog.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test lsp -- hover_shows_inferred_row_and_honesty_label`. A fixture with `load` (unwritten FS row), `populate(n, rng: &Rng)` and `twice` hovers `-[FS.Read]> · dishonest: reads files`, `honest` and `honest` respectively, and the same text equals `jet inspect expand --facts callable-signature`.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet doc` on the same fixture prints the same lines.

## Batch
`batch-host-cli`. Hover, doc and snapshot rendering are host tooling; the sema helper is small.

## Dependencies
#3708 for correct "can fail". The owner writes philosophy.md.

questions.text: I specifically wanted this to use the framing of honest vs dishonest not deterministic/nondeterministic from one of the videos we mined previously. Also the syntax is wrong, the return type arrow IS the effect arrow meaning fn load(path: String) -[FS.Read]> String
questions.answer:
You're right on both points.

The source is Logan Smith's video "How to write the perfect function" (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2OMRWPOSw9s). His idea: a function is honest when all of its outside-world access shows in its signature, and dishonesty spreads to every caller. Honest and deterministic are different things. A function that takes a seeded `Rng` parameter is honest, yet its result depends on that input.

The ratified outcome A does include honest and dishonest labels, but its title, gist, lesson, and one gain lead with a "determinism label". Its examples also use the old order `-> String -[FS.Read]>`. Current law is the fused arrow: `fn load(path: String) -[FS.Read]> String` (crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs:264-275; D-EFFECT-ROW2 and D-SIG-AFTER1 at Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:7496-7534; the shipped Examples/features/effects/*.jet files already use it). Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:2652-2672 still shows the old order and needs correcting.

A ratified decision cannot be edited, so I opened a small amendment ballot on this card, D-HONEST-SIG2. Its recommended option makes honest/dishonest the one label, keeps determinism as a separate fact you can ask for, and uses the correct arrow in every example.

Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-28.md:61-65 and 151-186; Docs/spec/reference/prior-art.md:349-360.

questions.text: need to define important info - honest, fallibility, and determinism, & repeatability (if different from determinism), please add all
questions.answer:
Added all four definitions to the ballot lesson and Q&A, and re-cut the options around them.

Honest: the function reaches the outside world only through its parameters and result, so its effect list is empty. Changing a & parameter stays honest, because the caller handed over that access.
Can fail: the function may return an error instead of its result. The contract is written T E!, or inferred, and Never! denies failure (D-FAIL-PUBSIG1=A). A missing T? value is not a failure, and neither is a panic.
Deterministic: the same arguments always give the same result. D-DET1 already makes an empty effect row mean this. An injected Clock or Rng counts as an argument, so a seeded Rng keeps a function deterministic.
Repeatable: running it again gives the same result while the files and databases it uses stay unchanged. It may have effects, but no clock, random numbers, network, or console except through an injected provider. This is exactly the existing #Replayable check (E0725).

Yes, repeatability differs from determinism. A function that reads a config file is repeatable but not deterministic, and it is not honest. The chain is: honest implies deterministic, and deterministic implies repeatable. Failure is independent; an honest parser can fail.

New options. A (recommended) shows honest or dishonest first, then can fail, and for dishonest functions repeatable or not repeatable. B shows honesty and failure only. C shows all four facts on every function. A leaves out only the facts that honest already implies.

cards.title: Typed flag sets over enums and checked packed fields
cards.body:
Harvest from the owner's playlist (mine-for-jet report mine-for-jet-2026-09-28):
- Andrew Reece, BSC 2025 (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i-h95QIGchY ~0:18:22-0:20:36, 1:25:35-1:30:43): enums used as one-bit flags form sets queried with AND/OR/NOT; flags can index lookup tables; mutually exclusive choices and independent flags should stay distinguishable even when both fit in two bits.
- Core Dumped (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z7wVUfnm7M0 ~0:09:49-0:14:14): set, clear, toggle, and read one bit with masks; packing eight toggles in a byte; the idiom matters for encoding, compression, hashing, and embedded storage.
- Code Guild short (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X40rcpLfMdY): Zig offers arbitrary-width integers.

Jet today: no typed flag-set or bitfield type exists in Core or the spec (searched Core/ and Docs/spec for EnumSet, BitSet, Flags, bitfield on 2026-09-28); users hand-write masks on U8/U32 values. A typed set over an enum would keep the beginner surface safe (no raw shifts) and give experts the one-instruction representation.
cards.plan:
1. Survey Jet's integer and enum surface for the smallest typed design (for example a Core Flags<E> value over a fieldless enum with has/set/clear/toggle/union/intersect, and checked packed record fields).
2. Raise a short ballot for the public API spelling with same-program alternatives (hand masks, Set<E>, Flags<E>).
3. Pair it with a two-program performance cell (Flags<E> versus hand masks) per the performance gate before ratification.
blockedBy: none

cards.title: Core JSON output differs from the Rust renderer Jetpack's lock and report bytes depend on
cards.body: Found by NixAreaPort (Opus 5.5) porting Jetpack Nix fallback records onto core.encoding.json (#3590). Differences vs jet_foundation::JSON / Rust renderers used by shipped Jetpack output: (1) key order: Core source keeps insertion order, but Examples/features/expected/serde/json_integer_fidelity.out line 2 shows parse+to_string emitting sorted keys - verify which is real; Rust keeps document order. (2) \\b and \\f: Rust writes \\u0008/\\u000c, Core writes \\b/\\f. (3) DEL and U+0080-U+009F: Rust escapes as \\u007f/\\u0080-\\u009f, Core writes raw. (4) non-finite floats: Rust errors, Core writes null. (5) float text (e.g. 1.0) unverified. (6) json.to_string is declared without a failure contract, so it is fallible (implicit Err) and callers with named contracts get E2404; it should be !Never like canonical. Byte parity of Jetpack lock/report/fallback output (Phase 2) needs one Core JSON rendering contract; decide per item whether Core or the Rust reference changes (owner-visible output format, may need a ballot).
cards.plan:
**Goal.** Core JSON gets one byte-exact rendering contract, so Jetpack lock, report and fallback files keep their bytes through the port (#3590, Phase 2). The contract covers:
- escapes
- non-finite floats
- float text
- key order
- an explicit failure contract for `to_string`

**Current state.** Confirmed in `Core/encoding/json.jet`:
- Key order: insertion order (:11-12), while `canonical()` sorts (:90-91). But `Examples/features/expected/serde/json_integer_fidelity.out:2` shows `parse`→`to_string` emitting **sorted** keys (`{"first":…,"max":…,"min":…,"second":…}`), while the typed path (:3) keeps field order. So the dynamic route probably still runs a Rust dispatcher renderer rather than the Jet body. That is an I9 split, and #3690 F1 removes it.
- Escapes: `\b`/`\f` are written short (:735-742). `\u00XX` is used only below 32 (:755-759), so DEL and U+0080–U+009F go out raw. Rust writes `\u0008`/`\u000c` and escapes DEL/C1.
- Non-finite floats become `null` (:708-709). Rust returns an error.
- Float text (`1.0`, exponent thresholds) is unverified.
- `to_string` (:81) is declared `-> String` with no failure contract, so callers with named contracts hit E2404.
- No owner ballot is open yet.

**Owner ballot (to raise: D-CORE-JSONBYTES1).**
- A) Core adopts the shipped Rust bytes: `\u0008`/`\u000c`, escaped DEL and C1, typed error on non-finite, document/insertion-order keys, and `to_string` declared `Never!` for finite trees.
- B) Keep Core's bytes and change the Rust reference and lock goldens.
- C) Mix per item.

Recommended: **A**, so lock bytes stay stable. The plan below assumes A.

**Changes (option A).**
1. `json.jet` escaping (:735-759): emit `\u0008`, `\u000c`, `\u007f` and `\u0080`–`\u009f`. Keep the `\n`/`\r`/`\t`/`\"`/`\\` short forms.
2. Non-finite floats are rejected where a DataTree Float is constructed from a non-finite value (`EncodingError` kind `Invalid`). Then `to_string(tree) -> String Never!` holds for every constructible tree. Where construction cannot guard it, `to_string` returns `String EncodingError!` instead. Pick whichever the ballot records.
3. Float text: match Rust `ryu`/shortest round-trip, including `1.0` staying `1.0`, and pin exponent thresholds in the example.
4. Key order: dynamic `to_string` keeps insertion order and `canonical` sorts. Delete the Jet-owned `core.encoding.json` dispatcher rows so the dynamic path runs the Jet body (#3690 F1), then regenerate `json_integer_fidelity.out` line 2.
5. Add `Examples/features/serde/json_byte_contract.jet` and its `.out`.

**Proof.** The command in add_criteria, plus `cargo test --test corelib_encoding_surface`.

**Batch.** `batch-core-encoding`: JSON source and golden bytes, retested with the encoding pass.

**Dependencies.** The owner ballot D-CORE-JSONBYTES1 (A/B/C above). It does not depend on other cards.

cards.title: Propagated failures report where they started and the path they took
cards.plan:
## Goal
When a failure propagates automatically to the program edge, the report names where it started (`failed here: file:line`) and every hop it passed through, identically on every tier (D-FAIL-MODEL1=A, D-ERRCTX1). Owner-directed P0 (2026-09-28, learnability report F2, probe p25).

## Current state
- Probe p25 (a `parse` that fails with `Err("empty input")`, called through `double`, `total`, `run`) prints only `start` then `Error: empty input` and exits 1, with or without `--verbose`. Re-run the probe on a fresh build first and record the result on the card.
- Rendering: `JetErrorReport::render_root` (`crates/jet-foundation/src/Outcome.rs:397-437`) prints message, code, causes, context frames and conversions, but no origin. The journey is composed afterwards by `render_with_style` (:464-469) from `source_journey` (:136), and the header reads "Trail [E3002] (N hops via ?, origin first)" (`jet_journey_header`, :1031). The existing golden `Examples/features/expected/errors/error_context.err.out` shows that trail for explicit `?` only.
- Capture: Jet codegen emits `core.errors.journey_frame_text` and `journey_reset` only on explicit `?`/try paths (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Expressions.jet:2763, 2796, 2854`). Automatic propagation and `Err(...)` construction record nothing. The shipped Rust path matches: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/routes.rs:9200-9205`, and `MIREval.rs:17098` for the interpreter.

## Changes
1. Jet compiler first. In `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Expressions.jet`, record the origin (file, line, column, function) where an `Err(...)` is constructed or a Core call fails, and add a hop at every automatic propagation site as well as at `?`. Use the existing `jet_journey_frame_text` route. No new Prelude symbol unless the origin needs a distinct kind.
2. Host mirror so the shipped binary proves the fix: the same capture in `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR` lowering. The interpreter reuses the `MIREval.rs` handler.
3. `Outcome.rs`: `render_root` prints `failed here: file:line` for the origin. The trail header stops saying "via ?" when hops include automatic propagation. Long journeys are capped with a count. `to_json` keeps origin plus every hop with file, line and column. `?(text)` context frames and conversions keep their order.
4. Tiers only marshal frames; none re-encodes the format (I9).

## Proof
- New golden `Examples/features/errors/propagation_journey.jet` (p25 in current syntax: `fn parse(raw: String) -> Int ParseError!`), with `.err.out`. Run `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=errors/propagation_journey cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` on AOT and default `jet run`.
- `jet run --interpret` on the same file prints an identical stderr report.
- Goldens for a direct `Err` at the edge, one hop, three hops and a missing-file Core origin (`errors/propagation_journey_core`).
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=errors/error_context cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` still passes after re-blessing only the header wording.
- `jet run --json` on p25 lists origin plus 3 hops with line and column.

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime`: the proof is a three-tier golden, and rendering lives in the host runtime.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: Every whole-value move out of a named place is spelled with ^, including bindings
cards.body:
What is wrong: the binding sigil silently decides ownership. Report finding
F4, probes p15 and p24:

    xs := [1, 2, 3]
    ys :: xs        // ys is a live read view of xs; xs.push(4) is E0212
    ys := xs        // xs is MOVED with no marker; later use of xs is E0121

At a call site, a consuming parameter already requires `^name`
(Examples/features/memory/ownership.jet). The binding position is the one
place a move happens with no mark. One character (`:` vs `=`) therefore
selects borrow vs move as well as immutable vs mutable. That is a hidden
dependency and a large reasoning footprint (Turon 2017).

Owner direction: adopt proposal P5 from the report. A whole-value move out of
a named place is always written `^name`. Writing the bare name where a
non-copy value would move is a teaching error with a `jet fix` edit.
Increment/decrement (report F3) is NOT part of this card; that stays in
discussion with the owner.

Owner instruction (chat, 2026-09-28): the owner reviewed the learnability report and directed that this fix be carded at P0. This card records that direction; it is not a ballot.

Probe sources live in the report's Appendix A. They ran from a directory with its own package.jet granting [IO, Mem.Alloc], on the working-tree debug binary of 2026-09-28 13:07 (HEAD 68e1f8fb plus another stream's uncommitted compiler edits). Re-run each probe on a fresh build before starting; a probe that no longer reproduces is recorded on the card, not silently dropped.
cards.plan:
## Goal
A bare name never silently kills its source, and `^name` is the programmer's exact move in every position. The rule follows D-COPY-DEFAULT1=A (ratified 2026-09-29; owner: "Compiler chooses if unmarked, programmer can manually put sigils where desired for exact. full control"). That ruling supersedes the 2026-09-28 P5 direction that made the bare form a teaching error. A last use moves at no cost, a non-last use shares (#3741), and `::` of a place stays a view.

## Current state
- Report finding F4 (probes p15, p24): `ys := xs` moves xs with no mark, and a later `xs.push(4)` is E0121. The owner carded this at P0 on 2026-09-28. The card was then blocked on #3741 because option A "makes last-use moves unmarked"; #3741's plan says to rewrite this card after ratification. D-COPY-DEFAULT1 is now ratified A.
- Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Ownership/Checks.jet records a binding initializer as a move with consumer "the binding `{name}`" (working-tree edit in the binding check that calls `sema_ownership_consume_expression`), so bare `ys := xs` still consumes xs. LastUse.jet already proves last use.
- The binding sigils are parsed in Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/Statements.jet.
- The new E0225 row in JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet (D-CAP-RECEIVER1=D) says "`^` is never a standalone expression". It must not reject `ys := ^xs`.

## Changes
1. Log the inventory on the card before any code change. Cover every implicit-move position: `:=` and `::` bindings of places, `a = b`, struct and record field initializers, collection elements, task and lambda captures, return, tail, break and yield. For each, record today's behavior and the target under A, and state the exemption: a last use moves unmarked.
2. JetSema Ownership/Checks.jet and Statements.jet: accept an explicit `^place` in every position as an exact move with consumer text. For a bare place, record a move only when LastUse.jet proves last use; otherwise defer to #3741's share/copy-on-write fact. Until #3741 lands, keep today's move, and #3715 shows where it happened.
3. JetParser Expressions.jet and Statements.jet: parse `^name` as a move-marked place in these positions. Limit E0225 to a mark that no consumer takes.
4. Rust mirror for the shipped binary: crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/bindings.rs, crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/bindings.rs and CheckerOwnership.rs.
5. Spec: update the ownership section of Docs/spec/spec.md, and add a Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md row citing P5 (2026-09-28) and D-COPY-DEFAULT1=A.
6. Add Examples/features/memory/view_move_copy.jet and its expected .out, showing `ys :: xs`, `ys := ^xs` and `ys := ~xs` side by side.
7. No migration: A keeps the bare spelling valid. Criteria 2, 4, 7 and 9 (a teaching error for the bare form, and "old spelling not accepted") are superseded by the ratified A, and Pip retires them on the card.

## Proof
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/move_mark_ cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` passes. move_mark_binding covers `ys := ^xs; xs.push(4)` → E0121 naming "the binding `ys`". move_mark_positions covers the other marked positions with no E0225.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=memory/view_move_copy cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes, and `safe-jet.sh run` and `run --interpret` print the same lines (I9).
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0. The self-hosted probe waits for #218.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: the ownership checker, the parser mark and the Rust mirror land in one build and one UI/golden retest.

## Dependencies
#3741 must implement shared storage for a bare non-last use; until then bare `:=` keeps moving. #3715 (in flight) renders E0121.

cards.plan:
## Goal
E0121 names what consumed the value and points a labelled caret at the move site with file:line:col. It never shows the placeholder "the earlier consuming operation" or byte offsets. `--json` keeps both spans.

## Current state
- Probe p24 (`ys := xs` then `xs.push(4)`) printed "consumed by `the earlier consuming operation`" and "move site: source bytes 235..237; reuse site: source bytes 242..244". Card #2387 (done) fixed call and method consumers only. The owner carded this at P0 on 2026-09-28.
- In flight in the working tree (uncommitted):
  - Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Ownership/Checks.jet:1187-1202 `sema_ownership_diag_moved` drops the fallback and returns `diagnostic_with_label(^diagnostic, origin.span, label)`. The label reads "moved to {consumer} here", or "… on an earlier loop iteration" when the move and the reuse are the same site. Binding, return, break and yield recorders now pass consumer text ("the binding `{name}`", "`return`", …).
  - The Rust mirror crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerOwnership.rs makes `consumer: String` mandatory, adds `.with_label` for the move site, and drops the "move site: source bytes" detail.
- Not re-blessed: 12 snapshots still show the old text, for example tests/ui/lambda_escape_no_take.stderr:1,8, frozen_capture_use_after_move.stderr:8, ownership_loop_reconsume_provenance.stderr:8 and struct_use_after_move.stderr:8.
- crates/jet-foundation/src/Diagnostics.rs:86 still prints "(source bytes a..b)" in the ICE panic text. That text is not a registered diagnostic, so it is out of scope, but note it.

## Changes
1. Finish the recorder audit in Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Ownership (Checks.jet, Crossings.jet, LastUse.jet): assignment, field initializer, capture ("the escaping lambda"), loop re-move and task spawn all pass a non-empty consumer. Add an assertion that an empty consumer is an internal error.

cards.title: Warn when else follows arms that already cover every case
cards.body:
What is wrong: probe p24 (second version) checks clean:

    if c == {
        .Red -> "red"
        .Green -> "green"
        .Blue -> "blue"
        else -> "unknown"
    }

The `else` can never run today. When a variant is added later, it goes to
`else` silently and E0307's exhaustiveness check is defeated. The flagship
example Examples/features/basics/pattern_matching.jet:12-17 teaches this
shape, and E0307's fix text says "or provide an `else` arm".

Owner instruction (chat, 2026-09-28): the owner reviewed the learnability report and directed that this fix be carded at P0. This card records that direction; it is not a ballot.

Probe sources live in the report's Appendix A. They ran from a directory with its own package.jet granting [IO, Mem.Alloc], on the working-tree debug binary of 2026-09-28 13:07 (HEAD 68e1f8fb plus another stream's uncommitted compiler edits). Re-run each probe on a fresh build before starting; a probe that no longer reproduces is recorded on the card, not silently dropped.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Warn on an `else` arm that can never run because the preceding arms already cover a closed set (enum, Bool, variant group, closed Optional/Result). A later variant would otherwise fall into `else` silently and defeat E0307. Owner directed P0 (chat, 2026-09-28; recorded direction, not a ballot).

## Current state
- Probe p24 (v2) checks clean: `if c == { .Red -> "red"  .Green -> "green"  .Blue -> "blue"  else -> "unknown" }`.
- The flagship example teaches this shape: `Examples/features/basics/pattern_matching.jet:12-17` (`describe_conn` covers Active|Reconnecting, Idle, Closed and still has `else -> "unknown"`).
- Self-hosted coverage lives in `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Coverage.jet`. `sema_coverage_check_table` (:144-164) emits E0307 only for else-less tables. `sema_coverage_missing` (:112) computes the missing leaves, and `sema_coverage_leaf_covered` (:66) handles group paths. Callers: `Statements.jet:357` (statement switch), `Statements.jet:2740` (no-else statement chain), and `Expressions/Control.jet:855` (value chain). No 'can never run' lint exists.
- E0307's Fix currently offers "or provide an `else` arm" (row at `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet:3415`, generated from `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Diagnostics.jet`).
- Archived Rust twin: `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/switches.rs:547` `check_pattern_coverage_complete`.
- In flight (working tree, 2026-09-28): the registry row `L0303 unreachable_else_arm` ("This `else` can never run; every case of `{type}` is already handled", Safe source edit) is now in `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Diagnostics.jet:305` and regenerated into `DiagnosticRows.jet:4775`. The emitters and fixtures are not in yet.

## Changes
1. JetSema `Coverage.jet`: add `sema_coverage_check_redundant_else(conditions, else_span, ...)`. When the table's subject is a closed set and `sema_coverage_missing` is empty, report L0303 on the `else` arm: "this `else` can never run; every case of `Color` is already handled; if you add a case later, the compiler will ask you to handle it". Attach a Safe delete-arm edit via `diagnostic_with_edit` (pattern: `MarkerRules.jet:1077`). Open sets (Int, text, open scalars, per `sema_coverage_is_open_scalar`) and non-exhaustive tables stay quiet. Call it from the three coverage call sites whenever the table has an `else`. The hooks wait on WaveJetCompilerBugs' in-flight coverage work (the #3587 fix is in the working tree at `switches.rs:786`).
2. Registry: use the in-flight `L0303 unreachable_else_arm` row (do not add a second one), and keep `DiagnosticRows.jet` regenerated with `node Compiler/Bootstrap/generate-diagnostic-rows.mjs`. Change E0307's Fix to name the missing arms first, with `else` only for open sets (Coverage.jet:153/160/163 texts and the row).
3. Rust mirror (the shipped binary must show the lint): the same check beside `switches.rs:547`.
4. Migrate `pattern_matching.jet` and every other in-repo trigger in Examples/, Core/, Compiler/, Jetpack/ and tests/ in one cutover (list the hits from the snapshot run on the card). Goldens stay byte-identical.

cards.title: Dropping the value of a pure call is a compile error
cards.body:
What is wrong: probe p03 checks and runs clean:

    fn double(n: Int) -> Int { n * 2 }
    fn run() { double(3)  print("done") }

The result of `double(3)` is thrown away. Must-use today covers only
fallible results (E0402) and `#MustUse` items. The Blackbox study
(100M compilations) found "ignored non-void return value" among the
costliest novice mistakes, with a median fix time at the 1000-second cap,
because nothing reports it.

Jet can report this with few false positives: effect inference already knows
when a call is pure. Throwing away the only output of a pure call is almost
always a bug. This is proposal P7.

Owner instruction (chat, 2026-09-28): the owner reviewed the learnability report and directed that this fix be carded at P0. This card records that direction; it is not a ballot.

Probe sources live in the report's Appendix A. They ran from a directory with its own package.jet granting [IO, Mem.Alloc], on the working-tree debug binary of 2026-09-28 13:07 (HEAD 68e1f8fb plus another stream's uncommitted compiler edits). Re-run each probe on a fresh build before starting; a probe that no longer reproduces is recorded on the card, not silently dropped.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Report a compile error when a statement discards the only output of a proven-pure call (`double(3)` on its own line). This is proposal P7. The Blackbox study (100M compilations) ranks the "ignored non-void return value" among the costliest novice mistakes, with a median fix time at the 1000 s cap. Owner directed P0 (chat, 2026-09-28; recorded direction, not a ballot).

## Current state
- Probe p03 checks and runs clean: `fn double(n: Int) -> Int { n * 2 }` / `fn run() { double(3)  print("done") }`.
- Must-use covers only fallible results (E0402) and `#MustUse` items. Self-hosted: E0402 is at `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Statements.jet:2759`, inside the statement-expression path (~2730-2762); `#MustUse` is gated at `FunctionHeaders.jet:58`. No discarded-pure-result rule exists in Compiler/ or crates/ (grep "thrown away": none).
- Solved effect rows come from `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Effects/Checks.jet` (`sema_effect_solve` :1013). Call-site facts (`SemaCallSiteFact.facts.effect_bound`) carry declared rows.
- Archived Rust twin: `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/statements.rs:2006` (E0402).
- New rows go in `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Diagnostics.jet`; `node Compiler/Bootstrap/generate-diagnostic-rows.mjs` regenerates `DiagnosticRows.jet`.

## Changes
1. JetSema `Statements.jet`, beside E0402: when a statement expression is a call or method call with a non-Unit result, record a pending discard fact (callee key, span). After the effect solve (`Effects/Checks.jet`), report a new registered error for each fact whose callee's solved row is empty (`-[]>`): "the result of `double(3)` is thrown away; `double` has no other effect, so this line does nothing". Offer two edits: bind it (`result :: double(3)`, Suggested) or `.drop("reason")`.
2. Stay quiet for unknown, generic, maximal or unresolved rows, for impure calls, for Unit/Never results, and for `.drop("reason")`. Never double-report a site that E0402 or `#MustUse` already reports.
3. Register the row (next free E04xx in the must-use family) with What/Why/Fix.
4. Rust mirror (the shipped binary must show it): the same check at `statements.rs` near 2006, using the Rust inferred-effect facts.
5. Run the rule over Examples/, tests/, Core/, Compiler/ and Jetpack/. Fix each hit (a real bug) or give it `.drop("reason")`, and log the count and list on the card.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0 (the Jet compiler source is itself clean under the rule).
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/discarded_pure_ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` passes. Firing cases: `discarded_pure_call.jet` (p03) and `discarded_pure_method.jet`. Quiet cases: `discarded_pure_quiet.jet` (impure call, Unit result, generic callee, E0402 site, `.drop("reason")`) snapshots `(no errors)` beyond the expected E0402.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` (full feature golden, a milestone-sized run for this card only because the rule is repo-wide) and `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` pass.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: this is a statement rule over JetSema's solved effect rows. The repo-wide migration and the Rust mirror land in the same build.

## Dependencies
None. It interacts with #3708/#3740 (failure-set inference), since a helper made infallible stops producing E0402 and may start producing this error. Land them in the same batch and run one migration.

cards.title: Authority errors read as a sentence, and printing or reading arguments needs no manifest grant
cards.body:
What is wrong, part 1: a package.jet with no authority block makes a
print-only program fail with E1803, and the Why line is a data dump:

    Why: required_effects=IO; granted_effects=; denied_effects=;
         denied_required_effects=none; undecided_effects=IO;
         authority=package.jet authority.holds

Part 2: the safety check fires before the program does anything a learner
would call risky (report F19; cliff principle L7; Swift 6's concurrency
cliff is the cautionary case). Card #2259 (done) fixed the `jet new`
scaffold and the fix line; hand-written or older manifests still hit the
wall on the first `print`.

Owner direction: fix both parts (proposals P16 and P17). Experts keep full
control by writing an authority block.

Owner instruction (chat, 2026-09-28): the owner reviewed the learnability report and directed that this fix be carded at P0. This card records that direction; it is not a ballot.

Probe sources live in the report's Appendix A. They ran from a directory with its own package.jet granting [IO, Mem.Alloc], on the working-tree debug binary of 2026-09-28 13:07 (HEAD 68e1f8fb plus another stream's uncommitted compiler edits). Re-run each probe on a fresh build before starting; a probe that no longer reproduces is recorded on the card, not silently dropped.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Owner-directed at P0 on 2026-09-28, from proposals P16 and P17.
- Part 1: E1803's human Why becomes one plain sentence. The key=value facts go only to `--verbose`/`--json`.
- Part 2: a package whose `package.jet` has no authority block may print, read stdin, allocate and read its own argv without a grant, on every tier and in the REPL.

An explicit authority block keeps today's exact behaviour.

## Current state
- The Rust host in the working tree already implements both parts in `crates/jet-foundation/src/Authority.rs` (modified, uncommitted):
  - `AMBIENT_BASIC_EFFECTS = ["IO","Mem.Alloc","Exec.Args"]` (`:294-295`), which never holds the `Exec` root (asserted at `:984-988`).
  - `PACKAGE_DEFAULT` "package.jet default" (`:303`), and `package_default()` (`:310`) gives a manifest with no holds the same floor.
  - `policy_why` (`:436-456`) renders "This program …, and package.jet (which has no authority block) has not allowed that yet."
  - `policy_facts` (`:476-493`) carries the key=value facts as structured detail, and `policy_refusal` (`:497`) is the one renderer.
- `crates/jet-pkg-model/src/EffectBudget.rs` is also modified.
- Remaining copies still render key=value: `crates/jet-repl/src/lib.rs:231` and `crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Methods/repl_process.rs:22`.
- Jet homes still render key=value too: `Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Policy/EffectProjection.jet:95`. `Jetpack/Foundation/Source/Authority.jet` has the ambient floor (`:17-20`, `:218-221`) but no package-default floor or plain Why. #3607 (building) ports PackageModel authority.

## Changes
1. Rust host, which the shipped binary uses: land the working-tree `Authority.rs` / `EffectBudget.rs` changes. Make the REPL (`jet-repl/src/lib.rs:230`) and `repl_process.rs:21` call `ApplicationAuthority::policy_why` / `policy_facts` instead of their own format strings, leaving one renderer.
2. Jet mirror: `EffectProjection.jet:95` builds the same sentence from projection facts, with the facts moved to detail. `Foundation/Source/Authority.jet` adds the package-default floor with the same three effects. Coordinate with #3607 on paths only.
3. Update `jet explain E1803` and the first-hour guide text in `Docs/`.

## Proof

cards.title: An unclosed bracket is reported at its opener, never as a missing comma before an invisible semicolon
cards.body:
What is broken: probe p16

    fn run() {
        print("hello"
    }

reports `Error [E0003]: Expected `,` between arguments, found `;``, pointing
past `"hello"`. There is no `;` in the source: the lexer inserts a synthetic
line terminator (crates/jet-lexer/src/Lexer/Terminators.rs:269-286) and the
parser's `expect` (crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/mod.rs:954) names it. The
error also never points at the `(` that was left open. Mismatched brackets
were the most frequent novice mistake in the Blackbox data.

Owner instruction (chat, 2026-09-28): the owner reviewed the learnability report and directed that this fix be carded at P0. This card records that direction; it is not a ballot.

Probe sources live in the report's Appendix A. They ran from a directory with its own package.jet granting [IO, Mem.Alloc], on the working-tree debug binary of 2026-09-28 13:07 (HEAD 68e1f8fb plus another stream's uncommitted compiler edits). Re-run each probe on a fresh build before starting; a probe that no longer reproduces is recorded on the card, not silently dropped.
cards.plan:
## Goal
An unclosed `(`, `[`, `{`, or `{` inside interpolated text is reported once, at its opener: E0083 ``(` opened on line 2 is never closed``, with the cut-off point as a secondary label and a Suggested insert-closer edit. No human diagnostic ever names the synthetic line terminator as `;`. Owner direction (chat 2026-09-28): carded at P0; this is not a ballot.

Probe p16:
```jet
fn run() {
    print("hello"
}
```
Today this reports `E0003 Expected `,` between arguments, found `;`` past `"hello"`.

## Current state
- In flight: E0083 is registered in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Diagnostics.jet:87 (working tree). UI fixtures tests/ui/unclosed_paren_call.jet, unclosed_bracket_list.jet, unclosed_brace_block.jet and unclosed_brace_interpolation.jet exist without .stderr snapshots. No parser emits E0083 yet, and E0083 is not in Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet.
- Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/State.jet:148 parser_expect prints `found `{token.payload.text}``, which is `;` for a synthetic terminator. Call args are in Expressions.jet (~:1035) and collections (~:768). There is no open-delimiter stack.
- The shipped front end (crates/jet-parser) renders the UI snapshots, so it needs the same behavior (user-visible mirror, as E0082 already did).

## Changes
1. JetParser State.jet: an open-delimiter stack (kind and opener span) pushed and popped by call, list/map, index, block and interpolation parsers (JetLexer for interpolation holes). When a list is cut off by a synthetic terminator (TOKEN_SEMI with an empty span), a closer of another kind, or EOF, emit E0083 with the opener as primary span, a cut-off secondary label and a Suggested insert-closer edit. Recover to the matching outer closer, so there is one report per delimiter and no cascade.
2. parser_expect/parser_add_error: a synthetic terminator is described as `end of line`.
3. The same behavior in crates/jet-parser (the `expect(Comma, "between arguments")` sites and the block/list/interpolation equivalents).
4. Regenerate rows: `node Compiler/Bootstrap/generate-diagnostic-rows.mjs`.
5. Add a test that fails if any human-rendered parser diagnostic in tests/ui/*.stderr contains the synthetic `;` (criterion 6).

## Proof
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/unclosed_ cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` passes with 4 reviewed snapshots, each with a single E0083 and a caret on the opener.
- `cargo test --test selfhost_parser generated_jet_call_arguments_match_native_parser_contract` passes with new CASES rows for p16 and the unclosed `[`/`{`/interpolation cases (identical diagnostics from the Jet and Rust parsers).
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.

## Batch
batch-jetc-front: parser diagnostics with the parser-slice proof.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: A clean jet check prints one line
cards.body:
What is wrong: a clean `jet check file.jet` (report F16, probe p03) prints a
key=value status line and four lines like

    proof: output=not-applicable entry resolution [not applicable]
      explicit-file checks resolve only the named source file (diagnostic=E2389)

before `ok: ... has no problems`. A learner reads five lines of internal
terms to learn "no problems" (Becker et al. 2019: reduce cognitive load).

Owner instruction (chat, 2026-09-28): the owner reviewed the learnability report and directed that this fix be carded at P0. This card records that direction; it is not a ballot.

Probe sources live in the report's Appendix A. They ran from a directory with its own package.jet granting [IO, Mem.Alloc], on the working-tree debug binary of 2026-09-28 13:07 (HEAD 68e1f8fb plus another stream's uncommitted compiler edits). Re-run each probe on a fresh build before starting; a probe that no longer reproduces is recorded on the card, not silently dropped.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
A clean `jet check` prints exactly one human line, for example ``ok: `p03.jet` has no problems``. The status line and proof rows move behind `--verbose`, and `--json` is byte-identical. The owner directed P0 (learnability report F16, probe p03).

**Current state**
- `Source/CmdCompile.rs:3230-3244` (the `cmd == "check"` branch of `run_native_execution_inner`, `:3009`): whenever output is neither JSON nor quiet, it writes `CmdInspect::check_result_text` and the `CmdFill::render_goal_report`.
- `Source/CmdInspect.rs:1161-1181` renders `check: passed (source=…, profile=…, scope=…, schema_version=…, elapsed_ms=…, …)` plus one `proof: output=… (diagnostic=E2389..E2392)` row per `check.proof_rows`.
- `CmdCompile.rs:3255-3256` then prints the `ok:` line, but only when there are no lints.
- `verbose` is already in scope (`:3026`), and `--verbose` is a global flag (`crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs:1891`).
- The project-check snapshots in `tests/project_check/fixtures/*/expected.stdout` expect the proof rows on the default path (see `proof_snapshot` in `tests/project_check.rs:195`).
- Dossier, expand, and impact print `check_result_text` themselves and are unaffected.

**Changes**
1. `Source/CmdCompile.rs:3230`: render `check_result_text` only when `verbose`. Leave the goal report unchanged: it prints only when goals exist.
2. With lints and no errors, print the lints (they already go through `report_problems`), then one summary line: ``ok: `file` has no errors (N warnings)``.
3. Update the `tests/project_check.rs` callers that snapshot proof rows (`run_check`, `run_uncached`, `run_project_check` users such as `frozen_dogfood_and_each_project_proof_witness_are_snapshotted` and `explicit_file_uses_owning_project_context`) to pass `--verbose`. The `expected.stdout` files stay as they are.
4. Update docs that quote the old output (grep `check: passed` under Docs/).

**Proof**
- New `cargo test --test cli_runtime -- clean_check_prints_one_line`: both `jet check file.jet` and project `jet check` produce exactly one line of stdout+stderr, the `ok:` line.
- New `cargo test --test cli_runtime -- check_warning_prints_warnings_and_summary`.
- `cargo test --test project_check` passes, with the proof snapshots unchanged under `--verbose` and the JSON rows test (`project_check_json_rows_are_versioned_and_warm_stable`) byte-identical.

**Batch**
`batch-host-cli`: CLI output only.

**Dependencies**
None.

cards.title: jet new creates a print-only project that runs, and the richer templates are opt-in
cards.body:
What is broken: the default `jet new` project (Source/CmdCompile.rs:5270-5275)
contains a `#CLI` struct with `#Doc` and a `String{"world"}` default, a
closure passed to `ui.reactive_render`, `ui.null_backend()`, and
`ui.constraint(0.0, 0.0, 320.0, 80.0)`, plus four `@*.jet` override files.
The first-hour guide (Docs/spec/guides/first-hour.md:92-103) says `jet run`
prints `hello, world` and never mentions the UI code.

On both working-tree binaries of 2026-09-28, `jet run` in a fresh scaffold
failed with seven errors, including errors inside Core/ui/ui.jet (E0768 at
lines 121 and 126, E1102 at line 141) and
"`ui.mount` needs a `UiNode` tree, but the second argument is
`<corelib>/Core/ui::Core/ui/ui.jet::UiNode`" — the same type shown as a
mismatch — with the first two errors printed twice.

Research: every concept before the first useful result is extraneous load
(Hermans; Guzdial "CS1 has too large a cognitive load"); setup failures make
newcomers conclude everything will be that hard.

Owner instruction (chat, 2026-09-28): the owner reviewed the learnability report and directed that this fix be carded at P0. This card records that direction; it is not a ballot.

Probe sources live in the report's Appendix A. They ran from a directory with its own package.jet granting [IO, Mem.Alloc], on the working-tree debug binary of 2026-09-28 13:07 (HEAD 68e1f8fb plus another stream's uncommitted compiler edits). Re-run each probe on a fresh build before starting; a probe that no longer reproduces is recorded on the card, not silently dropped.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Implement ratified D-NEW-TEMPLATE1=A. Plain `jet new hello` creates a print-only project that runs and prints `hello, world`. The richer starters become opt-in: `--template cli`, `--template ui`, `--template web`, and `--template overrides` (the `@*.jet` homes). Fix the Core/ui errors the UI starter hits at their root. The owner directed P0.

**Current state**
- `Source/CmdCompile.rs:5218` `run_new(name, annotated, web, mode)`.
- The default `run.jet` (`:5277`) has `#CLI struct GreetingArgs`, `ui.null_backend()`, `ui.reactive_render`, and `ui.mount(... ui.constraint(...))`.
- `web` (selected by `--target=web`, `Source/main.rs:2891`) writes the counter starter (`:5275`).
- `:5288-5311` always writes the four `@run/@build/@dev/@test.jet` homes.
- The manifest adds `Exec.Args` and `Browser` holds (`:5241-5250`).
- Dispatch is at `Source/main.rs:4745-4755`, and no `--template` flag exists.
- Core errors:
  - `Core/ui/ui.jet:121,126` pass positional `body` after the labelled `viewport:`, which is E0768 per `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Binder.jet:199`.
  - `:141` `reactive_render(body: fn())` hands off `body`, raising E1102 (`Ownership/Crossings.jet:393`).
  - `ui.jet` declares its own `pub struct UiNode` (`:78`) while delegating to `core.ui.*`, which yields the two-identity `UiNode`/`SizeConstraint` mismatch [INFERENCE: confirm on a fresh build].
- Tests pinning the old scaffold:
  - `tests/jet_test.rs:1264` `jet_new_creates_project` asserts `#CLI`/`GreetingArgs`.
  - `tests/web_scaffold.rs:277` `jet_new_native_scaffold_builds_for_explicit_web_target`.
  - `tests/web_scaffold.rs:180` uses `new web_app --target=web`.
- Docs: `Docs/spec/guides/first-hour.md:57-103` lists the `@*.jet` files and the `#CLI` starter.

**Changes**
1. `run_new` takes `template: Option<Template>` (Cli, Ui, Web, Overrides) parsed in `Source/main.rs` from `--template <name>`.
   - Add a `FlagSpec` row in `crates/jet-cli/src/CLI.rs` and update `jet new` usage.
   - An unknown value gives E2104 with the list of valid names.
   - Per greenfield cutover, `--target=web` stops selecting a starter.
2. Default writes `package.jet` (no extra holds), `run.jet`, and `.gitignore` only. `run.jet` holds `greeting`, `run() { print(greeting("world")) }`, and the `#Test("the greeting stays stable")` block.
3. Template contents:
   - `cli` is the typed `#CLI` starter without UI.
   - `ui` is today's native UI starter.
   - `web` is today's web starter with the `Browser` hold.
   - `overrides` adds the four comment-only homes.
4. `Core/ui/ui.jet`:
   - Label or reorder `body` in `preview`/`playground`.
   - Fix the `reactive_render` handoff.
   - Re-export the `core.ui` types instead of redeclaring `UiNode` and `SizeConstraint`, so there is one identity.
   - Deduplicate the repeated reports at their source.
5. Update the first-hour guide lessons 1-2 and `Examples/features/basics/onboarding/` to match the files exactly.

**Proof**
- `cargo test --test jet_test -- jet_new_creates_project` (rewritten): `jet new hello`, `jet run` prints exactly `hello, world`, `jet test` reports 1 passed, and `jet run --interpret` and `jet build`+binary agree.
- New `cargo test --test jet_test -- jet_new_every_template_runs_and_tests`: `cli`, `ui`, `web` (via `jet test` and `jet build --target web`), and `overrides` all succeed with no diagnostic located under Core/.
- `cargo test --test web_scaffold` passes after migrating to `--template web`.
- New fixture `tests/ui/ui_facade_single_uinode_identity.jet`: calls `ui.mount(ui.null_backend(), ui.text("x"), ui.constraint(0.0,0.0,1.0,1.0))`; expected clean.

**Batch**
`batch-host-cli`: the scaffold and flag are CLI code. The Core/ui fix rides in the same rebuild because embedded Core ships in the binary.

**Dependencies**
None. The `T?` migration of `Core/ui/ui.jet` is already in the working tree from the syntax wave.

cards.title: jet explain for a symbol answers in plain words with every meaning and an example
cards.body:
What is wrong: `jet explain ^` prints

    What this means:
      SIGIL_MOVE: registered sigil `^`
    Why Jet enforces it:
      owner decision D-CAP2

`jet explain ??` prints "OP_FALLBACK". The answer uses internal constant
names and a decision ID, omits that infix `^` means power, gives no example,
and does not say what happens to the old name after a move. Lattner's rule
for rare features is that a reader who meets one should be able to find out
what it does; Victor: "read the vocabulary".

Owner instruction (chat, 2026-09-28): the owner reviewed the learnability report and directed that this fix be carded at P0. This card records that direction; it is not a ballot.

Probe sources live in the report's Appendix A. They ran from a directory with its own package.jet granting [IO, Mem.Alloc], on the working-tree debug binary of 2026-09-28 13:07 (HEAD 68e1f8fb plus another stream's uncommitted compiler edits). Re-run each probe on a fresh build before starting; a probe that no longer reproduces is recorded on the card, not silently dropped.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
`jet explain <glyph>` answers in plain words: every meaning by position (prefix, infix, signature, pattern), an example for each, what the reader should expect afterwards, and related diagnostic codes — no internal constant names or decision IDs by default. Owner instruction (2026-09-28) carded this at P0 after the learnability report.

**Current state**
- `jet explain ^` prints "SIGIL_MOVE: registered sigil `^`" and "owner decision D-CAP2"; `jet explain ??` prints "OP_FALLBACK"; no mention that infix `^` is power, no example, nothing about the moved-from name.
- Source: crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/dictionary.rs — `SyntaxDictionaryRow` (line 23: token, name, meaning, …), `meaning()` falls back to "registered sigil `{token}`" (line 235), one row per token (`lookup`, line 38). crates/jet-cli/src/Explain.rs:111-125 maps a row to an Explanation; `render` (line 351) prints "What this means" / "Why Jet enforces it".
- Consumers: Source/CmdDevTools.rs:4247 (`jet explain`), crates/jet-repl/src/Docs.rs:124 (REPL `?`, prints `Decision:`), crates/jetpack/src/CLI/update_search_info.rs:526; snapshot test tests/explain_syntax.rs `explain_syntax_dictionary_golden` with goldens in tests/cli/.
- No Jet-side syntax dictionary exists under Compiler/; this is the retained CLI host surface.

**Changes**
1. dictionary.rs: give each row a list of meanings `{position, text, example (two lines), afterwards, related_codes}`; write plain text for every sigil and operator in the lexical ledger and OP_*/SIGIL_* tables (`^ & ! ~ ~| / * T{…} == # @ | ?? ?. ... :: := -[…]> ?`). `^`: prefix move (old name unusable afterwards; E-codes for use-after-move) and infix power. Say it once: rows are the only text home.
2. Explain.rs: render all meanings with examples; constant names and decision IDs appear only under `jet explain <glyph> --verbose`.
3. REPL Docs.rs and LSP hover render the same default text (drop `Decision:` from the default).
4. Refresh tests/cli/explain_syntax_*.txt goldens; add `^` and `??` goldens.
5. Add a registry walk test in tests/explain_syntax.rs: every sigil/operator row has ≥1 meaning with an example and its default render contains no `SIGIL_`, `OP_` or `D-` decision token.

**Proof**
- `cargo test --test explain_syntax explain_syntax_dictionary_golden` (new `explain_syntax_caret.txt` shows both meanings, examples, "afterwards").
- `cargo test --test explain_syntax explain_syntax_rows_are_plain_and_exampled` (new walk test).
- `cargo test --test repl` and `cargo test --test lsp` filtered to the hover/`?` cases show the same text; `jet explain ^ --verbose` still shows SIGIL_MOVE and D-CAP2.

**Batch**
batch-host-cli: CLI explain, REPL and LSP host tooling.

**Dependencies**
None.
